497 class InheritDocstrings(type):
498     """
499     This metaclass makes methods of a class automatically have their
500     docstrings filled in from the methods they override in the base
501     class.
502 
503     If the class uses multiple inheritance, the docstring will be
504     chosen from the first class in the bases list, in the same way as
505     methods are normally resolved in Python.  If this results in
506     selecting the wrong docstring, the docstring will need to be
507     explicitly included on the method.
508 
509     For example::
510 
511         >>> from astropy.utils.misc import InheritDocstrings
512         >>> class A(metaclass=InheritDocstrings):
513         ...     def wiggle(self):
514         ...         "Wiggle the thingamajig"
515         ...         pass
516         >>> class B(A):
517         ...     def wiggle(self):
518         ...         pass
519         >>> B.wiggle.__doc__
520         u'Wiggle the thingamajig'
521     """
522 
523     def __init__(cls, name, bases, dct):
524         def is_public_member(key):
525             return (
526                 (key.startswith('__') and key.endswith('__')
527                  and len(key) > 4) or
528                 not key.startswith('_'))
529 
530         for key, val in dct.items():
531             if (inspect.isfunction(val) and
532                 is_public_member(key) and
533                 val.__doc__ is None):
534                 for base in cls.__mro__[1:]:
535                     super_method = getattr(base, key, None)
536                     if super_method is not None:
537                         val.__doc__ = super_method.__doc__
538                         break
539 
540         super().__init__(name, bases, dct)

543 class OrderedDescriptor(metaclass=abc.ABCMeta):
544     """
545     Base class for descriptors whose order in the class body should be
546     preserved.  Intended for use in concert with the
547     `OrderedDescriptorContainer` metaclass.
548 
549     Subclasses of `OrderedDescriptor` must define a value for a class attribute
550     called ``_class_attribute_``.  This is the name of a class attribute on the
551     *container* class for these descriptors, which will be set to an
552     `~collections.OrderedDict` at class creation time.  This
553     `~collections.OrderedDict` will contain a mapping of all class attributes
554     that were assigned instances of the `OrderedDescriptor` subclass, to the
555     instances themselves.  See the documentation for
556     `OrderedDescriptorContainer` for a concrete example.
557 
558     Optionally, subclasses of `OrderedDescriptor` may define a value for a
559     class attribute called ``_name_attribute_``.  This should be the name of
560     an attribute on instances of the subclass.  When specified, during
561     creation of a class containing these descriptors, the name attribute on
562     each instance will be set to the name of the class attribute it was
563     assigned to on the class.
564 
565     .. note::
566 
567         Although this class is intended for use with *descriptors* (i.e.
568         classes that define any of the ``__get__``, ``__set__``, or
569         ``__delete__`` magic methods), this base class is not itself a
570         descriptor, and technically this could be used for classes that are
571         not descriptors too.  However, use with descriptors is the original
572         intended purpose.
573     """
574 
575     # This id increments for each OrderedDescriptor instance created, so they
576     # are always ordered in the order they were created.  Class bodies are
577     # guaranteed to be executed from top to bottom.  Not sure if this is
578     # thread-safe though.
579     _nextid = 1
580 
581     @property
582     @abc.abstractmethod
583     def _class_attribute_(self):
584         """
585         Subclasses should define this attribute to the name of an attribute on
586         classes containing this subclass.  That attribute will contain the mapping
587         of all instances of that `OrderedDescriptor` subclass defined in the class
588         body.  If the same descriptor needs to be used with different classes,
589         each with different names of this attribute, multiple subclasses will be
590         needed.
591         """
592 
593     _name_attribute_ = None
594     """
595     Subclasses may optionally define this attribute to specify the name of an
596     attribute on instances of the class that should be filled with the
597     instance's attribute name at class creation time.
598     """
599 
600     def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
601         # The _nextid attribute is shared across all subclasses so that
602         # different subclasses of OrderedDescriptors can be sorted correctly
603         # between themselves
604         self.__order = OrderedDescriptor._nextid
605         OrderedDescriptor._nextid += 1
606         super().__init__()
607 
608     def __lt__(self, other):
609         """
610         Defined for convenient sorting of `OrderedDescriptor` instances, which
611         are defined to sort in their creation order.
612         """
613 
614         if (isinstance(self, OrderedDescriptor) and
615                 isinstance(other, OrderedDescriptor)):
616             try:
617                 return self.__order < other.__order
618             except AttributeError:
619                 raise RuntimeError(
620                     'Could not determine ordering for {0} and {1}; at least '
621                     'one of them is not calling super().__init__ in its '
622                     '__init__.'.format(self, other))
623         else:
624             return NotImplemented

627 class OrderedDescriptorContainer(type):
628     """
629     Classes should use this metaclass if they wish to use `OrderedDescriptor`
630     attributes, which are class attributes that "remember" the order in which
631     they were defined in the class body.
632 
633     Every subclass of `OrderedDescriptor` has an attribute called
634     ``_class_attribute_``.  For example, if we have
635 
636     .. code:: python
637 
638         class ExampleDecorator(OrderedDescriptor):
639             _class_attribute_ = '_examples_'
640 
641     Then when a class with the `OrderedDescriptorContainer` metaclass is
642     created, it will automatically be assigned a class attribute ``_examples_``
643     referencing an `~collections.OrderedDict` containing all instances of
644     ``ExampleDecorator`` defined in the class body, mapped to by the names of
645     the attributes they were assigned to.
646 
647     When subclassing a class with this metaclass, the descriptor dict (i.e.
648     ``_examples_`` in the above example) will *not* contain descriptors
649     inherited from the base class.  That is, this only works by default with
650     decorators explicitly defined in the class body.  However, the subclass
651     *may* define an attribute ``_inherit_decorators_`` which lists
652     `OrderedDescriptor` classes that *should* be added from base classes.
653     See the examples section below for an example of this.
654 
655     Examples
656     --------
657 
658     >>> from astropy.utils import OrderedDescriptor, OrderedDescriptorContainer

35 def _flatten_units_collection(items):
36     """
37     Given a list of sequences, modules or dictionaries of units, or
38     single units, return a flat set of all the units found.
39     """
40     if not isinstance(items, list):
41         items = [items]
42 
43     result = set()
44     for item in items:
45         if isinstance(item, UnitBase):
46             result.add(item)
47         else:
48             if isinstance(item, dict):
49                 units = item.values()
50             elif inspect.ismodule(item):
51                 units = vars(item).values()
52             elif isiterable(item):
53                 units = item
54             else:
55                 continue
56 
57             for unit in units:
58                 if isinstance(unit, UnitBase):
59                     result.add(unit)

61     return result

64 def _normalize_equivalencies(equivalencies):
65     """
66     Normalizes equivalencies, ensuring each is a 4-tuple of the form::
67 
68     (from_unit, to_unit, forward_func, backward_func)
69 
70     Parameters
71     ----------
72     equivalencies : list of equivalency pairs
73 
74     Raises
75     ------
76     ValueError if an equivalency cannot be interpreted
77     """
78     if equivalencies is None:
79         return []
80 
81     normalized = []
82 
83     for i, equiv in enumerate(equivalencies):
84         if len(equiv) == 2:
85             funit, tunit = equiv
86             a = b = lambda x: x
87         elif len(equiv) == 3:
88             funit, tunit, a = equiv
89             b = a
90         elif len(equiv) == 4:
91             funit, tunit, a, b = equiv
92         else:
93             raise ValueError(
94                 "Invalid equivalence entry {0}: {1!r}".format(i, equiv))
95         if not (funit is Unit(funit) and
96                 (tunit is None or tunit is Unit(tunit)) and
97                 callable(a) and
98                 callable(b)):
99             raise ValueError(
100                 "Invalid equivalence entry {0}: {1!r}".format(i, equiv))
101         normalized.append((funit, tunit, a, b))
102 
103     return normalized

175         Adds to the set of units enabled in the unit registry.

183             This is a list of things in which units may be found

422     context = _UnitContext(get_current_unit_registry())
423     # in this new current registry, enable the equivalencies requested
424     get_current_unit_registry().set_enabled_equivalencies(equivalencies)

763     def is_equivalent(self, other, equivalencies=[]):
764         """
765         Returns `True` if this unit is equivalent to ``other``.
766 
767         Parameters
768         ----------
769         other : unit object or string or tuple
770             The unit to convert to. If a tuple of units is specified, this
771             method returns true if the unit matches any of those in the tuple.
772 
773         equivalencies : list of equivalence pairs, optional
774             A list of equivalence pairs to try if the units are not
775             directly convertible.  See :ref:`unit_equivalencies`.
776             This list is in addition to possible global defaults set by, e.g.,
777             `set_enabled_equivalencies`.
778             Use `None` to turn off all equivalencies.
779 
780         Returns
781         -------
782         bool
783         """
784         equivalencies = self._normalize_equivalencies(equivalencies)
785 
786         if isinstance(other, tuple):
787             return any(self.is_equivalent(u, equivalencies=equivalencies)
788                        for u in other)
789 
790         other = Unit(other, parse_strict='silent')
791 
792         return self._is_equivalent(other, equivalencies)
793 
794     def _is_equivalent(self, other, equivalencies=[]):
795         """Returns `True` if this unit is equivalent to `other`.
796         See `is_equivalent`, except that a proper Unit object should be
797         given (i.e., no string) and that the equivalency list should be
798         normalized using `_normalize_equivalencies`.
799         """
800         if isinstance(other, UnrecognizedUnit):
801             return False
802 
803         if (self._get_physical_type_id() ==
804                 other._get_physical_type_id()):
805             return True
806         elif len(equivalencies):
807             unit = self.decompose()
808             other = other.decompose()
809             for a, b, forward, backward in equivalencies:
810                 if b is None:
811                     # after canceling, is what's left convertible
812                     # to dimensionless (according to the equivalency)?
813                     try:
814                         (other/unit).decompose([a])
815                         return True
816                     except Exception:
817                         pass
818                 else:
819                     if(a._is_equivalent(unit) and b._is_equivalent(other) or
820                        b._is_equivalent(unit) and a._is_equivalent(other)):
821                         return True
822 
823         return False
824 
825     def _apply_equivalencies(self, unit, other, equivalencies):
826         """
827         Internal function (used from `_get_converter`) to apply
828         equivalence pairs.
829         """
830         def make_converter(scale1, func, scale2):
831             def convert(v):
832                 return func(_condition_arg(v) / scale1) * scale2
833             return convert
834 
835         for funit, tunit, a, b in equivalencies:
836             if tunit is None:
837                 try:
838                     ratio_in_funit = (other.decompose() /
839                                       unit.decompose()).decompose([funit])
840                     return make_converter(ratio_in_funit.scale, a, 1.)
841                 except UnitsError:
842                     pass
843             else:
844                 try:
845                     scale1 = funit._to(unit)
846                     scale2 = tunit._to(other)
847                     return make_converter(scale1, a, scale2)
848                 except UnitsError:
849                     pass
850                 try:
851                     scale1 = tunit._to(unit)
852                     scale2 = funit._to(other)
853                     return make_converter(scale1, b, scale2)
854                 except UnitsError:
855                     pass
856 
857         def get_err_str(unit):
858             unit_str = unit.to_string('unscaled')
859             physical_type = unit.physical_type
860             if physical_type != 'unknown':
861                 unit_str = "'{0}' ({1})".format(
862                     unit_str, physical_type)
863             else:
864                 unit_str = "'{0}'".format(unit_str)
865             return unit_str
866 
867         unit_str = get_err_str(unit)
868         other_str = get_err_str(other)
869 
870         raise UnitConversionError(
871             "{0} and {1} are not convertible".format(
872                 unit_str, other_str))
873 
874     def _get_converter(self, other, equivalencies=[]):
875         other = Unit(other)
876 
877         # First see if it is just a scaling.
878         try:
879             scale = self._to(other)
880         except UnitsError:
881             pass
882         else:
883             return lambda val: scale * _condition_arg(val)
884 
885         # if that doesn't work, maybe we can do it with equivalencies?
886         try:
887             return self._apply_equivalencies(
888                 self, other, self._normalize_equivalencies(equivalencies))
889         except UnitsError as exc:
890             # Last hope: maybe other knows how to do it?
891             # We assume the equivalencies have the unit itself as first item.
892             # TODO: maybe better for other to have a `_back_converter` method?
893             if hasattr(other, 'equivalencies'):
894                 for funit, tunit, a, b in other.equivalencies:
895                     if other is funit:
896                         try:
897                             return lambda v: b(self._get_converter(
898                                 tunit, equivalencies=equivalencies)(v))
899                         except Exception:
900                             pass
901 
902             raise exc
903 
904     def _to(self, other):
905         """
906         Returns the scale to the specified unit.
907 
908         See `to`, except that a Unit object should be given (i.e., no
909         string), and that all defaults are used, i.e., no
910         equivalencies and value=1.
911         """
912         # There are many cases where we just want to ensure a Quantity is
913         # of a particular unit, without checking whether it's already in
914         # a particular unit.  If we're being asked to convert from a unit
915         # to itself, we can short-circuit all of this.
916         if self is other:
917             return 1.0
918 
919         # Don't presume decomposition is possible; e.g.,
920         # conversion to function units is through equivalencies.
921         if isinstance(other, UnitBase):
922             self_decomposed = self.decompose()
923             other_decomposed = other.decompose()
924 
925             # Check quickly whether equivalent.  This is faster than
926             # `is_equivalent`, because it doesn't generate the entire
927             # physical type list of both units.  In other words it "fails
928             # fast".
929             if(self_decomposed.powers == other_decomposed.powers and
930                all(self_base is other_base for (self_base, other_base)
931                    in zip(self_decomposed.bases, other_decomposed.bases))):
932                 return self_decomposed.scale / other_decomposed.scale
933 
934         raise UnitConversionError(
935             "'{0!r}' is not a scaled version of '{1!r}'".format(self, other))
936 
937     def to(self, other, value=UNITY, equivalencies=[]):
938         """
939         Return the converted values in the specified unit.

941         Parameters
942         ----------

944             The unit to convert to.
945 
946         value : scalar int or float, or sequence convertible to array, optional
947             Value(s) in the current unit to be converted to the
948             specified unit.  If not provided, defaults to 1.0
949 
950         equivalencies : list of equivalence pairs, optional
951             A list of equivalence pairs to try if the units are not
952             directly convertible.  See :ref:`unit_equivalencies`.
953             This list is in addition to possible global defaults set by, e.g.,
954             `set_enabled_equivalencies`.

956 
957         Returns
958         -------
959         values : scalar or array
960             Converted value(s). Input value sequences are returned as
961             numpy arrays.
962 
963         Raises
964         ------
965         UnitsError
966             If units are inconsistent
967         """
968         if other is self and value is UNITY:
969             return UNITY
970         else:
971             return self._get_converter(other, equivalencies=equivalencies)(value)

980     def decompose(self, bases=set()):
981         """
982         Return a unit object composed of only irreducible units.
983 
984         Parameters
985         ----------
986         bases : sequence of UnitBase, optional
987             The bases to decompose into.  When not provided,
988             decomposes down to any irreducible units.  When provided,
989             the decomposed result will only contain the given units.
990             This will raises a `UnitsError` if it's not possible
991             to do so.
992 
993         Returns
994         -------
995         unit : CompositeUnit object
996             New object containing only irreducible unit objects.
997         """
998         raise NotImplementedError()
999 
1000     def _compose(self, equivalencies=[], namespace=[], max_depth=2, depth=0,
1001                  cached_results=None):
1002         def is_final_result(unit):
1003             # Returns True if this result contains only the expected
1004             # units
1005             for base in unit.bases:
1006                 if base not in namespace:
1007                     return False
1008             return True
1009 
1010         unit = self.decompose()
1011         key = hash(unit)
1012 
1013         cached = cached_results.get(key)
1014         if cached is not None:
1015             if isinstance(cached, Exception):
1016                 raise cached
1017             return cached
1018 
1019         # Prevent too many levels of recursion
1020         # And special case for dimensionless unit
1021         if depth >= max_depth:
1022             cached_results[key] = [unit]
1023             return [unit]
1024 
1025         # Make a list including all of the equivalent units
1026         units = [unit]
1027         for funit, tunit, a, b in equivalencies:
1028             if tunit is not None:
1029                 if self._is_equivalent(funit):
1030                     scale = funit.decompose().scale / unit.scale
1031                     units.append(Unit(a(1.0 / scale) * tunit).decompose())
1032                 elif self._is_equivalent(tunit):
1033                     scale = tunit.decompose().scale / unit.scale
1034                     units.append(Unit(b(1.0 / scale) * funit).decompose())
1035             else:
1036                 if self._is_equivalent(funit):
1037                     units.append(Unit(unit.scale))
1038 
1039         # Store partial results
1040         partial_results = []
1041         # Store final results that reduce to a single unit or pair of
1042         # units
1043         if len(unit.bases) == 0:
1044             final_results = [set([unit]), set()]
1045         else:
1046             final_results = [set(), set()]
1047 
1048         for tunit in namespace:
1049             tunit_decomposed = tunit.decompose()
1050             for u in units:
1051                 # If the unit is a base unit, look for an exact match
1052                 # to one of the bases of the target unit.  If found,
1053                 # factor by the same power as the target unit's base.
1054                 # This allows us to factor out fractional powers
1055                 # without needing to do an exhaustive search.
1056                 if len(tunit_decomposed.bases) == 1:
1057                     for base, power in zip(u.bases, u.powers):
1058                         if tunit_decomposed._is_equivalent(base):
1059                             tunit = tunit ** power
1060                             tunit_decomposed = tunit_decomposed ** power
1061                             break
1062 
1063                 composed = (u / tunit_decomposed).decompose()
1064                 factored = composed * tunit
1065                 len_bases = len(composed.bases)
1066                 if is_final_result(factored) and len_bases <= 1:
1067                     final_results[len_bases].add(factored)
1068                 else:
1069                     partial_results.append(
1070                         (len_bases, composed, tunit))
1071 
1072         # Do we have any minimal results?
1073         for final_result in final_results:
1074             if len(final_result):
1075                 results = final_results[0].union(final_results[1])
1076                 cached_results[key] = results
1077                 return results
1078 
1079         partial_results.sort(key=operator.itemgetter(0))
1080 
1081         # ...we have to recurse and try to further compose
1082         results = []
1083         for len_bases, composed, tunit in partial_results:
1084             try:
1085                 composed_list = composed._compose(
1086                     equivalencies=equivalencies,
1087                     namespace=namespace,
1088                     max_depth=max_depth, depth=depth + 1,
1089                     cached_results=cached_results)
1090             except UnitsError:
1091                 composed_list = []
1092             for subcomposed in composed_list:
1093                 results.append(
1094                     (len(subcomposed.bases), subcomposed, tunit))
1095 
1096         if len(results):
1097             results.sort(key=operator.itemgetter(0))
1098 
1099             min_length = results[0][0]
1100             subresults = set()
1101             for len_bases, composed, tunit in results:
1102                 if len_bases > min_length:
1103                     break
1104                 else:
1105                     factored = composed * tunit
1106                     if is_final_result(factored):
1107                         subresults.add(factored)
1108 
1109             if len(subresults):
1110                 cached_results[key] = subresults
1111                 return subresults
1112 
1113         if not is_final_result(self):
1114             result = UnitsError(
1115                 "Cannot represent unit {0} in terms of the given "
1116                 "units".format(self))
1117             cached_results[key] = result
1118             raise result
1119 
1120         cached_results[key] = [self]
1121         return [self]
1122 
1123     def compose(self, equivalencies=[], units=None, max_depth=2,
1124                 include_prefix_units=None):
1125         """
1126         Return the simplest possible composite unit(s) that represent
1127         the given unit.  Since there may be multiple equally simple
1128         compositions of the unit, a list of units is always returned.
1129 
1130         Parameters
1131         ----------
1132         equivalencies : list of equivalence pairs, optional
1133             A list of equivalence pairs to also list.  See
1134             :ref:`unit_equivalencies`.
1135             This list is in addition to possible global defaults set by, e.g.,
1136             `set_enabled_equivalencies`.
1137             Use `None` to turn off all equivalencies.
1138 
1139         units : set of units to compose to, optional
1140             If not provided, any known units may be used to compose
1141             into.  Otherwise, ``units`` is a dict, module or sequence
1142             containing the units to compose into.
1143 
1144         max_depth : int, optional
1145             The maximum recursion depth to use when composing into
1146             composite units.
1147 
1148         include_prefix_units : bool, optional
1149             When `True`, include prefixed units in the result.
1150             Default is `True` if a sequence is passed in to ``units``,
1151             `False` otherwise.
1152 
1153         Returns
1154         -------
1155         units : list of `CompositeUnit`
1156             A list of candidate compositions.  These will all be
1157             equally simple, but it may not be possible to
1158             automatically determine which of the candidates are
1159             better.
1160         """
1161         # if units parameter is specified and is a sequence (list|tuple),
1162         # include_prefix_units is turned on by default.  Ex: units=[u.kpc]
1163         if include_prefix_units is None:
1164             include_prefix_units = isinstance(units, (list, tuple))
1165 
1166         # Pre-normalize the equivalencies list
1167         equivalencies = self._normalize_equivalencies(equivalencies)
1168 
1169         # The namespace of units to compose into should be filtered to
1170         # only include units with bases in common with self, otherwise
1171         # they can't possibly provide useful results.  Having too many
1172         # destination units greatly increases the search space.
1173 
1174         def has_bases_in_common(a, b):
1175             if len(a.bases) == 0 and len(b.bases) == 0:
1176                 return True
1177             for ab in a.bases:
1178                 for bb in b.bases:
1179                     if ab == bb:
1180                         return True
1181             return False
1182 
1183         def has_bases_in_common_with_equiv(unit, other):
1184             if has_bases_in_common(unit, other):
1185                 return True
1186             for funit, tunit, a, b in equivalencies:
1187                 if tunit is not None:
1188                     if unit._is_equivalent(funit):
1189                         if has_bases_in_common(tunit.decompose(), other):
1190                             return True
1191                     elif unit._is_equivalent(tunit):
1192                         if has_bases_in_common(funit.decompose(), other):
1193                             return True
1194                 else:
1195                     if unit._is_equivalent(funit):
1196                         if has_bases_in_common(dimensionless_unscaled, other):
1197                             return True
1198             return False
1199 
1200         def filter_units(units):
1201             filtered_namespace = set()
1202             for tunit in units:
1203                 if (isinstance(tunit, UnitBase) and
1204                     (include_prefix_units or
1205                      not isinstance(tunit, PrefixUnit)) and
1206                     has_bases_in_common_with_equiv(
1207                         decomposed, tunit.decompose())):
1208                     filtered_namespace.add(tunit)
1209             return filtered_namespace
1210 
1211         decomposed = self.decompose()
1212 
1213         if units is None:
1214             units = filter_units(self._get_units_with_same_physical_type(
1215                 equivalencies=equivalencies))
1216             if len(units) == 0:
1217                 units = get_current_unit_registry().non_prefix_units
1218         elif isinstance(units, dict):
1219             units = set(filter_units(units.values()))
1220         elif inspect.ismodule(units):
1221             units = filter_units(vars(units).values())
1222         else:
1223             units = filter_units(_flatten_units_collection(units))
1224 
1225         def sort_results(results):
1226             if not len(results):
1227                 return []
1228 
1229             # Sort the results so the simplest ones appear first.
1230             # Simplest is defined as "the minimum sum of absolute
1231             # powers" (i.e. the fewest bases), and preference should
1232             # be given to results where the sum of powers is positive
1233             # and the scale is exactly equal to 1.0
1234             results = list(results)
1235             results.sort(key=lambda x: np.abs(x.scale))
1236             results.sort(key=lambda x: np.sum(np.abs(x.powers)))
1237             results.sort(key=lambda x: np.sum(x.powers) < 0.0)
1238             results.sort(key=lambda x: not is_effectively_unity(x.scale))
1239 
1240             last_result = results[0]
1241             filtered = [last_result]
1242             for result in results[1:]:
1243                 if str(result) != str(last_result):
1244                     filtered.append(result)
1245                 last_result = result
1246 
1247             return filtered
1248 
1249         return sort_results(self._compose(
1250             equivalencies=equivalencies, namespace=units,
1251             max_depth=max_depth, depth=0, cached_results={}))

1253     def to_system(self, system):
1254         """
1255         Converts this unit into ones belonging to the given system.
1256         Since more than one result may be possible, a list is always
1257         returned.
1258 
1259         Parameters
1260         ----------
1261         system : module
1262             The module that defines the unit system.  Commonly used
1263             ones include `astropy.units.si` and `astropy.units.cgs`.
1264 
1265             To use your own module it must contain unit objects and a
1266             sequence member named ``bases`` containing the base units of
1267             the system.
1268 
1269         Returns
1270         -------
1271         units : list of `CompositeUnit`
1272             The list is ranked so that units containing only the base
1273             units of that system will appear first.
1274         """
1275         bases = set(system.bases)
1276 
1277         def score(compose):
1278             # In case that compose._bases has no elements we return
1279             # 'np.inf' as 'score value'.  It does not really matter which
1280             # number we would return. This case occurs for instance for
1281             # dimensionless quantities:
1282             compose_bases = compose.bases
1283             if len(compose_bases) == 0:
1284                 return np.inf
1285             else:
1286                 sum = 0
1287                 for base in compose_bases:
1288                     if base in bases:
1289                         sum += 1
1290 
1291                 return sum / float(len(compose_bases))
1292 
1293         x = self.decompose(bases=bases)
1294         composed = x.compose(units=system)
1295         composed = sorted(composed, key=score, reverse=True)
1296         return composed

1364     class EquivalentUnitsList(list):

1367         `find_equivalent_units`.

1370         def __repr__(self):
1371             if len(self) == 0:
1372                 return "[]"
1373             else:
1374                 lines = []
1375                 for u in self:
1376                     irred = u.decompose().to_string()
1377                     if irred == u.name:
1378                         irred = "irreducible"
1379                     lines.append((u.name, irred, ', '.join(u.aliases)))
1380 
1381                 lines.sort()
1382                 lines.insert(0, ('Primary name', 'Unit definition', 'Aliases'))
1383                 widths = [0, 0, 0]
1384                 for line in lines:
1385                     for i, col in enumerate(line):
1386                         widths[i] = max(widths[i], len(col))
1387 
1388                 f = "  {{0:<{0}s}} | {{1:<{1}s}} | {{2:<{2}s}}".format(*widths)
1389                 lines = [f.format(*line) for line in lines]
1390                 lines = (lines[0:1] +
1391                          ['['] +
1392                          ['{0} ,'.format(x) for x in lines[1:]] +
1393                          [']'])
1394                 return '\n'.join(lines)

1396     def find_equivalent_units(self, equivalencies=[], units=None,

1401         Parameters
1402         ----------
1403         equivalencies : list of equivalence pairs, optional
1404             A list of equivalence pairs to also list.  See
1405             :ref:`unit_equivalencies`.
1406             Any list given, including an empty one, supercedes global defaults
1407             that may be in effect (as set by `set_enabled_equivalencies`)
1408 
1409         units : set of units to search in, optional
1410             If not provided, all defined units will be searched for
1411             equivalencies.  Otherwise, may be a dict, module or
1412             sequence containing the units to search for equivalencies.

1425         results = self.compose(
1426             equivalencies=equivalencies, units=units, max_depth=1,

1429             x.bases[0] for x in results if len(x.bases) == 1)

1439 class NamedUnit(UnitBase):
1440     """
1441     The base class of units that have a name.
1442 
1443     Parameters
1444     ----------
1445     st : str, list of str, 2-tuple
1446         The name of the unit.  If a list of strings, the first element
1447         is the canonical (short) name, and the rest of the elements
1448         are aliases.  If a tuple of lists, the first element is a list
1449         of short names, and the second element is a list of long
1450         names; all but the first short name are considered "aliases".
1451         Each name *should* be a valid Python identifier to make it
1452         easy to access, but this is not required.
1453 
1454     namespace : dict, optional
1455         When provided, inject the unit, and all of its aliases, in the
1456         given namespace dictionary.  If a unit by the same name is
1457         already in the namespace, a ValueError is raised.
1458 
1459     doc : str, optional
1460         A docstring describing the unit.
1461 
1462     format : dict, optional
1463         A mapping to format-specific representations of this unit.
1464         For example, for the ``Ohm`` unit, it might be nice to have it
1465         displayed as ``\\Omega`` by the ``latex`` formatter.  In that
1466         case, `format` argument should be set to::
1467 
1468             {'latex': r'\\Omega'}
1469 
1470     Raises
1471     ------
1472     ValueError
1473         If any of the given unit names are already in the registry.
1474 
1475     ValueError
1476         If any of the given unit names are not valid Python tokens.
1477     """
1478 
1479     def __init__(self, st, doc=None, format=None, namespace=None):
1480 
1481         UnitBase.__init__(self)
1482 
1483         if isinstance(st, (bytes, str)):
1484             self._names = [st]
1485             self._short_names = [st]
1486             self._long_names = []
1487         elif isinstance(st, tuple):
1488             if not len(st) == 2:
1489                 raise ValueError("st must be string, list or 2-tuple")
1490             self._names = st[0] + [n for n in st[1] if n not in st[0]]
1491             if not len(self._names):
1492                 raise ValueError("must provide at least one name")
1493             self._short_names = st[0][:]
1494             self._long_names = st[1][:]
1495         else:
1496             if len(st) == 0:
1497                 raise ValueError(
1498                     "st list must have at least one entry")
1499             self._names = st[:]
1500             self._short_names = [st[0]]
1501             self._long_names = st[1:]
1502 
1503         if format is None:
1504             format = {}
1505         self._format = format
1506 
1507         if doc is None:
1508             doc = self._generate_doc()
1509         else:
1510             doc = textwrap.dedent(doc)
1511             doc = textwrap.fill(doc)
1512 
1513         self.__doc__ = doc
1514 
1515         self._inject(namespace)

1584     def _inject(self, namespace=None):

1589         if namespace is None:

1592         # Loop through all of the names first, to ensure all of them
1593         # are new, then add them all as a single "transaction" below.
1594         for name in self._names:
1595             if name in namespace and self != namespace[name]:
1596                 raise ValueError(
1597                     "Object with name {0!r} already exists in "
1598                     "given namespace ({1!r}).".format(
1599                         name, namespace[name]))
1600 
1601         for name in self._names:
1602             namespace[name] = self

1605 def _recreate_irreducible_unit(cls, names, registered):
1606     """
1607     This is used to reconstruct units when passed around by
1608     multiprocessing.
1609     """
1610     registry = get_current_unit_registry().registry
1611     if names[0] in registry:
1612         # If in local registry return that object.
1613         return registry[names[0]]
1614     else:
1615         # otherwise, recreate the unit.
1616         unit = cls(names)
1617         if registered:
1618             # If not in local registry but registered in origin registry,
1619             # enable unit in local registry.
1620             get_current_unit_registry().add_enabled_units([unit])
1621 
1622         return unit

1625 class IrreducibleUnit(NamedUnit):
1626     """
1627     Irreducible units are the units that all other units are defined
1628     in terms of.

1630     Examples are meters, seconds, kilograms, amperes, etc.  There is
1631     only once instance of such a unit per type.
1632     """
1633 
1634     def __reduce__(self):
1635         # When IrreducibleUnit objects are passed to other processes
1636         # over multiprocessing, they need to be recreated to be the
1637         # ones already in the subprocesses' namespace, not new
1638         # objects, or they will be considered "unconvertible".
1639         # Therefore, we have a custom pickler/unpickler that
1640         # understands how to recreate the Unit on the other side.
1641         registry = get_current_unit_registry().registry
1642         return (_recreate_irreducible_unit,
1643                 (self.__class__, list(self.names), self.name in registry),
1644                 self.__dict__)

1654     def decompose(self, bases=set()):
1655         if len(bases) and self not in bases:
1656             for base in bases:
1657                 try:
1658                     scale = self._to(base)
1659                 except UnitsError:
1660                     pass
1661                 else:
1662                     if is_effectively_unity(scale):
1663                         return base
1664                     else:
1665                         return CompositeUnit(scale, [base], [1],
1666                                              _error_check=False)
1667 
1668             raise UnitConversionError(
1669                 "Unit {0} can not be decomposed into the requested "
1670                 "bases".format(self))
1671 
1672         return self

1736 class _UnitMetaClass(InheritDocstrings):
1737     """
1738     This metaclass exists because the Unit constructor should
1739     sometimes return instances that already exist.  This "overrides"
1740     the constructor before the new instance is actually created, so we
1741     can return an existing one.
1742     """
1743 
1744     def __call__(self, s, represents=None, format=None, namespace=None,
1745                  doc=None, parse_strict='raise'):
1746 
1747         # Short-circuit if we're already a unit
1748         if hasattr(s, '_get_physical_type_id'):
1749             return s
1750 
1751         # turn possible Quantity input for s or represents into a Unit
1752         from .quantity import Quantity
1753 
1754         if isinstance(represents, Quantity):
1755             if is_effectively_unity(represents.value):
1756                 represents = represents.unit
1757             else:
1758                 # cannot use _error_check=False: scale may be effectively unity
1759                 represents = CompositeUnit(represents.value *
1760                                            represents.unit.scale,
1761                                            bases=represents.unit.bases,
1762                                            powers=represents.unit.powers)
1763 
1764         if isinstance(s, Quantity):
1765             if is_effectively_unity(s.value):
1766                 s = s.unit
1767             else:
1768                 s = CompositeUnit(s.value * s.unit.scale,
1769                                   bases=s.unit.bases,
1770                                   powers=s.unit.powers)
1771 
1772         # now decide what we really need to do; define derived Unit?
1773         if isinstance(represents, UnitBase):
1774             # This has the effect of calling the real __new__ and
1775             # __init__ on the Unit class.
1776             return super().__call__(
1777                 s, represents, format=format, namespace=namespace, doc=doc)
1778 
1779         # or interpret a Quantity (now became unit), string or number?
1780         if isinstance(s, UnitBase):
1781             return s
1782 
1783         elif isinstance(s, (bytes, str)):
1784             if len(s.strip()) == 0:
1785                 # Return the NULL unit
1786                 return dimensionless_unscaled
1787 
1788             if format is None:
1789                 format = unit_format.Generic
1790 
1791             f = unit_format.get_format(format)
1792             if isinstance(s, bytes):
1793                 s = s.decode('ascii')
1794 
1795             try:
1796                 return f.parse(s)
1797             except Exception as e:
1798                 if parse_strict == 'silent':
1799                     pass
1800                 else:
1801                     # Deliberately not issubclass here. Subclasses
1802                     # should use their name.
1803                     if f is not unit_format.Generic:
1804                         format_clause = f.name + ' '
1805                     else:
1806                         format_clause = ''
1807                     msg = ("'{0}' did not parse as {1}unit: {2}"
1808                            .format(s, format_clause, str(e)))
1809                     if parse_strict == 'raise':
1810                         raise ValueError(msg)
1811                     elif parse_strict == 'warn':
1812                         warnings.warn(msg, UnitsWarning)
1813                     else:
1814                         raise ValueError("'parse_strict' must be 'warn', "
1815                                          "'raise' or 'silent'")
1816                 return UnrecognizedUnit(s)
1817 
1818         elif isinstance(s, (int, float, np.floating, np.integer)):
1819             return CompositeUnit(s, [], [])
1820 
1821         elif s is None:
1822             raise TypeError("None is not a valid Unit")
1823 
1824         else:
1825             raise TypeError("{0} can not be converted to a Unit".format(s))

Header.fromstring does not accept Python 3 bytes
According to [the docs](http://docs.astropy.org/en/stable/_modules/astropy/io/fits/header.html#Header.fromstring), the method `Header.fromstring` "...creates an HDU header from a byte string containing the entire header data."

By "byte string" here it really means the `str` type which on Python 2 could be raw binary data, but on Python 3 explicitly is not.   In fact it does work on Python 3's unicode `str`s, but here it assumes that the data can be ASCII-encoded.

Its counterpart, `Header.fromfile` will work with files opened in text or binary mode.  So probably the simplest solution for now (as opposed to adding new methods or something like that) is to change `Header.fromstring` to accept unicode or bytes string types.

`Card.fromstring` likely needs a similar treatment.

269                 raise ValueError('Illegal keyword name: {!r}.'.format(keyword))
270             self._keyword = keyword
271             self._modified = True
272         else:
273             raise ValueError('Keyword name {!r} is not a string.'.format(keyword))

275     @property
276     def value(self):
277         """The value associated with the keyword stored in this card."""
278 
279         if self.field_specifier:
280             return float(self._value)
281 
282         if self._value is not None:
283             value = self._value
284         elif self._valuestring is not None or self._image:
285             value = self._value = self._parse_value()
286         else:
287             if self._keyword == '':
288                 self._value = value = ''
289             else:
290                 self._value = value = UNDEFINED
291 
292         if conf.strip_header_whitespace and isinstance(value, str):
293             value = value.rstrip()
294 
295         return value

297     @value.setter
298     def value(self, value):
299         if self._invalid:
300             raise ValueError(
301                 'The value of invalid/unparseable cards cannot set.  Either '
302                 'delete this card from the header or replace it.')
303 
304         if value is None:
305             value = UNDEFINED
306 
307         try:
308             oldvalue = self.value
309         except VerifyError:
310             # probably a parsing error, falling back to the internal _value
311             # which should be None. This may happen while calling _fix_value.
312             oldvalue = self._value
313 
314         if oldvalue is None:
315             oldvalue = UNDEFINED
316 
317         if not isinstance(value,
318                           (str, int, float, complex, bool, Undefined,
319                            np.floating, np.integer, np.complexfloating,
320                            np.bool_)):
321             raise ValueError('Illegal value: {!r}.'.format(value))
322 
323         if isinstance(value, float) and (np.isnan(value) or np.isinf(value)):
324             raise ValueError("Floating point {!r} values are not allowed "
325                              "in FITS headers.".format(value))
326 
327         elif isinstance(value, str):
328             m = self._ascii_text_re.match(value)
329             if not m:
330                 raise ValueError(
331                     'FITS header values must contain standard printable ASCII '
332                     'characters; {!r} contains characters not representable in '
333                     'ASCII or non-printable characters.'.format(value))
334         elif isinstance(value, bytes):
335             # Allow str, but only if they can be decoded to ASCII text; note
336             # this is not even allowed on Python 3 since the `bytes` type is
337             # not included in `str`.  Presently we simply don't
338             # allow bytes to be assigned to headers, as doing so would too
339             # easily mask potential user error
340             valid = True
341             try:
342                 text_value = value.decode('ascii')
343             except UnicodeDecodeError:
344                 valid = False
345             else:
346                 # Check against the printable characters regexp as well
347                 m = self._ascii_text_re.match(text_value)
348                 valid = m is not None
349 
350             if not valid:
351                 raise ValueError(
352                     'FITS header values must contain standard printable ASCII '
353                     'characters; {!r} contains characters/bytes that do not '
354                     'represent printable characters in ASCII.'.format(value))
355         elif isinstance(value, np.bool_):
356             value = bool(value)
357 
358         if (conf.strip_header_whitespace and
359             (isinstance(oldvalue, str) and isinstance(value, str))):
360             # Ignore extra whitespace when comparing the new value to the old
361             different = oldvalue.rstrip() != value.rstrip()
362         elif isinstance(oldvalue, bool) or isinstance(value, bool):
363             different = oldvalue is not value
364         else:
365             different = (oldvalue != value or
366                          not isinstance(value, type(oldvalue)))
367 
368         if different:
369             self._value = value
370             self._rawvalue = None
371             self._modified = True
372             self._valuestring = None
373             self._valuemodified = True
374             if self.field_specifier:
375                 try:
376                     self._value = _int_or_float(self._value)
377                 except ValueError:
378                     raise ValueError('value {} is not a float'.format(
379                             self._value))
380

385                 'The value of invalid/unparseable cards cannot deleted.  '
386                 'Either delete this card from the header or replace it.')
387 
388         if not self.field_specifier:
389             self.value = ''

391             raise AttributeError('Values cannot be deleted from record-valued '
392                                  'keyword cards')

526     @property

529         `True` if the card is completely blank--that is, it has no keyword,
530         value, or comment.  It appears in the header as 80 spaces.
531 
532         Returns `False` otherwise.
533         """
534 
535         if not self._verified:
536             # The card image has not been parsed yet; compare directly with the
537             # string representation of a blank card
538             return self._image == BLANK_CARD
539 
540         # If the keyword, value, and comment are all empty (for self.value
541         # explicitly check that it is a string value, since a blank value is
542         # returned as '')

544                 (isinstance(self.value, str) and not self.value) and
545                 not self.comment)

547     @classmethod

551         if it is not the length of a card image (80 columns).  If the card
552         image is longer than 80 columns, assume it contains ``CONTINUE``
553         card(s).

561     @classmethod
562     def normalize_keyword(cls, keyword):
563         """
564         `classmethod` to convert a keyword value that may contain a
565         field-specifier to uppercase.  The effect is to raise the key to
566         uppercase and leave the field specifier in its original case.
567 
568         Parameters
569         ----------
570         keyword : or str
571             A keyword value or a ``keyword.field-specifier`` value
572         """
573 
574         # Test first for the most common case: a standard FITS keyword provided
575         # in standard all-caps
576         if (len(keyword) <= KEYWORD_LENGTH and
577                 cls._keywd_FSC_RE.match(keyword)):
578             return keyword
579 
580         # Test if this is a record-valued keyword
581         match = cls._rvkc_keyword_name_RE.match(keyword)
582 
583         if match:
584             return '.'.join((match.group('keyword').strip().upper(),
585                              match.group('field_specifier')))
586         elif len(keyword) > 9 and keyword[:9].upper() == 'HIERARCH ':
587             # Remove 'HIERARCH' from HIERARCH keywords; this could lead to
588             # ambiguity if there is actually a keyword card containing
589             # "HIERARCH HIERARCH", but shame on you if you do that.
590             return keyword[9:].strip().upper()
591         else:
592             # A normal FITS keyword, but provided in non-standard case
593             return keyword.strip().upper()
594 
595     def _check_if_rvkc(self, *args):
596         """
597         Determine whether or not the card is a record-valued keyword card.
598 
599         If one argument is given, that argument is treated as a full card image
600         and parsed as such.  If two arguments are given, the first is treated
601         as the card keyword (including the field-specifier if the card is
602         intended as a RVKC), and the second as the card value OR the first value
603         can be the base keyword, and the second value the 'field-specifier:
604         value' string.
605 
606         If the check passes the ._keyword, ._value, and .field_specifier
607         keywords are set.
608 
609         Examples
610         --------
611 
612         ::
613 
614             self._check_if_rvkc('DP1', 'AXIS.1: 2')
615             self._check_if_rvkc('DP1.AXIS.1', 2)
616             self._check_if_rvkc('DP1     = AXIS.1: 2')
617         """
618 
619         if not conf.enable_record_valued_keyword_cards:
620             return False
621 
622         if len(args) == 1:
623             return self._check_if_rvkc_image(*args)
624         elif len(args) == 2:
625             keyword, value = args
626             if not isinstance(keyword, str):
627                 return False
628             if keyword in self._commentary_keywords:
629                 return False
630             match = self._rvkc_keyword_name_RE.match(keyword)
631             if match and isinstance(value, (int, float)):
632                 self._init_rvkc(match.group('keyword'),
633                                 match.group('field_specifier'), None, value)
634                 return True
635 
636             # Testing for ': ' is a quick way to avoid running the full regular
637             # expression, speeding this up for the majority of cases
638             if isinstance(value, str) and value.find(': ') > 0:
639                 match = self._rvkc_field_specifier_val_RE.match(value)
640                 if match and self._keywd_FSC_RE.match(keyword):
641                     self._init_rvkc(keyword, match.group('keyword'), value,
642                                     match.group('val'))
643                     return True
644 
645     def _check_if_rvkc_image(self, *args):
646         """
647         Implements `Card._check_if_rvkc` for the case of an unparsed card
648         image.  If given one argument this is the full intact image.  If given
649         two arguments the card has already been split between keyword and
650         value+comment at the standard value indicator '= '.
651         """
652 
653         if len(args) == 1:
654             image = args[0]
655             eq_idx = image.find(VALUE_INDICATOR)
656             if eq_idx < 0 or eq_idx > 9:
657                 return False
658             keyword = image[:eq_idx]
659             rest = image[eq_idx + VALUE_INDICATOR_LEN:]
660         else:
661             keyword, rest = args
662 
663         rest = rest.lstrip()
664 
665         # This test allows us to skip running the full regular expression for
666         # the majority of cards that do not contain strings or that definitely
667         # do not contain RVKC field-specifiers; it's very much a
668         # micro-optimization but it does make a measurable difference
669         if not rest or rest[0] != "'" or rest.find(': ') < 2:
670             return False
671 
672         match = self._rvkc_keyword_val_comm_RE.match(rest)
673         if match:
674             self._init_rvkc(keyword, match.group('keyword'),
675                             match.group('rawval'), match.group('val'))
676             return True
677 
678     def _init_rvkc(self, keyword, field_specifier, field, value):
679         """
680         Sort of addendum to Card.__init__ to set the appropriate internal
681         attributes if the card was determined to be a RVKC.
682         """
683 
684         keyword_upper = keyword.upper()
685         self._keyword = '.'.join((keyword_upper, field_specifier))
686         self._rawkeyword = keyword_upper
687         self._field_specifier = field_specifier
688         self._value = _int_or_float(value)
689         self._rawvalue = field
690 
691     def _parse_keyword(self):
692         keyword = self._image[:KEYWORD_LENGTH].strip()
693         keyword_upper = keyword.upper()
694 
695         if keyword_upper in self._special_keywords:
696             return keyword_upper
697         elif (keyword_upper == 'HIERARCH' and self._image[8] == ' ' and
698               HIERARCH_VALUE_INDICATOR in self._image):
699             # This is valid HIERARCH card as described by the HIERARCH keyword
700             # convention:
701             # http://fits.gsfc.nasa.gov/registry/hierarch_keyword.html
702             self._hierarch = True
703             self._value_indicator = HIERARCH_VALUE_INDICATOR
704             keyword = self._image.split(HIERARCH_VALUE_INDICATOR, 1)[0][9:]
705             return keyword.strip()
706         else:
707             val_ind_idx = self._image.find(VALUE_INDICATOR)
708             if 0 <= val_ind_idx <= KEYWORD_LENGTH:
709                 # The value indicator should appear in byte 8, but we are
710                 # flexible and allow this to be fixed
711                 if val_ind_idx < KEYWORD_LENGTH:
712                     keyword = keyword[:val_ind_idx]
713                     keyword_upper = keyword_upper[:val_ind_idx]
714 
715                 rest = self._image[val_ind_idx + VALUE_INDICATOR_LEN:]
716 
717                 # So far this looks like a standard FITS keyword; check whether
718                 # the value represents a RVKC; if so then we pass things off to
719                 # the RVKC parser
720                 if self._check_if_rvkc_image(keyword, rest):
721                     return self._keyword
722 
723                 return keyword_upper
724             else:
725                 warnings.warn(
726                     'The following header keyword is invalid or follows an '
727                     'unrecognized non-standard convention:\n{}'
728                     .format(self._image), AstropyUserWarning)
729                 self._invalid = True
730                 return keyword
731 
732     def _parse_value(self):
733         """Extract the keyword value from the card image."""
734 
735         # for commentary cards, no need to parse further
736         # Likewise for invalid cards
737         if self.keyword.upper() in self._commentary_keywords or self._invalid:
738             return self._image[KEYWORD_LENGTH:].rstrip()
739 
740         if self._check_if_rvkc(self._image):
741             return self._value
742 
743         if len(self._image) > self.length:
744             values = []
745             for card in self._itersubcards():
746                 value = card.value.rstrip().replace("''", "'")
747                 if value and value[-1] == '&':
748                     value = value[:-1]
749                 values.append(value)
750 
751             value = ''.join(values)
752 
753             self._valuestring = value
754             return value
755 
756         m = self._value_NFSC_RE.match(self._split()[1])
757 
758         if m is None:
759             raise VerifyError("Unparsable card ({}), fix it first with "
760                               ".verify('fix').".format(self.keyword))
761 
762         if m.group('bool') is not None:
763             value = m.group('bool') == 'T'
764         elif m.group('strg') is not None:
765             value = re.sub("''", "'", m.group('strg'))
766         elif m.group('numr') is not None:
767             #  Check for numbers with leading 0s.
768             numr = self._number_NFSC_RE.match(m.group('numr'))
769             digt = translate(numr.group('digt'), FIX_FP_TABLE2, ' ')
770             if numr.group('sign') is None:
771                 sign = ''
772             else:
773                 sign = numr.group('sign')
774             value = _str_to_num(sign + digt)
775 
776         elif m.group('cplx') is not None:
777             #  Check for numbers with leading 0s.
778             real = self._number_NFSC_RE.match(m.group('real'))
779             rdigt = translate(real.group('digt'), FIX_FP_TABLE2, ' ')
780             if real.group('sign') is None:
781                 rsign = ''
782             else:
783                 rsign = real.group('sign')
784             value = _str_to_num(rsign + rdigt)
785             imag = self._number_NFSC_RE.match(m.group('imag'))
786             idigt = translate(imag.group('digt'), FIX_FP_TABLE2, ' ')
787             if imag.group('sign') is None:
788                 isign = ''
789             else:
790                 isign = imag.group('sign')
791             value += _str_to_num(isign + idigt) * 1j
792         else:
793             value = UNDEFINED
794 
795         if not self._valuestring:
796             self._valuestring = m.group('valu')
797         return value
798 
799     def _parse_comment(self):
800         """Extract the keyword value from the card image."""
801 
802         # for commentary cards, no need to parse further
803         # likewise for invalid/unparseable cards
804         if self.keyword in Card._commentary_keywords or self._invalid:
805             return ''
806 
807         if len(self._image) > self.length:
808             comments = []
809             for card in self._itersubcards():
810                 if card.comment:
811                     comments.append(card.comment)
812             comment = '/ ' + ' '.join(comments).rstrip()
813             m = self._value_NFSC_RE.match(comment)
814         else:
815             m = self._value_NFSC_RE.match(self._split()[1])
816 
817         if m is not None:
818             comment = m.group('comm')
819             if comment:
820                 return comment.rstrip()
821         return ''
822 
823     def _split(self):
824         """
825         Split the card image between the keyword and the rest of the card.
826         """
827 
828         if self._image is not None:
829             # If we already have a card image, don't try to rebuild a new card
830             # image, which self.image would do
831             image = self._image
832         else:
833             image = self.image
834 
835         if self.keyword in self._special_keywords:
836             keyword, valuecomment = image.split(' ', 1)
837         else:
838             try:
839                 delim_index = image.index(self._value_indicator)
840             except ValueError:
841                 delim_index = None
842 
843             # The equal sign may not be any higher than column 10; anything
844             # past that must be considered part of the card value
845             if delim_index is None:
846                 keyword = image[:KEYWORD_LENGTH]
847                 valuecomment = image[KEYWORD_LENGTH:]
848             elif delim_index > 10 and image[:9] != 'HIERARCH ':
849                 keyword = image[:8]
850                 valuecomment = image[8:]
851             else:
852                 keyword, valuecomment = image.split(self._value_indicator, 1)
853         return keyword.strip(), valuecomment.strip()
854 
855     def _fix_keyword(self):
856         if self.field_specifier:
857             keyword, field_specifier = self._keyword.split('.', 1)
858             self._keyword = '.'.join([keyword.upper(), field_specifier])
859         else:
860             self._keyword = self._keyword.upper()
861         self._modified = True
862 
863     def _fix_value(self):
864         """Fix the card image for fixable non-standard compliance."""
865 
866         value = None
867         keyword, valuecomment = self._split()
868         m = self._value_NFSC_RE.match(valuecomment)
869 
870         # for the unparsable case
871         if m is None:
872             try:
873                 value, comment = valuecomment.split('/', 1)
874                 self.value = value.strip()
875                 self.comment = comment.strip()
876             except (ValueError, IndexError):
877                 self.value = valuecomment
878             self._valuestring = self._value
879             return
880         elif m.group('numr') is not None:
881             numr = self._number_NFSC_RE.match(m.group('numr'))
882             value = translate(numr.group('digt'), FIX_FP_TABLE, ' ')
883             if numr.group('sign') is not None:
884                 value = numr.group('sign') + value
885 
886         elif m.group('cplx') is not None:
887             real = self._number_NFSC_RE.match(m.group('real'))
888             rdigt = translate(real.group('digt'), FIX_FP_TABLE, ' ')
889             if real.group('sign') is not None:
890                 rdigt = real.group('sign') + rdigt
891 
892             imag = self._number_NFSC_RE.match(m.group('imag'))
893             idigt = translate(imag.group('digt'), FIX_FP_TABLE, ' ')
894             if imag.group('sign') is not None:
895                 idigt = imag.group('sign') + idigt
896             value = '({}, {})'.format(rdigt, idigt)
897         self._valuestring = value
898         # The value itself has not been modified, but its serialized
899         # representation (as stored in self._valuestring) has been changed, so
900         # still set this card as having been modified (see ticket #137)
901         self._modified = True
902 
903     def _format_keyword(self):
904         if self.keyword:
905             if self.field_specifier:
906                 return '{:{len}}'.format(self.keyword.split('.', 1)[0],
907                                          len=KEYWORD_LENGTH)
908             elif self._hierarch:
909                 return 'HIERARCH {} '.format(self.keyword)
910             else:
911                 return '{:{len}}'.format(self.keyword, len=KEYWORD_LENGTH)
912         else:
913             return ' ' * KEYWORD_LENGTH
914 
915     def _format_value(self):
916         # value string
917         float_types = (float, np.floating, complex, np.complexfloating)
918 
919         # Force the value to be parsed out first
920         value = self.value
921         # But work with the underlying raw value instead (to preserve
922         # whitespace, for now...)
923         value = self._value
924 
925         if self.keyword in self._commentary_keywords:
926             # The value of a commentary card must be just a raw unprocessed
927             # string
928             value = str(value)
929         elif (self._valuestring and not self._valuemodified and
930               isinstance(self.value, float_types)):
931             # Keep the existing formatting for float/complex numbers
932             value = '{:>20}'.format(self._valuestring)
933         elif self.field_specifier:
934             value = _format_value(self._value).strip()
935             value = "'{}: {}'".format(self.field_specifier, value)
936         else:
937             value = _format_value(value)
938 
939         # For HIERARCH cards the value should be shortened to conserve space
940         if not self.field_specifier and len(self.keyword) > KEYWORD_LENGTH:
941             value = value.strip()
942 
943         return value
944 
945     def _format_comment(self):
946         if not self.comment:
947             return ''
948         else:
949             return ' / {}'.format(self._comment)
950 
951     def _format_image(self):
952         keyword = self._format_keyword()

1000     def _format_long_image(self):
1001         """
1002         Break up long string value/comment into ``CONTINUE`` cards.
1003         This is a primitive implementation: it will put the value
1004         string in one block and the comment string in another.  Also,
1005         it does not break at the blank space between words.  So it may
1006         not look pretty.
1007         """

1009         if self.keyword in Card._commentary_keywords:
1010             return self._format_long_commentary_image()
1011 
1012         value_length = 67
1013         comment_length = 64
1014         output = []
1015 
1016         # do the value string
1017         value = self._value.replace("'", "''")
1018         words = _words_group(value, value_length)
1019         for idx, word in enumerate(words):
1020             if idx == 0:
1021                 headstr = '{:{len}}= '.format(self.keyword, len=KEYWORD_LENGTH)
1022             else:
1023                 headstr = 'CONTINUE  '
1024 
1025             # If this is the final CONTINUE remove the '&'
1026             if not self.comment and idx == len(words) - 1:
1027                 value_format = "'{}'"
1028             else:
1029                 value_format = "'{}&'"
1030 
1031             value = value_format.format(word)
1032 
1033             output.append('{:80}'.format(headstr + value))
1034 
1035         # do the comment string
1036         comment_format = "{}"
1037 
1038         if self.comment:
1039             words = _words_group(self.comment, comment_length)
1040             for idx, word in enumerate(words):
1041                 # If this is the final CONTINUE remove the '&'
1042                 if idx == len(words) - 1:
1043                     headstr = "CONTINUE  '' / "
1044                 else:
1045                     headstr = "CONTINUE  '&' / "
1046 
1047                 comment = headstr + comment_format.format(word)
1048                 output.append('{:80}'.format(comment))

1200 def _format_value(value):
1201     """
1202     Converts a card value to its appropriate string representation as
1203     defined by the FITS format.
1204     """
1205 
1206     # string value should occupies at least 8 columns, unless it is
1207     # a null string
1208     if isinstance(value, str):
1209         if value == '':
1210             return "''"
1211         else:
1212             exp_val_str = value.replace("'", "''")
1213             val_str = "'{:8}'".format(exp_val_str)

1215 
1216     # must be before int checking since bool is also int
1217     elif isinstance(value, (bool, np.bool_)):
1218         return '{:>20}'.format(repr(value)[0])  # T or F
1219 
1220     elif _is_int(value):
1221         return '{:>20d}'.format(value)
1222 
1223     elif isinstance(value, (float, np.floating)):
1224         return '{:>20}'.format(_format_float(value))
1225 
1226     elif isinstance(value, (complex, np.complexfloating)):
1227         val_str = '({}, {})'.format(_format_float(value.real),
1228                                     _format_float(value.imag))
1229         return '{:>20}'.format(val_str)

1231     elif isinstance(value, Undefined):
1232         return ''
1233     else:
1234         return ''

1237 def _format_float(value):
1238     """Format a floating number to make sure it gets the decimal point."""
1239 
1240     value_str = '{:.16G}'.format(value)
1241     if '.' not in value_str and 'E' not in value_str:
1242         value_str += '.0'
1243     elif 'E' in value_str:
1244         # On some Windows builds of Python (and possibly other platforms?) the
1245         # exponent is zero-padded out to, it seems, three digits.  Normalize
1246         # the format to pad only to two digits.
1247         significand, exponent = value_str.split('E')
1248         if exponent[0] in ('+', '-'):
1249             sign = exponent[0]
1250             exponent = exponent[1:]
1251         else:
1252             sign = ''
1253         value_str = '{}E{}{:02d}'.format(significand, sign, int(exponent))
1254 
1255     # Limit the value string to at most 20 characters.
1256     str_len = len(value_str)
1257 
1258     if str_len > 20:
1259         idx = value_str.find('E')
1260 
1261         if idx < 0:
1262             value_str = value_str[:20]
1263         else:
1264             value_str = value_str[:20 - (str_len - idx)] + value_str[idx:]
1265 
1266     return value_str

1269 def _pad(input):
1270     """Pad blank space to the input string to be multiple of 80."""
1271 
1272     _len = len(input)
1273     if _len == Card.length:
1274         return input
1275     elif _len > Card.length:
1276         strlen = _len % Card.length
1277         if strlen == 0:
1278             return input
1279         else:
1280             return input + ' ' * (Card.length - strlen)
1281 
1282     # minimum length is 80
1283     else:
1284         strlen = _len % Card.length
1285         return input + ' ' * (Card.length - strlen)

375 
376             if image:
377                 if next_image[:8] == 'CONTINUE':
378                     image.append(next_image)
379                     continue
380                 cards.append(Card.fromstring(''.join(image)))
381 
382             if require_full_cardlength:
383                 if next_image == END_CARD:
384                     image = []
385                     break
386             else:
387                 if next_image.split(sep)[0].rstrip() == 'END':
388                     image = []
389                     break
390 
391             image = [next_image]
392 
393         # Add the last image that was found before the end, if any
394         if image:
395             cards.append(Card.fromstring(''.join(image)))
396 
397         return cls._fromcards(cards)
398 
399     @classmethod
400     def fromfile(cls, fileobj, sep='', endcard=True, padding=True):
401         """
402         Similar to :meth:`Header.fromstring`, but reads the header string from
403         a given file-like object or filename.
404 
405         Parameters
406         ----------
407         fileobj : str, file-like
408             A filename or an open file-like object from which a FITS header is
409             to be read.  For open file handles the file pointer must be at the
410             beginning of the header.
411 
412         sep : str, optional
413             The string separating cards from each other, such as a newline.  By
414             default there is no card separator (as is the case in a raw FITS
415             file).
416 
417         endcard : bool, optional
418             If True (the default) the header must end with an END card in order
419             to be considered valid.  If an END card is not found an
420             `OSError` is raised.
421 
422         padding : bool, optional
423             If True (the default) the header will be required to be padded out
424             to a multiple of 2880, the FITS header block size.  Otherwise any
425             padding, or lack thereof, is ignored.
426 
427         Returns
428         -------
429         header
430             A new `Header` instance.
431         """
432 
433         close_file = False
434         if isinstance(fileobj, str):
435             # Open in text mode by default to support newline handling; if a
436             # binary-mode file object is passed in, the user is on their own
437             # with respect to newline handling
438             fileobj = open(fileobj, 'r')
439             close_file = True
440 
441         try:
442             is_binary = fileobj_is_binary(fileobj)
443 
444             def block_iter(nbytes):
445                 while True:
446                     data = fileobj.read(nbytes)
447 
448                     if data:
449                         yield data
450                     else:
451                         break
452 
453             return cls._from_blocks(block_iter, is_binary, sep, endcard,
454                                     padding)[1]
455         finally:
456             if close_file:
457                 fileobj.close()
458 
459     @classmethod
460     def _fromcards(cls, cards):
461         header = cls()
462         for idx, card in enumerate(cards):
463             header._cards.append(card)
464             keyword = Card.normalize_keyword(card.keyword)
465             header._keyword_indices[keyword].append(idx)
466             if card.field_specifier is not None:
467                 header._rvkc_indices[card.rawkeyword].append(idx)
468 
469         header._modified = False
470         return header
