472     @classmethod
473     def _from_blocks(cls, block_iter, is_binary, sep, endcard, padding):
474         """
475         The meat of `Header.fromfile`; in a separate method so that
476         `Header.fromfile` itself is just responsible for wrapping file
477         handling.  Also used by `_BaseHDU.fromstring`.
478 
479         ``block_iter`` should be a callable which, given a block size n
480         (typically 2880 bytes as used by the FITS standard) returns an iterator
481         of byte strings of that block size.
482 
483         ``is_binary`` specifies whether the returned blocks are bytes or text
484 
485         Returns both the entire header *string*, and the `Header` object
486         returned by Header.fromstring on that string.
487         """
488 
489         actual_block_size = _block_size(sep)
490         clen = Card.length + len(sep)
491 
492         blocks = block_iter(actual_block_size)
493 
494         # Read the first header block.
495         try:
496             block = next(blocks)
497         except StopIteration:
498             raise EOFError()
499 
500         if not is_binary:
501             # TODO: There needs to be error handling at *this* level for
502             # non-ASCII characters; maybe at this stage decoding latin-1 might
503             # be safer
504             block = encode_ascii(block)
505 
506         read_blocks = []
507         is_eof = False
508         end_found = False
509 
510         # continue reading header blocks until END card or EOF is reached
511         while True:
512             # find the END card
513             end_found, block = cls._find_end_card(block, clen)
514 
515             read_blocks.append(decode_ascii(block))
516 
517             if end_found:
518                 break
519 
520             try:
521                 block = next(blocks)
522             except StopIteration:
523                 is_eof = True
524                 break
525 
526             if not block:
527                 is_eof = True
528                 break
529 
530             if not is_binary:
531                 block = encode_ascii(block)
532 
533         if not end_found and is_eof and endcard:
534             # TODO: Pass this error to validation framework as an ERROR,
535             # rather than raising an exception
536             raise OSError('Header missing END card.')
537 
538         header_str = ''.join(read_blocks)
539         _check_padding(header_str, actual_block_size, is_eof,
540                        check_block_size=padding)
541 
542         return header_str, cls.fromstring(header_str, sep=sep)
543 
544     @classmethod
545     def _find_end_card(cls, block, card_len):
546         """
547         Utility method to search a header block for the END card and handle
548         invalid END cards.
549 
550         This method can also returned a modified copy of the input header block
551         in case an invalid end card needs to be sanitized.
552         """
553 
554         for mo in HEADER_END_RE.finditer(block):
555             # Ensure the END card was found, and it started on the
556             # boundary of a new card (see ticket #142)
557             if mo.start() % card_len != 0:
558                 continue
559 
560             # This must be the last header block, otherwise the
561             # file is malformatted
562             if mo.group('invalid'):
563                 offset = mo.start()
564                 trailing = block[offset + 3:offset + card_len - 3].rstrip()
565                 if trailing:
566                     trailing = repr(trailing).lstrip('ub')
567                     # TODO: Pass this warning up to the validation framework
568                     warnings.warn(
569                         'Unexpected bytes trailing END keyword: {0}; these '
570                         'bytes will be replaced with spaces on write.'.format(
571                             trailing), AstropyUserWarning)
572                 else:
573                     # TODO: Pass this warning up to the validation framework
574                     warnings.warn(
575                         'Missing padding to end of the FITS block after the '
576                         'END keyword; additional spaces will be appended to '
577                         'the file upon writing to pad out to {0} '
578                         'bytes.'.format(BLOCK_SIZE), AstropyUserWarning)
579 
580                 # Sanitize out invalid END card now that the appropriate
581                 # warnings have been issued
582                 block = (block[:offset] + encode_ascii(END_CARD) +
583                          block[offset + len(END_CARD):])
584 
585             return True, block
586 
587         return False, block
588 
589     def tostring(self, sep='', endcard=True, padding=True):
590         r"""
591         Returns a string representation of the header.
592 
593         By default this uses no separator between cards, adds the END card, and
594         pads the string with spaces to the next multiple of 2880 bytes.  That
595         is, it returns the header exactly as it would appear in a FITS file.
596 
597         Parameters
598         ----------
599         sep : str, optional
600             The character or string with which to separate cards.  By default
601             there is no separator, but one could use ``'\\n'``, for example, to
602             separate each card with a new line
603 
604         endcard : bool, optional
605             If True (default) adds the END card to the end of the header
606             string
607 
608         padding : bool, optional
609             If True (default) pads the string with spaces out to the next
610             multiple of 2880 characters
611 
612         Returns
613         -------
614         s : str
615             A string representing a FITS header.
616         """
617 
618         lines = []
619         for card in self._cards:
620             s = str(card)
621             # Cards with CONTINUE cards may be longer than 80 chars; so break
622             # them into multiple lines
623             while s:
624                 lines.append(s[:Card.length])
625                 s = s[Card.length:]
626 
627         s = sep.join(lines)
628         if endcard:
629             s += sep + _pad('END')
630         if padding:
631             s += ' ' * _pad_length(len(s))
632         return s
633

835     def set(self, keyword, value=None, comment=None, before=None, after=None):
836         """
837         Set the value and/or comment and/or position of a specified keyword.
838 
839         If the keyword does not already exist in the header, a new keyword is
840         created in the specified position, or appended to the end of the header
841         if no position is specified.
842 
843         This method is similar to :meth:`Header.update` prior to Astropy v0.1.
844 
845         .. note::
846             It should be noted that ``header.set(keyword, value)`` and
847             ``header.set(keyword, value, comment)`` are equivalent to
848             ``header[keyword] = value`` and
849             ``header[keyword] = (value, comment)`` respectively.
850 
851             New keywords can also be inserted relative to existing keywords
852             using, for example::
853 
854                 >>> header.insert('NAXIS1', ('NAXIS', 2, 'Number of axes'))
855 
856             to insert before an existing keyword, or::
857 
858                 >>> header.insert('NAXIS', ('NAXIS1', 4096), after=True)
859 
860             to insert after an existing keyword.
861 
862             The only advantage of using :meth:`Header.set` is that it
863             easily replaces the old usage of :meth:`Header.update` both
864             conceptually and in terms of function signature.
865 
866         Parameters
867         ----------
868         keyword : str
869             A header keyword
870 
871         value : str, optional
872             The value to set for the given keyword; if None the existing value
873             is kept, but '' may be used to set a blank value
874 
875         comment : str, optional
876             The comment to set for the given keyword; if None the existing
877             comment is kept, but ``''`` may be used to set a blank comment
878 
879         before : str, int, optional
880             Name of the keyword, or index of the `Card` before which this card
881             should be located in the header.  The argument ``before`` takes
882             precedence over ``after`` if both specified.
883 
884         after : str, int, optional
885             Name of the keyword, or index of the `Card` after which this card
886             should be located in the header.
887 
888         """
889 
890         # Create a temporary card that looks like the one being set; if the
891         # temporary card turns out to be a RVKC this will make it easier to
892         # deal with the idiosyncrasies thereof
893         # Don't try to make a temporary card though if they keyword looks like
894         # it might be a HIERARCH card or is otherwise invalid--this step is
895         # only for validating RVKCs.
896         if (len(keyword) <= KEYWORD_LENGTH and
897             Card._keywd_FSC_RE.match(keyword) and
898                 keyword not in self._keyword_indices):
899             new_card = Card(keyword, value, comment)
900             new_keyword = new_card.keyword
901         else:
902             new_keyword = keyword
903 
904         if (new_keyword not in Card._commentary_keywords and
905                 new_keyword in self):
906             if comment is None:
907                 comment = self.comments[keyword]
908             if value is None:
909                 value = self[keyword]
910 
911             self[keyword] = (value, comment)
912 
913             if before is not None or after is not None:
914                 card = self._cards[self._cardindex(keyword)]
915                 self._relativeinsert(card, before=before, after=after,
916                                      replace=True)
917         elif before is not None or after is not None:
918             self._relativeinsert((keyword, value, comment), before=before,
919                                  after=after)
920         else:
921             self[keyword] = (value, comment)
922

966         del self[key]

988     def update(self, *args, **kwargs):
989         """
990         Update the Header with new keyword values, updating the values of
991         existing keywords and appending new keywords otherwise; similar to
992         `dict.update`.
993 
994         `update` accepts either a dict-like object or an iterable.  In the
995         former case the keys must be header keywords and the values may be
996         either scalar values or (value, comment) tuples.  In the case of an
997         iterable the items must be (keyword, value) tuples or (keyword, value,
998         comment) tuples.
999 
1000         Arbitrary arguments are also accepted, in which case the update() is
1001         called again with the kwargs dict as its only argument.  That is,
1002 
1003         ::
1004 
1005             >>> header.update(NAXIS1=100, NAXIS2=100)
1006 
1007         is equivalent to::
1008 
1009             header.update({'NAXIS1': 100, 'NAXIS2': 100})
1010 
1011         .. warning::
1012             As this method works similarly to `dict.update` it is very
1013             different from the ``Header.update()`` method in Astropy v0.1.
1014             Use of the old API was
1015             **deprecated** for a long time and is now removed. Most uses of the
1016             old API can be replaced as follows:
1017 
1018             * Replace ::
1019 
1020                   header.update(keyword, value)
1021 
1022               with ::
1023 
1024                   header[keyword] = value
1025 
1026             * Replace ::
1027 
1028                   header.update(keyword, value, comment=comment)
1029 
1030               with ::
1031 
1032                   header[keyword] = (value, comment)
1033 
1034             * Replace ::
1035 
1036                   header.update(keyword, value, before=before_keyword)
1037 
1038               with ::
1039 
1040                   header.insert(before_keyword, (keyword, value))
1041 
1042             * Replace ::
1043 
1044                   header.update(keyword, value, after=after_keyword)
1045 
1046               with ::
1047 
1048                   header.insert(after_keyword, (keyword, value),
1049                                 after=True)
1050 
1051             See also :meth:`Header.set` which is a new method that provides an
1052             interface similar to the old ``Header.update()`` and may help make
1053             transition a little easier.
1054 
1055         """
1056 
1057         if args:
1058             other = args[0]
1059         else:
1060             other = None
1061 
1062         def update_from_dict(k, v):
1063             if not isinstance(v, tuple):
1064                 card = Card(k, v)
1065             elif 0 < len(v) <= 2:
1066                 card = Card(*((k,) + v))
1067             else:
1068                 raise ValueError(
1069                     'Header update value for key %r is invalid; the '
1070                     'value must be either a scalar, a 1-tuple '
1071                     'containing the scalar value, or a 2-tuple '
1072                     'containing the value and a comment string.' % k)
1073             self._update(card)
1074 
1075         if other is None:
1076             pass
1077         elif hasattr(other, 'items'):
1078             for k, v in other.items():
1079                 update_from_dict(k, v)
1080         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
1081             for k in other.keys():
1082                 update_from_dict(k, other[k])
1083         else:
1084             for idx, card in enumerate(other):
1085                 if isinstance(card, Card):
1086                     self._update(card)
1087                 elif isinstance(card, tuple) and (1 < len(card) <= 3):
1088                     self._update(Card(*card))
1089                 else:
1090                     raise ValueError(
1091                         'Header update sequence item #{} is invalid; '
1092                         'the item must either be a 2-tuple containing '
1093                         'a keyword and value, or a 3-tuple containing '
1094                         'a keyword, value, and comment string.'.format(idx))
1095         if kwargs:
1096             self.update(kwargs)
1097 
1098     def append(self, card=None, useblanks=True, bottom=False, end=False):
1099         """
1100         Appends a new keyword+value card to the end of the Header, similar
1101         to `list.append`.
1102 
1103         By default if the last cards in the Header have commentary keywords,
1104         this will append the new keyword before the commentary (unless the new
1105         keyword is also commentary).
1106 
1107         Also differs from `list.append` in that it can be called with no
1108         arguments: In this case a blank card is appended to the end of the
1109         Header.  In the case all the keyword arguments are ignored.
1110 
1111         Parameters
1112         ----------
1113         card : str, tuple
1114             A keyword or a (keyword, value, [comment]) tuple representing a
1115             single header card; the comment is optional in which case a
1116             2-tuple may be used
1117 
1118         useblanks : bool, optional
1119             If there are blank cards at the end of the Header, replace the
1120             first blank card so that the total number of cards in the Header
1121             does not increase.  Otherwise preserve the number of blank cards.
1122 
1123         bottom : bool, optional
1124             If True, instead of appending after the last non-commentary card,
1125             append after the last non-blank card.
1126 
1127         end : bool, optional
1128             If True, ignore the useblanks and bottom options, and append at the
1129             very end of the Header.
1130 
1131         """
1132 
1133         if isinstance(card, str):
1134             card = Card(card)
1135         elif isinstance(card, tuple):
1136             card = Card(*card)
1137         elif card is None:
1138             card = Card()
1139         elif not isinstance(card, Card):
1140             raise ValueError(
1141                 'The value appended to a Header must be either a keyword or '
1142                 '(keyword, value, [comment]) tuple; got: {!r}'.format(card))
1143 
1144         if not end and card.is_blank:
1145             # Blank cards should always just be appended to the end
1146             end = True
1147 
1148         if end:
1149             self._cards.append(card)
1150             idx = len(self._cards) - 1
1151         else:
1152             idx = len(self._cards) - 1
1153             while idx >= 0 and self._cards[idx].is_blank:
1154                 idx -= 1
1155 
1156             if not bottom and card.keyword not in Card._commentary_keywords:
1157                 while (idx >= 0 and
1158                        self._cards[idx].keyword in Card._commentary_keywords):
1159                     idx -= 1
1160 
1161             idx += 1
1162             self._cards.insert(idx, card)
1163             self._updateindices(idx)
1164 
1165         keyword = Card.normalize_keyword(card.keyword)
1166         self._keyword_indices[keyword].append(idx)
1167         if card.field_specifier is not None:
1168             self._rvkc_indices[card.rawkeyword].append(idx)
1169 
1170         if not end:
1171             # If the appended card was a commentary card, and it was appended
1172             # before existing cards with the same keyword, the indices for
1173             # cards with that keyword may have changed
1174             if not bottom and card.keyword in Card._commentary_keywords:
1175                 self._keyword_indices[keyword].sort()
1176 
1177             # Finally, if useblanks, delete a blank cards from the end
1178             if useblanks and self._countblanks():
1179                 # Don't do this unless there is at least one blanks at the end
1180                 # of the header; we need to convert the card to its string
1181                 # image to see how long it is.  In the vast majority of cases
1182                 # this will just be 80 (Card.length) but it may be longer for
1183                 # CONTINUE cards
1184                 self._useblanks(len(str(card)) // Card.length)
1185 
1186         self._modified = True
1187 
1188     def extend(self, cards, strip=True, unique=False, update=False,
1189                update_first=False, useblanks=True, bottom=False, end=False):
1190         """
1191         Appends multiple keyword+value cards to the end of the header, similar
1192         to `list.extend`.
1193 
1194         Parameters
1195         ----------
1196         cards : iterable
1197             An iterable of (keyword, value, [comment]) tuples; see
1198             `Header.append`.
1199 
1200         strip : bool, optional
1201             Remove any keywords that have meaning only to specific types of
1202             HDUs, so that only more general keywords are added from extension
1203             Header or Card list (default: `True`).
1204 
1205         unique : bool, optional
1206             If `True`, ensures that no duplicate keywords are appended;
1207             keywords already in this header are simply discarded.  The
1208             exception is commentary keywords (COMMENT, HISTORY, etc.): they are
1209             only treated as duplicates if their values match.
1210 
1211         update : bool, optional
1212             If `True`, update the current header with the values and comments
1213             from duplicate keywords in the input header.  This supersedes the
1214             ``unique`` argument.  Commentary keywords are treated the same as
1215             if ``unique=True``.
1216 
1217         update_first : bool, optional
1218             If the first keyword in the header is 'SIMPLE', and the first
1219             keyword in the input header is 'XTENSION', the 'SIMPLE' keyword is
1220             replaced by the 'XTENSION' keyword.  Likewise if the first keyword
1221             in the header is 'XTENSION' and the first keyword in the input
1222             header is 'SIMPLE', the 'XTENSION' keyword is replaced by the
1223             'SIMPLE' keyword.  This behavior is otherwise dumb as to whether or
1224             not the resulting header is a valid primary or extension header.
1225             This is mostly provided to support backwards compatibility with the
1226             old ``Header.fromTxtFile`` method, and only applies if
1227             ``update=True``.
1228 
1229         useblanks, bottom, end : bool, optional
1230             These arguments are passed to :meth:`Header.append` while appending
1231             new cards to the header.
1232         """
1233 
1234         temp = Header(cards)
1235         if strip:
1236             temp._strip()
1237 
1238         if len(self):
1239             first = self._cards[0].keyword
1240         else:
1241             first = None
1242 
1243         # We don't immediately modify the header, because first we need to sift
1244         # out any duplicates in the new header prior to adding them to the
1245         # existing header, but while *allowing* duplicates from the header
1246         # being extended from (see ticket #156)
1247         extend_cards = []
1248 
1249         for idx, card in enumerate(temp.cards):
1250             keyword = card.keyword
1251             if keyword not in Card._commentary_keywords:
1252                 if unique and not update and keyword in self:
1253                     continue
1254                 elif update:
1255                     if idx == 0 and update_first:
1256                         # Dumbly update the first keyword to either SIMPLE or
1257                         # XTENSION as the case may be, as was in the case in
1258                         # Header.fromTxtFile
1259                         if ((keyword == 'SIMPLE' and first == 'XTENSION') or
1260                                 (keyword == 'XTENSION' and first == 'SIMPLE')):
1261                             del self[0]
1262                             self.insert(0, card)
1263                         else:
1264                             self[keyword] = (card.value, card.comment)
1265                     elif keyword in self:
1266                         self[keyword] = (card.value, card.comment)
1267                     else:
1268                         extend_cards.append(card)
1269                 else:
1270                     extend_cards.append(card)
1271             else:
1272                 if (unique or update) and keyword in self:
1273                     if card.is_blank:
1274                         extend_cards.append(card)
1275                         continue
1276 
1277                     for value in self[keyword]:
1278                         if value == card.value:
1279                             break
1280                     else:
1281                         extend_cards.append(card)
1282                 else:
1283                     extend_cards.append(card)
1284 
1285         for card in extend_cards:
1286             self.append(card, useblanks=useblanks, bottom=bottom, end=end)
1287 
1288     def count(self, keyword):
1289         """
1290         Returns the count of the given keyword in the header, similar to
1291         `list.count` if the Header object is treated as a list of keywords.
1292 
1293         Parameters
1294         ----------
1295         keyword : str
1296             The keyword to count instances of in the header
1297 
1298         """
1299 
1300         keyword = Card.normalize_keyword(keyword)
1301 
1302         # We have to look before we leap, since otherwise _keyword_indices,
1303         # being a defaultdict, will create an entry for the nonexistent keyword
1304         if keyword not in self._keyword_indices:
1305             raise KeyError("Keyword {!r} not found.".format(keyword))
1306 
1307         return len(self._keyword_indices[keyword])

1309     def index(self, keyword, start=None, stop=None):
1310         """
1311         Returns the index if the first instance of the given keyword in the
1312         header, similar to `list.index` if the Header object is treated as a
1313         list of keywords.
1314 
1315         Parameters
1316         ----------
1317         keyword : str
1318             The keyword to look up in the list of all keywords in the header
1319 
1320         start : int, optional
1321             The lower bound for the index
1322 
1323         stop : int, optional
1324             The upper bound for the index
1325 
1326         """
1327 
1328         if start is None:
1329             start = 0
1330 
1331         if stop is None:
1332             stop = len(self._cards)
1333 
1334         if stop < start:
1335             step = -1
1336         else:
1337             step = 1
1338 
1339         norm_keyword = Card.normalize_keyword(keyword)
1340 
1341         for idx in range(start, stop, step):
1342             if self._cards[idx].keyword.upper() == norm_keyword:
1343                 return idx
1344         else:
1345             raise ValueError('The keyword {!r} is not in the '
1346                              ' header.'.format(keyword))

1348     def insert(self, key, card, useblanks=True, after=False):
1349         """
1350         Inserts a new keyword+value card into the Header at a given location,
1351         similar to `list.insert`.
1352 
1353         Parameters
1354         ----------
1355         key : int, str, or tuple
1356             The index into the list of header keywords before which the
1357             new keyword should be inserted, or the name of a keyword before
1358             which the new keyword should be inserted.  Can also accept a
1359             (keyword, index) tuple for inserting around duplicate keywords.
1360 
1361         card : str, tuple
1362             A keyword or a (keyword, value, [comment]) tuple; see
1363             `Header.append`
1364 
1365         useblanks : bool, optional
1366             If there are blank cards at the end of the Header, replace the
1367             first blank card so that the total number of cards in the Header
1368             does not increase.  Otherwise preserve the number of blank cards.
1369 
1370         after : bool, optional
1371             If set to `True`, insert *after* the specified index or keyword,
1372             rather than before it.  Defaults to `False`.
1373         """
1374 
1375         if not isinstance(key, int):
1376             # Don't pass through ints to _cardindex because it will not take
1377             # kindly to indices outside the existing number of cards in the
1378             # header, which insert needs to be able to support (for example
1379             # when inserting into empty headers)
1380             idx = self._cardindex(key)
1381         else:
1382             idx = key
1383 
1384         if after:
1385             if idx == -1:
1386                 idx = len(self._cards)
1387             else:
1388                 idx += 1
1389 
1390         if idx >= len(self._cards):
1391             # This is just an append (Though it must be an append absolutely to
1392             # the bottom, ignoring blanks, etc.--the point of the insert method
1393             # is that you get exactly what you asked for with no surprises)
1394             self.append(card, end=True)
1395             return
1396 
1397         if isinstance(card, str):
1398             card = Card(card)
1399         elif isinstance(card, tuple):
1400             card = Card(*card)
1401         elif not isinstance(card, Card):
1402             raise ValueError(
1403                 'The value inserted into a Header must be either a keyword or '
1404                 '(keyword, value, [comment]) tuple; got: {!r}'.format(card))
1405 
1406         self._cards.insert(idx, card)
1407 
1408         keyword = card.keyword
1409 
1410         # If idx was < 0, determine the actual index according to the rules
1411         # used by list.insert()
1412         if idx < 0:
1413             idx += len(self._cards) - 1
1414             if idx < 0:
1415                 idx = 0
1416 
1417         # All the keyword indices above the insertion point must be updated
1418         self._updateindices(idx)
1419 
1420         keyword = Card.normalize_keyword(keyword)
1421         self._keyword_indices[keyword].append(idx)
1422         count = len(self._keyword_indices[keyword])
1423         if count > 1:
1424             # There were already keywords with this same name
1425             if keyword not in Card._commentary_keywords:
1426                 warnings.warn(
1427                     'A {!r} keyword already exists in this header.  Inserting '
1428                     'duplicate keyword.'.format(keyword), AstropyUserWarning)
1429             self._keyword_indices[keyword].sort()
1430 
1431         if card.field_specifier is not None:
1432             # Update the index of RVKC as well
1433             rvkc_indices = self._rvkc_indices[card.rawkeyword]
1434             rvkc_indices.append(idx)
1435             rvkc_indices.sort()
1436 
1437         if useblanks:
1438             self._useblanks(len(str(card)) // Card.length)
1439 
1440         self._modified = True
1441 
1442     def remove(self, keyword, ignore_missing=False, remove_all=False):
1443         """
1444         Removes the first instance of the given keyword from the header similar
1445         to `list.remove` if the Header object is treated as a list of keywords.
1446 
1447         Parameters
1448         ----------
1449         keyword : str
1450             The keyword of which to remove the first instance in the header.
1451 
1452         ignore_missing : bool, optional
1453             When True, ignores missing keywords.  Otherwise, if the keyword
1454             is not present in the header a KeyError is raised.
1455 
1456         remove_all : bool, optional
1457             When True, all instances of keyword will be removed.
1458             Otherwise only the first instance of the given keyword is removed.
1459 
1460         """
1461         keyword = Card.normalize_keyword(keyword)
1462         if keyword in self._keyword_indices:
1463             del self[self._keyword_indices[keyword][0]]
1464             if remove_all:
1465                 while keyword in self._keyword_indices:
1466                     del self[self._keyword_indices[keyword][0]]
1467         elif not ignore_missing:
1468             raise KeyError("Keyword '{}' not found.".format(keyword))

1470     def rename_keyword(self, oldkeyword, newkeyword, force=False):
1471         """
1472         Rename a card's keyword in the header.
1473 
1474         Parameters
1475         ----------
1476         oldkeyword : str or int
1477             Old keyword or card index
1478 
1479         newkeyword : str
1480             New keyword
1481 
1482         force : bool, optional
1483             When `True`, if the new keyword already exists in the header, force
1484             the creation of a duplicate keyword. Otherwise a
1485             `ValueError` is raised.
1486         """
1487 
1488         oldkeyword = Card.normalize_keyword(oldkeyword)
1489         newkeyword = Card.normalize_keyword(newkeyword)
1490 
1491         if newkeyword == 'CONTINUE':
1492             raise ValueError('Can not rename to CONTINUE')
1493 
1494         if (newkeyword in Card._commentary_keywords or
1495                 oldkeyword in Card._commentary_keywords):
1496             if not (newkeyword in Card._commentary_keywords and
1497                     oldkeyword in Card._commentary_keywords):
1498                 raise ValueError('Regular and commentary keys can not be '
1499                                  'renamed to each other.')
1500         elif not force and newkeyword in self:
1501             raise ValueError('Intended keyword {} already exists in header.'
1502                              .format(newkeyword))
1503 
1504         idx = self.index(oldkeyword)
1505         card = self._cards[idx]
1506         del self[idx]
1507         self.insert(idx, (newkeyword, card.value, card.comment))

1563     def _update(self, card):
1564         """
1565         The real update code.  If keyword already exists, its value and/or
1566         comment will be updated.  Otherwise a new card will be appended.
1567 
1568         This will not create a duplicate keyword except in the case of
1569         commentary cards.  The only other way to force creation of a duplicate
1570         is to use the insert(), append(), or extend() methods.
1571         """
1572 
1573         keyword, value, comment = card
1574 
1575         # Lookups for existing/known keywords are case-insensitive
1576         keyword = keyword.upper()
1577         if keyword.startswith('HIERARCH '):
1578             keyword = keyword[9:]
1579 
1580         if (keyword not in Card._commentary_keywords and
1581                 keyword in self._keyword_indices):
1582             # Easy; just update the value/comment
1583             idx = self._keyword_indices[keyword][0]
1584             existing_card = self._cards[idx]
1585             existing_card.value = value
1586             if comment is not None:
1587                 # '' should be used to explicitly blank a comment
1588                 existing_card.comment = comment
1589             if existing_card._modified:
1590                 self._modified = True
1591         elif keyword in Card._commentary_keywords:
1592             cards = self._splitcommentary(keyword, value)
1593             if keyword in self._keyword_indices:
1594                 # Append after the last keyword of the same type
1595                 idx = self.index(keyword, start=len(self) - 1, stop=-1)
1596                 isblank = not (keyword or value or comment)
1597                 for c in reversed(cards):
1598                     self.insert(idx + 1, c, useblanks=(not isblank))
1599             else:
1600                 for c in cards:
1601                     self.append(c, bottom=True)
1602         else:
1603             # A new keyword! self.append() will handle updating _modified
1604             self.append(card)
1605 
1606     def _cardindex(self, key):
1607         """Returns an index into the ._cards list given a valid lookup key."""
1608 
1609         # This used to just set key = (key, 0) and then go on to act as if the
1610         # user passed in a tuple, but it's much more common to just be given a
1611         # string as the key, so optimize more for that case
1612         if isinstance(key, str):
1613             keyword = key
1614             n = 0
1615         elif isinstance(key, int):
1616             # If < 0, determine the actual index
1617             if key < 0:
1618                 key += len(self._cards)
1619             if key < 0 or key >= len(self._cards):
1620                 raise IndexError('Header index out of range.')
1621             return key
1622         elif isinstance(key, slice):
1623             return key
1624         elif isinstance(key, tuple):
1625             if (len(key) != 2 or not isinstance(key[0], str) or
1626                     not isinstance(key[1], int)):
1627                 raise ValueError(
1628                     'Tuple indices must be 2-tuples consisting of a '
1629                     'keyword string and an integer index.')
1630             keyword, n = key
1631         else:
1632             raise ValueError(
1633                 'Header indices must be either a string, a 2-tuple, or '
1634                 'an integer.')
1635 
1636         keyword = Card.normalize_keyword(keyword)
1637         # Returns the index into _cards for the n-th card with the given
1638         # keyword (where n is 0-based)
1639         indices = self._keyword_indices.get(keyword, None)
1640 
1641         if keyword and not indices:
1642             if len(keyword) > KEYWORD_LENGTH or '.' in keyword:
1643                 raise KeyError("Keyword {!r} not found.".format(keyword))
1644             else:
1645                 # Maybe it's a RVKC?
1646                 indices = self._rvkc_indices.get(keyword, None)
1647 
1648         if not indices:
1649             raise KeyError("Keyword {!r} not found.".format(keyword))
1650 
1651         try:
1652             return indices[n]
1653         except IndexError:
1654             raise IndexError('There are only {} {!r} cards in the '
1655                              'header.'.format(len(indices), keyword))
1656 
1657     def _keyword_from_index(self, idx):
1658         """
1659         Given an integer index, return the (keyword, repeat) tuple that index
1660         refers to.  For most keywords the repeat will always be zero, but it
1661         may be greater than zero for keywords that are duplicated (especially
1662         commentary keywords).
1663 
1664         In a sense this is the inverse of self.index, except that it also
1665         supports duplicates.
1666         """
1667 
1668         if idx < 0:
1669             idx += len(self._cards)
1670 
1671         keyword = self._cards[idx].keyword
1672         keyword = Card.normalize_keyword(keyword)
1673         repeat = self._keyword_indices[keyword].index(idx)
1674         return keyword, repeat
1675 
1676     def _relativeinsert(self, card, before=None, after=None, replace=False):
1677         """
1678         Inserts a new card before or after an existing card; used to
1679         implement support for the legacy before/after keyword arguments to
1680         Header.update().
1681 
1682         If replace=True, move an existing card with the same keyword.
1683         """
1684 
1685         if before is None:
1686             insertionkey = after
1687         else:
1688             insertionkey = before
1689 
1690         def get_insertion_idx():
1691             if not (isinstance(insertionkey, int) and
1692                     insertionkey >= len(self._cards)):
1693                 idx = self._cardindex(insertionkey)
1694             else:
1695                 idx = insertionkey
1696 
1697             if before is None:
1698                 idx += 1
1699 
1700             return idx
1701 
1702         if replace:
1703             # The card presumably already exists somewhere in the header.
1704             # Check whether or not we actually have to move it; if it does need
1705             # to be moved we just delete it and then it will be reinserted
1706             # below
1707             old_idx = self._cardindex(card.keyword)
1708             insertion_idx = get_insertion_idx()
1709 
1710             if (insertion_idx >= len(self._cards) and
1711                     old_idx == len(self._cards) - 1):
1712                 # The card would be appended to the end, but it's already at
1713                 # the end
1714                 return
1715 
1716             if before is not None:
1717                 if old_idx == insertion_idx - 1:
1718                     return
1719             elif after is not None and old_idx == insertion_idx:
1720                 return
1721 
1722             del self[old_idx]
1723 
1724         # Even if replace=True, the insertion idx may have changed since the
1725         # old card was deleted
1726         idx = get_insertion_idx()
1727 
1728         if card[0] in Card._commentary_keywords:
1729             cards = reversed(self._splitcommentary(card[0], card[1]))
1730         else:
1731             cards = [card]
1732         for c in cards:
1733             self.insert(idx, c)
1734 
1735     def _updateindices(self, idx, increment=True):
1736         """
1737         For all cards with index above idx, increment or decrement its index
1738         value in the keyword_indices dict.
1739         """
1740         if idx > len(self._cards):
1741             # Save us some effort
1742             return
1743 
1744         increment = 1 if increment else -1
1745 
1746         for index_sets in (self._keyword_indices, self._rvkc_indices):
1747             for indices in index_sets.values():
1748                 for jdx, keyword_index in enumerate(indices):
1749                     if keyword_index >= idx:
1750                         indices[jdx] += increment
1751 
1752     def _countblanks(self):
1753         """Returns the number of blank cards at the end of the Header."""
1754 
1755         for idx in range(1, len(self._cards)):
1756             if not self._cards[-idx].is_blank:
1757                 return idx - 1
1758         return 0
1759 
1760     def _useblanks(self, count):
1761         for _ in range(count):
1762             if self._cards[-1].is_blank:
1763                 del self[-1]
1764             else:
1765                 break
1766 
1767     def _haswildcard(self, keyword):
1768         """Return `True` if the input keyword contains a wildcard pattern."""
1769 
1770         return (isinstance(keyword, str) and
1771                 (keyword.endswith('...') or '*' in keyword or '?' in keyword))
1772 
1773     def _wildcardmatch(self, pattern):
1774         """
1775         Returns a list of indices of the cards matching the given wildcard
1776         pattern.
1777 
1778          * '*' matches 0 or more characters
1779          * '?' matches a single character
1780          * '...' matches 0 or more of any non-whitespace character
1781         """
1782 
1783         pattern = pattern.replace('*', r'.*').replace('?', r'.')
1784         pattern = pattern.replace('...', r'\S*') + '$'
1785         pattern_re = re.compile(pattern, re.I)
1786 
1787         return [idx for idx, card in enumerate(self._cards)
1788                 if pattern_re.match(card.keyword)]
1789 
1790     def _set_slice(self, key, value, target):
1791         """
1792         Used to implement Header.__setitem__ and CardAccessor.__setitem__.
1793         """
1794 
1795         if isinstance(key, slice) or self._haswildcard(key):
1796             if isinstance(key, slice):
1797                 indices = range(*key.indices(len(target)))
1798             else:
1799                 indices = self._wildcardmatch(key)
1800 
1801             if isinstance(value, str) or not isiterable(value):
1802                 value = itertools.repeat(value, len(indices))
1803 
1804             for idx, val in zip(indices, value):
1805                 target[idx] = val
1806 
1807             return True
1808 
1809         return False
1810 
1811     def _splitcommentary(self, keyword, value):
1812         """
1813         Given a commentary keyword and value, returns a list of the one or more
1814         cards needed to represent the full value.  This is primarily used to
1815         create the multiple commentary cards needed to represent a long value
1816         that won't fit into a single commentary card.
1817         """
1818 
1819         # The maximum value in each card can be the maximum card length minus
1820         # the maximum key length (which can include spaces if they key length
1821         # less than 8
1822         maxlen = Card.length - KEYWORD_LENGTH

77     is not exported by the `~astropy.units` module.  Instead of
78     instantiating a `QuantityIterator` directly, use `Quantity.flat`.
79     """
80 
81     def __init__(self, q):
82         self._quantity = q
83         self._dataiter = q.view(np.ndarray).flat
84 
85     def __iter__(self):
86         return self
87 
88     def __getitem__(self, indx):
89         out = self._dataiter.__getitem__(indx)
90         # For single elements, ndarray.flat.__getitem__ returns scalars; these
91         # need a new view as a Quantity.
92         if isinstance(out, type(self._quantity)):
93             return out
94         else:
95             return self._quantity._new_view(out)
96 
97     def __setitem__(self, index, value):
98         self._dataiter[index] = self._quantity._to_own_unit(value)
99 
100     def __next__(self):
101         """
102         Return the next value, or raise StopIteration.
103         """
104         out = next(self._dataiter)
105         # ndarray.flat._dataiter returns scalars, so need a view as a Quantity.
106         return self._quantity._new_view(out)
107 
108     next = __next__
109

111 class QuantityInfoBase(ParentDtypeInfo):
112     # This is on a base class rather than QuantityInfo directly, so that
113     # it can be used for EarthLocationInfo yet make clear that that class
114     # should not be considered a typical Quantity subclass by Table.
115     attrs_from_parent = {'dtype', 'unit'}  # dtype and unit taken from parent
116     _supports_indexing = True

118     @staticmethod
119     def default_format(val):
120         return '{0.value:}'.format(val)
121 
122     @staticmethod
123     def possible_string_format_functions(format_):
124         """Iterate through possible string-derived format functions.
125 
126         A string can either be a format specifier for the format built-in,
127         a new-style format string, or an old-style format string.
128 
129         This method is overridden in order to suppress printing the unit
130         in each row since it is already at the top in the column header.
131         """
132         yield lambda format_, val: format(val.value, format_)
133         yield lambda format_, val: format_.format(val.value)
134         yield lambda format_, val: format_ % val.value

137 class QuantityInfo(QuantityInfoBase):
138     """
139     Container for meta information like name, description, format.  This is
140     required when the object is used as a mixin column within a table, but can
141     be used as a general way to store meta information.
142     """
143     _represent_as_dict_attrs = ('value', 'unit')
144     _construct_from_dict_args = ['value']
145     _represent_as_dict_primary_data = 'value'
146 
147     def new_like(self, cols, length, metadata_conflicts='warn', name=None):
148         """
149         Return a new Quantity instance which is consistent with the
150         input ``cols`` and has ``length`` rows.
151 
152         This is intended for creating an empty column object whose elements can
153         be set in-place for table operations like join or vstack.
154 
155         Parameters
156         ----------
157         cols : list
158             List of input columns
159         length : int
160             Length of the output column object
161         metadata_conflicts : str ('warn'|'error'|'silent')
162             How to handle metadata conflicts
163         name : str
164             Output column name
165 
166         Returns
167         -------
168         col : Quantity (or subclass)
169             Empty instance of this class consistent with ``cols``
170 
171         """
172 
173         # Get merged info attributes like shape, dtype, format, description, etc.
174         attrs = self.merge_cols_attributes(cols, metadata_conflicts, name,
175                                            ('meta', 'format', 'description'))
176 
177         # Make an empty quantity using the unit of the last one.
178         shape = (length,) + attrs.pop('shape')
179         dtype = attrs.pop('dtype')
180         # Use zeros so we do not get problems for Quantity subclasses such
181         # as Longitude and Latitude, which cannot take arbitrary values.
182         data = np.zeros(shape=shape, dtype=dtype)
183         # Get arguments needed to reconstruct class
184         map = {key: (data if key == 'value' else getattr(cols[-1], key))
185                for key in self._represent_as_dict_attrs}
186         map['copy'] = False
187         out = self._construct_from_dict(map)
188 
189         # Set remaining info attributes
190         for attr, value in attrs.items():
191             setattr(out.info, attr, value)
192 
193         return out
194

196 class Quantity(np.ndarray, metaclass=InheritDocstrings):
197     """A `~astropy.units.Quantity` represents a number with some associated unit.
198 
199     See also: http://docs.astropy.org/en/stable/units/quantity.html
200 
201     Parameters
202     ----------
203     value : number, `~numpy.ndarray`, `Quantity` object (sequence), str
204         The numerical value of this quantity in the units given by unit.  If a
205         `Quantity` or sequence of them (or any other valid object with a
206         ``unit`` attribute), creates a new `Quantity` object, converting to
207         `unit` units as needed.  If a string, it is converted to a number or
208         `Quantity`, depending on whether a unit is present.
209 
210     unit : `~astropy.units.UnitBase` instance, str
211         An object that represents the unit associated with the input value.
212         Must be an `~astropy.units.UnitBase` object or a string parseable by
213         the :mod:`~astropy.units` package.
214 
215     dtype : ~numpy.dtype, optional
216         The dtype of the resulting Numpy array or scalar that will
217         hold the value.  If not provided, it is determined from the input,
218         except that any input that cannot represent float (integer and bool)
219         is converted to float.
220 
221     copy : bool, optional
222         If `True` (default), then the value is copied.  Otherwise, a copy will
223         only be made if ``__array__`` returns a copy, if value is a nested
224         sequence, or if a copy is needed to satisfy an explicitly given
225         ``dtype``.  (The `False` option is intended mostly for internal use,
226         to speed up initialization where a copy is known to have been made.
227         Use with care.)
228 
229     order : {'C', 'F', 'A'}, optional
230         Specify the order of the array.  As in `~numpy.array`.  This parameter
231         is ignored if the input is a `Quantity` and ``copy=False``.
232 
233     subok : bool, optional
234         If `False` (default), the returned array will be forced to be a
235         `Quantity`.  Otherwise, `Quantity` subclasses will be passed through,
236         or a subclass appropriate for the unit will be used (such as
237         `~astropy.units.Dex` for ``u.dex(u.AA)``).
238 
239     ndmin : int, optional
240         Specifies the minimum number of dimensions that the resulting array
241         should have.  Ones will be pre-pended to the shape as needed to meet
242         this requirement.  This parameter is ignored if the input is a
243         `Quantity` and ``copy=False``.
244 
245     Raises
246     ------
247     TypeError
248         If the value provided is not a Python numeric type.
249     TypeError
250         If the unit provided is not either a :class:`~astropy.units.Unit`
251         object or a parseable string unit.
252 
253     Notes
254     -----
255     Quantities can also be created by multiplying a number or array with a
256     :class:`~astropy.units.Unit`. See http://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/units/
257 
258     """
259     # Need to set a class-level default for _equivalencies, or
260     # Constants can not initialize properly
261     _equivalencies = []
262 
263     # Default unit for initialization; can be overridden by subclasses,
264     # possibly to `None` to indicate there is no default unit.
265     _default_unit = dimensionless_unscaled
266 
267     # Ensures views have an undefined unit.
268     _unit = None
269 
270     __array_priority__ = 10000
271 
272     def __new__(cls, value, unit=None, dtype=None, copy=True, order=None,
273                 subok=False, ndmin=0):
274 
275         if unit is not None:
276             # convert unit first, to avoid multiple string->unit conversions
277             unit = Unit(unit)
278             # if we allow subclasses, allow a class from the unit.
279             if subok:
280                 qcls = getattr(unit, '_quantity_class', cls)
281                 if issubclass(qcls, cls):
282                     cls = qcls
283 
284         # optimize speed for Quantity with no dtype given, copy=False
285         if isinstance(value, Quantity):
286             if unit is not None and unit is not value.unit:
287                 value = value.to(unit)
288                 # the above already makes a copy (with float dtype)
289                 copy = False
290 
291             if type(value) is not cls and not (subok and
292                                                isinstance(value, cls)):
293                 value = value.view(cls)
294 
295             if dtype is None:
296                 if not copy:
297                     return value
298 
299                 if not (np.can_cast(np.float32, value.dtype) or
300                         value.dtype.fields):
301                     dtype = float
302 
303             return np.array(value, dtype=dtype, copy=copy, order=order,
304                             subok=True, ndmin=ndmin)
305 
306         # Maybe str, or list/tuple of Quantity? If so, this may set value_unit.
307         # To ensure array remains fast, we short-circuit it.
308         value_unit = None
309         if not isinstance(value, np.ndarray):
310             if isinstance(value, str):
311                 # The first part of the regex string matches any integer/float;
312                 # the second parts adds possible trailing .+-, which will break
313                 # the float function below and ensure things like 1.2.3deg
314                 # will not work.
315                 pattern = (r'\s*[+-]?'
316                            r'((\d+\.?\d*)|(\.\d+)|([nN][aA][nN])|'
317                            r'([iI][nN][fF]([iI][nN][iI][tT][yY]){0,1}))'
318                            r'([eE][+-]?\d+)?'
319                            r'[.+-]?')
320 
321                 v = re.match(pattern, value)
322                 unit_string = None
323                 try:
324                     value = float(v.group())
325 
326                 except Exception:
327                     raise TypeError('Cannot parse "{0}" as a {1}. It does not '
328                                     'start with a number.'
329                                     .format(value, cls.__name__))
330 
331                 unit_string = v.string[v.end():].strip()
332                 if unit_string:
333                     value_unit = Unit(unit_string)
334                     if unit is None:
335                         unit = value_unit  # signal no conversion needed below.
336 
337             elif (isiterable(value) and len(value) > 0 and
338                   all(isinstance(v, Quantity) for v in value)):
339                 # Convert all quantities to the same unit.
340                 if unit is None:
341                     unit = value[0].unit
342                 value = [q.to_value(unit) for q in value]
343                 value_unit = unit  # signal below that conversion has been done
344 
345         if value_unit is None:
346             # If the value has a `unit` attribute and if not None
347             # (for Columns with uninitialized unit), treat it like a quantity.
348             value_unit = getattr(value, 'unit', None)
349             if value_unit is None:
350                 # Default to dimensionless for no (initialized) unit attribute.
351                 if unit is None:
352                     unit = cls._default_unit
353                 value_unit = unit  # signal below that no conversion is needed
354             else:
355                 try:
356                     value_unit = Unit(value_unit)
357                 except Exception as exc:
358                     raise TypeError("The unit attribute {0!r} of the input could "
359                                     "not be parsed as an astropy Unit, raising "
360                                     "the following exception:\n{1}"
361                                     .format(value.unit, exc))
362 
363                 if unit is None:
364                     unit = value_unit
365                 elif unit is not value_unit:
366                     copy = False  # copy will be made in conversion at end
367 
368         value = np.array(value, dtype=dtype, copy=copy, order=order,
369                          subok=False, ndmin=ndmin)
370 
371         # check that array contains numbers or long int objects
372         if (value.dtype.kind in 'OSU' and
373             not (value.dtype.kind == 'O' and
374                  isinstance(value.item(() if value.ndim == 0 else 0),
375                             numbers.Number))):
376             raise TypeError("The value must be a valid Python or "
377                             "Numpy numeric type.")
378 
379         # by default, cast any integer, boolean, etc., to float
380         if dtype is None and (not (np.can_cast(np.float32, value.dtype)
381                                    or value.dtype.fields)
382                               or value.dtype.kind == 'O'):
383             value = value.astype(float)
384 
385         value = value.view(cls)
386         value._set_unit(value_unit)
387         if unit is value_unit:
388             return value
389         else:
390             # here we had non-Quantity input that had a "unit" attribute
391             # with a unit different from the desired one.  So, convert.
392             return value.to(unit)
393 
394     def __array_finalize__(self, obj):
395         # If we're a new object or viewing an ndarray, nothing has to be done.
396         if obj is None or obj.__class__ is np.ndarray:
397             return
398 
399         # If our unit is not set and obj has a valid one, use it.
400         if self._unit is None:
401             unit = getattr(obj, '_unit', None)
402             if unit is not None:
403                 self._set_unit(unit)
404 
405         # Copy info if the original had `info` defined.  Because of the way the
406         # DataInfo works, `'info' in obj.__dict__` is False until the
407         # `info` attribute is accessed or set.
408         if 'info' in obj.__dict__:
409             self.info = obj.info
410 
411     def __array_wrap__(self, obj, context=None):
412 
413         if context is None:
414             # Methods like .squeeze() created a new `ndarray` and then call
415             # __array_wrap__ to turn the array into self's subclass.
416             return self._new_view(obj)
417 
418         raise NotImplementedError('__array_wrap__ should not be used '
419                                   'with a context any more, since we require '
420                                   'numpy >=1.13.  Please raise an issue on '
421                                   'https://github.com/astropy/astropy')
422 
423     def __array_ufunc__(self, function, method, *inputs, **kwargs):
424         """Wrap numpy ufuncs, taking care of units.
425 
426         Parameters
427         ----------
428         function : callable
429             ufunc to wrap.
430         method : str
431             Ufunc method: ``__call__``, ``at``, ``reduce``, etc.
432         inputs : tuple
433             Input arrays.
434         kwargs : keyword arguments
435             As passed on, with ``out`` containing possible quantity output.
436 
437         Returns
438         -------
439         result : `~astropy.units.Quantity`
440             Results of the ufunc, with the unit set properly.
441         """
442         # Determine required conversion functions -- to bring the unit of the
443         # input to that expected (e.g., radian for np.sin), or to get
444         # consistent units between two inputs (e.g., in np.add) --
445         # and the unit of the result (or tuple of units for nout > 1).
446         converters, unit = converters_and_unit(function, method, *inputs)
447 
448         out = kwargs.get('out', None)
449         # Avoid loop back by turning any Quantity output into array views.
450         if out is not None:
451             # If pre-allocated output is used, check it is suitable.
452             # This also returns array view, to ensure we don't loop back.
453             if function.nout == 1:
454                 out = out[0]
455             out_array = check_output(out, unit, inputs, function=function)
456             # Ensure output argument remains a tuple.
457             kwargs['out'] = (out_array,) if function.nout == 1 else out_array
458 
459         # Same for inputs, but here also convert if necessary.
460         arrays = []
461         for input_, converter in zip(inputs, converters):
462             input_ = getattr(input_, 'value', input_)
463             arrays.append(converter(input_) if converter else input_)
464 
465         # Call our superclass's __array_ufunc__
466         result = super().__array_ufunc__(function, method, *arrays, **kwargs)
467         # If unit is None, a plain array is expected (e.g., comparisons), which
468         # means we're done.
469         # We're also done if the result was None (for method 'at') or
470         # NotImplemented, which can happen if other inputs/outputs override
471         # __array_ufunc__; hopefully, they can then deal with us.
472         if unit is None or result is None or result is NotImplemented:
473             return result
474 
475         return self._result_as_quantity(result, unit, out)
476 
477     def _result_as_quantity(self, result, unit, out):
478         """Turn result into a quantity with the given unit.
479 
480         If no output is given, it will take a view of the array as a quantity,
481         and set the unit.  If output is given, those should be quantity views
482         of the result arrays, and the function will just set the unit.
483 
484         Parameters
485         ----------
486         result : `~numpy.ndarray` or tuple of `~numpy.ndarray`
487             Array(s) which need to be turned into quantity.
488         unit : `~astropy.units.Unit`
489             Unit for the quantities to be returned (or `None` if the result
490             should not be a quantity).  Should be tuple if result is a tuple.
491         out : `~astropy.units.Quantity` or None
492             Possible output quantity. Should be `None` or a tuple if result
493             is a tuple.
494 
495         Returns
496         -------
497         out : `~astropy.units.Quantity`
498            With units set.
499         """
500         if isinstance(result, tuple):
501             if out is None:
502                 out = (None,) * len(result)
503             return tuple(self._result_as_quantity(result_, unit_, out_)
504                          for (result_, unit_, out_) in
505                          zip(result, unit, out))
506 
507         if out is None:
508             # View the result array as a Quantity with the proper unit.
509             return result if unit is None else self._new_view(result, unit)
510 
511         # For given output, just set the unit. We know the unit is not None and
512         # the output is of the correct Quantity subclass, as it was passed
513         # through check_output.
514         out._set_unit(unit)
515         return out
516 
517     def __quantity_subclass__(self, unit):
518         """
519         Overridden by subclasses to change what kind of view is
520         created based on the output unit of an operation.
521 
522         Parameters
523         ----------
524         unit : UnitBase
525             The unit for which the appropriate class should be returned
526 
527         Returns
528         -------
529         tuple :
530             - `Quantity` subclass
531             - bool: True if subclasses of the given class are ok
532         """
533         return Quantity, True
534 
535     def _new_view(self, obj=None, unit=None):
536         """
537         Create a Quantity view of some array-like input, and set the unit
538 
539         By default, return a view of ``obj`` of the same class as ``self`` and
540         with the same unit.  Subclasses can override the type of class for a
541         given unit using ``__quantity_subclass__``, and can ensure properties
542         other than the unit are copied using ``__array_finalize__``.
543 
544         If the given unit defines a ``_quantity_class`` of which ``self``
545         is not an instance, a view using this class is taken.
546 
547         Parameters
548         ----------
549         obj : ndarray or scalar, optional
550             The array to create a view of.  If obj is a numpy or python scalar,
551             it will be converted to an array scalar.  By default, ``self``
552             is converted.
553 
554         unit : `UnitBase`, or anything convertible to a :class:`~astropy.units.Unit`, optional
555             The unit of the resulting object.  It is used to select a
556             subclass, and explicitly assigned to the view if given.
557             If not given, the subclass and unit will be that of ``self``.
558 
559         Returns
560         -------
561         view : Quantity subclass
562         """
563         # Determine the unit and quantity subclass that we need for the view.
564         if unit is None:
565             unit = self.unit
566             quantity_subclass = self.__class__
567         elif unit is self.unit and self.__class__ is Quantity:
568             # The second part is because we should not presume what other
569             # classes want to do for the same unit.  E.g., Constant will
570             # always want to fall back to Quantity, and relies on going
571             # through `__quantity_subclass__`.
572             quantity_subclass = Quantity
573         else:
574             unit = Unit(unit)
575             quantity_subclass = getattr(unit, '_quantity_class', Quantity)
576             if isinstance(self, quantity_subclass):
577                 quantity_subclass, subok = self.__quantity_subclass__(unit)
578                 if subok:
579                     quantity_subclass = self.__class__
580 
581         # We only want to propagate information from ``self`` to our new view,
582         # so obj should be a regular array.  By using ``np.array``, we also
583         # convert python and numpy scalars, which cannot be viewed as arrays
584         # and thus not as Quantity either, to zero-dimensional arrays.
585         # (These are turned back into scalar in `.value`)
586         # Note that for an ndarray input, the np.array call takes only double
587         # ``obj.__class is np.ndarray``. So, not worth special-casing.
588         if obj is None:
589             obj = self.view(np.ndarray)
590         else:
591             obj = np.array(obj, copy=False)
592 
593         # Take the view, set the unit, and update possible other properties
594         # such as ``info``, ``wrap_angle`` in `Longitude`, etc.
595         view = obj.view(quantity_subclass)
596         view._set_unit(unit)
597         view.__array_finalize__(self)
598         return view
599 
600     def _set_unit(self, unit):
601         """Set the unit.
602 
603         This is used anywhere the unit is set or modified, i.e., in the
604         initilizer, in ``__imul__`` and ``__itruediv__`` for in-place
605         multiplication and division by another unit, as well as in
606         ``__array_finalize__`` for wrapping up views.  For Quantity, it just
607         sets the unit, but subclasses can override it to check that, e.g.,
608         a unit is consistent.
609         """
610         if not isinstance(unit, UnitBase):
611             # Trying to go through a string ensures that, e.g., Magnitudes with
612             # dimensionless physical unit become Quantity with units of mag.
613             unit = Unit(str(unit), parse_strict='silent')
614             if not isinstance(unit, UnitBase):
615                 raise UnitTypeError(
616                     "{0} instances require {1} units, not {2} instances."
617                     .format(type(self).__name__, UnitBase, type(unit)))
618 
619         self._unit = unit
620 
621     def __deepcopy__(self, memo):
622         # If we don't define this, ``copy.deepcopy(quantity)`` will
623         # return a bare Numpy array.
624         return self.copy()
625 
626     def __reduce__(self):
627         # patch to pickle Quantity objects (ndarray subclasses), see
628         # http://www.mail-archive.com/numpy-discussion@scipy.org/msg02446.html
629 
630         object_state = list(super().__reduce__())
631         object_state[2] = (object_state[2], self.__dict__)
632         return tuple(object_state)
633 
634     def __setstate__(self, state):
635         # patch to unpickle Quantity objects (ndarray subclasses), see
636         # http://www.mail-archive.com/numpy-discussion@scipy.org/msg02446.html
637 
638         nd_state, own_state = state
639         super().__setstate__(nd_state)
640         self.__dict__.update(own_state)
641 
642     info = QuantityInfo()
643 
644     def _to_value(self, unit, equivalencies=[]):
645         """Helper method for to and to_value."""
646         if equivalencies == []:
647             equivalencies = self._equivalencies
648         return self.unit.to(unit, self.view(np.ndarray),
649                             equivalencies=equivalencies)
650 
651     def to(self, unit, equivalencies=[]):
652         """
653         Return a new `~astropy.units.Quantity` object with the specified unit.
654 
655         Parameters
656         ----------
657         unit : `~astropy.units.UnitBase` instance, str
658             An object that represents the unit to convert to. Must be
659             an `~astropy.units.UnitBase` object or a string parseable
660             by the `~astropy.units` package.
661 
662         equivalencies : list of equivalence pairs, optional
663             A list of equivalence pairs to try if the units are not
664             directly convertible.  See :ref:`unit_equivalencies`.
665             If not provided or ``[]``, class default equivalencies will be used
666             (none for `~astropy.units.Quantity`, but may be set for subclasses)
667             If `None`, no equivalencies will be applied at all, not even any
668             set globally or within a context.
669 
670         See also
671         --------
672         to_value : get the numerical value in a given unit.
673         """
674         # We don't use `to_value` below since we always want to make a copy
675         # and don't want to slow down this method (esp. the scalar case).
676         unit = Unit(unit)
677         return self._new_view(self._to_value(unit, equivalencies), unit)
678 
679     def to_value(self, unit=None, equivalencies=[]):
680         """
681         The numerical value, possibly in a different unit.
682 
683         Parameters
684         ----------
685         unit : `~astropy.units.UnitBase` instance or str, optional
686             The unit in which the value should be given. If not given or `None`,
687             use the current unit.
688 
689         equivalencies : list of equivalence pairs, optional
690             A list of equivalence pairs to try if the units are not directly
691             convertible (see :ref:`unit_equivalencies`). If not provided or
692             ``[]``, class default equivalencies will be used (none for
693             `~astropy.units.Quantity`, but may be set for subclasses).
694             If `None`, no equivalencies will be applied at all, not even any
695             set globally or within a context.
696 
697         Returns
698         -------
699         value : `~numpy.ndarray` or scalar
700             The value in the units specified. For arrays, this will be a view
701             of the data if no unit conversion was necessary.
702 
703         See also
704         --------
705         to : Get a new instance in a different unit.
706         """
707         if unit is None or unit is self.unit:
708             value = self.view(np.ndarray)
709         else:
710             unit = Unit(unit)
711             # We want a view if the unit does not change.  One could check
712             # with "==", but that calculates the scale that we need anyway.
713             # TODO: would be better for `unit.to` to have an in-place flag.
714             try:
715                 scale = self.unit._to(unit)

1120     def to_string(self, unit=None, precision=None, format=None, subfmt=None):
1121         """
1122         Generate a string representation of the quantity and its unit.
1123 
1124         The behavior of this function can be altered via the
1125         `numpy.set_printoptions` function and its various keywords.  The
1126         exception to this is the ``threshold`` keyword, which is controlled via
1127         the ``[units.quantity]`` configuration item ``latex_array_threshold``.
1128         This is treated separately because the numpy default of 1000 is too big
1129         for most browsers to handle.
1130 
1131         Parameters
1132         ----------
1133         unit : `~astropy.units.UnitBase`, optional
1134             Specifies the unit.  If not provided,
1135             the unit used to initialize the quantity will be used.
1136 
1137         precision : numeric, optional
1138             The level of decimal precision. If `None`, or not provided,
1139             it will be determined from NumPy print options.
1140 
1141         format : str, optional
1142             The format of the result. If not provided, an unadorned
1143             string is returned. Supported values are:
1144 
1145             - 'latex': Return a LaTeX-formatted string
1146 
1147         subfmt : str, optional
1148             Subformat of the result. For the moment,
1149             only used for format="latex". Supported values are:
1150 
1151             - 'inline': Use ``$ ... $`` as delimiters.
1152 
1153             - 'display': Use ``$\\displaystyle ... $`` as delimiters.
1154 
1155         Returns
1156         -------
1157         lstr
1158             A string with the contents of this Quantity
1159         """
1160         if unit is not None and unit != self.unit:
1161             return self.to(unit).to_string(
1162                 unit=None, precision=precision, format=format, subfmt=subfmt)
1163 
1164         formats = {
1165             None: None,
1166             "latex": {
1167                 None: ("$", "$"),
1168                 "inline": ("$", "$"),
1169                 "display": (r"$\displaystyle ", r"$"),
1170             },
1171         }
1172 
1173         if format not in formats:
1174             raise ValueError("Unknown format '{0}'".format(format))
1175         elif format is None:
1176             return '{0}{1:s}'.format(self.value, self._unitstr)
1177 
1178         # else, for the moment we assume format="latex"
1179 
1180         # need to do try/finally because "threshold" cannot be overridden
1181         # with array2string
1182         pops = np.get_printoptions()
1183 
1184         format_spec = '.{}g'.format(
1185             precision if precision is not None else pops['precision'])
1186 
1187         def float_formatter(value):
1188             return Latex.format_exponential_notation(value,
1189                                                      format_spec=format_spec)
1190 
1191         def complex_formatter(value):
1192             return '({0}{1}i)'.format(
1193                 Latex.format_exponential_notation(value.real,
1194                                                   format_spec=format_spec),
1195                 Latex.format_exponential_notation(value.imag,
1196                                                   format_spec='+' + format_spec))
1197 
1198         try:
1199             formatter = {'float_kind': float_formatter,
1200                          'complex_kind': complex_formatter}
1201             if conf.latex_array_threshold > -1:
1202                 np.set_printoptions(threshold=conf.latex_array_threshold,
1203                                     formatter=formatter)
1204 
1205             # the view is needed for the scalar case - value might be float
1206             if NUMPY_LT_1_14:   # style deprecated in 1.14
1207                 latex_value = np.array2string(
1208                     self.view(np.ndarray),
1209                     style=(float_formatter if self.dtype.kind == 'f'
1210                            else complex_formatter if self.dtype.kind == 'c'
1211                            else repr),
1212                     max_line_width=np.inf, separator=',~')
1213             else:
1214                 latex_value = np.array2string(
1215                     self.view(np.ndarray),
1216                     max_line_width=np.inf, separator=',~')
1217 
1218             latex_value = latex_value.replace('...', r'\dots')
1219         finally:
1220             np.set_printoptions(**pops)
1221 
1222         # Format unit
1223         # [1:-1] strips the '$' on either side needed for math mode
1224         latex_unit = (self.unit._repr_latex_()[1:-1]  # note this is unicode
1225                       if self.unit is not None
1226                       else _UNIT_NOT_INITIALISED)
1227 
1228         delimiter_left, delimiter_right = formats[format][subfmt]
1229 
1230         return r'{left}{0} \; {1}{right}'.format(latex_value, latex_unit,
1231                                                  left=delimiter_left,
1232                                                  right=delimiter_right)

1298     def _decompose(self, allowscaledunits=False, bases=[]):

1301         units have only irreducible units in them (see
1302         `astropy.units.UnitBase.decompose`).

1304         Parameters
1305         ----------
1306         allowscaledunits : bool
1307             If True, the resulting `Quantity` may have a scale factor
1308             associated with it.  If False, any scaling in the unit will
1309             be subsumed into the value of the resulting `Quantity`

1311         bases : sequence of UnitBase, optional

1313             decomposes down to any irreducible units.  When provided,
1314             the decomposed result will only contain the given units.

1316             to do so.

1320         newq : `~astropy.units.Quantity`
1321             A new object equal to this quantity with units decomposed.

1328         # be sure that the original value is not being modified.
1329         if not allowscaledunits and hasattr(new_unit, 'scale'):
