750     def save_base(self, raw=False, force_insert=False,
751                   force_update=False, using=None, update_fields=None):
752         """
753         Handle the parts of saving which should be done only once per save,
754         yet need to be done in raw saves, too. This includes some sanity
755         checks and signal sending.
756 
757         The 'raw' argument is telling save_base not to save any parent
758         models and not to do any changes to the values before save. This
759         is used by fixture loading.
760         """
761         using = using or router.db_for_write(self.__class__, instance=self)
762         assert not (force_insert and (force_update or update_fields))
763         assert update_fields is None or update_fields
764         cls = origin = self.__class__
765         # Skip proxies, but keep the origin as the proxy model.
766         if cls._meta.proxy:
767             cls = cls._meta.concrete_model
768         meta = cls._meta
769         if not meta.auto_created:
770             pre_save.send(
771                 sender=origin, instance=self, raw=raw, using=using,
772                 update_fields=update_fields,
773             )
774         # A transaction isn't needed if one query is issued.
775         if meta.parents:
776             context_manager = transaction.atomic(using=using, savepoint=False)
777         else:
778             context_manager = transaction.mark_for_rollback_on_error(using=using)
779         with context_manager:
780             parent_inserted = False
781             if not raw:
782                 parent_inserted = self._save_parents(cls, using, update_fields)
783             updated = self._save_table(
784                 raw, cls, force_insert or parent_inserted,
785                 force_update, using, update_fields,
786             )
787         # Store the database on which the object was saved
788         self._state.db = using
789         # Once saved, this is no longer a to-be-added instance.
790         self._state.adding = False
791 
792         # Signal that the save is complete
793         if not meta.auto_created:
794             post_save.send(
795                 sender=origin, instance=self, created=(not updated),
796                 update_fields=update_fields, raw=raw, using=using,
797             )
798 
799     save_base.alters_data = True

801     def _save_parents(self, cls, using, update_fields):
802         """Save all the parents of cls using values from self."""
803         meta = cls._meta
804         inserted = False
805         for parent, field in meta.parents.items():
806             # Make sure the link fields are synced between parent and self.
807             if (field and getattr(self, parent._meta.pk.attname) is None and
808                     getattr(self, field.attname) is not None):
809                 setattr(self, parent._meta.pk.attname, getattr(self, field.attname))
810             parent_inserted = self._save_parents(cls=parent, using=using, update_fields=update_fields)
811             updated = self._save_table(
812                 cls=parent, using=using, update_fields=update_fields,
813                 force_insert=parent_inserted,
814             )
815             if not updated:
816                 inserted = True
817             # Set the parent's PK value to self.
818             if field:
819                 setattr(self, field.attname, self._get_pk_val(parent._meta))
820                 # Since we didn't have an instance of the parent handy set
821                 # attname directly, bypassing the descriptor. Invalidate
822                 # the related object cache, in case it's been accidentally
823                 # populated. A fresh instance will be re-built from the
824                 # database if necessary.
825                 if field.is_cached(self):
826                     field.delete_cached_value(self)
827         return inserted
828 
829     def _save_table(self, raw=False, cls=None, force_insert=False,
830                     force_update=False, using=None, update_fields=None):
831         """
832         Do the heavy-lifting involved in saving. Update or insert the data
833         for a single table.
834         """
835         meta = cls._meta
836         non_pks = [f for f in meta.local_concrete_fields if not f.primary_key]
837 
838         if update_fields:
839             non_pks = [f for f in non_pks
840                        if f.name in update_fields or f.attname in update_fields]
841 
842         pk_val = self._get_pk_val(meta)
843         if pk_val is None:
844             pk_val = meta.pk.get_pk_value_on_save(self)
845             setattr(self, meta.pk.attname, pk_val)
846         pk_set = pk_val is not None
847         if not pk_set and (force_update or update_fields):
848             raise ValueError("Cannot force an update in save() with no primary key.")
849         updated = False
850         # Skip an UPDATE when adding an instance and primary key has a default.
851         if (
852             not raw and
853             not force_insert and
854             self._state.adding and
855             self._meta.pk.default and
856             self._meta.pk.default is not NOT_PROVIDED
857         ):
858             force_insert = True
859         # If possible, try an UPDATE. If that doesn't update anything, do an INSERT.
860         if pk_set and not force_insert:
861             base_qs = cls._base_manager.using(using)
862             values = [(f, None, (getattr(self, f.attname) if raw else f.pre_save(self, False)))
863                       for f in non_pks]
864             forced_update = update_fields or force_update
865             updated = self._do_update(base_qs, using, pk_val, values, update_fields,
866                                       forced_update)
867             if force_update and not updated:
868                 raise DatabaseError("Forced update did not affect any rows.")
869             if update_fields and not updated:
870                 raise DatabaseError("Save with update_fields did not affect any rows.")
871         if not updated:
872             if meta.order_with_respect_to:
873                 # If this is a model with an order_with_respect_to
874                 # autopopulate the _order field
875                 field = meta.order_with_respect_to
876                 filter_args = field.get_filter_kwargs_for_object(self)
877                 self._order = cls._base_manager.using(using).filter(**filter_args).aggregate(
878                     _order__max=Coalesce(
879                         ExpressionWrapper(Max('_order') + Value(1), output_field=IntegerField()),
880                         Value(0),
881                     ),
882                 )['_order__max']
883             fields = meta.local_concrete_fields
884             if not pk_set:
885                 fields = [f for f in fields if f is not meta.auto_field]
886 
887             returning_fields = meta.db_returning_fields
888             results = self._do_insert(cls._base_manager, using, fields, returning_fields, raw)
889             for result, field in zip(results, returning_fields):
890                 setattr(self, field.attname, result)
891         return updated
892 
893     def _do_update(self, base_qs, using, pk_val, values, update_fields, forced_update):
894         """
895         Try to update the model. Return True if the model was updated (if an
896         update query was done and a matching row was found in the DB).
897         """
898         filtered = base_qs.filter(pk=pk_val)
899         if not values:
900             # We can end up here when saving a model in inheritance chain where
901             # update_fields doesn't target any field in current model. In that
902             # case we just say the update succeeded. Another case ending up here
903             # is a model with just PK - in that case check that the PK still
904             # exists.
905             return update_fields is not None or filtered.exists()
906         if self._meta.select_on_save and not forced_update:
907             return (
908                 filtered.exists() and
909                 # It may happen that the object is deleted from the DB right after
910                 # this check, causing the subsequent UPDATE to return zero matching
911                 # rows. The same result can occur in some rare cases when the
912                 # database returns zero despite the UPDATE being executed
913                 # successfully (a row is matched and updated). In order to
914                 # distinguish these two cases, the object's existence in the
915                 # database is again checked for if the UPDATE query returns 0.
916                 (filtered._update(values) > 0 or filtered.exists())
917             )
918         return filtered._update(values) > 0
919 
920     def _do_insert(self, manager, using, fields, returning_fields, raw):
921         """
922         Do an INSERT. If returning_fields is defined then this method should
923         return the newly created data for the model.
924         """
925         return manager._insert(
926             [self], fields=fields, returning_fields=returning_fields,
927             using=using, raw=raw,
928         )

930     def delete(self, using=None, keep_parents=False):
931         using = using or router.db_for_write(self.__class__, instance=self)
932         assert self.pk is not None, (
933             "%s object can't be deleted because its %s attribute is set to None." %
934             (self._meta.object_name, self._meta.pk.attname)
935         )
936 
937         collector = Collector(using=using)
938         collector.collect([self], keep_parents=keep_parents)
939         return collector.delete()

949     def _get_next_or_previous_by_FIELD(self, field, is_next, **kwargs):
950         if not self.pk:
951             raise ValueError("get_next/get_previous cannot be used on unsaved objects.")
952         op = 'gt' if is_next else 'lt'
953         order = '' if is_next else '-'
954         param = getattr(self, field.attname)
955         q = Q(**{'%s__%s' % (field.name, op): param})
956         q = q | Q(**{field.name: param, 'pk__%s' % op: self.pk})
957         qs = self.__class__._default_manager.using(self._state.db).filter(**kwargs).filter(q).order_by(
958             '%s%s' % (order, field.name), '%spk' % order
959         )
960         try:
961             return qs[0]
962         except IndexError:
963             raise self.DoesNotExist("%s matching query does not exist." % self.__class__._meta.object_name)
964 
965     def _get_next_or_previous_in_order(self, is_next):
966         cachename = "__%s_order_cache" % is_next
967         if not hasattr(self, cachename):
968             op = 'gt' if is_next else 'lt'
969             order = '_order' if is_next else '-_order'
970             order_field = self._meta.order_with_respect_to
971             filter_args = order_field.get_filter_kwargs_for_object(self)
972             obj = self.__class__._default_manager.filter(**filter_args).filter(**{
973                 '_order__%s' % op: self.__class__._default_manager.values('_order').filter(**{
974                     self._meta.pk.name: self.pk
975                 })
976             }).order_by(order)[:1].get()
977             setattr(self, cachename, obj)
978         return getattr(self, cachename)

994     def validate_unique(self, exclude=None):
995         """
996         Check unique constraints on the model and raise ValidationError if any
997         failed.
998         """
999         unique_checks, date_checks = self._get_unique_checks(exclude=exclude)
1000 
1001         errors = self._perform_unique_checks(unique_checks)
1002         date_errors = self._perform_date_checks(date_checks)
1003 
1004         for k, v in date_errors.items():
1005             errors.setdefault(k, []).extend(v)
1006 
1007         if errors:
1008             raise ValidationError(errors)

1010     def _get_unique_checks(self, exclude=None):
1011         """
1012         Return a list of checks to perform. Since validate_unique() could be
1013         called from a ModelForm, some fields may have been excluded; we can't
1014         perform a unique check on a model that is missing fields involved
1015         in that check. Fields that did not validate should also be excluded,
1016         but they need to be passed in via the exclude argument.
1017         """
1018         if exclude is None:
1019             exclude = []
1020         unique_checks = []
1021 
1022         unique_togethers = [(self.__class__, self._meta.unique_together)]
1023         constraints = [(self.__class__, self._meta.constraints)]
1024         for parent_class in self._meta.get_parent_list():
1025             if parent_class._meta.unique_together:
1026                 unique_togethers.append((parent_class, parent_class._meta.unique_together))
1027             if parent_class._meta.constraints:
1028                 constraints.append((parent_class, parent_class._meta.constraints))
1029 
1030         for model_class, unique_together in unique_togethers:
1031             for check in unique_together:
1032                 if not any(name in exclude for name in check):
1033                     # Add the check if the field isn't excluded.
1034                     unique_checks.append((model_class, tuple(check)))
1035 
1036         for model_class, model_constraints in constraints:
1037             for constraint in model_constraints:
1038                 if (isinstance(constraint, UniqueConstraint) and
1039                         # Partial unique constraints can't be validated.
1040                         constraint.condition is None and
1041                         not any(name in exclude for name in constraint.fields)):
1042                     unique_checks.append((model_class, constraint.fields))
1043 
1044         # These are checks for the unique_for_<date/year/month>.
1045         date_checks = []
1046 
1047         # Gather a list of checks for fields declared as unique and add them to
1048         # the list of checks.
1049 
1050         fields_with_class = [(self.__class__, self._meta.local_fields)]
1051         for parent_class in self._meta.get_parent_list():
1052             fields_with_class.append((parent_class, parent_class._meta.local_fields))
1053 
1054         for model_class, fields in fields_with_class:
1055             for f in fields:
1056                 name = f.name
1057                 if name in exclude:
1058                     continue
1059                 if f.unique:
1060                     unique_checks.append((model_class, (name,)))
1061                 if f.unique_for_date and f.unique_for_date not in exclude:
1062                     date_checks.append((model_class, 'date', name, f.unique_for_date))
1063                 if f.unique_for_year and f.unique_for_year not in exclude:
1064                     date_checks.append((model_class, 'year', name, f.unique_for_year))
1065                 if f.unique_for_month and f.unique_for_month not in exclude:
1066                     date_checks.append((model_class, 'month', name, f.unique_for_month))
1067         return unique_checks, date_checks
1068 
1069     def _perform_unique_checks(self, unique_checks):
1070         errors = {}
1071 
1072         for model_class, unique_check in unique_checks:
1073             # Try to look up an existing object with the same values as this
1074             # object's values for all the unique field.
1075 
1076             lookup_kwargs = {}
1077             for field_name in unique_check:
1078                 f = self._meta.get_field(field_name)
1079                 lookup_value = getattr(self, f.attname)
1080                 # TODO: Handle multiple backends with different feature flags.
1081                 if (lookup_value is None or
1082                         (lookup_value == '' and connection.features.interprets_empty_strings_as_nulls)):
1083                     # no value, skip the lookup
1084                     continue
1085                 if f.primary_key and not self._state.adding:
1086                     # no need to check for unique primary key when editing
1087                     continue
1088                 lookup_kwargs[str(field_name)] = lookup_value
1089 
1090             # some fields were skipped, no reason to do the check
1091             if len(unique_check) != len(lookup_kwargs):
1092                 continue
1093 
1094             qs = model_class._default_manager.filter(**lookup_kwargs)
1095 
1096             # Exclude the current object from the query if we are editing an
1097             # instance (as opposed to creating a new one)
1098             # Note that we need to use the pk as defined by model_class, not
1099             # self.pk. These can be different fields because model inheritance
1100             # allows single model to have effectively multiple primary keys.
1101             # Refs #17615.
1102             model_class_pk = self._get_pk_val(model_class._meta)
1103             if not self._state.adding and model_class_pk is not None:
1104                 qs = qs.exclude(pk=model_class_pk)
1105             if qs.exists():
1106                 if len(unique_check) == 1:
1107                     key = unique_check[0]
1108                 else:
1109                     key = NON_FIELD_ERRORS
1110                 errors.setdefault(key, []).append(self.unique_error_message(model_class, unique_check))
1111 
1112         return errors
1113 
1114     def _perform_date_checks(self, date_checks):
1115         errors = {}
1116         for model_class, lookup_type, field, unique_for in date_checks:
1117             lookup_kwargs = {}
1118             # there's a ticket to add a date lookup, we can remove this special
1119             # case if that makes it's way in
1120             date = getattr(self, unique_for)
1121             if date is None:
1122                 continue
1123             if lookup_type == 'date':
1124                 lookup_kwargs['%s__day' % unique_for] = date.day
1125                 lookup_kwargs['%s__month' % unique_for] = date.month
1126                 lookup_kwargs['%s__year' % unique_for] = date.year
1127             else:
1128                 lookup_kwargs['%s__%s' % (unique_for, lookup_type)] = getattr(date, lookup_type)
1129             lookup_kwargs[field] = getattr(self, field)
1130 
1131             qs = model_class._default_manager.filter(**lookup_kwargs)
1132             # Exclude the current object from the query if we are editing an
1133             # instance (as opposed to creating a new one)
1134             if not self._state.adding and self.pk is not None:
1135                 qs = qs.exclude(pk=self.pk)
1136 
1137             if qs.exists():
1138                 errors.setdefault(field, []).append(
1139                     self.date_error_message(lookup_type, field, unique_for)
1140                 )
1141         return errors

1143     def date_error_message(self, lookup_type, field_name, unique_for):
1144         opts = self._meta
1145         field = opts.get_field(field_name)
1146         return ValidationError(
1147             message=field.error_messages['unique_for_date'],
1148             code='unique_for_date',
1149             params={
1150                 'model': self,
1151                 'model_name': capfirst(opts.verbose_name),
1152                 'lookup_type': lookup_type,
1153                 'field': field_name,
1154                 'field_label': capfirst(field.verbose_name),
1155                 'date_field': unique_for,
1156                 'date_field_label': capfirst(opts.get_field(unique_for).verbose_name),
1157             }
1158         )

1160     def unique_error_message(self, model_class, unique_check):
1161         opts = model_class._meta
1162 
1163         params = {
1164             'model': self,
1165             'model_class': model_class,
1166             'model_name': capfirst(opts.verbose_name),
1167             'unique_check': unique_check,
1168         }
1169 
1170         # A unique field
1171         if len(unique_check) == 1:
1172             field = opts.get_field(unique_check[0])
1173             params['field_label'] = capfirst(field.verbose_name)
1174             return ValidationError(
1175                 message=field.error_messages['unique'],
1176                 code='unique',
1177                 params=params,
1178             )
1179 
1180         # unique_together
1181         else:
1182             field_labels = [capfirst(opts.get_field(f).verbose_name) for f in unique_check]
1183             params['field_labels'] = get_text_list(field_labels, _('and'))
1184             return ValidationError(
1185                 message=_("%(model_name)s with this %(field_labels)s already exists."),
1186                 code='unique_together',
1187                 params=params,
1188             )

1190     def full_clean(self, exclude=None, validate_unique=True):
1191         """
1192         Call clean_fields(), clean(), and validate_unique() on the model.
1193         Raise a ValidationError for any errors that occur.
1194         """
1195         errors = {}
1196         if exclude is None:
1197             exclude = []
1198         else:
1199             exclude = list(exclude)
1200 
1201         try:
1202             self.clean_fields(exclude=exclude)
1203         except ValidationError as e:
1204             errors = e.update_error_dict(errors)
1205 
1206         # Form.clean() is run even if other validation fails, so do the
1207         # same with Model.clean() for consistency.
1208         try:
1209             self.clean()
1210         except ValidationError as e:
1211             errors = e.update_error_dict(errors)
1212 
1213         # Run unique checks, but only for fields that passed validation.
1214         if validate_unique:
1215             for name in errors:
1216                 if name != NON_FIELD_ERRORS and name not in exclude:
1217                     exclude.append(name)
1218             try:
1219                 self.validate_unique(exclude=exclude)
1220             except ValidationError as e:
1221                 errors = e.update_error_dict(errors)
1222 
1223         if errors:
1224             raise ValidationError(errors)

1226     def clean_fields(self, exclude=None):
1227         """
1228         Clean all fields and raise a ValidationError containing a dict
1229         of all validation errors if any occur.
1230         """
1231         if exclude is None:
1232             exclude = []
1233 
1234         errors = {}
1235         for f in self._meta.fields:
1236             if f.name in exclude:
1237                 continue
1238             # Skip validation for empty fields with blank=True. The developer
1239             # is responsible for making sure they have a valid value.
1240             raw_value = getattr(self, f.attname)
1241             if f.blank and raw_value in f.empty_values:
1242                 continue
1243             try:
1244                 setattr(self, f.attname, f.clean(raw_value, self))
1245             except ValidationError as e:
1246                 errors[f.name] = e.error_list
1247 
1248         if errors:
1249             raise ValidationError(errors)

1389     @classmethod
1390     def _check_field_name_clashes(cls):
1391         """Forbid field shadowing in multi-table inheritance."""
1392         errors = []
1393         used_fields = {}  # name or attname -> field
1394 
1395         # Check that multi-inheritance doesn't cause field name shadowing.
1396         for parent in cls._meta.get_parent_list():
1397             for f in parent._meta.local_fields:
1398                 clash = used_fields.get(f.name) or used_fields.get(f.attname) or None
1399                 if clash:
1400                     errors.append(
1401                         checks.Error(
1402                             "The field '%s' from parent model "
1403                             "'%s' clashes with the field '%s' "
1404                             "from parent model '%s'." % (
1405                                 clash.name, clash.model._meta,
1406                                 f.name, f.model._meta
1407                             ),
1408                             obj=cls,
1409                             id='models.E005',
1410                         )
1411                     )
1412                 used_fields[f.name] = f
1413                 used_fields[f.attname] = f
1414 
1415         # Check that fields defined in the model don't clash with fields from
1416         # parents, including auto-generated fields like multi-table inheritance
1417         # child accessors.
1418         for parent in cls._meta.get_parent_list():
1419             for f in parent._meta.get_fields():
1420                 if f not in used_fields:
1421                     used_fields[f.name] = f
1422 
1423         for f in cls._meta.local_fields:
1424             clash = used_fields.get(f.name) or used_fields.get(f.attname) or None
1425             # Note that we may detect clash between user-defined non-unique
1426             # field "id" and automatically added unique field "id", both
1427             # defined at the same model. This special case is considered in
1428             # _check_id_field and here we ignore it.
1429             id_conflict = f.name == "id" and clash and clash.name == "id" and clash.model == cls
1430             if clash and not id_conflict:
1431                 errors.append(
1432                     checks.Error(
1433                         "The field '%s' clashes with the field '%s' "
1434                         "from model '%s'." % (
1435                             f.name, clash.name, clash.model._meta
1436                         ),
1437                         obj=f,
1438                         id='models.E006',
1439                     )
1440                 )
1441             used_fields[f.name] = f
1442             used_fields[f.attname] = f
1443 
1444         return errors

546 class ChoiceWidget(Widget):
547     allow_multiple_selected = False
548     input_type = None
549     template_name = None
550     option_template_name = None
551     add_id_index = True
552     checked_attribute = {'checked': True}
553     option_inherits_attrs = True
554 
555     def __init__(self, attrs=None, choices=()):
556         super().__init__(attrs)
557         # choices can be any iterable, but we may need to render this widget
558         # multiple times. Thus, collapse it into a list so it can be consumed
559         # more than once.
560         self.choices = list(choices)
561 
562     def __deepcopy__(self, memo):
563         obj = copy.copy(self)
564         obj.attrs = self.attrs.copy()
565         obj.choices = copy.copy(self.choices)
566         memo[id(self)] = obj
567         return obj
568 
569     def subwidgets(self, name, value, attrs=None):
570         """
571         Yield all "subwidgets" of this widget. Used to enable iterating
572         options from a BoundField for choice widgets.
573         """
574         value = self.format_value(value)
575         yield from self.options(name, value, attrs)
576 
577     def options(self, name, value, attrs=None):
578         """Yield a flat list of options for this widgets."""
579         for group in self.optgroups(name, value, attrs):
580             yield from group[1]
581 
582     def optgroups(self, name, value, attrs=None):
583         """Return a list of optgroups for this widget."""
584         groups = []
585         has_selected = False
586 
587         for index, (option_value, option_label) in enumerate(self.choices):
588             if option_value is None:
589                 option_value = ''
590 
591             subgroup = []
592             if isinstance(option_label, (list, tuple)):
593                 group_name = option_value
594                 subindex = 0
595                 choices = option_label
596             else:
597                 group_name = None
598                 subindex = None
599                 choices = [(option_value, option_label)]
600             groups.append((group_name, subgroup, index))
601 
602             for subvalue, sublabel in choices:
603                 selected = (
604                     str(subvalue) in value and
605                     (not has_selected or self.allow_multiple_selected)
606                 )
607                 has_selected |= selected
608                 subgroup.append(self.create_option(
609                     name, subvalue, sublabel, selected, index,
610                     subindex=subindex, attrs=attrs,
611                 ))
612                 if subindex is not None:
613                     subindex += 1
614         return groups
615 
616     def create_option(self, name, value, label, selected, index, subindex=None, attrs=None):
617         index = str(index) if subindex is None else "%s_%s" % (index, subindex)
618         if attrs is None:
619             attrs = {}
620         option_attrs = self.build_attrs(self.attrs, attrs) if self.option_inherits_attrs else {}
621         if selected:
622             option_attrs.update(self.checked_attribute)
623         if 'id' in option_attrs:
624             option_attrs['id'] = self.id_for_label(option_attrs['id'], index)
625         return {
626             'name': name,
627             'value': value,
628             'label': label,
629             'selected': selected,
630             'index': index,
631             'attrs': option_attrs,
632             'type': self.input_type,
633             'template_name': self.option_template_name,
634             'wrap_label': True,
635         }
636 
637     def get_context(self, name, value, attrs):
638         context = super().get_context(name, value, attrs)
639         context['widget']['optgroups'] = self.optgroups(name, context['widget']['value'], attrs)
640         return context
641 
642     def id_for_label(self, id_, index='0'):
643         """
644         Use an incremented id for each option where the main widget
645         references the zero index.
646         """
647         if id_ and self.add_id_index:
648             id_ = '%s_%s' % (id_, index)
649         return id_
650 
651     def value_from_datadict(self, data, files, name):
652         getter = data.get
653         if self.allow_multiple_selected:
654             try:
655                 getter = data.getlist
656             except AttributeError:
657                 pass
658         return getter(name)
659 
660     def format_value(self, value):
661         """Return selected values as a list."""
662         if value is None and self.allow_multiple_selected:
663             return []
664         if not isinstance(value, (tuple, list)):
665             value = [value]
666         return [str(v) if v is not None else '' for v in value]

789 class MultiWidget(Widget):
790     """
791     A widget that is composed of multiple widgets.
792 
793     In addition to the values added by Widget.get_context(), this widget
794     adds a list of subwidgets to the context as widget['subwidgets'].
795     These can be looped over and rendered like normal widgets.
796 
797     You'll probably want to use this class with MultiValueField.
798     """
799     template_name = 'django/forms/widgets/multiwidget.html'
800 
801     def __init__(self, widgets, attrs=None):
802         self.widgets = [w() if isinstance(w, type) else w for w in widgets]
803         super().__init__(attrs)
804 
805     @property
806     def is_hidden(self):
807         return all(w.is_hidden for w in self.widgets)
808 
809     def get_context(self, name, value, attrs):
810         context = super().get_context(name, value, attrs)
811         if self.is_localized:
812             for widget in self.widgets:
813                 widget.is_localized = self.is_localized
814         # value is a list of values, each corresponding to a widget
815         # in self.widgets.
816         if not isinstance(value, list):
817             value = self.decompress(value)
818 
819         final_attrs = context['widget']['attrs']
820         input_type = final_attrs.pop('type', None)
821         id_ = final_attrs.get('id')
822         subwidgets = []
823         for i, widget in enumerate(self.widgets):
824             if input_type is not None:
825                 widget.input_type = input_type
826             widget_name = '%s_%s' % (name, i)
827             try:
828                 widget_value = value[i]
829             except IndexError:
830                 widget_value = None
831             if id_:
832                 widget_attrs = final_attrs.copy()
833                 widget_attrs['id'] = '%s_%s' % (id_, i)
834             else:
835                 widget_attrs = final_attrs
836             subwidgets.append(widget.get_context(widget_name, widget_value, widget_attrs)['widget'])
837         context['widget']['subwidgets'] = subwidgets
838         return context
839 
840     def id_for_label(self, id_):
841         if id_:
842             id_ += '_0'
843         return id_
844 
845     def value_from_datadict(self, data, files, name):
846         return [widget.value_from_datadict(data, files, name + '_%s' % i) for i, widget in enumerate(self.widgets)]
847 
848     def value_omitted_from_data(self, data, files, name):
849         return all(
850             widget.value_omitted_from_data(data, files, name + '_%s' % i)
851             for i, widget in enumerate(self.widgets)
852         )
853 
854     def decompress(self, value):
855         """
856         Return a list of decompressed values for the given compressed value.
857         The given value can be assumed to be valid, but not necessarily
858         non-empty.
859         """
860         raise NotImplementedError('Subclasses must implement this method.')
861 
862     def _get_media(self):
863         """
864         Media for a multiwidget is the combination of all media of the
865         subwidgets.
866         """
867         media = Media()
868         for w in self.widgets:
869             media = media + w.media
870         return media
871     media = property(_get_media)
872 
873     def __deepcopy__(self, memo):
874         obj = super().__deepcopy__(memo)
875         obj.widgets = copy.deepcopy(self.widgets)
876         return obj
877

879     def needs_multipart_form(self):
880         return any(w.needs_multipart_form for w in self.widgets)

926     This also serves as an example of a Widget that has more than one HTML
927     element and hence implements value_from_datadict.
928     """
929     none_value = ('', '---')
930     month_field = '%s_month'
931     day_field = '%s_day'
932     year_field = '%s_year'
933     template_name = 'django/forms/widgets/select_date.html'
934     input_type = 'select'

938     def __init__(self, attrs=None, years=None, months=None, empty_label=None):
939         self.attrs = attrs or {}
940 
941         # Optional list or tuple of years to use in the "year" select box.
942         if years:
943             self.years = years
944         else:
945             this_year = datetime.date.today().year
946             self.years = range(this_year, this_year + 10)
947 
948         # Optional dict of months to use in the "month" select box.
949         if months:
950             self.months = months
951         else:
952             self.months = MONTHS
953 
954         # Optional string, list, or tuple to use as empty_label.
955         if isinstance(empty_label, (list, tuple)):
956             if not len(empty_label) == 3:
957                 raise ValueError('empty_label list/tuple must have 3 elements.')
958 
959             self.year_none_value = ('', empty_label[0])
960             self.month_none_value = ('', empty_label[1])
961             self.day_none_value = ('', empty_label[2])
962         else:
963             if empty_label is not None:
964                 self.none_value = ('', empty_label)
965 
966             self.year_none_value = self.none_value
967             self.month_none_value = self.none_value
968             self.day_none_value = self.none_value
969 
970     def get_context(self, name, value, attrs):
971         context = super().get_context(name, value, attrs)
972         date_context = {}
973         year_choices = [(i, str(i)) for i in self.years]
974         if not self.is_required:
975             year_choices.insert(0, self.year_none_value)
976         year_name = self.year_field % name
977         date_context['year'] = self.select_widget(attrs, choices=year_choices).get_context(
978             name=year_name,
979             value=context['widget']['value']['year'],
980             attrs={**context['widget']['attrs'], 'id': 'id_%s' % year_name},
981         )
982         month_choices = list(self.months.items())

588     def refresh_from_db(self, using=None, fields=None):
589         """
590         Reload field values from the database.
591 
592         By default, the reloading happens from the database this instance was
593         loaded from, or by the read router if this instance wasn't loaded from
594         any database. The using parameter will override the default.
595 
596         Fields can be used to specify which fields to reload. The fields
597         should be an iterable of field attnames. If fields is None, then
598         all non-deferred fields are reloaded.
599 
600         When accessing deferred fields of an instance, the deferred loading
601         of the field will call this method.
602         """
603         if fields is None:
604             self._prefetched_objects_cache = {}
605         else:
606             prefetched_objects_cache = getattr(self, '_prefetched_objects_cache', ())
607             for field in fields:
608                 if field in prefetched_objects_cache:
609                     del prefetched_objects_cache[field]
610                     fields.remove(field)
611             if not fields:
612                 return
613             if any(LOOKUP_SEP in f for f in fields):
614                 raise ValueError(
615                     'Found "%s" in fields argument. Relations and transforms '
616                     'are not allowed in fields.' % LOOKUP_SEP)
617 
618         hints = {'instance': self}
619         db_instance_qs = self.__class__._base_manager.db_manager(using, hints=hints).filter(pk=self.pk)
620 
621         # Use provided fields, if not set then reload all non-deferred fields.
622         deferred_fields = self.get_deferred_fields()
623         if fields is not None:
624             fields = list(fields)
625             db_instance_qs = db_instance_qs.only(*fields)
626         elif deferred_fields:
627             fields = [f.attname for f in self._meta.concrete_fields
628                       if f.attname not in deferred_fields]
629             db_instance_qs = db_instance_qs.only(*fields)
630 
631         db_instance = db_instance_qs.get()
632         non_loaded_fields = db_instance.get_deferred_fields()
633         for field in self._meta.concrete_fields:
634             if field.attname in non_loaded_fields:
635                 # This field wasn't refreshed - skip ahead.
636                 continue
637             setattr(self, field.attname, getattr(db_instance, field.attname))
638             # Clear cached foreign keys.
639             if field.is_relation and field.is_cached(self):
640                 field.delete_cached_value(self)
641 
642         # Clear cached relations.
643         for field in self._meta.related_objects:
644             if field.is_cached(self):
645                 field.delete_cached_value(self)
646 
647         self._state.db = db_instance._state.db
648 
649     def serializable_value(self, field_name):

652         a foreign key, return the id value instead of the object. If there's
653         no Field object with this name on the model, return the model
654         attribute's value.
655 
656         Used to serialize a field's value (in the serializer, or form output,
657         for example). Normally, you would just access the attribute directly
658         and not use this method.
659         """
660         try:
661             field = self._meta.get_field(field_name)
662         except FieldDoesNotExist:
663             return getattr(self, field_name)
664         return getattr(self, field.attname)

666     def save(self, force_insert=False, force_update=False, using=None,
667              update_fields=None):
668         """
669         Save the current instance. Override this in a subclass if you want to
670         control the saving process.
671 
672         The 'force_insert' and 'force_update' parameters can be used to insist
673         that the "save" must be an SQL insert or update (or equivalent for
674         non-SQL backends), respectively. Normally, they should not be set.
675         """
676         # Ensure that a model instance without a PK hasn't been assigned to
677         # a ForeignKey or OneToOneField on this model. If the field is
678         # nullable, allowing the save() would result in silent data loss.
679         for field in self._meta.concrete_fields:
680             # If the related field isn't cached, then an instance hasn't
681             # been assigned and there's no need to worry about this check.
682             if field.is_relation and field.is_cached(self):
683                 obj = getattr(self, field.name, None)
684                 if not obj:
685                     continue
686                 # A pk may have been assigned manually to a model instance not
687                 # saved to the database (or auto-generated in a case like
688                 # UUIDField), but we allow the save to proceed and rely on the
689                 # database to raise an IntegrityError if applicable. If
690                 # constraints aren't supported by the database, there's the
691                 # unavoidable risk of data corruption.
692                 if obj.pk is None:
693                     # Remove the object from a related instance cache.
694                     if not field.remote_field.multiple:
695                         field.remote_field.delete_cached_value(obj)
696                     raise ValueError(
697                         "save() prohibited to prevent data loss due to "
698                         "unsaved related object '%s'." % field.name
699                     )
700                 elif getattr(self, field.attname) is None:
701                     # Use pk from related object if it has been saved after
702                     # an assignment.
703                     setattr(self, field.attname, obj.pk)
704                 # If the relationship's pk/to_field was changed, clear the
705                 # cached relationship.
706                 if getattr(obj, field.target_field.attname) != getattr(self, field.attname):
707                     field.delete_cached_value(self)
708 
709         using = using or router.db_for_write(self.__class__, instance=self)
710         if force_insert and (force_update or update_fields):
711             raise ValueError("Cannot force both insert and updating in model saving.")
712 
713         deferred_fields = self.get_deferred_fields()
714         if update_fields is not None:
715             # If update_fields is empty, skip the save. We do also check for
716             # no-op saves later on for inheritance cases. This bailout is
717             # still needed for skipping signal sending.
718             if not update_fields:
719                 return
720 
721             update_fields = frozenset(update_fields)
722             field_names = set()
723 
724             for field in self._meta.fields:
725                 if not field.primary_key:
726                     field_names.add(field.name)
727 
728                     if field.name != field.attname:
729                         field_names.add(field.attname)
730 
731             non_model_fields = update_fields.difference(field_names)
732 
733             if non_model_fields:
734                 raise ValueError("The following fields do not exist in this "
735                                  "model or are m2m fields: %s"
736                                  % ', '.join(non_model_fields))
737 
738         # If saving to the same database, and this model is deferred, then
739         # automatically do an "update_fields" save on the loaded fields.
740         elif not force_insert and deferred_fields and using == self._state.db:
741             field_names = set()
742             for field in self._meta.concrete_fields:
743                 if not field.primary_key and not hasattr(field, 'through'):
744                     field_names.add(field.attname)
745             loaded_fields = field_names.difference(deferred_fields)
746             if loaded_fields:
747                 update_fields = frozenset(loaded_fields)
748 
749         self.save_base(using=using, force_insert=force_insert,
750                        force_update=force_update, update_fields=update_fields)
751     save.alters_data = True

753     def save_base(self, raw=False, force_insert=False,
754                   force_update=False, using=None, update_fields=None):
755         """
756         Handle the parts of saving which should be done only once per save,
757         yet need to be done in raw saves, too. This includes some sanity
758         checks and signal sending.
759 
760         The 'raw' argument is telling save_base not to save any parent
761         models and not to do any changes to the values before save. This
762         is used by fixture loading.
763         """
764         using = using or router.db_for_write(self.__class__, instance=self)
765         assert not (force_insert and (force_update or update_fields))
766         assert update_fields is None or update_fields
767         cls = origin = self.__class__
768         # Skip proxies, but keep the origin as the proxy model.
769         if cls._meta.proxy:
770             cls = cls._meta.concrete_model
771         meta = cls._meta
772         if not meta.auto_created:
773             pre_save.send(
774                 sender=origin, instance=self, raw=raw, using=using,
775                 update_fields=update_fields,
776             )
777         # A transaction isn't needed if one query is issued.
778         if meta.parents:
779             context_manager = transaction.atomic(using=using, savepoint=False)
780         else:
781             context_manager = transaction.mark_for_rollback_on_error(using=using)
782         with context_manager:
783             parent_inserted = False
784             if not raw:
785                 parent_inserted = self._save_parents(cls, using, update_fields)
786             updated = self._save_table(
787                 raw, cls, force_insert or parent_inserted,
788                 force_update, using, update_fields,
789             )
790         # Store the database on which the object was saved
791         self._state.db = using
792         # Once saved, this is no longer a to-be-added instance.
793         self._state.adding = False
794 
795         # Signal that the save is complete
796         if not meta.auto_created:
797             post_save.send(
798                 sender=origin, instance=self, created=(not updated),
799                 update_fields=update_fields, raw=raw, using=using,
800             )
801 
802     save_base.alters_data = True

804     def _save_parents(self, cls, using, update_fields):
805         """Save all the parents of cls using values from self."""
806         meta = cls._meta
807         inserted = False
808         for parent, field in meta.parents.items():
809             # Make sure the link fields are synced between parent and self.
810             if (field and getattr(self, parent._meta.pk.attname) is None and
811                     getattr(self, field.attname) is not None):
812                 setattr(self, parent._meta.pk.attname, getattr(self, field.attname))
813             parent_inserted = self._save_parents(cls=parent, using=using, update_fields=update_fields)
814             updated = self._save_table(
815                 cls=parent, using=using, update_fields=update_fields,
816                 force_insert=parent_inserted,
817             )
818             if not updated:
819                 inserted = True
820             # Set the parent's PK value to self.
821             if field:
822                 setattr(self, field.attname, self._get_pk_val(parent._meta))
823                 # Since we didn't have an instance of the parent handy set
824                 # attname directly, bypassing the descriptor. Invalidate
825                 # the related object cache, in case it's been accidentally
826                 # populated. A fresh instance will be re-built from the
827                 # database if necessary.
828                 if field.is_cached(self):
829                     field.delete_cached_value(self)
830         return inserted

832     def _save_table(self, raw=False, cls=None, force_insert=False,
833                     force_update=False, using=None, update_fields=None):
834         """
835         Do the heavy-lifting involved in saving. Update or insert the data
836         for a single table.
837         """
838         meta = cls._meta
839         non_pks = [f for f in meta.local_concrete_fields if not f.primary_key]
840 
841         if update_fields:
842             non_pks = [f for f in non_pks
843                        if f.name in update_fields or f.attname in update_fields]
844 
845         pk_val = self._get_pk_val(meta)
846         if pk_val is None:
847             pk_val = meta.pk.get_pk_value_on_save(self)
848             setattr(self, meta.pk.attname, pk_val)
849         pk_set = pk_val is not None
850         if not pk_set and (force_update or update_fields):
851             raise ValueError("Cannot force an update in save() with no primary key.")
852         updated = False
853         # Skip an UPDATE when adding an instance and primary key has a default.
854         if (
855             not raw and
856             not force_insert and
857             self._state.adding and
858             self._meta.pk.default and
859             self._meta.pk.default is not NOT_PROVIDED
860         ):
861             force_insert = True
862         # If possible, try an UPDATE. If that doesn't update anything, do an INSERT.
863         if pk_set and not force_insert:
864             base_qs = cls._base_manager.using(using)
865             values = [(f, None, (getattr(self, f.attname) if raw else f.pre_save(self, False)))
866                       for f in non_pks]
867             forced_update = update_fields or force_update
868             updated = self._do_update(base_qs, using, pk_val, values, update_fields,
869                                       forced_update)
870             if force_update and not updated:
871                 raise DatabaseError("Forced update did not affect any rows.")
872             if update_fields and not updated:
873                 raise DatabaseError("Save with update_fields did not affect any rows.")
874         if not updated:
875             if meta.order_with_respect_to:
876                 # If this is a model with an order_with_respect_to
877                 # autopopulate the _order field
878                 field = meta.order_with_respect_to
879                 filter_args = field.get_filter_kwargs_for_object(self)
880                 self._order = cls._base_manager.using(using).filter(**filter_args).aggregate(
881                     _order__max=Coalesce(
882                         ExpressionWrapper(Max('_order') + Value(1), output_field=IntegerField()),
883                         Value(0),
884                     ),
885                 )['_order__max']
886             fields = meta.local_concrete_fields
887             if not pk_set:
888                 fields = [f for f in fields if f is not meta.auto_field]
889 
890             returning_fields = meta.db_returning_fields
891             results = self._do_insert(cls._base_manager, using, fields, returning_fields, raw)
892             for result, field in zip(results, returning_fields):
893                 setattr(self, field.attname, result)
894         return updated
895 
896     def _do_update(self, base_qs, using, pk_val, values, update_fields, forced_update):
897         """
898         Try to update the model. Return True if the model was updated (if an
899         update query was done and a matching row was found in the DB).
900         """
901         filtered = base_qs.filter(pk=pk_val)
902         if not values:
903             # We can end up here when saving a model in inheritance chain where
904             # update_fields doesn't target any field in current model. In that
905             # case we just say the update succeeded. Another case ending up here
906             # is a model with just PK - in that case check that the PK still
907             # exists.
908             return update_fields is not None or filtered.exists()
909         if self._meta.select_on_save and not forced_update:
910             return (
911                 filtered.exists() and
912                 # It may happen that the object is deleted from the DB right after
913                 # this check, causing the subsequent UPDATE to return zero matching
914                 # rows. The same result can occur in some rare cases when the
915                 # database returns zero despite the UPDATE being executed
916                 # successfully (a row is matched and updated). In order to
917                 # distinguish these two cases, the object's existence in the
918                 # database is again checked for if the UPDATE query returns 0.
919                 (filtered._update(values) > 0 or filtered.exists())
920             )
921         return filtered._update(values) > 0

930             using=using, raw=raw,

952     def _get_next_or_previous_by_FIELD(self, field, is_next, **kwargs):
953         if not self.pk:
954             raise ValueError("get_next/get_previous cannot be used on unsaved objects.")

961             '%s%s' % (order, field.name), '%spk' % order
962         )

964             return qs[0]

997     def validate_unique(self, exclude=None):
998         """
999         Check unique constraints on the model and raise ValidationError if any
1000         failed.
1001         """
1002         unique_checks, date_checks = self._get_unique_checks(exclude=exclude)
1003 
1004         errors = self._perform_unique_checks(unique_checks)
1005         date_errors = self._perform_date_checks(date_checks)
1006 
1007         for k, v in date_errors.items():
1008             errors.setdefault(k, []).extend(v)
1009

1013     def _get_unique_checks(self, exclude=None):
1014         """
1015         Return a list of checks to perform. Since validate_unique() could be
1016         called from a ModelForm, some fields may have been excluded; we can't
1017         perform a unique check on a model that is missing fields involved
1018         in that check. Fields that did not validate should also be excluded,
1019         but they need to be passed in via the exclude argument.
1020         """
1021         if exclude is None:
1022             exclude = []
1023         unique_checks = []
1024 
1025         unique_togethers = [(self.__class__, self._meta.unique_together)]
1026         constraints = [(self.__class__, self._meta.constraints)]
1027         for parent_class in self._meta.get_parent_list():
1028             if parent_class._meta.unique_together:
1029                 unique_togethers.append((parent_class, parent_class._meta.unique_together))
1030             if parent_class._meta.constraints:
1031                 constraints.append((parent_class, parent_class._meta.constraints))
1032 
1033         for model_class, unique_together in unique_togethers:
1034             for check in unique_together:
1035                 if not any(name in exclude for name in check):
1036                     # Add the check if the field isn't excluded.
1037                     unique_checks.append((model_class, tuple(check)))
1038 
1039         for model_class, model_constraints in constraints:
1040             for constraint in model_constraints:
1041                 if (isinstance(constraint, UniqueConstraint) and
1042                         # Partial unique constraints can't be validated.
1043                         constraint.condition is None and
1044                         not any(name in exclude for name in constraint.fields)):
1045                     unique_checks.append((model_class, constraint.fields))
1046 
1047         # These are checks for the unique_for_<date/year/month>.
1048         date_checks = []
1049 
1050         # Gather a list of checks for fields declared as unique and add them to
1051         # the list of checks.
1052 
1053         fields_with_class = [(self.__class__, self._meta.local_fields)]
1054         for parent_class in self._meta.get_parent_list():
1055             fields_with_class.append((parent_class, parent_class._meta.local_fields))
1056 
1057         for model_class, fields in fields_with_class:
1058             for f in fields:
1059                 name = f.name
1060                 if name in exclude:
1061                     continue
1062                 if f.unique:
1063                     unique_checks.append((model_class, (name,)))
1064                 if f.unique_for_date and f.unique_for_date not in exclude:
1065                     date_checks.append((model_class, 'date', name, f.unique_for_date))
1066                 if f.unique_for_year and f.unique_for_year not in exclude:
1067                     date_checks.append((model_class, 'year', name, f.unique_for_year))
1068                 if f.unique_for_month and f.unique_for_month not in exclude:
1069                     date_checks.append((model_class, 'month', name, f.unique_for_month))
1070         return unique_checks, date_checks
1071 
1072     def _perform_unique_checks(self, unique_checks):
1073         errors = {}
1074 
1075         for model_class, unique_check in unique_checks:
1076             # Try to look up an existing object with the same values as this
1077             # object's values for all the unique field.
1078 
1079             lookup_kwargs = {}
1080             for field_name in unique_check:
1081                 f = self._meta.get_field(field_name)
1082                 lookup_value = getattr(self, f.attname)
1083                 # TODO: Handle multiple backends with different feature flags.
1084                 if (lookup_value is None or
1085                         (lookup_value == '' and connection.features.interprets_empty_strings_as_nulls)):
1086                     # no value, skip the lookup
1087                     continue
1088                 if f.primary_key and not self._state.adding:
1089                     # no need to check for unique primary key when editing
1090                     continue
1091                 lookup_kwargs[str(field_name)] = lookup_value
1092 
1093             # some fields were skipped, no reason to do the check
1094             if len(unique_check) != len(lookup_kwargs):
1095                 continue
1096 
1097             qs = model_class._default_manager.filter(**lookup_kwargs)
1098 
1099             # Exclude the current object from the query if we are editing an
1100             # instance (as opposed to creating a new one)
1101             # Note that we need to use the pk as defined by model_class, not
1102             # self.pk. These can be different fields because model inheritance
1103             # allows single model to have effectively multiple primary keys.
1104             # Refs #17615.
1105             model_class_pk = self._get_pk_val(model_class._meta)
1106             if not self._state.adding and model_class_pk is not None:
1107                 qs = qs.exclude(pk=model_class_pk)
1108             if qs.exists():
1109                 if len(unique_check) == 1:
1110                     key = unique_check[0]
1111                 else:
1112                     key = NON_FIELD_ERRORS
1113                 errors.setdefault(key, []).append(self.unique_error_message(model_class, unique_check))
1114 
1115         return errors
1116 
1117     def _perform_date_checks(self, date_checks):
1118         errors = {}
1119         for model_class, lookup_type, field, unique_for in date_checks:
1120             lookup_kwargs = {}
1121             # there's a ticket to add a date lookup, we can remove this special
1122             # case if that makes it's way in
1123             date = getattr(self, unique_for)
1124             if date is None:
1125                 continue
1126             if lookup_type == 'date':
1127                 lookup_kwargs['%s__day' % unique_for] = date.day
1128                 lookup_kwargs['%s__month' % unique_for] = date.month
1129                 lookup_kwargs['%s__year' % unique_for] = date.year

1135             # Exclude the current object from the query if we are editing an
1136             # instance (as opposed to creating a new one)
1137             if not self._state.adding and self.pk is not None:
1138                 qs = qs.exclude(pk=self.pk)
1139 
1140             if qs.exists():
1141                 errors.setdefault(field, []).append(
1142                     self.date_error_message(lookup_type, field, unique_for)

1193     def full_clean(self, exclude=None, validate_unique=True):
1194         """
1195         Call clean_fields(), clean(), and validate_unique() on the model.
1196         Raise a ValidationError for any errors that occur.
1197         """
1198         errors = {}
1199         if exclude is None:
1200             exclude = []
1201         else:
1202             exclude = list(exclude)
1203 
1204         try:
1205             self.clean_fields(exclude=exclude)
1206         except ValidationError as e:
1207             errors = e.update_error_dict(errors)
1208 
1209         # Form.clean() is run even if other validation fails, so do the
1210         # same with Model.clean() for consistency.
1211         try:
1212             self.clean()
1213         except ValidationError as e:
1214             errors = e.update_error_dict(errors)
1215 
1216         # Run unique checks, but only for fields that passed validation.
1217         if validate_unique:
1218             for name in errors:
1219                 if name != NON_FIELD_ERRORS and name not in exclude:
1220                     exclude.append(name)
1221             try:
1222                 self.validate_unique(exclude=exclude)
1223             except ValidationError as e:
1224                 errors = e.update_error_dict(errors)
1225 
1226         if errors:
1227             raise ValidationError(errors)

1229     def clean_fields(self, exclude=None):
1230         """
1231         Clean all fields and raise a ValidationError containing a dict
1232         of all validation errors if any occur.
1233         """
1234         if exclude is None:
1235             exclude = []
1236 
1237         errors = {}
1238         for f in self._meta.fields:
1239             if f.name in exclude:
1240                 continue
1241             # Skip validation for empty fields with blank=True. The developer
1242             # is responsible for making sure they have a valid value.
1243             raw_value = getattr(self, f.attname)
1244             if f.blank and raw_value in f.empty_values:
1245                 continue
1246             try:
1247                 setattr(self, f.attname, f.clean(raw_value, self))
1248             except ValidationError as e:
1249                 errors[f.name] = e.error_list
1250 
1251         if errors:
1252             raise ValidationError(errors)

1392     @classmethod
1393     def _check_field_name_clashes(cls):
1394         """Forbid field shadowing in multi-table inheritance."""
1395         errors = []
1396         used_fields = {}  # name or attname -> field
1397 
1398         # Check that multi-inheritance doesn't cause field name shadowing.
1399         for parent in cls._meta.get_parent_list():
1400             for f in parent._meta.local_fields:
1401                 clash = used_fields.get(f.name) or used_fields.get(f.attname) or None
1402                 if clash:
1403                     errors.append(
1404                         checks.Error(
1405                             "The field '%s' from parent model "
1406                             "'%s' clashes with the field '%s' "
1407                             "from parent model '%s'." % (
1408                                 clash.name, clash.model._meta,
1409                                 f.name, f.model._meta
1410                             ),
1411                             obj=cls,
1412                             id='models.E005',
1413                         )
1414                     )
1415                 used_fields[f.name] = f
1416                 used_fields[f.attname] = f
1417 
1418         # Check that fields defined in the model don't clash with fields from
1419         # parents, including auto-generated fields like multi-table inheritance
1420         # child accessors.
1421         for parent in cls._meta.get_parent_list():
1422             for f in parent._meta.get_fields():
1423                 if f not in used_fields:
1424                     used_fields[f.name] = f
1425 
1426         for f in cls._meta.local_fields:
1427             clash = used_fields.get(f.name) or used_fields.get(f.attname) or None
1428             # Note that we may detect clash between user-defined non-unique
1429             # field "id" and automatically added unique field "id", both
1430             # defined at the same model. This special case is considered in
1431             # _check_id_field and here we ignore it.
1432             id_conflict = f.name == "id" and clash and clash.name == "id" and clash.model == cls
1433             if clash and not id_conflict:
1434                 errors.append(
1435                     checks.Error(
1436                         "The field '%s' clashes with the field '%s' "
1437                         "from model '%s'." % (
1438                             f.name, clash.name, clash.model._meta
1439                         ),
1440                         obj=f,
1441                         id='models.E006',
1442                     )
1443                 )
1444             used_fields[f.name] = f
1445             used_fields[f.attname] = f
1446 
1447         return errors

1665     @classmethod
1666     def _check_ordering(cls):
1667         """
1668         Check "ordering" option -- is it a list of strings and do all fields
1669         exist?
1670         """
1671         if cls._meta._ordering_clash:
1672             return [
1673                 checks.Error(
1674                     "'ordering' and 'order_with_respect_to' cannot be used together.",
1675                     obj=cls,
1676                     id='models.E021',
1677                 ),
1678             ]
1679 
1680         if cls._meta.order_with_respect_to or not cls._meta.ordering:
1681             return []
1682 
1683         if not isinstance(cls._meta.ordering, (list, tuple)):
1684             return [
1685                 checks.Error(
1686                     "'ordering' must be a tuple or list (even if you want to order by only one field).",
1687                     obj=cls,
1688                     id='models.E014',
1689                 )
1690             ]
1691 
1692         errors = []
1693         fields = cls._meta.ordering
1694 
1695         # Skip expressions and '?' fields.
1696         fields = (f for f in fields if isinstance(f, str) and f != '?')
1697 
1698         # Convert "-field" to "field".
1699         fields = ((f[1:] if f.startswith('-') else f) for f in fields)
1700 
1701         # Separate related fields and non-related fields.
1702         _fields = []
1703         related_fields = []
1704         for f in fields:
1705             if LOOKUP_SEP in f:
1706                 related_fields.append(f)
1707             else:
1708                 _fields.append(f)
1709         fields = _fields
1710 
1711         # Check related fields.
1712         for field in related_fields:
1713             _cls = cls
1714             fld = None
1715             for part in field.split(LOOKUP_SEP):
1716                 try:
1717                     # pk is an alias that won't be found by opts.get_field.
1718                     if part == 'pk':
1719                         fld = _cls._meta.pk
1720                     else:
1721                         fld = _cls._meta.get_field(part)
1722                     if fld.is_relation:
1723                         _cls = fld.get_path_info()[-1].to_opts.model
1724                     else:
1725                         _cls = None
1726                 except (FieldDoesNotExist, AttributeError):
1727                     if fld is None or fld.get_transform(part) is None:
1728                         errors.append(
1729                             checks.Error(
1730                                 "'ordering' refers to the nonexistent field, "
1731                                 "related field, or lookup '%s'." % field,
1732                                 obj=cls,
1733                                 id='models.E015',
1734                             )
1735                         )
1736 
1737         # Skip ordering on pk. This is always a valid order_by field
1738         # but is an alias and therefore won't be found by opts.get_field.
1739         fields = {f for f in fields if f != 'pk'}
1740 
1741         # Check for invalid or nonexistent fields in ordering.
1742         invalid_fields = []
1743 
1744         # Any field name that is not present in field_names does not exist.
1745         # Also, ordering by m2m fields is not allowed.
1746         opts = cls._meta
1747         valid_fields = set(chain.from_iterable(
1748             (f.name, f.attname) if not (f.auto_created and not f.concrete) else (f.field.related_query_name(),)
1749             for f in chain(opts.fields, opts.related_objects)
1750         ))
1751 
1752         invalid_fields.extend(fields - valid_fields)
1753 
1754         for invalid_field in invalid_fields:
1755             errors.append(
1756                 checks.Error(
1757                     "'ordering' refers to the nonexistent field, related "
1758                     "field, or lookup '%s'." % invalid_field,
1759                     obj=cls,
1760                     id='models.E015',
1761                 )
1762             )
1763         return errors

1765     @classmethod
1766     def _check_long_column_names(cls):
1767         """
1768         Check that any auto-generated column names are shorter than the limits
1769         for each database in which the model will be created.
1770         """
1771         errors = []
1772         allowed_len = None
1773         db_alias = None
1774 
1775         # Find the minimum max allowed length among all specified db_aliases.
1776         for db in settings.DATABASES:
1777             # skip databases where the model won't be created
1778             if not router.allow_migrate_model(db, cls):
1779                 continue
1780             connection = connections[db]
1781             max_name_length = connection.ops.max_name_length()
1782             if max_name_length is None or connection.features.truncates_names:
1783                 continue
1784             else:
1785                 if allowed_len is None:
1786                     allowed_len = max_name_length

39 def normalize_together(option_together):
40     """
41     option_together can be either a tuple of tuples, or a single
42     tuple of two strings. Normalize it to a tuple of tuples, so that
43     calling code can uniformly expect that.

46         if not option_together:

50         first_element = option_together[0]
51         if not isinstance(first_element, (tuple, list)):

57         # verbatim; this will be picked up by the check framework later.

Description
	
#29406 added the ability for the SECURE_REFERRER_POLICY setting to set Referrer-Policy, released in Django 3.0.
I propose we change the default for this to "same-origin" to make Django applications leak less information to third party sites.
The main risk of breakage here would be linked websites breaking, if they depend on verification through the Referer header. This is a pretty fragile technique since it can be spoofed.
Documentation: ​https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Referrer-Policy
The MDN support grid is out of date: ​https://caniuse.com/#search=Referrer-Policy

376         olds = {tuple(fields) for fields in old_unique_together}
377         news = {tuple(fields) for fields in new_unique_together}
378         # Deleted uniques
379         for fields in olds.difference(news):
380             self._delete_composed_index(model, fields, {'unique': True}, self.sql_delete_unique)
381         # Created uniques
382         for fields in news.difference(olds):
383             columns = [model._meta.get_field(field).column for field in fields]
384             self.execute(self._create_unique_sql(model, columns))
385 
386     def alter_index_together(self, model, old_index_together, new_index_together):
387         """
388         Deal with a model changing its index_together. The input
389         index_togethers must be doubly-nested, not the single-nested
390         ["foo", "bar"] format.
391         """
392         olds = {tuple(fields) for fields in old_index_together}
393         news = {tuple(fields) for fields in new_index_together}
394         # Deleted indexes
395         for fields in olds.difference(news):
396             self._delete_composed_index(model, fields, {'index': True}, self.sql_delete_index)
397         # Created indexes
398         for field_names in news.difference(olds):
399             fields = [model._meta.get_field(field) for field in field_names]
400             self.execute(self._create_index_sql(model, fields, suffix="_idx"))
401 
402     def _delete_composed_index(self, model, fields, constraint_kwargs, sql):
403         meta_constraint_names = {constraint.name for constraint in model._meta.constraints}
404         meta_index_names = {constraint.name for constraint in model._meta.indexes}
405         columns = [model._meta.get_field(field).column for field in fields]
406         constraint_names = self._constraint_names(
407             model, columns, exclude=meta_constraint_names | meta_index_names,
408             **constraint_kwargs
409         )
410         if len(constraint_names) != 1:
411             raise ValueError("Found wrong number (%s) of constraints for %s(%s)" % (
412                 len(constraint_names),
413                 model._meta.db_table,
414                 ", ".join(columns),
415             ))
416         self.execute(self._delete_constraint_sql(sql, model, constraint_names[0]))
417 
418     def alter_db_table(self, model, old_db_table, new_db_table):
419         """Rename the table a model points to."""
420         if (old_db_table == new_db_table or
421             (self.connection.features.ignores_table_name_case and
422                 old_db_table.lower() == new_db_table.lower())):
423             return
424         self.execute(self.sql_rename_table % {
425             "old_table": self.quote_name(old_db_table),
426             "new_table": self.quote_name(new_db_table),
427         })
428         # Rename all references to the old table name.
429         for sql in self.deferred_sql:
430             if isinstance(sql, Statement):
431                 sql.rename_table_references(old_db_table, new_db_table)
432 
433     def alter_db_tablespace(self, model, old_db_tablespace, new_db_tablespace):
434         """Move a model's table between tablespaces."""
435         self.execute(self.sql_retablespace_table % {
436             "table": self.quote_name(model._meta.db_table),
437             "old_tablespace": self.quote_name(old_db_tablespace),
438             "new_tablespace": self.quote_name(new_db_tablespace),
439         })
