339 class BaseModelForm(BaseForm):
340     def __init__(
341         self,
342         data=None,
343         files=None,
344         auto_id="id_%s",
345         prefix=None,
346         initial=None,
347         error_class=ErrorList,
348         label_suffix=None,
349         empty_permitted=False,
350         instance=None,
351         use_required_attribute=None,
352         renderer=None,
353     ):
354         opts = self._meta
355         if opts.model is None:
356             raise ValueError("ModelForm has no model class specified.")
357         if instance is None:
358             # if we didn't get an instance, instantiate a new one
359             self.instance = opts.model()
360             object_data = {}
361         else:
362             self.instance = instance
363             object_data = model_to_dict(instance, opts.fields, opts.exclude)
364         # if initial was provided, it should override the values from instance
365         if initial is not None:
366             object_data.update(initial)
367         # self._validate_unique will be set to True by BaseModelForm.clean().
368         # It is False by default so overriding self.clean() and failing to call
369         # super will stop validate_unique from being called.
370         self._validate_unique = False
371         super().__init__(
372             data,
373             files,
374             auto_id,
375             prefix,
376             object_data,
377             error_class,
378             label_suffix,
379             empty_permitted,
380             use_required_attribute=use_required_attribute,
381             renderer=renderer,
382         )
383         for formfield in self.fields.values():
384             apply_limit_choices_to_to_formfield(formfield)
385 
386     def _get_validation_exclusions(self):
387         """
388         For backwards-compatibility, exclude several types of fields from model
389         validation. See tickets #12507, #12521, #12553.
390         """
391         exclude = set()
392         # Build up a list of fields that should be excluded from model field
393         # validation and unique checks.
394         for f in self.instance._meta.fields:
395             field = f.name
396             # Exclude fields that aren't on the form. The developer may be
397             # adding these values to the model after form validation.
398             if field not in self.fields:
399                 exclude.add(f.name)
400 
401             # Don't perform model validation on fields that were defined
402             # manually on the form and excluded via the ModelForm's Meta
403             # class. See #12901.
404             elif self._meta.fields and field not in self._meta.fields:
405                 exclude.add(f.name)
406             elif self._meta.exclude and field in self._meta.exclude:
407                 exclude.add(f.name)
408 
409             # Exclude fields that failed form validation. There's no need for
410             # the model fields to validate them as well.
411             elif field in self._errors:
412                 exclude.add(f.name)
413 
414             # Exclude empty fields that are not required by the form, if the
415             # underlying model field is required. This keeps the model field
416             # from raising a required error. Note: don't exclude the field from
417             # validation if the model field allows blanks. If it does, the blank
418             # value may be included in a unique check, so cannot be excluded
419             # from validation.
420             else:
421                 form_field = self.fields[field]
422                 field_value = self.cleaned_data.get(field)
423                 if (
424                     not f.blank
425                     and not form_field.required
426                     and field_value in form_field.empty_values
427                 ):
428                     exclude.add(f.name)
429         return exclude
430 
431     def clean(self):
432         self._validate_unique = True
433         return self.cleaned_data
434 
435     def _update_errors(self, errors):
436         # Override any validation error messages defined at the model level
437         # with those defined at the form level.
438         opts = self._meta
439 
440         # Allow the model generated by construct_instance() to raise
441         # ValidationError and have them handled in the same way as others.
442         if hasattr(errors, "error_dict"):
443             error_dict = errors.error_dict
444         else:
445             error_dict = {NON_FIELD_ERRORS: errors}
446 
447         for field, messages in error_dict.items():
448             if (
449                 field == NON_FIELD_ERRORS
450                 and opts.error_messages
451                 and NON_FIELD_ERRORS in opts.error_messages
452             ):
453                 error_messages = opts.error_messages[NON_FIELD_ERRORS]
454             elif field in self.fields:
455                 error_messages = self.fields[field].error_messages
456             else:
457                 continue
458 
459             for message in messages:
460                 if (
461                     isinstance(message, ValidationError)
462                     and message.code in error_messages
463                 ):
464                     message.message = error_messages[message.code]
465 
466         self.add_error(None, errors)
467 
468     def _post_clean(self):
469         opts = self._meta
470 
471         exclude = self._get_validation_exclusions()
472 
473         # Foreign Keys being used to represent inline relationships
474         # are excluded from basic field value validation. This is for two
475         # reasons: firstly, the value may not be supplied (#12507; the
476         # case of providing new values to the admin); secondly the
477         # object being referred to may not yet fully exist (#12749).
478         # However, these fields *must* be included in uniqueness checks,
479         # so this can't be part of _get_validation_exclusions().
480         for name, field in self.fields.items():
481             if isinstance(field, InlineForeignKeyField):
482                 exclude.add(name)
483 
484         try:
485             self.instance = construct_instance(
486                 self, self.instance, opts.fields, opts.exclude
487             )
488         except ValidationError as e:
489             self._update_errors(e)
490 
491         try:
492             self.instance.full_clean(exclude=exclude, validate_unique=False)
493         except ValidationError as e:
494             self._update_errors(e)
495 
496         # Validate uniqueness if needed.
497         if self._validate_unique:
498             self.validate_unique()
499 
500     def validate_unique(self):
501         """
502         Call the instance's validate_unique() method and update the form's
503         validation errors if any were raised.
504         """
505         exclude = self._get_validation_exclusions()
506         try:
507             self.instance.validate_unique(exclude=exclude)
508         except ValidationError as e:
509             self._update_errors(e)
510 
511     def _save_m2m(self):
512         """
513         Save the many-to-many fields and generic relations for this form.
514         """
515         cleaned_data = self.cleaned_data
516         exclude = self._meta.exclude
517         fields = self._meta.fields
518         opts = self.instance._meta
519         # Note that for historical reasons we want to include also
520         # private_fields here. (GenericRelation was previously a fake
521         # m2m field).
522         for f in chain(opts.many_to_many, opts.private_fields):
523             if not hasattr(f, "save_form_data"):
524                 continue
525             if fields and f.name not in fields:
526                 continue
527             if exclude and f.name in exclude:
528                 continue
529             if f.name in cleaned_data:
530                 f.save_form_data(self.instance, cleaned_data[f.name])
531 
532     def save(self, commit=True):
533         """
534         Save this form's self.instance object if commit=True. Otherwise, add
535         a save_m2m() method to the form which can be called after the instance
536         is saved manually at a later time. Return the model instance.
537         """
538         if self.errors:
539             raise ValueError(
540                 "The %s could not be %s because the data didn't validate."
541                 % (
542                     self.instance._meta.object_name,
543                     "created" if self.instance._state.adding else "changed",
544                 )
545             )
546         if commit:
547             # If committing, save the instance and the m2m data immediately.
548             self.instance.save()
549             self._save_m2m()
550         else:
551             # If not committing, add a method to the form to allow deferred
552             # saving of m2m data.
553             self.save_m2m = self._save_m2m
554         return self.instance
555 
556     save.alters_data = True
557

563 def modelform_factory(
564     model,
565     form=ModelForm,
566     fields=None,
567     exclude=None,
568     formfield_callback=None,
569     widgets=None,
570     localized_fields=None,
571     labels=None,
572     help_texts=None,
573     error_messages=None,
574     field_classes=None,
575 ):
576     """
577     Return a ModelForm containing form fields for the given model. You can
578     optionally pass a `form` argument to use as a starting point for
579     constructing the ModelForm.
580 
581     ``fields`` is an optional list of field names. If provided, include only
582     the named fields in the returned fields. If omitted or '__all__', use all
583     fields.
584 
585     ``exclude`` is an optional list of field names. If provided, exclude the
586     named fields from the returned fields, even if they are listed in the
587     ``fields`` argument.
588 
589     ``widgets`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a widget.
590 
591     ``localized_fields`` is a list of names of fields which should be localized.
592 
593     ``formfield_callback`` is a callable that takes a model field and returns
594     a form field.
595 
596     ``labels`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a label.
597 
598     ``help_texts`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a help text.
599 
600     ``error_messages`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a
601     dictionary of error messages.
602 
603     ``field_classes`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a form
604     field class.
605     """
606     # Create the inner Meta class. FIXME: ideally, we should be able to
607     # construct a ModelForm without creating and passing in a temporary
608     # inner class.
609 
610     # Build up a list of attributes that the Meta object will have.
611     attrs = {"model": model}
612     if fields is not None:
613         attrs["fields"] = fields
614     if exclude is not None:
615         attrs["exclude"] = exclude
616     if widgets is not None:
617         attrs["widgets"] = widgets
618     if localized_fields is not None:
619         attrs["localized_fields"] = localized_fields
620     if labels is not None:
621         attrs["labels"] = labels
622     if help_texts is not None:
623         attrs["help_texts"] = help_texts
624     if error_messages is not None:
625         attrs["error_messages"] = error_messages
626     if field_classes is not None:
627         attrs["field_classes"] = field_classes
628 
629     # If parent form class already has an inner Meta, the Meta we're
630     # creating needs to inherit from the parent's inner meta.
631     bases = (form.Meta,) if hasattr(form, "Meta") else ()
632     Meta = type("Meta", bases, attrs)
633     if formfield_callback:
634         Meta.formfield_callback = staticmethod(formfield_callback)
635     # Give this new form class a reasonable name.
636     class_name = model.__name__ + "Form"
637 
638     # Class attributes for the new form class.
639     form_class_attrs = {"Meta": Meta, "formfield_callback": formfield_callback}
640 
641     if getattr(Meta, "fields", None) is None and getattr(Meta, "exclude", None) is None:
642         raise ImproperlyConfigured(
643             "Calling modelform_factory without defining 'fields' or "
644             "'exclude' explicitly is prohibited."
645         )
646 
647     # Instantiate type(form) in order to use the same metaclass as form.
648     return type(form)(class_name, (form,), form_class_attrs)

654 class BaseModelFormSet(BaseFormSet):
655     """
656     A ``FormSet`` for editing a queryset and/or adding new objects to it.
657     """
658 
659     model = None
660     edit_only = False
661 
662     # Set of fields that must be unique among forms of this set.
663     unique_fields = set()
664 
665     def __init__(
666         self,
667         data=None,
668         files=None,
669         auto_id="id_%s",
670         prefix=None,
671         queryset=None,
672         *,
673         initial=None,
674         **kwargs,
675     ):
676         self.queryset = queryset
677         self.initial_extra = initial
678         super().__init__(
679             **{
680                 "data": data,
681                 "files": files,
682                 "auto_id": auto_id,
683                 "prefix": prefix,
684                 **kwargs,
685             }
686         )
687 
688     def initial_form_count(self):
689         """Return the number of forms that are required in this FormSet."""
690         if not self.is_bound:
691             return len(self.get_queryset())
692         return super().initial_form_count()
693 
694     def _existing_object(self, pk):
695         if not hasattr(self, "_object_dict"):
696             self._object_dict = {o.pk: o for o in self.get_queryset()}
697         return self._object_dict.get(pk)
698 
699     def _get_to_python(self, field):
700         """
701         If the field is a related field, fetch the concrete field's (that
702         is, the ultimate pointed-to field's) to_python.
703         """
704         while field.remote_field is not None:
705             field = field.remote_field.get_related_field()
706         return field.to_python
707 
708     def _construct_form(self, i, **kwargs):
709         pk_required = i < self.initial_form_count()
710         if pk_required:
711             if self.is_bound:
712                 pk_key = "%s-%s" % (self.add_prefix(i), self.model._meta.pk.name)
713                 try:
714                     pk = self.data[pk_key]
715                 except KeyError:
716                     # The primary key is missing. The user may have tampered
717                     # with POST data.
718                     pass
719                 else:
720                     to_python = self._get_to_python(self.model._meta.pk)
721                     try:
722                         pk = to_python(pk)
723                     except ValidationError:
724                         # The primary key exists but is an invalid value. The
725                         # user may have tampered with POST data.
726                         pass
727                     else:
728                         kwargs["instance"] = self._existing_object(pk)
729             else:
730                 kwargs["instance"] = self.get_queryset()[i]
731         elif self.initial_extra:
732             # Set initial values for extra forms
733             try:
734                 kwargs["initial"] = self.initial_extra[i - self.initial_form_count()]
735             except IndexError:
736                 pass
737         form = super()._construct_form(i, **kwargs)
738         if pk_required:
739             form.fields[self.model._meta.pk.name].required = True
740         return form
741

785

797     def validate_unique(self):
798         # Collect unique_checks and date_checks to run from all the forms.
799         all_unique_checks = set()
800         all_date_checks = set()
801         forms_to_delete = self.deleted_forms
802         valid_forms = [
803             form
804             for form in self.forms
805             if form.is_valid() and form not in forms_to_delete
806         ]
807         for form in valid_forms:
808             exclude = form._get_validation_exclusions()
809             unique_checks, date_checks = form.instance._get_unique_checks(
810                 exclude=exclude,
811                 include_meta_constraints=True,
812             )
813             all_unique_checks.update(unique_checks)
814             all_date_checks.update(date_checks)
815 
816         errors = []
817         # Do each of the unique checks (unique and unique_together)
818         for uclass, unique_check in all_unique_checks:
819             seen_data = set()
820             for form in valid_forms:
821                 # Get the data for the set of fields that must be unique among
822                 # the forms.
823                 row_data = (
824                     field if field in self.unique_fields else form.cleaned_data[field]
825                     for field in unique_check
826                     if field in form.cleaned_data
827                 )
828                 # Reduce Model instances to their primary key values
829                 row_data = tuple(
830                     d._get_pk_val() if hasattr(d, "_get_pk_val")
831                     # Prevent "unhashable type: list" errors later on.
832                     else tuple(d) if isinstance(d, list) else d
833                     for d in row_data
834                 )
835                 if row_data and None not in row_data:
836                     # if we've already seen it then we have a uniqueness failure
837                     if row_data in seen_data:
838                         # poke error messages into the right places and mark
839                         # the form as invalid
840                         errors.append(self.get_unique_error_message(unique_check))
841                         form._errors[NON_FIELD_ERRORS] = self.error_class(
842                             [self.get_form_error()],
843                             renderer=self.renderer,
844                         )
845                         # Remove the data from the cleaned_data dict since it
846                         # was invalid.
847                         for field in unique_check:
848                             if field in form.cleaned_data:
849                                 del form.cleaned_data[field]
850                     # mark the data as seen
851                     seen_data.add(row_data)
852         # iterate over each of the date checks now
853         for date_check in all_date_checks:
854             seen_data = set()
855             uclass, lookup, field, unique_for = date_check
856             for form in valid_forms:
857                 # see if we have data for both fields
858                 if (
859                     form.cleaned_data
860                     and form.cleaned_data[field] is not None
861                     and form.cleaned_data[unique_for] is not None
862                 ):
863                     # if it's a date lookup we need to get the data for all the fields
864                     if lookup == "date":
865                         date = form.cleaned_data[unique_for]
866                         date_data = (date.year, date.month, date.day)
867                     # otherwise it's just the attribute on the date/datetime
868                     # object
869                     else:
870                         date_data = (getattr(form.cleaned_data[unique_for], lookup),)
871                     data = (form.cleaned_data[field],) + date_data
872                     # if we've already seen it then we have a uniqueness failure
873                     if data in seen_data:
874                         # poke error messages into the right places and mark
875                         # the form as invalid
876                         errors.append(self.get_date_error_message(date_check))
877                         form._errors[NON_FIELD_ERRORS] = self.error_class(
878                             [self.get_form_error()],
879                             renderer=self.renderer,
880                         )
881                         # Remove the data from the cleaned_data dict since it
882                         # was invalid.
883                         del form.cleaned_data[field]
884                     # mark the data as seen
885                     seen_data.add(data)
886 
887         if errors:
888             raise ValidationError(errors)
889 
890     def get_unique_error_message(self, unique_check):
891         if len(unique_check) == 1:
892             return gettext("Please correct the duplicate data for %(field)s.") % {
893                 "field": unique_check[0],
894             }
895         else:
896             return gettext(
897                 "Please correct the duplicate data for %(field)s, which must be unique."
898             ) % {
899                 "field": get_text_list(unique_check, _("and")),
900             }
901 
902     def get_date_error_message(self, date_check):
903         return gettext(
904             "Please correct the duplicate data for %(field_name)s "
905             "which must be unique for the %(lookup)s in %(date_field)s."
906         ) % {
907             "field_name": date_check[2],
908             "date_field": date_check[3],
909             "lookup": str(date_check[1]),
910         }
911 
912     def get_form_error(self):
913         return gettext("Please correct the duplicate values below.")

915     def save_existing_objects(self, commit=True):
916         self.changed_objects = []
917         self.deleted_objects = []
918         if not self.initial_forms:
919             return []
920 
921         saved_instances = []
922         forms_to_delete = self.deleted_forms
923         for form in self.initial_forms:
924             obj = form.instance
925             # If the pk is None, it means either:
926             # 1. The object is an unexpected empty model, created by invalid
927             #    POST data such as an object outside the formset's queryset.
928             # 2. The object was already deleted from the database.
929             if obj.pk is None:
930                 continue
931             if form in forms_to_delete:
932                 self.deleted_objects.append(obj)
933                 self.delete_existing(obj, commit=commit)
934             elif form.has_changed():
935                 self.changed_objects.append((obj, form.changed_data))
936                 saved_instances.append(self.save_existing(form, obj, commit=commit))
937                 if not commit:
938                     self.saved_forms.append(form)
939         return saved_instances
940 
941     def save_new_objects(self, commit=True):
942         self.new_objects = []
943         for form in self.extra_forms:
944             if not form.has_changed():
945                 continue
946             # If someone has marked an add form for deletion, don't save the
947             # object.
948             if self.can_delete and self._should_delete_form(form):
949                 continue
950             self.new_objects.append(self.save_new(form, commit=commit))
951             if not commit:
952                 self.saved_forms.append(form)
953         return self.new_objects

955     def add_fields(self, form, index):
956         """Add a hidden field for the object's primary key."""
957         from django.db.models import AutoField, ForeignKey, OneToOneField
958 
959         self._pk_field = pk = self.model._meta.pk
960         # If a pk isn't editable, then it won't be on the form, so we need to
961         # add it here so we can tell which object is which when we get the
962         # data back. Generally, pk.editable should be false, but for some
963         # reason, auto_created pk fields and AutoField's editable attribute is
964         # True, so check for that as well.
965 
966         def pk_is_not_editable(pk):
967             return (
968                 (not pk.editable)
969                 or (pk.auto_created or isinstance(pk, AutoField))
970                 or (
971                     pk.remote_field
972                     and pk.remote_field.parent_link
973                     and pk_is_not_editable(pk.remote_field.model._meta.pk)
974                 )
975             )
976 
977         if pk_is_not_editable(pk) or pk.name not in form.fields:
978             if form.is_bound:
979                 # If we're adding the related instance, ignore its primary key
980                 # as it could be an auto-generated default which isn't actually
981                 # in the database.
982                 pk_value = None if form.instance._state.adding else form.instance.pk
983             else:
984                 try:
985                     if index is not None:
986                         pk_value = self.get_queryset()[index].pk
987                     else:
988                         pk_value = None
989                 except IndexError:
990                     pk_value = None
991             if isinstance(pk, (ForeignKey, OneToOneField)):
992                 qs = pk.remote_field.model._default_manager.get_queryset()
993             else:
994                 qs = self.model._default_manager.get_queryset()
995             qs = qs.using(form.instance._state.db)
996             if form._meta.widgets:
997                 widget = form._meta.widgets.get(self._pk_field.name, HiddenInput)
998             else:
999                 widget = HiddenInput
1000             form.fields[self._pk_field.name] = ModelChoiceField(
1001                 qs, initial=pk_value, required=False, widget=widget
1002             )
1003         super().add_fields(form, index)

1077 class BaseInlineFormSet(BaseModelFormSet):
1078     """A formset for child objects related to a parent."""
1079 
1080     def __init__(
1081         self,
1082         data=None,
1083         files=None,
1084         instance=None,
1085         save_as_new=False,
1086         prefix=None,
1087         queryset=None,
1088         **kwargs,
1089     ):
1090         if instance is None:
1091             self.instance = self.fk.remote_field.model()
1092         else:
1093             self.instance = instance
1094         self.save_as_new = save_as_new
1095         if queryset is None:
1096             queryset = self.model._default_manager
1097         if self.instance.pk is not None:
1098             qs = queryset.filter(**{self.fk.name: self.instance})
1099         else:
1100             qs = queryset.none()
1101         self.unique_fields = {self.fk.name}
1102         super().__init__(data, files, prefix=prefix, queryset=qs, **kwargs)
1103 
1104         # Add the generated field to form._meta.fields if it's defined to make
1105         # sure validation isn't skipped on that field.
1106         if self.form._meta.fields and self.fk.name not in self.form._meta.fields:
1107             if isinstance(self.form._meta.fields, tuple):
1108                 self.form._meta.fields = list(self.form._meta.fields)
1109             self.form._meta.fields.append(self.fk.name)
1110 
1111     def initial_form_count(self):
1112         if self.save_as_new:
1113             return 0
1114         return super().initial_form_count()
1115 
1116     def _construct_form(self, i, **kwargs):
1117         form = super()._construct_form(i, **kwargs)
1118         if self.save_as_new:
1119             mutable = getattr(form.data, "_mutable", None)
1120             # Allow modifying an immutable QueryDict.
1121             if mutable is not None:
1122                 form.data._mutable = True
1123             # Remove the primary key from the form's data, we are only
1124             # creating new instances
1125             form.data[form.add_prefix(self._pk_field.name)] = None
1126             # Remove the foreign key from the form's data
1127             form.data[form.add_prefix(self.fk.name)] = None
1128             if mutable is not None:
1129                 form.data._mutable = mutable
1130 
1131         # Set the fk value here so that the form can do its validation.
1132         fk_value = self.instance.pk
1133         if self.fk.remote_field.field_name != self.fk.remote_field.model._meta.pk.name:
1134             fk_value = getattr(self.instance, self.fk.remote_field.field_name)
1135             fk_value = getattr(fk_value, "pk", fk_value)
1136         setattr(form.instance, self.fk.get_attname(), fk_value)
1137         return form
1138 
1139     @classmethod
1140     def get_default_prefix(cls):
1141         return cls.fk.remote_field.get_accessor_name(model=cls.model).replace("+", "")
1142 
1143     def save_new(self, form, commit=True):
1144         # Ensure the latest copy of the related instance is present on each
1145         # form (it may have been saved after the formset was originally
1146         # instantiated).
1147         setattr(form.instance, self.fk.name, self.instance)
1148         return super().save_new(form, commit=commit)
1149 
1150     def add_fields(self, form, index):
1151         super().add_fields(form, index)
1152         if self._pk_field == self.fk:
1153             name = self._pk_field.name
1154             kwargs = {"pk_field": True}
1155         else:
1156             # The foreign key field might not be on the form, so we poke at the
1157             # Model field to get the label, since we need that for error messages.
1158             name = self.fk.name
1159             kwargs = {
1160                 "label": getattr(
1161                     form.fields.get(name), "label", capfirst(self.fk.verbose_name)
1162                 )
1163             }
1164 
1165         # The InlineForeignKeyField assumes that the foreign key relation is
1166         # based on the parent model's pk. If this isn't the case, set to_field
1167         # to correctly resolve the initial form value.
1168         if self.fk.remote_field.field_name != self.fk.remote_field.model._meta.pk.name:
1169             kwargs["to_field"] = self.fk.remote_field.field_name
1170 
1171         # If we're adding a new object, ignore a parent's auto-generated key
1172         # as it will be regenerated on the save request.
1173         if self.instance._state.adding:
1174             if kwargs.get("to_field") is not None:
1175                 to_field = self.instance._meta.get_field(kwargs["to_field"])
1176             else:
1177                 to_field = self.instance._meta.pk
1178             if to_field.has_default():
1179                 setattr(self.instance, to_field.attname, None)
1180 
1181         form.fields[name] = InlineForeignKeyField(self.instance, **kwargs)
1182 
1183     def get_unique_error_message(self, unique_check):
1184         unique_check = [field for field in unique_check if field != self.fk.name]
1185         return super().get_unique_error_message(unique_check)

1188 def _get_foreign_key(parent_model, model, fk_name=None, can_fail=False):
1189     """
1190     Find and return the ForeignKey from model to parent if there is one
1191     (return None if can_fail is True and no such field exists). If fk_name is
1192     provided, assume it is the name of the ForeignKey field. Unless can_fail is
1193     True, raise an exception if there isn't a ForeignKey from model to
1194     parent_model.
1195     """
1196     # avoid circular import
1197     from django.db.models import ForeignKey
1198 
1199     opts = model._meta
1200     if fk_name:
1201         fks_to_parent = [f for f in opts.fields if f.name == fk_name]
1202         if len(fks_to_parent) == 1:
1203             fk = fks_to_parent[0]
1204             parent_list = parent_model._meta.get_parent_list()
1205             if (
1206                 not isinstance(fk, ForeignKey)
1207                 or (
1208                     # ForeignKey to proxy models.
1209                     fk.remote_field.model._meta.proxy
1210                     and fk.remote_field.model._meta.proxy_for_model not in parent_list
1211                 )
1212                 or (
1213                     # ForeignKey to concrete models.
1214                     not fk.remote_field.model._meta.proxy
1215                     and fk.remote_field.model != parent_model
1216                     and fk.remote_field.model not in parent_list
1217                 )
1218             ):
1219                 raise ValueError(
1220                     "fk_name '%s' is not a ForeignKey to '%s'."
1221                     % (fk_name, parent_model._meta.label)
1222                 )
1223         elif not fks_to_parent:
1224             raise ValueError(
1225                 "'%s' has no field named '%s'." % (model._meta.label, fk_name)
1226             )
1227     else:
1228         # Try to discover what the ForeignKey from model to parent_model is
1229         parent_list = parent_model._meta.get_parent_list()
1230         fks_to_parent = [
1231             f
1232             for f in opts.fields
1233             if isinstance(f, ForeignKey)
1234             and (
1235                 f.remote_field.model == parent_model
1236                 or f.remote_field.model in parent_list
1237                 or (
1238                     f.remote_field.model._meta.proxy
1239                     and f.remote_field.model._meta.proxy_for_model in parent_list
1240                 )
1241             )
1242         ]
1243         if len(fks_to_parent) == 1:
1244             fk = fks_to_parent[0]
1245         elif not fks_to_parent:
1246             if can_fail:
1247                 return
1248             raise ValueError(
1249                 "'%s' has no ForeignKey to '%s'."
1250                 % (
1251                     model._meta.label,
1252                     parent_model._meta.label,
1253                 )
1254             )
1255         else:
1256             raise ValueError(
1257                 "'%s' has more than one ForeignKey to '%s'. You must specify "
1258                 "a 'fk_name' attribute."
1259                 % (
1260                     model._meta.label,
1261                     parent_model._meta.label,
1262                 )
1263             )
1264     return fk
1265

328             source for source in self.get_source_fields() if source is not None

335                         "set output_field."

600 def register_combinable_fields(lhs, connector, rhs, result):
601     """
602     Register combinable types:
603         lhs <connector> rhs -> result
604     e.g.
605         register_combinable_fields(
606             IntegerField, Combinable.ADD, FloatField, FloatField
607         )
608     """
609     _connector_combinators[connector].append((lhs, rhs, result))

619 def _resolve_combined_type(connector, lhs_type, rhs_type):

622         if issubclass(lhs_type, combinator_lhs_type) and issubclass(
623             rhs_type, combinator_rhs_type

628 class CombinedExpression(SQLiteNumericMixin, Expression):
629     def __init__(self, lhs, connector, rhs, output_field=None):
630         super().__init__(output_field=output_field)
631         self.connector = connector
632         self.lhs = lhs
633         self.rhs = rhs
634 
635     def __repr__(self):
636         return "<{}: {}>".format(self.__class__.__name__, self)
637 
638     def __str__(self):
639         return "{} {} {}".format(self.lhs, self.connector, self.rhs)
640 
641     def get_source_expressions(self):
642         return [self.lhs, self.rhs]
643 
644     def set_source_expressions(self, exprs):
645         self.lhs, self.rhs = exprs
646 
647     def _resolve_output_field(self):
648         # We avoid using super() here for reasons given in
649         # Expression._resolve_output_field()
650         combined_type = _resolve_combined_type(
651             self.connector,
652             type(self.lhs._output_field_or_none),
653             type(self.rhs._output_field_or_none),
654         )
655         if combined_type is None:
656             raise FieldError(
657                 f"Cannot infer type of {self.connector!r} expression involving these "
658                 f"types: {self.lhs.output_field.__class__.__name__}, "
659                 f"{self.rhs.output_field.__class__.__name__}. You must set "
660                 f"output_field."
661             )
662         return combined_type()
663 
664     def as_sql(self, compiler, connection):
665         expressions = []
666         expression_params = []
667         sql, params = compiler.compile(self.lhs)
668         expressions.append(sql)
669         expression_params.extend(params)
670         sql, params = compiler.compile(self.rhs)
671         expressions.append(sql)
672         expression_params.extend(params)
673         # order of precedence
674         expression_wrapper = "(%s)"
675         sql = connection.ops.combine_expression(self.connector, expressions)
676         return expression_wrapper % sql, expression_params
677 
678     def resolve_expression(
679         self, query=None, allow_joins=True, reuse=None, summarize=False, for_save=False
680     ):
681         lhs = self.lhs.resolve_expression(
682             query, allow_joins, reuse, summarize, for_save
683         )
684         rhs = self.rhs.resolve_expression(
685             query, allow_joins, reuse, summarize, for_save
686         )
687         if not isinstance(self, (DurationExpression, TemporalSubtraction)):
688             try:
689                 lhs_type = lhs.output_field.get_internal_type()
690             except (AttributeError, FieldError):
691                 lhs_type = None
692             try:
693                 rhs_type = rhs.output_field.get_internal_type()
694             except (AttributeError, FieldError):
695                 rhs_type = None
696             if "DurationField" in {lhs_type, rhs_type} and lhs_type != rhs_type:
697                 return DurationExpression(
698                     self.lhs, self.connector, self.rhs
699                 ).resolve_expression(
700                     query,
701                     allow_joins,
702                     reuse,
703                     summarize,
704                     for_save,
705                 )
706             datetime_fields = {"DateField", "DateTimeField", "TimeField"}
707             if (
708                 self.connector == self.SUB
709                 and lhs_type in datetime_fields
710                 and lhs_type == rhs_type
711             ):
712                 return TemporalSubtraction(self.lhs, self.rhs).resolve_expression(
713                     query,
714                     allow_joins,
715                     reuse,
716                     summarize,
717                     for_save,
718                 )
719         c = self.copy()
720         c.is_summary = summarize
721         c.lhs = lhs
722         c.rhs = rhs
723         return c

726 class DurationExpression(CombinedExpression):
727     def compile(self, side, compiler, connection):
728         try:
729             output = side.output_field
730         except FieldError:
731             pass
732         else:
733             if output.get_internal_type() == "DurationField":
734                 sql, params = compiler.compile(side)
735                 return connection.ops.format_for_duration_arithmetic(sql), params
736         return compiler.compile(side)
737 
738     def as_sql(self, compiler, connection):
739         if connection.features.has_native_duration_field:
740             return super().as_sql(compiler, connection)
741         connection.ops.check_expression_support(self)
742         expressions = []
743         expression_params = []
744         sql, params = self.compile(self.lhs, compiler, connection)
745         expressions.append(sql)
746         expression_params.extend(params)
747         sql, params = self.compile(self.rhs, compiler, connection)
748         expressions.append(sql)
749         expression_params.extend(params)
750         # order of precedence
751         expression_wrapper = "(%s)"
752         sql = connection.ops.combine_duration_expression(self.connector, expressions)
753         return expression_wrapper % sql, expression_params
754 
755     def as_sqlite(self, compiler, connection, **extra_context):
756         sql, params = self.as_sql(compiler, connection, **extra_context)
757         if self.connector in {Combinable.MUL, Combinable.DIV}:
758             try:
759                 lhs_type = self.lhs.output_field.get_internal_type()
760                 rhs_type = self.rhs.output_field.get_internal_type()
761             except (AttributeError, FieldError):
762                 pass
763             else:
764                 allowed_fields = {
765                     "DecimalField",
766                     "DurationField",
767                     "FloatField",
768                     "IntegerField",
769                 }
770                 if lhs_type not in allowed_fields or rhs_type not in allowed_fields:
771                     raise DatabaseError(
772                         f"Invalid arguments for operator {self.connector}."
773                     )
774         return sql, params

871 class Func(SQLiteNumericMixin, Expression):
872     """An SQL function call."""

874     function = None

876     arg_joiner = ", "
877     arity = None  # The number of arguments the function accepts.
878 
879     def __init__(self, *expressions, output_field=None, **extra):
880         if self.arity is not None and len(expressions) != self.arity:
881             raise TypeError(
882                 "'%s' takes exactly %s %s (%s given)"
883                 % (
884                     self.__class__.__name__,
885                     self.arity,
886                     "argument" if self.arity == 1 else "arguments",
887                     len(expressions),
888                 )
889             )
890         super().__init__(output_field=output_field)
891         self.source_expressions = self._parse_expressions(*expressions)
892         self.extra = extra
893 
894     def __repr__(self):
895         args = self.arg_joiner.join(str(arg) for arg in self.source_expressions)
896         extra = {**self.extra, **self._get_repr_options()}
897         if extra:
898             extra = ", ".join(
899                 str(key) + "=" + str(val) for key, val in sorted(extra.items())
900             )
901             return "{}({}, {})".format(self.__class__.__name__, args, extra)
902         return "{}({})".format(self.__class__.__name__, args)
903 
904     def _get_repr_options(self):
905         """Return a dict of extra __init__() options to include in the repr."""
906         return {}
907

909         return self.source_expressions
910

912         self.source_expressions = exprs

915         self, query=None, allow_joins=True, reuse=None, summarize=False, for_save=False
916     ):
917         c = self.copy()
918         c.is_summary = summarize
919         for pos, arg in enumerate(c.source_expressions):
920             c.source_expressions[pos] = arg.resolve_expression(
921                 query, allow_joins, reuse, summarize, for_save
922             )
923         return c
924 
925     def as_sql(
926         self,
927         compiler,
928         connection,
929         function=None,
930         template=None,
931         arg_joiner=None,
932         **extra_context,
933     ):
934         connection.ops.check_expression_support(self)
935         sql_parts = []
936         params = []
937         for arg in self.source_expressions:
938             try:
939                 arg_sql, arg_params = compiler.compile(arg)
940             except EmptyResultSet:
941                 empty_result_set_value = getattr(
942                     arg, "empty_result_set_value", NotImplemented
943                 )
944                 if empty_result_set_value is NotImplemented:
945                     raise
946                 arg_sql, arg_params = compiler.compile(Value(empty_result_set_value))
947             sql_parts.append(arg_sql)
948             params.extend(arg_params)
949         data = {**self.extra, **extra_context}
950         # Use the first supplied value in this order: the parameter to this
951         # method, a value supplied in __init__()'s **extra (the value in
952         # `data`), or the value defined on the class.
953         if function is not None:
954             data["function"] = function
955         else:
956             data.setdefault("function", self.function)
957         template = template or data.get("template", self.template)
958         arg_joiner = arg_joiner or data.get("arg_joiner", self.arg_joiner)
959         data["expressions"] = data["field"] = arg_joiner.join(sql_parts)
960         return template % data, params
961 
962     def copy(self):
963         copy = super().copy()
964         copy.source_expressions = self.source_expressions[:]
965         copy.extra = self.extra.copy()
966         return copy

4 When a field defines a relation between two models, each model class provides

341         if self.field.primary_key and self.field.remote_field.parent_link:
342             opts = instance._meta
343             # Inherited primary key fields from this object's base classes.
344             inherited_pk_fields = [
345                 field
346                 for field in opts.concrete_fields
347                 if field.primary_key and field.remote_field
348             ]
349             for field in inherited_pk_fields:
350                 rel_model_pk_name = field.remote_field.model._meta.pk.attname
351                 raw_value = (
352                     getattr(value, rel_model_pk_name) if value is not None else None
353                 )
354                 setattr(instance, rel_model_pk_name, raw_value)

357 class ReverseOneToOneDescriptor:
358     """
359     Accessor to the related object on the reverse side of a one-to-one
360     relation.
361 
362     In the example::
363 
364         class Restaurant(Model):
365             place = OneToOneField(Place, related_name='restaurant')
366 
367     ``Place.restaurant`` is a ``ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`` instance.
368     """
369 
370     def __init__(self, related):
371         # Following the example above, `related` is an instance of OneToOneRel
372         # which represents the reverse restaurant field (place.restaurant).
373         self.related = related
374 
375     @cached_property
376     def RelatedObjectDoesNotExist(self):
377         # The exception isn't created at initialization time for the sake of
378         # consistency with `ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`.
379         return type(
380             "RelatedObjectDoesNotExist",
381             (self.related.related_model.DoesNotExist, AttributeError),
382             {
383                 "__module__": self.related.model.__module__,
384                 "__qualname__": "%s.%s.RelatedObjectDoesNotExist"
385                 % (
386                     self.related.model.__qualname__,
387                     self.related.name,
388                 ),
389             },
390         )
391 
392     def is_cached(self, instance):
393         return self.related.is_cached(instance)
394 
395     def get_queryset(self, **hints):
396         return self.related.related_model._base_manager.db_manager(hints=hints).all()
397 
398     def get_prefetch_queryset(self, instances, queryset=None):
399         if queryset is None:
400             queryset = self.get_queryset()
401         queryset._add_hints(instance=instances[0])
402 
403         rel_obj_attr = self.related.field.get_local_related_value
404         instance_attr = self.related.field.get_foreign_related_value
405         instances_dict = {instance_attr(inst): inst for inst in instances}
406         query = {"%s__in" % self.related.field.name: instances}
407         queryset = queryset.filter(**query)
408 
409         # Since we're going to assign directly in the cache,
410         # we must manage the reverse relation cache manually.
411         for rel_obj in queryset:
412             instance = instances_dict[rel_obj_attr(rel_obj)]
413             self.related.field.set_cached_value(rel_obj, instance)
414         return (
415             queryset,
416             rel_obj_attr,
417             instance_attr,
418             True,
419             self.related.get_cache_name(),
420             False,
421         )
422 
423     def __get__(self, instance, cls=None):
424         """
425         Get the related instance through the reverse relation.
426 
427         With the example above, when getting ``place.restaurant``:
428 
429         - ``self`` is the descriptor managing the ``restaurant`` attribute
430         - ``instance`` is the ``place`` instance
431         - ``cls`` is the ``Place`` class (unused)
432 
433         Keep in mind that ``Restaurant`` holds the foreign key to ``Place``.
434         """
435         if instance is None:
436             return self
437 
438         # The related instance is loaded from the database and then cached
439         # by the field on the model instance state. It can also be pre-cached
440         # by the forward accessor (ForwardManyToOneDescriptor).
441         try:
442             rel_obj = self.related.get_cached_value(instance)
443         except KeyError:
444             related_pk = instance.pk
445             if related_pk is None:
446                 rel_obj = None
447             else:
448                 filter_args = self.related.field.get_forward_related_filter(instance)
449                 try:
450                     rel_obj = self.get_queryset(instance=instance).get(**filter_args)
451                 except self.related.related_model.DoesNotExist:
452                     rel_obj = None
453                 else:
454                     # Set the forward accessor cache on the related object to
455                     # the current instance to avoid an extra SQL query if it's
456                     # accessed later on.
457                     self.related.field.set_cached_value(rel_obj, instance)
458             self.related.set_cached_value(instance, rel_obj)
459 
460         if rel_obj is None:
461             raise self.RelatedObjectDoesNotExist(
462                 "%s has no %s."
463                 % (instance.__class__.__name__, self.related.get_accessor_name())
464             )
465         else:
466             return rel_obj
467 
468     def __set__(self, instance, value):
469         """
470         Set the related instance through the reverse relation.
471 
472         With the example above, when setting ``place.restaurant = restaurant``:
473 
474         - ``self`` is the descriptor managing the ``restaurant`` attribute
475         - ``instance`` is the ``place`` instance
476         - ``value`` is the ``restaurant`` instance on the right of the equal sign
477 
478         Keep in mind that ``Restaurant`` holds the foreign key to ``Place``.
479         """
480         # The similarity of the code below to the code in
481         # ForwardManyToOneDescriptor is annoying, but there's a bunch
482         # of small differences that would make a common base class convoluted.
483 
484         if value is None:
485             # Update the cached related instance (if any) & clear the cache.
486             # Following the example above, this would be the cached
487             # ``restaurant`` instance (if any).
488             rel_obj = self.related.get_cached_value(instance, default=None)
489             if rel_obj is not None:
490                 # Remove the ``restaurant`` instance from the ``place``
491                 # instance cache.
492                 self.related.delete_cached_value(instance)
493                 # Set the ``place`` field on the ``restaurant``
494                 # instance to None.
495                 setattr(rel_obj, self.related.field.name, None)
496         elif not isinstance(value, self.related.related_model):
497             # An object must be an instance of the related class.
498             raise ValueError(
499                 'Cannot assign "%r": "%s.%s" must be a "%s" instance.'
500                 % (
501                     value,
502                     instance._meta.object_name,
503                     self.related.get_accessor_name(),
504                     self.related.related_model._meta.object_name,
505                 )
506             )
507         else:
508             if instance._state.db is None:
509                 instance._state.db = router.db_for_write(
510                     instance.__class__, instance=value
511                 )
512             if value._state.db is None:
513                 value._state.db = router.db_for_write(
514                     value.__class__, instance=instance
515                 )
516             if not router.allow_relation(value, instance):
517                 raise ValueError(
518                     'Cannot assign "%r": the current database router prevents this '
519                     "relation." % value
520                 )
521 
522             related_pk = tuple(
523                 getattr(instance, field.attname)
524                 for field in self.related.field.foreign_related_fields
525             )
526             # Set the value of the related field to the value of the related
527             # object's related field.
528             for index, field in enumerate(self.related.field.local_related_fields):
529                 setattr(value, field.attname, related_pk[index])
530 
531             # Set the related instance cache used by __get__ to avoid an SQL query
532             # when accessing the attribute we just set.
533             self.related.set_cached_value(instance, value)
534 
535             # Set the forward accessor cache on the related object to the current
536             # instance to avoid an extra SQL query if it's accessed later on.
537             self.related.field.set_cached_value(value, instance)
538 
539     def __reduce__(self):
540         # Same purpose as ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.__reduce__().
541         return getattr, (self.related.model, self.related.name)
542

544 class ReverseManyToOneDescriptor:
545     """
546     Accessor to the related objects manager on the reverse side of a
547     many-to-one relation.
548 
549     In the example::
550 
551         class Child(Model):
552             parent = ForeignKey(Parent, related_name='children')
553 
554     ``Parent.children`` is a ``ReverseManyToOneDescriptor`` instance.
555 
556     Most of the implementation is delegated to a dynamically defined manager
557     class built by ``create_forward_many_to_many_manager()`` defined below.
558     """
559 
560     def __init__(self, rel):
561         self.rel = rel
562         self.field = rel.field
563 
564     @cached_property
565     def related_manager_cache_key(self):
566         # Being able to access the manager instance precludes it from being
567         # hidden. The rel's accessor name is used to allow multiple managers
568         # to the same model to coexist. e.g. post.attached_comment_set and
569         # post.attached_link_set are separately cached.
570         return self.rel.get_cache_name()

572     @cached_property

575 
576         return create_reverse_many_to_one_manager(
577             related_model._default_manager.__class__,
578             self.rel,
579         )

581     def __get__(self, instance, cls=None):

583         Get the related objects through the reverse relation.
584 
585         With the example above, when getting ``parent.children``:
586

588         - ``instance`` is the ``parent`` instance
589         - ``cls`` is the ``Parent`` class (unused)
590         """
591         if instance is None:
592             return self
593         key = self.related_manager_cache_key

595         if key not in instance_cache:
596             instance_cache[key] = self.related_manager_cls(instance)
597         return instance_cache[key]
598 
599     def _get_set_deprecation_msg_params(self):
600         return (
601             "reverse side of a related set",
602             self.rel.get_accessor_name(),
603         )
604 
605     def __set__(self, instance, value):
606         raise TypeError(
607             "Direct assignment to the %s is prohibited. Use %s.set() instead."
608             % self._get_set_deprecation_msg_params(),
609         )

612 def create_reverse_many_to_one_manager(superclass, rel):
613     """
614     Create a manager for the reverse side of a many-to-one relation.
615 
616     This manager subclasses another manager, generally the default manager of
617     the related model, and adds behaviors specific to many-to-one relations.
618     """
619 
620     class RelatedManager(superclass):
621         def __init__(self, instance):
622             super().__init__()
623 
624             self.instance = instance
625             self.model = rel.related_model
626             self.field = rel.field
627 
628             self.core_filters = {self.field.name: instance}
629 
630             # Even if this relation is not to pk, we require still pk value.
631             # The wish is that the instance has been already saved to DB,
632             # although having a pk value isn't a guarantee of that.
633             if self.instance.pk is None:
634                 raise ValueError(
635                     f"{instance.__class__.__name__!r} instance needs to have a primary "
636                     f"key value before this relationship can be used."
637                 )
638 
639         def __call__(self, *, manager):
640             manager = getattr(self.model, manager)
641             manager_class = create_reverse_many_to_one_manager(manager.__class__, rel)
642             return manager_class(self.instance)
643 
644         do_not_call_in_templates = True
645 
646         def _check_fk_val(self):
647             for field in self.field.foreign_related_fields:
648                 if getattr(self.instance, field.attname) is None:
649                     raise ValueError(
650                         f'"{self.instance!r}" needs to have a value for field '
651                         f'"{field.attname}" before this relationship can be used.'
652                     )
653 
654         def _apply_rel_filters(self, queryset):
655             """
656             Filter the queryset for the instance this manager is bound to.
657             """
658             db = self._db or router.db_for_read(self.model, instance=self.instance)
659             empty_strings_as_null = connections[
660                 db
661             ].features.interprets_empty_strings_as_nulls
662             queryset._add_hints(instance=self.instance)
663             if self._db:
664                 queryset = queryset.using(self._db)
665             queryset._defer_next_filter = True
666             queryset = queryset.filter(**self.core_filters)
667             for field in self.field.foreign_related_fields:
668                 val = getattr(self.instance, field.attname)
669                 if val is None or (val == "" and empty_strings_as_null):
670                     return queryset.none()
671             if self.field.many_to_one:
672                 # Guard against field-like objects such as GenericRelation
673                 # that abuse create_reverse_many_to_one_manager() with reverse
674                 # one-to-many relationships instead and break known related
675                 # objects assignment.
676                 try:
677                     target_field = self.field.target_field
678                 except FieldError:
679                     # The relationship has multiple target fields. Use a tuple
680                     # for related object id.
681                     rel_obj_id = tuple(
682                         [
683                             getattr(self.instance, target_field.attname)
684                             for target_field in self.field.path_infos[-1].target_fields
685                         ]
686                     )
687                 else:
688                     rel_obj_id = getattr(self.instance, target_field.attname)
689                 queryset._known_related_objects = {
690                     self.field: {rel_obj_id: self.instance}
691                 }
692             return queryset
693 
694         def _remove_prefetched_objects(self):
695             try:
696                 self.instance._prefetched_objects_cache.pop(
697                     self.field.remote_field.get_cache_name()
698                 )
699             except (AttributeError, KeyError):
700                 pass  # nothing to clear from cache
701 
702         def get_queryset(self):
703             try:
704                 return self.instance._prefetched_objects_cache[
705                     self.field.remote_field.get_cache_name()
706                 ]
707             except (AttributeError, KeyError):
708                 queryset = super().get_queryset()
709                 return self._apply_rel_filters(queryset)
710 
711         def get_prefetch_queryset(self, instances, queryset=None):
712             if queryset is None:
713                 queryset = super().get_queryset()
714 
715             queryset._add_hints(instance=instances[0])
716             queryset = queryset.using(queryset._db or self._db)
717 
718             rel_obj_attr = self.field.get_local_related_value
719             instance_attr = self.field.get_foreign_related_value
720             instances_dict = {instance_attr(inst): inst for inst in instances}
721             query = {"%s__in" % self.field.name: instances}
722             queryset = queryset.filter(**query)
723 
724             # Since we just bypassed this class' get_queryset(), we must manage
725             # the reverse relation manually.
726             for rel_obj in queryset:
727                 if not self.field.is_cached(rel_obj):
728                     instance = instances_dict[rel_obj_attr(rel_obj)]
729                     setattr(rel_obj, self.field.name, instance)
730             cache_name = self.field.remote_field.get_cache_name()
731             return queryset, rel_obj_attr, instance_attr, False, cache_name, False
732 
733         def add(self, *objs, bulk=True):
734             self._check_fk_val()
735             self._remove_prefetched_objects()
736             db = router.db_for_write(self.model, instance=self.instance)
737 
738             def check_and_update_obj(obj):
739                 if not isinstance(obj, self.model):
740                     raise TypeError(
741                         "'%s' instance expected, got %r"
742                         % (
743                             self.model._meta.object_name,
744                             obj,
745                         )
746                     )
747                 setattr(obj, self.field.name, self.instance)
748 
749             if bulk:
750                 pks = []
751                 for obj in objs:
752                     check_and_update_obj(obj)
753                     if obj._state.adding or obj._state.db != db:
754                         raise ValueError(
755                             "%r instance isn't saved. Use bulk=False or save "
756                             "the object first." % obj
757                         )
758                     pks.append(obj.pk)
759                 self.model._base_manager.using(db).filter(pk__in=pks).update(
760                     **{
761                         self.field.name: self.instance,
762                     }
763                 )
764             else:
765                 with transaction.atomic(using=db, savepoint=False):
766                     for obj in objs:
767                         check_and_update_obj(obj)
768                         obj.save()
769 
770         add.alters_data = True
771 
772         def create(self, **kwargs):
773             self._check_fk_val()
774             kwargs[self.field.name] = self.instance
775             db = router.db_for_write(self.model, instance=self.instance)
776             return super(RelatedManager, self.db_manager(db)).create(**kwargs)
777 
778         create.alters_data = True
779 
780         def get_or_create(self, **kwargs):
781             self._check_fk_val()
782             kwargs[self.field.name] = self.instance
783             db = router.db_for_write(self.model, instance=self.instance)
784             return super(RelatedManager, self.db_manager(db)).get_or_create(**kwargs)
785 
786         get_or_create.alters_data = True
787 
788         def update_or_create(self, **kwargs):
789             self._check_fk_val()
790             kwargs[self.field.name] = self.instance
791             db = router.db_for_write(self.model, instance=self.instance)
792             return super(RelatedManager, self.db_manager(db)).update_or_create(**kwargs)
793 
794         update_or_create.alters_data = True
795 
796         # remove() and clear() are only provided if the ForeignKey can have a
797         # value of null.
798         if rel.field.null:
799 
800             def remove(self, *objs, bulk=True):
801                 if not objs:
802                     return
803                 self._check_fk_val()
804                 val = self.field.get_foreign_related_value(self.instance)
805                 old_ids = set()
806                 for obj in objs:
807                     if not isinstance(obj, self.model):
808                         raise TypeError(
809                             "'%s' instance expected, got %r"
810                             % (
811                                 self.model._meta.object_name,
812                                 obj,
813                             )
814                         )
815                     # Is obj actually part of this descriptor set?
816                     if self.field.get_local_related_value(obj) == val:
817                         old_ids.add(obj.pk)
818                     else:
819                         raise self.field.remote_field.model.DoesNotExist(
820                             "%r is not related to %r." % (obj, self.instance)
821                         )
822                 self._clear(self.filter(pk__in=old_ids), bulk)
823 
824             remove.alters_data = True
825 
826             def clear(self, *, bulk=True):
827                 self._check_fk_val()
828                 self._clear(self, bulk)
829 
830             clear.alters_data = True
831 
832             def _clear(self, queryset, bulk):
833                 self._remove_prefetched_objects()
834                 db = router.db_for_write(self.model, instance=self.instance)
835                 queryset = queryset.using(db)
836                 if bulk:
837                     # `QuerySet.update()` is intrinsically atomic.
838                     queryset.update(**{self.field.name: None})
839                 else:
840                     with transaction.atomic(using=db, savepoint=False):
841                         for obj in queryset:
842                             setattr(obj, self.field.name, None)
843                             obj.save(update_fields=[self.field.name])
844 
845             _clear.alters_data = True
846 
847         def set(self, objs, *, bulk=True, clear=False):
848             self._check_fk_val()
849             # Force evaluation of `objs` in case it's a queryset whose value
850             # could be affected by `manager.clear()`. Refs #19816.
851             objs = tuple(objs)
852 
853             if self.field.null:
854                 db = router.db_for_write(self.model, instance=self.instance)
855                 with transaction.atomic(using=db, savepoint=False):
856                     if clear:
857                         self.clear(bulk=bulk)
858                         self.add(*objs, bulk=bulk)
859                     else:
860                         old_objs = set(self.using(db).all())
861                         new_objs = []
862                         for obj in objs:
863                             if obj in old_objs:
864                                 old_objs.remove(obj)
865                             else:
866                                 new_objs.append(obj)
867 
868                         self.remove(*old_objs, bulk=bulk)
869                         self.add(*new_objs, bulk=bulk)
870             else:
871                 self.add(*objs, bulk=bulk)
872 
873         set.alters_data = True
874 
875     return RelatedManager
876

878 class ManyToManyDescriptor(ReverseManyToOneDescriptor):
879     """
880     Accessor to the related objects manager on the forward and reverse sides of
881     a many-to-many relation.
882 
883     In the example::
884 
885         class Pizza(Model):
886             toppings = ManyToManyField(Topping, related_name='pizzas')
887 
888     ``Pizza.toppings`` and ``Topping.pizzas`` are ``ManyToManyDescriptor``
889     instances.
890 
891     Most of the implementation is delegated to a dynamically defined manager
892     class built by ``create_forward_many_to_many_manager()`` defined below.
893     """
894 
895     def __init__(self, rel, reverse=False):
896         super().__init__(rel)
897 
898         self.reverse = reverse
899 
900     @property
901     def through(self):
902         # through is provided so that you have easy access to the through
903         # model (Book.authors.through) for inlines, etc. This is done as
904         # a property to ensure that the fully resolved value is returned.
905         return self.rel.through
906 
907     @cached_property
908     def related_manager_cls(self):
909         related_model = self.rel.related_model if self.reverse else self.rel.model
910 
911         return create_forward_many_to_many_manager(
912             related_model._default_manager.__class__,
913             self.rel,
914             reverse=self.reverse,
915         )
916 
917     @cached_property
918     def related_manager_cache_key(self):
919         if self.reverse:
920             # Symmetrical M2Ms won't have an accessor name, but should never
921             # end up in the reverse branch anyway, as the related_name ends up
922             # being hidden, and no public manager is created.
923             return self.rel.get_cache_name()
924         else:
925             # For forward managers, defer to the field name.
926             return self.field.get_cache_name()
927 
928     def _get_set_deprecation_msg_params(self):
929         return (
930             "%s side of a many-to-many set"
931             % ("reverse" if self.reverse else "forward"),
932             self.rel.get_accessor_name() if self.reverse else self.field.name,
933         )
934 
935 
936 def create_forward_many_to_many_manager(superclass, rel, reverse):
937     """
938     Create a manager for the either side of a many-to-many relation.
939 
940     This manager subclasses another manager, generally the default manager of
941     the related model, and adds behaviors specific to many-to-many relations.
942     """
943 
944     class ManyRelatedManager(superclass):
945         def __init__(self, instance=None):
946             super().__init__()
947 
948             self.instance = instance
949 
950             if not reverse:
951                 self.model = rel.model
952                 self.query_field_name = rel.field.related_query_name()
953                 self.prefetch_cache_name = rel.field.name
954                 self.source_field_name = rel.field.m2m_field_name()
955                 self.target_field_name = rel.field.m2m_reverse_field_name()
956                 self.symmetrical = rel.symmetrical
957             else:
958                 self.model = rel.related_model
959                 self.query_field_name = rel.field.name
960                 self.prefetch_cache_name = rel.field.related_query_name()
961                 self.source_field_name = rel.field.m2m_reverse_field_name()
962                 self.target_field_name = rel.field.m2m_field_name()
963                 self.symmetrical = False
964 
965             self.through = rel.through
966             self.reverse = reverse
967 
968             self.source_field = self.through._meta.get_field(self.source_field_name)
969             self.target_field = self.through._meta.get_field(self.target_field_name)
970 
971             self.core_filters = {}
972             self.pk_field_names = {}
973             for lh_field, rh_field in self.source_field.related_fields:
974                 core_filter_key = "%s__%s" % (self.query_field_name, rh_field.name)
975                 self.core_filters[core_filter_key] = getattr(instance, rh_field.attname)
976                 self.pk_field_names[lh_field.name] = rh_field.name
977 
978             self.related_val = self.source_field.get_foreign_related_value(instance)
979             if None in self.related_val:
980                 raise ValueError(
981                     '"%r" needs to have a value for field "%s" before '
982                     "this many-to-many relationship can be used."
983                     % (instance, self.pk_field_names[self.source_field_name])
984                 )
985             # Even if this relation is not to pk, we require still pk value.
986             # The wish is that the instance has been already saved to DB,
987             # although having a pk value isn't a guarantee of that.
988             if instance.pk is None:
989                 raise ValueError(
990                     "%r instance needs to have a primary key value before "
991                     "a many-to-many relationship can be used."

52     def deep_deconstruct(self, obj):
53         """
54         Recursive deconstruction for a field and its arguments.
55         Used for full comparison for rename/alter; sometimes a single-level
56         deconstruction will not compare correctly.
57         """
58         if isinstance(obj, list):
59             return [self.deep_deconstruct(value) for value in obj]
60         elif isinstance(obj, tuple):
61             return tuple(self.deep_deconstruct(value) for value in obj)
62         elif isinstance(obj, dict):
63             return {key: self.deep_deconstruct(value) for key, value in obj.items()}
64         elif isinstance(obj, functools.partial):
65             return (
66                 obj.func,
67                 self.deep_deconstruct(obj.args),
68                 self.deep_deconstruct(obj.keywords),
69             )
70         elif isinstance(obj, COMPILED_REGEX_TYPE):
71             return RegexObject(obj)
72         elif isinstance(obj, type):
73             # If this is a type that implements 'deconstruct' as an instance method,
74             # avoid treating this as being deconstructible itself - see #22951
75             return obj
76         elif hasattr(obj, "deconstruct"):
77             deconstructed = obj.deconstruct()
78             if isinstance(obj, models.Field):
79                 # we have a field which also returns a name
80                 deconstructed = deconstructed[1:]
81             path, args, kwargs = deconstructed
82             return (
83                 path,
84                 [self.deep_deconstruct(value) for value in args],
85                 {key: self.deep_deconstruct(value) for key, value in kwargs.items()},
86             )
87         else:
88             return obj
