614     def combine(self, rhs, connector):
615         """
616         Merge the 'rhs' query into the current one (with any 'rhs' effects
617         being applied *after* (that is, "to the right of") anything in the
618         current query. 'rhs' is not modified during a call to this function.
619 
620         The 'connector' parameter describes how to connect filters from the
621         'rhs' query.
622         """
623         if self.model != rhs.model:
624             raise TypeError("Cannot combine queries on two different base models.")
625         if self.is_sliced:
626             raise TypeError("Cannot combine queries once a slice has been taken.")
627         if self.distinct != rhs.distinct:
628             raise TypeError("Cannot combine a unique query with a non-unique query.")
629         if self.distinct_fields != rhs.distinct_fields:
630             raise TypeError("Cannot combine queries with different distinct fields.")
631 
632         # If lhs and rhs shares the same alias prefix, it is possible to have
633         # conflicting alias changes like T4 -> T5, T5 -> T6, which might end up
634         # as T4 -> T6 while combining two querysets. To prevent this, change an
635         # alias prefix of the rhs and update current aliases accordingly,
636         # except if the alias is the base table since it must be present in the
637         # query on both sides.
638         initial_alias = self.get_initial_alias()
639         rhs.bump_prefix(self, exclude={initial_alias})
640 
641         # Work out how to relabel the rhs aliases, if necessary.
642         change_map = {}
643         conjunction = connector == AND
644 
645         # Determine which existing joins can be reused. When combining the
646         # query with AND we must recreate all joins for m2m filters. When
647         # combining with OR we can reuse joins. The reason is that in AND
648         # case a single row can't fulfill a condition like:
649         #     revrel__col=1 & revrel__col=2
650         # But, there might be two different related rows matching this
651         # condition. In OR case a single True is enough, so single row is
652         # enough, too.
653         #
654         # Note that we will be creating duplicate joins for non-m2m joins in
655         # the AND case. The results will be correct but this creates too many
656         # joins. This is something that could be fixed later on.
657         reuse = set() if conjunction else set(self.alias_map)
658         joinpromoter = JoinPromoter(connector, 2, False)
659         joinpromoter.add_votes(
660             j for j in self.alias_map if self.alias_map[j].join_type == INNER
661         )
662         rhs_votes = set()
663         # Now, add the joins from rhs query into the new query (skipping base
664         # table).
665         rhs_tables = list(rhs.alias_map)[1:]
666         for alias in rhs_tables:
667             join = rhs.alias_map[alias]
668             # If the left side of the join was already relabeled, use the
669             # updated alias.
670             join = join.relabeled_clone(change_map)
671             new_alias = self.join(join, reuse=reuse)
672             if join.join_type == INNER:
673                 rhs_votes.add(new_alias)
674             # We can't reuse the same join again in the query. If we have two
675             # distinct joins for the same connection in rhs query, then the
676             # combined query must have two joins, too.
677             reuse.discard(new_alias)
678             if alias != new_alias:
679                 change_map[alias] = new_alias
680             if not rhs.alias_refcount[alias]:
681                 # The alias was unused in the rhs query. Unref it so that it
682                 # will be unused in the new query, too. We have to add and
683                 # unref the alias so that join promotion has information of
684                 # the join type for the unused alias.
685                 self.unref_alias(new_alias)
686         joinpromoter.add_votes(rhs_votes)
687         joinpromoter.update_join_types(self)
688 
689         # Combine subqueries aliases to ensure aliases relabelling properly
690         # handle subqueries when combining where and select clauses.
691         self.subq_aliases |= rhs.subq_aliases
692 
693         # Now relabel a copy of the rhs where-clause and add it to the current
694         # one.
695         w = rhs.where.clone()
696         w.relabel_aliases(change_map)
697         self.where.add(w, connector)
698 
699         # Selection columns and extra extensions are those provided by 'rhs'.
700         if rhs.select:
701             self.set_select([col.relabeled_clone(change_map) for col in rhs.select])
702         else:
703             self.select = ()
704 
705         if connector == OR:
706             # It would be nice to be able to handle this, but the queries don't
707             # really make sense (or return consistent value sets). Not worth
708             # the extra complexity when you can write a real query instead.
709             if self.extra and rhs.extra:
710                 raise ValueError(
711                     "When merging querysets using 'or', you cannot have "
712                     "extra(select=...) on both sides."
713                 )
714         self.extra.update(rhs.extra)
715         extra_select_mask = set()
716         if self.extra_select_mask is not None:
717             extra_select_mask.update(self.extra_select_mask)
718         if rhs.extra_select_mask is not None:
719             extra_select_mask.update(rhs.extra_select_mask)
720         if extra_select_mask:
721             self.set_extra_mask(extra_select_mask)
722         self.extra_tables += rhs.extra_tables
723 
724         # Ordering uses the 'rhs' ordering, unless it has none, in which case
725         # the current ordering is used.
726         self.order_by = rhs.order_by or self.order_by
727         self.extra_order_by = rhs.extra_order_by or self.extra_order_by
728 
729     def _get_defer_select_mask(self, opts, mask, select_mask=None):
730         if select_mask is None:
731             select_mask = {}
732         select_mask[opts.pk] = {}
733         # All concrete fields that are not part of the defer mask must be
734         # loaded. If a relational field is encountered it gets added to the
735         # mask for it be considered if `select_related` and the cycle continues
736         # by recursively calling this function.
737         for field in opts.concrete_fields:
738             field_mask = mask.pop(field.name, None)
739             field_att_mask = mask.pop(field.attname, None)
740             if field_mask is None and field_att_mask is None:
741                 select_mask.setdefault(field, {})
742             elif field_mask:
743                 if not field.is_relation:
744                     raise FieldError(next(iter(field_mask)))
745                 field_select_mask = select_mask.setdefault(field, {})
746                 related_model = field.remote_field.model._meta.concrete_model
747                 self._get_defer_select_mask(
748                     related_model._meta, field_mask, field_select_mask
749                 )
750         # Remaining defer entries must be references to reverse relationships.
751         # The following code is expected to raise FieldError if it encounters
752         # a malformed defer entry.
753         for field_name, field_mask in mask.items():
754             if filtered_relation := self._filtered_relations.get(field_name):
755                 relation = opts.get_field(filtered_relation.relation_name)
756                 field_select_mask = select_mask.setdefault((field_name, relation), {})
757                 field = relation.field
758             else:
759                 reverse_rel = opts.get_field(field_name)
760                 # While virtual fields such as many-to-many and generic foreign
761                 # keys cannot be effectively deferred we've historically
762                 # allowed them to be passed to QuerySet.defer(). Ignore such
763                 # field references until a layer of validation at mask
764                 # alteration time will be implemented eventually.
765                 if not hasattr(reverse_rel, "field"):
766                     continue
767                 field = reverse_rel.field
768                 field_select_mask = select_mask.setdefault(field, {})
769             related_model = field.model._meta.concrete_model
770             self._get_defer_select_mask(
771                 related_model._meta, field_mask, field_select_mask
772             )
773         return select_mask
774 
775     def _get_only_select_mask(self, opts, mask, select_mask=None):
776         if select_mask is None:
777             select_mask = {}
778         select_mask[opts.pk] = {}
779         # Only include fields mentioned in the mask.
780         for field_name, field_mask in mask.items():
781             field = opts.get_field(field_name)
782             # Retrieve the actual field associated with reverse relationships
783             # as that's what is expected in the select mask.
784             if field in opts.related_objects:
785                 field_key = field.field
786             else:
787                 field_key = field
788             field_select_mask = select_mask.setdefault(field_key, {})
789             if field_mask:
790                 if not field.is_relation:
791                     raise FieldError(next(iter(field_mask)))
792                 related_model = field.remote_field.model._meta.concrete_model
793                 self._get_only_select_mask(
794                     related_model._meta, field_mask, field_select_mask
795                 )
796         return select_mask
797 
798     def get_select_mask(self):
799         """
800         Convert the self.deferred_loading data structure to an alternate data
801         structure, describing the field that *will* be loaded. This is used to
802         compute the columns to select from the database and also by the
803         QuerySet class to work out which fields are being initialized on each
804         model. Models that have all their fields included aren't mentioned in
805         the result, only those that have field restrictions in place.
806         """
807         field_names, defer = self.deferred_loading
808         if not field_names:
809             return {}
810         mask = {}
811         for field_name in field_names:
812             part_mask = mask
813             for part in field_name.split(LOOKUP_SEP):
814                 part_mask = part_mask.setdefault(part, {})
815         opts = self.get_meta()
816         if defer:
817             return self._get_defer_select_mask(opts, mask)
818         return self._get_only_select_mask(opts, mask)

820     def table_alias(self, table_name, create=False, filtered_relation=None):
821         """
822         Return a table alias for the given table_name and whether this is a
823         new alias or not.
824 
825         If 'create' is true, a new alias is always created. Otherwise, the
826         most recently created alias for the table (if one exists) is reused.
827         """
828         alias_list = self.table_map.get(table_name)
829         if not create and alias_list:
830             alias = alias_list[0]
831             self.alias_refcount[alias] += 1
832             return alias, False
833 
834         # Create a new alias for this table.
835         if alias_list:
836             alias = "%s%d" % (self.alias_prefix, len(self.alias_map) + 1)
837             alias_list.append(alias)
838         else:
839             # The first occurrence of a table uses the table name directly.
840             alias = (
841                 filtered_relation.alias if filtered_relation is not None else table_name
842             )
843             self.table_map[table_name] = [alias]
844         self.alias_refcount[alias] = 1
845         return alias, True
846 
847     def ref_alias(self, alias):
848         """Increases the reference count for this alias."""
849         self.alias_refcount[alias] += 1

851     def unref_alias(self, alias, amount=1):
852         """Decreases the reference count for this alias."""
853         self.alias_refcount[alias] -= amount

855     def promote_joins(self, aliases):
856         """
857         Promote recursively the join type of given aliases and its children to
858         an outer join. If 'unconditional' is False, only promote the join if
859         it is nullable or the parent join is an outer join.
860 
861         The children promotion is done to avoid join chains that contain a LOUTER
862         b INNER c. So, if we have currently a INNER b INNER c and a->b is promoted,
863         then we must also promote b->c automatically, or otherwise the promotion
864         of a->b doesn't actually change anything in the query results.
865         """
866         aliases = list(aliases)
867         while aliases:
868             alias = aliases.pop(0)
869             if self.alias_map[alias].join_type is None:
870                 # This is the base table (first FROM entry) - this table
871                 # isn't really joined at all in the query, so we should not
872                 # alter its join type.
873                 continue
874             # Only the first alias (skipped above) should have None join_type
875             assert self.alias_map[alias].join_type is not None
876             parent_alias = self.alias_map[alias].parent_alias
877             parent_louter = (
878                 parent_alias and self.alias_map[parent_alias].join_type == LOUTER
879             )
880             already_louter = self.alias_map[alias].join_type == LOUTER
881             if (self.alias_map[alias].nullable or parent_louter) and not already_louter:
882                 self.alias_map[alias] = self.alias_map[alias].promote()
883                 # Join type of 'alias' changed, so re-examine all aliases that
884                 # refer to this one.
885                 aliases.extend(
886                     join
887                     for join in self.alias_map
888                     if self.alias_map[join].parent_alias == alias
889                     and join not in aliases
890                 )
891 
892     def demote_joins(self, aliases):
893         """
894         Change join type from LOUTER to INNER for all joins in aliases.
895 
896         Similarly to promote_joins(), this method must ensure no join chains
897         containing first an outer, then an inner join are generated. If we
898         are demoting b->c join in chain a LOUTER b LOUTER c then we must
899         demote a->b automatically, or otherwise the demotion of b->c doesn't
900         actually change anything in the query results. .
901         """
902         aliases = list(aliases)
903         while aliases:
904             alias = aliases.pop(0)
905             if self.alias_map[alias].join_type == LOUTER:
906                 self.alias_map[alias] = self.alias_map[alias].demote()
907                 parent_alias = self.alias_map[alias].parent_alias
908                 if self.alias_map[parent_alias].join_type == INNER:
909                     aliases.append(parent_alias)
910 
911     def reset_refcounts(self, to_counts):
912         """
913         Reset reference counts for aliases so that they match the value passed
914         in `to_counts`.
915         """
916         for alias, cur_refcount in self.alias_refcount.copy().items():
917             unref_amount = cur_refcount - to_counts.get(alias, 0)
918             self.unref_alias(alias, unref_amount)

920     def change_aliases(self, change_map):
921         """
922         Change the aliases in change_map (which maps old-alias -> new-alias),
923         relabelling any references to them in select columns and the where
924         clause.
925         """
926         # If keys and values of change_map were to intersect, an alias might be
927         # updated twice (e.g. T4 -> T5, T5 -> T6, so also T4 -> T6) depending
928         # on their order in change_map.
929         assert set(change_map).isdisjoint(change_map.values())
930 
931         # 1. Update references in "select" (normal columns plus aliases),
932         # "group by" and "where".
933         self.where.relabel_aliases(change_map)
934         if isinstance(self.group_by, tuple):
935             self.group_by = tuple(
936                 [col.relabeled_clone(change_map) for col in self.group_by]
937             )
938         self.select = tuple([col.relabeled_clone(change_map) for col in self.select])
939         self.annotations = self.annotations and {
940             key: col.relabeled_clone(change_map)
941             for key, col in self.annotations.items()
942         }
943 
944         # 2. Rename the alias in the internal table/alias datastructures.
945         for old_alias, new_alias in change_map.items():
946             if old_alias not in self.alias_map:
947                 continue
948             alias_data = self.alias_map[old_alias].relabeled_clone(change_map)
949             self.alias_map[new_alias] = alias_data
950             self.alias_refcount[new_alias] = self.alias_refcount[old_alias]
951             del self.alias_refcount[old_alias]
952             del self.alias_map[old_alias]
953 
954             table_aliases = self.table_map[alias_data.table_name]
955             for pos, alias in enumerate(table_aliases):
956                 if alias == old_alias:
957                     table_aliases[pos] = new_alias
958                     break
959         self.external_aliases = {
960             # Table is aliased or it's being changed and thus is aliased.
961             change_map.get(alias, alias): (aliased or alias in change_map)
962             for alias, aliased in self.external_aliases.items()
963         }
964 
965     def bump_prefix(self, other_query, exclude=None):
966         """
967         Change the alias prefix to the next letter in the alphabet in a way
968         that the other query's aliases and this query's aliases will not
969         conflict. Even tables that previously had no alias will get an alias
970         after this call. To prevent changing aliases use the exclude parameter.
971         """
972 
973         def prefix_gen():
974             """
975             Generate a sequence of characters in alphabetical order:
976                 -> 'A', 'B', 'C', ...
977 
978             When the alphabet is finished, the sequence will continue with the
979             Cartesian product:
980                 -> 'AA', 'AB', 'AC', ...
981             """
982             alphabet = ascii_uppercase
983             prefix = chr(ord(self.alias_prefix) + 1)
984             yield prefix
985             for n in count(1):
986                 seq = alphabet[alphabet.index(prefix) :] if prefix else alphabet
987                 for s in product(seq, repeat=n):
988                     yield "".join(s)
989                 prefix = None
990 
991         if self.alias_prefix != other_query.alias_prefix:
992             # No clashes between self and outer query should be possible.
993             return
994 
995         # Explicitly avoid infinite loop. The constant divider is based on how
996         # much depth recursive subquery references add to the stack. This value
997         # might need to be adjusted when adding or removing function calls from
998         # the code path in charge of performing these operations.
999         local_recursion_limit = sys.getrecursionlimit() // 16
1000         for pos, prefix in enumerate(prefix_gen()):
1001             if prefix not in self.subq_aliases:
1002                 self.alias_prefix = prefix
1003                 break
1004             if pos > local_recursion_limit:
1005                 raise RecursionError(
1006                     "Maximum recursion depth exceeded: too many subqueries."
1007                 )
1008         self.subq_aliases = self.subq_aliases.union([self.alias_prefix])
1009         other_query.subq_aliases = other_query.subq_aliases.union(self.subq_aliases)
1010         if exclude is None:
1011             exclude = {}
1012         self.change_aliases(
1013             {
1014                 alias: "%s%d" % (self.alias_prefix, pos)
1015                 for pos, alias in enumerate(self.alias_map)
1016                 if alias not in exclude
1017             }
1018         )
1019

1042     def join(self, join, reuse=None):
1043         """
1044         Return an alias for the 'join', either reusing an existing alias for
1045         that join or creating a new one. 'join' is either a base_table_class or
1046         join_class.
1047 
1048         The 'reuse' parameter can be either None which means all joins are
1049         reusable, or it can be a set containing the aliases that can be reused.
1050 
1051         A join is always created as LOUTER if the lhs alias is LOUTER to make
1052         sure chains like t1 LOUTER t2 INNER t3 aren't generated. All new
1053         joins are created as LOUTER if the join is nullable.
1054         """
1055         reuse_aliases = [
1056             a
1057             for a, j in self.alias_map.items()
1058             if (reuse is None or a in reuse) and j == join
1059         ]
1060         if reuse_aliases:
1061             if join.table_alias in reuse_aliases:
1062                 reuse_alias = join.table_alias
1063             else:
1064                 # Reuse the most recent alias of the joined table
1065                 # (a many-to-many relation may be joined multiple times).
1066                 reuse_alias = reuse_aliases[-1]
1067             self.ref_alias(reuse_alias)
1068             return reuse_alias
1069 
1070         # No reuse is possible, so we need a new alias.
1071         alias, _ = self.table_alias(
1072             join.table_name, create=True, filtered_relation=join.filtered_relation
1073         )
1074         if join.join_type:
1075             if self.alias_map[join.parent_alias].join_type == LOUTER or join.nullable:
1076                 join_type = LOUTER
1077             else:
1078                 join_type = INNER
1079             join.join_type = join_type
1080         join.table_alias = alias
1081         self.alias_map[alias] = join
1082         if filtered_relation := join.filtered_relation:
1083             resolve_reuse = reuse
1084             if resolve_reuse is not None:
1085                 resolve_reuse = set(reuse) | {alias}
1086             joins_len = len(self.alias_map)
1087             join.filtered_relation = filtered_relation.resolve_expression(
1088                 self, reuse=resolve_reuse
1089             )
1090             # Some joins were during expression resolving, they must be present
1091             # before the one we just added.
1092             if joins_len < len(self.alias_map):
1093                 self.alias_map[alias] = self.alias_map.pop(alias)
1094         return alias
1095 
1096     def join_parent_model(self, opts, model, alias, seen):
1097         """
1098         Make sure the given 'model' is joined in the query. If 'model' isn't
1099         a parent of 'opts' or if it is None this method is a no-op.
1100 
1101         The 'alias' is the root alias for starting the join, 'seen' is a dict
1102         of model -> alias of existing joins. It must also contain a mapping
1103         of None -> some alias. This will be returned in the no-op case.
1104         """
1105         if model in seen:
1106             return seen[model]
1107         chain = opts.get_base_chain(model)
1108         if not chain:
1109             return alias
1110         curr_opts = opts
1111         for int_model in chain:
1112             if int_model in seen:
1113                 curr_opts = int_model._meta
1114                 alias = seen[int_model]
1115                 continue
1116             # Proxy model have elements in base chain
1117             # with no parents, assign the new options
1118             # object and skip to the next base in that
1119             # case
1120             if not curr_opts.parents[int_model]:
1121                 curr_opts = int_model._meta
1122                 continue
1123             link_field = curr_opts.get_ancestor_link(int_model)
1124             join_info = self.setup_joins([link_field.name], curr_opts, alias)
1125             curr_opts = int_model._meta
1126             alias = seen[int_model] = join_info.joins[-1]
1127         return alias or seen[None]

1151     def resolve_expression(self, query, *args, **kwargs):
1152         clone = self.clone()
1153         # Subqueries need to use a different set of aliases than the outer query.
1154         clone.bump_prefix(query)
1155         clone.subquery = True
1156         clone.where.resolve_expression(query, *args, **kwargs)
1157         # Resolve combined queries.
1158         if clone.combinator:
1159             clone.combined_queries = tuple(
1160                 [
1161                     combined_query.resolve_expression(query, *args, **kwargs)
1162                     for combined_query in clone.combined_queries
1163                 ]
1164             )
1165         for key, value in clone.annotations.items():
1166             resolved = value.resolve_expression(query, *args, **kwargs)
1167             if hasattr(resolved, "external_aliases"):
1168                 resolved.external_aliases.update(clone.external_aliases)
1169             clone.annotations[key] = resolved
1170         # Outer query's aliases are considered external.
1171         for alias, table in query.alias_map.items():
1172             clone.external_aliases[alias] = (
1173                 isinstance(table, Join)
1174                 and table.join_field.related_model._meta.db_table != alias
1175             ) or (
1176                 isinstance(table, BaseTable) and table.table_name != table.table_alias
1177             )
1178         return clone

1180     def get_external_cols(self):

1182         return [
1183             col
1184             for col in self._gen_cols(exprs, include_external=True)
1185             if col.alias in self.external_aliases
1186         ]

1213     def resolve_lookup_value(self, value, can_reuse, allow_joins):

1216                 self,

1220         elif isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
1221             # The items of the iterable may be expressions and therefore need
1222             # to be resolved independently.
1223             values = (
1224                 self.resolve_lookup_value(sub_value, can_reuse, allow_joins)
1225                 for sub_value in value
1226             )

1228             if hasattr(type_, "_make"):  # namedtuple
1229                 return type_(*values)
1230             return type_(values)
1231         return value

1233     def solve_lookup_type(self, lookup, summarize=False):
1234         """
1235         Solve the lookup type from the lookup (e.g.: 'foobar__id__icontains').
1236         """
1237         lookup_splitted = lookup.split(LOOKUP_SEP)
1238         if self.annotations:
1239             annotation, expression_lookups = refs_expression(
1240                 lookup_splitted, self.annotations
1241             )
1242             if annotation:
1243                 expression = self.annotations[annotation]
1244                 if summarize:
1245                     expression = Ref(annotation, expression)
1246                 return expression_lookups, (), expression
1247         _, field, _, lookup_parts = self.names_to_path(lookup_splitted, self.get_meta())
1248         field_parts = lookup_splitted[0 : len(lookup_splitted) - len(lookup_parts)]
1249         if len(lookup_parts) > 1 and not field_parts:
1250             raise FieldError(
1251                 'Invalid lookup "%s" for model %s".'
1252                 % (lookup, self.get_meta().model.__name__)
1253             )
1254         return lookup_parts, field_parts, False

1256     def check_query_object_type(self, value, opts, field):
1257         """
1258         Check whether the object passed while querying is of the correct type.
1259         If not, raise a ValueError specifying the wrong object.
1260         """
1261         if hasattr(value, "_meta"):
1262             if not check_rel_lookup_compatibility(value._meta.model, opts, field):
1263                 raise ValueError(
1264                     'Cannot query "%s": Must be "%s" instance.'
1265                     % (value, opts.object_name)
1266                 )

1268     def check_related_objects(self, field, value, opts):
1269         """Check the type of object passed to query relations."""
1270         if field.is_relation:
1271             # Check that the field and the queryset use the same model in a
1272             # query like .filter(author=Author.objects.all()). For example, the
1273             # opts would be Author's (from the author field) and value.model
1274             # would be Author.objects.all() queryset's .model (Author also).
1275             # The field is the related field on the lhs side.
1276             if (
1277                 isinstance(value, Query)
1278                 and not value.has_select_fields
1279                 and not check_rel_lookup_compatibility(value.model, opts, field)
1280             ):
1281                 raise ValueError(
1282                     'Cannot use QuerySet for "%s": Use a QuerySet for "%s".'
1283                     % (value.model._meta.object_name, opts.object_name)
1284                 )
1285             elif hasattr(value, "_meta"):
1286                 self.check_query_object_type(value, opts, field)
1287             elif hasattr(value, "__iter__"):
1288                 for v in value:
1289                     self.check_query_object_type(v, opts, field)

1291     def check_filterable(self, expression):
1292         """Raise an error if expression cannot be used in a WHERE clause."""
1293         if hasattr(expression, "resolve_expression") and not getattr(
1294             expression, "filterable", True
1295         ):
1296             raise NotSupportedError(
1297                 expression.__class__.__name__ + " is disallowed in the filter "
1298                 "clause."
1299             )
1300         if hasattr(expression, "get_source_expressions"):
1301             for expr in expression.get_source_expressions():
1302                 self.check_filterable(expr)

1304     def build_lookup(self, lookups, lhs, rhs):
1305         """
1306         Try to extract transforms and lookup from given lhs.
1307 
1308         The lhs value is something that works like SQLExpression.
1309         The rhs value is what the lookup is going to compare against.
1310         The lookups is a list of names to extract using get_lookup()
1311         and get_transform().
1312         """
1313         # __exact is the default lookup if one isn't given.
1314         *transforms, lookup_name = lookups or ["exact"]
1315         for name in transforms:
1316             lhs = self.try_transform(lhs, name)
1317         # First try get_lookup() so that the lookup takes precedence if the lhs
1318         # supports both transform and lookup for the name.
1319         lookup_class = lhs.get_lookup(lookup_name)
1320         if not lookup_class:
1321             # A lookup wasn't found. Try to interpret the name as a transform
1322             # and do an Exact lookup against it.
1323             lhs = self.try_transform(lhs, lookup_name)
1324             lookup_name = "exact"
1325             lookup_class = lhs.get_lookup(lookup_name)
1326             if not lookup_class:
1327                 return
1328 
1329         lookup = lookup_class(lhs, rhs)
1330         # Interpret '__exact=None' as the sql 'is NULL'; otherwise, reject all
1331         # uses of None as a query value unless the lookup supports it.
1332         if lookup.rhs is None and not lookup.can_use_none_as_rhs:
1333             if lookup_name not in ("exact", "iexact"):
1334                 raise ValueError("Cannot use None as a query value")
1335             return lhs.get_lookup("isnull")(lhs, True)
1336 
1337         # For Oracle '' is equivalent to null. The check must be done at this
1338         # stage because join promotion can't be done in the compiler. Using
1339         # DEFAULT_DB_ALIAS isn't nice but it's the best that can be done here.
1340         # A similar thing is done in is_nullable(), too.
1341         if (
1342             lookup_name == "exact"
1343             and lookup.rhs == ""
1344             and connections[DEFAULT_DB_ALIAS].features.interprets_empty_strings_as_nulls
1345         ):
1346             return lhs.get_lookup("isnull")(lhs, True)
1347 
1348         return lookup
1349 
1350     def try_transform(self, lhs, name):
1351         """
1352         Helper method for build_lookup(). Try to fetch and initialize
1353         a transform for name parameter from lhs.
1354         """
1355         transform_class = lhs.get_transform(name)
1356         if transform_class:
1357             return transform_class(lhs)
1358         else:
1359             output_field = lhs.output_field.__class__
1360             suggested_lookups = difflib.get_close_matches(
1361                 name, lhs.output_field.get_lookups()
1362             )
1363             if suggested_lookups:
1364                 suggestion = ", perhaps you meant %s?" % " or ".join(suggested_lookups)
1365             else:
1366                 suggestion = "."
1367             raise FieldError(
1368                 "Unsupported lookup '%s' for %s or join on the field not "
1369                 "permitted%s" % (name, output_field.__name__, suggestion)
1370             )
1371 
1372     def build_filter(
1373         self,
1374         filter_expr,
1375         branch_negated=False,
1376         current_negated=False,
1377         can_reuse=None,
1378         allow_joins=True,
1379         split_subq=True,
1380         check_filterable=True,
1381         summarize=False,
1382         update_join_types=True,
1383     ):
1384         """
1385         Build a WhereNode for a single filter clause but don't add it
1386         to this Query. Query.add_q() will then add this filter to the where
1387         Node.
1388 
1389         The 'branch_negated' tells us if the current branch contains any
1390         negations. This will be used to determine if subqueries are needed.
1391 
1392         The 'current_negated' is used to determine if the current filter is
1393         negated or not and this will be used to determine if IS NULL filtering
1394         is needed.
1395 
1396         The difference between current_negated and branch_negated is that
1397         branch_negated is set on first negation, but current_negated is
1398         flipped for each negation.
1399 
1400         Note that add_filter will not do any negating itself, that is done
1401         upper in the code by add_q().
1402 
1403         The 'can_reuse' is a set of reusable joins for multijoins.
1404 
1405         The method will create a filter clause that can be added to the current
1406         query. However, if the filter isn't added to the query then the caller
1407         is responsible for unreffing the joins used.
1408         """
1409         if isinstance(filter_expr, dict):
1410             raise FieldError("Cannot parse keyword query as dict")
1411         if isinstance(filter_expr, Q):
1412             return self._add_q(
1413                 filter_expr,
1414                 branch_negated=branch_negated,
1415                 current_negated=current_negated,
1416                 used_aliases=can_reuse,
1417                 allow_joins=allow_joins,
1418                 split_subq=split_subq,
1419                 check_filterable=check_filterable,
1420                 summarize=summarize,
1421                 update_join_types=update_join_types,
1422             )
1423         if hasattr(filter_expr, "resolve_expression"):
1424             if not getattr(filter_expr, "conditional", False):
1425                 raise TypeError("Cannot filter against a non-conditional expression.")
1426             condition = filter_expr.resolve_expression(
1427                 self, allow_joins=allow_joins, reuse=can_reuse, summarize=summarize
1428             )
1429             if not isinstance(condition, Lookup):
1430                 condition = self.build_lookup(["exact"], condition, True)
1431             return WhereNode([condition], connector=AND), []
1432         arg, value = filter_expr
1433         if not arg:
1434             raise FieldError("Cannot parse keyword query %r" % arg)
1435         lookups, parts, reffed_expression = self.solve_lookup_type(arg, summarize)
1436 
1437         if check_filterable:
1438             self.check_filterable(reffed_expression)
1439 
1440         if not allow_joins and len(parts) > 1:
1441             raise FieldError("Joined field references are not permitted in this query")
1442 
1443         pre_joins = self.alias_refcount.copy()
1444         value = self.resolve_lookup_value(value, can_reuse, allow_joins)
1445         used_joins = {
1446             k for k, v in self.alias_refcount.items() if v > pre_joins.get(k, 0)
1447         }
1448 
1449         if check_filterable:
1450             self.check_filterable(value)
1451 
1452         if reffed_expression:
1453             condition = self.build_lookup(lookups, reffed_expression, value)
1454             return WhereNode([condition], connector=AND), []
1455 
1456         opts = self.get_meta()
1457         alias = self.get_initial_alias()
1458         allow_many = not branch_negated or not split_subq
1459 
1460         try:
1461             join_info = self.setup_joins(
1462                 parts,
1463                 opts,
1464                 alias,
1465                 can_reuse=can_reuse,
1466                 allow_many=allow_many,
1467             )
1468 
1469             # Prevent iterator from being consumed by check_related_objects()
1470             if isinstance(value, Iterator):
1471                 value = list(value)
1472             self.check_related_objects(join_info.final_field, value, join_info.opts)
1473 
1474             # split_exclude() needs to know which joins were generated for the
1475             # lookup parts
1476             self._lookup_joins = join_info.joins
1477         except MultiJoin as e:
1478             return self.split_exclude(filter_expr, can_reuse, e.names_with_path)
1479 
1480         # Update used_joins before trimming since they are reused to determine
1481         # which joins could be later promoted to INNER.
1482         used_joins.update(join_info.joins)
1483         targets, alias, join_list = self.trim_joins(
1484             join_info.targets, join_info.joins, join_info.path
1485         )
1486         if can_reuse is not None:
1487             can_reuse.update(join_list)
1488 
1489         if join_info.final_field.is_relation:
1490             if len(targets) == 1:
1491                 col = self._get_col(targets[0], join_info.final_field, alias)
1492             else:
1493                 col = MultiColSource(
1494                     alias, targets, join_info.targets, join_info.final_field
1495                 )
1496         else:
1497             col = self._get_col(targets[0], join_info.final_field, alias)
1498 
1499         condition = self.build_lookup(lookups, col, value)
1500         lookup_type = condition.lookup_name
1501         clause = WhereNode([condition], connector=AND)
1502 
1503         require_outer = (
1504             lookup_type == "isnull" and condition.rhs is True and not current_negated
1505         )
1506         if (
1507             current_negated
1508             and (lookup_type != "isnull" or condition.rhs is False)
1509             and condition.rhs is not None
1510         ):
1511             require_outer = True
1512             if lookup_type != "isnull":
1513                 # The condition added here will be SQL like this:
1514                 # NOT (col IS NOT NULL), where the first NOT is added in
1515                 # upper layers of code. The reason for addition is that if col
1516                 # is null, then col != someval will result in SQL "unknown"
1517                 # which isn't the same as in Python. The Python None handling
1518                 # is wanted, and it can be gotten by
1519                 # (col IS NULL OR col != someval)
1520                 #   <=>
1521                 # NOT (col IS NOT NULL AND col = someval).
1522                 if (
1523                     self.is_nullable(targets[0])
1524                     or self.alias_map[join_list[-1]].join_type == LOUTER
1525                 ):
1526                     lookup_class = targets[0].get_lookup("isnull")
1527                     col = self._get_col(targets[0], join_info.targets[0], alias)
1528                     clause.add(lookup_class(col, False), AND)
1529                 # If someval is a nullable column, someval IS NOT NULL is
1530                 # added.
1531                 if isinstance(value, Col) and self.is_nullable(value.target):
1532                     lookup_class = value.target.get_lookup("isnull")
1533                     clause.add(lookup_class(value, False), AND)
1534         return clause, used_joins if not require_outer else ()
1535 
1536     def add_filter(self, filter_lhs, filter_rhs):
1537         self.add_q(Q((filter_lhs, filter_rhs)))
1538 
1539     def add_q(self, q_object):
1540         """
1541         A preprocessor for the internal _add_q(). Responsible for doing final
1542         join promotion.
1543         """
1544         # For join promotion this case is doing an AND for the added q_object
1545         # and existing conditions. So, any existing inner join forces the join
1546         # type to remain inner. Existing outer joins can however be demoted.
1547         # (Consider case where rel_a is LOUTER and rel_a__col=1 is added - if
1548         # rel_a doesn't produce any rows, then the whole condition must fail.
1549         # So, demotion is OK.
1550         existing_inner = {
1551             a for a in self.alias_map if self.alias_map[a].join_type == INNER
1552         }
1553         clause, _ = self._add_q(q_object, self.used_aliases)
1554         if clause:
1555             self.where.add(clause, AND)
1556         self.demote_joins(existing_inner)
1557 
1558     def build_where(self, filter_expr):
1559         return self.build_filter(filter_expr, allow_joins=False)[0]
1560 
1561     def clear_where(self):
1562         self.where = WhereNode()
1563 
1564     def _add_q(
1565         self,
1566         q_object,
1567         used_aliases,
1568         branch_negated=False,
1569         current_negated=False,
1570         allow_joins=True,
1571         split_subq=True,
1572         check_filterable=True,
1573         summarize=False,
1574         update_join_types=True,
1575     ):
1576         """Add a Q-object to the current filter."""
1577         connector = q_object.connector
1578         current_negated ^= q_object.negated
1579         branch_negated = branch_negated or q_object.negated
1580         target_clause = WhereNode(connector=connector, negated=q_object.negated)
1581         joinpromoter = JoinPromoter(
1582             q_object.connector, len(q_object.children), current_negated
1583         )
1584         for child in q_object.children:
1585             child_clause, needed_inner = self.build_filter(
1586                 child,
1587                 can_reuse=used_aliases,
1588                 branch_negated=branch_negated,
1589                 current_negated=current_negated,
1590                 allow_joins=allow_joins,
1591                 split_subq=split_subq,
1592                 check_filterable=check_filterable,
1593                 summarize=summarize,
1594                 update_join_types=update_join_types,
1595             )
1596             joinpromoter.add_votes(needed_inner)
1597             if child_clause:
1598                 target_clause.add(child_clause, connector)
1599         if update_join_types:
1600             needed_inner = joinpromoter.update_join_types(self)
1601         else:
1602             needed_inner = []
1603         return target_clause, needed_inner
1604 
1605     def add_filtered_relation(self, filtered_relation, alias):
1606         filtered_relation.alias = alias
1607         lookups = dict(get_children_from_q(filtered_relation.condition))
1608         relation_lookup_parts, relation_field_parts, _ = self.solve_lookup_type(
1609             filtered_relation.relation_name
1610         )
1611         if relation_lookup_parts:
1612             raise ValueError(
1613                 "FilteredRelation's relation_name cannot contain lookups "
1614                 "(got %r)." % filtered_relation.relation_name
1615             )
1616         for lookup in chain(lookups):
1617             lookup_parts, lookup_field_parts, _ = self.solve_lookup_type(lookup)
1618             shift = 2 if not lookup_parts else 1
1619             lookup_field_path = lookup_field_parts[:-shift]
1620             for idx, lookup_field_part in enumerate(lookup_field_path):
1621                 if len(relation_field_parts) > idx:
1622                     if relation_field_parts[idx] != lookup_field_part:
1623                         raise ValueError(
1624                             "FilteredRelation's condition doesn't support "
1625                             "relations outside the %r (got %r)."
1626                             % (filtered_relation.relation_name, lookup)
1627                         )
1628                 else:
1629                     raise ValueError(
1630                         "FilteredRelation's condition doesn't support nested "
1631                         "relations deeper than the relation_name (got %r for "
1632                         "%r)." % (lookup, filtered_relation.relation_name)
1633                     )
1634         filtered_relation.condition = rename_prefix_from_q(
1635             filtered_relation.relation_name,
1636             alias,
1637             filtered_relation.condition,
1638         )
1639         self._filtered_relations[filtered_relation.alias] = filtered_relation

1641     def names_to_path(self, names, opts, allow_many=True, fail_on_missing=False):
1642         """
1643         Walk the list of names and turns them into PathInfo tuples. A single
1644         name in 'names' can generate multiple PathInfos (m2m, for example).
1645 
1646         'names' is the path of names to travel, 'opts' is the model Options we
1647         start the name resolving from, 'allow_many' is as for setup_joins().
1648         If fail_on_missing is set to True, then a name that can't be resolved
1649         will generate a FieldError.
1650 
1651         Return a list of PathInfo tuples. In addition return the final field
1652         (the last used join field) and target (which is a field guaranteed to
1653         contain the same value as the final field). Finally, return those names
1654         that weren't found (which are likely transforms and the final lookup).
1655         """
1656         path, names_with_path = [], []
1657         for pos, name in enumerate(names):
1658             cur_names_with_path = (name, [])
1659             if name == "pk":
1660                 name = opts.pk.name
1661 
1662             field = None
1663             filtered_relation = None
1664             try:
1665                 if opts is None:
1666                     raise FieldDoesNotExist
1667                 field = opts.get_field(name)
1668             except FieldDoesNotExist:
1669                 if name in self.annotation_select:
1670                     field = self.annotation_select[name].output_field
1671                 elif name in self._filtered_relations and pos == 0:
1672                     filtered_relation = self._filtered_relations[name]
1673                     if LOOKUP_SEP in filtered_relation.relation_name:
1674                         parts = filtered_relation.relation_name.split(LOOKUP_SEP)
1675                         filtered_relation_path, field, _, _ = self.names_to_path(
1676                             parts,
1677                             opts,
1678                             allow_many,
1679                             fail_on_missing,
1680                         )
1681                         path.extend(filtered_relation_path[:-1])
1682                     else:
1683                         field = opts.get_field(filtered_relation.relation_name)
1684             if field is not None:
1685                 # Fields that contain one-to-many relations with a generic
1686                 # model (like a GenericForeignKey) cannot generate reverse
1687                 # relations and therefore cannot be used for reverse querying.
1688                 if field.is_relation and not field.related_model:
1689                     raise FieldError(
1690                         "Field %r does not generate an automatic reverse "
1691                         "relation and therefore cannot be used for reverse "
1692                         "querying. If it is a GenericForeignKey, consider "
1693                         "adding a GenericRelation." % name
1694                     )
1695                 try:
1696                     model = field.model._meta.concrete_model
1697                 except AttributeError:
1698                     # QuerySet.annotate() may introduce fields that aren't
1699                     # attached to a model.
1700                     model = None
1701             else:
1702                 # We didn't find the current field, so move position back
1703                 # one step.
1704                 pos -= 1
1705                 if pos == -1 or fail_on_missing:
1706                     available = sorted(
1707                         [
1708                             *get_field_names_from_opts(opts),
1709                             *self.annotation_select,
1710                             *self._filtered_relations,
1711                         ]
1712                     )
1713                     raise FieldError(
1714                         "Cannot resolve keyword '%s' into field. "
1715                         "Choices are: %s" % (name, ", ".join(available))
1716                     )
1717                 break
1718             # Check if we need any joins for concrete inheritance cases (the
1719             # field lives in parent, but we are currently in one of its
1720             # children)
1721             if opts is not None and model is not opts.model:
1722                 path_to_parent = opts.get_path_to_parent(model)
1723                 if path_to_parent:
1724                     path.extend(path_to_parent)
1725                     cur_names_with_path[1].extend(path_to_parent)
1726                     opts = path_to_parent[-1].to_opts
1727             if hasattr(field, "path_infos"):
1728                 if filtered_relation:
1729                     pathinfos = field.get_path_info(filtered_relation)
1730                 else:
1731                     pathinfos = field.path_infos
1732                 if not allow_many:
1733                     for inner_pos, p in enumerate(pathinfos):
1734                         if p.m2m:
1735                             cur_names_with_path[1].extend(pathinfos[0 : inner_pos + 1])
1736                             names_with_path.append(cur_names_with_path)
1737                             raise MultiJoin(pos + 1, names_with_path)
1738                 last = pathinfos[-1]
1739                 path.extend(pathinfos)
1740                 final_field = last.join_field
1741                 opts = last.to_opts
1742                 targets = last.target_fields
1743                 cur_names_with_path[1].extend(pathinfos)
1744                 names_with_path.append(cur_names_with_path)
1745             else:
1746                 # Local non-relational field.
1747                 final_field = field
1748                 targets = (field,)
1749                 if fail_on_missing and pos + 1 != len(names):
1750                     raise FieldError(
1751                         "Cannot resolve keyword %r into field. Join on '%s'"
1752                         " not permitted." % (names[pos + 1], name)
1753                     )
1754                 break
1755         return path, final_field, targets, names[pos + 1 :]
1756 
1757     def setup_joins(
1758         self,
1759         names,
1760         opts,
1761         alias,
1762         can_reuse=None,
1763         allow_many=True,
1764     ):
1765         """
1766         Compute the necessary table joins for the passage through the fields
1767         given in 'names'. 'opts' is the Options class for the current model
1768         (which gives the table we are starting from), 'alias' is the alias for
1769         the table to start the joining from.
1770 
1771         The 'can_reuse' defines the reverse foreign key joins we can reuse. It
1772         can be None in which case all joins are reusable or a set of aliases
1773         that can be reused. Note that non-reverse foreign keys are always
1774         reusable when using setup_joins().
1775 
1776         If 'allow_many' is False, then any reverse foreign key seen will
1777         generate a MultiJoin exception.
1778 
1779         Return the final field involved in the joins, the target field (used
1780         for any 'where' constraint), the final 'opts' value, the joins, the
1781         field path traveled to generate the joins, and a transform function
1782         that takes a field and alias and is equivalent to `field.get_col(alias)`
1783         in the simple case but wraps field transforms if they were included in
1784         names.
1785 
1786         The target field is the field containing the concrete value. Final
1787         field can be something different, for example foreign key pointing to
1788         that value. Final field is needed for example in some value
1789         conversions (convert 'obj' in fk__id=obj to pk val using the foreign
1790         key field for example).
1791         """
1792         joins = [alias]
1793         # The transform can't be applied yet, as joins must be trimmed later.
1794         # To avoid making every caller of this method look up transforms
1795         # directly, compute transforms here and create a partial that converts
1796         # fields to the appropriate wrapped version.
1797 
1798         def final_transformer(field, alias):
1799             if not self.alias_cols:
1800                 alias = None
1801             return field.get_col(alias)
1802 
1803         # Try resolving all the names as fields first. If there's an error,
1804         # treat trailing names as lookups until a field can be resolved.
1805         last_field_exception = None
1806         for pivot in range(len(names), 0, -1):
1807             try:
1808                 path, final_field, targets, rest = self.names_to_path(
1809                     names[:pivot],
1810                     opts,
1811                     allow_many,
1812                     fail_on_missing=True,
1813                 )
1814             except FieldError as exc:
1815                 if pivot == 1:
1816                     # The first item cannot be a lookup, so it's safe
1817                     # to raise the field error here.
1818                     raise
1819                 else:
1820                     last_field_exception = exc
1821             else:
1822                 # The transforms are the remaining items that couldn't be
1823                 # resolved into fields.
1824                 transforms = names[pivot:]
1825                 break
1826         for name in transforms:
1827 
1828             def transform(field, alias, *, name, previous):
1829                 try:
1830                     wrapped = previous(field, alias)
1831                     return self.try_transform(wrapped, name)
1832                 except FieldError:
1833                     # FieldError is raised if the transform doesn't exist.
1834                     if isinstance(final_field, Field) and last_field_exception:
1835                         raise last_field_exception
1836                     else:
1837                         raise
1838 
1839             final_transformer = functools.partial(
1840                 transform, name=name, previous=final_transformer
1841             )
1842             final_transformer.has_transforms = True
1843         # Then, add the path to the query's joins. Note that we can't trim
1844         # joins at this stage - we will need the information about join type
1845         # of the trimmed joins.
1846         for join in path:
1847             if join.filtered_relation:
1848                 filtered_relation = join.filtered_relation.clone()
1849                 table_alias = filtered_relation.alias
1850             else:
1851                 filtered_relation = None
1852                 table_alias = None
1853             opts = join.to_opts
1854             if join.direct:
1855                 nullable = self.is_nullable(join.join_field)
1856             else:
1857                 nullable = True
1858             connection = self.join_class(
1859                 opts.db_table,
1860                 alias,
1861                 table_alias,
1862                 INNER,
1863                 join.join_field,
1864                 nullable,
1865                 filtered_relation=filtered_relation,
1866             )
1867             reuse = can_reuse if join.m2m else None
1868             alias = self.join(connection, reuse=reuse)
1869             joins.append(alias)
1870         return JoinInfo(final_field, targets, opts, joins, path, final_transformer)

1872     def trim_joins(self, targets, joins, path):
1873         """
1874         The 'target' parameter is the final field being joined to, 'joins'
1875         is the full list of join aliases. The 'path' contain the PathInfos
1876         used to create the joins.
1877 
1878         Return the final target field and table alias and the new active
1879         joins.
1880 
1881         Always trim any direct join if the target column is already in the
1882         previous table. Can't trim reverse joins as it's unknown if there's
1883         anything on the other side of the join.
1884         """
1885         joins = joins[:]
1886         for pos, info in enumerate(reversed(path)):
1887             if len(joins) == 1 or not info.direct:
1888                 break
1889             if info.filtered_relation:
1890                 break
1891             join_targets = {t.column for t in info.join_field.foreign_related_fields}
1892             cur_targets = {t.column for t in targets}
1893             if not cur_targets.issubset(join_targets):
1894                 break
1895             targets_dict = {
1896                 r[1].column: r[0]
1897                 for r in info.join_field.related_fields
1898                 if r[1].column in cur_targets
1899             }
1900             targets = tuple(targets_dict[t.column] for t in targets)
1901             self.unref_alias(joins.pop())
1902         return targets, joins[-1], joins

1926     def resolve_ref(self, name, allow_joins=True, reuse=None, summarize=False):
1927         annotation = self.annotations.get(name)
1928         if annotation is not None:
1929             if not allow_joins:
1930                 for alias in self._gen_col_aliases([annotation]):
1931                     if isinstance(self.alias_map[alias], Join):
1932                         raise FieldError(
1933                             "Joined field references are not permitted in this query"
1934                         )
1935             if summarize:
1936                 # Summarize currently means we are doing an aggregate() query
1937                 # which is executed as a wrapped subquery if any of the
1938                 # aggregate() elements reference an existing annotation. In
1939                 # that case we need to return a Ref to the subquery's annotation.
1940                 if name not in self.annotation_select:
1941                     raise FieldError(
1942                         "Cannot aggregate over the '%s' alias. Use annotate() "
1943                         "to promote it." % name
1944                     )
1945                 return Ref(name, self.annotation_select[name])
1946             else:
1947                 return annotation
1948         else:
1949             field_list = name.split(LOOKUP_SEP)
1950             annotation = self.annotations.get(field_list[0])
1951             if annotation is not None:
1952                 for transform in field_list[1:]:
1953                     annotation = self.try_transform(annotation, transform)
1954                 return annotation
1955             join_info = self.setup_joins(
1956                 field_list, self.get_meta(), self.get_initial_alias(), can_reuse=reuse
1957             )
1958             targets, final_alias, join_list = self.trim_joins(
1959                 join_info.targets, join_info.joins, join_info.path
1960             )
1961             if not allow_joins and len(join_list) > 1:
1962                 raise FieldError(
1963                     "Joined field references are not permitted in this query"
1964                 )
1965             if len(targets) > 1:
1966                 raise FieldError(
1967                     "Referencing multicolumn fields with F() objects isn't supported"
1968                 )
1969             # Verify that the last lookup in name is a field or a transform:
1970             # transform_function() raises FieldError if not.
1971             transform = join_info.transform_function(targets[0], final_alias)
1972             if reuse is not None:
1973                 reuse.update(join_list)
1974             return transform

1976     def split_exclude(self, filter_expr, can_reuse, names_with_path):
1977         """
1978         When doing an exclude against any kind of N-to-many relation, we need
1979         to use a subquery. This method constructs the nested query, given the
1980         original exclude filter (filter_expr) and the portion up to the first
1981         N-to-many relation field.
1982 
1983         For example, if the origin filter is ~Q(child__name='foo'), filter_expr
1984         is ('child__name', 'foo') and can_reuse is a set of joins usable for
1985         filters in the original query.
1986 
1987         We will turn this into equivalent of:
1988             WHERE NOT EXISTS(
1989                 SELECT 1
1990                 FROM child
1991                 WHERE name = 'foo' AND child.parent_id = parent.id
1992                 LIMIT 1
1993             )
1994         """
1995         # Generate the inner query.
1996         query = self.__class__(self.model)
1997         query._filtered_relations = self._filtered_relations
1998         filter_lhs, filter_rhs = filter_expr
1999         if isinstance(filter_rhs, OuterRef):
2000             filter_rhs = OuterRef(filter_rhs)
2001         elif isinstance(filter_rhs, F):
2002             filter_rhs = OuterRef(filter_rhs.name)
2003         query.add_filter(filter_lhs, filter_rhs)
2004         query.clear_ordering(force=True)
2005         # Try to have as simple as possible subquery -> trim leading joins from
2006         # the subquery.
2007         trimmed_prefix, contains_louter = query.trim_start(names_with_path)
2008 
2009         col = query.select[0]
2010         select_field = col.target
2011         alias = col.alias
2012         if alias in can_reuse:
2013             pk = select_field.model._meta.pk
2014             # Need to add a restriction so that outer query's filters are in effect for
2015             # the subquery, too.
2016             query.bump_prefix(self)
2017             lookup_class = select_field.get_lookup("exact")
2018             # Note that the query.select[0].alias is different from alias
2019             # due to bump_prefix above.
2020             lookup = lookup_class(pk.get_col(query.select[0].alias), pk.get_col(alias))
2021             query.where.add(lookup, AND)
2022             query.external_aliases[alias] = True
2023         else:
2024             lookup_class = select_field.get_lookup("exact")
2025             lookup = lookup_class(col, ResolvedOuterRef(trimmed_prefix))
2026             query.where.add(lookup, AND)
2027 
2028         condition, needed_inner = self.build_filter(Exists(query))
2029 
2030         if contains_louter:
2031             or_null_condition, _ = self.build_filter(
2032                 ("%s__isnull" % trimmed_prefix, True),
2033                 current_negated=True,
2034                 branch_negated=True,
2035                 can_reuse=can_reuse,
2036             )
2037             condition.add(or_null_condition, OR)
2038             # Note that the end result will be:
2039             #   NOT EXISTS (inner_q) OR outercol IS NULL
2040             # this might look crazy but due to how NULL works, this seems to be
2041             # correct. If the IS NULL check is removed, then if outercol
2042             # IS NULL we will not match the row.
2043         return condition, needed_inner

2056         as it makes it more Pythonic to read and write. When the SQL query is
2057         created, convert them to the appropriate offset and limit values.

2060         to the current low value and clamp both to any existing high value.

2070             else:
2071                 self.low_mark = self.low_mark + low

2311     def add_deferred_loading(self, field_names):

2313         Add the given list of model field names to the set of fields to
2314         exclude from loading from the database when automatic column selection
2315         is done. Add the new field names to any existing field names that
2316         are deferred (or removed from any existing field names that are marked
2317         as the only ones for immediate loading).
2318         """
2319         # Fields on related models are stored in the literal double-underscore
2320         # format, so that we can use a set datastructure. We do the foo__bar
2321         # splitting and handling when computing the SQL column names (as part of
2322         # get_columns()).
2323         existing, defer = self.deferred_loading
2324         if defer:
2325             # Add to existing deferred names.
2326             self.deferred_loading = existing.union(field_names), True
2327         else:
2328             # Remove names from the set of any existing "immediate load" names.
2329             if new_existing := existing.difference(field_names):
2330                 self.deferred_loading = new_existing, False
2331             else:
2332                 self.clear_deferred_loading()
2333                 if new_only := set(field_names).difference(existing):
2334                     self.deferred_loading = new_only, True

2336     def add_immediate_loading(self, field_names):
2337         """
2338         Add the given list of model field names to the set of fields to
2339         retrieve when the SQL is executed ("immediate loading" fields). The
2340         field names replace any existing immediate loading field names. If
2341         there are field names already specified for deferred loading, remove
2342         those names from the new field_names before storing the new names
2343         for immediate loading. (That is, immediate loading overrides any
2344         existing immediate values, but respects existing deferrals.)
2345         """
2346         existing, defer = self.deferred_loading
2347         field_names = set(field_names)
2348         if "pk" in field_names:
2349             field_names.remove("pk")
2350             field_names.add(self.get_meta().pk.name)
2351 
2352         if defer:
2353             # Remove any existing deferred names from the current set before
2354             # setting the new names.
2355             self.deferred_loading = field_names.difference(existing), False
2356         else:
2357             # Replace any existing "immediate load" field names.
2358             self.deferred_loading = frozenset(field_names), False

2437                 if isinstance(expr, Ref) and expr.refs not in selected:
2438                     expr = self.annotations[expr.refs]
2439                 group_by.append(expr)

2442         self.values_select = tuple(field_names)

2623     def update_join_types(self, query):
2624         """
2625         Change join types so that the generated query is as efficient as
2626         possible, but still correct. So, change as many joins as possible
2627         to INNER, but don't make OUTER joins INNER if that could remove
2628         results from the query.
2629         """
2630         to_promote = set()
2631         to_demote = set()
2632         # The effective_connector is used so that NOT (a AND b) is treated
2633         # similarly to (a OR b) for join promotion.
2634         for table, votes in self.votes.items():
2635             # We must use outer joins in OR case when the join isn't contained
2636             # in all of the joins. Otherwise the INNER JOIN itself could remove
2637             # valid results. Consider the case where a model with rel_a and
2638             # rel_b relations is queried with rel_a__col=1 | rel_b__col=2. Now,
2639             # if rel_a join doesn't produce any results is null (for example
2640             # reverse foreign key or null value in direct foreign key), and
2641             # there is a matching row in rel_b with col=2, then an INNER join
2642             # to rel_a would remove a valid match from the query. So, we need
2643             # to promote any existing INNER to LOUTER (it is possible this
2644             # promotion in turn will be demoted later on).
2645             if self.effective_connector == OR and votes < self.num_children:
2646                 to_promote.add(table)
2647             # If connector is AND and there is a filter that can match only
2648             # when there is a joinable row, then use INNER. For example, in
2649             # rel_a__col=1 & rel_b__col=2, if either of the rels produce NULL
2650             # as join output, then the col=1 or col=2 can't match (as
2651             # NULL=anything is always false).
2652             # For the OR case, if all children voted for a join to be inner,
2653             # then we can use INNER for the join. For example:
2654             #     (rel_a__col__icontains=Alex | rel_a__col__icontains=Russell)
2655             # then if rel_a doesn't produce any rows, the whole condition
2656             # can't match. Hence we can safely use INNER join.
2657             if self.effective_connector == AND or (
2658                 self.effective_connector == OR and votes == self.num_children
2659             ):
2660                 to_demote.add(table)
2661             # Finally, what happens in cases where we have:
2662             #    (rel_a__col=1|rel_b__col=2) & rel_a__col__gte=0
2663             # Now, we first generate the OR clause, and promote joins for it
2664             # in the first if branch above. Both rel_a and rel_b are promoted
2665             # to LOUTER joins. After that we do the AND case. The OR case
2666             # voted no inner joins but the rel_a__col__gte=0 votes inner join
2667             # for rel_a. We demote it back to INNER join (in AND case a single
2668             # vote is enough). The demotion is OK, if rel_a doesn't produce
2669             # rows, then the rel_a__col__gte=0 clause can't be true, and thus
2670             # the whole clause must be false. So, it is safe to use INNER
2671             # join.
2672             # Note that in this example we could just as well have the __gte
2673             # clause and the OR clause swapped. Or we could replace the __gte
2674             # clause with an OR clause containing rel_a__col=1|rel_a__col=2,
2675             # and again we could safely demote to INNER.
2676         query.promote_joins(to_promote)
2677         query.demote_joins(to_demote)

66 def _make_inset_locator(bounds, trans, parent):
67     """
68     Helper function to locate inset axes, used in
69     `.Axes.inset_axes`.
70 
71     A locator gets used in `Axes.set_aspect` to override the default
72     locations...  It is a function that takes an axes object and
73     a renderer and tells `set_aspect` where it is to be placed.
74 
75     Here *rect* is a rectangle [l, b, w, h] that specifies the
76     location for the axes in the transform given by *trans* on the
77     *parent*.
78     """
79     _bounds = mtransforms.Bbox.from_bounds(*bounds)
80     _trans = trans
81     _parent = parent
82 
83     def inset_locator(ax, renderer):
84         bbox = _bounds
85         bb = mtransforms.TransformedBbox(bbox, _trans)
86         tr = _parent.figure.transFigure.inverted()
87         bb = mtransforms.TransformedBbox(bb, tr)
88         return bb
89 
90     return inset_locator

484         Add an inset indicator to the axes.  This is a rectangle on the plot
485         at the position indicated by *bounds* that optionally has lines that
486         connect the rectangle to an inset axes
487         (`.Axes.inset_axes`).
488 
489         Warnings
490         --------
491 
492         This method is experimental as of 3.0, and the API may change.
493 
494 
495         Parameters
496         ----------
497 
498         bounds : [x0, y0, width, height]
499             Lower-left corner of rectangle to be marked, and its width
500             and height.
501 
502         inset_ax : `.Axes`
503             An optional inset axes to draw connecting lines to.  Two lines are
504             drawn connecting the indicator box to the inset axes on corners
505             chosen so as to not overlap with the indicator box.
506 
507         transform : `.Transform`
508             Transform for the rectangle co-ordinates. Defaults to
509             `ax.transAxes`, i.e. the units of *rect* are in axes-relative
510             coordinates.
511 
512         facecolor : Matplotlib color
513             Facecolor of the rectangle (default 'none').
514 
515         edgecolor : Matplotlib color
516             Color of the rectangle and color of the connecting lines.  Default
517             is '0.5'.
518 
519         alpha : number
520             Transparency of the rectangle and connector lines.  Default is 0.5.
521 
522         zorder : number
523             Drawing order of the rectangle and connector lines. Default is 4.99
524             (just below the default level of inset axes).
525 
526         **kwargs
527             Other *kwargs* are passed on to the rectangle patch.
528 
529         Returns
530         -------
531 
532         rectangle_patch : `.Patches.Rectangle`
533              Rectangle artist.
534 
535         connector_lines : 4-tuple of `.Patches.ConnectionPatch`
536             One for each of four connector lines.  Two are set with visibility
537             to *False*,  but the user can set the visibility to True if the
538             automatic choice is not deemed correct.
539 
540         """
541 
542         # to make the axes connectors work, we need to apply the aspect to
543         # the parent axes.
544         self.apply_aspect()
545 
546         if transform is None:
547             transform = self.transData
548         label = kwargs.pop('label', 'indicate_inset')
549 
550         xy = (bounds[0], bounds[1])
551         rectpatch = mpatches.Rectangle(xy, bounds[2], bounds[3],
552                 facecolor=facecolor, edgecolor=edgecolor, alpha=alpha,
553                 zorder=zorder,  label=label, transform=transform, **kwargs)
554         self.add_patch(rectpatch)
555 
556         if inset_ax is not None:
557             # want to connect the indicator to the rect....
558             connects = []
559             xr = [bounds[0], bounds[0]+bounds[2]]
560             yr = [bounds[1], bounds[1]+bounds[3]]
561             for xc in range(2):
562                 for yc in range(2):
563                     xyA = (xc, yc)
564                     xyB = (xr[xc], yr[yc])
565                     connects += [mpatches.ConnectionPatch(xyA, xyB,
566                             'axes fraction', 'data',
567                             axesA=inset_ax, axesB=self, arrowstyle="-",
568                             zorder=zorder, edgecolor=edgecolor, alpha=alpha)]
569                     self.add_patch(connects[-1])
570             # decide which two of the lines to keep visible....
571             pos = inset_ax.get_position()
572             bboxins = pos.transformed(self.figure.transFigure)
573             rectbbox = mtransforms.Bbox.from_bounds(
574                         *bounds).transformed(transform)
575             x0 = rectbbox.x0 < bboxins.x0
576             x1 = rectbbox.x1 < bboxins.x1
577             y0 = rectbbox.y0 < bboxins.y0
578             y1 = rectbbox.y1 < bboxins.y1
579             connects[0].set_visible(x0 ^ y0)
580             connects[1].set_visible(x0 == y1)
581             connects[2].set_visible(x1 == y0)
582             connects[3].set_visible(x1 ^ y1)
583 
584         return rectpatch, connects

1072         xmin, xmax : scalar or 1D array_like
1073             Respective beginning and end of each line. If scalars are

1075 
1076         colors : array_like of colors, optional, default: 'k'

1078         linestyles : {'solid', 'dashed', 'dashdot', 'dotted'}, optional
1079

1091         --------

1096         # We do the conversion first since not all unitized data is uniform
1097         # process the unit information

1099         y = self.convert_yunits(y)
1100         xmin = self.convert_xunits(xmin)
1101         xmax = self.convert_xunits(xmax)
1102 
1103         if not np.iterable(y):
1104             y = [y]
1105         if not np.iterable(xmin):
1106             xmin = [xmin]
1107         if not np.iterable(xmax):

1116         verts = [((thisxmin, thisy), (thisxmax, thisy))
1117                  for thisxmin, thisxmax, thisy in zip(xmin, xmax, y)]
1118         lines = mcoll.LineCollection(verts, colors=colors,
1119                                      linestyles=linestyles, label=label)
1120         self.add_collection(lines, autolim=False)
