1181     def _rendercursor(self):
1182         # this is a hack to figure out where the cursor should go.
1183         # we draw the text up to where the cursor should go, measure
1184         # and save its dimensions, draw the real text, then put the cursor
1185         # at the saved dimensions
1186 
1187         # This causes a single extra draw if the figure has never been rendered
1188         # yet, which should be fine as we're going to repeatedly re-render the
1189         # figure later anyways.
1190         if self.ax.figure._cachedRenderer is None:
1191             self.ax.figure.canvas.draw()
1192 
1193         text = self.text_disp.get_text()  # Save value before overwriting it.
1194         widthtext = text[:self.cursor_index]
1195         self.text_disp.set_text(widthtext or ",")
1196         bb = self.text_disp.get_window_extent()
1197         if not widthtext:  # Use the comma for the height, but keep width to 0.
1198             bb.x1 = bb.x0
1199         self.cursor.set(
1200             segments=[[(bb.x1, bb.y0), (bb.x1, bb.y1)]], visible=True)
1201         self.text_disp.set_text(text)
1202 
1203         self.ax.figure.canvas.draw()
1204 
1205     def _release(self, event):
1206         if self.ignore(event):
1207             return
1208         if event.canvas.mouse_grabber != self.ax:
1209             return
1210         event.canvas.release_mouse(self.ax)
1211 
1212     def _keypress(self, event):
1213         if self.ignore(event):
1214             return
1215         if self.capturekeystrokes:
1216             key = event.key
1217             text = self.text
1218             if len(key) == 1:
1219                 text = (text[:self.cursor_index] + key +
1220                         text[self.cursor_index:])
1221                 self.cursor_index += 1
1222             elif key == "right":
1223                 if self.cursor_index != len(text):
1224                     self.cursor_index += 1
1225             elif key == "left":
1226                 if self.cursor_index != 0:
1227                     self.cursor_index -= 1
1228             elif key == "home":
1229                 self.cursor_index = 0
1230             elif key == "end":
1231                 self.cursor_index = len(text)
1232             elif key == "backspace":
1233                 if self.cursor_index != 0:
1234                     text = (text[:self.cursor_index - 1] +
1235                             text[self.cursor_index:])
1236                     self.cursor_index -= 1
1237             elif key == "delete":
1238                 if self.cursor_index != len(self.text):
1239                     text = (text[:self.cursor_index] +
1240                             text[self.cursor_index + 1:])
1241             self.text_disp.set_text(text)
1242             self._rendercursor()
1243             if self.eventson:
1244                 self._observers.process('change', self.text)
1245                 if key in ["enter", "return"]:
1246                     self._observers.process('submit', self.text)
1247 
1248     def set_val(self, val):
1249         newval = str(val)
1250         if self.text == newval:
1251             return
1252         self.text_disp.set_text(newval)
1253         self._rendercursor()
1254         if self.eventson:
1255             self._observers.process('change', self.text)
1256             self._observers.process('submit', self.text)
1257 
1258     def begin_typing(self, x):
1259         self.capturekeystrokes = True
1260         # Disable keypress shortcuts, which may otherwise cause the figure to
1261         # be saved, closed, etc., until the user stops typing.  The way to
1262         # achieve this depends on whether toolmanager is in use.
1263         stack = ExitStack()  # Register cleanup actions when user stops typing.
1264         self._on_stop_typing = stack.close
1265         toolmanager = getattr(
1266             self.ax.figure.canvas.manager, "toolmanager", None)
1267         if toolmanager is not None:
1268             # If using toolmanager, lock keypresses, and plan to release the
1269             # lock when typing stops.
1270             toolmanager.keypresslock(self)
1271             stack.push(toolmanager.keypresslock.release, self)
1272         else:
1273             # If not using toolmanager, disable all keypress-related rcParams.
1274             # Avoid spurious warnings if keymaps are getting deprecated.
1275             with _api.suppress_matplotlib_deprecation_warning():
1276                 stack.enter_context(mpl.rc_context(
1277                     {k: [] for k in mpl.rcParams if k.startswith("keymap.")}))
1278 
1279     def stop_typing(self):
1280         if self.capturekeystrokes:
1281             self._on_stop_typing()
1282             self._on_stop_typing = None
1283             notifysubmit = True
1284         else:
1285             notifysubmit = False
1286         self.capturekeystrokes = False
1287         self.cursor.set_visible(False)
1288         self.ax.figure.canvas.draw()
1289         if notifysubmit and self.eventson:
1290             # Because process() might throw an error in the user's code, only
1291             # call it once we've already done our cleanup.
1292             self._observers.process('submit', self.text)
1293 
1294     def position_cursor(self, x):
1295         # now, we have to figure out where the cursor goes.
1296         # approximate it based on assuming all characters the same length
1297         if len(self.text) == 0:
1298             self.cursor_index = 0
1299         else:
1300             bb = self.text_disp.get_window_extent()
1301             ratio = np.clip((x - bb.x0) / bb.width, 0, 1)
1302             self.cursor_index = int(len(self.text) * ratio)
1303         self._rendercursor()
1304 
1305     def _click(self, event):
1306         if self.ignore(event):
1307             return
1308         if event.inaxes != self.ax:
1309             self.stop_typing()
1310             return
1311         if not self.eventson:
1312             return
1313         if event.canvas.mouse_grabber != self.ax:
1314             event.canvas.grab_mouse(self.ax)
1315         if not self.capturekeystrokes:
1316             self.begin_typing(event.x)
1317         self.position_cursor(event.x)
1318 
1319     def _resize(self, event):
1320         self.stop_typing()
1321 
1322     def _motion(self, event):
1323         if self.ignore(event):
1324             return
1325         c = self.hovercolor if event.inaxes == self.ax else self.color
1326         if not colors.same_color(c, self.ax.get_facecolor()):
1327             self.ax.set_facecolor(c)
1328             if self.drawon:
1329                 self.ax.figure.canvas.draw()
1330 
1331     def on_text_change(self, func):
1332         """
1333         When the text changes, call this *func* with event.
1334 
1335         A connection id is returned which can be used to disconnect.
1336         """
1337         return self._observers.connect('change', lambda text: func(text))
1338 
1339     def on_submit(self, func):
1340         """
1341         When the user hits enter or leaves the submission box, call this
1342         *func* with event.
1343 
1344         A connection id is returned which can be used to disconnect.
1345         """
1346         return self._observers.connect('submit', lambda text: func(text))
1347 
1348     def disconnect(self, cid):
1349         """Remove the observer with connection id *cid*."""
1350         self._observers.disconnect(cid)

1353 class RadioButtons(AxesWidget):
1354     """
1355     A GUI neutral radio button.
1356 
1357     For the buttons to remain responsive you must keep a reference to this
1358     object.
1359 
1360     Connect to the RadioButtons with the `.on_clicked` method.
1361 
1362     Attributes
1363     ----------
1364     ax : `~matplotlib.axes.Axes`
1365         The parent axes for the widget.
1366     activecolor : color
1367         The color of the selected button.
1368     labels : list of `.Text`
1369         The button labels.
1370     circles : list of `~.patches.Circle`
1371         The buttons.
1372     value_selected : str
1373         The label text of the currently selected button.
1374     """
1375 
1376     def __init__(self, ax, labels, active=0, activecolor='blue'):
1377         """
1378         Add radio buttons to an `~.axes.Axes`.
1379 
1380         Parameters
1381         ----------
1382         ax : `~matplotlib.axes.Axes`
1383             The axes to add the buttons to.
1384         labels : list of str
1385             The button labels.
1386         active : int
1387             The index of the initially selected button.
1388         activecolor : color
1389             The color of the selected button.
1390         """
1391         super().__init__(ax)
1392         self.activecolor = activecolor
1393         self.value_selected = None
1394 
1395         ax.set_xticks([])
1396         ax.set_yticks([])
1397         ax.set_navigate(False)
1398         dy = 1. / (len(labels) + 1)
1399         ys = np.linspace(1 - dy, dy, len(labels))
1400         cnt = 0
1401         axcolor = ax.get_facecolor()
1402 
1403         # scale the radius of the circle with the spacing between each one
1404         circle_radius = dy / 2 - 0.01
1405         # default to hard-coded value if the radius becomes too large
1406         circle_radius = min(circle_radius, 0.05)
1407 
1408         self.labels = []
1409         self.circles = []
1410         for y, label in zip(ys, labels):
1411             t = ax.text(0.25, y, label, transform=ax.transAxes,
1412                         horizontalalignment='left',
1413                         verticalalignment='center')
1414 
1415             if cnt == active:
1416                 self.value_selected = label
1417                 facecolor = activecolor
1418             else:
1419                 facecolor = axcolor
1420 
1421             p = Circle(xy=(0.15, y), radius=circle_radius, edgecolor='black',
1422                        facecolor=facecolor, transform=ax.transAxes)
1423 
1424             self.labels.append(t)
1425             self.circles.append(p)
1426             ax.add_patch(p)
1427             cnt += 1
1428 
1429         self.connect_event('button_press_event', self._clicked)
1430 
1431         self._observers = cbook.CallbackRegistry()
1432 
1433     cnt = _api.deprecated("3.4")(property(  # Not real, but close enough.
1434         lambda self: len(self._observers.callbacks['clicked'])))
1435     observers = _api.deprecated("3.4")(property(
1436         lambda self: self._observers.callbacks['clicked']))
1437 
1438     def _clicked(self, event):
1439         if self.ignore(event) or event.button != 1 or event.inaxes != self.ax:
1440             return
1441         pclicked = self.ax.transAxes.inverted().transform((event.x, event.y))
1442         distances = {}
1443         for i, (p, t) in enumerate(zip(self.circles, self.labels)):
1444             if (t.get_window_extent().contains(event.x, event.y)
1445                     or np.linalg.norm(pclicked - p.center) < p.radius):
1446                 distances[i] = np.linalg.norm(pclicked - p.center)
1447         if len(distances) > 0:
1448             closest = min(distances, key=distances.get)
1449             self.set_active(closest)
1450 
1451     def set_active(self, index):
1452         """
1453         Select button with number *index*.
1454 
1455         Callbacks will be triggered if :attr:`eventson` is True.
1456         """
1457         if index not in range(len(self.labels)):
1458             raise ValueError(f'Invalid RadioButton index: {index}')
1459 
1460         self.value_selected = self.labels[index].get_text()
1461 
1462         for i, p in enumerate(self.circles):
1463             if i == index:
1464                 color = self.activecolor
1465             else:
1466                 color = self.ax.get_facecolor()
1467             p.set_facecolor(color)
1468 
1469         if self.drawon:
1470             self.ax.figure.canvas.draw()
1471 
1472         if self.eventson:
1473             self._observers.process('clicked', self.labels[index].get_text())
1474 
1475     def on_clicked(self, func):
1476         """
1477         Connect the callback function *func* to button click events.
1478 
1479         Returns a connection id, which can be used to disconnect the callback.
1480         """
1481         return self._observers.connect('clicked', func)
1482 
1483     def disconnect(self, cid):
1484         """Remove the observer with connection id *cid*."""
1485         self._observers.disconnect(cid)

1488 class SubplotTool(Widget):
1489     """
1490     A tool to adjust the subplot params of a `matplotlib.figure.Figure`.
1491     """
1492 
1493     def __init__(self, targetfig, toolfig):
1494         """
1495         Parameters
1496         ----------
1497         targetfig : `.Figure`
1498             The figure instance to adjust.
1499         toolfig : `.Figure`
1500             The figure instance to embed the subplot tool into.
1501         """
1502 
1503         self.figure = toolfig
1504         self.targetfig = targetfig
1505         toolfig.subplots_adjust(left=0.2, right=0.9)
1506         toolfig.suptitle("Click on slider to adjust subplot param")
1507 
1508         self._sliders = []
1509         names = ["left", "bottom", "right", "top", "wspace", "hspace"]
1510         # The last subplot, removed below, keeps space for the "Reset" button.
1511         for name, ax in zip(names, toolfig.subplots(len(names) + 1)):
1512             ax.set_navigate(False)
1513             slider = Slider(ax, name,
1514                             0, 1, getattr(targetfig.subplotpars, name))
1515             slider.on_changed(self._on_slider_changed)
1516             self._sliders.append(slider)
1517         toolfig.axes[-1].remove()
1518         (self.sliderleft, self.sliderbottom, self.sliderright, self.slidertop,
1519          self.sliderwspace, self.sliderhspace) = self._sliders
1520         for slider in [self.sliderleft, self.sliderbottom,
1521                        self.sliderwspace, self.sliderhspace]:
1522             slider.closedmax = False
1523         for slider in [self.sliderright, self.slidertop]:
1524             slider.closedmin = False
1525 
1526         # constraints
1527         self.sliderleft.slidermax = self.sliderright
1528         self.sliderright.slidermin = self.sliderleft
1529         self.sliderbottom.slidermax = self.slidertop
1530         self.slidertop.slidermin = self.sliderbottom
1531 
1532         bax = toolfig.add_axes([0.8, 0.05, 0.15, 0.075])
1533         self.buttonreset = Button(bax, 'Reset')
1534         self.buttonreset.on_clicked(self._on_reset)
1535 
1536     def _on_slider_changed(self, _):
1537         self.targetfig.subplots_adjust(
1538             **{slider.label.get_text(): slider.val
1539                for slider in self._sliders})
1540         if self.drawon:
1541             self.targetfig.canvas.draw()
1542 
1543     def _on_reset(self, event):
1544         with ExitStack() as stack:
1545             # Temporarily disable drawing on self and self's sliders, and
1546             # disconnect slider events (as the subplotparams can be temporarily
1547             # invalid, depending on the order in which they are restored).
1548             stack.enter_context(cbook._setattr_cm(self, drawon=False))
1549             for slider in self._sliders:
1550                 stack.enter_context(
1551                     cbook._setattr_cm(slider, drawon=False, eventson=False))
1552             # Reset the slider to the initial position.
1553             for slider in self._sliders:
1554                 slider.reset()
1555         if self.drawon:
1556             event.canvas.draw()  # Redraw the subplottool canvas.
1557         self._on_slider_changed(None)  # Apply changes to the target window.

1560 class Cursor(AxesWidget):
1561     """
1562     A crosshair cursor that spans the axes and moves with mouse cursor.
1563 
1564     For the cursor to remain responsive you must keep a reference to it.
1565 
1566     Parameters
1567     ----------
1568     ax : `matplotlib.axes.Axes`
1569         The `~.axes.Axes` to attach the cursor to.
1570     horizOn : bool, default: True
1571         Whether to draw the horizontal line.
1572     vertOn : bool, default: True
1573         Whether to draw the vertical line.
1574     useblit : bool, default: False
1575         Use blitting for faster drawing if supported by the backend.
1576 
1577     Other Parameters
1578     ----------------
1579     **lineprops
1580         `.Line2D` properties that control the appearance of the lines.
1581         See also `~.Axes.axhline`.

1583     Examples
1584     --------
1585     See :doc:`/gallery/widgets/cursor`.

1587 
1588     def __init__(self, ax, horizOn=True, vertOn=True, useblit=False,
1589                  **lineprops):
1590         super().__init__(ax)
1591 
1592         self.connect_event('motion_notify_event', self.onmove)
1593         self.connect_event('draw_event', self.clear)
1594 
1595         self.visible = True
1596         self.horizOn = horizOn
1597         self.vertOn = vertOn
1598         self.useblit = useblit and self.canvas.supports_blit
1599 
1600         if self.useblit:
1601             lineprops['animated'] = True
1602         self.lineh = ax.axhline(ax.get_ybound()[0], visible=False, **lineprops)
1603         self.linev = ax.axvline(ax.get_xbound()[0], visible=False, **lineprops)
1604 
1605         self.background = None
1606         self.needclear = False
1607 
1608     def clear(self, event):
1609         """Internal event handler to clear the cursor."""
1610         if self.ignore(event):
1611             return
1612         if self.useblit:
1613             self.background = self.canvas.copy_from_bbox(self.ax.bbox)
1614         self.linev.set_visible(False)
1615         self.lineh.set_visible(False)
1616 
1617     def onmove(self, event):
1618         """Internal event handler to draw the cursor when the mouse moves."""
1619         if self.ignore(event):
1620             return
1621         if not self.canvas.widgetlock.available(self):
1622             return
1623         if event.inaxes != self.ax:
1624             self.linev.set_visible(False)
1625             self.lineh.set_visible(False)
1626 
1627             if self.needclear:
1628                 self.canvas.draw()
1629                 self.needclear = False
1630             return
1631         self.needclear = True
1632         if not self.visible:
1633             return
1634         self.linev.set_xdata((event.xdata, event.xdata))
1635 
1636         self.lineh.set_ydata((event.ydata, event.ydata))
1637         self.linev.set_visible(self.visible and self.vertOn)
1638         self.lineh.set_visible(self.visible and self.horizOn)
1639 
1640         self._update()
1641 
1642     def _update(self):
1643         if self.useblit:
1644             if self.background is not None:
1645                 self.canvas.restore_region(self.background)
1646             self.ax.draw_artist(self.linev)
1647             self.ax.draw_artist(self.lineh)
1648             self.canvas.blit(self.ax.bbox)
1649         else:
1650             self.canvas.draw_idle()
1651         return False

1654 class MultiCursor(Widget):
1655     """
1656     Provide a vertical (default) and/or horizontal line cursor shared between
1657     multiple axes.
1658 
1659     For the cursor to remain responsive you must keep a reference to it.
1660 
1661     Example usage::
1662 
1663         from matplotlib.widgets import MultiCursor
1664         import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
1665         import numpy as np
1666 
1667         fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(nrows=2, sharex=True)
1668         t = np.arange(0.0, 2.0, 0.01)
1669         ax1.plot(t, np.sin(2*np.pi*t))
1670         ax2.plot(t, np.sin(4*np.pi*t))
1671 
1672         multi = MultiCursor(fig.canvas, (ax1, ax2), color='r', lw=1,
1673                             horizOn=False, vertOn=True)
1674         plt.show()
1675 
1676     """
1677     def __init__(self, canvas, axes, useblit=True, horizOn=False, vertOn=True,
1678                  **lineprops):
1679 
1680         self.canvas = canvas
1681         self.axes = axes
1682         self.horizOn = horizOn
1683         self.vertOn = vertOn
1684 
1685         xmin, xmax = axes[-1].get_xlim()
1686         ymin, ymax = axes[-1].get_ylim()
1687         xmid = 0.5 * (xmin + xmax)
1688         ymid = 0.5 * (ymin + ymax)
1689 
1690         self.visible = True
1691         self.useblit = useblit and self.canvas.supports_blit
1692         self.background = None
1693         self.needclear = False
1694 
1695         if self.useblit:
1696             lineprops['animated'] = True
1697 
1698         if vertOn:
1699             self.vlines = [ax.axvline(xmid, visible=False, **lineprops)
1700                            for ax in axes]
1701         else:
1702             self.vlines = []
1703 
1704         if horizOn:
1705             self.hlines = [ax.axhline(ymid, visible=False, **lineprops)
1706                            for ax in axes]
1707         else:
1708             self.hlines = []
1709 
1710         self.connect()
1711 
1712     def connect(self):
1713         """Connect events."""
1714         self._cidmotion = self.canvas.mpl_connect('motion_notify_event',
1715                                                   self.onmove)
1716         self._ciddraw = self.canvas.mpl_connect('draw_event', self.clear)
1717 
1718     def disconnect(self):
1719         """Disconnect events."""
1720         self.canvas.mpl_disconnect(self._cidmotion)
1721         self.canvas.mpl_disconnect(self._ciddraw)
1722 
1723     def clear(self, event):
1724         """Clear the cursor."""
1725         if self.ignore(event):
1726             return
1727         if self.useblit:
1728             self.background = (
1729                 self.canvas.copy_from_bbox(self.canvas.figure.bbox))
1730         for line in self.vlines + self.hlines:
1731             line.set_visible(False)
1732 
1733     def onmove(self, event):
1734         if self.ignore(event):
1735             return
1736         if event.inaxes not in self.axes:
1737             return
1738         if not self.canvas.widgetlock.available(self):
1739             return
1740         self.needclear = True
1741         if not self.visible:
1742             return
1743         if self.vertOn:
1744             for line in self.vlines:
1745                 line.set_xdata((event.xdata, event.xdata))
1746                 line.set_visible(self.visible)
1747         if self.horizOn:
1748             for line in self.hlines:
1749                 line.set_ydata((event.ydata, event.ydata))
1750                 line.set_visible(self.visible)
1751         self._update()

2462                  'linestyle': 'none', 'alpha': 0.5, 'visible': False,
2463                  'label': '_nolegend_',
2464                  **cbook.normalize_kwargs(marker_props, Line2D._alias_map)}

2477     def set_data(self, pts, y=None):
2478         """Set x and y positions of handles."""

2490     def closest(self, x, y):
2491         """Return index and pixel distance to closest index."""
2492         pts = np.column_stack([self.x, self.y])
2493         # Transform data coordinates to pixel coordinates.
2494         pts = self.ax.transData.transform(pts)
2495         diff = pts - [x, y]

2497         min_index = np.argmin(dist)

2755     def _onmove(self, event):

2757         # resize an existing shape

2760             if self._active_handle in ['E', 'W'] + self._corner_order:
2761                 x1 = event.xdata
2762             if self._active_handle in ['N', 'S'] + self._corner_order:
2763                 y1 = event.ydata
2764 
2765         # move existing shape
2766         elif (('move' in self._state or self._active_handle == 'C' or
2767                (self.drag_from_anywhere and self._contains(event))) and
2768               self._extents_on_press is not None):
2769             x0, x1, y0, y1 = self._extents_on_press
2770             dx = event.xdata - self._eventpress.xdata
2771             dy = event.ydata - self._eventpress.ydata
2772             x0 += dx
2773             x1 += dx
2774             y0 += dy
2775             y1 += dy
2776 
2777         # new shape
2778         else:
2779             center = [self._eventpress.xdata, self._eventpress.ydata]
2780             center_pix = [self._eventpress.x, self._eventpress.y]
2781             dx = (event.xdata - center[0]) / 2.
2782             dy = (event.ydata - center[1]) / 2.
2783 
2784             # square shape
2785             if 'square' in self._state:
2786                 dx_pix = abs(event.x - center_pix[0])
2787                 dy_pix = abs(event.y - center_pix[1])
2788                 if not dx_pix:
2789                     return
2790                 maxd = max(abs(dx_pix), abs(dy_pix))
2791                 if abs(dx_pix) < maxd:
2792                     dx *= maxd / (abs(dx_pix) + 1e-6)
2793                 if abs(dy_pix) < maxd:
2794                     dy *= maxd / (abs(dy_pix) + 1e-6)
2795 
2796             # from center
2797             if 'center' in self._state:
2798                 dx *= 2
2799                 dy *= 2
2800 
2801             # from corner
2802             else:
2803                 center[0] += dx
2804                 center[1] += dy
2805 
2806             x0, x1, y0, y1 = (center[0] - dx, center[0] + dx,
2807                               center[1] - dy, center[1] + dy)
2808 
2809         self.extents = x0, x1, y0, y1

2891     def _set_active_handle(self, event):

2904             self._active_handle = 'C'
2905         elif c_dist > self.maxdist and e_dist > self.maxdist:

3 drawing legends associated with axes and/or figures.

5 .. important::

16 defined in the :mod:`~matplotlib.legend_handler` module. While not all artist
17 types are covered by the default legend handlers, custom legend handlers can be

53     def __init__(self, legend, use_blit=False, update="loc"):
54         """
55         Wrapper around a `.Legend` to support mouse dragging.
56 
57         Parameters
58         ----------
59         legend : `.Legend`
60             The `.Legend` instance to wrap.
61         use_blit : bool, optional
62             Use blitting for faster image composition. For details see
63             :ref:`func-animation`.
64         update : {'loc', 'bbox'}, optional
65             If "loc", update the *loc* parameter of the legend upon finalizing.
66             If "bbox", update the *bbox_to_anchor* parameter.
67         """
68         self.legend = legend
69 
70         _api.check_in_list(["loc", "bbox"], update=update)
71         self._update = update
72 
73         super().__init__(legend, legend._legend_box, use_blit=use_blit)
74 
75     def finalize_offset(self):
76         if self._update == "loc":
77             self._update_loc(self.get_loc_in_canvas())
78         elif self._update == "bbox":
79             self._bbox_to_anchor(self.get_loc_in_canvas())
80 
81     def _update_loc(self, loc_in_canvas):
82         bbox = self.legend.get_bbox_to_anchor()
83         # if bbox has zero width or height, the transformation is
84         # ill-defined. Fall back to the default bbox_to_anchor.
85         if bbox.width == 0 or bbox.height == 0:
86             self.legend.set_bbox_to_anchor(None)
87             bbox = self.legend.get_bbox_to_anchor()
88         _bbox_transform = BboxTransformFrom(bbox)
89         self.legend._loc = tuple(_bbox_transform.transform(loc_in_canvas))
90 
91     def _update_bbox_to_anchor(self, loc_in_canvas):
92         loc_in_bbox = self.legend.axes.transAxes.transform(loc_in_canvas)
93         self.legend.set_bbox_to_anchor(loc_in_bbox)

580     def _findoffset(self, width, height, xdescent, ydescent, renderer):
581         """Helper function to locate the legend."""
582 
583         if self._loc == 0:  # "best".
584             x, y = self._find_best_position(width, height, renderer)
585         elif self._loc in Legend.codes.values():  # Fixed location.
586             bbox = Bbox.from_bounds(0, 0, width, height)
587             x, y = self._get_anchored_bbox(self._loc, bbox,
588                                            self.get_bbox_to_anchor(),
589                                            renderer)
590         else:  # Axes or figure coordinates.
591             fx, fy = self._loc
592             bbox = self.get_bbox_to_anchor()
593             x, y = bbox.x0 + bbox.width * fx, bbox.y0 + bbox.height * fy
594 
595         return x + xdescent, y + ydescent

686     def get_legend_handler(legend_handler_map, orig_handle):
687         """
688         Return a legend handler from *legend_handler_map* that
689         corresponds to *orig_handler*.
690 
691         *legend_handler_map* should be a dictionary object (that is
692         returned by the get_legend_handler_map method).
693 
694         It first checks if the *orig_handle* itself is a key in the
695         *legend_handler_map* and return the associated value.
696         Otherwise, it checks for each of the classes in its
697         method-resolution-order. If no matching key is found, it
698         returns ``None``.
699         """
700         try:
701             return legend_handler_map[orig_handle]
702         except (TypeError, KeyError):  # TypeError if unhashable.
703             pass
704         for handle_type in type(orig_handle).mro():
705             try:
706                 return legend_handler_map[handle_type]
707             except KeyError:
708                 pass
709         return None

711     def _init_legend_box(self, handles, labels, markerfirst=True):
712         """
713         Initialize the legend_box. The legend_box is an instance of
714         the OffsetBox, which is packed with legend handles and
715         texts. Once packed, their location is calculated during the
716         drawing time.
717         """
718 
719         fontsize = self._fontsize
720 
721         # legend_box is a HPacker, horizontally packed with
722         # columns. Each column is a VPacker, vertically packed with
723         # legend items. Each legend item is HPacker packed with
724         # legend handleBox and labelBox. handleBox is an instance of
725         # offsetbox.DrawingArea which contains legend handle. labelBox
726         # is an instance of offsetbox.TextArea which contains legend
727         # text.
728 
729         text_list = []  # the list of text instances
730         handle_list = []  # the list of handle instances
731         handles_and_labels = []
732 
733         label_prop = dict(verticalalignment='baseline',
734                           horizontalalignment='left',
735                           fontproperties=self.prop,
736                           )
737 
738         # The approximate height and descent of text. These values are
739         # only used for plotting the legend handle.
740         descent = 0.35 * fontsize * (self.handleheight - 0.7)
741         # 0.35 and 0.7 are just heuristic numbers and may need to be improved.
742         height = fontsize * self.handleheight - descent
743         # each handle needs to be drawn inside a box of (x, y, w, h) =
744         # (0, -descent, width, height).  And their coordinates should
745         # be given in the display coordinates.
746 
747         # The transformation of each handle will be automatically set
748         # to self.get_transform(). If the artist does not use its
749         # default transform (e.g., Collections), you need to
750         # manually set their transform to the self.get_transform().
751         legend_handler_map = self.get_legend_handler_map()
752 
753         for orig_handle, lab in zip(handles, labels):
754             handler = self.get_legend_handler(legend_handler_map, orig_handle)
755             if handler is None:
756                 _api.warn_external(
757                     "Legend does not support {!r} instances.\nA proxy artist "
758                     "may be used instead.\nSee: "
759                     "https://matplotlib.org/users/legend_guide.html"
760                     "#creating-artists-specifically-for-adding-to-the-legend-"
761                     "aka-proxy-artists".format(orig_handle))
762                 # We don't have a handle for this artist, so we just defer
763                 # to None.
764                 handle_list.append(None)
765             else:
766                 textbox = TextArea(lab, textprops=label_prop,
767                                    multilinebaseline=True)
768                 handlebox = DrawingArea(width=self.handlelength * fontsize,
769                                         height=height,
770                                         xdescent=0., ydescent=descent)
771 
772                 text_list.append(textbox._text)
773                 # Create the artist for the legend which represents the
774                 # original artist/handle.
775                 handle_list.append(handler.legend_artist(self, orig_handle,
776                                                          fontsize, handlebox))
777                 handles_and_labels.append((handlebox, textbox))
778 
779         if handles_and_labels:
780             # We calculate number of rows in each column. The first
781             # (num_largecol) columns will have (nrows+1) rows, and remaining
782             # (num_smallcol) columns will have (nrows) rows.
783             ncol = min(self._ncol, len(handles_and_labels))
784             nrows, num_largecol = divmod(len(handles_and_labels), ncol)
785             num_smallcol = ncol - num_largecol
786             # starting index of each column and number of rows in it.
787             rows_per_col = [nrows + 1] * num_largecol + [nrows] * num_smallcol
788             start_idxs = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(rows_per_col)[:-1]])
789             cols = zip(start_idxs, rows_per_col)
790         else:
791             cols = []
792 
793         columnbox = []
794         for i0, di in cols:
795             # pack handleBox and labelBox into itemBox
796             itemBoxes = [HPacker(pad=0,
797                                  sep=self.handletextpad * fontsize,
798                                  children=[h, t] if markerfirst else [t, h],
799                                  align="baseline")
800                          for h, t in handles_and_labels[i0:i0 + di]]
801             # pack columnBox
802             alignment = "baseline" if markerfirst else "right"
803             columnbox.append(VPacker(pad=0,
804                                      sep=self.labelspacing * fontsize,
805                                      align=alignment,
806                                      children=itemBoxes))
807 
808         mode = "expand" if self._mode == "expand" else "fixed"
809         sep = self.columnspacing * fontsize
810         self._legend_handle_box = HPacker(pad=0,
811                                           sep=sep, align="baseline",
812                                           mode=mode,
813                                           children=columnbox)
814         self._legend_title_box = TextArea("")
815         self._legend_box = VPacker(pad=self.borderpad * fontsize,
816                                    sep=self.labelspacing * fontsize,
817                                    align="center",
818                                    children=[self._legend_title_box,
819                                              self._legend_handle_box])
820         self._legend_box.set_figure(self.figure)
821         self._legend_box.axes = self.axes
822         self.texts = text_list
823         self.legendHandles = handle_list
824 
825     def _auto_legend_data(self):
826         """
827         Return display coordinates for hit testing for "best" positioning.
828 
829         Returns
830         -------
831         bboxes
832             List of bounding boxes of all patches.
833         lines
834             List of `.Path` corresponding to each line.
835         offsets
836             List of (x, y) offsets of all collection.
837         """
838         assert self.isaxes  # always holds, as this is only called internally
839         bboxes = []
840         lines = []
841         offsets = []
842         for artist in self.parent._children:
843             if isinstance(artist, Line2D):
844                 lines.append(
845                     artist.get_transform().transform_path(artist.get_path()))
846             elif isinstance(artist, Rectangle):
847                 bboxes.append(
848                     artist.get_bbox().transformed(artist.get_data_transform()))

850                 bboxes.append(
851                     artist.get_path().get_extents(artist.get_transform()))
852             elif isinstance(artist, Collection):
853                 _, transOffset, hoffsets, _ = artist._prepare_points()
854                 for offset in transOffset.transform(hoffsets):
855                     offsets.append(offset)
856         return bboxes, lines, offsets

1012     def _find_best_position(self, width, height, renderer, consider=None):
1013         """
1014         Determine the best location to place the legend.
1015 
1016         *consider* is a list of ``(x, y)`` pairs to consider as a potential
1017         lower-left corner of the legend. All are display coords.
1018         """
1019         assert self.isaxes  # always holds, as this is only called internally
1020 
1021         start_time = time.perf_counter()
1022 
1023         bboxes, lines, offsets = self._auto_legend_data()
1024 
1025         bbox = Bbox.from_bounds(0, 0, width, height)
1026         if consider is None:
1027             consider = [self._get_anchored_bbox(x, bbox,
1028                                                 self.get_bbox_to_anchor(),
1029                                                 renderer)
1030                         for x in range(1, len(self.codes))]
1031 
1032         candidates = []
1033         for idx, (l, b) in enumerate(consider):
1034             legendBox = Bbox.from_bounds(l, b, width, height)
1035             badness = 0
1036             # XXX TODO: If markers are present, it would be good to take them
1037             # into account when checking vertex overlaps in the next line.
1038             badness = (sum(legendBox.count_contains(line.vertices)
1039                            for line in lines)
1040                        + legendBox.count_contains(offsets)
1041                        + legendBox.count_overlaps(bboxes)
1042                        + sum(line.intersects_bbox(legendBox, filled=False)
1043                              for line in lines))
1044             if badness == 0:
1045                 return l, b
1046             # Include the index to favor lower codes in case of a tie.
1047             candidates.append((badness, idx, (l, b)))
1048 
1049         _, _, (l, b) = min(candidates)
1050 
1051         if self._loc_used_default and time.perf_counter() - start_time > 1:
1052             _api.warn_external(
1053                 'Creating legend with loc="best" can be slow with large '
1054                 'amounts of data.')
1055 
1056         return l, b
1057

1116             *ax.containers]

1121                     *(a for a in axx._children
1122                       if isinstance(a, (Line2D, Patch, Collection))),

1128         handler_map = handler_map.copy()
1129         handler_map.update(legend_handler_map)

1132 
1133     for handle in handles_original:
1134         label = handle.get_label()

1155 def _parse_legend_args(axs, *args, handles=None, labels=None, **kwargs):
1156     """
1157     Get the handles and labels from the calls to either ``figure.legend``
1158     or ``axes.legend``.
1159 
1160     The parser is a bit involved because we support::
1161 
1162         legend()
1163         legend(labels)
1164         legend(handles, labels)
1165         legend(labels=labels)
1166         legend(handles=handles)
1167         legend(handles=handles, labels=labels)
1168 
1169     The behavior for a mixture of positional and keyword handles and labels
1170     is undefined and issues a warning.
1171 
1172     Parameters
1173     ----------
1174     axs : list of `.Axes`
1175         If handles are not given explicitly, the artists in these Axes are
1176         used as handles.
1177     *args : tuple
1178         Positional parameters passed to ``legend()``.
1179     handles
1180         The value of the keyword argument ``legend(handles=...)``, or *None*
1181         if that keyword argument was not used.
1182     labels
1183         The value of the keyword argument ``legend(labels=...)``, or *None*
1184         if that keyword argument was not used.
1185     **kwargs
1186         All other keyword arguments passed to ``legend()``.
1187 
1188     Returns
1189     -------
1190     handles : list of `.Artist`
1191         The legend handles.
1192     labels : list of str
1193         The legend labels.
1194     extra_args : tuple
1195         *args* with positional handles and labels removed.
1196     kwargs : dict
1197         *kwargs* with keywords handles and labels removed.
1198 
1199     """
1200     log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
1201 
1202     handlers = kwargs.get('handler_map', {}) or {}
1203     extra_args = ()
1204 
1205     if (handles is not None or labels is not None) and args:
1206         _api.warn_external("You have mixed positional and keyword arguments, "
1207                            "some input may be discarded.")
1208 
1209     # if got both handles and labels as kwargs, make same length
1210     if handles and labels:

405 def date2num(d):
406     """
407     Convert datetime objects to Matplotlib dates.
408 
409     Parameters
410     ----------
411     d : `datetime.datetime` or `numpy.datetime64` or sequences of these
412 
413     Returns
414     -------
415     float or sequence of floats
416         Number of days since the epoch.  See `.get_epoch` for the
417         epoch, which can be changed by :rc:`date.epoch` or `.set_epoch`.  If
418         the epoch is "1970-01-01T00:00:00" (default) then noon Jan 1 1970
419         ("1970-01-01T12:00:00") returns 0.5.
420 
421     Notes
422     -----
423     The Gregorian calendar is assumed; this is not universal practice.
424     For details see the module docstring.
425     """
426     if hasattr(d, "values"):
427         # this unpacks pandas series or dataframes...
428         d = d.values
429 
430     # make an iterable, but save state to unpack later:
431     iterable = np.iterable(d)
432     if not iterable:
433         d = [d]
434 
435     d = np.asarray(d)
436     # convert to datetime64 arrays, if not already:
437     if not np.issubdtype(d.dtype, np.datetime64):
438         # datetime arrays
439         if not d.size:
440             # deals with an empty array...
441             return d
442         tzi = getattr(d[0], 'tzinfo', None)
443         if tzi is not None:
444             # make datetime naive:
445             d = [dt.astimezone(UTC).replace(tzinfo=None) for dt in d]
446             d = np.asarray(d)
447         d = d.astype('datetime64[us]')
448 
449     d = _dt64_to_ordinalf(d)
450 
451     return d if iterable else d[0]
452

454 def julian2num(j):
455     """
456     Convert a Julian date (or sequence) to a Matplotlib date (or sequence).
457 
458     Parameters
459     ----------
460     j : float or sequence of floats
461         Julian dates (days relative to 4713 BC Jan 1, 12:00:00 Julian
462         calendar or 4714 BC Nov 24, 12:00:00, proleptic Gregorian calendar).
463 
464     Returns
465     -------
466     float or sequence of floats
467         Matplotlib dates (days relative to `.get_epoch`).
468     """
469     ep = np.datetime64(get_epoch(), 'h').astype(float) / 24.
470     ep0 = np.datetime64('0000-12-31T00:00:00', 'h').astype(float) / 24.
471     # Julian offset defined above is relative to 0000-12-31, but we need
472     # relative to our current epoch:
473     dt = JULIAN_OFFSET - ep0 + ep
474     return np.subtract(j, dt)  # Handles both scalar & nonscalar j.

477 def num2julian(n):

480 
481     Parameters

483     n : float or sequence of floats
484         Matplotlib dates (days relative to `.get_epoch`).
485 
486     Returns
487     -------
488     float or sequence of floats
489         Julian dates (days relative to 4713 BC Jan 1, 12:00:00).
490     """
491     ep = np.datetime64(get_epoch(), 'h').astype(float) / 24.
492     ep0 = np.datetime64('0000-12-31T00:00:00', 'h').astype(float) / 24.
493     # Julian offset defined above is relative to 0000-12-31, but we need
494     # relative to our current epoch:
495     dt = JULIAN_OFFSET - ep0 + ep
496     return np.add(n, dt)  # Handles both scalar & nonscalar j.

554 def drange(dstart, dend, delta):
555     """
556     Return a sequence of equally spaced Matplotlib dates.
557 
558     The dates start at *dstart* and reach up to, but not including *dend*.
559     They are spaced by *delta*.
560 
561     Parameters
562     ----------
563     dstart, dend : `~datetime.datetime`
564         The date limits.
565     delta : `datetime.timedelta`
566         Spacing of the dates.
567 
568     Returns
569     -------
570     `numpy.array`
571         A list floats representing Matplotlib dates.
572 
573     """
574     f1 = date2num(dstart)
575     f2 = date2num(dend)
576     step = delta.total_seconds() / SEC_PER_DAY
577 
578     # calculate the difference between dend and dstart in times of delta
579     num = int(np.ceil((f2 - f1) / step))
580 
581     # calculate end of the interval which will be generated
582     dinterval_end = dstart + num * delta
583 
584     # ensure, that an half open interval will be generated [dstart, dend)
585     if dinterval_end >= dend:
586         # if the endpoint is greater than dend, just subtract one delta
587         dinterval_end -= delta
588         num -= 1
589 
590     f2 = date2num(dinterval_end)  # new float-endpoint
591     return np.linspace(f1, f2, num + 1)
592

594 def _wrap_in_tex(text):
595     p = r'([a-zA-Z]+)'
596     ret_text = re.sub(p, r'}$\1$\\mathdefault{', text)
597 
598     # Braces ensure dashes are not spaced like binary operators.
599     ret_text = '$\\mathdefault{'+ret_text.replace('-', '{-}')+'}$'
600     ret_text = ret_text.replace('$\\mathdefault{}$', '')
601     return ret_text

640 class ConciseDateFormatter(ticker.Formatter):
641     """
642     A `.Formatter` which attempts to figure out the best format to use for the
643     date, and to make it as compact as possible, but still be complete. This is
644     most useful when used with the `AutoDateLocator`::
645 
646     >>> locator = AutoDateLocator()
647     >>> formatter = ConciseDateFormatter(locator)
648 
649     Parameters
650     ----------
651     locator : `.ticker.Locator`
652         Locator that this axis is using.
653 
654     tz : str, optional
655         Passed to `.dates.date2num`.
656 
657     formats : list of 6 strings, optional
658         Format strings for 6 levels of tick labelling: mostly years,
659         months, days, hours, minutes, and seconds.  Strings use
660         the same format codes as `~datetime.datetime.strftime`.  Default is
661         ``['%Y', '%b', '%d', '%H:%M', '%H:%M', '%S.%f']``
662 
663     zero_formats : list of 6 strings, optional
664         Format strings for tick labels that are "zeros" for a given tick
665         level.  For instance, if most ticks are months, ticks around 1 Jan 2005
666         will be labeled "Dec", "2005", "Feb".  The default is
667         ``['', '%Y', '%b', '%b-%d', '%H:%M', '%H:%M']``
668 
669     offset_formats : list of 6 strings, optional
670         Format strings for the 6 levels that is applied to the "offset"
671         string found on the right side of an x-axis, or top of a y-axis.
672         Combined with the tick labels this should completely specify the
673         date.  The default is::
674 
675             ['', '%Y', '%Y-%b', '%Y-%b-%d', '%Y-%b-%d', '%Y-%b-%d %H:%M']
676 
677     show_offset : bool, default: True
678         Whether to show the offset or not.
679 
680     usetex : bool, default: :rc:`text.usetex`
681         To enable/disable the use of TeX's math mode for rendering the results
682         of the formatter.
683 
684     Examples
685     --------
686     See :doc:`/gallery/ticks/date_concise_formatter`
687 
688     .. plot::
689 
690         import datetime
691         import matplotlib.dates as mdates
692 
693         base = datetime.datetime(2005, 2, 1)
694         dates = np.array([base + datetime.timedelta(hours=(2 * i))
695                           for i in range(732)])
696         N = len(dates)
697         np.random.seed(19680801)
698         y = np.cumsum(np.random.randn(N))
699 
700         fig, ax = plt.subplots(constrained_layout=True)
701         locator = mdates.AutoDateLocator()
702         formatter = mdates.ConciseDateFormatter(locator)
703         ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(locator)
704         ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
705 
706         ax.plot(dates, y)
707         ax.set_title('Concise Date Formatter')
708 
709     """
710 
711     def __init__(self, locator, tz=None, formats=None, offset_formats=None,
712                  zero_formats=None, show_offset=True, *, usetex=None):
713         """
714         Autoformat the date labels.  The default format is used to form an
715         initial string, and then redundant elements are removed.
716         """
717         self._locator = locator
718         self._tz = tz
719         self.defaultfmt = '%Y'
720         # there are 6 levels with each level getting a specific format
721         # 0: mostly years,  1: months,  2: days,
722         # 3: hours, 4: minutes, 5: seconds
723         if formats:
724             if len(formats) != 6:
725                 raise ValueError('formats argument must be a list of '
726                                  '6 format strings (or None)')
727             self.formats = formats
728         else:
729             self.formats = ['%Y',  # ticks are mostly years
730                             '%b',          # ticks are mostly months
731                             '%d',          # ticks are mostly days
732                             '%H:%M',       # hrs
733                             '%H:%M',       # min
734                             '%S.%f',       # secs
735                             ]
736         # fmt for zeros ticks at this level.  These are
737         # ticks that should be labeled w/ info the level above.
738         # like 1 Jan can just be labelled "Jan".  02:02:00 can
739         # just be labeled 02:02.
740         if zero_formats:
741             if len(zero_formats) != 6:
742                 raise ValueError('zero_formats argument must be a list of '
743                                  '6 format strings (or None)')
744             self.zero_formats = zero_formats
745         elif formats:
746             # use the users formats for the zero tick formats
747             self.zero_formats = [''] + self.formats[:-1]
748         else:
749             # make the defaults a bit nicer:
750             self.zero_formats = [''] + self.formats[:-1]
751             self.zero_formats[3] = '%b-%d'
752 
753         if offset_formats:
754             if len(offset_formats) != 6:
755                 raise ValueError('offsetfmts argument must be a list of '
756                                  '6 format strings (or None)')
757             self.offset_formats = offset_formats
758         else:
759             self.offset_formats = ['',
760                                    '%Y',
761                                    '%Y-%b',
762                                    '%Y-%b-%d',
763                                    '%Y-%b-%d',
764                                    '%Y-%b-%d %H:%M']
765         self.offset_string = ''
766         self.show_offset = show_offset
767         self._usetex = (usetex if usetex is not None else
768                         mpl.rcParams['text.usetex'])
769 
770     def __call__(self, x, pos=None):
771         formatter = DateFormatter(self.defaultfmt, self._tz,
772                                   usetex=self._usetex)
773         return formatter(x, pos=pos)
774 
775     def format_ticks(self, values):
776         tickdatetime = [num2date(value, tz=self._tz) for value in values]
777         tickdate = np.array([tdt.timetuple()[:6] for tdt in tickdatetime])
778 
779         # basic algorithm:
780         # 1) only display a part of the date if it changes over the ticks.
781         # 2) don't display the smaller part of the date if:
782         #    it is always the same or if it is the start of the
783         #    year, month, day etc.
784         # fmt for most ticks at this level
785         fmts = self.formats
786         # format beginnings of days, months, years, etc.
787         zerofmts = self.zero_formats
788         # offset fmt are for the offset in the upper left of the
789         # or lower right of the axis.
790         offsetfmts = self.offset_formats
791 
792         # determine the level we will label at:
793         # mostly 0: years,  1: months,  2: days,
794         # 3: hours, 4: minutes, 5: seconds, 6: microseconds
795         for level in range(5, -1, -1):
796             if len(np.unique(tickdate[:, level])) > 1:
797                 # level is less than 2 so a year is already present in the axis
798                 if (level < 2):
799                     self.show_offset = False
800                 break
801             elif level == 0:
802                 # all tickdate are the same, so only micros might be different
803                 # set to the most precise (6: microseconds doesn't exist...)
804                 level = 5
805 
806         # level is the basic level we will label at.
807         # now loop through and decide the actual ticklabels
808         zerovals = [0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0]
809         labels = [''] * len(tickdate)
810         for nn in range(len(tickdate)):
811             if level < 5:
812                 if tickdate[nn][level] == zerovals[level]:
813                     fmt = zerofmts[level]
814                 else:
815                     fmt = fmts[level]
816             else:
817                 # special handling for seconds + microseconds
818                 if (tickdatetime[nn].second == tickdatetime[nn].microsecond
819                         == 0):
820                     fmt = zerofmts[level]
821                 else:
822                     fmt = fmts[level]
823             labels[nn] = tickdatetime[nn].strftime(fmt)
824 
825         # special handling of seconds and microseconds:
826         # strip extra zeros and decimal if possible.
827         # this is complicated by two factors.  1) we have some level-4 strings
828         # here (i.e. 03:00, '0.50000', '1.000') 2) we would like to have the
829         # same number of decimals for each string (i.e. 0.5 and 1.0).
830         if level >= 5:
831             trailing_zeros = min(
832                 (len(s) - len(s.rstrip('0')) for s in labels if '.' in s),
833                 default=None)
834             if trailing_zeros:
835                 for nn in range(len(labels)):
836                     if '.' in labels[nn]:
837                         labels[nn] = labels[nn][:-trailing_zeros].rstrip('.')
838 
839         if self.show_offset:
840             # set the offset string:
841             self.offset_string = tickdatetime[-1].strftime(offsetfmts[level])
842             if self._usetex:
843                 self.offset_string = _wrap_in_tex(self.offset_string)
844 
845         if self._usetex:
846             return [_wrap_in_tex(l) for l in labels]
847         else:
848             return labels
849 
850     def get_offset(self):
851         return self.offset_string
852 
853     def format_data_short(self, value):
854         return num2date(value, tz=self._tz).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')

857 class AutoDateFormatter(ticker.Formatter):
858     """
859     A `.Formatter` which attempts to figure out the best format to use.  This
860     is most useful when used with the `AutoDateLocator`.
861 
862     `.AutoDateFormatter` has a ``.scale`` dictionary that maps tick scales (the
863     interval in days between one major tick) to format strings; this dictionary
864     defaults to ::
865 
866         self.scaled = {
867             DAYS_PER_YEAR: rcParams['date.autoformat.year'],
868             DAYS_PER_MONTH: rcParams['date.autoformat.month'],
869             1: rcParams['date.autoformat.day'],
870             1 / HOURS_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformat.hour'],
871             1 / MINUTES_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformat.minute'],
872             1 / SEC_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformat.second'],
873             1 / MUSECONDS_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformat.microsecond'],
874         }
875 
876     The formatter uses the format string corresponding to the lowest key in
877     the dictionary that is greater or equal to the current scale.  Dictionary
878     entries can be customized::
879 
880         locator = AutoDateLocator()
881         formatter = AutoDateFormatter(locator)
882         formatter.scaled[1/(24*60)] = '%M:%S' # only show min and sec
883 
884     Custom callables can also be used instead of format strings.  The following
885     example shows how to use a custom format function to strip trailing zeros
886     from decimal seconds and adds the date to the first ticklabel::
887 
888         def my_format_function(x, pos=None):
889             x = matplotlib.dates.num2date(x)
890             if pos == 0:
891                 fmt = '%D %H:%M:%S.%f'
892             else:
893                 fmt = '%H:%M:%S.%f'
894             label = x.strftime(fmt)
895             label = label.rstrip("0")
896             label = label.rstrip(".")
897             return label
898 
899         formatter.scaled[1/(24*60)] = my_format_function
900     """
901 
902     # This can be improved by providing some user-level direction on
903     # how to choose the best format (precedence, etc.).
904 
905     # Perhaps a 'struct' that has a field for each time-type where a
906     # zero would indicate "don't show" and a number would indicate
907     # "show" with some sort of priority.  Same priorities could mean
908     # show all with the same priority.
909 
910     # Or more simply, perhaps just a format string for each
911     # possibility...
912 
913     def __init__(self, locator, tz=None, defaultfmt='%Y-%m-%d', *,
914                  usetex=None):
915         """
916         Autoformat the date labels.
917 
918         Parameters
919         ----------
920         locator : `.ticker.Locator`
921             Locator that this axis is using.
922 
923         tz : str, optional
924             Passed to `.dates.date2num`.
925 
926         defaultfmt : str
927             The default format to use if none of the values in ``self.scaled``
928             are greater than the unit returned by ``locator._get_unit()``.
929 
930         usetex : bool, default: :rc:`text.usetex`
931             To enable/disable the use of TeX's math mode for rendering the
932             results of the formatter. If any entries in ``self.scaled`` are set
933             as functions, then it is up to the customized function to enable or
934             disable TeX's math mode itself.
935         """
936         self._locator = locator
937         self._tz = tz
938         self.defaultfmt = defaultfmt
939         self._formatter = DateFormatter(self.defaultfmt, tz)
940         rcParams = mpl.rcParams
941         self._usetex = (usetex if usetex is not None else
942                         mpl.rcParams['text.usetex'])
943         self.scaled = {
944             DAYS_PER_YEAR: rcParams['date.autoformatter.year'],
945             DAYS_PER_MONTH: rcParams['date.autoformatter.month'],
946             1: rcParams['date.autoformatter.day'],
947             1 / HOURS_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformatter.hour'],
948             1 / MINUTES_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformatter.minute'],
949             1 / SEC_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformatter.second'],
950             1 / MUSECONDS_PER_DAY: rcParams['date.autoformatter.microsecond']
951         }
952 
953     def _set_locator(self, locator):
954         self._locator = locator
955 
956     def __call__(self, x, pos=None):
957         try:
958             locator_unit_scale = float(self._locator._get_unit())
959         except AttributeError:
960             locator_unit_scale = 1
961         # Pick the first scale which is greater than the locator unit.
962         fmt = next((fmt for scale, fmt in sorted(self.scaled.items())
963                     if scale >= locator_unit_scale),
964                    self.defaultfmt)
965 
966         if isinstance(fmt, str):
967             self._formatter = DateFormatter(fmt, self._tz, usetex=self._usetex)
968             result = self._formatter(x, pos)
969         elif callable(fmt):
970             result = fmt(x, pos)
971         else:
972             raise TypeError('Unexpected type passed to {0!r}.'.format(self))
973 
974         return result

977 class rrulewrapper:
978     def __init__(self, freq, tzinfo=None, **kwargs):
979         kwargs['freq'] = freq
980         self._base_tzinfo = tzinfo
981 
982         self._update_rrule(**kwargs)
983 
984     def set(self, **kwargs):
985         self._construct.update(kwargs)
986 
987         self._update_rrule(**self._construct)
988 
989     def _update_rrule(self, **kwargs):
990         tzinfo = self._base_tzinfo
991 
992         # rrule does not play nicely with time zones - especially pytz time
993         # zones, it's best to use naive zones and attach timezones once the
994         # datetimes are returned
995         if 'dtstart' in kwargs:
996             dtstart = kwargs['dtstart']
997             if dtstart.tzinfo is not None:
998                 if tzinfo is None:
999                     tzinfo = dtstart.tzinfo
1000                 else:
1001                     dtstart = dtstart.astimezone(tzinfo)
1002 
1003                 kwargs['dtstart'] = dtstart.replace(tzinfo=None)
1004 
1005         if 'until' in kwargs:
1006             until = kwargs['until']
1007             if until.tzinfo is not None:
1008                 if tzinfo is not None:
1009                     until = until.astimezone(tzinfo)
1010                 else:
1011                     raise ValueError('until cannot be aware if dtstart '
1012                                      'is naive and tzinfo is None')
1013 
1014                 kwargs['until'] = until.replace(tzinfo=None)
1015 
1016         self._construct = kwargs.copy()
1017         self._tzinfo = tzinfo
1018         self._rrule = rrule(**self._construct)
1019 
1020     def _attach_tzinfo(self, dt, tzinfo):
1021         # pytz zones are attached by "localizing" the datetime
1022         if hasattr(tzinfo, 'localize'):
1023             return tzinfo.localize(dt, is_dst=True)
1024 
1025         return dt.replace(tzinfo=tzinfo)
1026 
1027     def _aware_return_wrapper(self, f, returns_list=False):
1028         """Decorator function that allows rrule methods to handle tzinfo."""
1029         # This is only necessary if we're actually attaching a tzinfo
1030         if self._tzinfo is None:
1031             return f
1032 
1033         # All datetime arguments must be naive. If they are not naive, they are
1034         # converted to the _tzinfo zone before dropping the zone.
1035         def normalize_arg(arg):
1036             if isinstance(arg, datetime.datetime) and arg.tzinfo is not None:
1037                 if arg.tzinfo is not self._tzinfo:
1038                     arg = arg.astimezone(self._tzinfo)
1039 
1040                 return arg.replace(tzinfo=None)
1041 
1042             return arg
1043 
1044         def normalize_args(args, kwargs):
1045             args = tuple(normalize_arg(arg) for arg in args)
1046             kwargs = {kw: normalize_arg(arg) for kw, arg in kwargs.items()}
1047 
1048             return args, kwargs
1049 
1050         # There are two kinds of functions we care about - ones that return
1051         # dates and ones that return lists of dates.
1052         if not returns_list:
1053             def inner_func(*args, **kwargs):
1054                 args, kwargs = normalize_args(args, kwargs)
1055                 dt = f(*args, **kwargs)
1056                 return self._attach_tzinfo(dt, self._tzinfo)
1057         else:
1058             def inner_func(*args, **kwargs):
1059                 args, kwargs = normalize_args(args, kwargs)
1060                 dts = f(*args, **kwargs)
1061                 return [self._attach_tzinfo(dt, self._tzinfo) for dt in dts]
1062 
1063         return functools.wraps(f)(inner_func)
1064 
1065     def __getattr__(self, name):
1066         if name in self.__dict__:
1067             return self.__dict__[name]
1068 
1069         f = getattr(self._rrule, name)
1070 
1071         if name in {'after', 'before'}:
1072             return self._aware_return_wrapper(f)
1073         elif name in {'xafter', 'xbefore', 'between'}:
1074             return self._aware_return_wrapper(f, returns_list=True)
1075         else:
1076             return f
1077 
1078     def __setstate__(self, state):
1079         self.__dict__.update(state)

1087     is not meant to be used on its own.

1093         Parameters
1094         ----------

1111             dmin, dmax = dmax, dmin

1116         """Convert the view interval to datetime objects."""

1119             vmin, vmax = vmax, vmin

1124         Return how many days a unit of the locator is; used for
1125         intelligent autoscaling.
1126         """

1129     def _get_interval(self):
1130         """

1135     def nonsingular(self, vmin, vmax):
1136         """
1137         Given the proposed upper and lower extent, adjust the range
1138         if it is too close to being singular (i.e. a range of ~0).
1139         """
1140         if not np.isfinite(vmin) or not np.isfinite(vmax):
1141             # Except if there is no data, then use 2000-2010 as default.
1142             return (date2num(datetime.date(2000, 1, 1)),
1143                     date2num(datetime.date(2010, 1, 1)))
1144         if vmax < vmin:
1145             vmin, vmax = vmax, vmin
1146         unit = self._get_unit()
1147         interval = self._get_interval()
1148         if abs(vmax - vmin) < 1e-6:
1149             vmin -= 2 * unit * interval

1154 class RRuleLocator(DateLocator):
1155     # use the dateutil rrule instance
1156 
1157     def __init__(self, o, tz=None):
1158         super().__init__(tz)
1159         self.rule = o
1160 
1161     def __call__(self):
1162         # if no data have been set, this will tank with a ValueError
1163         try:
1164             dmin, dmax = self.viewlim_to_dt()
1165         except ValueError:
1166             return []
1167 
1168         return self.tick_values(dmin, dmax)
1169 
1170     def tick_values(self, vmin, vmax):
1171         start, stop = self._create_rrule(vmin, vmax)
1172         dates = self.rule.between(start, stop, True)
1173         if len(dates) == 0:
1174             return date2num([vmin, vmax])
1175         return self.raise_if_exceeds(date2num(dates))
1176 
1177     def _create_rrule(self, vmin, vmax):
1178         # set appropriate rrule dtstart and until and return
1179         # start and end
1180         delta = relativedelta(vmax, vmin)
1181 
1182         # We need to cap at the endpoints of valid datetime
1183         try:
1184             start = vmin - delta
1185         except (ValueError, OverflowError):
1186             # cap
1187             start = datetime.datetime(1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0,
1188                                       tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
1189 
1190         try:
1191             stop = vmax + delta
1192         except (ValueError, OverflowError):
1193             # cap
1194             stop = datetime.datetime(9999, 12, 31, 23, 59, 59,
1195                                      tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
1196 
1197         self.rule.set(dtstart=start, until=stop)
1198 
1199         return vmin, vmax
1200 
1201     def _get_unit(self):
1202         # docstring inherited
1203         freq = self.rule._rrule._freq
1204         return self.get_unit_generic(freq)
1205 
1206     @staticmethod
1207     def get_unit_generic(freq):
1208         if freq == YEARLY:
1209             return DAYS_PER_YEAR
1210         elif freq == MONTHLY:
1211             return DAYS_PER_MONTH
1212         elif freq == WEEKLY:
1213             return DAYS_PER_WEEK
1214         elif freq == DAILY:
1215             return 1.0
1216         elif freq == HOURLY:
1217             return 1.0 / HOURS_PER_DAY
1218         elif freq == MINUTELY:
1219             return 1.0 / MINUTES_PER_DAY
1220         elif freq == SECONDLY:
1221             return 1.0 / SEC_PER_DAY
1222         else:
1223             # error
1224             return -1   # or should this just return '1'?
1225 
1226     def _get_interval(self):
1227         return self.rule._rrule._interval
