1230 class AutoDateLocator(DateLocator):
1231     """
1232     On autoscale, this class picks the best `DateLocator` to set the view
1233     limits and the tick locations.
1234 
1235     Attributes
1236     ----------
1237     intervald : dict
1238 
1239         Mapping of tick frequencies to multiples allowed for that ticking.
1240         The default is ::
1241 
1242             self.intervald = {
1243                 YEARLY  : [1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 40, 50, 100, 200, 400, 500,
1244                            1000, 2000, 4000, 5000, 10000],
1245                 MONTHLY : [1, 2, 3, 4, 6],
1246                 DAILY   : [1, 2, 3, 7, 14, 21],
1247                 HOURLY  : [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12],
1248                 MINUTELY: [1, 5, 10, 15, 30],
1249                 SECONDLY: [1, 5, 10, 15, 30],
1250                 MICROSECONDLY: [1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500,
1251                                 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, 20000, 50000,
1252                                 100000, 200000, 500000, 1000000],
1253             }
1254 
1255         where the keys are defined in `dateutil.rrule`.
1256 
1257         The interval is used to specify multiples that are appropriate for
1258         the frequency of ticking. For instance, every 7 days is sensible
1259         for daily ticks, but for minutes/seconds, 15 or 30 make sense.
1260 
1261         When customizing, you should only modify the values for the existing
1262         keys. You should not add or delete entries.
1263 
1264         Example for forcing ticks every 3 hours::
1265 
1266             locator = AutoDateLocator()
1267             locator.intervald[HOURLY] = [3]  # only show every 3 hours
1268     """
1269 
1270     def __init__(self, tz=None, minticks=5, maxticks=None,
1271                  interval_multiples=True):
1272         """
1273         Parameters
1274         ----------
1275         tz : `datetime.tzinfo`
1276             Ticks timezone.
1277         minticks : int
1278             The minimum number of ticks desired; controls whether ticks occur
1279             yearly, monthly, etc.
1280         maxticks : int
1281             The maximum number of ticks desired; controls the interval between
1282             ticks (ticking every other, every 3, etc.).  For fine-grained
1283             control, this can be a dictionary mapping individual rrule
1284             frequency constants (YEARLY, MONTHLY, etc.) to their own maximum
1285             number of ticks.  This can be used to keep the number of ticks
1286             appropriate to the format chosen in `AutoDateFormatter`. Any
1287             frequency not specified in this dictionary is given a default
1288             value.
1289         interval_multiples : bool, default: True
1290             Whether ticks should be chosen to be multiple of the interval,
1291             locking them to 'nicer' locations.  For example, this will force
1292             the ticks to be at hours 0, 6, 12, 18 when hourly ticking is done
1293             at 6 hour intervals.
1294         """
1295         super().__init__(tz)
1296         self._freq = YEARLY
1297         self._freqs = [YEARLY, MONTHLY, DAILY, HOURLY, MINUTELY,
1298                        SECONDLY, MICROSECONDLY]
1299         self.minticks = minticks
1300 
1301         self.maxticks = {YEARLY: 11, MONTHLY: 12, DAILY: 11, HOURLY: 12,
1302                          MINUTELY: 11, SECONDLY: 11, MICROSECONDLY: 8}
1303         if maxticks is not None:
1304             try:
1305                 self.maxticks.update(maxticks)
1306             except TypeError:
1307                 # Assume we were given an integer. Use this as the maximum
1308                 # number of ticks for every frequency and create a
1309                 # dictionary for this
1310                 self.maxticks = dict.fromkeys(self._freqs, maxticks)
1311         self.interval_multiples = interval_multiples
1312         self.intervald = {
1313             YEARLY:   [1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 40, 50, 100, 200, 400, 500,
1314                        1000, 2000, 4000, 5000, 10000],
1315             MONTHLY:  [1, 2, 3, 4, 6],
1316             DAILY:    [1, 2, 3, 7, 14, 21],
1317             HOURLY:   [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12],
1318             MINUTELY: [1, 5, 10, 15, 30],
1319             SECONDLY: [1, 5, 10, 15, 30],
1320             MICROSECONDLY: [1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000,
1321                             5000, 10000, 20000, 50000, 100000, 200000, 500000,
1322                             1000000],
1323                             }
1324         if interval_multiples:
1325             # Swap "3" for "4" in the DAILY list; If we use 3 we get bad
1326             # tick loc for months w/ 31 days: 1, 4, ..., 28, 31, 1
1327             # If we use 4 then we get: 1, 5, ... 25, 29, 1
1328             self.intervald[DAILY] = [1, 2, 4, 7, 14]
1329 
1330         self._byranges = [None, range(1, 13), range(1, 32),
1331                           range(0, 24), range(0, 60), range(0, 60), None]
1332 
1333     def __call__(self):
1334         # docstring inherited
1335         dmin, dmax = self.viewlim_to_dt()
1336         locator = self.get_locator(dmin, dmax)
1337         return locator()
1338 
1339     def tick_values(self, vmin, vmax):
1340         return self.get_locator(vmin, vmax).tick_values(vmin, vmax)
1341 
1342     def nonsingular(self, vmin, vmax):
1343         # whatever is thrown at us, we can scale the unit.
1344         # But default nonsingular date plots at an ~4 year period.
1345         if not np.isfinite(vmin) or not np.isfinite(vmax):
1346             # Except if there is no data, then use 2000-2010 as default.
1347             return (date2num(datetime.date(2000, 1, 1)),
1348                     date2num(datetime.date(2010, 1, 1)))
1349         if vmax < vmin:
1350             vmin, vmax = vmax, vmin
1351         if vmin == vmax:
1352             vmin = vmin - DAYS_PER_YEAR * 2
1353             vmax = vmax + DAYS_PER_YEAR * 2
1354         return vmin, vmax
1355 
1356     def _get_unit(self):
1357         if self._freq in [MICROSECONDLY]:
1358             return 1. / MUSECONDS_PER_DAY
1359         else:
1360             return RRuleLocator.get_unit_generic(self._freq)
1361 
1362     def get_locator(self, dmin, dmax):
1363         """Pick the best locator based on a distance."""
1364         delta = relativedelta(dmax, dmin)
1365         tdelta = dmax - dmin
1366 
1367         # take absolute difference
1368         if dmin > dmax:
1369             delta = -delta
1370             tdelta = -tdelta
1371         # The following uses a mix of calls to relativedelta and timedelta
1372         # methods because there is incomplete overlap in the functionality of
1373         # these similar functions, and it's best to avoid doing our own math
1374         # whenever possible.
1375         numYears = float(delta.years)
1376         numMonths = numYears * MONTHS_PER_YEAR + delta.months
1377         numDays = tdelta.days   # Avoids estimates of days/month, days/year
1378         numHours = numDays * HOURS_PER_DAY + delta.hours
1379         numMinutes = numHours * MIN_PER_HOUR + delta.minutes
1380         numSeconds = np.floor(tdelta.total_seconds())
1381         numMicroseconds = np.floor(tdelta.total_seconds() * 1e6)
1382 
1383         nums = [numYears, numMonths, numDays, numHours, numMinutes,
1384                 numSeconds, numMicroseconds]
1385 
1386         use_rrule_locator = [True] * 6 + [False]
1387 
1388         # Default setting of bymonth, etc. to pass to rrule
1389         # [unused (for year), bymonth, bymonthday, byhour, byminute,
1390         #  bysecond, unused (for microseconds)]
1391         byranges = [None, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, None]
1392 
1393         # Loop over all the frequencies and try to find one that gives at
1394         # least a minticks tick positions.  Once this is found, look for
1395         # an interval from an list specific to that frequency that gives no
1396         # more than maxticks tick positions. Also, set up some ranges
1397         # (bymonth, etc.) as appropriate to be passed to rrulewrapper.
1398         for i, (freq, num) in enumerate(zip(self._freqs, nums)):
1399             # If this particular frequency doesn't give enough ticks, continue
1400             if num < self.minticks:
1401                 # Since we're not using this particular frequency, set
1402                 # the corresponding by_ to None so the rrule can act as
1403                 # appropriate
1404                 byranges[i] = None
1405                 continue
1406 
1407             # Find the first available interval that doesn't give too many
1408             # ticks
1409             for interval in self.intervald[freq]:
1410                 if num <= interval * (self.maxticks[freq] - 1):
1411                     break
1412             else:
1413                 if not (self.interval_multiples and freq == DAILY):
1414                     _api.warn_external(
1415                         f"AutoDateLocator was unable to pick an appropriate "
1416                         f"interval for this date range. It may be necessary "
1417                         f"to add an interval value to the AutoDateLocator's "
1418                         f"intervald dictionary. Defaulting to {interval}.")
1419 
1420             # Set some parameters as appropriate
1421             self._freq = freq
1422 
1423             if self._byranges[i] and self.interval_multiples:
1424                 byranges[i] = self._byranges[i][::interval]
1425                 if i in (DAILY, WEEKLY):
1426                     if interval == 14:
1427                         # just make first and 15th.  Avoids 30th.
1428                         byranges[i] = [1, 15]
1429                     elif interval == 7:
1430                         byranges[i] = [1, 8, 15, 22]
1431 
1432                 interval = 1
1433             else:
1434                 byranges[i] = self._byranges[i]
1435             break
1436         else:
1437             interval = 1
1438 
1439         if (freq == YEARLY) and self.interval_multiples:
1440             locator = YearLocator(interval, tz=self.tz)
1441         elif use_rrule_locator[i]:
1442             _, bymonth, bymonthday, byhour, byminute, bysecond, _ = byranges
1443             rrule = rrulewrapper(self._freq, interval=interval,
1444                                  dtstart=dmin, until=dmax,
1445                                  bymonth=bymonth, bymonthday=bymonthday,
1446                                  byhour=byhour, byminute=byminute,
1447                                  bysecond=bysecond)
1448 
1449             locator = RRuleLocator(rrule, self.tz)
1450         else:
1451             locator = MicrosecondLocator(interval, tz=self.tz)
1452             if date2num(dmin) > 70 * 365 and interval < 1000:
1453                 _api.warn_external(
1454                     'Plotting microsecond time intervals for dates far from '
1455                     f'the epoch (time origin: {get_epoch()}) is not well-'
1456                     'supported. See matplotlib.dates.set_epoch to change the '
1457                     'epoch.')
1458 
1459         locator.set_axis(self.axis)
1460         return locator
1461

1463 class YearLocator(RRuleLocator):
1464     """
1465     Make ticks on a given day of each year that is a multiple of base.
1466 
1467     Examples::
1468 
1469       # Tick every year on Jan 1st
1470       locator = YearLocator()
1471 
1472       # Tick every 5 years on July 4th
1473       locator = YearLocator(5, month=7, day=4)
1474     """
1475     def __init__(self, base=1, month=1, day=1, tz=None):
1476         """
1477         Mark years that are multiple of base on a given month and day
1478         (default jan 1).
1479         """
1480         rule = rrulewrapper(YEARLY, interval=base, bymonth=month,
1481                             bymonthday=day, **self.hms0d)
1482         super().__init__(rule, tz)
1483         self.base = ticker._Edge_integer(base, 0)
1484 
1485     def _create_rrule(self, vmin, vmax):
1486         # 'start' needs to be a multiple of the interval to create ticks on
1487         # interval multiples when the tick frequency is YEARLY
1488         ymin = max(self.base.le(vmin.year) * self.base.step, 1)
1489         ymax = min(self.base.ge(vmax.year) * self.base.step, 9999)
1490 
1491         c = self.rule._construct
1492         replace = {'year': ymin,
1493                    'month': c.get('bymonth', 1),
1494                    'day': c.get('bymonthday', 1),
1495                    'hour': 0, 'minute': 0, 'second': 0}
1496 
1497         start = vmin.replace(**replace)
1498         stop = start.replace(year=ymax)
1499         self.rule.set(dtstart=start, until=stop)
1500 
1501         return start, stop
1502

219 class _ColorbarAxesLocator:
220     """
221     Shrink the axes if there are triangular or rectangular extends.
222     """
223     def __init__(self, cbar):
224         self._cbar = cbar
225         self._orig_locator = cbar.ax._axes_locator
226 
227     def __call__(self, ax, renderer):
228         if self._orig_locator is not None:
229             pos = self._orig_locator(ax, renderer)
230         else:
231             pos = ax.get_position(original=True)
232         if self._cbar.extend == 'neither':
233             return pos
234 
235         y, extendlen = self._cbar._proportional_y()
236         if not self._cbar._extend_lower():
237             extendlen[0] = 0
238         if not self._cbar._extend_upper():
239             extendlen[1] = 0
240         len = sum(extendlen) + 1
241         shrink = 1 / len
242         offset = extendlen[0] / len
243         # we need to reset the aspect ratio of the axes to account
244         # of the extends...
245         if hasattr(ax, '_colorbar_info'):
246             aspect = ax._colorbar_info['aspect']
247         else:
248             aspect = False
249         # now shrink and/or offset to take into account the
250         # extend tri/rectangles.
251         if self._cbar.orientation == 'vertical':
252             if aspect:
253                 self._cbar.ax.set_box_aspect(aspect*shrink)
254             pos = pos.shrunk(1, shrink).translated(0, offset * pos.height)
255         else:
256             if aspect:
257                 self._cbar.ax.set_box_aspect(1/(aspect * shrink))
258             pos = pos.shrunk(shrink, 1).translated(offset * pos.width, 0)
259         return pos
260 
261     def get_subplotspec(self):
262         # make tight_layout happy..
263         ss = getattr(self._cbar.ax, 'get_subplotspec', None)
264         if ss is None:
265             if not hasattr(self._orig_locator, "get_subplotspec"):
266                 return None
267             ss = self._orig_locator.get_subplotspec
268         return ss()

546     def update_normal(self, mappable):

574     @_api.deprecated("3.6", alternative="fig.draw_without_rendering()")
575     def draw_all(self):

577         Calculate any free parameters based on the current cmap and norm,
578         and do all the drawing.
579         """
580         self._draw_all()

582     def _draw_all(self):
583         """
584         Calculate any free parameters based on the current cmap and norm,
585         and do all the drawing.
586         """
587         if self.orientation == 'vertical':
588             if mpl.rcParams['ytick.minor.visible']:
589                 self.minorticks_on()
590         else:
591             if mpl.rcParams['xtick.minor.visible']:
592                 self.minorticks_on()
593         self._long_axis().set(label_position=self.ticklocation,
594                               ticks_position=self.ticklocation)
595         self._short_axis().set_ticks([])
596         self._short_axis().set_ticks([], minor=True)
597 
598         # Set self._boundaries and self._values, including extensions.
599         # self._boundaries are the edges of each square of color, and
600         # self._values are the value to map into the norm to get the
601         # color:
602         self._process_values()
603         # Set self.vmin and self.vmax to first and last boundary, excluding
604         # extensions:
605         self.vmin, self.vmax = self._boundaries[self._inside][[0, -1]]
606         # Compute the X/Y mesh.
607         X, Y = self._mesh()
608         # draw the extend triangles, and shrink the inner axes to accommodate.
609         # also adds the outline path to self.outline spine:
610         self._do_extends()
611         lower, upper = self.vmin, self.vmax
612         if self._long_axis().get_inverted():
613             # If the axis is inverted, we need to swap the vmin/vmax
614             lower, upper = upper, lower
615         if self.orientation == 'vertical':
616             self.ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
617             self.ax.set_ylim(lower, upper)
618         else:
619             self.ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
620             self.ax.set_xlim(lower, upper)
621 
622         # set up the tick locators and formatters.  A bit complicated because
623         # boundary norms + uniform spacing requires a manual locator.
624         self.update_ticks()
625 
626         if self._filled:
627             ind = np.arange(len(self._values))
628             if self._extend_lower():
629                 ind = ind[1:]
630             if self._extend_upper():
631                 ind = ind[:-1]
632             self._add_solids(X, Y, self._values[ind, np.newaxis])
633 
634     def _add_solids(self, X, Y, C):
635         """Draw the colors; optionally add separators."""
636         # Cleanup previously set artists.
637         if self.solids is not None:
638             self.solids.remove()
639         for solid in self.solids_patches:
640             solid.remove()
641         # Add new artist(s), based on mappable type.  Use individual patches if
642         # hatching is needed, pcolormesh otherwise.
643         mappable = getattr(self, 'mappable', None)
644         if (isinstance(mappable, contour.ContourSet)
645                 and any(hatch is not None for hatch in mappable.hatches)):
646             self._add_solids_patches(X, Y, C, mappable)
647         else:
648             self.solids = self.ax.pcolormesh(
649                 X, Y, C, cmap=self.cmap, norm=self.norm, alpha=self.alpha,
650                 edgecolors='none', shading='flat')
651             if not self.drawedges:
652                 if len(self._y) >= self.n_rasterize:
653                     self.solids.set_rasterized(True)
654         self.dividers.set_segments(
655             np.dstack([X, Y])[1:-1] if self.drawedges else [])
656 
657     def _add_solids_patches(self, X, Y, C, mappable):
658         hatches = mappable.hatches * len(C)  # Have enough hatches.
659         patches = []
660         for i in range(len(X) - 1):
661             xy = np.array([[X[i, 0], Y[i, 0]],
662                            [X[i, 1], Y[i, 0]],
663                            [X[i + 1, 1], Y[i + 1, 0]],
664                            [X[i + 1, 0], Y[i + 1, 1]]])
665             patch = mpatches.PathPatch(mpath.Path(xy),
666                                        facecolor=self.cmap(self.norm(C[i][0])),
667                                        hatch=hatches[i], linewidth=0,
668                                        antialiased=False, alpha=self.alpha)
669             self.ax.add_patch(patch)
670             patches.append(patch)
671         self.solids_patches = patches
672 
673     def _do_extends(self, ax=None):
674         """
675         Add the extend tri/rectangles on the outside of the axes.
676 
677         ax is unused, but required due to the callbacks on xlim/ylim changed
678         """
679         # Clean up any previous extend patches
680         for patch in self._extend_patches:
681             patch.remove()
682         self._extend_patches = []
683         # extend lengths are fraction of the *inner* part of colorbar,
684         # not the total colorbar:
685         _, extendlen = self._proportional_y()
686         bot = 0 - (extendlen[0] if self._extend_lower() else 0)
687         top = 1 + (extendlen[1] if self._extend_upper() else 0)
688 
689         # xyout is the outline of the colorbar including the extend patches:
690         if not self.extendrect:
691             # triangle:
692             xyout = np.array([[0, 0], [0.5, bot], [1, 0],
693                               [1, 1], [0.5, top], [0, 1], [0, 0]])
694         else:
695             # rectangle:
696             xyout = np.array([[0, 0], [0, bot], [1, bot], [1, 0],
697                               [1, 1], [1, top], [0, top], [0, 1],
698                               [0, 0]])
699 
700         if self.orientation == 'horizontal':
701             xyout = xyout[:, ::-1]
702 
703         # xyout is the path for the spine:
704         self.outline.set_xy(xyout)
705         if not self._filled:
706             return
707 
708         # Make extend triangles or rectangles filled patches.  These are
709         # defined in the outer parent axes' coordinates:
710         mappable = getattr(self, 'mappable', None)
711         if (isinstance(mappable, contour.ContourSet)
712                 and any(hatch is not None for hatch in mappable.hatches)):
713             hatches = mappable.hatches
714         else:
715             hatches = [None]
716 
717         if self._extend_lower():
718             if not self.extendrect:
719                 # triangle
720                 xy = np.array([[0, 0], [0.5, bot], [1, 0]])
721             else:
722                 # rectangle
723                 xy = np.array([[0, 0], [0, bot], [1., bot], [1, 0]])
724             if self.orientation == 'horizontal':
725                 xy = xy[:, ::-1]
726             # add the patch
727             val = -1 if self._long_axis().get_inverted() else 0
728             color = self.cmap(self.norm(self._values[val]))
729             patch = mpatches.PathPatch(
730                 mpath.Path(xy), facecolor=color, linewidth=0,
731                 antialiased=False, transform=self.ax.transAxes,
732                 hatch=hatches[0], clip_on=False,
733                 # Place it right behind the standard patches, which is
734                 # needed if we updated the extends
735                 zorder=np.nextafter(self.ax.patch.zorder, -np.inf))
736             self.ax.add_patch(patch)
737             self._extend_patches.append(patch)
738         if self._extend_upper():
739             if not self.extendrect:
740                 # triangle
741                 xy = np.array([[0, 1], [0.5, top], [1, 1]])
742             else:
743                 # rectangle
744                 xy = np.array([[0, 1], [0, top], [1, top], [1, 1]])
745             if self.orientation == 'horizontal':
746                 xy = xy[:, ::-1]
747             # add the patch
748             val = 0 if self._long_axis().get_inverted() else -1
749             color = self.cmap(self.norm(self._values[val]))
750             patch = mpatches.PathPatch(
751                 mpath.Path(xy), facecolor=color,
752                 linewidth=0, antialiased=False,
753                 transform=self.ax.transAxes, hatch=hatches[-1], clip_on=False,
754                 # Place it right behind the standard patches, which is
755                 # needed if we updated the extends
756                 zorder=np.nextafter(self.ax.patch.zorder, -np.inf))
757             self.ax.add_patch(patch)
758             self._extend_patches.append(patch)

761     def add_lines(self, *args, **kwargs):
762         """
763         Draw lines on the colorbar.
764 
765         The lines are appended to the list :attr:`lines`.
766 
767         Parameters
768         ----------
769         levels : array-like
770             The positions of the lines.
771         colors : color or list of colors
772             Either a single color applying to all lines or one color value for
773             each line.
774         linewidths : float or array-like
775             Either a single linewidth applying to all lines or one linewidth
776             for each line.
777         erase : bool, default: True
778             Whether to remove any previously added lines.
779 
780         Notes
781         -----
782         Alternatively, this method can also be called with the signature
783         ``colorbar.add_lines(contour_set, erase=True)``, in which case
784         *levels*, *colors*, and *linewidths* are taken from *contour_set*.
785         """
786         params = _api.select_matching_signature(
787             [lambda self, CS, erase=True: locals(),
788              lambda self, levels, colors, linewidths, erase=True: locals()],
789             self, *args, **kwargs)
790         if "CS" in params:
791             self, CS, erase = params.values()
792             if not isinstance(CS, contour.ContourSet) or CS.filled:
793                 raise ValueError("If a single artist is passed to add_lines, "
794                                  "it must be a ContourSet of lines")
795             # TODO: Make colorbar lines auto-follow changes in contour lines.
796             return self.add_lines(
797                 CS.levels,
798                 [c[0] for c in CS.tcolors],
799                 [t[0] for t in CS.tlinewidths],
800                 erase=erase)
801         else:
802             self, levels, colors, linewidths, erase = params.values()
803 
804         y = self._locate(levels)
805         rtol = (self._y[-1] - self._y[0]) * 1e-10
806         igood = (y < self._y[-1] + rtol) & (y > self._y[0] - rtol)
807         y = y[igood]
808         if np.iterable(colors):
809             colors = np.asarray(colors)[igood]
810         if np.iterable(linewidths):
811             linewidths = np.asarray(linewidths)[igood]
812         X, Y = np.meshgrid([0, 1], y)
813         if self.orientation == 'vertical':
814             xy = np.stack([X, Y], axis=-1)
815         else:
816             xy = np.stack([Y, X], axis=-1)
817         col = collections.LineCollection(xy, linewidths=linewidths,
818                                          colors=colors)
819 
820         if erase and self.lines:
821             for lc in self.lines:
822                 lc.remove()
823             self.lines = []
824         self.lines.append(col)
825 
826         # make a clip path that is just a linewidth bigger than the axes...
827         fac = np.max(linewidths) / 72
828         xy = np.array([[0, 0], [1, 0], [1, 1], [0, 1], [0, 0]])
829         inches = self.ax.get_figure().dpi_scale_trans
830         # do in inches:
831         xy = inches.inverted().transform(self.ax.transAxes.transform(xy))
832         xy[[0, 1, 4], 1] -= fac
833         xy[[2, 3], 1] += fac
834         # back to axes units...
835         xy = self.ax.transAxes.inverted().transform(inches.transform(xy))
836         col.set_clip_path(mpath.Path(xy, closed=True),
837                           self.ax.transAxes)
838         self.ax.add_collection(col)
839         self.stale = True

851     def _get_ticker_locator_formatter(self):
852         """
853         Return the ``locator`` and ``formatter`` of the colorbar.
854 
855         If they have not been defined (i.e. are *None*), the formatter and
856         locator are retrieved from the axis, or from the value of the
857         boundaries for a boundary norm.
858 
859         Called by update_ticks...
860         """
861         locator = self._locator
862         formatter = self._formatter
863         minorlocator = self._minorlocator
864         if isinstance(self.norm, colors.BoundaryNorm):
865             b = self.norm.boundaries
866             if locator is None:
867                 locator = ticker.FixedLocator(b, nbins=10)
868             if minorlocator is None:
869                 minorlocator = ticker.FixedLocator(b)
870         elif isinstance(self.norm, colors.NoNorm):
871             if locator is None:
872                 # put ticks on integers between the boundaries of NoNorm
873                 nv = len(self._values)
874                 base = 1 + int(nv / 10)
875                 locator = ticker.IndexLocator(base=base, offset=.5)
876         elif self.boundaries is not None:
877             b = self._boundaries[self._inside]
878             if locator is None:
879                 locator = ticker.FixedLocator(b, nbins=10)
880         else:  # most cases:
881             if locator is None:
882                 # we haven't set the locator explicitly, so use the default
883                 # for this axis:
884                 locator = self._long_axis().get_major_locator()
885             if minorlocator is None:
886                 minorlocator = self._long_axis().get_minor_locator()
887 
888         if minorlocator is None:
889             minorlocator = ticker.NullLocator()
890 
891         if formatter is None:
892             formatter = self._long_axis().get_major_formatter()
893 
894         self._locator = locator
895         self._formatter = formatter
896         self._minorlocator = minorlocator
897         _log.debug('locator: %r', locator)

1097     def _ticker(self, locator, formatter):
1098         """
1099         Return the sequence of ticks (colorbar data locations),
1100         ticklabels (strings), and the corresponding offset string.
1101         """
1102         if isinstance(self.norm, colors.NoNorm) and self.boundaries is None:
1103             intv = self._values[0], self._values[-1]
1104         else:
1105             intv = self.vmin, self.vmax
1106         locator.create_dummy_axis(minpos=intv[0])
1107         locator.axis.set_view_interval(*intv)
1108         locator.axis.set_data_interval(*intv)
1109         formatter.set_axis(locator.axis)
1110 
1111         b = np.array(locator())
1112         if isinstance(locator, ticker.LogLocator):
1113             eps = 1e-10
1114             b = b[(b <= intv[1] * (1 + eps)) & (b >= intv[0] * (1 - eps))]
1115         else:
1116             eps = (intv[1] - intv[0]) * 1e-10
1117             b = b[(b <= intv[1] + eps) & (b >= intv[0] - eps)]
1118         ticks = self._locate(b)
1119         ticklabels = formatter.format_ticks(b)
1120         offset_string = formatter.get_offset()
1121         return ticks, ticklabels, offset_string

1123     def _process_values(self):
1124         """
1125         Set `_boundaries` and `_values` based on the self.boundaries and
1126         self.values if not None, or based on the size of the colormap and
1127         the vmin/vmax of the norm.
1128         """
1129         if self.values is not None:
1130             # set self._boundaries from the values...
1131             self._values = np.array(self.values)
1132             if self.boundaries is None:
1133                 # bracket values by 1/2 dv:
1134                 b = np.zeros(len(self.values) + 1)
1135                 b[1:-1] = 0.5 * (self._values[:-1] + self._values[1:])
1136                 b[0] = 2.0 * b[1] - b[2]
1137                 b[-1] = 2.0 * b[-2] - b[-3]
1138                 self._boundaries = b
1139                 return
1140             self._boundaries = np.array(self.boundaries)
1141             return
1142 
1143         # otherwise values are set from the boundaries
1144         if isinstance(self.norm, colors.BoundaryNorm):
1145             b = self.norm.boundaries
1146         elif isinstance(self.norm, colors.NoNorm):
1147             # NoNorm has N blocks, so N+1 boundaries, centered on integers:
1148             b = np.arange(self.cmap.N + 1) - .5
1149         elif self.boundaries is not None:
1150             b = self.boundaries
1151         else:
1152             # otherwise make the boundaries from the size of the cmap:
1153             N = self.cmap.N + 1
1154             b, _ = self._uniform_y(N)
1155         # add extra boundaries if needed:
1156         if self._extend_lower():
1157             b = np.hstack((b[0] - 1, b))
1158         if self._extend_upper():
1159             b = np.hstack((b, b[-1] + 1))
1160 
1161         # transform from 0-1 to vmin-vmax:
1162         if not self.norm.scaled():
1163             self.norm.vmin = 0
1164             self.norm.vmax = 1
1165         self.norm.vmin, self.norm.vmax = mtransforms.nonsingular(
1166             self.norm.vmin, self.norm.vmax, expander=0.1)
1167         if (not isinstance(self.norm, colors.BoundaryNorm) and
1168                 (self.boundaries is None)):
1169             b = self.norm.inverse(b)
1170 
1171         self._boundaries = np.asarray(b, dtype=float)
1172         self._values = 0.5 * (self._boundaries[:-1] + self._boundaries[1:])
1173         if isinstance(self.norm, colors.NoNorm):
1174             self._values = (self._values + 0.00001).astype(np.int16)
1175 
1176     def _mesh(self):
1177         """
1178         Return the coordinate arrays for the colorbar pcolormesh/patches.
1179 
1180         These are scaled between vmin and vmax, and already handle colorbar
1181         orientation.
1182         """
1183         y, _ = self._proportional_y()
1184         # Use the vmin and vmax of the colorbar, which may not be the same
1185         # as the norm. There are situations where the colormap has a
1186         # narrower range than the colorbar and we want to accommodate the
1187         # extra contours.
1188         if (isinstance(self.norm, (colors.BoundaryNorm, colors.NoNorm))
1189                 or self.boundaries is not None):
1190             # not using a norm.
1191             y = y * (self.vmax - self.vmin) + self.vmin
1192         else:
1193             # Update the norm values in a context manager as it is only
1194             # a temporary change and we don't want to propagate any signals
1195             # attached to the norm (callbacks.blocked).
1196             with self.norm.callbacks.blocked(), \
1197                     cbook._setattr_cm(self.norm,
1198                                       vmin=self.vmin,
1199                                       vmax=self.vmax):
1200                 y = self.norm.inverse(y)
1201         self._y = y
1202         X, Y = np.meshgrid([0., 1.], y)
1203         if self.orientation == 'vertical':
1204             return (X, Y)
1205         else:
1206             return (Y, X)
1207 
1208     def _forward_boundaries(self, x):
1209         # map boundaries equally between 0 and 1...
1210         b = self._boundaries
1211         y = np.interp(x, b, np.linspace(0, 1, len(b)))
1212         # the following avoids ticks in the extends:
1213         eps = (b[-1] - b[0]) * 1e-6
1214         # map these _well_ out of bounds to keep any ticks out
1215         # of the extends region...
1216         y[x < b[0]-eps] = -1
1217         y[x > b[-1]+eps] = 2
1218         return y
1219 
1220     def _inverse_boundaries(self, x):
1221         # invert the above...
1222         b = self._boundaries
1223         return np.interp(x, np.linspace(0, 1, len(b)), b)
1224 
1225     def _reset_locator_formatter_scale(self):
1226         """
1227         Reset the locator et al to defaults.  Any user-hardcoded changes
1228         need to be re-entered if this gets called (either at init, or when
1229         the mappable normal gets changed: Colorbar.update_normal)
1230         """
1231         self._process_values()
1232         self._locator = None
1233         self._minorlocator = None
1234         self._formatter = None
1235         self._minorformatter = None
1236         if (self.boundaries is not None or
1237                 isinstance(self.norm, colors.BoundaryNorm)):
1238             if self.spacing == 'uniform':
1239                 funcs = (self._forward_boundaries, self._inverse_boundaries)
1240                 self._set_scale('function', functions=funcs)
1241             elif self.spacing == 'proportional':
1242                 self._set_scale('linear')
1243         elif getattr(self.norm, '_scale', None):
1244             # use the norm's scale (if it exists and is not None):
1245             self._set_scale(self.norm._scale)
1246         elif type(self.norm) is colors.Normalize:
1247             # plain Normalize:
1248             self._set_scale('linear')
1249         else:
1250             # norm._scale is None or not an attr: derive the scale from
1251             # the Norm:
1252             funcs = (self.norm, self.norm.inverse)
1253             self._set_scale('function', functions=funcs)
1254 
1255     def _locate(self, x):
1256         """
1257         Given a set of color data values, return their
1258         corresponding colorbar data coordinates.
1259         """
1260         if isinstance(self.norm, (colors.NoNorm, colors.BoundaryNorm)):
1261             b = self._boundaries
1262             xn = x
1263         else:
1264             # Do calculations using normalized coordinates so
1265             # as to make the interpolation more accurate.
1266             b = self.norm(self._boundaries, clip=False).filled()
1267             xn = self.norm(x, clip=False).filled()
1268 
1269         bunique = b[self._inside]
1270         yunique = self._y
1271 
1272         z = np.interp(xn, bunique, yunique)
1273         return z
1274 
1275     # trivial helpers
1276 
1277     def _uniform_y(self, N):
1278         """
1279         Return colorbar data coordinates for *N* uniformly
1280         spaced boundaries, plus extension lengths if required.
1281         """
1282         automin = automax = 1. / (N - 1.)
1283         extendlength = self._get_extension_lengths(self.extendfrac,
1284                                                    automin, automax,
1285                                                    default=0.05)
1286         y = np.linspace(0, 1, N)
1287         return y, extendlength
1288 
1289     def _proportional_y(self):
1290         """
1291         Return colorbar data coordinates for the boundaries of
1292         a proportional colorbar, plus extension lengths if required:
1293         """
1294         if (isinstance(self.norm, colors.BoundaryNorm) or
1295                 self.boundaries is not None):
1296             y = (self._boundaries - self._boundaries[self._inside][0])
1297             y = y / (self._boundaries[self._inside][-1] -
1298                      self._boundaries[self._inside][0])
1299             # need yscaled the same as the axes scale to get
1300             # the extend lengths.
1301             if self.spacing == 'uniform':
1302                 yscaled = self._forward_boundaries(self._boundaries)
1303             else:
1304                 yscaled = y
1305         else:
1306             y = self.norm(self._boundaries.copy())
1307             y = np.ma.filled(y, np.nan)
1308             # the norm and the scale should be the same...
1309             yscaled = y
1310         y = y[self._inside]
1311         yscaled = yscaled[self._inside]
1312         # normalize from 0..1:
1313         norm = colors.Normalize(y[0], y[-1])
1314         y = np.ma.filled(norm(y), np.nan)
1315         norm = colors.Normalize(yscaled[0], yscaled[-1])
1316         yscaled = np.ma.filled(norm(yscaled), np.nan)
1317         # make the lower and upper extend lengths proportional to the lengths
1318         # of the first and last boundary spacing (if extendfrac='auto'):
1319         automin = yscaled[1] - yscaled[0]
1320         automax = yscaled[-1] - yscaled[-2]
1321         extendlength = [0, 0]
1322         if self._extend_lower() or self._extend_upper():
1323             extendlength = self._get_extension_lengths(

76             from its location along the +x axis towards the +y axis.

304 
305             =====   =====================
306             value   description
307             =====   =====================
308             'C'     centered
309             'SW'    lower left corner
310             'S'     middle of bottom edge
311             'SE'    lower right corner

313             =====   =====================

319 
320         See Also
321         --------
322         mpl_toolkits.mplot3d.axes3d.Axes3D.set_box_aspect

326                 "Axes3D currently only supports the aspect argument "

332     def set_box_aspect(self, aspect, *, zoom=1):
333         """
334         Set the Axes box aspect.
335 
336         The box aspect is the ratio of height to width in display
337         units for each face of the box when viewed perpendicular to
338         that face.  This is not to be confused with the data aspect
339         (which for Axes3D is always 'auto').  The default ratios are
340         4:4:3 (x:y:z).
341 
342         To simulate having equal aspect in data space, set the box
343         aspect to match your data range in each dimension.
344 
345         *zoom* controls the overall size of the Axes3D in the figure.
346 
347         Parameters
348         ----------
349         aspect : 3-tuple of floats or None
350             Changes the physical dimensions of the Axes3D, such that the ratio
351             of the axis lengths in display units is x:y:z.
352             If None, defaults to (4,4,3).
353 
354         zoom : float, default: 1
355             Control overall size of the Axes3D in the figure. Must be > 0.
356         """
357         if zoom <= 0:
358             raise ValueError(f'Argument zoom = {zoom} must be > 0')
359 
360         if aspect is None:
361             aspect = np.asarray((4, 4, 3), dtype=float)
362         else:
363             aspect = np.asarray(aspect, dtype=float)
364             _api.check_shape((3,), aspect=aspect)
365         # default scale tuned to match the mpl32 appearance.
366         aspect *= 1.8294640721620434 * zoom / np.linalg.norm(aspect)
367 
368         self._box_aspect = aspect
369         self.stale = True
370 
371     def apply_aspect(self, position=None):
372         if position is None:
373             position = self.get_position(original=True)
374 
375         # in the superclass, we would go through and actually deal with axis
376         # scales and box/datalim. Those are all irrelevant - all we need to do
377         # is make sure our coordinate system is square.
378         trans = self.get_figure().transSubfigure
379         bb = mtransforms.Bbox.unit().transformed(trans)
380         # this is the physical aspect of the panel (or figure):
381         fig_aspect = bb.height / bb.width
382 
383         box_aspect = 1
384         pb = position.frozen()
385         pb1 = pb.shrunk_to_aspect(box_aspect, pb, fig_aspect)
386         self._set_position(pb1.anchored(self.get_anchor(), pb), 'active')

388     @martist.allow_rasterization
389     def draw(self, renderer):
390         self._unstale_viewLim()
391 
392         # draw the background patch
393         self.patch.draw(renderer)
394         self._frameon = False
395 
396         # first, set the aspect
397         # this is duplicated from `axes._base._AxesBase.draw`
398         # but must be called before any of the artist are drawn as
399         # it adjusts the view limits and the size of the bounding box
400         # of the Axes
401         locator = self.get_axes_locator()
402         if locator:
403             pos = locator(self, renderer)
404             self.apply_aspect(pos)
405         else:
406             self.apply_aspect()
407 
408         # add the projection matrix to the renderer
409         self.M = self.get_proj()
410 
411         collections_and_patches = (
412             artist for artist in self._children
413             if isinstance(artist, (mcoll.Collection, mpatches.Patch))
414             and artist.get_visible())
415         if self.computed_zorder:
416             # Calculate projection of collections and patches and zorder
417             # them. Make sure they are drawn above the grids.
418             zorder_offset = max(axis.get_zorder()
419                                 for axis in self._axis_map.values()) + 1
420             collection_zorder = patch_zorder = zorder_offset
421 
422             for artist in sorted(collections_and_patches,
423                                  key=lambda artist: artist.do_3d_projection(),
424                                  reverse=True):
425                 if isinstance(artist, mcoll.Collection):
426                     artist.zorder = collection_zorder
427                     collection_zorder += 1
428                 elif isinstance(artist, mpatches.Patch):
429                     artist.zorder = patch_zorder
430                     patch_zorder += 1
431         else:
432             for artist in collections_and_patches:
433                 artist.do_3d_projection()
434 
435         if self._axis3don:
436             # Draw panes first
437             for axis in self._axis_map.values():
438                 axis.draw_pane(renderer)
439             # Then axes
440             for axis in self._axis_map.values():
441                 axis.draw(renderer)
442 
443         # Then rest
444         super().draw(renderer)
445

506         if x is not None:

509             self.set_ymargin(y)

553     def auto_scale_xyz(self, X, Y, Z=None, had_data=None):
554         # This updates the bounding boxes as to keep a record as to what the
555         # minimum sized rectangular volume holds the data.
556         if np.shape(X) == np.shape(Y):
557             self.xy_dataLim.update_from_data_xy(
558                 np.column_stack([np.ravel(X), np.ravel(Y)]), not had_data)
559         else:
560             self.xy_dataLim.update_from_data_x(X, not had_data)
561             self.xy_dataLim.update_from_data_y(Y, not had_data)
562         if Z is not None:
563             self.zz_dataLim.update_from_data_x(Z, not had_data)
564         # Let autoscale_view figure out how to use this data.
565         self.autoscale_view()

567     def autoscale_view(self, tight=None, scalex=True, scaley=True,
568                        scalez=True):
569         """
570         Autoscale the view limits using the data limits.
571 
572         See `.Axes.autoscale_view` for full documentation.  Because this
573         function applies to 3D Axes, it also takes a *scalez* argument.
574         """
575         # This method looks at the rectangular volume (see above)
576         # of data and decides how to scale the view portal to fit it.
577         if tight is None:
578             _tight = self._tight
579             if not _tight:
580                 # if image data only just use the datalim
581                 for artist in self._children:
582                     if isinstance(artist, mimage.AxesImage):
583                         _tight = True
584                     elif isinstance(artist, (mlines.Line2D, mpatches.Patch)):
585                         _tight = False
586                         break
587         else:
588             _tight = self._tight = bool(tight)
589 
590         if scalex and self.get_autoscalex_on():
591             self._shared_axes["x"].clean()
592             x0, x1 = self.xy_dataLim.intervalx
593             xlocator = self.xaxis.get_major_locator()
594             x0, x1 = xlocator.nonsingular(x0, x1)
595             if self._xmargin > 0:
596                 delta = (x1 - x0) * self._xmargin
597                 x0 -= delta
598                 x1 += delta
599             if not _tight:
600                 x0, x1 = xlocator.view_limits(x0, x1)
601             self.set_xbound(x0, x1)
602 
603         if scaley and self.get_autoscaley_on():
604             self._shared_axes["y"].clean()
605             y0, y1 = self.xy_dataLim.intervaly
606             ylocator = self.yaxis.get_major_locator()
607             y0, y1 = ylocator.nonsingular(y0, y1)
608             if self._ymargin > 0:
609                 delta = (y1 - y0) * self._ymargin
610                 y0 -= delta
611                 y1 += delta
612             if not _tight:
613                 y0, y1 = ylocator.view_limits(y0, y1)
614             self.set_ybound(y0, y1)
615 
616         if scalez and self.get_autoscalez_on():
617             self._shared_axes["z"].clean()
618             z0, z1 = self.zz_dataLim.intervalx
619             zlocator = self.zaxis.get_major_locator()
620             z0, z1 = zlocator.nonsingular(z0, z1)
621             if self._zmargin > 0:
622                 delta = (z1 - z0) * self._zmargin
623                 z0 -= delta
624                 z1 += delta
625             if not _tight:
626                 z0, z1 = zlocator.view_limits(z0, z1)
627             self.set_zbound(z0, z1)

740     def view_init(self, elev=None, azim=None, roll=None, vertical_axis="z"):
741         """
742         Set the elevation and azimuth of the axes in degrees (not radians).
743 
744         This can be used to rotate the axes programmatically.
745 
746         Parameters
747         ----------
748         elev : float, default: None
749             The elevation angle in degrees rotates the camera above the plane
750             pierced by the vertical axis, with a positive angle corresponding
751             to a location above that plane. For example, with the default
752             vertical axis of 'z', the elevation defines the angle of the camera
753             location above the x-y plane.
754             If None, then the initial value as specified in the `Axes3D`
755             constructor is used.
756         azim : float, default: None
757             The azimuthal angle in degrees rotates the camera about the
758             vertical axis, with a positive angle corresponding to a
759             right-handed rotation. For example, with the default vertical axis
760             of 'z', a positive azimuth rotates the camera about the origin from
761             its location along the +x axis towards the +y axis.
762             If None, then the initial value as specified in the `Axes3D`
763             constructor is used.
764         roll : float, default: None
765             The roll angle in degrees rotates the camera about the viewing
766             axis. A positive angle spins the camera clockwise, causing the
767             scene to rotate counter-clockwise.
768             If None, then the initial value as specified in the `Axes3D`
769             constructor is used.
770         vertical_axis : {"z", "x", "y"}, default: "z"
771             The axis to align vertically. *azim* rotates about this axis.
772         """
773 
774         self._dist = 10  # The camera distance from origin. Behaves like zoom
775 
776         if elev is None:
777             self.elev = self.initial_elev
778         else:
779             self.elev = elev
780 
781         if azim is None:
782             self.azim = self.initial_azim
783         else:
784             self.azim = azim
785 
786         if roll is None:
787             self.roll = self.initial_roll
788         else:
789             self.roll = roll
790 
791         self._vertical_axis = _api.check_getitem(
792             dict(x=0, y=1, z=2), vertical_axis=vertical_axis
793         )

795     def set_proj_type(self, proj_type, focal_length=None):
796         """
797         Set the projection type.
798 
799         Parameters
800         ----------
801         proj_type : {'persp', 'ortho'}
802             The projection type.
803         focal_length : float, default: None
804             For a projection type of 'persp', the focal length of the virtual
805             camera. Must be > 0. If None, defaults to 1.
806             The focal length can be computed from a desired Field Of View via
807             the equation: focal_length = 1/tan(FOV/2)
808         """
809         _api.check_in_list(['persp', 'ortho'], proj_type=proj_type)
810         if proj_type == 'persp':
811             if focal_length is None:
812                 focal_length = 1
813             elif focal_length <= 0:
814                 raise ValueError(f"focal_length = {focal_length} must be "
815                                  "greater than 0")
816             self._focal_length = focal_length
817         elif proj_type == 'ortho':
818             if focal_length not in (None, np.inf):
819                 raise ValueError(f"focal_length = {focal_length} must be "
820                                  f"None for proj_type = {proj_type}")
821             self._focal_length = np.inf
822 
823     def _roll_to_vertical(self, arr):
824         """Roll arrays to match the different vertical axis."""
825         return np.roll(arr, self._vertical_axis - 2)
826 
827     def get_proj(self):
828         """Create the projection matrix from the current viewing position."""
829 
830         # Transform to uniform world coordinates 0-1, 0-1, 0-1
831         box_aspect = self._roll_to_vertical(self._box_aspect)
832         worldM = proj3d.world_transformation(
833             *self.get_xlim3d(),
834             *self.get_ylim3d(),
835             *self.get_zlim3d(),
836             pb_aspect=box_aspect,
837         )
838 
839         # Look into the middle of the new coordinates:
840         R = 0.5 * box_aspect
841 
842         # elev stores the elevation angle in the z plane
843         # azim stores the azimuth angle in the x,y plane
844         # roll stores the roll angle about the view axis
845         elev_rad = np.deg2rad(art3d._norm_angle(self.elev))
846         azim_rad = np.deg2rad(art3d._norm_angle(self.azim))
847         roll_rad = np.deg2rad(art3d._norm_angle(self.roll))
848 
849         # Coordinates for a point that rotates around the box of data.
850         # p0, p1 corresponds to rotating the box only around the
851         # vertical axis.
852         # p2 corresponds to rotating the box only around the horizontal
853         # axis.
854         p0 = np.cos(elev_rad) * np.cos(azim_rad)
855         p1 = np.cos(elev_rad) * np.sin(azim_rad)
856         p2 = np.sin(elev_rad)
857 
858         # When changing vertical axis the coordinates changes as well.
859         # Roll the values to get the same behaviour as the default:
860         ps = self._roll_to_vertical([p0, p1, p2])
861 
862         # The coordinates for the eye viewing point. The eye is looking
863         # towards the middle of the box of data from a distance:
864         eye = R + self._dist * ps
865 
866         # TODO: Is this being used somewhere? Can it be removed?
867         self.eye = eye
868         self.vvec = R - eye
869         self.vvec = self.vvec / np.linalg.norm(self.vvec)
870 
871         # Define which axis should be vertical. A negative value
872         # indicates the plot is upside down and therefore the values
873         # have been reversed:
874         V = np.zeros(3)
875         V[self._vertical_axis] = -1 if abs(elev_rad) > 0.5 * np.pi else 1
876 
877         # Generate the view and projection transformation matrices
878         if self._focal_length == np.inf:
879             # Orthographic projection
880             viewM = proj3d.view_transformation(eye, R, V, roll_rad)
881             projM = proj3d.ortho_transformation(-self._dist, self._dist)
882         else:
883             # Perspective projection
884             # Scale the eye dist to compensate for the focal length zoom effect
885             eye_focal = R + self._dist * ps * self._focal_length
886             viewM = proj3d.view_transformation(eye_focal, R, V, roll_rad)
887             projM = proj3d.persp_transformation(-self._dist,
888                                                 self._dist,
889                                                 self._focal_length)
890 
891         # Combine all the transformation matrices to get the final projection
892         M0 = np.dot(viewM, worldM)
893         M = np.dot(projM, M0)
894         return M

1000     def format_coord(self, xd, yd):
1001         """
1002         Given the 2D view coordinates attempt to guess a 3D coordinate.
1003         Looks for the nearest edge to the point and then assumes that
1004         the point is at the same z location as the nearest point on the edge.
1005         """
1006 
1007         if self.M is None:
1008             return ''
1009 
1010         if self.button_pressed in self._rotate_btn:
1011             # ignore xd and yd and display angles instead
1012             norm_elev = art3d._norm_angle(self.elev)
1013             norm_azim = art3d._norm_angle(self.azim)
1014             norm_roll = art3d._norm_angle(self.roll)
1015             return (f"elevation={norm_elev:.0f}\N{DEGREE SIGN}, "
1016                     f"azimuth={norm_azim:.0f}\N{DEGREE SIGN}, "
1017                     f"roll={norm_roll:.0f}\N{DEGREE SIGN}"
1018                     ).replace("-", "\N{MINUS SIGN}")
1019 
1020         # nearest edge
1021         p0, p1 = min(self.tunit_edges(),
1022                      key=lambda edge: proj3d._line2d_seg_dist(
1023                          edge[0], edge[1], (xd, yd)))
1024 
1025         # scale the z value to match
1026         x0, y0, z0 = p0
1027         x1, y1, z1 = p1
1028         d0 = np.hypot(x0-xd, y0-yd)
1029         d1 = np.hypot(x1-xd, y1-yd)
1030         dt = d0+d1
1031         z = d1/dt * z0 + d0/dt * z1
1032 
1033         x, y, z = proj3d.inv_transform(xd, yd, z, self.M)
1034 
1035         xs = self.format_xdata(x)
1036         ys = self.format_ydata(y)
1037         zs = self.format_zdata(z)
1038         return 'x=%s, y=%s, z=%s' % (xs, ys, zs)
1039 
1040     def _on_move(self, event):
1041         """
1042         Mouse moving.
1043 
1044         By default, button-1 rotates and button-3 zooms; these buttons can be
1045         modified via `mouse_init`.
1046         """
1047 
1048         if not self.button_pressed:
1049             return
1050 
1051         if self.M is None:
1052             return
1053 
1054         x, y = event.xdata, event.ydata
1055         # In case the mouse is out of bounds.
1056         if x is None:
1057             return
1058 
1059         dx, dy = x - self.sx, y - self.sy
1060         w = self._pseudo_w
1061         h = self._pseudo_h
1062         self.sx, self.sy = x, y
1063 
1064         # Rotation
1065         if self.button_pressed in self._rotate_btn:
1066             # rotate viewing point
1067             # get the x and y pixel coords
1068             if dx == 0 and dy == 0:
1069                 return
1070 
1071             roll = np.deg2rad(self.roll)
1072             delev = -(dy/h)*180*np.cos(roll) + (dx/w)*180*np.sin(roll)
1073             dazim = -(dy/h)*180*np.sin(roll) - (dx/w)*180*np.cos(roll)
1074             self.elev = self.elev + delev
1075             self.azim = self.azim + dazim
1076             self.get_proj()
1077             self.stale = True
1078             self.figure.canvas.draw_idle()
1079 
1080         elif self.button_pressed == 2:
1081             # pan view
1082             # get the x and y pixel coords
1083             if dx == 0 and dy == 0:
1084                 return
1085             minx, maxx, miny, maxy, minz, maxz = self.get_w_lims()
1086             dx = 1-((w - dx)/w)
1087             dy = 1-((h - dy)/h)
1088             elev = np.deg2rad(self.elev)
1089             azim = np.deg2rad(self.azim)
1090             # project xv, yv, zv -> xw, yw, zw
1091             dxx = (maxx-minx)*(dy*np.sin(elev)*np.cos(azim) + dx*np.sin(azim))
1092             dyy = (maxy-miny)*(-dx*np.cos(azim) + dy*np.sin(elev)*np.sin(azim))
1093             dzz = (maxz-minz)*(-dy*np.cos(elev))
1094             # pan
1095             self.set_xlim3d(minx + dxx, maxx + dxx)
1096             self.set_ylim3d(miny + dyy, maxy + dyy)
1097             self.set_zlim3d(minz + dzz, maxz + dzz)
1098             self.get_proj()
1099             self.figure.canvas.draw_idle()
1100 
1101         # Zoom
1102         elif self.button_pressed in self._zoom_btn:
1103             # zoom view
1104             # hmmm..this needs some help from clipping....
1105             minx, maxx, miny, maxy, minz, maxz = self.get_w_lims()
1106             df = 1-((h - dy)/h)
1107             dx = (maxx-minx)*df
1108             dy = (maxy-miny)*df
1109             dz = (maxz-minz)*df
1110             self.set_xlim3d(minx - dx, maxx + dx)
1111             self.set_ylim3d(miny - dy, maxy + dy)
1112             self.set_zlim3d(minz - dz, maxz + dz)
1113             self.get_proj()
1114             self.figure.canvas.draw_idle()
1115

1305            The *rcount* and *ccount* kwargs, which both default to 50,
1306            determine the maximum number of samples used in each direction.  If
1307            the input data is larger, it will be downsampled (by slicing) to
1308            these numbers of points.
1309 
1310         .. note::
1311 
1312            To maximize rendering speed consider setting *rstride* and *cstride*
1313            to divisors of the number of rows minus 1 and columns minus 1
1314            respectively. For example, given 51 rows rstride can be any of the
1315            divisors of 50.
1316 
1317            Similarly, a setting of *rstride* and *cstride* equal to 1 (or
1318            *rcount* and *ccount* equal the number of rows and columns) can use
1319            the optimized path.
1320 
1321         Parameters
1322         ----------
1323         X, Y, Z : 2D arrays
1324             Data values.
1325 
1326         rcount, ccount : int
1327             Maximum number of samples used in each direction.  If the input
1328             data is larger, it will be downsampled (by slicing) to these
1329             numbers of points.  Defaults to 50.
1330 
1331         rstride, cstride : int
1332             Downsampling stride in each direction.  These arguments are
1333             mutually exclusive with *rcount* and *ccount*.  If only one of
1334             *rstride* or *cstride* is set, the other defaults to 10.
1335 
1336             'classic' mode uses a default of ``rstride = cstride = 10`` instead
1337             of the new default of ``rcount = ccount = 50``.
1338 
1339         color : color-like
1340             Color of the surface patches.
1341 
1342         cmap : Colormap
1343             Colormap of the surface patches.
1344 
1345         facecolors : array-like of colors.
1346             Colors of each individual patch.
1347 
1348         norm : Normalize
1349             Normalization for the colormap.
1350 
1351         vmin, vmax : float
1352             Bounds for the normalization.
1353 
1354         shade : bool, default: True
1355             Whether to shade the facecolors.  Shading is always disabled when
1356             *cmap* is specified.
1357 
1358         lightsource : `~matplotlib.colors.LightSource`
1359             The lightsource to use when *shade* is True.
1360 
1361         **kwargs
1362             Other arguments are forwarded to `.Poly3DCollection`.
1363         """
1364 
1365         had_data = self.has_data()
1366 
1367         if Z.ndim != 2:
1368             raise ValueError("Argument Z must be 2-dimensional.")
1369 
1370         Z = cbook._to_unmasked_float_array(Z)
1371         X, Y, Z = np.broadcast_arrays(X, Y, Z)
1372         rows, cols = Z.shape
1373 
1374         has_stride = 'rstride' in kwargs or 'cstride' in kwargs
1375         has_count = 'rcount' in kwargs or 'ccount' in kwargs
1376 
1377         if has_stride and has_count:
1378             raise ValueError("Cannot specify both stride and count arguments")
1379 
1380         rstride = kwargs.pop('rstride', 10)
1381         cstride = kwargs.pop('cstride', 10)
1382         rcount = kwargs.pop('rcount', 50)
1383         ccount = kwargs.pop('ccount', 50)
1384 
1385         if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']:
1386             # Strides have priority over counts in classic mode.
1387             # So, only compute strides from counts
1388             # if counts were explicitly given
1389             compute_strides = has_count
1390         else:
1391             # If the strides are provided then it has priority.
1392             # Otherwise, compute the strides from the counts.
1393             compute_strides = not has_stride
1394 
1395         if compute_strides:
1396             rstride = int(max(np.ceil(rows / rcount), 1))
1397             cstride = int(max(np.ceil(cols / ccount), 1))
1398 
1399         if 'facecolors' in kwargs:
1400             fcolors = kwargs.pop('facecolors')
1401         else:
1402             color = kwargs.pop('color', None)
1403             if color is None:
1404                 color = self._get_lines.get_next_color()
1405             color = np.array(mcolors.to_rgba(color))
1406             fcolors = None
1407 
1408         cmap = kwargs.get('cmap', None)
1409         shade = kwargs.pop('shade', cmap is None)
1410         if shade is None:
1411             raise ValueError("shade cannot be None.")
1412 
1413         colset = []  # the sampled facecolor
1414         if (rows - 1) % rstride == 0 and \
1415            (cols - 1) % cstride == 0 and \
1416            fcolors is None:
1417             polys = np.stack(
1418                 [cbook._array_patch_perimeters(a, rstride, cstride)
1419                  for a in (X, Y, Z)],
1420                 axis=-1)
1421         else:
1422             # evenly spaced, and including both endpoints
1423             row_inds = list(range(0, rows-1, rstride)) + [rows-1]
1424             col_inds = list(range(0, cols-1, cstride)) + [cols-1]
1425 
1426             polys = []
1427             for rs, rs_next in zip(row_inds[:-1], row_inds[1:]):
1428                 for cs, cs_next in zip(col_inds[:-1], col_inds[1:]):
1429                     ps = [
1430                         # +1 ensures we share edges between polygons
1431                         cbook._array_perimeter(a[rs:rs_next+1, cs:cs_next+1])
1432                         for a in (X, Y, Z)
1433                     ]
1434                     # ps = np.stack(ps, axis=-1)
1435                     ps = np.array(ps).T
1436                     polys.append(ps)
1437 
1438                     if fcolors is not None:
1439                         colset.append(fcolors[rs][cs])
1440 
1441         # In cases where there are NaNs in the data (possibly from masked
1442         # arrays), artifacts can be introduced. Here check whether NaNs exist
1443         # and remove the entries if so
1444         if not isinstance(polys, np.ndarray) or np.isnan(polys).any():
1445             new_polys = []
1446             new_colset = []
1447 
1448             # Depending on fcolors, colset is either an empty list or has as
1449             # many elements as polys. In the former case new_colset results in
1450             # a list with None entries, that is discarded later.
1451             for p, col in itertools.zip_longest(polys, colset):
1452                 new_poly = np.array(p)[~np.isnan(p).any(axis=1)]
1453                 if len(new_poly):
1454                     new_polys.append(new_poly)
1455                     new_colset.append(col)
1456 
1457             # Replace previous polys and, if fcolors is not None, colset
1458             polys = new_polys
1459             if fcolors is not None:
1460                 colset = new_colset
1461 
1462         # note that the striding causes some polygons to have more coordinates
1463         # than others
1464         polyc = art3d.Poly3DCollection(polys, **kwargs)
1465 
1466         if fcolors is not None:
1467             if shade:
1468                 colset = self._shade_colors(
1469                     colset, self._generate_normals(polys), lightsource)
1470             polyc.set_facecolors(colset)
1471             polyc.set_edgecolors(colset)
1472         elif cmap:
1473             # can't always vectorize, because polys might be jagged
1474             if isinstance(polys, np.ndarray):
1475                 avg_z = polys[..., 2].mean(axis=-1)
1476             else:
1477                 avg_z = np.array([ps[:, 2].mean() for ps in polys])
1478             polyc.set_array(avg_z)
1479             if vmin is not None or vmax is not None:
1480                 polyc.set_clim(vmin, vmax)
1481             if norm is not None:
1482                 polyc.set_norm(norm)
1483         else:
1484             if shade:
1485                 colset = self._shade_colors(
1486                     color, self._generate_normals(polys), lightsource)
1487             else:
1488                 colset = color
1489             polyc.set_facecolors(colset)
1490 
1491         self.add_collection(polyc)
1492         self.auto_scale_xyz(X, Y, Z, had_data)
1493 
1494         return polyc
1495 
1496     def _generate_normals(self, polygons):
1497         """
1498         Compute the normals of a list of polygons.
1499 
1500         Normals point towards the viewer for a face with its vertices in
1501         counterclockwise order, following the right hand rule.
1502 
1503         Uses three points equally spaced around the polygon.
1504         This normal of course might not make sense for polygons with more than
1505         three points not lying in a plane, but it's a plausible and fast
1506         approximation.
1507 
1508         Parameters
1509         ----------
1510         polygons : list of (M_i, 3) array-like, or (..., M, 3) array-like
1511             A sequence of polygons to compute normals for, which can have
1512             varying numbers of vertices. If the polygons all have the same
1513             number of vertices and array is passed, then the operation will
1514             be vectorized.
1515 
1516         Returns
1517         -------
1518         normals : (..., 3) array
1519             A normal vector estimated for the polygon.
1520         """
1521         if isinstance(polygons, np.ndarray):
1522             # optimization: polygons all have the same number of points, so can
1523             # vectorize
1524             n = polygons.shape[-2]
1525             i1, i2, i3 = 0, n//3, 2*n//3
1526             v1 = polygons[..., i1, :] - polygons[..., i2, :]
1527             v2 = polygons[..., i2, :] - polygons[..., i3, :]
1528         else:
1529             # The subtraction doesn't vectorize because polygons is jagged.
1530             v1 = np.empty((len(polygons), 3))
1531             v2 = np.empty((len(polygons), 3))
1532             for poly_i, ps in enumerate(polygons):
1533                 n = len(ps)
1534                 i1, i2, i3 = 0, n//3, 2*n//3
1535                 v1[poly_i, :] = ps[i1, :] - ps[i2, :]
1536                 v2[poly_i, :] = ps[i2, :] - ps[i3, :]
1537         return np.cross(v1, v2)
1538 
1539     def _shade_colors(self, color, normals, lightsource=None):
1540         """
1541         Shade *color* using normal vectors given by *normals*.
1542         *color* can also be an array of the same length as *normals*.
1543         """
1544         if lightsource is None:
1545             # chosen for backwards-compatibility
1546             lightsource = mcolors.LightSource(azdeg=225, altdeg=19.4712)
1547 
1548         with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
1549             shade = ((normals / np.linalg.norm(normals, axis=1, keepdims=True))
1550                      @ lightsource.direction)
1551         mask = ~np.isnan(shade)
1552 
1553         if mask.any():
1554             # convert dot product to allowed shading fractions
1555             in_norm = mcolors.Normalize(-1, 1)
1556             out_norm = mcolors.Normalize(0.3, 1).inverse
1557 
1558             def norm(x):
1559                 return out_norm(in_norm(x))
1560 
1561             shade[~mask] = 0
1562 
1563             color = mcolors.to_rgba_array(color)
1564             # shape of color should be (M, 4) (where M is number of faces)
1565             # shape of shade should be (M,)
1566             # colors should have final shape of (M, 4)
1567             alpha = color[:, 3]
1568             colors = norm(shade)[:, np.newaxis] * color
1569             colors[:, 3] = alpha
1570         else:
1571             colors = np.asanyarray(color).copy()
1572 
1573         return colors
1574 
1575     def plot_wireframe(self, X, Y, Z, **kwargs):
1576         """
1577         Plot a 3D wireframe.
1578 
1579         .. note::
1580 
1581            The *rcount* and *ccount* kwargs, which both default to 50,
1582            determine the maximum number of samples used in each direction.  If
1583            the input data is larger, it will be downsampled (by slicing) to
1584            these numbers of points.
1585 
1586         Parameters
1587         ----------
1588         X, Y, Z : 2D arrays
1589             Data values.
1590 
1591         rcount, ccount : int
1592             Maximum number of samples used in each direction.  If the input
1593             data is larger, it will be downsampled (by slicing) to these
1594             numbers of points.  Setting a count to zero causes the data to be
1595             not sampled in the corresponding direction, producing a 3D line
1596             plot rather than a wireframe plot.  Defaults to 50.
1597 
1598         rstride, cstride : int
1599             Downsampling stride in each direction.  These arguments are
1600             mutually exclusive with *rcount* and *ccount*.  If only one of
1601             *rstride* or *cstride* is set, the other defaults to 1.  Setting a
1602             stride to zero causes the data to be not sampled in the
1603             corresponding direction, producing a 3D line plot rather than a
1604             wireframe plot.
1605 
1606             'classic' mode uses a default of ``rstride = cstride = 1`` instead
1607             of the new default of ``rcount = ccount = 50``.
1608 
1609         **kwargs
1610             Other arguments are forwarded to `.Line3DCollection`.
1611         """
1612 
1613         had_data = self.has_data()
1614         if Z.ndim != 2:
1615             raise ValueError("Argument Z must be 2-dimensional.")
1616         # FIXME: Support masked arrays
1617         X, Y, Z = np.broadcast_arrays(X, Y, Z)
1618         rows, cols = Z.shape
1619 
1620         has_stride = 'rstride' in kwargs or 'cstride' in kwargs
1621         has_count = 'rcount' in kwargs or 'ccount' in kwargs
1622 
1623         if has_stride and has_count:
1624             raise ValueError("Cannot specify both stride and count arguments")
1625 
1626         rstride = kwargs.pop('rstride', 1)
1627         cstride = kwargs.pop('cstride', 1)
1628         rcount = kwargs.pop('rcount', 50)
1629         ccount = kwargs.pop('ccount', 50)
1630 
1631         if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']:
1632             # Strides have priority over counts in classic mode.
1633             # So, only compute strides from counts
1634             # if counts were explicitly given
1635             if has_count:
1636                 rstride = int(max(np.ceil(rows / rcount), 1)) if rcount else 0
1637                 cstride = int(max(np.ceil(cols / ccount), 1)) if ccount else 0
1638         else:
1639             # If the strides are provided then it has priority.
1640             # Otherwise, compute the strides from the counts.
1641             if not has_stride:
1642                 rstride = int(max(np.ceil(rows / rcount), 1)) if rcount else 0
1643                 cstride = int(max(np.ceil(cols / ccount), 1)) if ccount else 0
1644 
1645         # We want two sets of lines, one running along the "rows" of
1646         # Z and another set of lines running along the "columns" of Z.
1647         # This transpose will make it easy to obtain the columns.
1648         tX, tY, tZ = np.transpose(X), np.transpose(Y), np.transpose(Z)
1649 
1650         if rstride:
1651             rii = list(range(0, rows, rstride))
1652             # Add the last index only if needed
1653             if rows > 0 and rii[-1] != (rows - 1):
1654                 rii += [rows-1]
1655         else:
1656             rii = []
1657         if cstride:
1658             cii = list(range(0, cols, cstride))
1659             # Add the last index only if needed
1660             if cols > 0 and cii[-1] != (cols - 1):
1661                 cii += [cols-1]
1662         else:
1663             cii = []
1664 
1665         if rstride == 0 and cstride == 0:
1666             raise ValueError("Either rstride or cstride must be non zero")
1667 
1668         # If the inputs were empty, then just
1669         # reset everything.
1670         if Z.size == 0:
1671             rii = []
1672             cii = []
1673 
1674         xlines = [X[i] for i in rii]
1675         ylines = [Y[i] for i in rii]
1676         zlines = [Z[i] for i in rii]
1677 
1678         txlines = [tX[i] for i in cii]
1679         tylines = [tY[i] for i in cii]
1680         tzlines = [tZ[i] for i in cii]
1681 
1682         lines = ([list(zip(xl, yl, zl))
1683                  for xl, yl, zl in zip(xlines, ylines, zlines)]
1684                  + [list(zip(xl, yl, zl))
1685                  for xl, yl, zl in zip(txlines, tylines, tzlines)])
1686 
1687         linec = art3d.Line3DCollection(lines, **kwargs)
1688         self.add_collection(linec)
1689         self.auto_scale_xyz(X, Y, Z, had_data)
1690 
1691         return linec
