2239 class LightSource:
2240     """
2241     Create a light source coming from the specified azimuth and elevation.
2242     Angles are in degrees, with the azimuth measured
2243     clockwise from north and elevation up from the zero plane of the surface.
2244 
2245     `shade` is used to produce "shaded" RGB values for a data array.
2246     `shade_rgb` can be used to combine an RGB image with an elevation map.
2247     `hillshade` produces an illumination map of a surface.
2248     """
2249 
2250     def __init__(self, azdeg=315, altdeg=45, hsv_min_val=0, hsv_max_val=1,
2251                  hsv_min_sat=1, hsv_max_sat=0):
2252         """
2253         Specify the azimuth (measured clockwise from south) and altitude
2254         (measured up from the plane of the surface) of the light source
2255         in degrees.
2256 
2257         Parameters
2258         ----------
2259         azdeg : float, default: 315 degrees (from the northwest)
2260             The azimuth (0-360, degrees clockwise from North) of the light
2261             source.
2262         altdeg : float, default: 45 degrees
2263             The altitude (0-90, degrees up from horizontal) of the light
2264             source.
2265 
2266         Notes
2267         -----
2268         For backwards compatibility, the parameters *hsv_min_val*,
2269         *hsv_max_val*, *hsv_min_sat*, and *hsv_max_sat* may be supplied at
2270         initialization as well.  However, these parameters will only be used if
2271         "blend_mode='hsv'" is passed into `shade` or `shade_rgb`.
2272         See the documentation for `blend_hsv` for more details.
2273         """
2274         self.azdeg = azdeg
2275         self.altdeg = altdeg
2276         self.hsv_min_val = hsv_min_val
2277         self.hsv_max_val = hsv_max_val
2278         self.hsv_min_sat = hsv_min_sat
2279         self.hsv_max_sat = hsv_max_sat
2280 
2281     @property
2282     def direction(self):
2283         """The unit vector direction towards the light source."""
2284         # Azimuth is in degrees clockwise from North. Convert to radians
2285         # counterclockwise from East (mathematical notation).
2286         az = np.radians(90 - self.azdeg)
2287         alt = np.radians(self.altdeg)
2288         return np.array([
2289             np.cos(az) * np.cos(alt),
2290             np.sin(az) * np.cos(alt),
2291             np.sin(alt)
2292         ])
2293 
2294     def hillshade(self, elevation, vert_exag=1, dx=1, dy=1, fraction=1.):
2295         """
2296         Calculate the illumination intensity for a surface using the defined
2297         azimuth and elevation for the light source.
2298 
2299         This computes the normal vectors for the surface, and then passes them
2300         on to `shade_normals`
2301 
2302         Parameters
2303         ----------
2304         elevation : 2D array-like
2305             The height values used to generate an illumination map
2306         vert_exag : number, optional
2307             The amount to exaggerate the elevation values by when calculating
2308             illumination. This can be used either to correct for differences in
2309             units between the x-y coordinate system and the elevation
2310             coordinate system (e.g. decimal degrees vs. meters) or to
2311             exaggerate or de-emphasize topographic effects.
2312         dx : number, optional
2313             The x-spacing (columns) of the input *elevation* grid.
2314         dy : number, optional
2315             The y-spacing (rows) of the input *elevation* grid.
2316         fraction : number, optional
2317             Increases or decreases the contrast of the hillshade.  Values
2318             greater than one will cause intermediate values to move closer to
2319             full illumination or shadow (and clipping any values that move
2320             beyond 0 or 1). Note that this is not visually or mathematically
2321             the same as vertical exaggeration.
2322 
2323         Returns
2324         -------
2325         `~numpy.ndarray`
2326             A 2D array of illumination values between 0-1, where 0 is
2327             completely in shadow and 1 is completely illuminated.
2328         """
2329 
2330         # Because most image and raster GIS data has the first row in the array
2331         # as the "top" of the image, dy is implicitly negative.  This is
2332         # consistent to what `imshow` assumes, as well.
2333         dy = -dy
2334 
2335         # compute the normal vectors from the partial derivatives
2336         e_dy, e_dx = np.gradient(vert_exag * elevation, dy, dx)
2337 
2338         # .view is to keep subclasses
2339         normal = np.empty(elevation.shape + (3,)).view(type(elevation))
2340         normal[..., 0] = -e_dx
2341         normal[..., 1] = -e_dy
2342         normal[..., 2] = 1
2343         normal /= _vector_magnitude(normal)
2344 
2345         return self.shade_normals(normal, fraction)
2346 
2347     def shade_normals(self, normals, fraction=1.):
2348         """
2349         Calculate the illumination intensity for the normal vectors of a
2350         surface using the defined azimuth and elevation for the light source.
2351 
2352         Imagine an artificial sun placed at infinity in some azimuth and
2353         elevation position illuminating our surface. The parts of the surface
2354         that slope toward the sun should brighten while those sides facing away
2355         should become darker.
2356 
2357         Parameters
2358         ----------
2359         fraction : number, optional
2360             Increases or decreases the contrast of the hillshade.  Values
2361             greater than one will cause intermediate values to move closer to
2362             full illumination or shadow (and clipping any values that move
2363             beyond 0 or 1). Note that this is not visually or mathematically
2364             the same as vertical exaggeration.
2365 
2366         Returns
2367         -------
2368         `~numpy.ndarray`
2369             A 2D array of illumination values between 0-1, where 0 is
2370             completely in shadow and 1 is completely illuminated.
2371         """
2372 
2373         intensity = normals.dot(self.direction)
2374 
2375         # Apply contrast stretch
2376         imin, imax = intensity.min(), intensity.max()
2377         intensity *= fraction
2378 
2379         # Rescale to 0-1, keeping range before contrast stretch
2380         # If constant slope, keep relative scaling (i.e. flat should be 0.5,
2381         # fully occluded 0, etc.)
2382         if (imax - imin) > 1e-6:
2383             # Strictly speaking, this is incorrect. Negative values should be
2384             # clipped to 0 because they're fully occluded. However, rescaling
2385             # in this manner is consistent with the previous implementation and
2386             # visually appears better than a "hard" clip.
2387             intensity -= imin
2388             intensity /= (imax - imin)
2389         intensity = np.clip(intensity, 0, 1)
2390 
2391         return intensity
2392 
2393     def shade(self, data, cmap, norm=None, blend_mode='overlay', vmin=None,
2394               vmax=None, vert_exag=1, dx=1, dy=1, fraction=1, **kwargs):
2395         """
2396         Combine colormapped data values with an illumination intensity map
2397         (a.k.a.  "hillshade") of the values.
2398 
2399         Parameters
2400         ----------
2401         data : 2D array-like
2402             The height values used to generate a shaded map.
2403         cmap : `~matplotlib.colors.Colormap`
2404             The colormap used to color the *data* array. Note that this must be
2405             a `~matplotlib.colors.Colormap` instance.  For example, rather than
2406             passing in ``cmap='gist_earth'``, use
2407             ``cmap=plt.get_cmap('gist_earth')`` instead.
2408         norm : `~matplotlib.colors.Normalize` instance, optional
2409             The normalization used to scale values before colormapping. If
2410             None, the input will be linearly scaled between its min and max.
2411         blend_mode : {'hsv', 'overlay', 'soft'} or callable, optional
2412             The type of blending used to combine the colormapped data
2413             values with the illumination intensity.  Default is
2414             "overlay".  Note that for most topographic surfaces,
2415             "overlay" or "soft" appear more visually realistic. If a
2416             user-defined function is supplied, it is expected to
2417             combine an (M, N, 3) RGB array of floats (ranging 0 to 1) with
2418             an (M, N, 1) hillshade array (also 0 to 1).  (Call signature
2419             ``func(rgb, illum, **kwargs)``) Additional kwargs supplied
2420             to this function will be passed on to the *blend_mode*
2421             function.
2422         vmin : float or None, optional
2423             The minimum value used in colormapping *data*. If *None* the
2424             minimum value in *data* is used. If *norm* is specified, then this
2425             argument will be ignored.
2426         vmax : float or None, optional
2427             The maximum value used in colormapping *data*. If *None* the
2428             maximum value in *data* is used. If *norm* is specified, then this
2429             argument will be ignored.
2430         vert_exag : number, optional
2431             The amount to exaggerate the elevation values by when calculating
2432             illumination. This can be used either to correct for differences in
2433             units between the x-y coordinate system and the elevation
2434             coordinate system (e.g. decimal degrees vs. meters) or to
2435             exaggerate or de-emphasize topography.
2436         dx : number, optional
2437             The x-spacing (columns) of the input *elevation* grid.
2438         dy : number, optional
2439             The y-spacing (rows) of the input *elevation* grid.
2440         fraction : number, optional
2441             Increases or decreases the contrast of the hillshade.  Values
2442             greater than one will cause intermediate values to move closer to
2443             full illumination or shadow (and clipping any values that move
2444             beyond 0 or 1). Note that this is not visually or mathematically
2445             the same as vertical exaggeration.
2446         **kwargs
2447             Additional kwargs are passed on to the *blend_mode* function.
2448 
2449         Returns
2450         -------
2451         `~numpy.ndarray`
2452             An (M, N, 4) array of floats ranging between 0-1.
2453         """
2454         if vmin is None:
2455             vmin = data.min()
2456         if vmax is None:
2457             vmax = data.max()
2458         if norm is None:
2459             norm = Normalize(vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)
2460 
2461         rgb0 = cmap(norm(data))
2462         rgb1 = self.shade_rgb(rgb0, elevation=data, blend_mode=blend_mode,
2463                               vert_exag=vert_exag, dx=dx, dy=dy,
2464                               fraction=fraction, **kwargs)
2465         # Don't overwrite the alpha channel, if present.
2466         rgb0[..., :3] = rgb1[..., :3]
2467         return rgb0
2468 
2469     def shade_rgb(self, rgb, elevation, fraction=1., blend_mode='hsv',
2470                   vert_exag=1, dx=1, dy=1, **kwargs):
2471         """
2472         Use this light source to adjust the colors of the *rgb* input array to
2473         give the impression of a shaded relief map with the given *elevation*.
2474 
2475         Parameters
2476         ----------
2477         rgb : array-like
2478             An (M, N, 3) RGB array, assumed to be in the range of 0 to 1.
2479         elevation : array-like
2480             An (M, N) array of the height values used to generate a shaded map.
2481         fraction : number
2482             Increases or decreases the contrast of the hillshade.  Values
2483             greater than one will cause intermediate values to move closer to
2484             full illumination or shadow (and clipping any values that move
2485             beyond 0 or 1). Note that this is not visually or mathematically
2486             the same as vertical exaggeration.
2487         blend_mode : {'hsv', 'overlay', 'soft'} or callable, optional
2488             The type of blending used to combine the colormapped data values
2489             with the illumination intensity.  For backwards compatibility, this
2490             defaults to "hsv". Note that for most topographic surfaces,
2491             "overlay" or "soft" appear more visually realistic. If a
2492             user-defined function is supplied, it is expected to combine an
2493             (M, N, 3) RGB array of floats (ranging 0 to 1) with an (M, N, 1)
2494             hillshade array (also 0 to 1).  (Call signature
2495             ``func(rgb, illum, **kwargs)``)
2496             Additional kwargs supplied to this function will be passed on to
2497             the *blend_mode* function.
2498         vert_exag : number, optional
2499             The amount to exaggerate the elevation values by when calculating
2500             illumination. This can be used either to correct for differences in
2501             units between the x-y coordinate system and the elevation
2502             coordinate system (e.g. decimal degrees vs. meters) or to
2503             exaggerate or de-emphasize topography.
2504         dx : number, optional
2505             The x-spacing (columns) of the input *elevation* grid.
2506         dy : number, optional
2507             The y-spacing (rows) of the input *elevation* grid.
2508         **kwargs
2509             Additional kwargs are passed on to the *blend_mode* function.
2510 
2511         Returns
2512         -------
2513         `~numpy.ndarray`
2514             An (m, n, 3) array of floats ranging between 0-1.

311     def _suplabels(self, t, info, **kwargs):
312         """
313         Add a centered %(name)s to the figure.
314 
315         Parameters
316         ----------
317         t : str
318             The %(name)s text.
319         x : float, default: %(x0)s
320             The x location of the text in figure coordinates.
321         y : float, default: %(y0)s
322             The y location of the text in figure coordinates.
323         horizontalalignment, ha : {'center', 'left', 'right'}, default: %(ha)s
324             The horizontal alignment of the text relative to (*x*, *y*).
325         verticalalignment, va : {'top', 'center', 'bottom', 'baseline'}, \
326 default: %(va)s
327             The vertical alignment of the text relative to (*x*, *y*).
328         fontsize, size : default: :rc:`figure.%(rc)ssize`
329             The font size of the text. See `.Text.set_size` for possible
330             values.
331         fontweight, weight : default: :rc:`figure.%(rc)sweight`
332             The font weight of the text. See `.Text.set_weight` for possible
333             values.
334 
335         Returns
336         -------
337         text
338             The `.Text` instance of the %(name)s.
339 
340         Other Parameters
341         ----------------
342         fontproperties : None or dict, optional
343             A dict of font properties. If *fontproperties* is given the
344             default values for font size and weight are taken from the
345             `.FontProperties` defaults. :rc:`figure.%(rc)ssize` and
346             :rc:`figure.%(rc)sweight` are ignored in this case.
347 
348         **kwargs
349             Additional kwargs are `matplotlib.text.Text` properties.
350         """
351 
352         suplab = getattr(self, info['name'])
353 
354         x = kwargs.pop('x', None)
355         y = kwargs.pop('y', None)
356         if info['name'] in ['_supxlabel', '_suptitle']:
357             autopos = y is None
358         elif info['name'] == '_supylabel':
359             autopos = x is None
360         if x is None:
361             x = info['x0']
362         if y is None:
363             y = info['y0']
364 
365         if 'horizontalalignment' not in kwargs and 'ha' not in kwargs:
366             kwargs['horizontalalignment'] = info['ha']
367         if 'verticalalignment' not in kwargs and 'va' not in kwargs:
368             kwargs['verticalalignment'] = info['va']
369         if 'rotation' not in kwargs:
370             kwargs['rotation'] = info['rotation']
371 
372         if 'fontproperties' not in kwargs:
373             if 'fontsize' not in kwargs and 'size' not in kwargs:
374                 kwargs['size'] = mpl.rcParams[info['size']]
375             if 'fontweight' not in kwargs and 'weight' not in kwargs:
376                 kwargs['weight'] = mpl.rcParams[info['weight']]
377 
378         sup = self.text(x, y, t, **kwargs)
379         if suplab is not None:
380             suplab.set_text(t)
381             suplab.set_position((x, y))
382             suplab.update_from(sup)
383             sup.remove()
384         else:
385             suplab = sup
386         suplab._autopos = autopos
387         setattr(self, info['name'], suplab)
388         self.stale = True
389         return suplab

798     def subplots(self, nrows=1, ncols=1, *, sharex=False, sharey=False,
799                  squeeze=True, width_ratios=None, height_ratios=None,
800                  subplot_kw=None, gridspec_kw=None):
801         """
802         Add a set of subplots to this figure.
803 
804         This utility wrapper makes it convenient to create common layouts of
805         subplots in a single call.
806 
807         Parameters
808         ----------
809         nrows, ncols : int, default: 1
810             Number of rows/columns of the subplot grid.
811 
812         sharex, sharey : bool or {'none', 'all', 'row', 'col'}, default: False
813             Controls sharing of x-axis (*sharex*) or y-axis (*sharey*):
814 
815             - True or 'all': x- or y-axis will be shared among all subplots.
816             - False or 'none': each subplot x- or y-axis will be independent.
817             - 'row': each subplot row will share an x- or y-axis.
818             - 'col': each subplot column will share an x- or y-axis.
819 
820             When subplots have a shared x-axis along a column, only the x tick
821             labels of the bottom subplot are created. Similarly, when subplots
822             have a shared y-axis along a row, only the y tick labels of the
823             first column subplot are created. To later turn other subplots'
824             ticklabels on, use `~matplotlib.axes.Axes.tick_params`.
825 
826             When subplots have a shared axis that has units, calling
827             `.Axis.set_units` will update each axis with the new units.
828 
829         squeeze : bool, default: True
830             - If True, extra dimensions are squeezed out from the returned
831               array of Axes:
832 
833               - if only one subplot is constructed (nrows=ncols=1), the
834                 resulting single Axes object is returned as a scalar.
835               - for Nx1 or 1xM subplots, the returned object is a 1D numpy
836                 object array of Axes objects.
837               - for NxM, subplots with N>1 and M>1 are returned as a 2D array.
838 
839             - If False, no squeezing at all is done: the returned Axes object
840               is always a 2D array containing Axes instances, even if it ends
841               up being 1x1.
842 
843         width_ratios : array-like of length *ncols*, optional
844             Defines the relative widths of the columns. Each column gets a
845             relative width of ``width_ratios[i] / sum(width_ratios)``.
846             If not given, all columns will have the same width.  Equivalent
847             to ``gridspec_kw={'width_ratios': [...]}``.
848 
849         height_ratios : array-like of length *nrows*, optional
850             Defines the relative heights of the rows. Each row gets a
851             relative height of ``height_ratios[i] / sum(height_ratios)``.
852             If not given, all rows will have the same height. Equivalent
853             to ``gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [...]}``.
854 
855         subplot_kw : dict, optional
856             Dict with keywords passed to the `.Figure.add_subplot` call used to
857             create each subplot.
858 
859         gridspec_kw : dict, optional
860             Dict with keywords passed to the
861             `~matplotlib.gridspec.GridSpec` constructor used to create
862             the grid the subplots are placed on.
863 
864         Returns
865         -------
866         `~.axes.Axes` or array of Axes
867             Either a single `~matplotlib.axes.Axes` object or an array of Axes
868             objects if more than one subplot was created. The dimensions of the
869             resulting array can be controlled with the *squeeze* keyword, see
870             above.
871 
872         See Also
873         --------
874         .pyplot.subplots
875         .Figure.add_subplot
876         .pyplot.subplot
877 
878         Examples
879         --------
880         ::
881 
882             # First create some toy data:
883             x = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 400)
884             y = np.sin(x**2)
885 
886             # Create a figure
887             fig = plt.figure()
888 
889             # Create a subplot
890             ax = fig.subplots()
891             ax.plot(x, y)
892             ax.set_title('Simple plot')
893 
894             # Create two subplots and unpack the output array immediately
895             ax1, ax2 = fig.subplots(1, 2, sharey=True)
896             ax1.plot(x, y)
897             ax1.set_title('Sharing Y axis')
898             ax2.scatter(x, y)
899 
900             # Create four polar Axes and access them through the returned array
901             axes = fig.subplots(2, 2, subplot_kw=dict(projection='polar'))
902             axes[0, 0].plot(x, y)
903             axes[1, 1].scatter(x, y)
904 
905             # Share an X-axis with each column of subplots

1364 
1365         If a label is on the bottom, it is aligned with labels on Axes that
1366         also have their label on the bottom and that have the same
1367         bottom-most subplot row.  If the label is on the top,
1368         it is aligned with labels on Axes with the same top-most row.
1369

1371         ----------
1372         axs : list of `~matplotlib.axes.Axes`
1373             Optional list of (or `~numpy.ndarray`) `~matplotlib.axes.Axes`
1374             to align the xlabels.

1376

1378         --------
1379         matplotlib.figure.Figure.align_ylabels
1380         matplotlib.figure.Figure.align_labels
1381 
1382         Notes
1383         -----
1384         This assumes that ``axs`` are from the same `.GridSpec`, so that
1385         their `.SubplotSpec` positions correspond to figure positions.

1387         Examples
1388         --------
1389         Example with rotated xtick labels::
1390 
1391             fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2)
1392             for tick in axs[0].get_xticklabels():
1393                 tick.set_rotation(55)
1394             axs[0].set_xlabel('XLabel 0')
1395             axs[1].set_xlabel('XLabel 1')
1396             fig.align_xlabels()

1398         if axs is None:
1399             axs = self.axes
1400         axs = [ax for ax in np.ravel(axs) if ax.get_subplotspec() is not None]

1403             rowspan = ax.get_subplotspec().rowspan
1404             pos = ax.xaxis.get_label_position()  # top or bottom
1405             # Search through other axes for label positions that are same as
1406             # this one and that share the appropriate row number.
1407             # Add to a grouper associated with each axes of siblings.
1408             # This list is inspected in `axis.draw` by

1411                 if axc.xaxis.get_label_position() == pos:
1412                     rowspanc = axc.get_subplotspec().rowspan

1532             fig = plt.figure()
1533             gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2)
1534             ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
1535             ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
1536             # spans two rows:
1537             ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[:, 1])
1538 
1539         """
1540 
1541         _ = kwargs.pop('figure', None)  # pop in case user has added this...
1542         gs = GridSpec(nrows=nrows, ncols=ncols, figure=self, **kwargs)
1543         return gs

1545     def subfigures(self, nrows=1, ncols=1, squeeze=True,
1546                    wspace=None, hspace=None,
1547                    width_ratios=None, height_ratios=None,
1548                    **kwargs):
1549         """
1550         Add a set of subfigures to this figure or subfigure.
1551 
1552         A subfigure has the same artist methods as a figure, and is logically
1553         the same as a figure, but cannot print itself.
1554         See :doc:`/gallery/subplots_axes_and_figures/subfigures`.
1555 
1556         .. note::
1557             The *subfigure* concept is new in v3.4, and the API is still provisional.
1558 
1559         Parameters
1560         ----------
1561         nrows, ncols : int, default: 1
1562             Number of rows/columns of the subfigure grid.
1563 
1564         squeeze : bool, default: True
1565             If True, extra dimensions are squeezed out from the returned
1566             array of subfigures.
1567 
1568         wspace, hspace : float, default: None
1569             The amount of width/height reserved for space between subfigures,
1570             expressed as a fraction of the average subfigure width/height.
1571             If not given, the values will be inferred from a figure or
1572             rcParams when necessary.
1573 
1574         width_ratios : array-like of length *ncols*, optional
1575             Defines the relative widths of the columns. Each column gets a
1576             relative width of ``width_ratios[i] / sum(width_ratios)``.
1577             If not given, all columns will have the same width.
1578 
1579         height_ratios : array-like of length *nrows*, optional
1580             Defines the relative heights of the rows. Each row gets a
1581             relative height of ``height_ratios[i] / sum(height_ratios)``.
1582             If not given, all rows will have the same height.
1583         """
1584         gs = GridSpec(nrows=nrows, ncols=ncols, figure=self,
1585                       wspace=wspace, hspace=hspace,
1586                       width_ratios=width_ratios,
1587                       height_ratios=height_ratios)
1588 
1589         sfarr = np.empty((nrows, ncols), dtype=object)
1590         for i in range(ncols):
1591             for j in range(nrows):
1592                 sfarr[j, i] = self.add_subfigure(gs[j, i], **kwargs)
1593 
1594         if squeeze:
1595             # Discarding unneeded dimensions that equal 1.  If we only have one
1596             # subfigure, just return it instead of a 1-element array.
1597             return sfarr.item() if sfarr.size == 1 else sfarr.squeeze()
1598         else:
1599             # Returned axis array will be always 2-d, even if nrows=ncols=1.
1600             return sfarr

1648     def _gci(self):
1649         # Helper for `~matplotlib.pyplot.gci`.  Do not use elsewhere.
1650         """
1651         Get the current colorable artist.
1652 
1653         Specifically, returns the current `.ScalarMappable` instance (`.Image`
1654         created by `imshow` or `figimage`, `.Collection` created by `pcolor` or
1655         `scatter`, etc.), or *None* if no such instance has been defined.
1656 
1657         The current image is an attribute of the current Axes, or the nearest
1658         earlier Axes in the current figure that contains an image.
1659 
1660         Notes
1661         -----
1662         Historically, the only colorable artists were images; hence the name
1663         ``gci`` (get current image).
1664         """
1665         # Look first for an image in the current Axes.
1666         ax = self._axstack.current()
1667         if ax is None:
1668             return None
1669         im = ax._gci()
1670         if im is not None:
1671             return im
1672         # If there is no image in the current Axes, search for
1673         # one in a previously created Axes.  Whether this makes
1674         # sense is debatable, but it is the documented behavior.
1675         for ax in reversed(self.axes):
1676             im = ax._gci()
1677             if im is not None:
1678                 return im
1679         return None

1681     def _process_projection_requirements(self, *, axes_class=None, polar=False,
1682                                          projection=None, **kwargs):

1686             (axes_proj_class, proj_class_kwargs)

1699                     raise ValueError(
1700                         f"polar={polar}, yet projection={projection!r}. "
1701                         "Only one of these arguments should be supplied."
1702                     )

1705             if isinstance(projection, str) or projection is None:

1711                 raise TypeError(
1712                     f"projection must be a string, None or implement a "
1713                     f"_as_mpl_axes method, not {projection!r}")

1724     @_api.make_keyword_only("3.8", "bbox_extra_artists")
1725     def get_tightbbox(self, renderer=None, bbox_extra_artists=None):
1726         """
1727         Return a (tight) bounding box of the figure *in inches*.
1728 
1729         Note that `.FigureBase` differs from all other artists, which return
1730         their `.Bbox` in pixels.
1731 
1732         Artists that have ``artist.set_in_layout(False)`` are not included
1733         in the bbox.
1734 
1735         Parameters
1736         ----------
1737         renderer : `.RendererBase` subclass
1738             Renderer that will be used to draw the figures (i.e.
1739             ``fig.canvas.get_renderer()``)
1740 
1741         bbox_extra_artists : list of `.Artist` or ``None``
1742             List of artists to include in the tight bounding box.  If
1743             ``None`` (default), then all artist children of each Axes are
1744             included in the tight bounding box.
1745 
1746         Returns
1747         -------
1748         `.BboxBase`
1749             containing the bounding box (in figure inches).
1750         """
1751 
1752         if renderer is None:
1753             renderer = self.figure._get_renderer()
1754 
1755         bb = []
1756         if bbox_extra_artists is None:
1757             artists = self.get_default_bbox_extra_artists()
1758         else:
1759             artists = bbox_extra_artists
1760 
1761         for a in artists:
1762             bbox = a.get_tightbbox(renderer)
1763             if bbox is not None:
1764                 bb.append(bbox)
1765 
1766         for ax in self.axes:
1767             if ax.get_visible():
1768                 # some axes don't take the bbox_extra_artists kwarg so we
1769                 # need this conditional....
1770                 try:
1771                     bbox = ax.get_tightbbox(
1772                         renderer, bbox_extra_artists=bbox_extra_artists)
1773                 except TypeError:
1774                     bbox = ax.get_tightbbox(renderer)
1775                 bb.append(bbox)
1776         bb = [b for b in bb
1777               if (np.isfinite(b.width) and np.isfinite(b.height)
1778                   and (b.width != 0 or b.height != 0))]
1779 
1780         isfigure = hasattr(self, 'bbox_inches')
1781         if len(bb) == 0:
1782             if isfigure:
1783                 return self.bbox_inches
1784             else:
1785                 # subfigures do not have bbox_inches, but do have a bbox
1786                 bb = [self.bbox]
1787 
1788         _bbox = Bbox.union(bb)
1789 
1790         if isfigure:
1791             # transform from pixels to inches...
1792             _bbox = TransformedBbox(_bbox, self.dpi_scale_trans.inverted())
1793 
1794         return _bbox

1805                             )
1806                     expanded[sub_key] = v
1807             else:

1809                     raise ValueError(
1810                         f'The key {k!r} appears multiple times.'
1811                     )

1825     def subplot_mosaic(self, mosaic, *, sharex=False, sharey=False,
1826                        width_ratios=None, height_ratios=None,
1827                        empty_sentinel='.',
1828                        subplot_kw=None, per_subplot_kw=None, gridspec_kw=None):
1829         """
1830         Build a layout of Axes based on ASCII art or nested lists.
1831 
1832         This is a helper function to build complex GridSpec layouts visually.
1833 
1834         See :ref:`mosaic`
1835         for an example and full API documentation
1836 
1837         Parameters
1838         ----------
1839         mosaic : list of list of {hashable or nested} or str
1840 
1841             A visual layout of how you want your Axes to be arranged
1842             labeled as strings.  For example ::
1843 
1844                x = [['A panel', 'A panel', 'edge'],
1845                     ['C panel', '.',       'edge']]
1846 
1847             produces 4 Axes:
1848 
1849             - 'A panel' which is 1 row high and spans the first two columns
1850             - 'edge' which is 2 rows high and is on the right edge
1851             - 'C panel' which in 1 row and 1 column wide in the bottom left
1852             - a blank space 1 row and 1 column wide in the bottom center
1853 
1854             Any of the entries in the layout can be a list of lists
1855             of the same form to create nested layouts.
1856 
1857             If input is a str, then it can either be a multi-line string of
1858             the form ::
1859 
1860               '''
1861               AAE
1862               C.E
1863               '''
1864 
1865             where each character is a column and each line is a row. Or it
1866             can be a single-line string where rows are separated by ``;``::
1867 
1868               'AB;CC'
1869 
1870             The string notation allows only single character Axes labels and
1871             does not support nesting but is very terse.
1872 
1873             The Axes identifiers may be `str` or a non-iterable hashable
1874             object (e.g. `tuple` s may not be used).
1875 
1876         sharex, sharey : bool, default: False
1877             If True, the x-axis (*sharex*) or y-axis (*sharey*) will be shared
1878             among all subplots.  In that case, tick label visibility and axis
1879             units behave as for `subplots`.  If False, each subplot's x- or
1880             y-axis will be independent.
1881 
1882         width_ratios : array-like of length *ncols*, optional
1883             Defines the relative widths of the columns. Each column gets a
1884             relative width of ``width_ratios[i] / sum(width_ratios)``.
1885             If not given, all columns will have the same width.  Equivalent
1886             to ``gridspec_kw={'width_ratios': [...]}``. In the case of nested
1887             layouts, this argument applies only to the outer layout.
1888 
1889         height_ratios : array-like of length *nrows*, optional
1890             Defines the relative heights of the rows. Each row gets a
1891             relative height of ``height_ratios[i] / sum(height_ratios)``.
1892             If not given, all rows will have the same height. Equivalent
1893             to ``gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [...]}``. In the case of nested
1894             layouts, this argument applies only to the outer layout.
1895 
1896         subplot_kw : dict, optional
1897             Dictionary with keywords passed to the `.Figure.add_subplot` call
1898             used to create each subplot.  These values may be overridden by
1899             values in *per_subplot_kw*.
1900 
1901         per_subplot_kw : dict, optional
1902             A dictionary mapping the Axes identifiers or tuples of identifiers
1903             to a dictionary of keyword arguments to be passed to the
1904             `.Figure.add_subplot` call used to create each subplot.  The values
1905             in these dictionaries have precedence over the values in
1906             *subplot_kw*.
1907 
1908             If *mosaic* is a string, and thus all keys are single characters,
1909             it is possible to use a single string instead of a tuple as keys;
1910             i.e. ``"AB"`` is equivalent to ``("A", "B")``.
1911 
1912             .. versionadded:: 3.7
1913 
1914         gridspec_kw : dict, optional
1915             Dictionary with keywords passed to the `.GridSpec` constructor used
1916             to create the grid the subplots are placed on. In the case of
1917             nested layouts, this argument applies only to the outer layout.
1918             For more complex layouts, users should use `.Figure.subfigures`
1919             to create the nesting.
1920 
1921         empty_sentinel : object, optional
1922             Entry in the layout to mean "leave this space empty".  Defaults
1923             to ``'.'``. Note, if *layout* is a string, it is processed via
1924             `inspect.cleandoc` to remove leading white space, which may
1925             interfere with using white-space as the empty sentinel.
1926 
1927         Returns
1928         -------
1929         dict[label, Axes]
1930            A dictionary mapping the labels to the Axes objects.  The order of
1931            the axes is left-to-right and top-to-bottom of their position in the
1932            total layout.
1933 
1934         """
1935         subplot_kw = subplot_kw or {}
1936         gridspec_kw = dict(gridspec_kw or {})
1937         per_subplot_kw = per_subplot_kw or {}
1938 
1939         if height_ratios is not None:
1940             if 'height_ratios' in gridspec_kw:
1941                 raise ValueError("'height_ratios' must not be defined both as "
1942                                  "parameter and as key in 'gridspec_kw'")
1943             gridspec_kw['height_ratios'] = height_ratios
1944         if width_ratios is not None:
1945             if 'width_ratios' in gridspec_kw:
1946                 raise ValueError("'width_ratios' must not be defined both as "
1947                                  "parameter and as key in 'gridspec_kw'")
1948             gridspec_kw['width_ratios'] = width_ratios
1949 
1950         # special-case string input
1951         if isinstance(mosaic, str):
1952             mosaic = self._normalize_grid_string(mosaic)
1953             per_subplot_kw = {
1954                 tuple(k): v for k, v in per_subplot_kw.items()
1955             }
1956 
1957         per_subplot_kw = self._norm_per_subplot_kw(per_subplot_kw)
1958 
1959         # Only accept strict bools to allow a possible future API expansion.
1960         _api.check_isinstance(bool, sharex=sharex, sharey=sharey)
1961 
1962         def _make_array(inp):
1963             """
1964             Convert input into 2D array
1965 
1966             We need to have this internal function rather than
1967             ``np.asarray(..., dtype=object)`` so that a list of lists
1968             of lists does not get converted to an array of dimension > 2.
1969 
1970             Returns
1971             -------
1972             2D object array
1973             """
1974             r0, *rest = inp
1975             if isinstance(r0, str):
1976                 raise ValueError('List mosaic specification must be 2D')
1977             for j, r in enumerate(rest, start=1):
1978                 if isinstance(r, str):
1979                     raise ValueError('List mosaic specification must be 2D')
1980                 if len(r0) != len(r):
1981                     raise ValueError(
1982                         "All of the rows must be the same length, however "
1983                         f"the first row ({r0!r}) has length {len(r0)} "
1984                         f"and row {j} ({r!r}) has length {len(r)}."
1985                     )
1986             out = np.zeros((len(inp), len(r0)), dtype=object)
1987             for j, r in enumerate(inp):
1988                 for k, v in enumerate(r):
1989                     out[j, k] = v
1990             return out
1991 
1992         def _identify_keys_and_nested(mosaic):
1993             """
1994             Given a 2D object array, identify unique IDs and nested mosaics
1995 
1996             Parameters
1997             ----------
1998             mosaic : 2D object array
1999 
2000             Returns
2001             -------
2002             unique_ids : tuple
2003                 The unique non-sub mosaic entries in this mosaic
2004             nested : dict[tuple[int, int], 2D object array]
2005             """
2006             # make sure we preserve the user supplied order
2007             unique_ids = cbook._OrderedSet()
2008             nested = {}
2009             for j, row in enumerate(mosaic):
2010                 for k, v in enumerate(row):
2011                     if v == empty_sentinel:
2012                         continue
2013                     elif not cbook.is_scalar_or_string(v):
2014                         nested[(j, k)] = _make_array(v)
2015                     else:
2016                         unique_ids.add(v)
2017 
2018             return tuple(unique_ids), nested
2019 
2020         def _do_layout(gs, mosaic, unique_ids, nested):
2021             """
2022             Recursively do the mosaic.
2023 
2024             Parameters
2025             ----------
2026             gs : GridSpec
2027             mosaic : 2D object array
2028                 The input converted to a 2D array for this level.
2029             unique_ids : tuple
2030                 The identified scalar labels at this level of nesting.
2031             nested : dict[tuple[int, int]], 2D object array
2032                 The identified nested mosaics, if any.
2033 
2034             Returns
2035             -------
2036             dict[label, Axes]
2037                 A flat dict of all of the Axes created.
2038             """
2039             output = dict()
2040 
2041             # we need to merge together the Axes at this level and the axes
2042             # in the (recursively) nested sub-mosaics so that we can add
2043             # them to the figure in the "natural" order if you were to
2044             # ravel in c-order all of the Axes that will be created
2045             #
2046             # This will stash the upper left index of each object (axes or
2047             # nested mosaic) at this level
2048             this_level = dict()
2049 
2050             # go through the unique keys,
2051             for name in unique_ids:
2052                 # sort out where each axes starts/ends
2053                 indx = np.argwhere(mosaic == name)
2054                 start_row, start_col = np.min(indx, axis=0)
2055                 end_row, end_col = np.max(indx, axis=0) + 1
2056                 # and construct the slice object
2057                 slc = (slice(start_row, end_row), slice(start_col, end_col))
2058                 # some light error checking
2059                 if (mosaic[slc] != name).any():
2060                     raise ValueError(
2061                         f"While trying to layout\n{mosaic!r}\n"
2062                         f"we found that the label {name!r} specifies a "
2063                         "non-rectangular or non-contiguous area.")
2064                 # and stash this slice for later
2065                 this_level[(start_row, start_col)] = (name, slc, 'axes')
2066 
2067             # do the same thing for the nested mosaics (simpler because these
2068             # cannot be spans yet!)
2069             for (j, k), nested_mosaic in nested.items():
2070                 this_level[(j, k)] = (None, nested_mosaic, 'nested')
2071 
2072             # now go through the things in this level and add them
2073             # in order left-to-right top-to-bottom
2074             for key in sorted(this_level):
2075                 name, arg, method = this_level[key]
2076                 # we are doing some hokey function dispatch here based
2077                 # on the 'method' string stashed above to sort out if this
2078                 # element is an Axes or a nested mosaic.
2079                 if method == 'axes':
2080                     slc = arg
2081                     # add a single axes
2082                     if name in output:
2083                         raise ValueError(f"There are duplicate keys {name} "
2084                                          f"in the layout\n{mosaic!r}")
2085                     ax = self.add_subplot(
2086                         gs[slc], **{
2087                             'label': str(name),
2088                             **subplot_kw,
2089                             **per_subplot_kw.get(name, {})
2090                         }
2091                     )
2092                     output[name] = ax
2093                 elif method == 'nested':
2094                     nested_mosaic = arg
2095                     j, k = key
2096                     # recursively add the nested mosaic
2097                     rows, cols = nested_mosaic.shape
2098                     nested_output = _do_layout(
2099                         gs[j, k].subgridspec(rows, cols),
2100                         nested_mosaic,
2101                         *_identify_keys_and_nested(nested_mosaic)
2102                     )
2103                     overlap = set(output) & set(nested_output)
2104                     if overlap:
2105                         raise ValueError(
2106                             f"There are duplicate keys {overlap} "
2107                             f"between the outer layout\n{mosaic!r}\n"
2108                             f"and the nested layout\n{nested_mosaic}"
2109                         )
2110                     output.update(nested_output)
2111                 else:
2112                     raise RuntimeError("This should never happen")
2113             return output
2114 
2115         mosaic = _make_array(mosaic)
2116         rows, cols = mosaic.shape
2117         gs = self.add_gridspec(rows, cols, **gridspec_kw)
2118         ret = _do_layout(gs, mosaic, *_identify_keys_and_nested(mosaic))
2119         ax0 = next(iter(ret.values()))
2120         for ax in ret.values():
2121             if sharex:
2122                 ax.sharex(ax0)
2123                 ax._label_outer_xaxis(check_patch=True)
2124             if sharey:
2125                 ax.sharey(ax0)
2126                 ax._label_outer_yaxis(check_patch=True)
2127         if extra := set(per_subplot_kw) - set(ret):
2128             raise ValueError(
2129                 f"The keys {extra} are in *per_subplot_kw* "
2130                 "but not in the mosaic."
2131             )
2132         return ret

2604             - 'compressed' will also use `~.ConstrainedLayoutEngine`, but with

2621             like padding and margin sizes.  Only used if *layout* is a string.

2634         elif layout == 'constrained':

2636         elif layout == 'compressed':

3349         with ExitStack() as stack:

3351                 def _recursively_make_subfig_transparent(exit_stack, subfig):

3353                         subfig.patch._cm_set(
3354                             facecolor="none", edgecolor="none"))
3355                     for ax in subfig.axes:
3356                         exit_stack.enter_context(
3357                             ax.patch._cm_set(
3358                                 facecolor="none", edgecolor="none"))
3359                     for sub_subfig in subfig.subfigs:
3360                         _recursively_make_subfig_transparent(

3401         *mouse_add*, *mouse_pop* and *mouse_stop*.

235     def get_datalim(self, transData):
236         # Calculate the data limits and return them as a `.Bbox`.
237         #
238         # This operation depends on the transforms for the data in the
239         # collection and whether the collection has offsets:
240         #
241         # 1. offsets = None, transform child of transData: use the paths for
242         # the automatic limits (i.e. for LineCollection in streamline).
243         # 2. offsets != None: offset_transform is child of transData:
244         #
245         #    a. transform is child of transData: use the path + offset for
246         #       limits (i.e for bar).
247         #    b. transform is not a child of transData: just use the offsets
248         #       for the limits (i.e. for scatter)
249         #
250         # 3. otherwise return a null Bbox.
251 
252         transform = self.get_transform()
253         offset_trf = self.get_offset_transform()
254         if not (isinstance(offset_trf, transforms.IdentityTransform)
255                 or offset_trf.contains_branch(transData)):
256             # if the offsets are in some coords other than data,
257             # then don't use them for autoscaling.
258             return transforms.Bbox.null()
259 
260         paths = self.get_paths()
261         if not len(paths):
262             # No paths to transform
263             return transforms.Bbox.null()
264 
265         if not transform.is_affine:
266             paths = [transform.transform_path_non_affine(p) for p in paths]
267             # Don't convert transform to transform.get_affine() here because
268             # we may have transform.contains_branch(transData) but not
269             # transforms.get_affine().contains_branch(transData).  But later,
270             # be careful to only apply the affine part that remains.
271 
272         offsets = self.get_offsets()
273 
274         if any(transform.contains_branch_seperately(transData)):
275             # collections that are just in data units (like quiver)
276             # can properly have the axes limits set by their shape +
277             # offset.  LineCollections that have no offsets can
278             # also use this algorithm (like streamplot).
279             if isinstance(offsets, np.ma.MaskedArray):
280                 offsets = offsets.filled(np.nan)
281                 # get_path_collection_extents handles nan but not masked arrays
282             return mpath.get_path_collection_extents(
283                 transform.get_affine() - transData, paths,
284                 self.get_transforms(),
285                 offset_trf.transform_non_affine(offsets),
286                 offset_trf.get_affine().frozen())
287 
288         # NOTE: None is the default case where no offsets were passed in
289         if self._offsets is not None:
290             # this is for collections that have their paths (shapes)
291             # in physical, axes-relative, or figure-relative units
292             # (i.e. like scatter). We can't uniquely set limits based on
293             # those shapes, so we just set the limits based on their
294             # location.
295             offsets = (offset_trf - transData).transform(offsets)
296             # note A-B means A B^{-1}
297             offsets = np.ma.masked_invalid(offsets)
298             if not offsets.mask.all():
299                 bbox = transforms.Bbox.null()
300                 bbox.update_from_data_xy(offsets)
301                 return bbox
302         return transforms.Bbox.null()
303 
304     def get_window_extent(self, renderer=None):
305         # TODO: check to ensure that this does not fail for
306         # cases other than scatter plot legend
307         return self.get_datalim(transforms.IdentityTransform())

309     def _prepare_points(self):
310         # Helper for drawing and hit testing.
311 
312         transform = self.get_transform()
313         offset_trf = self.get_offset_transform()
314         offsets = self.get_offsets()
315         paths = self.get_paths()
316 
317         if self.have_units():
318             paths = []
319             for path in self.get_paths():
320                 vertices = path.vertices
321                 xs, ys = vertices[:, 0], vertices[:, 1]
322                 xs = self.convert_xunits(xs)
323                 ys = self.convert_yunits(ys)
324                 paths.append(mpath.Path(np.column_stack([xs, ys]), path.codes))
325             xs = self.convert_xunits(offsets[:, 0])
326             ys = self.convert_yunits(offsets[:, 1])
327             offsets = np.ma.column_stack([xs, ys])
328 
329         if not transform.is_affine:
330             paths = [transform.transform_path_non_affine(path)
331                      for path in paths]
332             transform = transform.get_affine()
333         if not offset_trf.is_affine:
334             offsets = offset_trf.transform_non_affine(offsets)
335             # This might have changed an ndarray into a masked array.
336             offset_trf = offset_trf.get_affine()
337 
338         if isinstance(offsets, np.ma.MaskedArray):
339             offsets = offsets.filled(np.nan)
340             # Changing from a masked array to nan-filled ndarray
341             # is probably most efficient at this point.
342 
343         return transform, offset_trf, offsets, paths
344 
345     @artist.allow_rasterization
346     def draw(self, renderer):
347         if not self.get_visible():
348             return
349         renderer.open_group(self.__class__.__name__, self.get_gid())
350 
351         self.update_scalarmappable()
352 
353         transform, offset_trf, offsets, paths = self._prepare_points()
354 
355         gc = renderer.new_gc()
356         self._set_gc_clip(gc)
357         gc.set_snap(self.get_snap())
358 
359         if self._hatch:
360             gc.set_hatch(self._hatch)
361             gc.set_hatch_color(self._hatch_color)
362 
363         if self.get_sketch_params() is not None:
364             gc.set_sketch_params(*self.get_sketch_params())
365 
366         if self.get_path_effects():
367             from matplotlib.patheffects import PathEffectRenderer
368             renderer = PathEffectRenderer(self.get_path_effects(), renderer)
369 
370         # If the collection is made up of a single shape/color/stroke,
371         # it can be rendered once and blitted multiple times, using
372         # `draw_markers` rather than `draw_path_collection`.  This is
373         # *much* faster for Agg, and results in smaller file sizes in
374         # PDF/SVG/PS.
375 
376         trans = self.get_transforms()
377         facecolors = self.get_facecolor()
378         edgecolors = self.get_edgecolor()
379         do_single_path_optimization = False
380         if (len(paths) == 1 and len(trans) <= 1 and
381                 len(facecolors) == 1 and len(edgecolors) == 1 and
382                 len(self._linewidths) == 1 and
383                 all(ls[1] is None for ls in self._linestyles) and
384                 len(self._antialiaseds) == 1 and len(self._urls) == 1 and
385                 self.get_hatch() is None):
386             if len(trans):
387                 combined_transform = transforms.Affine2D(trans[0]) + transform
388             else:
389                 combined_transform = transform
390             extents = paths[0].get_extents(combined_transform)
391             if (extents.width < self.figure.bbox.width
392                     and extents.height < self.figure.bbox.height):
393                 do_single_path_optimization = True
394 
395         if self._joinstyle:
396             gc.set_joinstyle(self._joinstyle)
397 
398         if self._capstyle:
399             gc.set_capstyle(self._capstyle)
400 
401         if do_single_path_optimization:
402             gc.set_foreground(tuple(edgecolors[0]))
403             gc.set_linewidth(self._linewidths[0])
404             gc.set_dashes(*self._linestyles[0])
405             gc.set_antialiased(self._antialiaseds[0])
406             gc.set_url(self._urls[0])
407             renderer.draw_markers(
408                 gc, paths[0], combined_transform.frozen(),
409                 mpath.Path(offsets), offset_trf, tuple(facecolors[0]))
410         else:
411             if self._gapcolor is not None:
412                 # First draw paths within the gaps.
413                 ipaths, ilinestyles = self._get_inverse_paths_linestyles()
414                 renderer.draw_path_collection(
415                     gc, transform.frozen(), ipaths,
416                     self.get_transforms(), offsets, offset_trf,
417                     [mcolors.to_rgba("none")], self._gapcolor,
418                     self._linewidths, ilinestyles,
419                     self._antialiaseds, self._urls,
420                     "screen")
421 
422             renderer.draw_path_collection(
423                 gc, transform.frozen(), paths,
424                 self.get_transforms(), offsets, offset_trf,
425                 self.get_facecolor(), self.get_edgecolor(),
426                 self._linewidths, self._linestyles,
427                 self._antialiaseds, self._urls,
428                 "screen")  # offset_position, kept for backcompat.
429 
430         gc.restore()
431         renderer.close_group(self.__class__.__name__)
432         self.stale = False
433

451     def contains(self, mouseevent):
452         """
453         Test whether the mouse event occurred in the collection.
454 
455         Returns ``bool, dict(ind=itemlist)``, where every item in itemlist
456         contains the event.
457         """
458         if self._different_canvas(mouseevent) or not self.get_visible():
459             return False, {}
460         pickradius = (
461             float(self._picker)
462             if isinstance(self._picker, Number) and
463                self._picker is not True  # the bool, not just nonzero or 1
464             else self._pickradius)
465         if self.axes:
466             self.axes._unstale_viewLim()
467         transform, offset_trf, offsets, paths = self._prepare_points()
468         # Tests if the point is contained on one of the polygons formed
469         # by the control points of each of the paths. A point is considered
470         # "on" a path if it would lie within a stroke of width 2*pickradius
471         # following the path. If pickradius <= 0, then we instead simply check
472         # if the point is *inside* of the path instead.
473         ind = _path.point_in_path_collection(
474             mouseevent.x, mouseevent.y, pickradius,
475             transform.frozen(), paths, self.get_transforms(),
476             offsets, offset_trf, pickradius <= 0)
477         return len(ind) > 0, dict(ind=ind)
478

596         ===========================   =================
597         ``'-'`` or ``'solid'``        solid line
598         ``'--'`` or  ``'dashed'``     dashed line
599         ``'-.'`` or  ``'dashdot'``    dash-dotted line
600         ``':'`` or ``'dotted'``       dotted line
601         ===========================   =================
602 
603         Alternatively a dash tuple of the following form can be provided::
604 
605             (offset, onoffseq),

607         where ``onoffseq`` is an even length tuple of on and off ink in points.

610         ----------

613             ':', '', (offset, on-off-seq)}. See `.Line2D.set_linestyle` for a
614             complete description.

616         try:
617             dashes = [mlines._get_dash_pattern(ls)]
618         except ValueError:
619             try:
620                 dashes = [mlines._get_dash_pattern(x) for x in ls]
621             except ValueError as err:
622                 emsg = f'Do not know how to convert {ls!r} to dashes'

626         self._us_linestyles = dashes

629         self._linewidths, self._linestyles = self._bcast_lwls(
630             self._us_lw, self._us_linestyles)

660     @staticmethod
661     def _bcast_lwls(linewidths, dashes):
662         """
663         Internal helper function to broadcast + scale ls/lw
664 
665         In the collection drawing code, the linewidth and linestyle are cycled
666         through as circular buffers (via ``v[i % len(v)]``).  Thus, if we are
667         going to scale the dash pattern at set time (not draw time) we need to
668         do the broadcasting now and expand both lists to be the same length.
669 
670         Parameters
671         ----------
672         linewidths : list
673             line widths of collection
674         dashes : list
675             dash specification (offset, (dash pattern tuple))
676 
677         Returns
678         -------
679         linewidths, dashes : list
680             Will be the same length, dashes are scaled by paired linewidth
681         """
682         if mpl.rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']:
683             return linewidths, dashes
684         # make sure they are the same length so we can zip them
685         if len(dashes) != len(linewidths):
686             l_dashes = len(dashes)
687             l_lw = len(linewidths)
688             gcd = math.gcd(l_dashes, l_lw)
689             dashes = list(dashes) * (l_lw // gcd)
690             linewidths = list(linewidths) * (l_dashes // gcd)
691 
692         # scale the dash patterns
693         dashes = [mlines._scale_dashes(o, d, lw)
694                   for (o, d), lw in zip(dashes, linewidths)]
695 
696         return linewidths, dashes

846         # the first time it is called.

850         self._edge_is_mapped = False

861         mapped = self._face_is_mapped or self._edge_is_mapped
862         changed = (edge0 is None or face0 is None
863                    or self._edge_is_mapped != edge0
864                    or self._face_is_mapped != face0)

867     def update_scalarmappable(self):

870 
871         Assign colors to edges and faces based on the array and/or
872         colors that were directly set, as appropriate.

889                         'in which a row and/or column of the data '

1012     def legend_elements(self, prop="colors", num="auto",
1013                         fmt=None, func=lambda x: x, **kwargs):
1014         """
1015         Create legend handles and labels for a PathCollection.
1016 
1017         Each legend handle is a `.Line2D` representing the Path that was drawn,
1018         and each label is a string what each Path represents.
1019 
1020         This is useful for obtaining a legend for a `~.Axes.scatter` plot;
1021         e.g.::
1022 
1023             scatter = plt.scatter([1, 2, 3],  [4, 5, 6],  c=[7, 2, 3])
1024             plt.legend(*scatter.legend_elements())
1025 
1026         creates three legend elements, one for each color with the numerical
1027         values passed to *c* as the labels.
1028 
1029         Also see the :ref:`automatedlegendcreation` example.
1030 
1031         Parameters
1032         ----------
1033         prop : {"colors", "sizes"}, default: "colors"
1034             If "colors", the legend handles will show the different colors of
1035             the collection. If "sizes", the legend will show the different
1036             sizes. To set both, use *kwargs* to directly edit the `.Line2D`
1037             properties.
1038         num : int, None, "auto" (default), array-like, or `~.ticker.Locator`
1039             Target number of elements to create.
1040             If None, use all unique elements of the mappable array. If an
1041             integer, target to use *num* elements in the normed range.
1042             If *"auto"*, try to determine which option better suits the nature
1043             of the data.
1044             The number of created elements may slightly deviate from *num* due
1045             to a `~.ticker.Locator` being used to find useful locations.
1046             If a list or array, use exactly those elements for the legend.
1047             Finally, a `~.ticker.Locator` can be provided.
1048         fmt : str, `~matplotlib.ticker.Formatter`, or None (default)
1049             The format or formatter to use for the labels. If a string must be
1050             a valid input for a `.StrMethodFormatter`. If None (the default),
1051             use a `.ScalarFormatter`.
1052         func : function, default: ``lambda x: x``
1053             Function to calculate the labels.  Often the size (or color)
1054             argument to `~.Axes.scatter` will have been pre-processed by the
1055             user using a function ``s = f(x)`` to make the markers visible;
1056             e.g. ``size = np.log10(x)``.  Providing the inverse of this
1057             function here allows that pre-processing to be inverted, so that
1058             the legend labels have the correct values; e.g. ``func = lambda
1059             x: 10**x``.
1060         **kwargs
1061             Allowed keyword arguments are *color* and *size*. E.g. it may be
1062             useful to set the color of the markers if *prop="sizes"* is used;
1063             similarly to set the size of the markers if *prop="colors"* is
1064             used. Any further parameters are passed onto the `.Line2D`
1065             instance. This may be useful to e.g. specify a different
1066             *markeredgecolor* or *alpha* for the legend handles.
1067 
1068         Returns
1069         -------
1070         handles : list of `.Line2D`
1071             Visual representation of each element of the legend.
1072         labels : list of str
1073             The string labels for elements of the legend.
1074         """
1075         handles = []
1076         labels = []
1077         hasarray = self.get_array() is not None
1078         if fmt is None:
1079             fmt = mpl.ticker.ScalarFormatter(useOffset=False, useMathText=True)
1080         elif isinstance(fmt, str):
1081             fmt = mpl.ticker.StrMethodFormatter(fmt)
1082         fmt.create_dummy_axis()
1083 
1084         if prop == "colors":
1085             if not hasarray:
1086                 warnings.warn("Collection without array used. Make sure to "
1087                               "specify the values to be colormapped via the "
1088                               "`c` argument.")
1089                 return handles, labels
1090             u = np.unique(self.get_array())
1091             size = kwargs.pop("size", mpl.rcParams["lines.markersize"])
1092         elif prop == "sizes":
1093             u = np.unique(self.get_sizes())
1094             color = kwargs.pop("color", "k")
1095         else:
1096             raise ValueError("Valid values for `prop` are 'colors' or "
1097                              f"'sizes'. You supplied '{prop}' instead.")
1098 
1099         fu = func(u)
1100         fmt.axis.set_view_interval(fu.min(), fu.max())
1101         fmt.axis.set_data_interval(fu.min(), fu.max())
1102         if num == "auto":
1103             num = 9
1104             if len(u) <= num:
1105                 num = None
1106         if num is None:
1107             values = u
1108             label_values = func(values)
1109         else:
1110             if prop == "colors":
1111                 arr = self.get_array()
1112             elif prop == "sizes":
1113                 arr = self.get_sizes()
1114             if isinstance(num, mpl.ticker.Locator):
1115                 loc = num
1116             elif np.iterable(num):
1117                 loc = mpl.ticker.FixedLocator(num)
1118             else:
1119                 num = int(num)
1120                 loc = mpl.ticker.MaxNLocator(nbins=num, min_n_ticks=num-1,
1121                                              steps=[1, 2, 2.5, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10])
1122             label_values = loc.tick_values(func(arr).min(), func(arr).max())
1123             cond = ((label_values >= func(arr).min()) &
1124                     (label_values <= func(arr).max()))
1125             label_values = label_values[cond]
1126             yarr = np.linspace(arr.min(), arr.max(), 256)
1127             xarr = func(yarr)
1128             ix = np.argsort(xarr)
1129             values = np.interp(label_values, xarr[ix], yarr[ix])
1130 
1131         kw = {"markeredgewidth": self.get_linewidths()[0],
1132               "alpha": self.get_alpha(),
1133               **kwargs}
1134 
1135         for val, lab in zip(values, label_values):
1136             if prop == "colors":
1137                 color = self.cmap(self.norm(val))
1138             elif prop == "sizes":
1139                 size = np.sqrt(val)
1140                 if np.isclose(size, 0.0):
1141                     continue
1142             h = mlines.Line2D([0], [0], ls="", color=color, ms=size,
1143                               marker=self.get_paths()[0], **kw)
1144             handles.append(h)
1145             if hasattr(fmt, "set_locs"):
1146                 fmt.set_locs(label_values)
1147             l = fmt(lab)
1148             labels.append(l)
1149 
1150         return handles, labels
1151

1154 
1155     def __init__(self, verts, sizes=None, *, closed=True, **kwargs):
1156         """
1157         Parameters
1158         ----------
1159         verts : list of array-like
1160             The sequence of polygons [*verts0*, *verts1*, ...] where each
1161             element *verts_i* defines the vertices of polygon *i* as a 2D
1162             array-like of shape (M, 2).
1163         sizes : array-like, default: None
1164             Squared scaling factors for the polygons. The coordinates of each
1165             polygon *verts_i* are multiplied by the square-root of the
1166             corresponding entry in *sizes* (i.e., *sizes* specify the scaling
1167             of areas). The scaling is applied before the Artist master
1168             transform.
1169         closed : bool, default: True
1170             Whether the polygon should be closed by adding a CLOSEPOLY
1171             connection at the end.
1172         **kwargs
1173             Forwarded to `.Collection`.
1174         """
1175         super().__init__(**kwargs)
1176         self.set_sizes(sizes)
1177         self.set_verts(verts, closed)
1178         self.stale = True
1179 
1180     def set_verts(self, verts, closed=True):
1181         """
1182         Set the vertices of the polygons.
1183 
1184         Parameters
1185         ----------
1186         verts : list of array-like
1187             The sequence of polygons [*verts0*, *verts1*, ...] where each
1188             element *verts_i* defines the vertices of polygon *i* as a 2D
1189             array-like of shape (M, 2).
1190         closed : bool, default: True
1191             Whether the polygon should be closed by adding a CLOSEPOLY
1192             connection at the end.
1193         """
1194         self.stale = True
1195         if isinstance(verts, np.ma.MaskedArray):
1196             verts = verts.astype(float).filled(np.nan)
1197 
1198         # No need to do anything fancy if the path isn't closed.
1199         if not closed:
1200             self._paths = [mpath.Path(xy) for xy in verts]
1201             return
1202 
1203         # Fast path for arrays
1204         if isinstance(verts, np.ndarray) and len(verts.shape) == 3:
1205             verts_pad = np.concatenate((verts, verts[:, :1]), axis=1)
1206             # Creating the codes once is much faster than having Path do it
1207             # separately each time by passing closed=True.
1208             codes = np.empty(verts_pad.shape[1], dtype=mpath.Path.code_type)
1209             codes[:] = mpath.Path.LINETO
1210             codes[0] = mpath.Path.MOVETO
1211             codes[-1] = mpath.Path.CLOSEPOLY
1212             self._paths = [mpath.Path(xy, codes) for xy in verts_pad]
1213             return
1214 
1215         self._paths = []
1216         for xy in verts:
1217             if len(xy):
1218                 self._paths.append(mpath.Path._create_closed(xy))
1219             else:
1220                 self._paths.append(mpath.Path(xy))
1221 
1222     set_paths = set_verts
1223 
1224     def set_verts_and_codes(self, verts, codes):
1225         """Initialize vertices with path codes."""
1226         if len(verts) != len(codes):
1227             raise ValueError("'codes' must be a 1D list or array "
1228                              "with the same length of 'verts'")
1229         self._paths = [mpath.Path(xy, cds) if len(xy) else mpath.Path(xy)
1230                        for xy, cds in zip(verts, codes)]
1231         self.stale = True

1235     def span_where(cls, x, ymin, ymax, where, **kwargs):
1236         """
1237         Return a `.BrokenBarHCollection` that plots horizontal bars from
1238         over the regions in *x* where *where* is True.  The bars range
1239         on the y-axis from *ymin* to *ymax*

1241         *kwargs* are passed on to the collection.

1243         xranges = []

1248             xranges.append((xslice[0], xslice[-1] - xslice[0]))
1249         return BrokenBarHCollection(xranges, [ymin, ymax - ymin], **kwargs)

1355 class LineCollection(Collection):

1357     Represents a sequence of `.Line2D`\s that should be drawn together.
1358 
1359     This class extends `.Collection` to represent a sequence of
1360     `.Line2D`\s instead of just a sequence of `.Patch`\s.
1361     Just as in `.Collection`, each property of a *LineCollection* may be either
1362     a single value or a list of values. This list is then used cyclically for
1363     each element of the LineCollection, so the property of the ``i``\th element
1364     of the collection is::
1365 
1366       prop[i % len(prop)]
1367 
1368     The properties of each member of a *LineCollection* default to their values
1369     in :rc:`lines.*` instead of :rc:`patch.*`, and the property *colors* is
1370     added in place of *edgecolors*.
1371     """
1372 
1373     _edge_default = True

1375     def __init__(self, segments,  # Can be None.
1376                  *,
1377                  zorder=2,        # Collection.zorder is 1
1378                  **kwargs
1379                  ):
1380         """
1381         Parameters
1382         ----------
1383         segments : list of array-like
1384             A sequence of (*line0*, *line1*, *line2*), where::
1385 
1386                 linen = (x0, y0), (x1, y1), ... (xm, ym)
1387 
1388             or the equivalent numpy array with two columns. Each line
1389             can have a different number of segments.
1390         linewidths : float or list of float, default: :rc:`lines.linewidth`
1391             The width of each line in points.
1392         colors : color or list of color, default: :rc:`lines.color`
1393             A sequence of RGBA tuples (e.g., arbitrary color strings, etc, not
1394             allowed).
1395         antialiaseds : bool or list of bool, default: :rc:`lines.antialiased`
1396             Whether to use antialiasing for each line.
1397         zorder : float, default: 2
1398             zorder of the lines once drawn.
1399 
1400         facecolors : color or list of color, default: 'none'
1401             When setting *facecolors*, each line is interpreted as a boundary
1402             for an area, implicitly closing the path from the last point to the
1403             first point. The enclosed area is filled with *facecolor*.
1404             In order to manually specify what should count as the "interior" of
1405             each line, please use `.PathCollection` instead, where the
1406             "interior" can be specified by appropriate usage of
1407             `~.path.Path.CLOSEPOLY`.
1408 
1409         **kwargs
1410             Forwarded to `.Collection`.
1411         """
1412         # Unfortunately, mplot3d needs this explicit setting of 'facecolors'.
1413         kwargs.setdefault('facecolors', 'none')
1414         super().__init__(
1415             zorder=zorder,
1416             **kwargs)

1419     def set_segments(self, segments):
1420         if segments is None:
1421             return
1422 
1423         self._paths = [mpath.Path(seg) if isinstance(seg, np.ma.MaskedArray)
1424                        else mpath.Path(np.asarray(seg, float))
1425                        for seg in segments]

1433         Returns
1434         -------
1435         list
1436             List of segments in the LineCollection. Each list item contains an
1437             array of vertices.
1438         """
1439         segments = []
1440 
1441         for path in self._paths:
1442             vertices = [
1443                 vertex
1444                 for vertex, _
1445                 # Never simplify here, we want to get the data-space values
1446                 # back and there in no way to know the "right" simplification
1447                 # threshold so never try.
1448                 in path.iter_segments(simplify=False)
1449             ]
1450             vertices = np.asarray(vertices)

1496 
1497         .. note::
1498 
1499             Striped lines are created by drawing two interleaved dashed lines.
1500             There can be overlaps between those two, which may result in
1501             artifacts when using transparency.
1502 
1503             This functionality is experimental and may change.

1505         Parameters
1506         ----------
1507         gapcolor : color or list of colors or None
1508             The color with which to fill the gaps. If None, the gaps are
1509             unfilled.

1523     def _get_inverse_paths_linestyles(self):
1524         """
1525         Returns the path and pattern for the gaps in the non-solid lines.
1526 
1527         This path and pattern is the inverse of the path and pattern used to
1528         construct the non-solid lines. For solid lines, we set the inverse path
1529         to nans to prevent drawing an inverse line.
1530         """
1531         path_patterns = [
1532             (mpath.Path(np.full((1, 2), np.nan)), ls)
1533             if ls == (0, None) else
1534             (path, mlines._get_inverse_dash_pattern(*ls))
1535             for (path, ls) in
1536             zip(self._paths, itertools.cycle(self._linestyles))]
1537 
1538         return zip(*path_patterns)
