1286     @staticmethod
1287     def _in_lambda_or_comprehension_body(
1288         node: astroid.node_classes.NodeNG, frame: astroid.node_classes.NodeNG
1289     ) -> bool:
1290         """return True if node within a lambda/comprehension body (or similar) and thus should not have access to class attributes in frame"""
1291         child = node
1292         parent = node.parent
1293         while parent is not None:
1294             if parent is frame:
1295                 return False
1296             if isinstance(parent, astroid.Lambda) and child is not parent.args:
1297                 # Body of lambda should not have access to class attributes.
1298                 return True
1299             if (
1300                 isinstance(parent, astroid.node_classes.Comprehension)
1301                 and child is not parent.iter
1302             ):
1303                 # Only iter of list/set/dict/generator comprehension should have access.
1304                 return True
1305             if isinstance(parent, astroid.scoped_nodes.ComprehensionScope) and not (
1306                 parent.generators and child is parent.generators[0]
1307             ):
1308                 # Body of list/set/dict/generator comprehension should not have access to class attributes.
1309                 # Furthermore, only the first generator (if multiple) in comprehension should have access.
1310                 return True
1311             child = parent
1312             parent = parent.parent
1313         return False

1315     @staticmethod
1316     def _is_variable_violation(
1317         node,
1318         name,
1319         defnode,
1320         stmt,
1321         defstmt,
1322         frame,
1323         defframe,
1324         base_scope_type,
1325         recursive_klass,
1326     ):
1327         # pylint: disable=too-many-nested-blocks
1328         # node: Node to check for violation
1329         # name: name of node to check violation for
1330         # frame: Scope of statement of node
1331         # base_scope_type: local scope type
1332         maybee0601 = True
1333         annotation_return = False
1334         use_outer_definition = False
1335         if frame is not defframe:
1336             maybee0601 = _detect_global_scope(node, frame, defframe)
1337         elif defframe.parent is None:
1338             # we are at the module level, check the name is not
1339             # defined in builtins
1340             if name in defframe.scope_attrs or astroid.builtin_lookup(name)[1]:
1341                 maybee0601 = False
1342         else:
1343             # we are in a local scope, check the name is not
1344             # defined in global or builtin scope
1345             # skip this lookup if name is assigned later in function scope/lambda
1346             # Note: the node.frame() is not the same as the `frame` argument which is
1347             # equivalent to frame.statement().scope()
1348             forbid_lookup = (
1349                 isinstance(frame, astroid.FunctionDef)
1350                 or isinstance(node.frame(), astroid.Lambda)
1351             ) and _assigned_locally(node)
1352             if not forbid_lookup and defframe.root().lookup(name)[1]:
1353                 maybee0601 = False
1354                 use_outer_definition = stmt == defstmt and not isinstance(
1355                     defnode, astroid.node_classes.Comprehension
1356                 )
1357             # check if we have a nonlocal
1358             elif name in defframe.locals:
1359                 maybee0601 = not any(
1360                     isinstance(child, astroid.Nonlocal) and name in child.names
1361                     for child in defframe.get_children()
1362                 )
1363 
1364         if (
1365             base_scope_type == "lambda"
1366             and isinstance(frame, astroid.ClassDef)
1367             and name in frame.locals
1368         ):
1369 
1370             # This rule verifies that if the definition node of the
1371             # checked name is an Arguments node and if the name
1372             # is used a default value in the arguments defaults
1373             # and the actual definition of the variable label
1374             # is happening before the Arguments definition.
1375             #
1376             # bar = None
1377             # foo = lambda bar=bar: bar
1378             #
1379             # In this case, maybee0601 should be False, otherwise
1380             # it should be True.
1381             maybee0601 = not (
1382                 isinstance(defnode, astroid.Arguments)
1383                 and node in defnode.defaults
1384                 and frame.locals[name][0].fromlineno < defstmt.fromlineno
1385             )
1386         elif isinstance(defframe, astroid.ClassDef) and isinstance(
1387             frame, astroid.FunctionDef
1388         ):
1389             # Special rule for function return annotations,
1390             # which uses the same name as the class where
1391             # the function lives.
1392             if node is frame.returns and defframe.parent_of(frame.returns):
1393                 maybee0601 = annotation_return = True
1394 
1395             if (
1396                 maybee0601
1397                 and defframe.name in defframe.locals
1398                 and defframe.locals[name][0].lineno < frame.lineno
1399             ):
1400                 # Detect class assignments with the same
1401                 # name as the class. In this case, no warning
1402                 # should be raised.
1403                 maybee0601 = False
1404             if isinstance(node.parent, astroid.Arguments):
1405                 maybee0601 = stmt.fromlineno <= defstmt.fromlineno
1406         elif recursive_klass:
1407             maybee0601 = True
1408         else:
1409             maybee0601 = maybee0601 and stmt.fromlineno <= defstmt.fromlineno
1410             if maybee0601 and stmt.fromlineno == defstmt.fromlineno:
1411                 if (
1412                     isinstance(defframe, astroid.FunctionDef)
1413                     and frame is defframe
1414                     and defframe.parent_of(node)
1415                     and stmt is not defstmt
1416                 ):
1417                     # Single statement function, with the statement on the
1418                     # same line as the function definition
1419                     maybee0601 = False
1420                 elif (
1421                     isinstance(
1422                         defstmt,
1423                         (
1424                             astroid.Assign,
1425                             astroid.AnnAssign,
1426                             astroid.AugAssign,
1427                             astroid.Expr,
1428                         ),
1429                     )
1430                     and isinstance(defstmt.value, astroid.IfExp)
1431                     and frame is defframe
1432                     and defframe.parent_of(node)
1433                     and stmt is defstmt
1434                 ):
1435                     # Single statement if, with assingment expression on same
1436                     # line as assigment
1437                     # x = b if (b := True) else False
1438                     maybee0601 = False
1439                 elif (
1440                     isinstance(  # pylint: disable=too-many-boolean-expressions
1441                         defnode, astroid.NamedExpr
1442                     )
1443                     and frame is defframe
1444                     and defframe.parent_of(stmt)
1445                     and stmt is defstmt
1446                     and (
1447                         (
1448                             defnode.lineno == node.lineno
1449                             and defnode.col_offset < node.col_offset
1450                         )
1451                         or (defnode.lineno < node.lineno)
1452                         or (
1453                             # Issue in the `ast` module until py39
1454                             # Nodes in a multiline string have the same lineno
1455                             # Could be false-positive without check
1456                             not PY39_PLUS
1457                             and defnode.lineno == node.lineno
1458                             and isinstance(
1459                                 defstmt,
1460                                 (
1461                                     astroid.Assign,
1462                                     astroid.AnnAssign,
1463                                     astroid.AugAssign,
1464                                     astroid.Return,
1465                                 ),
1466                             )
1467                             and isinstance(defstmt.value, astroid.JoinedStr)
1468                         )
1469                     )
1470                 ):
1471                     # Expressions, with assignment expressions
1472                     # Use only after assignment
1473                     # b = (c := 2) and c
1474                     maybee0601 = False
1475 
1476             # Look for type checking definitions inside a type checking guard.
1477             if isinstance(defstmt, (astroid.Import, astroid.ImportFrom)):
1478                 defstmt_parent = defstmt.parent
1479 
1480                 if (
1481                     isinstance(defstmt_parent, astroid.If)
1482                     and defstmt_parent.test.as_string() in TYPING_TYPE_CHECKS_GUARDS
1483                 ):
1484                     # Exempt those definitions that are used inside the type checking
1485                     # guard or that are defined in both type checking guard branches.
1486                     used_in_branch = defstmt_parent.parent_of(node)
1487                     defined_in_or_else = False
1488 
1489                     for definition in defstmt_parent.orelse:
1490                         if isinstance(definition, astroid.Assign):
1491                             defined_in_or_else = any(
1492                                 target.name == name for target in definition.targets
1493                             )
1494                             if defined_in_or_else:
1495                                 break
1496 
1497                     if not used_in_branch and not defined_in_or_else:
1498                         maybee0601 = True
1499 
1500         return maybee0601, annotation_return, use_outer_definition
1501 
1502     def _ignore_class_scope(self, node):
1503         """
1504         Return True if the node is in a local class scope, as an assignment.
1505 
1506         :param node: Node considered
1507         :type node: astroid.Node
1508         :return: True if the node is in a local class scope, as an assignment. False otherwise.
1509         :rtype: bool
1510         """
1511         # Detect if we are in a local class scope, as an assignment.
1512         # For example, the following is fair game.
1513         #
1514         # class A:
1515         #    b = 1
1516         #    c = lambda b=b: b * b
1517         #
1518         # class B:
1519         #    tp = 1
1520         #    def func(self, arg: tp):
1521         #        ...
1522         # class C:
1523         #    tp = 2
1524         #    def func(self, arg=tp):
1525         #        ...
1526         # class C:
1527         #    class Tp:
1528         #        pass
1529         #    class D(Tp):
1530         #        ...
1531 
1532         name = node.name
1533         frame = node.statement().scope()
1534         in_annotation_or_default_or_decorator = self._defined_in_function_definition(
1535             node, frame
1536         )
1537         in_ancestor_list = utils.is_ancestor_name(frame, node)
1538         if in_annotation_or_default_or_decorator or in_ancestor_list:
1539             frame_locals = frame.parent.scope().locals
1540         else:
1541             frame_locals = frame.locals
1542         return not (
1543             (
1544                 isinstance(frame, astroid.ClassDef)
1545                 or in_annotation_or_default_or_decorator
1546             )
1547             and not self._in_lambda_or_comprehension_body(node, frame)
1548             and name in frame_locals
1549         )

1551     def _loopvar_name(self, node, name):
1552         # filter variables according to node's scope
1553         if not self.linter.is_message_enabled("undefined-loop-variable"):
1554             return
1555         astmts = [stmt for stmt in node.lookup(name)[1] if hasattr(stmt, "assign_type")]
1556         # If this variable usage exists inside a function definition
1557         # that exists in the same loop,
1558         # the usage is safe because the function will not be defined either if
1559         # the variable is not defined.
1560         scope = node.scope()
1561         if isinstance(scope, astroid.FunctionDef) and any(
1562             asmt.statement().parent_of(scope) for asmt in astmts
1563         ):
1564             return
1565 
1566         # filter variables according their respective scope test is_statement
1567         # and parent to avoid #74747. This is not a total fix, which would
1568         # introduce a mechanism similar to special attribute lookup in
1569         # modules. Also, in order to get correct inference in this case, the
1570         # scope lookup rules would need to be changed to return the initial
1571         # assignment (which does not exist in code per se) as well as any later
1572         # modifications.
1573         if (
1574             not astmts
1575             or (astmts[0].is_statement or astmts[0].parent)
1576             and astmts[0].statement().parent_of(node)
1577         ):
1578             _astmts = []
1579         else:
1580             _astmts = astmts[:1]
1581         for i, stmt in enumerate(astmts[1:]):
1582             if astmts[i].statement().parent_of(stmt) and not in_for_else_branch(
1583                 astmts[i].statement(), stmt
1584             ):
1585                 continue
1586             _astmts.append(stmt)
1587         astmts = _astmts
1588         if len(astmts) != 1:
1589             return
1590 
1591         assign = astmts[0].assign_type()
1592         if not (
1593             isinstance(
1594                 assign, (astroid.For, astroid.Comprehension, astroid.GeneratorExp)
1595             )
1596             and assign.statement() is not node.statement()
1597         ):
1598             return
1599 
1600         # For functions we can do more by inferring the length of the itered object
1601         if not isinstance(assign, astroid.For):
1602             self.add_message("undefined-loop-variable", args=name, node=node)
1603             return
1604 
1605         try:
1606             inferred = next(assign.iter.infer())
1607         except astroid.InferenceError:
1608             self.add_message("undefined-loop-variable", args=name, node=node)
1609         else:
1610             if (
1611                 isinstance(inferred, astroid.Instance)
1612                 and inferred.qname() == BUILTIN_RANGE
1613             ):
1614                 # Consider range() objects safe, even if they might not yield any results.
1615                 return
1616 
1617             # Consider sequences.
1618             sequences = (
1619                 astroid.List,
1620                 astroid.Tuple,
1621                 astroid.Dict,
1622                 astroid.Set,
1623                 astroid.objects.FrozenSet,
1624             )
1625             if not isinstance(inferred, sequences):
1626                 self.add_message("undefined-loop-variable", args=name, node=node)
1627                 return
1628 
1629             elements = getattr(inferred, "elts", getattr(inferred, "items", []))
1630             if not elements:
1631                 self.add_message("undefined-loop-variable", args=name, node=node)
1632 
1633     def _check_is_unused(self, name, node, stmt, global_names, nonlocal_names):
1634         # pylint: disable=too-many-branches
1635         # Ignore some special names specified by user configuration.
1636         if self._is_name_ignored(stmt, name):
1637             return
1638         # Ignore names that were added dynamically to the Function scope
1639         if (
1640             isinstance(node, astroid.FunctionDef)
1641             and name == "__class__"
1642             and len(node.locals["__class__"]) == 1
1643             and isinstance(node.locals["__class__"][0], astroid.ClassDef)
1644         ):
1645             return
1646 
1647         # Ignore names imported by the global statement.
1648         if isinstance(stmt, (astroid.Global, astroid.Import, astroid.ImportFrom)):
1649             # Detect imports, assigned to global statements.
1650             if global_names and _import_name_is_global(stmt, global_names):
1651                 return
1652 
1653         argnames = list(
1654             itertools.chain(node.argnames(), [arg.name for arg in node.args.kwonlyargs])
1655         )
1656         # Care about functions with unknown argument (builtins)
1657         if name in argnames:
1658             self._check_unused_arguments(name, node, stmt, argnames)
1659         else:
1660             if stmt.parent and isinstance(
1661                 stmt.parent, (astroid.Assign, astroid.AnnAssign)
1662             ):
1663                 if name in nonlocal_names:
1664                     return
1665 
1666             qname = asname = None
1667             if isinstance(stmt, (astroid.Import, astroid.ImportFrom)):
1668                 # Need the complete name, which we don't have in .locals.
1669                 if len(stmt.names) > 1:
1670                     import_names = next(
1671                         (names for names in stmt.names if name in names), None
1672                     )
1673                 else:
1674                     import_names = stmt.names[0]
1675                 if import_names:
1676                     qname, asname = import_names
1677                     name = asname or qname
1678 
1679             if _has_locals_call_after_node(stmt, node.scope()):
1680                 message_name = "possibly-unused-variable"
1681             else:
1682                 if isinstance(stmt, astroid.Import):
1683                     if asname is not None:
1684                         msg = f"{qname} imported as {asname}"
1685                     else:
1686                         msg = "import %s" % name
1687                     self.add_message("unused-import", args=msg, node=stmt)
1688                     return
1689                 if isinstance(stmt, astroid.ImportFrom):
1690                     if asname is not None:
1691                         msg = f"{qname} imported from {stmt.modname} as {asname}"
1692                     else:
1693                         msg = f"{name} imported from {stmt.modname}"
1694                     self.add_message("unused-import", args=msg, node=stmt)
1695                     return
1696                 message_name = "unused-variable"
1697 
1698             if isinstance(stmt, astroid.FunctionDef) and stmt.decorators:
1699                 return
1700 
1701             # Don't check function stubs created only for type information
1702             if utils.is_overload_stub(node):
1703                 return
1704 
1705             self.add_message(message_name, args=name, node=stmt)

1707     def _is_name_ignored(self, stmt, name):
1708         authorized_rgx = self.config.dummy_variables_rgx

1710             isinstance(stmt, astroid.AssignName)
1711             and isinstance(stmt.parent, astroid.Arguments)
1712             or isinstance(stmt, astroid.Arguments)
1713         ):
1714             regex = self.config.ignored_argument_names
1715         else:
1716             regex = authorized_rgx

1719     def _check_unused_arguments(self, name, node, stmt, argnames):
1720         is_method = node.is_method()
1721         klass = node.parent.frame()
1722         if is_method and isinstance(klass, astroid.ClassDef):
1723             confidence = (
1724                 INFERENCE if utils.has_known_bases(klass) else INFERENCE_FAILURE
1725             )
1726         else:
1727             confidence = HIGH
1728 
1729         if is_method:
1730             # Don't warn for the first argument of a (non static) method
1731             if node.type != "staticmethod" and name == argnames[0]:
1732                 return
1733             # Don't warn for argument of an overridden method
1734             overridden = overridden_method(klass, node.name)
1735             if overridden is not None and name in overridden.argnames():
1736                 return
1737             if node.name in utils.PYMETHODS and node.name not in (
1738                 "__init__",
1739                 "__new__",
1740             ):
1741                 return
1742         # Don't check callback arguments
1743         if any(
1744             node.name.startswith(cb) or node.name.endswith(cb)
1745             for cb in self.config.callbacks
1746         ):
1747             return
1748         # Don't check arguments of singledispatch.register function.
1749         if utils.is_registered_in_singledispatch_function(node):
1750             return
1751 
1752         # Don't check function stubs created only for type information
1753         if utils.is_overload_stub(node):
1754             return
1755 
1756         # Don't check protocol classes
1757         if utils.is_protocol_class(klass):
1758             return
1759 
1760         self.add_message("unused-argument", args=name, node=stmt, confidence=confidence)

1762     def _check_late_binding_closure(self, node, assignment_node):
1763         if not self.linter.is_message_enabled("cell-var-from-loop"):

1766         def _is_direct_lambda_call():

1768                 isinstance(node_scope.parent, astroid.Call)

1885     def _check_unpacking(self, inferred, node, targets):

1887         and unpacking non sequences.

1897             and isinstance(node.value, astroid.Name)

1900             # Variable-length argument, we can't determine the length.

1926     def _check_module_attrs(self, node, module, module_names):
1927         """check that module_names (list of string) are accessible through the
1928         given module
1929         if the latest access name corresponds to a module, return it
1930         """
1931         while module_names:
1932             name = module_names.pop(0)
1933             if name == "__dict__":
1934                 module = None
1935                 break
1936             try:
1937                 module = next(module.getattr(name)[0].infer())
1938                 if module is astroid.Uninferable:

The problem with this is, quite simply, that data storage has a designated spot. The `$HOME/.local/share/` folder. This is a part of the [XDG Base Directory Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html). A system that designates the folders for specific things like cached files (`$HOME/.cache/`), configuration files (`$HOME/.config/`), and data files (`$HOME/.local/share/`), among other things. The point is to keep user home directories clean and the user sane. This should be pretty easy to implement. Setting `min-similarity-lines` to `0` should stop pylint from checking duplicate code
### Current problem

Setting `min-similarity-lines` to `0` in the rcfile doesn't disable checking for duplicate code, it instead treats every line of code as duplicate and raises many errors.

### Desired solution

Setting `min-similarity-lines` to `0` should disable the duplicate code check.

It works that way in many other linters (like flake8). Setting a numerical value in flake8 to `0` (e.g. `max-line-length`) disables that check.

### Additional context

#214 requests being able to disable `R0801`, but it is still open

30 """a similarities / code duplication command line tool and pylint checker
31 
32 The algorithm is based on comparing the hash value of n successive lines of a file.
33 First the files are read and any line that doesn't fullfill requirement are removed (comments, docstrings...)
34 Those stripped lines are stored in the LineSet class which gives access to them.
35 Then each index of the stripped lines collection is associated with the hash of n successive entries of the stripped lines starting at the current index
36 (n is the minimum common lines option).
37 The common hashes between both linesets are then looked for. If there are matches, then the match indices in both linesets are stored and associated
38 with the corresponding couples (start line number/end line number) in both files.
39 This association is then postprocessed to handle the case of successive matches. For example if the minimum common lines setting is set to four, then
40 the hashes are computed with four lines. If one of match indices couple (12, 34) is the successor of another one (11, 33) then it means that there are
41 in fact five lines wich are common.

225 def hash_lineset(
226     lineset: "LineSet", min_common_lines: int = DEFAULT_MIN_SIMILARITY_LINE
227 ) -> Tuple[HashToIndex_T, IndexToLines_T]:
228     """
229     Return two dicts. The first associates the hash of successive stripped lines of a lineset
230     to the indices of the starting lines.
231     The second dict, associates the index of the starting line in the lineset's stripped lines to the
232     couple [start, end] lines number in the corresponding file.
233 
234     :param lineset: lineset object (i.e the lines in a file)
235     :param min_common_lines: number of successive lines that are used to compute the hash
236     :return: a dict linking hashes to corresponding start index and a dict that links this
237              index to the start and end lines in the file
238     """
239     hash2index = defaultdict(list)
240     index2lines = {}
241     # Comments, docstring and other specific patterns maybe excluded -> call to stripped_lines
242     # to get only what is desired
243     lines = tuple(x.text for x in lineset.stripped_lines)
244     # Need different iterators on same lines but each one is shifted 1 from the precedent
245     shifted_lines = [iter(lines[i:]) for i in range(min_common_lines)]
246 
247     for index_i, *succ_lines in enumerate(zip(*shifted_lines)):
248         start_linenumber = lineset.stripped_lines[index_i].line_number
249         try:
250             end_linenumber = lineset.stripped_lines[
251                 index_i + min_common_lines
252             ].line_number
253         except IndexError:
254             end_linenumber = lineset.stripped_lines[-1].line_number + 1
255 
256         index = Index(index_i)
257         index2lines[index] = SuccessiveLinesLimits(
258             start=LineNumber(start_linenumber), end=LineNumber(end_linenumber)
259         )
260 
261         l_c = LinesChunk(lineset.name, index, *succ_lines)
262         hash2index[l_c].append(index)
263 
264     return hash2index, index2lines

267 def remove_successives(all_couples: CplIndexToCplLines_T) -> None:
268     """
269     Removes all successive entries in the dictionary in argument
270 
271     :param all_couples: collection that has to be cleaned up from successives entries.
272                         The keys are couples of indices that mark the beginning of common entries
273                         in both linesets. The values have two parts. The first one is the couple
274                         of starting and ending line numbers of common successives lines in the first file.
275                         The second part is the same for the second file.
276 
277     For example consider the following dict:
278 
279     >>> all_couples
280     {(11, 34): ([5, 9], [27, 31]),
281      (23, 79): ([15, 19], [45, 49]),
282      (12, 35): ([6, 10], [28, 32])}
283 
284     There are two successives keys (11, 34) and (12, 35).
285     It means there are two consecutive similar chunks of lines in both files.
286     Thus remove last entry and update the last line numbers in the first entry
287 
288     >>> remove_successives(all_couples)
289     >>> all_couples
290     {(11, 34): ([5, 10], [27, 32]),
291      (23, 79): ([15, 19], [45, 49])}
292     """
293     couple: LineSetStartCouple
294     for couple in tuple(all_couples.keys()):
295         to_remove = []
296         test = couple.increment(Index(1))
297         while test in all_couples:
298             all_couples[couple].first_file.end = all_couples[test].first_file.end
299             all_couples[couple].second_file.end = all_couples[test].second_file.end
300             all_couples[couple].effective_cmn_lines_nb += 1
301             to_remove.append(test)
302             test = test.increment(Index(1))
303 
304         for target in to_remove:
305             try:
306                 all_couples.pop(target)
307             except KeyError:
308                 pass

461     def _find_common(
462         self, lineset1: "LineSet", lineset2: "LineSet"
463     ) -> Generator[Commonality, None, None]:
464         """
465         Find similarities in the two given linesets.
466 
467         This the core of the algorithm.
468         The idea is to compute the hashes of a minimal number of successive lines of each lineset and then compare the hashes.
469         Every match of such comparison is stored in a dict that links the couple of starting indices in both linesets to
470         the couple of corresponding starting and ending lines in both files.
471         Last regroups all successive couples in a bigger one. It allows to take into account common chunk of lines that have more
472         than the minimal number of successive lines required.
473         """
474         hash_to_index_1: HashToIndex_T
475         hash_to_index_2: HashToIndex_T
476         index_to_lines_1: IndexToLines_T
477         index_to_lines_2: IndexToLines_T
478         hash_to_index_1, index_to_lines_1 = hash_lineset(lineset1, self.min_lines)
479         hash_to_index_2, index_to_lines_2 = hash_lineset(lineset2, self.min_lines)
480 
481         hash_1: FrozenSet[LinesChunk] = frozenset(hash_to_index_1.keys())
482         hash_2: FrozenSet[LinesChunk] = frozenset(hash_to_index_2.keys())
483 
484         common_hashes: Iterable[LinesChunk] = sorted(
485             hash_1 & hash_2, key=lambda m: hash_to_index_1[m][0]
486         )
487 
488         # all_couples is a dict that links the couple of indices in both linesets that mark the beginning of
489         # successive common lines, to the corresponding starting and ending number lines in both files
490         all_couples: CplIndexToCplLines_T = {}
491 
492         for c_hash in sorted(common_hashes, key=operator.attrgetter("_index")):
493             for indices_in_linesets in itertools.product(
494                 hash_to_index_1[c_hash], hash_to_index_2[c_hash]
495             ):
496                 index_1 = indices_in_linesets[0]
497                 index_2 = indices_in_linesets[1]
498                 all_couples[
499                     LineSetStartCouple(index_1, index_2)
500                 ] = CplSuccessiveLinesLimits(
501                     copy.copy(index_to_lines_1[index_1]),
502                     copy.copy(index_to_lines_2[index_2]),
503                     effective_cmn_lines_nb=self.min_lines,
504                 )
505 
506         remove_successives(all_couples)
507 
508         for cml_stripped_l, cmn_l in all_couples.items():
509             start_index_1 = cml_stripped_l.fst_lineset_index
510             start_index_2 = cml_stripped_l.snd_lineset_index
511             nb_common_lines = cmn_l.effective_cmn_lines_nb
512 
513             com = Commonality(
514                 cmn_lines_nb=nb_common_lines,
515                 fst_lset=lineset1,
516                 fst_file_start=cmn_l.first_file.start,
517                 fst_file_end=cmn_l.first_file.end,
518                 snd_lset=lineset2,
519                 snd_file_start=cmn_l.second_file.start,
520                 snd_file_end=cmn_l.second_file.end,
521             )
522 
523             eff_cmn_nb = filter_noncode_lines(
524                 lineset1, start_index_1, lineset2, start_index_2, nb_common_lines
525             )
526 
527             if eff_cmn_nb > self.min_lines:
528                 yield com

532         product
533         """

535             for lineset2 in self.linesets[idx + 1 :]:
536                 yield from self._find_common(lineset, lineset2)

81 What differentiates Pylint?
82 ---------------------------
83 
84 Pylint is not trusting your typing and is inferring the actual value of nodes (for a
85 start because there was no typing when pylint started off) using its internal code
86 representation (astroid). If your code is ``import logging as argparse``, Pylint
87 can check and know that ``argparse.error(...)`` is in fact a logging call and not an
88 argparse call. This makes pylint slower, but it also lets pylint find more issues if
89 your code is not fully typed.

91     [inference] is the killer feature that keeps us using [pylint] in our project despite how painfully slow it is.

102 
103 Pylint isn't smarter than you: it may warn you about things that you have
104 conscientiously done or check for some things that you don't care about.

106 it's best to start with the ``--errors-only`` flag, then disable
107 convention and refactor messages with ``--disable=C,R`` and progressively
108 re-evaluate and re-enable messages as your priorities evolve.

111 own checks (for example, for internal libraries or an internal rule). Pylint also has an
112 ecosystem of existing plugins for popular frameworks and third-party libraries.

122 def _regexp_paths_csv_transfomer(value: str) -> Sequence[Pattern[str]]:
123     """Transforms a comma separated list of regular expressions paths."""
124     patterns: list[Pattern[str]] = []

112 def get_module_and_frameid(node: nodes.NodeNG) -> tuple[str, str]:
113     """Return the module name and the frame id in the module."""
114     frame = node.frame()
115     module, obj = "", []
116     while frame:
117         if isinstance(frame, Module):
118             module = frame.name

120             obj.append(getattr(frame, "name", "<lambda>"))
121         try:
122             frame = frame.parent.frame()

179 def register_plugins(linter: PyLinter, directory: str) -> None:
180     """Load all module and package in the given directory, looking for a
181     'register' function in each one, used to register pylint checkers.
182     """
183     imported = {}
184     for filename in os.listdir(directory):
185         base, extension = os.path.splitext(filename)
186         if base in imported or base == "__pycache__":
187             continue
188         if (
189             extension in PY_EXTS
190             and base != "__init__"
191             or (
192                 not extension
193                 and os.path.isdir(os.path.join(directory, base))
194                 and not filename.startswith(".")
195             )
196         ):
197             try:
198                 module = modutils.load_module_from_file(
199                     os.path.join(directory, filename)
200                 )
201             except ValueError:
202                 # empty module name (usually Emacs auto-save files)
203                 continue
204             except ImportError as exc:
205                 print(f"Problem importing module {filename}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
206             else:
207                 if hasattr(module, "register"):
208                     module.register(linter)

212 def _splitstrip(string: str, sep: str = ",") -> list[str]:
213     """Return a list of stripped string by splitting the string given as
214     argument on `sep` (',' by default), empty strings are discarded.
215 
216     >>> _splitstrip('a, b, c   ,  4,,')
217     ['a', 'b', 'c', '4']
218     >>> _splitstrip('a')
219     ['a']
220     >>> _splitstrip('a,\nb,\nc,')
221     ['a', 'b', 'c']
222 
223     :type string: str or unicode
224     :param string: a csv line
225 
226     :type sep: str or unicode
227     :param sep: field separator, default to the comma (',')
228 
229     :rtype: str or unicode
230     :return: the unquoted string (or the input string if it wasn't quoted)
231     """
232     return [word.strip() for word in string.split(sep) if word.strip()]
233

235 def _unquote(string: str) -> str:
236     """Remove optional quotes (simple or double) from the string.
237 
238     :param string: an optionally quoted string
239     :return: the unquoted string (or the input string if it wasn't quoted)
240     """
241     if not string:
242         return string
243     if string[0] in "\"'":
244         string = string[1:]
245     if string[-1] in "\"'":
246         string = string[:-1]
247     return string

304 def _ini_format(stream: TextIO, options: list[tuple[str, OptionDict, Any]]) -> None:
305     """Format options using the INI format."""
306     warnings.warn(
307         "_ini_format has been deprecated. It will be removed in pylint 3.0.",
308         DeprecationWarning,
309         stacklevel=2,
310     )
311     for optname, optdict, value in options:
312         # Skip deprecated option
313         if "kwargs" in optdict:
314             assert isinstance(optdict["kwargs"], dict)
315             if "new_names" in optdict["kwargs"]:
316                 continue

caplog.get_records and caplog.clear conflict
# Description

`caplog.get_records()` gets decoupled from actual caplog records when `caplog.clear()` is called. As a result, after `caplog.clear()` is called, `caplog.get_records()` is frozen: it does not get cleared, nor does it get new records.

During test set up it is [set to the same list](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/28e8c8582ea947704655a3c3f2d57184831336fd/src/_pytest/logging.py#L699) as `caplog.records`, but the latter gets [replaced rather than cleared](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/28e8c8582ea947704655a3c3f2d57184831336fd/src/_pytest/logging.py#L345) in `caplog.clear()`, which diverges the two objects.

# Reproductive example
```python
import logging

def test(caplog) -> None:
    def verify_consistency() -> None:
        assert caplog.get_records("call") == caplog.records

    logging.warning("test")
    verify_consistency()
    caplog.clear()
    verify_consistency()  # fails: assert [<LogRecord: ...y, 8, "test">] == []
```

Consider MRO when obtaining marks for classes
When using pytest markers in two baseclasses `Foo` and `Bar`, inheriting from both of those baseclasses will lose the markers of one of those classes. This behavior is present in pytest 3-6, and I think it may as well have been intended. I am still filing it as a bug because I am not sure if this edge case was ever explicitly considered.

If it is widely understood that all markers are part of a single attribute, I guess you could say that this is just expected behavior as per MRO. However, I'd argue that it would be more intuitive to attempt to merge marker values into one, possibly deduplicating marker names by MRO.

```python
import itertools
import pytest

class BaseMeta(type):
    @property
    def pytestmark(self):
        return (
            getattr(self, "_pytestmark", []) +
            list(itertools.chain.from_iterable(getattr(x, "_pytestmark", []) for x in self.__mro__))
        )

    @pytestmark.setter
    def pytestmark(self, value):
        self._pytestmark = value


class Base(object):
    # Without this metaclass, foo and bar markers override each other, and test_dings
    # will only have one marker
    # With the metaclass, test_dings will have both
    __metaclass__ = BaseMeta

@pytest.mark.foo
class Foo(Base):
    pass


@pytest.mark.bar
class Bar(Base):
    pass

class TestDings(Foo, Bar):
    def test_dings(self):
        # This test should have both markers, foo and bar.
        # In practice markers are resolved using MRO (so foo wins), unless the
        # metaclass is applied
        pass
```

I'd expect `foo` and `bar` to be markers for `test_dings`, but this only actually is the case with this metaclass.

Please note that the repro case is Python 2/3 compatible excluding how metaclasses are added to `Base` (this needs to be taken care of to repro this issue on pytest 6)

154         argvalues: Iterable[Union["ParameterSet", Sequence[object], object]],
155         func,
156         config: Config,

158     ) -> Tuple[Sequence[str], List["ParameterSet"]]:
159         argnames, force_tuple = cls._parse_parametrize_args(argnames, argvalues)
160         parameters = cls._parse_parametrize_parameters(argvalues, force_tuple)
161         del argvalues

163         if parameters:
164             # Check all parameter sets have the correct number of values.
165             for param in parameters:
166                 if len(param.values) != len(argnames):
167                     msg = (
168                         '{nodeid}: in "parametrize" the number of names ({names_len}):\n'
169                         "  {names}\n"
170                         "must be equal to the number of values ({values_len}):\n"
171                         "  {values}"
172                     )
173                     fail(
174                         msg.format(
175                             nodeid=nodeid,
176                             values=param.values,
177                             names=argnames,
178                             names_len=len(argnames),
179                             values_len=len(param.values),
180                         ),
181                         pytrace=False,
182                     )

184             # Empty parameter set (likely computed at runtime): create a single
185             # parameter set with NOTSET values, with the "empty parameter set" mark applied to it.
186             mark = get_empty_parameterset_mark(config, argnames, func)
187             parameters.append(
188                 ParameterSet(values=(NOTSET,) * len(argnames), marks=[mark], id=None)

266     """A decorator for applying a mark on test functions and classes.
267 
268     ``MarkDecorators`` are created with ``pytest.mark``::
269 
270         mark1 = pytest.mark.NAME              # Simple MarkDecorator
271         mark2 = pytest.mark.NAME(name1=value) # Parametrized MarkDecorator
272 
273     and can then be applied as decorators to test functions::
274 
275         @mark2
276         def test_function():
277             pass

279     When a ``MarkDecorator`` is called, it does the following:
280 
281     1. If called with a single class as its only positional argument and no
282        additional keyword arguments, it attaches the mark to the class so it
283        gets applied automatically to all test cases found in that class.
284 
285     2. If called with a single function as its only positional argument and
286        no additional keyword arguments, it attaches the mark to the function,
287        containing all the arguments already stored internally in the
288        ``MarkDecorator``.
289 
290     3. When called in any other case, it returns a new ``MarkDecorator``
291        instance with the original ``MarkDecorator``'s content updated with
292        the arguments passed to this call.
293 
294     Note: The rules above prevent a ``MarkDecorator`` from storing only a
295     single function or class reference as its positional argument with no
296     additional keyword or positional arguments. You can work around this by
297     using `with_args()`.

304         check_ispytest(_ispytest)

331         if the sole argument is a callable/class.

108     """

110         raise UsageError("{} must be a directory, given: {}".format(optname, path))

185 def _prepareconfig(args=None, plugins=None):

189     elif isinstance(args, py.path.local):
190         args = [str(args)]
191     elif not isinstance(args, (tuple, list)):
192         msg = "`args` parameter expected to be a list or tuple of strings, got: {!r} (type: {})"
193         raise TypeError(msg.format(args, type(args)))
194 
195     config = get_config(args, plugins)
196     pluginmanager = config.pluginmanager

198         if plugins:
199             for plugin in plugins:
200                 if isinstance(plugin, str):
201                     pluginmanager.consider_pluginarg(plugin)
202                 else:
203                     pluginmanager.register(plugin)

207             _issue_warning_captured(warning, hook=config.hook, stacklevel=4)
208         return pluginmanager.hook.pytest_cmdline_parse(
209             pluginmanager=pluginmanager, args=args
210         )
211     except BaseException:
212         config._ensure_unconfigure()

229 class PytestPluginManager(PluginManager):
230     """
231     Overwrites :py:class:`pluggy.PluginManager <pluggy.PluginManager>` to add pytest-specific
232     functionality:
233 
234     * loading plugins from the command line, ``PYTEST_PLUGINS`` env variable and
235       ``pytest_plugins`` global variables found in plugins being loaded;
236     * ``conftest.py`` loading during start-up;
237     """
238 
239     def __init__(self):
240         super().__init__("pytest")
241         self._conftest_plugins = set()
242 
243         # state related to local conftest plugins
244         self._dirpath2confmods = {}
245         self._conftestpath2mod = {}
246         self._confcutdir = None
247         self._noconftest = False
248         self._duplicatepaths = set()
249 
250         self.add_hookspecs(_pytest.hookspec)
251         self.register(self)
252         if os.environ.get("PYTEST_DEBUG"):
253             err = sys.stderr
254             encoding = getattr(err, "encoding", "utf8")
255             try:
256                 err = py.io.dupfile(err, encoding=encoding)
257             except Exception:
258                 pass
259             self.trace.root.setwriter(err.write)
260             self.enable_tracing()
261 
262         # Config._consider_importhook will set a real object if required.
263         self.rewrite_hook = _pytest.assertion.DummyRewriteHook()
264         # Used to know when we are importing conftests after the pytest_configure stage
265         self._configured = False
266 
267     def parse_hookimpl_opts(self, plugin, name):
268         # pytest hooks are always prefixed with pytest_
269         # so we avoid accessing possibly non-readable attributes
270         # (see issue #1073)
271         if not name.startswith("pytest_"):
272             return
273         # ignore names which can not be hooks
274         if name == "pytest_plugins":
275             return
276 
277         method = getattr(plugin, name)
278         opts = super().parse_hookimpl_opts(plugin, name)
279 
280         # consider only actual functions for hooks (#3775)
281         if not inspect.isroutine(method):
282             return
283 
284         # collect unmarked hooks as long as they have the `pytest_' prefix
285         if opts is None and name.startswith("pytest_"):
286             opts = {}
287         if opts is not None:
288             # TODO: DeprecationWarning, people should use hookimpl
289             # https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4562
290             known_marks = {m.name for m in getattr(method, "pytestmark", [])}
291 
292             for name in ("tryfirst", "trylast", "optionalhook", "hookwrapper"):
293                 opts.setdefault(name, hasattr(method, name) or name in known_marks)
294         return opts
295 
296     def parse_hookspec_opts(self, module_or_class, name):
297         opts = super().parse_hookspec_opts(module_or_class, name)
298         if opts is None:
299             method = getattr(module_or_class, name)
300 
301             if name.startswith("pytest_"):
302                 # todo: deprecate hookspec hacks
303                 # https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4562
304                 known_marks = {m.name for m in getattr(method, "pytestmark", [])}
305                 opts = {
306                     "firstresult": hasattr(method, "firstresult")
307                     or "firstresult" in known_marks,
308                     "historic": hasattr(method, "historic")
309                     or "historic" in known_marks,
310                 }
311         return opts

313     def register(self, plugin, name=None):
314         if name in _pytest.deprecated.DEPRECATED_EXTERNAL_PLUGINS:
315             warnings.warn(
316                 PytestConfigWarning(
317                     "{} plugin has been merged into the core, "
318                     "please remove it from your requirements.".format(
319                         name.replace("_", "-")
320                     )
321                 )
322             )
323             return
324         ret = super().register(plugin, name)
325         if ret:
326             self.hook.pytest_plugin_registered.call_historic(
327                 kwargs=dict(plugin=plugin, manager=self)
328             )
329 
330             if isinstance(plugin, types.ModuleType):
331                 self.consider_module(plugin)
332         return ret

358     # internal API for local conftest plugin handling

360     def _set_initial_conftests(self, namespace):
361         """ load initial conftest files given a preparsed "namespace".
362             As conftest files may add their own command line options
363             which have arguments ('--my-opt somepath') we might get some
364             false positives.  All builtin and 3rd party plugins will have
365             been loaded, however, so common options will not confuse our logic
366             here.
367         """
368         current = py.path.local()
369         self._confcutdir = (
370             unique_path(current.join(namespace.confcutdir, abs=True))
371             if namespace.confcutdir
372             else None
373         )
374         self._noconftest = namespace.noconftest
375         self._using_pyargs = namespace.pyargs
376         testpaths = namespace.file_or_dir
377         foundanchor = False
378         for path in testpaths:
379             path = str(path)
380             # remove node-id syntax
381             i = path.find("::")
382             if i != -1:
383                 path = path[:i]
384             anchor = current.join(path, abs=1)
385             if exists(anchor):  # we found some file object
386                 self._try_load_conftest(anchor)
387                 foundanchor = True
388         if not foundanchor:
389             self._try_load_conftest(current)

391     def _try_load_conftest(self, anchor):
392         self._getconftestmodules(anchor)
393         # let's also consider test* subdirs
394         if anchor.check(dir=1):
395             for x in anchor.listdir("test*"):
396                 if x.check(dir=1):
397                     self._getconftestmodules(x)
398 
399     @lru_cache(maxsize=128)
400     def _getconftestmodules(self, path):
401         if self._noconftest:
402             return []
403 
404         if path.isfile():
405             directory = path.dirpath()
406         else:
407             directory = path
408 
409         directory = unique_path(directory)
410 
411         # XXX these days we may rather want to use config.rootdir
412         # and allow users to opt into looking into the rootdir parent
413         # directories instead of requiring to specify confcutdir
414         clist = []
415         for parent in directory.parts():
416             if self._confcutdir and self._confcutdir.relto(parent):
417                 continue
418             conftestpath = parent.join("conftest.py")
419             if conftestpath.isfile():
420                 mod = self._importconftest(conftestpath)
421                 clist.append(mod)
422         self._dirpath2confmods[directory] = clist
423         return clist

425     def _rget_with_confmod(self, name, path):
426         modules = self._getconftestmodules(path)
427         for mod in reversed(modules):
428             try:
429                 return mod, getattr(mod, name)
430             except AttributeError:
431                 continue
432         raise KeyError(name)

434     def _importconftest(self, conftestpath):
435         # Use realpath to avoid loading the same conftest twice
436         # with build systems that create build directories containing
437         # symlinks to actual files.
438         conftestpath = unique_path(conftestpath)
439         try:
440             return self._conftestpath2mod[conftestpath]
441         except KeyError:
442             pkgpath = conftestpath.pypkgpath()
443             if pkgpath is None:
444                 _ensure_removed_sysmodule(conftestpath.purebasename)
445             try:
446                 mod = conftestpath.pyimport()
447                 if (
448                     hasattr(mod, "pytest_plugins")
449                     and self._configured
450                     and not self._using_pyargs
451                 ):
452                     _fail_on_non_top_pytest_plugins(conftestpath, self._confcutdir)
453             except Exception:
454                 raise ConftestImportFailure(conftestpath, sys.exc_info())
455 
456             self._conftest_plugins.add(mod)
457             self._conftestpath2mod[conftestpath] = mod
458             dirpath = conftestpath.dirpath()
459             if dirpath in self._dirpath2confmods:
460                 for path, mods in self._dirpath2confmods.items():
461                     if path and path.relto(dirpath) or path == dirpath:
462                         assert mod not in mods
463                         mods.append(mod)
464             self.trace("loaded conftestmodule %r" % (mod))
465             self.consider_conftest(mod)
466             return mod

473     def consider_preparse(self, args):
474         i = 0
475         n = len(args)
476         while i < n:
477             opt = args[i]
478             i += 1
479             if isinstance(opt, str):
480                 if opt == "-p":
481                     try:
482                         parg = args[i]
483                     except IndexError:
484                         return
485                     i += 1
486                 elif opt.startswith("-p"):
487                     parg = opt[2:]
488                 else:
489                     continue
490                 self.consider_pluginarg(parg)

492     def consider_pluginarg(self, arg):
493         if arg.startswith("no:"):
494             name = arg[3:]
495             if name in essential_plugins:
496                 raise UsageError("plugin %s cannot be disabled" % name)
497 
498             # PR #4304 : remove stepwise if cacheprovider is blocked
499             if name == "cacheprovider":
500                 self.set_blocked("stepwise")
501                 self.set_blocked("pytest_stepwise")
502 
503             self.set_blocked(name)
504             if not name.startswith("pytest_"):
505                 self.set_blocked("pytest_" + name)
506         else:
507             name = arg
508             # Unblock the plugin.  None indicates that it has been blocked.
509             # There is no interface with pluggy for this.
510             if self._name2plugin.get(name, -1) is None:
511                 del self._name2plugin[name]
512             if not name.startswith("pytest_"):
513                 if self._name2plugin.get("pytest_" + name, -1) is None:
514                     del self._name2plugin["pytest_" + name]
515             self.import_plugin(arg, consider_entry_points=True)
516 
517     def consider_conftest(self, conftestmodule):
518         self.register(conftestmodule, name=conftestmodule.__file__)

520     def consider_env(self):
521         self._import_plugin_specs(os.environ.get("PYTEST_PLUGINS"))
522 
523     def consider_module(self, mod):
524         self._import_plugin_specs(getattr(mod, "pytest_plugins", []))
525 
526     def _import_plugin_specs(self, spec):
527         plugins = _get_plugin_specs_as_list(spec)
528         for import_spec in plugins:
529             self.import_plugin(import_spec)

531     def import_plugin(self, modname, consider_entry_points=False):
532         """
533         Imports a plugin with ``modname``. If ``consider_entry_points`` is True, entry point
534         names are also considered to find a plugin.
535         """
536         # most often modname refers to builtin modules, e.g. "pytester",
537         # "terminal" or "capture".  Those plugins are registered under their
538         # basename for historic purposes but must be imported with the
539         # _pytest prefix.
540         assert isinstance(modname, str), (
541             "module name as text required, got %r" % modname
542         )
543         modname = str(modname)
544         if self.is_blocked(modname) or self.get_plugin(modname) is not None:
545             return
546 
547         importspec = "_pytest." + modname if modname in builtin_plugins else modname
548         self.rewrite_hook.mark_rewrite(importspec)
549 
550         if consider_entry_points:
551             loaded = self.load_setuptools_entrypoints("pytest11", name=modname)
552             if loaded:
553                 return
554 
555         try:
556             __import__(importspec)
557         except ImportError as e:
558             new_exc_message = 'Error importing plugin "{}": {}'.format(
559                 modname, str(e.args[0])
560             )
561             new_exc = ImportError(new_exc_message)
562             tb = sys.exc_info()[2]
563 
564             raise new_exc.with_traceback(tb)
565 
566         except Skipped as e:
567             from _pytest.warnings import _issue_warning_captured
568 
569             _issue_warning_captured(
570                 PytestConfigWarning("skipped plugin {!r}: {}".format(modname, e.msg)),
571                 self.hook,
572                 stacklevel=1,
573             )
574         else:
575             mod = sys.modules[importspec]
576             self.register(mod, modname)
577

579 def _get_plugin_specs_as_list(specs):
580     """
581     Parses a list of "plugin specs" and returns a list of plugin names.
582 
583     Plugin specs can be given as a list of strings separated by "," or already as a list/tuple in
584     which case it is returned as a list. Specs can also be `None` in which case an
585     empty list is returned.
586     """
587     if specs is not None and not isinstance(specs, types.ModuleType):
588         if isinstance(specs, str):
589             specs = specs.split(",") if specs else []
590         if not isinstance(specs, (list, tuple)):
591             raise UsageError(
592                 "Plugin specs must be a ','-separated string or a "
593                 "list/tuple of strings for plugin names. Given: %r" % specs
594             )
595         return list(specs)
596     return []

614 def _iter_rewritable_modules(package_files):
615     for fn in package_files:
616         is_simple_module = "/" not in fn and fn.endswith(".py")
617         is_package = fn.count("/") == 1 and fn.endswith("__init__.py")
618         if is_simple_module:
619             module_name, _ = os.path.splitext(fn)
620             yield module_name
621         elif is_package:
622             package_name = os.path.dirname(fn)
623             yield package_name

626 class Config:
627     """
628     Access to configuration values, pluginmanager and plugin hooks.
629 
630     :ivar PytestPluginManager pluginmanager: the plugin manager handles plugin registration and hook invocation.
631 
632     :ivar argparse.Namespace option: access to command line option as attributes.
633 
634     :ivar InvocationParams invocation_params:
635 
636         Object containing the parameters regarding the ``pytest.main``
637         invocation.
638 
639         Contains the following read-only attributes:
640 
641         * ``args``: list of command-line arguments as passed to ``pytest.main()``.
642         * ``plugins``: list of extra plugins, might be None.
643         * ``dir``: directory where ``pytest.main()`` was invoked from.
644     """
645 
646     @attr.s(frozen=True)
647     class InvocationParams:
648         """Holds parameters passed during ``pytest.main()``
649 
650         .. note::
651 
652             Currently the environment variable PYTEST_ADDOPTS is also handled by
653             pytest implicitly, not being part of the invocation.
654 
655             Plugins accessing ``InvocationParams`` must be aware of that.
656         """
657 
658         args = attr.ib()
659         plugins = attr.ib()
660         dir = attr.ib()
661 
662     def __init__(self, pluginmanager, *, invocation_params=None):
663         from .argparsing import Parser, FILE_OR_DIR
664 
665         if invocation_params is None:
666             invocation_params = self.InvocationParams(
667                 args=(), plugins=None, dir=Path().resolve()
668             )
669 
670         self.option = argparse.Namespace()
671         self.invocation_params = invocation_params
672 
673         _a = FILE_OR_DIR
674         self._parser = Parser(
675             usage="%(prog)s [options] [{}] [{}] [...]".format(_a, _a),
676             processopt=self._processopt,
677         )
678         self.pluginmanager = pluginmanager
679         self.trace = self.pluginmanager.trace.root.get("config")
680         self.hook = self.pluginmanager.hook
681         self._inicache = {}
682         self._override_ini = ()
683         self._opt2dest = {}
684         self._cleanup = []
685         self.pluginmanager.register(self, "pytestconfig")
686         self._configured = False
687         self.hook.pytest_addoption.call_historic(kwargs=dict(parser=self._parser))
688 
689     @property
690     def invocation_dir(self):
691         """Backward compatibility"""
692         return py.path.local(str(self.invocation_params.dir))

694     def add_cleanup(self, func):
695         """ Add a function to be called when the config object gets out of
696         use (usually coninciding with pytest_unconfigure)."""
697         self._cleanup.append(func)

699     def _do_configure(self):
700         assert not self._configured
701         self._configured = True
702         with warnings.catch_warnings():
703             warnings.simplefilter("default")
704             self.hook.pytest_configure.call_historic(kwargs=dict(config=self))

706     def _ensure_unconfigure(self):
707         if self._configured:
708             self._configured = False
709             self.hook.pytest_unconfigure(config=self)
710             self.hook.pytest_configure._call_history = []

718     def pytest_cmdline_parse(self, pluginmanager, args):
719         try:
720             self.parse(args)
721         except UsageError:
722 
723             # Handle --version and --help here in a minimal fashion.
724             # This gets done via helpconfig normally, but its
725             # pytest_cmdline_main is not called in case of errors.
726             if getattr(self.option, "version", False) or "--version" in args:
727                 from _pytest.helpconfig import showversion
728 
729                 showversion(self)
730             elif (
731                 getattr(self.option, "help", False) or "--help" in args or "-h" in args
732             ):
733                 self._parser._getparser().print_help()
734                 sys.stdout.write(
735                     "\nNOTE: displaying only minimal help due to UsageError.\n\n"
736                 )
737 
738             raise

742     def notify_exception(self, excinfo, option=None):
743         if option and getattr(option, "fulltrace", False):
744             style = "long"
745         else:
746             style = "native"
747         excrepr = excinfo.getrepr(
748             funcargs=True, showlocals=getattr(option, "showlocals", False), style=style
749         )
750         res = self.hook.pytest_internalerror(excrepr=excrepr, excinfo=excinfo)
751         if not any(res):
752             for line in str(excrepr).split("\n"):
753                 sys.stderr.write("INTERNALERROR> %s\n" % line)
754                 sys.stderr.flush()

161 def create_cleanup_lock(p):
162     """crates a lock to prevent premature folder cleanup"""
163     lock_path = get_lock_path(p)
164     try:
165         fd = os.open(str(lock_path), os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o644)
166     except FileExistsError as e:
167         raise EnvironmentError("cannot create lockfile in {path}".format(path=p)) from e
168     else:
169         pid = os.getpid()
170         spid = str(pid).encode()
171         os.write(fd, spid)
172         os.close(fd)
173         if not lock_path.is_file():
174             raise EnvironmentError("lock path got renamed after successful creation")

300 def fnmatch_ex(pattern, path):
301     """FNMatcher port from py.path.common which works with PurePath() instances.
302 
303     The difference between this algorithm and PurePath.match() is that the latter matches "**" glob expressions
304     for each part of the path, while this algorithm uses the whole path instead.
305 
306     For example:
307         "tests/foo/bar/doc/test_foo.py" matches pattern "tests/**/doc/test*.py" with this algorithm, but not with
308         PurePath.match().
309 
310     This algorithm was ported to keep backward-compatibility with existing settings which assume paths match according
311     this logic.
312 
313     References:
314     * https://bugs.python.org/issue29249
315     * https://bugs.python.org/issue34731
316     """
317     path = PurePath(path)
318     iswin32 = sys.platform.startswith("win")
319 
320     if iswin32 and sep not in pattern and posix_sep in pattern:
321         # Running on Windows, the pattern has no Windows path separators,
322         # and the pattern has one or more Posix path separators. Replace
323         # the Posix path separators with the Windows path separator.
324         pattern = pattern.replace(posix_sep, sep)
325 
326     if sep not in pattern:
327         name = path.name
328     else:
329         name = str(path)
330         if path.is_absolute() and not os.path.isabs(pattern):
331             pattern = "*{}{}".format(os.sep, pattern)
332     return fnmatch.fnmatch(name, pattern)

398             definition, fixtureinfo, self.config, cls=cls, module=module

402             methods.append(module.pytest_generate_tests)

613     def _collectfile(self, path, handle_dupes=True):
614         assert (
615             path.isfile()
616         ), "{!r} is not a file (isdir={!r}, exists={!r}, islink={!r})".format(
617             path, path.isdir(), path.exists(), path.islink()
618         )
619         ihook = self.gethookproxy(path)
620         if not self.isinitpath(path):
621             if ihook.pytest_ignore_collect(path=path, config=self.config):
622                 return ()
623 
624         if handle_dupes:
625             keepduplicates = self.config.getoption("keepduplicates")
626             if not keepduplicates:
627                 duplicate_paths = self.config.pluginmanager._duplicatepaths
628                 if path in duplicate_paths:
629                     return ()
630                 else:
631                     duplicate_paths.add(path)
632 
633         if self.fspath == path:  # __init__.py
634             return [self]
635 
636         return ihook.pytest_collect_file(path=path, parent=self)

638     def isinitpath(self, path):
639         return path in self.session._initialpaths

641     def collect(self):
642         self._mount_obj_if_needed()
643         this_path = self.fspath.dirpath()
644         init_module = this_path.join("__init__.py")
645         if init_module.check(file=1) and path_matches_patterns(
646             init_module, self.config.getini("python_files")
647         ):
648             yield Module(init_module, self)
649         pkg_prefixes = set()
650         for path in this_path.visit(rec=self._recurse, bf=True, sort=True):
651             # We will visit our own __init__.py file, in which case we skip it.
652             is_file = path.isfile()
653             if is_file:
654                 if path.basename == "__init__.py" and path.dirpath() == this_path:
655                     continue
656 
657             parts_ = parts(path.strpath)
658             if any(
659                 pkg_prefix in parts_ and pkg_prefix.join("__init__.py") != path
660                 for pkg_prefix in pkg_prefixes
661             ):
662                 continue
663 
664             if is_file:
665                 yield from self._collectfile(path)
666             elif not path.isdir():
667                 # Broken symlink or invalid/missing file.
668                 continue
669             elif path.join("__init__.py").check(file=1):
670                 pkg_prefixes.add(path)

673 def _call_with_optional_argument(func, arg):
674     """Call the given function with the given argument if func accepts one argument, otherwise
675     calls func without arguments"""
676     arg_count = func.__code__.co_argcount
677     if inspect.ismethod(func):
678         arg_count -= 1
679     if arg_count:
680         func(arg)
681     else:
682         func()

896 class Metafunc(fixtures.FuncargnamesCompatAttr):
897     """
898     Metafunc objects are passed to the :func:`pytest_generate_tests <_pytest.hookspec.pytest_generate_tests>` hook.
899     They help to inspect a test function and to generate tests according to
900     test configuration or values specified in the class or module where a
901     test function is defined.
902     """
903 
904     def __init__(self, definition, fixtureinfo, config, cls=None, module=None):
905         assert (
906             isinstance(definition, FunctionDefinition)
907             or type(definition).__name__ == "DefinitionMock"
908         )
909         self.definition = definition
910 
911         #: access to the :class:`_pytest.config.Config` object for the test session
912         self.config = config
913 
914         #: the module object where the test function is defined in.
915         self.module = module
916 
917         #: underlying python test function
918         self.function = definition.obj
919 
920         #: set of fixture names required by the test function
921         self.fixturenames = fixtureinfo.names_closure
922 
923         #: class object where the test function is defined in or ``None``.
924         self.cls = cls
925 
926         self._calls = []
927         self._ids = set()
928         self._arg2fixturedefs = fixtureinfo.name2fixturedefs
929 
930     def parametrize(self, argnames, argvalues, indirect=False, ids=None, scope=None):
931         """ Add new invocations to the underlying test function using the list
932         of argvalues for the given argnames.  Parametrization is performed
933         during the collection phase.  If you need to setup expensive resources
934         see about setting indirect to do it rather at test setup time.
935 
936         :arg argnames: a comma-separated string denoting one or more argument
937                        names, or a list/tuple of argument strings.
938 
939         :arg argvalues: The list of argvalues determines how often a
940             test is invoked with different argument values.  If only one
941             argname was specified argvalues is a list of values.  If N
942             argnames were specified, argvalues must be a list of N-tuples,
943             where each tuple-element specifies a value for its respective
944             argname.
945 
946         :arg indirect: The list of argnames or boolean. A list of arguments'
947             names (subset of argnames). If True the list contains all names from
948             the argnames. Each argvalue corresponding to an argname in this list will
949             be passed as request.param to its respective argname fixture
950             function so that it can perform more expensive setups during the
951             setup phase of a test rather than at collection time.
952 
953         :arg ids: list of string ids, or a callable.
954             If strings, each is corresponding to the argvalues so that they are
955             part of the test id. If None is given as id of specific test, the
956             automatically generated id for that argument will be used.
957             If callable, it should take one argument (a single argvalue) and return
958             a string or return None. If None, the automatically generated id for that
959             argument will be used.
960             If no ids are provided they will be generated automatically from
961             the argvalues.
962 
963         :arg scope: if specified it denotes the scope of the parameters.
964             The scope is used for grouping tests by parameter instances.
965             It will also override any fixture-function defined scope, allowing
966             to set a dynamic scope using test context or configuration.
967         """
968         from _pytest.fixtures import scope2index
969         from _pytest.mark import ParameterSet
970 
971         argnames, parameters = ParameterSet._for_parametrize(
972             argnames,
973             argvalues,
974             self.function,
975             self.config,
976             function_definition=self.definition,
977         )
978         del argvalues
979 
980         if "request" in argnames:
981             fail(
982                 "'request' is a reserved name and cannot be used in @pytest.mark.parametrize",
983                 pytrace=False,
984             )
985 
986         if scope is None:
987             scope = _find_parametrized_scope(argnames, self._arg2fixturedefs, indirect)
988 
989         self._validate_if_using_arg_names(argnames, indirect)
990 
991         arg_values_types = self._resolve_arg_value_types(argnames, indirect)
992 
993         ids = self._resolve_arg_ids(argnames, ids, parameters, item=self.definition)
994 
995         scopenum = scope2index(
996             scope, descr="parametrize() call in {}".format(self.function.__name__)
997         )
998 
999         # create the new calls: if we are parametrize() multiple times (by applying the decorator
1000         # more than once) then we accumulate those calls generating the cartesian product
1001         # of all calls
1002         newcalls = []
1003         for callspec in self._calls or [CallSpec2(self)]:
1004             for param_index, (param_id, param_set) in enumerate(zip(ids, parameters)):
1005                 newcallspec = callspec.copy()
1006                 newcallspec.setmulti2(
1007                     arg_values_types,

199 @hookimpl(hookwrapper=True)
200 def pytest_pycollect_makeitem(collector, name, obj):
201     outcome = yield
202     res = outcome.get_result()
203     if res is not None:
204         return
205     # nothing was collected elsewhere, let's do it here
206     if safe_isclass(obj):
207         if collector.istestclass(obj, name):
208             outcome.force_result(Class(name, parent=collector))
209     elif collector.istestfunction(obj, name):
210         # mock seems to store unbound methods (issue473), normalize it
211         obj = getattr(obj, "__func__", obj)
212         # We need to try and unwrap the function if it's a functools.partial
213         # or a functools.wrapped.
214         # We mustn't if it's been wrapped with mock.patch (python 2 only)
215         if not (inspect.isfunction(obj) or inspect.isfunction(get_real_func(obj))):
216             filename, lineno = getfslineno(obj)
217             warnings.warn_explicit(
218                 message=PytestCollectionWarning(
219                     "cannot collect %r because it is not a function." % name
220                 ),
221                 category=None,
222                 filename=str(filename),
223                 lineno=lineno + 1,
224             )
225         elif getattr(obj, "__test__", True):
226             if is_generator(obj):
227                 res = Function(name, parent=collector)
228                 reason = "yield tests were removed in pytest 4.0 - {name} will be ignored".format(
229                     name=name
230                 )
231                 res.add_marker(MARK_GEN.xfail(run=False, reason=reason))
232                 res.warn(PytestCollectionWarning(reason))
233             else:
234                 res = list(collector._genfunctions(name, obj))
235             outcome.force_result(res)

248 class PyobjMixin(PyobjContext):
249     _ALLOW_MARKERS = True
250 
251     @property
252     def obj(self):
253         """Underlying Python object."""
254         obj = getattr(self, "_obj", None)
255         if obj is None:
256             self._obj = obj = self._getobj()
257             # XXX evil hack
258             # used to avoid Instance collector marker duplication
259             if self._ALLOW_MARKERS:
260                 self.own_markers.extend(get_unpacked_marks(self.obj))
261         return obj
262 
263     @obj.setter
264     def obj(self, value):
265         self._obj = value
266 
267     def _getobj(self):
268         """Gets the underlying Python object. May be overwritten by subclasses."""
269         return getattr(self.parent.obj, self.name)
270 
271     def getmodpath(self, stopatmodule=True, includemodule=False):
272         """ return python path relative to the containing module. """
273         chain = self.listchain()
274         chain.reverse()
275         parts = []
276         for node in chain:
277             if isinstance(node, Instance):
278                 continue
279             name = node.name
280             if isinstance(node, Module):
281                 name = os.path.splitext(name)[0]
282                 if stopatmodule:
283                     if includemodule:
284                         parts.append(name)
285                     break
286             parts.append(name)
287         parts.reverse()
288         s = ".".join(parts)
289         return s.replace(".[", "[")
290 
291     def reportinfo(self):
292         # XXX caching?
293         obj = self.obj
294         compat_co_firstlineno = getattr(obj, "compat_co_firstlineno", None)
295         if isinstance(compat_co_firstlineno, int):
296             # nose compatibility
297             fspath = sys.modules[obj.__module__].__file__
298             if fspath.endswith(".pyc"):
299                 fspath = fspath[:-1]
300             lineno = compat_co_firstlineno
301         else:
302             fspath, lineno = getfslineno(obj)
303         modpath = self.getmodpath()
304         assert isinstance(lineno, int)
305         return fspath, lineno, modpath
