308 class PyCollector(PyobjMixin, nodes.Collector):
309     def funcnamefilter(self, name):
310         return self._matches_prefix_or_glob_option("python_functions", name)
311 
312     def isnosetest(self, obj):
313         """ Look for the __test__ attribute, which is applied by the
314         @nose.tools.istest decorator
315         """
316         # We explicitly check for "is True" here to not mistakenly treat
317         # classes with a custom __getattr__ returning something truthy (like a
318         # function) as test classes.
319         return safe_getattr(obj, "__test__", False) is True
320 
321     def classnamefilter(self, name):
322         return self._matches_prefix_or_glob_option("python_classes", name)
323 
324     def istestfunction(self, obj, name):
325         if self.funcnamefilter(name) or self.isnosetest(obj):
326             if isinstance(obj, staticmethod):
327                 # static methods need to be unwrapped
328                 obj = safe_getattr(obj, "__func__", False)
329             return (
330                 safe_getattr(obj, "__call__", False)
331                 and fixtures.getfixturemarker(obj) is None
332             )
333         else:
334             return False
335 
336     def istestclass(self, obj, name):
337         return self.classnamefilter(name) or self.isnosetest(obj)
338 
339     def _matches_prefix_or_glob_option(self, option_name, name):
340         """
341         checks if the given name matches the prefix or glob-pattern defined
342         in ini configuration.
343         """
344         for option in self.config.getini(option_name):
345             if name.startswith(option):
346                 return True
347             # check that name looks like a glob-string before calling fnmatch
348             # because this is called for every name in each collected module,
349             # and fnmatch is somewhat expensive to call
350             elif ("*" in option or "?" in option or "[" in option) and fnmatch.fnmatch(
351                 name, option
352             ):
353                 return True
354         return False
355 
356     def collect(self):
357         if not getattr(self.obj, "__test__", True):
358             return []
359 
360         # NB. we avoid random getattrs and peek in the __dict__ instead
361         # (XXX originally introduced from a PyPy need, still true?)
362         dicts = [getattr(self.obj, "__dict__", {})]
363         for basecls in inspect.getmro(self.obj.__class__):
364             dicts.append(basecls.__dict__)
365         seen = {}
366         values = []
367         for dic in dicts:
368             for name, obj in list(dic.items()):
369                 if name in seen:
370                     continue
371                 seen[name] = True
372                 res = self._makeitem(name, obj)
373                 if res is None:
374                     continue
375                 if not isinstance(res, list):
376                     res = [res]
377                 values.extend(res)
378         values.sort(key=lambda item: item.reportinfo()[:2])
379         return values
380 
381     def _makeitem(self, name, obj):
382         # assert self.ihook.fspath == self.fspath, self
383         return self.ihook.pytest_pycollect_makeitem(collector=self, name=name, obj=obj)
384 
385     def _genfunctions(self, name, funcobj):
386         module = self.getparent(Module).obj
387         clscol = self.getparent(Class)
388         cls = clscol and clscol.obj or None
389         fm = self.session._fixturemanager
390 
391         definition = FunctionDefinition(name=name, parent=self, callobj=funcobj)
392         fixtureinfo = fm.getfixtureinfo(definition, funcobj, cls)
393 
394         metafunc = Metafunc(
395             definition, fixtureinfo, self.config, cls=cls, module=module
396         )
397         methods = []
398         if hasattr(module, "pytest_generate_tests"):
399             methods.append(module.pytest_generate_tests)
400         if hasattr(cls, "pytest_generate_tests"):
401             methods.append(cls().pytest_generate_tests)
402 
403         self.ihook.pytest_generate_tests.call_extra(methods, dict(metafunc=metafunc))
404 
405         if not metafunc._calls:
406             yield Function(name, parent=self, fixtureinfo=fixtureinfo)
407         else:
408             # add funcargs() as fixturedefs to fixtureinfo.arg2fixturedefs
409             fixtures.add_funcarg_pseudo_fixture_def(self, metafunc, fm)
410 
411             # add_funcarg_pseudo_fixture_def may have shadowed some fixtures
412             # with direct parametrization, so make sure we update what the
413             # function really needs.
414             fixtureinfo.prune_dependency_tree()
415 
416             for callspec in metafunc._calls:
417                 subname = "{}[{}]".format(name, callspec.id)
418                 yield Function(
419                     name=subname,
420                     parent=self,
421                     callspec=callspec,
422                     callobj=funcobj,
423                     fixtureinfo=fixtureinfo,
424                     keywords={callspec.id: True},
425                     originalname=name,
426                 )

441     def _inject_setup_module_fixture(self):
442         """Injects a hidden autouse, module scoped fixture into the collected module object
443         that invokes setUpModule/tearDownModule if either or both are available.
444 
445         Using a fixture to invoke this methods ensures we play nicely and unsurprisingly with
446         other fixtures (#517).
447         """
448         setup_module = _get_first_non_fixture_func(
449             self.obj, ("setUpModule", "setup_module")
450         )
451         teardown_module = _get_first_non_fixture_func(
452             self.obj, ("tearDownModule", "teardown_module")
453         )
454 
455         if setup_module is None and teardown_module is None:
456             return
457 
458         @fixtures.fixture(autouse=True, scope="module")
459         def xunit_setup_module_fixture(request):
460             if setup_module is not None:
461                 _call_with_optional_argument(setup_module, request.module)
462             yield
463             if teardown_module is not None:
464                 _call_with_optional_argument(teardown_module, request.module)
465 
466         self.obj.__pytest_setup_module = xunit_setup_module_fixture
467 
468     def _inject_setup_function_fixture(self):
469         """Injects a hidden autouse, function scoped fixture into the collected module object
470         that invokes setup_function/teardown_function if either or both are available.
471 
472         Using a fixture to invoke this methods ensures we play nicely and unsurprisingly with
473         other fixtures (#517).
474         """
475         setup_function = _get_first_non_fixture_func(self.obj, ("setup_function",))
476         teardown_function = _get_first_non_fixture_func(
477             self.obj, ("teardown_function",)
478         )
479         if setup_function is None and teardown_function is None:
480             return
481 
482         @fixtures.fixture(autouse=True, scope="function")
483         def xunit_setup_function_fixture(request):
484             if request.instance is not None:
485                 # in this case we are bound to an instance, so we need to let
486                 # setup_method handle this
487                 yield
488                 return
489             if setup_function is not None:
490                 _call_with_optional_argument(setup_function, request.function)
491             yield
492             if teardown_function is not None:
493                 _call_with_optional_argument(teardown_function, request.function)
494 
495         self.obj.__pytest_setup_function = xunit_setup_function_fixture

497     def _importtestmodule(self):
498         # we assume we are only called once per module
499         importmode = self.config.getoption("--import-mode")
500         try:
501             mod = self.fspath.pyimport(ensuresyspath=importmode)
502         except SyntaxError:
503             raise self.CollectError(
504                 _pytest._code.ExceptionInfo.from_current().getrepr(style="short")
505             )
506         except self.fspath.ImportMismatchError:
507             e = sys.exc_info()[1]
508             raise self.CollectError(
509                 "import file mismatch:\n"
510                 "imported module %r has this __file__ attribute:\n"
511                 "  %s\n"
512                 "which is not the same as the test file we want to collect:\n"
513                 "  %s\n"
514                 "HINT: remove __pycache__ / .pyc files and/or use a "
515                 "unique basename for your test file modules" % e.args
516             )
517         except ImportError:
518             from _pytest._code.code import ExceptionInfo
519 
520             exc_info = ExceptionInfo.from_current()
521             if self.config.getoption("verbose") < 2:
522                 exc_info.traceback = exc_info.traceback.filter(filter_traceback)
523             exc_repr = (
524                 exc_info.getrepr(style="short")
525                 if exc_info.traceback
526                 else exc_info.exconly()
527             )
528             formatted_tb = str(exc_repr)
529             raise self.CollectError(
530                 "ImportError while importing test module '{fspath}'.\n"
531                 "Hint: make sure your test modules/packages have valid Python names.\n"
532                 "Traceback:\n"
533                 "{traceback}".format(fspath=self.fspath, traceback=formatted_tb)
534             )
535         except _pytest.runner.Skipped as e:
536             if e.allow_module_level:
537                 raise
538             raise self.CollectError(
539                 "Using pytest.skip outside of a test is not allowed. "
540                 "To decorate a test function, use the @pytest.mark.skip "
541                 "or @pytest.mark.skipif decorators instead, and to skip a "
542                 "module use `pytestmark = pytest.mark.{skip,skipif}."
543             )
544         self.config.pluginmanager.consider_module(mod)
545         return mod

575     def _recurse(self, dirpath):
576         if dirpath.basename == "__pycache__":
577             return False
578         ihook = self.gethookproxy(dirpath.dirpath())
579         if ihook.pytest_ignore_collect(path=dirpath, config=self.config):
580             return
581         for pat in self._norecursepatterns:
582             if dirpath.check(fnmatch=pat):
583                 return False
584         ihook = self.gethookproxy(dirpath)
585         ihook.pytest_collect_directory(path=dirpath, parent=self)
586         return True

588     def gethookproxy(self, fspath):
589         # check if we have the common case of running
590         # hooks with all conftest.py filesall conftest.py
591         pm = self.config.pluginmanager
592         my_conftestmodules = pm._getconftestmodules(fspath)
593         remove_mods = pm._conftest_plugins.difference(my_conftestmodules)
594         if remove_mods:
595             # one or more conftests are not in use at this fspath
596             proxy = FSHookProxy(fspath, pm, remove_mods)
597         else:
598             # all plugins are active for this fspath

602     def _collectfile(self, path, handle_dupes=True):
603         assert (
604             path.isfile()
605         ), "{!r} is not a file (isdir={!r}, exists={!r}, islink={!r})".format(
606             path, path.isdir(), path.exists(), path.islink()
607         )
608         ihook = self.gethookproxy(path)
609         if not self.isinitpath(path):
610             if ihook.pytest_ignore_collect(path=path, config=self.config):
611                 return ()
612 
613         if handle_dupes:
614             keepduplicates = self.config.getoption("keepduplicates")
615             if not keepduplicates:
616                 duplicate_paths = self.config.pluginmanager._duplicatepaths
617                 if path in duplicate_paths:
618                     return ()
619                 else:
620                     duplicate_paths.add(path)
621 
622         if self.fspath == path:  # __init__.py
623             return [self]
624 
625         return ihook.pytest_collect_file(path=path, parent=self)

627     def isinitpath(self, path):
628         return path in self.session._initialpaths

630     def collect(self):
631         this_path = self.fspath.dirpath()
632         init_module = this_path.join("__init__.py")
633         if init_module.check(file=1) and path_matches_patterns(
634             init_module, self.config.getini("python_files")
635         ):
636             yield Module(init_module, self)
637         pkg_prefixes = set()
638         for path in this_path.visit(rec=self._recurse, bf=True, sort=True):
639             # We will visit our own __init__.py file, in which case we skip it.
640             is_file = path.isfile()
641             if is_file:
642                 if path.basename == "__init__.py" and path.dirpath() == this_path:
643                     continue
644 
645             parts_ = parts(path.strpath)
646             if any(
647                 pkg_prefix in parts_ and pkg_prefix.join("__init__.py") != path
648                 for pkg_prefix in pkg_prefixes
649             ):
650                 continue
651 
652             if is_file:
653                 yield from self._collectfile(path)
654             elif not path.isdir():
655                 # Broken symlink or invalid/missing file.
656                 continue
657             elif path.join("__init__.py").check(file=1):
658                 pkg_prefixes.add(path)

661 def _call_with_optional_argument(func, arg):
662     """Call the given function with the given argument if func accepts one argument, otherwise
663     calls func without arguments"""

665     if inspect.ismethod(func):
666         arg_count -= 1
667     if arg_count:
668         func(arg)
669     else:
670         func()

884 class Metafunc(fixtures.FuncargnamesCompatAttr):
885     """
886     Metafunc objects are passed to the :func:`pytest_generate_tests <_pytest.hookspec.pytest_generate_tests>` hook.
887     They help to inspect a test function and to generate tests according to
888     test configuration or values specified in the class or module where a
889     test function is defined.
890     """
891 
892     def __init__(self, definition, fixtureinfo, config, cls=None, module=None):
893         assert (
894             isinstance(definition, FunctionDefinition)
895             or type(definition).__name__ == "DefinitionMock"
896         )
897         self.definition = definition
898 
899         #: access to the :class:`_pytest.config.Config` object for the test session
900         self.config = config
901 
902         #: the module object where the test function is defined in.
903         self.module = module
904 
905         #: underlying python test function
906         self.function = definition.obj
907 
908         #: set of fixture names required by the test function
909         self.fixturenames = fixtureinfo.names_closure
910 
911         #: class object where the test function is defined in or ``None``.
912         self.cls = cls
913 
914         self._calls = []
915         self._ids = set()
916         self._arg2fixturedefs = fixtureinfo.name2fixturedefs
917 
918     def parametrize(self, argnames, argvalues, indirect=False, ids=None, scope=None):
919         """ Add new invocations to the underlying test function using the list
920         of argvalues for the given argnames.  Parametrization is performed
921         during the collection phase.  If you need to setup expensive resources
922         see about setting indirect to do it rather at test setup time.
923 
924         :arg argnames: a comma-separated string denoting one or more argument
925                        names, or a list/tuple of argument strings.
926 
927         :arg argvalues: The list of argvalues determines how often a
928             test is invoked with different argument values.  If only one
929             argname was specified argvalues is a list of values.  If N
930             argnames were specified, argvalues must be a list of N-tuples,
931             where each tuple-element specifies a value for its respective
932             argname.
933 
934         :arg indirect: The list of argnames or boolean. A list of arguments'
935             names (subset of argnames). If True the list contains all names from
936             the argnames. Each argvalue corresponding to an argname in this list will
937             be passed as request.param to its respective argname fixture
938             function so that it can perform more expensive setups during the
939             setup phase of a test rather than at collection time.
940 
941         :arg ids: list of string ids, or a callable.
942             If strings, each is corresponding to the argvalues so that they are
943             part of the test id. If None is given as id of specific test, the
944             automatically generated id for that argument will be used.
945             If callable, it should take one argument (a single argvalue) and return
946             a string or return None. If None, the automatically generated id for that
947             argument will be used.
948             If no ids are provided they will be generated automatically from
949             the argvalues.
950 
951         :arg scope: if specified it denotes the scope of the parameters.
952             The scope is used for grouping tests by parameter instances.
953             It will also override any fixture-function defined scope, allowing
954             to set a dynamic scope using test context or configuration.
955         """
956         from _pytest.fixtures import scope2index
957         from _pytest.mark import ParameterSet
958 
959         argnames, parameters = ParameterSet._for_parametrize(
960             argnames,
961             argvalues,
962             self.function,
963             self.config,
964             function_definition=self.definition,
965         )
966         del argvalues
967 
968         if "request" in argnames:
969             fail(
970                 "'request' is a reserved name and cannot be used in @pytest.mark.parametrize",
971                 pytrace=False,
972             )
973 
974         if scope is None:
975             scope = _find_parametrized_scope(argnames, self._arg2fixturedefs, indirect)
976 
977         self._validate_if_using_arg_names(argnames, indirect)
978 
979         arg_values_types = self._resolve_arg_value_types(argnames, indirect)
980 
981         ids = self._resolve_arg_ids(argnames, ids, parameters, item=self.definition)
982 
983         scopenum = scope2index(
984             scope, descr="parametrize() call in {}".format(self.function.__name__)
985         )
986 
987         # create the new calls: if we are parametrize() multiple times (by applying the decorator
988         # more than once) then we accumulate those calls generating the cartesian product
989         # of all calls
990         newcalls = []
991         for callspec in self._calls or [CallSpec2(self)]:
992             for param_index, (param_id, param_set) in enumerate(zip(ids, parameters)):
993                 newcallspec = callspec.copy()
994                 newcallspec.setmulti2(
995                     arg_values_types,
996                     argnames,
997                     param_set.values,
998                     param_id,
999                     param_set.marks,
1000                     scopenum,
1001                     param_index,
1002                 )
1003                 newcalls.append(newcallspec)
1004         self._calls = newcalls
1005 
1006     def _resolve_arg_ids(self, argnames, ids, parameters, item):
1007         """Resolves the actual ids for the given argnames, based on the ``ids`` parameter given
1008         to ``parametrize``.
1009 
1010         :param List[str] argnames: list of argument names passed to ``parametrize()``.
1011         :param ids: the ids parameter of the parametrized call (see docs).
1012         :param List[ParameterSet] parameters: the list of parameter values, same size as ``argnames``.
1013         :param Item item: the item that generated this parametrized call.
1014         :rtype: List[str]
1015         :return: the list of ids for each argname given
1016         """
1017         from _pytest._io.saferepr import saferepr
1018 
1019         idfn = None
1020         if callable(ids):
1021             idfn = ids
1022             ids = None
1023         if ids:
1024             func_name = self.function.__name__
1025             if len(ids) != len(parameters):
1026                 msg = "In {}: {} parameter sets specified, with different number of ids: {}"
1027                 fail(msg.format(func_name, len(parameters), len(ids)), pytrace=False)
1028             for id_value in ids:
1029                 if id_value is not None and not isinstance(id_value, str):
1030                     msg = "In {}: ids must be list of strings, found: {} (type: {!r})"
1031                     fail(
1032                         msg.format(func_name, saferepr(id_value), type(id_value)),
1033                         pytrace=False,
1034                     )

1038     def _resolve_arg_value_types(self, argnames, indirect):
1039         """Resolves if each parametrized argument must be considered a parameter to a fixture or a "funcarg"

1101 def _find_parametrized_scope(argnames, arg2fixturedefs, indirect):
1102     """Find the most appropriate scope for a parametrized call based on its arguments.
1103 
1104     When there's at least one direct argument, always use "function" scope.
1105 
1106     When a test function is parametrized and all its arguments are indirect
1107     (e.g. fixtures), return the most narrow scope based on the fixtures used.
1108 
1109     Related to issue #1832, based on code posted by @Kingdread.
1110     """
1111     from _pytest.fixtures import scopes
1112 
1113     if isinstance(indirect, (list, tuple)):
1114         all_arguments_are_fixtures = len(indirect) == len(argnames)
1115     else:
1116         all_arguments_are_fixtures = bool(indirect)
1117 
1118     if all_arguments_are_fixtures:
1119         fixturedefs = arg2fixturedefs or {}
1120         used_scopes = [
1121             fixturedef[0].scope
1122             for name, fixturedef in fixturedefs.items()
1123             if name in argnames
1124         ]
1125         if used_scopes:
1126             # Takes the most narrow scope from used fixtures
1127             for scope in reversed(scopes):
1128                 if scope in used_scopes:
1129                     return scope
1130 
1131     return "function"

1188 def idmaker(argnames, parametersets, idfn=None, ids=None, config=None, item=None):

1190         _idvalset(valindex, parameterset, argnames, idfn, ids, config=config, item=item)
1191         for valindex, parameterset in enumerate(parametersets)

87 def evaluate_condition(item: Item, mark: Mark, condition: object) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
88     """Evaluate a single skipif/xfail condition.
89 
90     If an old-style string condition is given, it is eval()'d, otherwise the
91     condition is bool()'d. If this fails, an appropriately formatted pytest.fail
92     is raised.
93 
94     Returns (result, reason). The reason is only relevant if the result is True.
95     """
96     # String condition.
97     if isinstance(condition, str):
98         globals_ = {
99             "os": os,
100             "sys": sys,
101             "platform": platform,
102             "config": item.config,
103         }
104         if hasattr(item, "obj"):
105             globals_.update(item.obj.__globals__)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
106         try:
107             filename = "<{} condition>".format(mark.name)
108             condition_code = compile(condition, filename, "eval")
109             result = eval(condition_code, globals_)
110         except SyntaxError as exc:
111             msglines = [
112                 "Error evaluating %r condition" % mark.name,
113                 "    " + condition,
114                 "    " + " " * (exc.offset or 0) + "^",
115                 "SyntaxError: invalid syntax",
116             ]
117             fail("\n".join(msglines), pytrace=False)
118         except Exception as exc:
119             msglines = [
120                 "Error evaluating %r condition" % mark.name,
121                 "    " + condition,
122                 *traceback.format_exception_only(type(exc), exc),
123             ]
124             fail("\n".join(msglines), pytrace=False)
125 
126     # Boolean condition.
127     else:
128         try:
129             result = bool(condition)
130         except Exception as exc:
131             msglines = [
132                 "Error evaluating %r condition as a boolean" % mark.name,
133                 *traceback.format_exception_only(type(exc), exc),
134             ]
135             fail("\n".join(msglines), pytrace=False)
136 
137     reason = mark.kwargs.get("reason", None)
138     if reason is None:
139         if isinstance(condition, str):
140             reason = "condition: " + condition
141         else:
142             # XXX better be checked at collection time
143             msg = (
144                 "Error evaluating %r: " % mark.name
145                 + "you need to specify reason=STRING when using booleans as conditions."
146             )
147             fail(msg, pytrace=False)
148 
149     return result, reason

159 def evaluate_skip_marks(item: Item) -> Optional[Skip]:
160     """Evaluate skip and skipif marks on item, returning Skip if triggered."""
161     for mark in item.iter_markers(name="skipif"):
162         if "condition" not in mark.kwargs:
163             conditions = mark.args
164         else:
165             conditions = (mark.kwargs["condition"],)
166 
167         # Unconditional.
168         if not conditions:
169             reason = mark.kwargs.get("reason", "")
170             return Skip(reason)
171 
172         # If any of the conditions are true.
173         for condition in conditions:
174             result, reason = evaluate_condition(item, mark, condition)
175             if result:
176                 return Skip(reason)
177 
178     for mark in item.iter_markers(name="skip"):
179         if "reason" in mark.kwargs:
180             reason = mark.kwargs["reason"]
181         elif mark.args:
182             reason = mark.args[0]
183         else:
184             reason = "unconditional skip"
185         return Skip(reason)
186

349 class FDCaptureBinary:
350     """Capture IO to/from a given os-level filedescriptor.
351 
352     snap() produces `bytes`
353     """
354 
355     EMPTY_BUFFER = b""
356 
357     def __init__(self, targetfd: int) -> None:
358         self.targetfd = targetfd
359 
360         try:
361             os.fstat(targetfd)
362         except OSError:
363             # FD capturing is conceptually simple -- create a temporary file,
364             # redirect the FD to it, redirect back when done. But when the
365             # target FD is invalid it throws a wrench into this loveley scheme.
366             #
367             # Tests themselves shouldn't care if the FD is valid, FD capturing
368             # should work regardless of external circumstances. So falling back
369             # to just sys capturing is not a good option.
370             #
371             # Further complications are the need to support suspend() and the
372             # possibility of FD reuse (e.g. the tmpfile getting the very same
373             # target FD). The following approach is robust, I believe.
374             self.targetfd_invalid = os.open(
375                 os.devnull, os.O_RDWR
376             )  # type: Optional[int]
377             os.dup2(self.targetfd_invalid, targetfd)
378         else:
379             self.targetfd_invalid = None
380         self.targetfd_save = os.dup(targetfd)
381 
382         if targetfd == 0:
383             self.tmpfile = open(os.devnull)
384             self.syscapture = SysCapture(targetfd)
385         else:
386             self.tmpfile = EncodedFile(
387                 # TODO: Remove type ignore, fixed in next mypy release.
388                 TemporaryFile(buffering=0),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
389                 encoding="utf-8",
390                 errors="replace",
391                 write_through=True,
392             )
393             if targetfd in patchsysdict:
394                 self.syscapture = SysCapture(targetfd, self.tmpfile)
395             else:
396                 self.syscapture = NoCapture()
397 
398         self._state = "initialized"
399 
400     def __repr__(self) -> str:
401         return "<{} {} oldfd={} _state={!r} tmpfile={!r}>".format(
402             self.__class__.__name__,
403             self.targetfd,
404             self.targetfd_save,
405             self._state,
406             self.tmpfile,
407         )
408 
409     def _assert_state(self, op: str, states: Tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
410         assert (
411             self._state in states
412         ), "cannot {} in state {!r}: expected one of {}".format(
413             op, self._state, ", ".join(states)
414         )
415 
416     def start(self) -> None:
417         """ Start capturing on targetfd using memorized tmpfile. """
418         self._assert_state("start", ("initialized",))
419         os.dup2(self.tmpfile.fileno(), self.targetfd)
420         self.syscapture.start()
421         self._state = "started"
422 
423     def snap(self):
424         self._assert_state("snap", ("started", "suspended"))
425         self.tmpfile.seek(0)
426         res = self.tmpfile.buffer.read()
427         self.tmpfile.seek(0)
428         self.tmpfile.truncate()
429         return res
430 
431     def done(self) -> None:
432         """ stop capturing, restore streams, return original capture file,
433         seeked to position zero. """
434         self._assert_state("done", ("initialized", "started", "suspended", "done"))
435         if self._state == "done":
436             return
437         os.dup2(self.targetfd_save, self.targetfd)
438         os.close(self.targetfd_save)
439         if self.targetfd_invalid is not None:
440             if self.targetfd_invalid != self.targetfd:
441                 os.close(self.targetfd)
442             os.close(self.targetfd_invalid)
443         self.syscapture.done()
444         self.tmpfile.close()
445         self._state = "done"
446 
447     def suspend(self) -> None:
448         self._assert_state("suspend", ("started", "suspended"))
449         if self._state == "suspended":
450             return
451         self.syscapture.suspend()
452         os.dup2(self.targetfd_save, self.targetfd)
453         self._state = "suspended"
454 
455     def resume(self) -> None:
456         self._assert_state("resume", ("started", "suspended"))
457         if self._state == "started":
458             return
459         self.syscapture.resume()
460         os.dup2(self.tmpfile.fileno(), self.targetfd)
461         self._state = "started"
462 
463     def writeorg(self, data):
464         """ write to original file descriptor. """
465         self._assert_state("writeorg", ("started", "suspended"))
466         os.write(self.targetfd_save, data)

496 class MultiCapture:
497     _state = None
498     _in_suspended = False
499 
500     def __init__(self, in_, out, err) -> None:
501         self.in_ = in_
502         self.out = out
503         self.err = err
504 
505     def __repr__(self) -> str:
506         return "<MultiCapture out={!r} err={!r} in_={!r} _state={!r} _in_suspended={!r}>".format(
507             self.out, self.err, self.in_, self._state, self._in_suspended,
508         )
509 
510     def start_capturing(self) -> None:
511         self._state = "started"
512         if self.in_:
513             self.in_.start()
514         if self.out:
515             self.out.start()
516         if self.err:
517             self.err.start()
518 
519     def pop_outerr_to_orig(self):
520         """ pop current snapshot out/err capture and flush to orig streams. """
521         out, err = self.readouterr()
522         if out:
523             self.out.writeorg(out)
524         if err:
525             self.err.writeorg(err)
526         return out, err
527 
528     def suspend_capturing(self, in_: bool = False) -> None:
529         self._state = "suspended"
530         if self.out:
531             self.out.suspend()
532         if self.err:
533             self.err.suspend()
534         if in_ and self.in_:
535             self.in_.suspend()
536             self._in_suspended = True
537 
538     def resume_capturing(self) -> None:
539         self._state = "resumed"
540         if self.out:
541             self.out.resume()
542         if self.err:
543             self.err.resume()
544         if self._in_suspended:
545             self.in_.resume()
546             self._in_suspended = False
547 
548     def stop_capturing(self) -> None:
549         """ stop capturing and reset capturing streams """
550         if self._state == "stopped":
551             raise ValueError("was already stopped")
552         self._state = "stopped"
553         if self.out:
554             self.out.done()
555         if self.err:
556             self.err.done()
557         if self.in_:
558             self.in_.done()
559 
560     def readouterr(self) -> CaptureResult:
561         if self.out:
562             out = self.out.snap()
563         else:
564             out = ""
565         if self.err:
566             err = self.err.snap()
567         else:
568             err = ""
569         return CaptureResult(out, err)

572 def _get_multicapture(method: "_CaptureMethod") -> MultiCapture:
573     if method == "fd":
574         return MultiCapture(in_=FDCapture(0), out=FDCapture(1), err=FDCapture(2))
575     elif method == "sys":
576         return MultiCapture(in_=SysCapture(0), out=SysCapture(1), err=SysCapture(2))
577     elif method == "no":

579     elif method == "tee-sys":

581             in_=None, out=SysCapture(1, tee=True), err=SysCapture(2, tee=True)
582         )

590     """
591     Capture plugin, manages that the appropriate capture method is enabled/disabled during collection and each
592     test phase (setup, call, teardown). After each of those points, the captured output is obtained and
593     attached to the collection/runtest report.

595     There are two levels of capture:
596     * global: which is enabled by default and can be suppressed by the ``-s`` option. This is always enabled/disabled
597       during collection and each test phase.

603         self._method = method

605         self._capture_fixture = None  # type: Optional[CaptureFixture]

609             self._method, self._global_capturing, self._capture_fixture

613         if self.is_globally_capturing():
614             return "global"

447     def _genfunctions(self, name: str, funcobj) -> Iterator["Function"]:
448         modulecol = self.getparent(Module)
449         assert modulecol is not None
450         module = modulecol.obj
451         clscol = self.getparent(Class)
452         cls = clscol and clscol.obj or None
453         fm = self.session._fixturemanager
454 
455         definition = FunctionDefinition.from_parent(self, name=name, callobj=funcobj)
456         fixtureinfo = definition._fixtureinfo
457 
458         metafunc = Metafunc(
459             definition=definition,
460             fixtureinfo=fixtureinfo,
461             config=self.config,
462             cls=cls,
463             module=module,
464             _ispytest=True,
465         )
466         methods = []
467         if hasattr(module, "pytest_generate_tests"):
468             methods.append(module.pytest_generate_tests)
469         if cls is not None and hasattr(cls, "pytest_generate_tests"):
470             methods.append(cls().pytest_generate_tests)
471 
472         self.ihook.pytest_generate_tests.call_extra(methods, dict(metafunc=metafunc))
473 
474         if not metafunc._calls:
475             yield Function.from_parent(self, name=name, fixtureinfo=fixtureinfo)
476         else:
477             # Add funcargs() as fixturedefs to fixtureinfo.arg2fixturedefs.
478             fixtures.add_funcarg_pseudo_fixture_def(self, metafunc, fm)
479 
480             # Add_funcarg_pseudo_fixture_def may have shadowed some fixtures
481             # with direct parametrization, so make sure we update what the
482             # function really needs.
483             fixtureinfo.prune_dependency_tree()
484 
485             for callspec in metafunc._calls:
486                 subname = f"{name}[{callspec.id}]"
487                 yield Function.from_parent(
488                     self,
489                     name=subname,
490                     callspec=callspec,
491                     callobj=funcobj,
492                     fixtureinfo=fixtureinfo,
493                     keywords={callspec.id: True},
494                     originalname=name,
495                 )

581         except SyntaxError as e:
582             raise self.CollectError(
583                 ExceptionInfo.from_current().getrepr(style="short")
584             ) from e
585         except ImportPathMismatchError as e:
586             raise self.CollectError(
587                 "import file mismatch:\n"
588                 "imported module %r has this __file__ attribute:\n"
589                 "  %s\n"
590                 "which is not the same as the test file we want to collect:\n"
591                 "  %s\n"
592                 "HINT: remove __pycache__ / .pyc files and/or use a "
593                 "unique basename for your test file modules" % e.args
594             ) from e
595         except ImportError as e:
596             exc_info = ExceptionInfo.from_current()
597             if self.config.getoption("verbose") < 2:
598                 exc_info.traceback = exc_info.traceback.filter(filter_traceback)
599             exc_repr = (

613                 raise

615                 "Using pytest.skip outside of a test is not allowed. "
616                 "To decorate a test function, use the @pytest.mark.skip "
617                 "or @pytest.mark.skipif decorators instead, and to skip a "
618                 "module use `pytestmark = pytest.mark.{skip,skipif}."

620         self.config.pluginmanager.consider_module(mod)

666     def _recurse(self, direntry: "os.DirEntry[str]") -> bool:
667         if direntry.name == "__pycache__":
668             return False
669         fspath = Path(direntry.path)
670         path = py.path.local(fspath)
671         ihook = self.session.gethookproxy(fspath.parent)
672         if ihook.pytest_ignore_collect(fspath=fspath, path=path, config=self.config):
673             return False
674         norecursepatterns = self.config.getini("norecursedirs")
675         if any(fnmatch_ex(pat, fspath) for pat in norecursepatterns):
676             return False
677         return True

679     def _collectfile(
680         self, fspath: Path, handle_dupes: bool = True
681     ) -> Sequence[nodes.Collector]:
682         path = py.path.local(fspath)
683         assert (
684             fspath.is_file()
685         ), "{!r} is not a file (isdir={!r}, exists={!r}, islink={!r})".format(
686             path, fspath.is_dir(), fspath.exists(), fspath.is_symlink()
687         )
688         ihook = self.session.gethookproxy(fspath)
689         if not self.session.isinitpath(fspath):
690             if ihook.pytest_ignore_collect(
691                 fspath=fspath, path=path, config=self.config
692             ):
693                 return ()
694 
695         if handle_dupes:
696             keepduplicates = self.config.getoption("keepduplicates")
697             if not keepduplicates:
698                 duplicate_paths = self.config.pluginmanager._duplicatepaths
699                 if fspath in duplicate_paths:
700                     return ()
701                 else:
702                     duplicate_paths.add(fspath)
703 
704         return ihook.pytest_collect_file(fspath=fspath, path=path, parent=self)  # type: ignore[no-any-return]
705 
706     def collect(self) -> Iterable[Union[nodes.Item, nodes.Collector]]:
707         this_path = Path(self.fspath).parent
708         init_module = this_path / "__init__.py"
709         if init_module.is_file() and path_matches_patterns(
710             init_module, self.config.getini("python_files")
711         ):
712             yield Module.from_parent(self, fspath=py.path.local(init_module))
713         pkg_prefixes: Set[Path] = set()
714         for direntry in visit(str(this_path), recurse=self._recurse):
715             path = Path(direntry.path)
716 
717             # We will visit our own __init__.py file, in which case we skip it.
718             if direntry.is_file():
719                 if direntry.name == "__init__.py" and path.parent == this_path:
720                     continue
721 
722             parts_ = parts(direntry.path)
723             if any(
724                 str(pkg_prefix) in parts_ and pkg_prefix / "__init__.py" != path
725                 for pkg_prefix in pkg_prefixes
726             ):
727                 continue
728 
729             if direntry.is_file():
730                 yield from self._collectfile(path)
731             elif not direntry.is_dir():
732                 # Broken symlink or invalid/missing file.
733                 continue
734             elif path.joinpath("__init__.py").is_file():
735                 pkg_prefixes.add(path)

738 def _call_with_optional_argument(func, arg) -> None:
739     """Call the given function with the given argument if func accepts one argument, otherwise
740     calls func without arguments."""
741     arg_count = func.__code__.co_argcount
742     if inspect.ismethod(func):
743         arg_count -= 1
744     if arg_count:
745         func(arg)
746     else:
747         func()

950 class Metafunc:
951     """Objects passed to the :func:`pytest_generate_tests <_pytest.hookspec.pytest_generate_tests>` hook.
952 
953     They help to inspect a test function and to generate tests according to
954     test configuration or values specified in the class or module where a
955     test function is defined.
956     """
957 
958     def __init__(
959         self,
960         definition: "FunctionDefinition",
961         fixtureinfo: fixtures.FuncFixtureInfo,
962         config: Config,
963         cls=None,
964         module=None,
965         *,
966         _ispytest: bool = False,
967     ) -> None:
968         check_ispytest(_ispytest)
969 
970         #: Access to the underlying :class:`_pytest.python.FunctionDefinition`.
971         self.definition = definition
972 
973         #: Access to the :class:`_pytest.config.Config` object for the test session.
974         self.config = config
975 
976         #: The module object where the test function is defined in.
977         self.module = module
978 
979         #: Underlying Python test function.
980         self.function = definition.obj
981 
982         #: Set of fixture names required by the test function.
983         self.fixturenames = fixtureinfo.names_closure
984 
985         #: Class object where the test function is defined in or ``None``.
986         self.cls = cls
987 
988         self._calls: List[CallSpec2] = []
989         self._arg2fixturedefs = fixtureinfo.name2fixturedefs
990 
991     def parametrize(
992         self,
993         argnames: Union[str, List[str], Tuple[str, ...]],
994         argvalues: Iterable[Union[ParameterSet, Sequence[object], object]],
995         indirect: Union[bool, Sequence[str]] = False,
996         ids: Optional[
997             Union[
998                 Iterable[Union[None, str, float, int, bool]],
999                 Callable[[Any], Optional[object]],
1000             ]
1001         ] = None,
1002         scope: "Optional[_Scope]" = None,
1003         *,
1004         _param_mark: Optional[Mark] = None,
1005     ) -> None:
1006         """Add new invocations to the underlying test function using the list
1007         of argvalues for the given argnames.  Parametrization is performed
1008         during the collection phase.  If you need to setup expensive resources
1009         see about setting indirect to do it rather at test setup time.
1010 
1011         :param argnames:
1012             A comma-separated string denoting one or more argument names, or
1013             a list/tuple of argument strings.
1014 
1015         :param argvalues:
1016             The list of argvalues determines how often a test is invoked with
1017             different argument values.
1018 
1019             If only one argname was specified argvalues is a list of values.
1020             If N argnames were specified, argvalues must be a list of
1021             N-tuples, where each tuple-element specifies a value for its
1022             respective argname.
1023 
1024         :param indirect:
1025             A list of arguments' names (subset of argnames) or a boolean.
1026             If True the list contains all names from the argnames. Each
1027             argvalue corresponding to an argname in this list will
1028             be passed as request.param to its respective argname fixture
1029             function so that it can perform more expensive setups during the
1030             setup phase of a test rather than at collection time.
1031 
1032         :param ids:
1033             Sequence of (or generator for) ids for ``argvalues``,
1034             or a callable to return part of the id for each argvalue.
1035 
1036             With sequences (and generators like ``itertools.count()``) the
1037             returned ids should be of type ``string``, ``int``, ``float``,
1038             ``bool``, or ``None``.
1039             They are mapped to the corresponding index in ``argvalues``.
1040             ``None`` means to use the auto-generated id.
1041 
1042             If it is a callable it will be called for each entry in
1043             ``argvalues``, and the return value is used as part of the
1044             auto-generated id for the whole set (where parts are joined with
1045             dashes ("-")).
1046             This is useful to provide more specific ids for certain items, e.g.
1047             dates.  Returning ``None`` will use an auto-generated id.
1048 
1049             If no ids are provided they will be generated automatically from
1050             the argvalues.
1051 
1052         :param scope:
1053             If specified it denotes the scope of the parameters.
1054             The scope is used for grouping tests by parameter instances.
1055             It will also override any fixture-function defined scope, allowing
1056             to set a dynamic scope using test context or configuration.
1057         """
1058         from _pytest.fixtures import scope2index
1059 
1060         argnames, parameters = ParameterSet._for_parametrize(
1061             argnames,
1062             argvalues,
1063             self.function,
1064             self.config,
1065             nodeid=self.definition.nodeid,
1066         )
1067         del argvalues
1068 
1069         if "request" in argnames:
1070             fail(
1071                 "'request' is a reserved name and cannot be used in @pytest.mark.parametrize",
1072                 pytrace=False,
1073             )
1074 
1075         if scope is None:
1076             scope = _find_parametrized_scope(argnames, self._arg2fixturedefs, indirect)
1077 
1078         self._validate_if_using_arg_names(argnames, indirect)
1079 
1080         arg_values_types = self._resolve_arg_value_types(argnames, indirect)
1081 
1082         # Use any already (possibly) generated ids with parametrize Marks.
1083         if _param_mark and _param_mark._param_ids_from:
1084             generated_ids = _param_mark._param_ids_from._param_ids_generated
1085             if generated_ids is not None:
1086                 ids = generated_ids
1087 
1088         ids = self._resolve_arg_ids(
1089             argnames, ids, parameters, nodeid=self.definition.nodeid
1090         )
1091 
1092         # Store used (possibly generated) ids with parametrize Marks.
1093         if _param_mark and _param_mark._param_ids_from and generated_ids is None:
1094             object.__setattr__(_param_mark._param_ids_from, "_param_ids_generated", ids)
1095 
1096         scopenum = scope2index(
1097             scope, descr=f"parametrize() call in {self.function.__name__}"
1098         )
1099 
1100         # Create the new calls: if we are parametrize() multiple times (by applying the decorator
1101         # more than once) then we accumulate those calls generating the cartesian product
1102         # of all calls.
1103         newcalls = []
1104         for callspec in self._calls or [CallSpec2(self)]:
1105             for param_index, (param_id, param_set) in enumerate(zip(ids, parameters)):
1106                 newcallspec = callspec.copy()
1107                 newcallspec.setmulti2(
1108                     arg_values_types,
1109                     argnames,
1110                     param_set.values,
1111                     param_id,
1112                     param_set.marks,
1113                     scopenum,
1114                     param_index,
1115                 )
1116                 newcalls.append(newcallspec)
1117         self._calls = newcalls

1119     def _resolve_arg_ids(
1120         self,
1121         argnames: Sequence[str],
1122         ids: Optional[
1123             Union[
1124                 Iterable[Union[None, str, float, int, bool]],
1125                 Callable[[Any], Optional[object]],
1126             ]
1127         ],
1128         parameters: Sequence[ParameterSet],
1129         nodeid: str,
1130     ) -> List[str]:
1131         """Resolve the actual ids for the given argnames, based on the ``ids`` parameter given
1132         to ``parametrize``.
1133 
1134         :param List[str] argnames: List of argument names passed to ``parametrize()``.
1135         :param ids: The ids parameter of the parametrized call (see docs).
1136         :param List[ParameterSet] parameters: The list of parameter values, same size as ``argnames``.
1137         :param str str: The nodeid of the item that generated this parametrized call.
1138         :rtype: List[str]
1139         :returns: The list of ids for each argname given.
1140         """
1141         if ids is None:
1142             idfn = None
1143             ids_ = None
1144         elif callable(ids):
1145             idfn = ids
1146             ids_ = None
1147         else:
1148             idfn = None
1149             ids_ = self._validate_ids(ids, parameters, self.function.__name__)
1150         return idmaker(argnames, parameters, idfn, ids_, self.config, nodeid=nodeid)

1152     def _validate_ids(
1153         self,
1154         ids: Iterable[Union[None, str, float, int, bool]],
1155         parameters: Sequence[ParameterSet],
1156         func_name: str,
1157     ) -> List[Union[None, str]]:
1158         try:
1159             num_ids = len(ids)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
1160         except TypeError:
1161             try:
1162                 iter(ids)
1163             except TypeError as e:
1164                 raise TypeError("ids must be a callable or an iterable") from e
1165             num_ids = len(parameters)
1166 
1167         # num_ids == 0 is a special case: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1849
1168         if num_ids != len(parameters) and num_ids != 0:
1169             msg = "In {}: {} parameter sets specified, with different number of ids: {}"
1170             fail(msg.format(func_name, len(parameters), num_ids), pytrace=False)
1171 
1172         new_ids = []
1173         for idx, id_value in enumerate(itertools.islice(ids, num_ids)):
1174             if id_value is None or isinstance(id_value, str):
1175                 new_ids.append(id_value)
1176             elif isinstance(id_value, (float, int, bool)):
1177                 new_ids.append(str(id_value))
1178             else:
1179                 msg = (  # type: ignore[unreachable]
1180                     "In {}: ids must be list of string/float/int/bool, "
1181                     "found: {} (type: {!r}) at index {}"
1182                 )
1183                 fail(
1184                     msg.format(func_name, saferepr(id_value), type(id_value), idx),
1185                     pytrace=False,
1186                 )
1187         return new_ids

1189     def _resolve_arg_value_types(
1190         self,
1191         argnames: Sequence[str],
1192         indirect: Union[bool, Sequence[str]],
1193     ) -> Dict[str, "Literal['params', 'funcargs']"]:
1194         """Resolve if each parametrized argument must be considered a
1195         parameter to a fixture or a "funcarg" to the function, based on the
1196         ``indirect`` parameter of the parametrized() call.
1197 
1198         :param List[str] argnames: List of argument names passed to ``parametrize()``.
1199         :param indirect: Same as the ``indirect`` parameter of ``parametrize()``.
1200         :rtype: Dict[str, str]
1201             A dict mapping each arg name to either:
1202             * "params" if the argname should be the parameter of a fixture of the same name.
1203             * "funcargs" if the argname should be a parameter to the parametrized test function.
1204         """
1205         if isinstance(indirect, bool):
1206             valtypes: Dict[str, Literal["params", "funcargs"]] = dict.fromkeys(
1207                 argnames, "params" if indirect else "funcargs"
1208             )
1209         elif isinstance(indirect, Sequence):
1210             valtypes = dict.fromkeys(argnames, "funcargs")
1211             for arg in indirect:
1212                 if arg not in argnames:
1213                     fail(
1214                         "In {}: indirect fixture '{}' doesn't exist".format(
1215                             self.function.__name__, arg
1216                         ),
1217                         pytrace=False,
1218                     )
1219                 valtypes[arg] = "params"
1220         else:
1221             fail(
1222                 "In {func}: expected Sequence or boolean for indirect, got {type}".format(
1223                     type=type(indirect).__name__, func=self.function.__name__
1224                 ),
1225                 pytrace=False,
1226             )
1227         return valtypes

1229     def _validate_if_using_arg_names(
1230         self,
1231         argnames: Sequence[str],
1232         indirect: Union[bool, Sequence[str]],
1233     ) -> None:
1234         """Check if all argnames are being used, by default values, or directly/indirectly.
1235 
1236         :param List[str] argnames: List of argument names passed to ``parametrize()``.
1237         :param indirect: Same as the ``indirect`` parameter of ``parametrize()``.
1238         :raises ValueError: If validation fails.
1239         """
1240         default_arg_names = set(get_default_arg_names(self.function))
1241         func_name = self.function.__name__
1242         for arg in argnames:
1243             if arg not in self.fixturenames:
1244                 if arg in default_arg_names:
1245                     fail(
1246                         "In {}: function already takes an argument '{}' with a default value".format(
1247                             func_name, arg
1248                         ),
1249                         pytrace=False,
1250                     )
1251                 else:
1252                     if isinstance(indirect, Sequence):
1253                         name = "fixture" if arg in indirect else "argument"
1254                     else:
1255                         name = "fixture" if indirect else "argument"
1256                     fail(
1257                         f"In {func_name}: function uses no {name} '{arg}'",
1258                         pytrace=False,
1259                     )

1262 def _find_parametrized_scope(
1263     argnames: Sequence[str],
1264     arg2fixturedefs: Mapping[str, Sequence[fixtures.FixtureDef[object]]],
1265     indirect: Union[bool, Sequence[str]],
1266 ) -> "fixtures._Scope":
1267     """Find the most appropriate scope for a parametrized call based on its arguments.
1268 
1269     When there's at least one direct argument, always use "function" scope.
1270 
1271     When a test function is parametrized and all its arguments are indirect
1272     (e.g. fixtures), return the most narrow scope based on the fixtures used.
1273 
1274     Related to issue #1832, based on code posted by @Kingdread.
1275     """
1276     if isinstance(indirect, Sequence):
1277         all_arguments_are_fixtures = len(indirect) == len(argnames)
1278     else:
1279         all_arguments_are_fixtures = bool(indirect)
1280 
1281     if all_arguments_are_fixtures:
1282         fixturedefs = arg2fixturedefs or {}
1283         used_scopes = [
1284             fixturedef[0].scope
1285             for name, fixturedef in fixturedefs.items()
1286             if name in argnames
1287         ]
1288         if used_scopes:
1289             # Takes the most narrow scope from used fixtures.
1290             for scope in reversed(fixtures.scopes):
1291                 if scope in used_scopes:
1292                     return scope
1293 
1294     return "function"

1297 def _ascii_escaped_by_config(val: Union[str, bytes], config: Optional[Config]) -> str:
1298     if config is None:
1299         escape_option = False
1300     else:
1301         escape_option = config.getini(
1302             "disable_test_id_escaping_and_forfeit_all_rights_to_community_support"
1303         )
1304     # TODO: If escaping is turned off and the user passes bytes,
1305     #       will return a bytes. For now we ignore this but the

1310 def _idval(
1311     val: object,
1312     argname: str,
1313     idx: int,
1314     idfn: Optional[Callable[[Any], Optional[object]]],
1315     nodeid: Optional[str],
1316     config: Optional[Config],
1317 ) -> str:
1318     if idfn:
1319         try:
1320             generated_id = idfn(val)
1321             if generated_id is not None:
1322                 val = generated_id
1323         except Exception as e:
1324             prefix = f"{nodeid}: " if nodeid is not None else ""
1325             msg = "error raised while trying to determine id of parameter '{}' at position {}"
1326             msg = prefix + msg.format(argname, idx)
1327             raise ValueError(msg) from e
1328     elif config:
1329         hook_id: Optional[str] = config.hook.pytest_make_parametrize_id(
1330             config=config, val=val, argname=argname
1331         )
1332         if hook_id:
1333             return hook_id
1334 
1335     if isinstance(val, STRING_TYPES):
1336         return _ascii_escaped_by_config(val, config)
1337     elif val is None or isinstance(val, (float, int, bool)):
1338         return str(val)
1339     elif isinstance(val, REGEX_TYPE):
1340         return ascii_escaped(val.pattern)
1341     elif val is NOTSET:
1342         # Fallback to default. Note that NOTSET is an enum.Enum.
1343         pass
1344     elif isinstance(val, enum.Enum):
1345         return str(val)
1346     elif isinstance(getattr(val, "__name__", None), str):
1347         # Name of a class, function, module, etc.
1348         name: str = getattr(val, "__name__")
1349         return name
1350     return str(argname) + str(idx)

1353 def _idvalset(
1354     idx: int,
1355     parameterset: ParameterSet,
1356     argnames: Iterable[str],
1357     idfn: Optional[Callable[[Any], Optional[object]]],
1358     ids: Optional[List[Union[None, str]]],
1359     nodeid: Optional[str],
1360     config: Optional[Config],
1361 ) -> str:
1362     if parameterset.id is not None:
1363         return parameterset.id
1364     id = None if ids is None or idx >= len(ids) else ids[idx]
1365     if id is None:
1366         this_id = [
1367             _idval(val, argname, idx, idfn, nodeid=nodeid, config=config)
1368             for val, argname in zip(parameterset.values, argnames)
1369         ]
1370         return "-".join(this_id)
1371     else:
1372         return _ascii_escaped_by_config(id, config)

1375 def idmaker(
1376     argnames: Iterable[str],
1377     parametersets: Iterable[ParameterSet],
1378     idfn: Optional[Callable[[Any], Optional[object]]] = None,
1379     ids: Optional[List[Union[None, str]]] = None,
1380     config: Optional[Config] = None,
1381     nodeid: Optional[str] = None,
1382 ) -> List[str]:
1383     resolved_ids = [
1384         _idvalset(
1385             valindex, parameterset, argnames, idfn, ids, config=config, nodeid=nodeid
1386         )
1387         for valindex, parameterset in enumerate(parametersets)
1388     ]
1389 
1390     # All IDs must be unique!
1391     unique_ids = set(resolved_ids)
1392     if len(unique_ids) != len(resolved_ids):
1393 
1394         # Record the number of occurrences of each test ID.
1395         test_id_counts = Counter(resolved_ids)
1396 
1397         # Map the test ID to its next suffix.
1398         test_id_suffixes: Dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
1399 
1400         # Suffix non-unique IDs to make them unique.
1401         for index, test_id in enumerate(resolved_ids):
1402             if test_id_counts[test_id] > 1:
1403                 resolved_ids[index] = "{}{}".format(test_id, test_id_suffixes[test_id])
1404                 test_id_suffixes[test_id] += 1
1405 
1406     return resolved_ids

1471 def _showfixtures_main(config: Config, session: Session) -> None:

1474     session.perform_collect()
1475     curdir = Path.cwd()
1476     tw = _pytest.config.create_terminal_writer(config)
1477     verbose = config.getvalue("verbose")

1479     fm = session._fixturemanager

1481     available = []
1482     seen: Set[Tuple[str, str]] = set()
1483 
1484     for argname, fixturedefs in fm._arg2fixturedefs.items():
1485         assert fixturedefs is not None

1488         for fixturedef in fixturedefs:

1493             available.append(
1494                 (
1495                     len(fixturedef.baseid),
1496                     fixturedef.func.__module__,
1497                     bestrelpath(curdir, Path(loc)),
1498                     fixturedef.argname,
1499                     fixturedef,
1500                 )
1501             )
1502

1504     currentmodule = None
1505     for baseid, module, bestrel, argname, fixturedef in available:
1506         if currentmodule != module:
1507             if not module.startswith("_pytest."):
1508                 tw.line()

1533 class Function(PyobjMixin, nodes.Item):

1536     param name:
1537         The full function name, including any decorations like those
1538         added by parametrization (``my_func[my_param]``).
1539     param parent:
1540         The parent Node.

1542         The pytest Config object.

1545         meta information about the parametrization.
1546     param callobj:
1547         If given, the object which will be called when the Function is invoked,
1548         otherwise the callobj will be obtained from ``parent`` using ``originalname``.
1549     param keywords:

1552         The pytest Session object.

1555     param originalname:
1556         The attribute name to use for accessing the underlying function object.

1558         for example when it contains decorations like those added by parametrization
1559         (``my_func[my_param]``).

1668                 if ntraceback == traceback:

1670                     if not ntraceback:
1671                         ntraceback = traceback

1674             # issue364: mark all but first and last frames to

36 def _solve_sparse_cg(X, y, alpha, max_iter=None, tol=1e-3, verbose=0):
37     n_samples, n_features = X.shape
38     X1 = sp_linalg.aslinearoperator(X)
39     coefs = np.empty((y.shape[1], n_features), dtype=X.dtype)
40 
41     if n_features > n_samples:
42         def create_mv(curr_alpha):
43             def _mv(x):
44                 return X1.matvec(X1.rmatvec(x)) + curr_alpha * x
45             return _mv
46     else:
47         def create_mv(curr_alpha):
48             def _mv(x):
49                 return X1.rmatvec(X1.matvec(x)) + curr_alpha * x
50             return _mv
51 
52     for i in range(y.shape[1]):
53         y_column = y[:, i]
54 
55         mv = create_mv(alpha[i])
56         if n_features > n_samples:
57             # kernel ridge
58             # w = X.T * inv(X X^t + alpha*Id) y
59             C = sp_linalg.LinearOperator(
60                 (n_samples, n_samples), matvec=mv, dtype=X.dtype)
61             coef, info = sp_linalg.cg(C, y_column, tol=tol)
62             coefs[i] = X1.rmatvec(coef)
63         else:
64             # linear ridge
65             # w = inv(X^t X + alpha*Id) * X.T y
66             y_column = X1.rmatvec(y_column)
67             C = sp_linalg.LinearOperator(
68                 (n_features, n_features), matvec=mv, dtype=X.dtype)
69             coefs[i], info = sp_linalg.cg(C, y_column, maxiter=max_iter,
70                                           tol=tol)
71         if info < 0:
72             raise ValueError("Failed with error code %d" % info)
73 
74         if max_iter is None and info > 0 and verbose:
75             warnings.warn("sparse_cg did not converge after %d iterations." %
76                           info)
77 
78     return coefs

81 def _solve_lsqr(X, y, alpha, max_iter=None, tol=1e-3):
82     n_samples, n_features = X.shape
83     coefs = np.empty((y.shape[1], n_features), dtype=X.dtype)
84     n_iter = np.empty(y.shape[1], dtype=np.int32)
85 
86     # According to the lsqr documentation, alpha = damp^2.
87     sqrt_alpha = np.sqrt(alpha)
88 
89     for i in range(y.shape[1]):
90         y_column = y[:, i]
91         info = sp_linalg.lsqr(X, y_column, damp=sqrt_alpha[i],
92                               atol=tol, btol=tol, iter_lim=max_iter)
93         coefs[i] = info[0]
94         n_iter[i] = info[2]
95 
96     return coefs, n_iter

99 def _solve_cholesky(X, y, alpha):
100     # w = inv(X^t X + alpha*Id) * X.T y
101     n_samples, n_features = X.shape
102     n_targets = y.shape[1]
103 
104     A = safe_sparse_dot(X.T, X, dense_output=True)
105     Xy = safe_sparse_dot(X.T, y, dense_output=True)
106 
107     one_alpha = np.array_equal(alpha, len(alpha) * [alpha[0]])
108 
109     if one_alpha:
110         A.flat[::n_features + 1] += alpha[0]
111         return linalg.solve(A, Xy, sym_pos=True,
112                             overwrite_a=True).T
113     else:
114         coefs = np.empty([n_targets, n_features], dtype=X.dtype)
115         for coef, target, current_alpha in zip(coefs, Xy.T, alpha):
116             A.flat[::n_features + 1] += current_alpha
117             coef[:] = linalg.solve(A, target, sym_pos=True,
118                                    overwrite_a=False).ravel()
119             A.flat[::n_features + 1] -= current_alpha
120         return coefs

123 def _solve_cholesky_kernel(K, y, alpha, sample_weight=None, copy=False):
124     # dual_coef = inv(X X^t + alpha*Id) y
125     n_samples = K.shape[0]
126     n_targets = y.shape[1]
127 
128     if copy:
129         K = K.copy()
130 
131     alpha = np.atleast_1d(alpha)
132     one_alpha = (alpha == alpha[0]).all()
133     has_sw = isinstance(sample_weight, np.ndarray) \
134         or sample_weight not in [1.0, None]
135 
136     if has_sw:
137         # Unlike other solvers, we need to support sample_weight directly
138         # because K might be a pre-computed kernel.
139         sw = np.sqrt(np.atleast_1d(sample_weight))
140         y = y * sw[:, np.newaxis]
141         K *= np.outer(sw, sw)
142 
143     if one_alpha:
144         # Only one penalty, we can solve multi-target problems in one time.
145         K.flat[::n_samples + 1] += alpha[0]
146 
147         try:
148             # Note: we must use overwrite_a=False in order to be able to
149             #       use the fall-back solution below in case a LinAlgError
150             #       is raised
151             dual_coef = linalg.solve(K, y, sym_pos=True,
152                                      overwrite_a=False)
153         except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
154             warnings.warn("Singular matrix in solving dual problem. Using "
155                           "least-squares solution instead.")
156             dual_coef = linalg.lstsq(K, y)[0]
157 
158         # K is expensive to compute and store in memory so change it back in
159         # case it was user-given.
160         K.flat[::n_samples + 1] -= alpha[0]
161 
162         if has_sw:
163             dual_coef *= sw[:, np.newaxis]
164 
165         return dual_coef
166     else:
167         # One penalty per target. We need to solve each target separately.
168         dual_coefs = np.empty([n_targets, n_samples], K.dtype)
169 
170         for dual_coef, target, current_alpha in zip(dual_coefs, y.T, alpha):
171             K.flat[::n_samples + 1] += current_alpha
172 
173             dual_coef[:] = linalg.solve(K, target, sym_pos=True,
174                                         overwrite_a=False).ravel()
175 
176             K.flat[::n_samples + 1] -= current_alpha
177 
178         if has_sw:
179             dual_coefs *= sw[np.newaxis, :]
180 
181         return dual_coefs.T

184 def _solve_svd(X, y, alpha):
185     U, s, Vt = linalg.svd(X, full_matrices=False)
186     idx = s > 1e-15  # same default value as scipy.linalg.pinv
187     s_nnz = s[idx][:, np.newaxis]
188     UTy = np.dot(U.T, y)
189     d = np.zeros((s.size, alpha.size), dtype=X.dtype)
190     d[idx] = s_nnz / (s_nnz ** 2 + alpha)
191     d_UT_y = d * UTy
192     return np.dot(Vt.T, d_UT_y).T
