655 def export_graphviz(decision_tree, out_file=None, max_depth=None,
656                     feature_names=None, class_names=None, label='all',
657                     filled=False, leaves_parallel=False, impurity=True,
658                     node_ids=False, proportion=False, rotate=False,
659                     rounded=False, special_characters=False, precision=3):
660     """Export a decision tree in DOT format.
661 
662     This function generates a GraphViz representation of the decision tree,
663     which is then written into `out_file`. Once exported, graphical renderings
664     can be generated using, for example::
665 
666         $ dot -Tps tree.dot -o tree.ps      (PostScript format)
667         $ dot -Tpng tree.dot -o tree.png    (PNG format)
668 
669     The sample counts that are shown are weighted with any sample_weights that
670     might be present.
671 
672     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <tree>`.
673 
674     Parameters
675     ----------
676     decision_tree : decision tree classifier
677         The decision tree to be exported to GraphViz.
678 
679     out_file : file object or string, optional (default=None)
680         Handle or name of the output file. If ``None``, the result is
681         returned as a string.
682 
683         .. versionchanged:: 0.20
684             Default of out_file changed from "tree.dot" to None.
685 
686     max_depth : int, optional (default=None)
687         The maximum depth of the representation. If None, the tree is fully
688         generated.
689 
690     feature_names : list of strings, optional (default=None)
691         Names of each of the features.
692 
693     class_names : list of strings, bool or None, optional (default=None)
694         Names of each of the target classes in ascending numerical order.
695         Only relevant for classification and not supported for multi-output.
696         If ``True``, shows a symbolic representation of the class name.
697 
698     label : {'all', 'root', 'none'}, optional (default='all')
699         Whether to show informative labels for impurity, etc.
700         Options include 'all' to show at every node, 'root' to show only at
701         the top root node, or 'none' to not show at any node.
702 
703     filled : bool, optional (default=False)
704         When set to ``True``, paint nodes to indicate majority class for
705         classification, extremity of values for regression, or purity of node
706         for multi-output.
707 
708     leaves_parallel : bool, optional (default=False)
709         When set to ``True``, draw all leaf nodes at the bottom of the tree.
710 
711     impurity : bool, optional (default=True)
712         When set to ``True``, show the impurity at each node.
713 
714     node_ids : bool, optional (default=False)
715         When set to ``True``, show the ID number on each node.
716 
717     proportion : bool, optional (default=False)
718         When set to ``True``, change the display of 'values' and/or 'samples'
719         to be proportions and percentages respectively.
720 
721     rotate : bool, optional (default=False)
722         When set to ``True``, orient tree left to right rather than top-down.
723 
724     rounded : bool, optional (default=False)
725         When set to ``True``, draw node boxes with rounded corners and use
726         Helvetica fonts instead of Times-Roman.
727 
728     special_characters : bool, optional (default=False)
729         When set to ``False``, ignore special characters for PostScript
730         compatibility.
731 
732     precision : int, optional (default=3)
733         Number of digits of precision for floating point in the values of
734         impurity, threshold and value attributes of each node.
735 
736     Returns
737     -------
738     dot_data : string
739         String representation of the input tree in GraphViz dot format.
740         Only returned if ``out_file`` is None.
741 
742         .. versionadded:: 0.18
743 
744     Examples
745     --------
746     >>> from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
747     >>> from sklearn import tree
748 
749     >>> clf = tree.DecisionTreeClassifier()
750     >>> iris = load_iris()
751 
752     >>> clf = clf.fit(iris.data, iris.target)
753     >>> tree.export_graphviz(clf)
754     'digraph Tree {...
755     """
756 
757     check_is_fitted(decision_tree, 'tree_')
758     own_file = False
759     return_string = False
760     try:
761         if isinstance(out_file, str):
762             out_file = open(out_file, "w", encoding="utf-8")
763             own_file = True
764 
765         if out_file is None:
766             return_string = True

369             duration = time() - fit_start_time
370             n_total_leaves = sum(
371                 predictor.get_n_leaf_nodes()
372                 for predictors_at_ith_iteration in self._predictors
373                 for predictor in predictors_at_ith_iteration
374             )
375             n_predictors = sum(
376                 len(predictors_at_ith_iteration)
377                 for predictors_at_ith_iteration in self._predictors)
378             print("Fit {} trees in {:.3f} s, ({} total leaves)".format(
379                 n_predictors, duration, n_total_leaves))
380             print("{:<32} {:.3f}s".format('Time spent computing histograms:',
381                                           acc_compute_hist_time))
382             print("{:<32} {:.3f}s".format('Time spent finding best splits:',
383                                           acc_find_split_time))
384             print("{:<32} {:.3f}s".format('Time spent applying splits:',
385                                           acc_apply_split_time))
386             print("{:<32} {:.3f}s".format('Time spent predicting:',
387                                           acc_prediction_time))
388 
389         self.train_score_ = np.asarray(self.train_score_)
390         self.validation_score_ = np.asarray(self.validation_score_)
391         del self._in_fit  # hard delete so we're sure it can't be used anymore
392         return self
393 
394     def _is_fitted(self):
395         return len(getattr(self, '_predictors', [])) > 0
396 
397     def _clear_state(self):
398         """Clear the state of the gradient boosting model."""
399         for var in ('train_score_', 'validation_score_', '_rng'):
400             if hasattr(self, var):
401                 delattr(self, var)
402 
403     def _get_small_trainset(self, X_binned_train, y_train, seed):
404         """Compute the indices of the subsample set and return this set.
405 
406         For efficiency, we need to subsample the training set to compute scores
407         with scorers.
408         """
409         subsample_size = 10000
410         if X_binned_train.shape[0] > subsample_size:
411             indices = np.arange(X_binned_train.shape[0])
412             stratify = y_train if is_classifier(self) else None
413             indices = resample(indices, n_samples=subsample_size,
414                                replace=False, random_state=seed,
415                                stratify=stratify)
416             X_binned_small_train = X_binned_train[indices]
417             y_small_train = y_train[indices]
418             X_binned_small_train = np.ascontiguousarray(X_binned_small_train)
419             return X_binned_small_train, y_small_train
420         else:
421             return X_binned_train, y_train
422 
423     def _check_early_stopping_scorer(self, X_binned_small_train, y_small_train,
424                                      X_binned_val, y_val):
425         """Check if fitting should be early-stopped based on scorer.
426 
427         Scores are computed on validation data or on training data.
428         """
429         self.train_score_.append(
430             self.scorer_(self, X_binned_small_train, y_small_train)
431         )
432 
433         if self._use_validation_data:
434             self.validation_score_.append(
435                 self.scorer_(self, X_binned_val, y_val)
436             )
437             return self._should_stop(self.validation_score_)
438         else:
439             return self._should_stop(self.train_score_)
440 
441     def _check_early_stopping_loss(self,
442                                    raw_predictions,
443                                    y_train,
444                                    raw_predictions_val,
445                                    y_val):
446         """Check if fitting should be early-stopped based on loss.
447 
448         Scores are computed on validation data or on training data.
449         """
450 
451         self.train_score_.append(
452             -self.loss_(y_train, raw_predictions)
453         )
454 
455         if self._use_validation_data:
456             self.validation_score_.append(
457                 -self.loss_(y_val, raw_predictions_val)
458             )
459             return self._should_stop(self.validation_score_)
460         else:
461             return self._should_stop(self.train_score_)
462 
463     def _should_stop(self, scores):
464         """
465         Return True (do early stopping) if the last n scores aren't better
466         than the (n-1)th-to-last score, up to some tolerance.
467         """
468         reference_position = self.n_iter_no_change + 1
469         if len(scores) < reference_position:
470             return False
471 
472         # A higher score is always better. Higher tol means that it will be
473         # harder for subsequent iteration to be considered an improvement upon
474         # the reference score, and therefore it is more likely to early stop
475         # because of the lack of significant improvement.
476         tol = 0 if self.tol is None else self.tol
477         reference_score = scores[-reference_position] + tol
478         recent_scores = scores[-reference_position + 1:]
479         recent_improvements = [score > reference_score
480                                for score in recent_scores]
481         return not any(recent_improvements)
482 
483     def _bin_data(self, X, rng, is_training_data):
484         """Bin data X.
485 
486         If is_training_data, then set the bin_mapper_ attribute.
487         Else, the binned data is converted to a C-contiguous array.
488         """
489 
490         description = 'training' if is_training_data else 'validation'
491         if self.verbose:
492             print("Binning {:.3f} GB of {} data: ".format(
493                 X.nbytes / 1e9, description), end="", flush=True)
494         tic = time()
495         if is_training_data:
496             X_binned = self.bin_mapper_.fit_transform(X)  # F-aligned array
497         else:
498             X_binned = self.bin_mapper_.transform(X)  # F-aligned array
499             # We convert the array to C-contiguous since predicting is faster
500             # with this layout (training is faster on F-arrays though)
501             X_binned = np.ascontiguousarray(X_binned)
502         toc = time()
503         if self.verbose:
504             duration = toc - tic
505             print("{:.3f} s".format(duration))
506 
507         return X_binned
508 
509     def _print_iteration_stats(self, iteration_start_time):
510         """Print info about the current fitting iteration."""
511         log_msg = ''
512 
513         predictors_of_ith_iteration = [
514             predictors_list for predictors_list in self._predictors[-1]
515             if predictors_list
516         ]
517         n_trees = len(predictors_of_ith_iteration)
518         max_depth = max(predictor.get_max_depth()
519                         for predictor in predictors_of_ith_iteration)
520         n_leaves = sum(predictor.get_n_leaf_nodes()
521                        for predictor in predictors_of_ith_iteration)
522 
523         if n_trees == 1:
524             log_msg += ("{} tree, {} leaves, ".format(n_trees, n_leaves))
525         else:
526             log_msg += ("{} trees, {} leaves ".format(n_trees, n_leaves))
527             log_msg += ("({} on avg), ".format(int(n_leaves / n_trees)))
528 
529         log_msg += "max depth = {}, ".format(max_depth)
530 
531         if self.do_early_stopping_:
532             if self.scoring == 'loss':
533                 factor = -1  # score_ arrays contain the negative loss
534                 name = 'loss'
535             else:
536                 factor = 1
537                 name = 'score'
538             log_msg += "train {}: {:.5f}, ".format(name, factor *
539                                                    self.train_score_[-1])
540             if self._use_validation_data:
541                 log_msg += "val {}: {:.5f}, ".format(
542                     name, factor * self.validation_score_[-1])
543 
544         iteration_time = time() - iteration_start_time
545         log_msg += "in {:0.3f}s".format(iteration_time)
546 
547         print(log_msg)
548 
549     def _raw_predict(self, X):
550         """Return the sum of the leaves values over all predictors.
551 
552         Parameters
553         ----------
554         X : array-like, shape=(n_samples, n_features)
555             The input samples.
556 
557         Returns
558         -------
559         raw_predictions : array, shape (n_samples * n_trees_per_iteration,)
560             The raw predicted values.
561         """
562         X = check_array(X, dtype=[X_DTYPE, X_BINNED_DTYPE],
563                         force_all_finite=False)
564         check_is_fitted(self)
565         if X.shape[1] != self.n_features_:
566             raise ValueError(
567                 'X has {} features but this estimator was trained with '
568                 '{} features.'.format(X.shape[1], self.n_features_)
569             )
570         is_binned = getattr(self, '_in_fit', False)
571         n_samples = X.shape[0]
572         raw_predictions = np.zeros(
573             shape=(self.n_trees_per_iteration_, n_samples),
574             dtype=self._baseline_prediction.dtype
575         )
576         raw_predictions += self._baseline_prediction
577         for predictors_of_ith_iteration in self._predictors:
578             for k, predictor in enumerate(predictors_of_ith_iteration):
579                 if is_binned:
580                     predict = partial(
581                         predictor.predict_binned,
582                         missing_values_bin_idx=self.bin_mapper_.missing_values_bin_idx_  # noqa
583                     )
584                 else:
585                     predict = predictor.predict
586                 raw_predictions[k, :] += predict(X)
587 
588         return raw_predictions
589 
590     def _compute_partial_dependence_recursion(self, grid, target_features):
591         """Fast partial dependence computation.
592 
593         Parameters
594         ----------
595         grid : ndarray, shape (n_samples, n_target_features)
596             The grid points on which the partial dependence should be
597             evaluated.
598         target_features : ndarray, shape (n_target_features)
599             The set of target features for which the partial dependence
600             should be evaluated.
601 
602         Returns
603         -------
604         averaged_predictions : ndarray, shape \
605                 (n_trees_per_iteration, n_samples)
606             The value of the partial dependence function on each grid point.
607         """
608         grid = np.asarray(grid, dtype=X_DTYPE, order='C')
609         averaged_predictions = np.zeros(
610             (self.n_trees_per_iteration_, grid.shape[0]), dtype=Y_DTYPE)
611 
612         for predictors_of_ith_iteration in self._predictors:
613             for k, predictor in enumerate(predictors_of_ith_iteration):
614                 predictor.compute_partial_dependence(grid, target_features,
615                                                      averaged_predictions[k])
616         # Note that the learning rate is already accounted for in the leaves
617         # values.
618 
619         return averaged_predictions
620 
621     def _more_tags(self):
622         return {'allow_nan': True}
623 
624     @abstractmethod
625     def _get_loss(self):
626         pass
627 
628     @abstractmethod
629     def _encode_y(self, y=None):
630         pass
631 
632     @property
633     def n_iter_(self):
634         check_is_fitted(self)
635         return len(self._predictors)

638 class HistGradientBoostingRegressor(BaseHistGradientBoosting, RegressorMixin):
639     """Histogram-based Gradient Boosting Regression Tree.
640 
641     This estimator is much faster than
642     :class:`GradientBoostingRegressor<sklearn.ensemble.GradientBoostingRegressor>`
643     for big datasets (n_samples >= 10 000).
644 
645     This estimator has native support for missing values (NaNs). During
646     training, the tree grower learns at each split point whether samples
647     with missing values should go to the left or right child, based on the
648     potential gain. When predicting, samples with missing values are
649     assigned to the left or right child consequently. If no missing values
650     were encountered for a given feature during training, then samples with
651     missing values are mapped to whichever child has the most samples.
652 
653     This implementation is inspired by
654     `LightGBM <https://github.com/Microsoft/LightGBM>`_.
655 
656     .. note::
657 
658       This estimator is still **experimental** for now: the predictions
659       and the API might change without any deprecation cycle. To use it,
660       you need to explicitly import ``enable_hist_gradient_boosting``::
661 
662         >>> # explicitly require this experimental feature
663         >>> from sklearn.experimental import enable_hist_gradient_boosting  # noqa
664         >>> # now you can import normally from ensemble
665         >>> from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier
666 
667     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <histogram_based_gradient_boosting>`.
668 
669     Parameters
670     ----------
671     loss : {'least_squares'}, optional (default='least_squares')
672         The loss function to use in the boosting process. Note that the
673         "least squares" loss actually implements an "half least squares loss"
674         to simplify the computation of the gradient.
675     learning_rate : float, optional (default=0.1)
676         The learning rate, also known as *shrinkage*. This is used as a
677         multiplicative factor for the leaves values. Use ``1`` for no
678         shrinkage.
679     max_iter : int, optional (default=100)
680         The maximum number of iterations of the boosting process, i.e. the
681         maximum number of trees.
682     max_leaf_nodes : int or None, optional (default=31)
683         The maximum number of leaves for each tree. Must be strictly greater
684         than 1. If None, there is no maximum limit.
685     max_depth : int or None, optional (default=None)
686         The maximum depth of each tree. The depth of a tree is the number of
687         nodes to go from the root to the deepest leaf. Must be strictly greater
688         than 1. Depth isn't constrained by default.
689     min_samples_leaf : int, optional (default=20)
690         The minimum number of samples per leaf. For small datasets with less
691         than a few hundred samples, it is recommended to lower this value
692         since only very shallow trees would be built.
693     l2_regularization : float, optional (default=0)
694         The L2 regularization parameter. Use ``0`` for no regularization
695         (default).
696     max_bins : int, optional (default=255)
697         The maximum number of bins to use for non-missing values. Before
698         training, each feature of the input array `X` is binned into
699         integer-valued bins, which allows for a much faster training stage.
700         Features with a small number of unique values may use less than
701         ``max_bins`` bins. In addition to the ``max_bins`` bins, one more bin
702         is always reserved for missing values. Must be no larger than 255.
703     warm_start : bool, optional (default=False)
704         When set to ``True``, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit
705         and add more estimators to the ensemble. For results to be valid, the
706         estimator should be re-trained on the same data only.
707         See :term:`the Glossary <warm_start>`.
708     scoring : str or callable or None, optional (default=None)
709         Scoring parameter to use for early stopping. It can be a single
710         string (see :ref:`scoring_parameter`) or a callable (see
711         :ref:`scoring`). If None, the estimator's default scorer is used. If
712         ``scoring='loss'``, early stopping is checked w.r.t the loss value.
713         Only used if ``n_iter_no_change`` is not None.
714     validation_fraction : int or float or None, optional (default=0.1)
715         Proportion (or absolute size) of training data to set aside as
716         validation data for early stopping. If None, early stopping is done on
717         the training data. Only used if ``n_iter_no_change`` is not None.
718     n_iter_no_change : int or None, optional (default=None)
719         Used to determine when to "early stop". The fitting process is
720         stopped when none of the last ``n_iter_no_change`` scores are better
721         than the ``n_iter_no_change - 1`` -th-to-last one, up to some
722         tolerance. If None or 0, no early-stopping is done.
723     tol : float or None, optional (default=1e-7)
724         The absolute tolerance to use when comparing scores during early
725         stopping. The higher the tolerance, the more likely we are to early
726         stop: higher tolerance means that it will be harder for subsequent
727         iterations to be considered an improvement upon the reference score.
728     verbose: int, optional (default=0)
729         The verbosity level. If not zero, print some information about the
730         fitting process.
731     random_state : int, np.random.RandomStateInstance or None, \
732         optional (default=None)
733         Pseudo-random number generator to control the subsampling in the
734         binning process, and the train/validation data split if early stopping
735         is enabled. See :term:`random_state`.
736 
737     Attributes
738     ----------
739     n_iter_ : int
740         The number of iterations as selected by early stopping (if
741         n_iter_no_change is not None). Otherwise it corresponds to max_iter.
742     n_trees_per_iteration_ : int
743         The number of tree that are built at each iteration. For regressors,
744         this is always 1.
745     train_score_ : ndarray, shape (n_iter_ + 1,)
746         The scores at each iteration on the training data. The first entry
747         is the score of the ensemble before the first iteration. Scores are
748         computed according to the ``scoring`` parameter. If ``scoring`` is
749         not 'loss', scores are computed on a subset of at most 10 000
750         samples. Empty if no early stopping.
751     validation_score_ : ndarray, shape (n_iter_ + 1,)
752         The scores at each iteration on the held-out validation data. The
753         first entry is the score of the ensemble before the first iteration.
754         Scores are computed according to the ``scoring`` parameter. Empty if
755         no early stopping or if ``validation_fraction`` is None.
756 
757     Examples
758     --------
759     >>> # To use this experimental feature, we need to explicitly ask for it:
760     >>> from sklearn.experimental import enable_hist_gradient_boosting  # noqa
761     >>> from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingRegressor
762     >>> from sklearn.datasets import load_boston
763     >>> X, y = load_boston(return_X_y=True)
764     >>> est = HistGradientBoostingRegressor().fit(X, y)
765     >>> est.score(X, y)
766     0.98...
767     """
768 
769     _VALID_LOSSES = ('least_squares',)
770 
771     def __init__(self, loss='least_squares', learning_rate=0.1,
772                  max_iter=100, max_leaf_nodes=31, max_depth=None,
773                  min_samples_leaf=20, l2_regularization=0., max_bins=255,
774                  warm_start=False, scoring=None, validation_fraction=0.1,
775                  n_iter_no_change=None, tol=1e-7, verbose=0,
776                  random_state=None):
777         super(HistGradientBoostingRegressor, self).__init__(
778             loss=loss, learning_rate=learning_rate, max_iter=max_iter,
779             max_leaf_nodes=max_leaf_nodes, max_depth=max_depth,
780             min_samples_leaf=min_samples_leaf,
781             l2_regularization=l2_regularization, max_bins=max_bins,
782             warm_start=warm_start, scoring=scoring,
783             validation_fraction=validation_fraction,
784             n_iter_no_change=n_iter_no_change, tol=tol, verbose=verbose,
785             random_state=random_state)
786 
787     def predict(self, X):
788         """Predict values for X.
789 
790         Parameters
791         ----------
792         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
793             The input samples.
794 
795         Returns
796         -------
797         y : ndarray, shape (n_samples,)
798             The predicted values.
799         """
800         # Return raw predictions after converting shape
801         # (n_samples, 1) to (n_samples,)
802         return self._raw_predict(X).ravel()
803 
804     def _encode_y(self, y):
805         # Just convert y to the expected dtype
806         self.n_trees_per_iteration_ = 1
807         y = y.astype(Y_DTYPE, copy=False)
808         return y
809 
810     def _get_loss(self):
811         return _LOSSES[self.loss]()
812

25 def _one_vs_one_coef(dual_coef, n_support, support_vectors):
26     """Generate primal coefficients from dual coefficients
27     for the one-vs-one multi class LibSVM in the case
28     of a linear kernel."""
29 
30     # get 1vs1 weights for all n*(n-1) classifiers.
31     # this is somewhat messy.
32     # shape of dual_coef_ is nSV * (n_classes -1)
33     # see docs for details
34     n_class = dual_coef.shape[0] + 1
35 
36     # XXX we could do preallocation of coef but
37     # would have to take care in the sparse case
38     coef = []
39     sv_locs = np.cumsum(np.hstack([[0], n_support]))
40     for class1 in range(n_class):
41         # SVs for class1:
42         sv1 = support_vectors[sv_locs[class1]:sv_locs[class1 + 1], :]
43         for class2 in range(class1 + 1, n_class):
44             # SVs for class1:
45             sv2 = support_vectors[sv_locs[class2]:sv_locs[class2 + 1], :]
46 
47             # dual coef for class1 SVs:
48             alpha1 = dual_coef[class2 - 1, sv_locs[class1]:sv_locs[class1 + 1]]
49             # dual coef for class2 SVs:
50             alpha2 = dual_coef[class1, sv_locs[class2]:sv_locs[class2 + 1]]
51             # build weight for class1 vs class2
52 
53             coef.append(safe_sparse_dot(alpha1, sv1)
54                         + safe_sparse_dot(alpha2, sv2))
55     return coef

242 
243         libsvm.set_verbosity_wrap(self.verbose)
244 
245         # we don't pass **self.get_params() to allow subclasses to
246         # add other parameters to __init__
247         self.support_, self.support_vectors_, self._n_support, \
248             self.dual_coef_, self.intercept_, self.probA_, \
249             self.probB_, self.fit_status_ = libsvm.fit(
250                 X, y,
251                 svm_type=solver_type, sample_weight=sample_weight,
252                 class_weight=self.class_weight_, kernel=kernel, C=self.C,
253                 nu=self.nu, probability=self.probability, degree=self.degree,
254                 shrinking=self.shrinking, tol=self.tol,
255                 cache_size=self.cache_size, coef0=self.coef0,
256                 gamma=self._gamma, epsilon=self.epsilon,
257                 max_iter=self.max_iter, random_seed=random_seed)
258 
259         self._warn_from_fit_status()
260 
261     def _sparse_fit(self, X, y, sample_weight, solver_type, kernel,
262                     random_seed):
263         X.data = np.asarray(X.data, dtype=np.float64, order='C')
264         X.sort_indices()
265 
266         kernel_type = self._sparse_kernels.index(kernel)
267 
268         libsvm_sparse.set_verbosity_wrap(self.verbose)
269 
270         self.support_, self.support_vectors_, dual_coef_data, \
271             self.intercept_, self._n_support, \
272             self.probA_, self.probB_, self.fit_status_ = \
273             libsvm_sparse.libsvm_sparse_train(
274                 X.shape[1], X.data, X.indices, X.indptr, y, solver_type,
275                 kernel_type, self.degree, self._gamma, self.coef0, self.tol,
276                 self.C, self.class_weight_,
277                 sample_weight, self.nu, self.cache_size, self.epsilon,
278                 int(self.shrinking), int(self.probability), self.max_iter,
279                 random_seed)
280 
281         self._warn_from_fit_status()
282 
283         if hasattr(self, "classes_"):
284             n_class = len(self.classes_) - 1
285         else:  # regression
286             n_class = 1
287         n_SV = self.support_vectors_.shape[0]
288 
289         dual_coef_indices = np.tile(np.arange(n_SV), n_class)
290         dual_coef_indptr = np.arange(0, dual_coef_indices.size + 1,
291                                      dual_coef_indices.size / n_class)
292         self.dual_coef_ = sp.csr_matrix(
293             (dual_coef_data, dual_coef_indices, dual_coef_indptr),
294             (n_class, n_SV))
295 
296     def predict(self, X):
297         """Perform regression on samples in X.
298 
299         For an one-class model, +1 (inlier) or -1 (outlier) is returned.
300 
301         Parameters
302         ----------
303         X : {array-like, sparse matrix}, shape (n_samples, n_features)
304             For kernel="precomputed", the expected shape of X is
305             (n_samples_test, n_samples_train).
306 
307         Returns
308         -------
309         y_pred : array, shape (n_samples,)
310         """
311         X = self._validate_for_predict(X)
312         predict = self._sparse_predict if self._sparse else self._dense_predict
313         return predict(X)
314 
315     def _dense_predict(self, X):
316         X = self._compute_kernel(X)
317         if X.ndim == 1:
318             X = check_array(X, order='C', accept_large_sparse=False)
319 
320         kernel = self.kernel
321         if callable(self.kernel):
322             kernel = 'precomputed'
323             if X.shape[1] != self.shape_fit_[0]:
324                 raise ValueError("X.shape[1] = %d should be equal to %d, "
325                                  "the number of samples at training time" %
326                                  (X.shape[1], self.shape_fit_[0]))
327 
328         svm_type = LIBSVM_IMPL.index(self._impl)
329 
330         return libsvm.predict(
331             X, self.support_, self.support_vectors_, self._n_support,
332             self._dual_coef_, self._intercept_,
333             self.probA_, self.probB_, svm_type=svm_type, kernel=kernel,
334             degree=self.degree, coef0=self.coef0, gamma=self._gamma,
335             cache_size=self.cache_size)
336 
337     def _sparse_predict(self, X):
338         # Precondition: X is a csr_matrix of dtype np.float64.
339         kernel = self.kernel
340         if callable(kernel):
341             kernel = 'precomputed'
342 
343         kernel_type = self._sparse_kernels.index(kernel)
344 
345         C = 0.0  # C is not useful here
346 
347         return libsvm_sparse.libsvm_sparse_predict(
348             X.data, X.indices, X.indptr,
349             self.support_vectors_.data,
350             self.support_vectors_.indices,
351             self.support_vectors_.indptr,
352             self._dual_coef_.data, self._intercept_,
353             LIBSVM_IMPL.index(self._impl), kernel_type,
354             self.degree, self._gamma, self.coef0, self.tol,
355             C, self.class_weight_,
356             self.nu, self.epsilon, self.shrinking,
357             self.probability, self._n_support,
358             self.probA_, self.probB_)
359 
360     def _compute_kernel(self, X):
361         """Return the data transformed by a callable kernel"""
362         if callable(self.kernel):
363             # in the case of precomputed kernel given as a function, we
364             # have to compute explicitly the kernel matrix
365             kernel = self.kernel(X, self.__Xfit)
366             if sp.issparse(kernel):
367                 kernel = kernel.toarray()
368             X = np.asarray(kernel, dtype=np.float64, order='C')
369         return X
370 
371     def _decision_function(self, X):
372         """Evaluates the decision function for the samples in X.
373 
374         Parameters
375         ----------
376         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
377 
378         Returns
379         -------
380         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_class * (n_class-1) / 2)
381             Returns the decision function of the sample for each class
382             in the model.
383         """
384         # NOTE: _validate_for_predict contains check for is_fitted
385         # hence must be placed before any other attributes are used.
386         X = self._validate_for_predict(X)
387         X = self._compute_kernel(X)
388 
389         if self._sparse:
390             dec_func = self._sparse_decision_function(X)
391         else:
392             dec_func = self._dense_decision_function(X)
393 
394         # In binary case, we need to flip the sign of coef, intercept and
395         # decision function.
396         if self._impl in ['c_svc', 'nu_svc'] and len(self.classes_) == 2:
397             return -dec_func.ravel()
398 
399         return dec_func
400 
401     def _dense_decision_function(self, X):
402         X = check_array(X, dtype=np.float64, order="C",
403                         accept_large_sparse=False)
404 
405         kernel = self.kernel
406         if callable(kernel):
407             kernel = 'precomputed'
408 
409         return libsvm.decision_function(
410             X, self.support_, self.support_vectors_, self._n_support,
411             self._dual_coef_, self._intercept_,
412             self.probA_, self.probB_,
413             svm_type=LIBSVM_IMPL.index(self._impl),
414             kernel=kernel, degree=self.degree, cache_size=self.cache_size,
415             coef0=self.coef0, gamma=self._gamma)
416 
417     def _sparse_decision_function(self, X):
418         X.data = np.asarray(X.data, dtype=np.float64, order='C')
419 
420         kernel = self.kernel
421         if hasattr(kernel, '__call__'):
422             kernel = 'precomputed'
423 
424         kernel_type = self._sparse_kernels.index(kernel)
425 
426         return libsvm_sparse.libsvm_sparse_decision_function(
427             X.data, X.indices, X.indptr,
428             self.support_vectors_.data,
429             self.support_vectors_.indices,
430             self.support_vectors_.indptr,
431             self._dual_coef_.data, self._intercept_,
432             LIBSVM_IMPL.index(self._impl), kernel_type,
433             self.degree, self._gamma, self.coef0, self.tol,
434             self.C, self.class_weight_,
435             self.nu, self.epsilon, self.shrinking,
436             self.probability, self._n_support,
437             self.probA_, self.probB_)
438 
439     def _validate_for_predict(self, X):
440         check_is_fitted(self)
441 
442         X = check_array(X, accept_sparse='csr', dtype=np.float64, order="C",
443                         accept_large_sparse=False)
444         if self._sparse and not sp.isspmatrix(X):
445             X = sp.csr_matrix(X)
446         if self._sparse:
447             X.sort_indices()
448 
449         if sp.issparse(X) and not self._sparse and not callable(self.kernel):
450             raise ValueError(
451                 "cannot use sparse input in %r trained on dense data"
452                 % type(self).__name__)
453         n_samples, n_features = X.shape
454 
455         if self.kernel == "precomputed":
456             if X.shape[1] != self.shape_fit_[0]:
457                 raise ValueError("X.shape[1] = %d should be equal to %d, "
458                                  "the number of samples at training time" %
459                                  (X.shape[1], self.shape_fit_[0]))
460         elif n_features != self.shape_fit_[1]:
461             raise ValueError("X.shape[1] = %d should be equal to %d, "
462                              "the number of features at training time" %
463                              (n_features, self.shape_fit_[1]))
464         return X
465 
466     @property
467     def coef_(self):
468         if self.kernel != 'linear':
469             raise AttributeError('coef_ is only available when using a '
470                                  'linear kernel')
471 
472         coef = self._get_coef()
473 
474         # coef_ being a read-only property, it's better to mark the value as
475         # immutable to avoid hiding potential bugs for the unsuspecting user.
476         if sp.issparse(coef):
477             # sparse matrix do not have global flags
478             coef.data.flags.writeable = False
479         else:
480             # regular dense array
481             coef.flags.writeable = False
482         return coef
483 
484     def _get_coef(self):
485         return safe_sparse_dot(self._dual_coef_, self.support_vectors_)
486 
487     @property
488     def n_support_(self):
489         try:
490             check_is_fitted(self)
491         except NotFittedError:
492             raise AttributeError
493 
494         svm_type = LIBSVM_IMPL.index(self._impl)
495         if svm_type in (0, 1):
496             return self._n_support
497         else:
498             # SVR and OneClass
499             # _n_support has size 2, we make it size 1
500             return np.array([self._n_support[0]])

503 class BaseSVC(ClassifierMixin, BaseLibSVM, metaclass=ABCMeta):
504     """ABC for LibSVM-based classifiers."""
505     @abstractmethod
506     def __init__(self, kernel, degree, gamma, coef0, tol, C, nu,
507                  shrinking, probability, cache_size, class_weight, verbose,
508                  max_iter, decision_function_shape, random_state,
509                  break_ties):
510         self.decision_function_shape = decision_function_shape
511         self.break_ties = break_ties
512         super().__init__(
513             kernel=kernel, degree=degree, gamma=gamma,
514             coef0=coef0, tol=tol, C=C, nu=nu, epsilon=0., shrinking=shrinking,
515             probability=probability, cache_size=cache_size,
516             class_weight=class_weight, verbose=verbose, max_iter=max_iter,
517             random_state=random_state)
518 
519     def _validate_targets(self, y):
520         y_ = column_or_1d(y, warn=True)
521         check_classification_targets(y)
522         cls, y = np.unique(y_, return_inverse=True)
523         self.class_weight_ = compute_class_weight(self.class_weight, cls, y_)
524         if len(cls) < 2:
525             raise ValueError(
526                 "The number of classes has to be greater than one; got %d"
527                 " class" % len(cls))
528 
529         self.classes_ = cls
530 
531         return np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64, order='C')
532 
533     def decision_function(self, X):
534         """Evaluates the decision function for the samples in X.
535 
536         Parameters
537         ----------
538         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
539 
540         Returns
541         -------
542         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_classes * (n_classes-1) / 2)
543             Returns the decision function of the sample for each class
544             in the model.
545             If decision_function_shape='ovr', the shape is (n_samples,
546             n_classes).
547 
548         Notes
549         -----
550         If decision_function_shape='ovo', the function values are proportional
551         to the distance of the samples X to the separating hyperplane. If the
552         exact distances are required, divide the function values by the norm of
553         the weight vector (``coef_``). See also `this question
554         <https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/14876/
555         interpreting-distance-from-hyperplane-in-svm>`_ for further details.
556         If decision_function_shape='ovr', the decision function is a monotonic
557         transformation of ovo decision function.
558         """
559         dec = self._decision_function(X)
560         if self.decision_function_shape == 'ovr' and len(self.classes_) > 2:
561             return _ovr_decision_function(dec < 0, -dec, len(self.classes_))
562         return dec
563 
564     def predict(self, X):
565         """Perform classification on samples in X.
566 
567         For an one-class model, +1 or -1 is returned.
568 
569         Parameters
570         ----------
571         X : {array-like, sparse matrix}, shape (n_samples, n_features)
572             For kernel="precomputed", the expected shape of X is
573             [n_samples_test, n_samples_train]
574 
575         Returns
576         -------
577         y_pred : array, shape (n_samples,)
578             Class labels for samples in X.
579         """
580         check_is_fitted(self)
581         if self.break_ties and self.decision_function_shape == 'ovo':
582             raise ValueError("break_ties must be False when "
583                              "decision_function_shape is 'ovo'")
584 
585         if (self.break_ties
586                 and self.decision_function_shape == 'ovr'
587                 and len(self.classes_) > 2):
588             y = np.argmax(self.decision_function(X), axis=1)
589         else:
590             y = super().predict(X)
591         return self.classes_.take(np.asarray(y, dtype=np.intp))
592 
593     # Hacky way of getting predict_proba to raise an AttributeError when
594     # probability=False using properties. Do not use this in new code; when
595     # probabilities are not available depending on a setting, introduce two
596     # estimators.
597     def _check_proba(self):
598         if not self.probability:
599             raise AttributeError("predict_proba is not available when "
600                                  " probability=False")
601         if self._impl not in ('c_svc', 'nu_svc'):
602             raise AttributeError("predict_proba only implemented for SVC"
603                                  " and NuSVC")
604 
605     @property
606     def predict_proba(self):
607         """Compute probabilities of possible outcomes for samples in X.
608 
609         The model need to have probability information computed at training
610         time: fit with attribute `probability` set to True.
611 
612         Parameters
613         ----------
614         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
615             For kernel="precomputed", the expected shape of X is
616             [n_samples_test, n_samples_train]
617 
618         Returns
619         -------
620         T : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_classes)
621             Returns the probability of the sample for each class in
622             the model. The columns correspond to the classes in sorted
623             order, as they appear in the attribute :term:`classes_`.
624 
625         Notes
626         -----
627         The probability model is created using cross validation, so
628         the results can be slightly different than those obtained by
629         predict. Also, it will produce meaningless results on very small
630         datasets.
631         """
632         self._check_proba()
633         return self._predict_proba
634 
635     def _predict_proba(self, X):
636         X = self._validate_for_predict(X)
637         if self.probA_.size == 0 or self.probB_.size == 0:
638             raise NotFittedError("predict_proba is not available when fitted "
639                                  "with probability=False")
640         pred_proba = (self._sparse_predict_proba
641                       if self._sparse else self._dense_predict_proba)
642         return pred_proba(X)
643 
644     @property
645     def predict_log_proba(self):
646         """Compute log probabilities of possible outcomes for samples in X.
647 
648         The model need to have probability information computed at training
649         time: fit with attribute `probability` set to True.
650 
651         Parameters
652         ----------
653         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
654             For kernel="precomputed", the expected shape of X is
655             [n_samples_test, n_samples_train]
656 
657         Returns
658         -------
659         T : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_classes)
660             Returns the log-probabilities of the sample for each class in
661             the model. The columns correspond to the classes in sorted
662             order, as they appear in the attribute :term:`classes_`.
663 
664         Notes
665         -----
666         The probability model is created using cross validation, so
667         the results can be slightly different than those obtained by
668         predict. Also, it will produce meaningless results on very small
669         datasets.
670         """
671         self._check_proba()
672         return self._predict_log_proba
673 
674     def _predict_log_proba(self, X):
675         return np.log(self.predict_proba(X))
676 
677     def _dense_predict_proba(self, X):
678         X = self._compute_kernel(X)
679 
680         kernel = self.kernel
681         if callable(kernel):
682             kernel = 'precomputed'
683 
684         svm_type = LIBSVM_IMPL.index(self._impl)
685         pprob = libsvm.predict_proba(
686             X, self.support_, self.support_vectors_, self._n_support,
687             self._dual_coef_, self._intercept_,
688             self.probA_, self.probB_,
689             svm_type=svm_type, kernel=kernel, degree=self.degree,
690             cache_size=self.cache_size, coef0=self.coef0, gamma=self._gamma)
691 
692         return pprob
693 
694     def _sparse_predict_proba(self, X):
695         X.data = np.asarray(X.data, dtype=np.float64, order='C')
696 
697         kernel = self.kernel
698         if callable(kernel):
699             kernel = 'precomputed'
700 
701         kernel_type = self._sparse_kernels.index(kernel)
702 
703         return libsvm_sparse.libsvm_sparse_predict_proba(
704             X.data, X.indices, X.indptr,
705             self.support_vectors_.data,
706             self.support_vectors_.indices,
707             self.support_vectors_.indptr,
708             self._dual_coef_.data, self._intercept_,
709             LIBSVM_IMPL.index(self._impl), kernel_type,
710             self.degree, self._gamma, self.coef0, self.tol,
711             self.C, self.class_weight_,
712             self.nu, self.epsilon, self.shrinking,
713             self.probability, self._n_support,
714             self.probA_, self.probB_)
715 
716     def _get_coef(self):
717         if self.dual_coef_.shape[0] == 1:
718             # binary classifier
719             coef = safe_sparse_dot(self.dual_coef_, self.support_vectors_)
720         else:
721             # 1vs1 classifier
722             coef = _one_vs_one_coef(self.dual_coef_, self._n_support,
723                                     self.support_vectors_)
724             if sp.issparse(coef[0]):
725                 coef = sp.vstack(coef).tocsr()
726             else:
727                 coef = np.vstack(coef)
728 
729         return coef

732 def _get_liblinear_solver_type(multi_class, penalty, loss, dual):
733     """Find the liblinear magic number for the solver.
734 
735     This number depends on the values of the following attributes:
736       - multi_class
737       - penalty
738       - loss
739       - dual
740 
741     The same number is also internally used by LibLinear to determine
742     which solver to use.
743     """
744     # nested dicts containing level 1: available loss functions,
745     # level2: available penalties for the given loss function,
746     # level3: wether the dual solver is available for the specified
747     # combination of loss function and penalty
748     _solver_type_dict = {
749         'logistic_regression': {
750             'l1': {False: 6},
751             'l2': {False: 0, True: 7}},
752         'hinge': {
753             'l2': {True: 3}},
754         'squared_hinge': {
755             'l1': {False: 5},
756             'l2': {False: 2, True: 1}},
757         'epsilon_insensitive': {
758             'l2': {True: 13}},
759         'squared_epsilon_insensitive': {
760             'l2': {False: 11, True: 12}},
761         'crammer_singer': 4
762     }
763 
764     if multi_class == 'crammer_singer':
765         return _solver_type_dict[multi_class]
766     elif multi_class != 'ovr':
767         raise ValueError("`multi_class` must be one of `ovr`, "
768                          "`crammer_singer`, got %r" % multi_class)
769 
770     _solver_pen = _solver_type_dict.get(loss, None)
771     if _solver_pen is None:
772         error_string = ("loss='%s' is not supported" % loss)
773     else:
774         _solver_dual = _solver_pen.get(penalty, None)
775         if _solver_dual is None:
776             error_string = ("The combination of penalty='%s' "
777                             "and loss='%s' is not supported"
778                             % (penalty, loss))
779         else:
780             solver_num = _solver_dual.get(dual, None)
781             if solver_num is None:
782                 error_string = ("The combination of penalty='%s' and "
783                                 "loss='%s' are not supported when dual=%s"
784                                 % (penalty, loss, dual))
785             else:
786                 return solver_num
787     raise ValueError('Unsupported set of arguments: %s, '
788                      'Parameters: penalty=%r, loss=%r, dual=%r'
789                      % (error_string, penalty, loss, dual))
790 
791 
792 def _fit_liblinear(X, y, C, fit_intercept, intercept_scaling, class_weight,
793                    penalty, dual, verbose, max_iter, tol,
794                    random_state=None, multi_class='ovr',
795                    loss='logistic_regression', epsilon=0.1,
796                    sample_weight=None):
797     """Used by Logistic Regression (and CV) and LinearSVC/LinearSVR.
798 
799     Preprocessing is done in this function before supplying it to liblinear.
800 
801     Parameters
802     ----------
803     X : {array-like, sparse matrix}, shape (n_samples, n_features)
804         Training vector, where n_samples in the number of samples and
805         n_features is the number of features.
806 
807     y : array-like, shape (n_samples,)
808         Target vector relative to X
809 
810     C : float
811         Inverse of cross-validation parameter. Lower the C, the more
812         the penalization.
813 
814     fit_intercept : bool
815         Whether or not to fit the intercept, that is to add a intercept
816         term to the decision function.
817 
818     intercept_scaling : float
819         LibLinear internally penalizes the intercept and this term is subject
820         to regularization just like the other terms of the feature vector.
821         In order to avoid this, one should increase the intercept_scaling.
822         such that the feature vector becomes [x, intercept_scaling].
823 
824     class_weight : {dict, 'balanced'}, optional
825         Weights associated with classes in the form ``{class_label: weight}``.
826         If not given, all classes are supposed to have weight one. For
827         multi-output problems, a list of dicts can be provided in the same
828         order as the columns of y.
829 
830         The "balanced" mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust
831         weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data
832         as ``n_samples / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))``
833 
834     penalty : str, {'l1', 'l2'}
835         The norm of the penalty used in regularization.
836 
837     dual : bool
838         Dual or primal formulation,
839 
840     verbose : int
841         Set verbose to any positive number for verbosity.
842 
843     max_iter : int
844         Number of iterations.
845 
846     tol : float
847         Stopping condition.
848 
849     random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, optional (default=None)
850         The seed of the pseudo random number generator to use when shuffling
851         the data.  If int, random_state is the seed used by the random number
852         generator; If RandomState instance, random_state is the random number
853         generator; If None, the random number generator is the RandomState
854         instance used by `np.random`.
855 
856     multi_class : str, {'ovr', 'crammer_singer'}
857         `ovr` trains n_classes one-vs-rest classifiers, while `crammer_singer`
858         optimizes a joint objective over all classes.
859         While `crammer_singer` is interesting from an theoretical perspective
860         as it is consistent it is seldom used in practice and rarely leads to
861         better accuracy and is more expensive to compute.

221     See Also
222     --------
223     SimpleImputer : Univariate imputer for completing missing values
224         with simple strategies.
225     KNNImputer : Multivariate imputer that estimates missing features using
226         nearest samples.
227 
228     Notes
229     -----
230     To support imputation in inductive mode we store each feature's estimator
231     during the :meth:`fit` phase, and predict without refitting (in order)
232     during the :meth:`transform` phase.
233 
234     Features which contain all missing values at :meth:`fit` are discarded upon
235     :meth:`transform`.
236 
237     Using defaults, the imputer scales in :math:`\\mathcal{O}(knp^3\\min(n,p))`
238     where :math:`k` = `max_iter`, :math:`n` the number of samples and
239     :math:`p` the number of features. It thus becomes prohibitively costly when
240     the number of features increases. Setting
241     `n_nearest_features << n_features`, `skip_complete=True` or increasing `tol`
242     can help to reduce its computational cost.
243 
244     Depending on the nature of missing values, simple imputers can be
245     preferable in a prediction context.
246 
247     References
248     ----------
249     .. [1] `Stef van Buuren, Karin Groothuis-Oudshoorn (2011). "mice:
250         Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations in R". Journal of
251         Statistical Software 45: 1-67.
252         <https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v045i03>`_
253 
254     .. [2] `S. F. Buck, (1960). "A Method of Estimation of Missing Values in
255         Multivariate Data Suitable for use with an Electronic Computer".
256         Journal of the Royal Statistical Society 22(2): 302-306.
257         <https://www.jstor.org/stable/2984099>`_
258 
259     Examples
260     --------
261     >>> import numpy as np
262     >>> from sklearn.experimental import enable_iterative_imputer
263     >>> from sklearn.impute import IterativeImputer
264     >>> imp_mean = IterativeImputer(random_state=0)
265     >>> imp_mean.fit([[7, 2, 3], [4, np.nan, 6], [10, 5, 9]])
266     IterativeImputer(random_state=0)
267     >>> X = [[np.nan, 2, 3], [4, np.nan, 6], [10, np.nan, 9]]
268     >>> imp_mean.transform(X)
269     array([[ 6.9584...,  2.       ,  3.        ],
270            [ 4.       ,  2.6000...,  6.        ],
271            [10.       ,  4.9999...,  9.        ]])
272     """

332     def _impute_one_feature(
333         self,
334         X_filled,
335         mask_missing_values,
336         feat_idx,
337         neighbor_feat_idx,
338         estimator=None,
339         fit_mode=True,
340     ):
341         """Impute a single feature from the others provided.
342 
343         This function predicts the missing values of one of the features using
344         the current estimates of all the other features. The `estimator` must
345         support `return_std=True` in its `predict` method for this function
346         to work.
347 
348         Parameters
349         ----------
350         X_filled : ndarray
351             Input data with the most recent imputations.
352 
353         mask_missing_values : ndarray
354             Input data's missing indicator matrix.
355 
356         feat_idx : int
357             Index of the feature currently being imputed.
358 
359         neighbor_feat_idx : ndarray
360             Indices of the features to be used in imputing `feat_idx`.
361 
362         estimator : object
363             The estimator to use at this step of the round-robin imputation.
364             If `sample_posterior=True`, the estimator must support
365             `return_std` in its `predict` method.
366             If None, it will be cloned from self._estimator.
367 
368         fit_mode : boolean, default=True
369             Whether to fit and predict with the estimator or just predict.
370 
371         Returns
372         -------
373         X_filled : ndarray
374             Input data with `X_filled[missing_row_mask, feat_idx]` updated.
375 
376         estimator : estimator with sklearn API
377             The fitted estimator used to impute
378             `X_filled[missing_row_mask, feat_idx]`.
379         """
380         if estimator is None and fit_mode is False:
381             raise ValueError(
382                 "If fit_mode is False, then an already-fitted "
383                 "estimator should be passed in."
384             )
385 
386         if estimator is None:
387             estimator = clone(self._estimator)
388 
389         missing_row_mask = mask_missing_values[:, feat_idx]
390         if fit_mode:
391             X_train = _safe_indexing(
392                 _safe_indexing(X_filled, neighbor_feat_idx, axis=1),
393                 ~missing_row_mask,
394                 axis=0,
395             )
396             y_train = _safe_indexing(
397                 _safe_indexing(X_filled, feat_idx, axis=1),
398                 ~missing_row_mask,
399                 axis=0,
400             )
401             estimator.fit(X_train, y_train)
402 
403         # if no missing values, don't predict
404         if np.sum(missing_row_mask) == 0:
405             return X_filled, estimator
406 
407         # get posterior samples if there is at least one missing value
408         X_test = _safe_indexing(
409             _safe_indexing(X_filled, neighbor_feat_idx, axis=1),
410             missing_row_mask,
411             axis=0,
412         )
413         if self.sample_posterior:
414             mus, sigmas = estimator.predict(X_test, return_std=True)
415             imputed_values = np.zeros(mus.shape, dtype=X_filled.dtype)
416             # two types of problems: (1) non-positive sigmas
417             # (2) mus outside legal range of min_value and max_value
418             # (results in inf sample)
419             positive_sigmas = sigmas > 0
420             imputed_values[~positive_sigmas] = mus[~positive_sigmas]
421             mus_too_low = mus < self._min_value[feat_idx]
422             imputed_values[mus_too_low] = self._min_value[feat_idx]
423             mus_too_high = mus > self._max_value[feat_idx]
424             imputed_values[mus_too_high] = self._max_value[feat_idx]
425             # the rest can be sampled without statistical issues
426             inrange_mask = positive_sigmas & ~mus_too_low & ~mus_too_high
427             mus = mus[inrange_mask]
428             sigmas = sigmas[inrange_mask]
429             a = (self._min_value[feat_idx] - mus) / sigmas
430             b = (self._max_value[feat_idx] - mus) / sigmas
431 
432             truncated_normal = stats.truncnorm(a=a, b=b, loc=mus, scale=sigmas)
433             imputed_values[inrange_mask] = truncated_normal.rvs(
434                 random_state=self.random_state_
435             )
436         else:
437             imputed_values = estimator.predict(X_test)
438             imputed_values = np.clip(
439                 imputed_values, self._min_value[feat_idx], self._max_value[feat_idx]
440             )
441 
442         # update the feature
443         _safe_assign(
444             X_filled,
445             imputed_values,
446             row_indexer=missing_row_mask,
447             column_indexer=feat_idx,
448         )
449         return X_filled, estimator
450 
451     def _get_neighbor_feat_idx(self, n_features, feat_idx, abs_corr_mat):
452         """Get a list of other features to predict `feat_idx`.
453 
454         If `self.n_nearest_features` is less than or equal to the total
455         number of features, then use a probability proportional to the absolute
456         correlation between `feat_idx` and each other feature to randomly
457         choose a subsample of the other features (without replacement).
458 
459         Parameters
460         ----------
461         n_features : int
462             Number of features in `X`.
463 
464         feat_idx : int
465             Index of the feature currently being imputed.
466 
467         abs_corr_mat : ndarray, shape (n_features, n_features)
468             Absolute correlation matrix of `X`. The diagonal has been zeroed
469             out and each feature has been normalized to sum to 1. Can be None.
470 
471         Returns
472         -------
473         neighbor_feat_idx : array-like
474             The features to use to impute `feat_idx`.
475         """
476         if self.n_nearest_features is not None and self.n_nearest_features < n_features:
477             p = abs_corr_mat[:, feat_idx]
478             neighbor_feat_idx = self.random_state_.choice(
479                 np.arange(n_features), self.n_nearest_features, replace=False, p=p
480             )
481         else:
482             inds_left = np.arange(feat_idx)
483             inds_right = np.arange(feat_idx + 1, n_features)
484             neighbor_feat_idx = np.concatenate((inds_left, inds_right))
485         return neighbor_feat_idx
486 
487     def _get_ordered_idx(self, mask_missing_values):
488         """Decide in what order we will update the features.
489 
490         As a homage to the MICE R package, we will have 4 main options of
491         how to order the updates, and use a random order if anything else
492         is specified.
493 
494         Also, this function skips features which have no missing values.
495 
496         Parameters
497         ----------
498         mask_missing_values : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
499             Input data's missing indicator matrix, where `n_samples` is the
500             number of samples and `n_features` is the number of features.
501 
502         Returns
503         -------
504         ordered_idx : ndarray, shape (n_features,)
505             The order in which to impute the features.
506         """
507         frac_of_missing_values = mask_missing_values.mean(axis=0)
508         if self.skip_complete:
509             missing_values_idx = np.flatnonzero(frac_of_missing_values)
510         else:
511             missing_values_idx = np.arange(np.shape(frac_of_missing_values)[0])
512         if self.imputation_order == "roman":
513             ordered_idx = missing_values_idx
514         elif self.imputation_order == "arabic":
515             ordered_idx = missing_values_idx[::-1]
516         elif self.imputation_order == "ascending":
517             n = len(frac_of_missing_values) - len(missing_values_idx)
518             ordered_idx = np.argsort(frac_of_missing_values, kind="mergesort")[n:]
519         elif self.imputation_order == "descending":
520             n = len(frac_of_missing_values) - len(missing_values_idx)
521             ordered_idx = np.argsort(frac_of_missing_values, kind="mergesort")[n:][::-1]
522         elif self.imputation_order == "random":
523             ordered_idx = missing_values_idx
524             self.random_state_.shuffle(ordered_idx)
525         return ordered_idx
526 
527     def _get_abs_corr_mat(self, X_filled, tolerance=1e-6):
528         """Get absolute correlation matrix between features.
529 
530         Parameters
531         ----------
532         X_filled : ndarray, shape (n_samples, n_features)
533             Input data with the most recent imputations.
534 
535         tolerance : float, default=1e-6
536             `abs_corr_mat` can have nans, which will be replaced
537             with `tolerance`.
538 
539         Returns
540         -------
541         abs_corr_mat : ndarray, shape (n_features, n_features)
542             Absolute correlation matrix of `X` at the beginning of the
543             current round. The diagonal has been zeroed out and each feature's
544             absolute correlations with all others have been normalized to sum
545             to 1.
546         """
547         n_features = X_filled.shape[1]
548         if self.n_nearest_features is None or self.n_nearest_features >= n_features:
549             return None
550         with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
551             # if a feature in the neighborhood has only a single value
552             # (e.g., categorical feature), the std. dev. will be null and
553             # np.corrcoef will raise a warning due to a division by zero
554             abs_corr_mat = np.abs(np.corrcoef(X_filled.T))
555         # np.corrcoef is not defined for features with zero std
556         abs_corr_mat[np.isnan(abs_corr_mat)] = tolerance
557         # ensures exploration, i.e. at least some probability of sampling
558         np.clip(abs_corr_mat, tolerance, None, out=abs_corr_mat)
559         # features are not their own neighbors
560         np.fill_diagonal(abs_corr_mat, 0)
561         # needs to sum to 1 for np.random.choice sampling
562         abs_corr_mat = normalize(abs_corr_mat, norm="l1", axis=0, copy=False)
563         return abs_corr_mat
564 
565     def _initial_imputation(self, X, in_fit=False):
566         """Perform initial imputation for input `X`.
567 
568         Parameters
569         ----------
570         X : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_features)
571             Input data, where `n_samples` is the number of samples and
572             `n_features` is the number of features.
573 
574         in_fit : bool, default=False
575             Whether function is called in :meth:`fit`.
576 
577         Returns
578         -------
579         Xt : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_features)
580             Input data, where `n_samples` is the number of samples and
581             `n_features` is the number of features.
582 
583         X_filled : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_features)
584             Input data with the most recent imputations.
585 
586         mask_missing_values : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_features)
587             Input data's missing indicator matrix, where `n_samples` is the
588             number of samples and `n_features` is the number of features,
589             masked by non-missing features.
590 
591         X_missing_mask : ndarray, shape (n_samples, n_features)
592             Input data's mask matrix indicating missing datapoints, where
593             `n_samples` is the number of samples and `n_features` is the
594             number of features.
595         """
596         if is_scalar_nan(self.missing_values):
597             force_all_finite = "allow-nan"
598         else:
599             force_all_finite = True
600 
601         X = self._validate_data(
602             X,
603             dtype=FLOAT_DTYPES,
604             order="F",
605             reset=in_fit,
606             force_all_finite=force_all_finite,
607         )
608         _check_inputs_dtype(X, self.missing_values)
609 
610         X_missing_mask = _get_mask(X, self.missing_values)
611         mask_missing_values = X_missing_mask.copy()
612         if self.initial_imputer_ is None:
613             self.initial_imputer_ = SimpleImputer(
614                 missing_values=self.missing_values,
615                 strategy=self.initial_strategy,
616                 keep_empty_features=self.keep_empty_features,
617             )
618             X_filled = self.initial_imputer_.fit_transform(X)
619         else:
620             X_filled = self.initial_imputer_.transform(X)
621 
622         valid_mask = np.flatnonzero(
623             np.logical_not(np.isnan(self.initial_imputer_.statistics_))
624         )
625 
626         if not self.keep_empty_features:
627             # drop empty features
628             Xt = X[:, valid_mask]
629             mask_missing_values = mask_missing_values[:, valid_mask]
630         else:
631             # mark empty features as not missing and keep the original
632             # imputation
633             mask_missing_values[:, valid_mask] = True
634             Xt = X
635 
636         return Xt, X_filled, mask_missing_values, X_missing_mask

638     @staticmethod
639     def _validate_limit(limit, limit_type, n_features):
640         """Validate the limits (min/max) of the feature values.
641 
642         Converts scalar min/max limits to vectors of shape `(n_features,)`.
643 
644         Parameters
645         ----------
646         limit: scalar or array-like
647             The user-specified limit (i.e, min_value or max_value).
648         limit_type: {'max', 'min'}
649             Type of limit to validate.
650         n_features: int
651             Number of features in the dataset.
652 
653         Returns
654         -------
655         limit: ndarray, shape(n_features,)
656             Array of limits, one for each feature.
657         """
658         limit_bound = np.inf if limit_type == "max" else -np.inf
659         limit = limit_bound if limit is None else limit
660         if np.isscalar(limit):
661             limit = np.full(n_features, limit)
662         limit = check_array(limit, force_all_finite=False, copy=False, ensure_2d=False)
663         if not limit.shape[0] == n_features:
664             raise ValueError(
665                 f"'{limit_type}_value' should be of "
666                 f"shape ({n_features},) when an array-like "
667                 f"is provided. Got {limit.shape}, instead."
668             )
669         return limit
670 
671     def fit_transform(self, X, y=None):
672         """Fit the imputer on `X` and return the transformed `X`.
673 
674         Parameters
675         ----------
676         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
677             Input data, where `n_samples` is the number of samples and
678             `n_features` is the number of features.
679 
680         y : Ignored
681             Not used, present for API consistency by convention.
682 
683         Returns
684         -------
685         Xt : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
686             The imputed input data.
687         """
688         self._validate_params()
689         self.random_state_ = getattr(
690             self, "random_state_", check_random_state(self.random_state)
691         )
692 
693         if self.estimator is None:
694             from ..linear_model import BayesianRidge
695 
696             self._estimator = BayesianRidge()
697         else:
698             self._estimator = clone(self.estimator)
699 
700         self.imputation_sequence_ = []
701 
702         self.initial_imputer_ = None
703 
704         X, Xt, mask_missing_values, complete_mask = self._initial_imputation(
705             X, in_fit=True
706         )
707 
708         super()._fit_indicator(complete_mask)
709         X_indicator = super()._transform_indicator(complete_mask)
710 
711         if self.max_iter == 0 or np.all(mask_missing_values):
712             self.n_iter_ = 0
713             return super()._concatenate_indicator(Xt, X_indicator)
714 
715         # Edge case: a single feature. We return the initial ...
716         if Xt.shape[1] == 1:
717             self.n_iter_ = 0
718             return super()._concatenate_indicator(Xt, X_indicator)
719 
720         self._min_value = self._validate_limit(self.min_value, "min", X.shape[1])
721         self._max_value = self._validate_limit(self.max_value, "max", X.shape[1])
722 
723         if not np.all(np.greater(self._max_value, self._min_value)):
724             raise ValueError("One (or more) features have min_value >= max_value.")
725 
726         # order in which to impute
727         # note this is probably too slow for large feature data (d > 100000)
728         # and a better way would be good.
729         # see: https://goo.gl/KyCNwj and subsequent comments
730         ordered_idx = self._get_ordered_idx(mask_missing_values)
731         self.n_features_with_missing_ = len(ordered_idx)
732 
733         abs_corr_mat = self._get_abs_corr_mat(Xt)
734 
735         n_samples, n_features = Xt.shape
736         if self.verbose > 0:
737             print("[IterativeImputer] Completing matrix with shape %s" % (X.shape,))
738         start_t = time()
739         if not self.sample_posterior:
740             Xt_previous = Xt.copy()
741             normalized_tol = self.tol * np.max(np.abs(X[~mask_missing_values]))
742         for self.n_iter_ in range(1, self.max_iter + 1):
743             if self.imputation_order == "random":
744                 ordered_idx = self._get_ordered_idx(mask_missing_values)
745 
746             for feat_idx in ordered_idx:
747                 neighbor_feat_idx = self._get_neighbor_feat_idx(
748                     n_features, feat_idx, abs_corr_mat
749                 )
750                 Xt, estimator = self._impute_one_feature(
751                     Xt,
752                     mask_missing_values,
753                     feat_idx,
754                     neighbor_feat_idx,
755                     estimator=None,
756                     fit_mode=True,
757                 )
758                 estimator_triplet = _ImputerTriplet(
759                     feat_idx, neighbor_feat_idx, estimator
760                 )
761                 self.imputation_sequence_.append(estimator_triplet)
762 
763             if self.verbose > 1:
764                 print(
765                     "[IterativeImputer] Ending imputation round "
766                     "%d/%d, elapsed time %0.2f"
767                     % (self.n_iter_, self.max_iter, time() - start_t)
768                 )
769 
770             if not self.sample_posterior:
771                 inf_norm = np.linalg.norm(Xt - Xt_previous, ord=np.inf, axis=None)
772                 if self.verbose > 0:
773                     print(
774                         "[IterativeImputer] Change: {}, scaled tolerance: {} ".format(
775                             inf_norm, normalized_tol
776                         )
777                     )
778                 if inf_norm < normalized_tol:
779                     if self.verbose > 0:
780                         print("[IterativeImputer] Early stopping criterion reached.")
781                     break
782                 Xt_previous = Xt.copy()
783         else:
784             if not self.sample_posterior:
785                 warnings.warn(
786                     "[IterativeImputer] Early stopping criterion not reached.",
787                     ConvergenceWarning,
788                 )
789         _assign_where(Xt, X, cond=~mask_missing_values)
790 
791         return super()._concatenate_indicator(Xt, X_indicator)
792 
793     def transform(self, X):
794         """Impute all missing values in `X`.
795 
796         Note that this is stochastic, and that if `random_state` is not fixed,
797         repeated calls, or permuted input, results will differ.
798 
799         Parameters
800         ----------
801         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
802             The input data to complete.
803 
804         Returns
805         -------
806         Xt : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
807              The imputed input data.
808         """
809         check_is_fitted(self)
810 
811         X, Xt, mask_missing_values, complete_mask = self._initial_imputation(
812             X, in_fit=False
813         )
814 
815         X_indicator = super()._transform_indicator(complete_mask)
816 
817         if self.n_iter_ == 0 or np.all(mask_missing_values):
818             return super()._concatenate_indicator(Xt, X_indicator)
819 
820         imputations_per_round = len(self.imputation_sequence_) // self.n_iter_
821         i_rnd = 0
822         if self.verbose > 0:
823             print("[IterativeImputer] Completing matrix with shape %s" % (X.shape,))
824         start_t = time()
825         for it, estimator_triplet in enumerate(self.imputation_sequence_):
826             Xt, _ = self._impute_one_feature(
827                 Xt,
828                 mask_missing_values,
829                 estimator_triplet.feat_idx,
830                 estimator_triplet.neighbor_feat_idx,
831                 estimator=estimator_triplet.estimator,
832                 fit_mode=False,
833             )
834             if not (it + 1) % imputations_per_round:
835                 if self.verbose > 1:
836                     print(
837                         "[IterativeImputer] Ending imputation round "
838                         "%d/%d, elapsed time %0.2f"
839                         % (i_rnd + 1, self.n_iter_, time() - start_t)
840                     )
841                 i_rnd += 1
842 
843         _assign_where(Xt, X, cond=~mask_missing_values)
844 
845         return super()._concatenate_indicator(Xt, X_indicator)

Thresholds can exceed 1 in `roc_curve` while providing probability estimate
While working on https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/26120, I found out that something was odd with `roc_curve` that returns a threshold greater than 1. A non-regression test (that could be part of `sklearn/metrics/tests/test_ranking.py`) could be as follow:

```python
def test_roc_curve_with_probablity_estimates():
    rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
    y_true = rng.randint(0, 2, size=10)
    y_score = rng.rand(10)
    _, _, thresholds = roc_curve(y_true, y_score)
    assert np.logical_or(thresholds <= 1, thresholds >= 0).all()
```

The reason is due to the following:

https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/e886ce4e1444c61b865e7839c9cff5464ee20ace/sklearn/metrics/_ranking.py#L1086

Basically, this is to add a point for `fpr=0` and `tpr=0`. However, the `+ 1` rule does not make sense in the case `y_score` is a probability estimate.

I am not sure what would be the best fix here. A potential workaround would be to check `thresholds.max() <= 1` in which case we should clip `thresholds` to not be above 1.
