135         def _walk_toc(
136             node: Element, secnums: Dict, depth: int, titlenode: Optional[nodes.title] = None
137         ) -> None:
138             # titlenode is the title of the document, it will get assigned a
139             # secnumber too, so that it shows up in next/prev/parent rellinks
140             for subnode in node.children:
141                 if isinstance(subnode, nodes.bullet_list):
142                     numstack.append(0)
143                     _walk_toc(subnode, secnums, depth - 1, titlenode)
144                     numstack.pop()
145                     titlenode = None
146                 elif isinstance(subnode, nodes.list_item):
147                     _walk_toc(subnode, secnums, depth, titlenode)
148                     titlenode = None
149                 elif isinstance(subnode, addnodes.only):
150                     # at this stage we don't know yet which sections are going
151                     # to be included; just include all of them, even if it leads
152                     # to gaps in the numbering
153                     _walk_toc(subnode, secnums, depth, titlenode)
154                     titlenode = None
155                 elif isinstance(subnode, addnodes.compact_paragraph):
156                     numstack[-1] += 1
157                     reference = cast(nodes.reference, subnode[0])
158                     if depth > 0:
159                         number = list(numstack)
160                         secnums[reference['anchorname']] = tuple(numstack)
161                     else:
162                         number = None
163                         secnums[reference['anchorname']] = None
164                     reference['secnumber'] = number
165                     if titlenode:
166                         titlenode['secnumber'] = number
167                         titlenode = None
168                 elif isinstance(subnode, addnodes.toctree):
169                     _walk_toctree(subnode, depth)
170 
171         def _walk_toctree(toctreenode: addnodes.toctree, depth: int) -> None:
172             if depth == 0:
173                 return
174             for (_title, ref) in toctreenode['entries']:
175                 if url_re.match(ref) or ref == 'self':
176                     # don't mess with those
177                     continue
178                 elif ref in assigned:
179                     logger.warning(__('%s is already assigned section numbers '
180                                       '(nested numbered toctree?)'), ref,
181                                    location=toctreenode, type='toc', subtype='secnum')
182                 elif ref in env.tocs:
183                     secnums: Dict[str, Tuple[int, ...]] = {}
184                     env.toc_secnumbers[ref] = secnums
185                     assigned.add(ref)
186                     _walk_toc(env.tocs[ref], secnums, depth, env.titles.get(ref))
187                     if secnums != old_secnumbers.get(ref):
188                         rewrite_needed.append(ref)
189 
190         for docname in env.numbered_toctrees:
191             assigned.add(docname)
192             doctree = env.get_doctree(docname)
193             for toctreenode in doctree.findall(addnodes.toctree):
194                 depth = toctreenode.get('numbered', 0)
195                 if depth:
196                     # every numbered toctree gets new numbering
197                     numstack = [0]
198                     _walk_toctree(toctreenode, depth)
199 
200         return rewrite_needed

234         def get_next_fignumber(figtype: str, secnum: Tuple[int, ...]) -> Tuple[int, ...]:

256                         _walk_doctree(docname, subnode, secnum)
257                 elif isinstance(subnode, addnodes.toctree):
258                     for _title, subdocname in subnode['entries']:
259                         if url_re.match(subdocname) or subdocname == 'self':

264                 elif isinstance(subnode, nodes.Element):

269                     _walk_doctree(docname, subnode, secnum)

280                 if fignums != old_fignumbers.get(docname):

181 class Cmdoption(ObjectDescription):
182     """
183     Description of a command-line option (.. option).
184     """
185 
186     def handle_signature(self, sig: str, signode: desc_signature) -> str:
187         """Transform an option description into RST nodes."""
188         count = 0
189         firstname = ''
190         for potential_option in sig.split(', '):
191             potential_option = potential_option.strip()
192             m = option_desc_re.match(potential_option)
193             if not m:
194                 logger.warning(__('Malformed option description %r, should '
195                                   'look like "opt", "-opt args", "--opt args", '
196                                   '"/opt args" or "+opt args"'), potential_option,
197                                location=signode)
198                 continue
199             optname, args = m.groups()
200             if count:
201                 signode += addnodes.desc_addname(', ', ', ')
202             signode += addnodes.desc_name(optname, optname)
203             signode += addnodes.desc_addname(args, args)
204             if not count:
205                 firstname = optname
206                 signode['allnames'] = [optname]
207             else:
208                 signode['allnames'].append(optname)
209             count += 1
210         if not firstname:
211             raise ValueError
212         return firstname
213 
214     def add_target_and_index(self, firstname: str, sig: str, signode: desc_signature) -> None:
215         currprogram = self.env.ref_context.get('std:program')
216         for optname in signode.get('allnames', []):
217             prefixes = ['cmdoption']
218             if currprogram:
219                 prefixes.append(currprogram)
220             if not optname.startswith(('-', '/')):
221                 prefixes.append('arg')
222             prefix = '-'.join(prefixes)
223             node_id = make_id(self.env, self.state.document, prefix, optname)
224             signode['ids'].append(node_id)
225 
226         self.state.document.note_explicit_target(signode)
227 
228         domain = cast(StandardDomain, self.env.get_domain('std'))
229         for optname in signode.get('allnames', []):
230             domain.add_program_option(currprogram, optname,
231                                       self.env.docname, signode['ids'][0])
232 
233         # create an index entry
234         if currprogram:
235             descr = _('%s command line option') % currprogram
236         else:
237             descr = _('command line option')
238         for option in sig.split(', '):
239             entry = '; '.join([descr, option])
240             self.indexnode['entries'].append(('pair', entry, signode['ids'][0], '', None))

276 def make_glossary_term(env: "BuildEnvironment", textnodes: Iterable[Node], index_key: str,
277                        source: str, lineno: int, node_id: str = None,
278                        document: nodes.document = None) -> nodes.term:
279     # get a text-only representation of the term and register it
280     # as a cross-reference target
281     term = nodes.term('', '', *textnodes)
282     term.source = source
283     term.line = lineno
284     termtext = term.astext()
285 
286     if node_id:
287         # node_id is given from outside (mainly i18n module), use it forcedly
288         term['ids'].append(node_id)
289     elif document:
290         node_id = make_id(env, document, 'term', termtext)
291         term['ids'].append(node_id)
292         document.note_explicit_target(term)
293     else:
294         warnings.warn('make_glossary_term() expects document is passed as an argument.',
295                       RemovedInSphinx40Warning)
296         gloss_entries = env.temp_data.setdefault('gloss_entries', set())
297         node_id = nodes.make_id('term-' + termtext)
298         if node_id == 'term':
299             # "term" is not good for node_id.  Generate it by sequence number instead.
300             node_id = 'term-%d' % env.new_serialno('glossary')
301 
302         while node_id in gloss_entries:
303             node_id = 'term-%d' % env.new_serialno('glossary')
304         gloss_entries.add(node_id)
305         term['ids'].append(node_id)
306 
307     std = cast(StandardDomain, env.get_domain('std'))
308     std.note_object('term', termtext.lower(), node_id, location=term)
309 
310     # add an index entry too
311     indexnode = addnodes.index()
312     indexnode['entries'] = [('single', termtext, node_id, 'main', index_key)]
313     indexnode.source, indexnode.line = term.source, term.line
314     term.append(indexnode)
315 
316     return term

319 class Glossary(SphinxDirective):
320     """
321     Directive to create a glossary with cross-reference targets for :term:
322     roles.
323     """
324 
325     has_content = True
326     required_arguments = 0
327     optional_arguments = 0
328     final_argument_whitespace = False
329     option_spec = {
330         'sorted': directives.flag,
331     }
332 
333     def run(self) -> List[Node]:
334         node = addnodes.glossary()
335         node.document = self.state.document
336 
337         # This directive implements a custom format of the reST definition list
338         # that allows multiple lines of terms before the definition.  This is
339         # easy to parse since we know that the contents of the glossary *must
340         # be* a definition list.
341 
342         # first, collect single entries
343         entries = []  # type: List[Tuple[List[Tuple[str, str, int]], StringList]]
344         in_definition = True
345         in_comment = False
346         was_empty = True
347         messages = []  # type: List[Node]
348         for line, (source, lineno) in zip(self.content, self.content.items):
349             # empty line -> add to last definition
350             if not line:
351                 if in_definition and entries:
352                     entries[-1][1].append('', source, lineno)
353                 was_empty = True
354                 continue
355             # unindented line -> a term
356             if line and not line[0].isspace():
357                 # enable comments
358                 if line.startswith('.. '):
359                     in_comment = True
360                     continue
361                 else:
362                     in_comment = False
363 
364                 # first term of definition
365                 if in_definition:
366                     if not was_empty:
367                         messages.append(self.state.reporter.warning(
368                             _('glossary term must be preceded by empty line'),
369                             source=source, line=lineno))
370                     entries.append(([(line, source, lineno)], StringList()))
371                     in_definition = False
372                 # second term and following
373                 else:
374                     if was_empty:
375                         messages.append(self.state.reporter.warning(
376                             _('glossary terms must not be separated by empty lines'),
377                             source=source, line=lineno))
378                     if entries:
379                         entries[-1][0].append((line, source, lineno))
380                     else:
381                         messages.append(self.state.reporter.warning(
382                             _('glossary seems to be misformatted, check indentation'),
383                             source=source, line=lineno))
384             elif in_comment:
385                 pass
386             else:
387                 if not in_definition:
388                     # first line of definition, determines indentation
389                     in_definition = True
390                     indent_len = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
391                 if entries:
392                     entries[-1][1].append(line[indent_len:], source, lineno)
393                 else:
394                     messages.append(self.state.reporter.warning(
395                         _('glossary seems to be misformatted, check indentation'),
396                         source=source, line=lineno))
397             was_empty = False
398 
399         # now, parse all the entries into a big definition list
400         items = []
401         for terms, definition in entries:
402             termtexts = []          # type: List[str]
403             termnodes = []          # type: List[Node]
404             system_messages = []    # type: List[Node]
405             for line, source, lineno in terms:
406                 parts = split_term_classifiers(line)
407                 # parse the term with inline markup
408                 # classifiers (parts[1:]) will not be shown on doctree
409                 textnodes, sysmsg = self.state.inline_text(parts[0], lineno)
410 
411                 # use first classifier as a index key
412                 term = make_glossary_term(self.env, textnodes, parts[1], source, lineno,
413                                           document=self.state.document)
414                 term.rawsource = line
415                 system_messages.extend(sysmsg)
416                 termtexts.append(term.astext())
417                 termnodes.append(term)
418 
419             termnodes.extend(system_messages)
420 
421             defnode = nodes.definition()
422             if definition:
423                 self.state.nested_parse(definition, definition.items[0][1],
424                                         defnode)
425             termnodes.append(defnode)
426             items.append((termtexts,
427                           nodes.definition_list_item('', *termnodes)))
428 
429         if 'sorted' in self.options:
430             items.sort(key=lambda x:
431                        unicodedata.normalize('NFD', x[0][0].lower()))
432 
433         dlist = nodes.definition_list()
434         dlist['classes'].append('glossary')
435         dlist.extend(item[1] for item in items)
436         node += dlist
437         return messages + [node]

440 def token_xrefs(text: str, productionGroup: str = '') -> List[Node]:
441     if len(productionGroup) != 0:
442         productionGroup += ':'
443     retnodes = []  # type: List[Node]
444     pos = 0
445     for m in token_re.finditer(text):
446         if m.start() > pos:
447             txt = text[pos:m.start()]
448             retnodes.append(nodes.Text(txt, txt))
449         refnode = pending_xref(m.group(1), reftype='token', refdomain='std',
450                                reftarget=productionGroup + m.group(1))
451         refnode += nodes.literal(m.group(1), m.group(1), classes=['xref'])
452         retnodes.append(refnode)
453         pos = m.end()
454     if pos < len(text):
455         retnodes.append(nodes.Text(text[pos:], text[pos:]))
456     return retnodes

459 class ProductionList(SphinxDirective):
460     """
461     Directive to list grammar productions.
462     """
463 
464     has_content = False
465     required_arguments = 1
466     optional_arguments = 0
467     final_argument_whitespace = True
468     option_spec = {}  # type: Dict
469 
470     def run(self) -> List[Node]:
471         domain = cast(StandardDomain, self.env.get_domain('std'))
472         node = addnodes.productionlist()  # type: Element
473         self.set_source_info(node)
474         # The backslash handling is from ObjectDescription.get_signatures
475         nl_escape_re = re.compile(r'\\\n')
476         lines = nl_escape_re.sub('', self.arguments[0]).split('\n')
477 
478         productionGroup = ""
479         i = 0
480         for rule in lines:
481             if i == 0 and ':' not in rule:
482                 productionGroup = rule.strip()
483                 continue
484             i += 1
485             try:
486                 name, tokens = rule.split(':', 1)
487             except ValueError:
488                 break
489             subnode = addnodes.production(rule)
490             subnode['tokenname'] = name.strip()
491             if subnode['tokenname']:
492                 prefix = 'grammar-token-%s' % productionGroup
493                 node_id = make_id(self.env, self.state.document, prefix, name)
494                 subnode['ids'].append(node_id)
495 
496                 # Assign old styled node_id not to break old hyperlinks (if possible)
497                 # Note: Will be removed in Sphinx-5.0 (RemovedInSphinx50Warning)
498                 old_node_id = self.make_old_id(name)
499                 if (old_node_id not in self.state.document.ids and
500                         old_node_id not in subnode['ids']):
501                     subnode['ids'].append(old_node_id)
502 
503                 self.state.document.note_implicit_target(subnode, subnode)
504 
505                 if len(productionGroup) != 0:
506                     objName = "%s:%s" % (productionGroup, name)
507                 else:
508                     objName = name
509                 domain.note_object('token', objName, node_id, location=node)
510             subnode.extend(token_xrefs(tokens, productionGroup))
511             node.append(subnode)
512         return [node]
513 
514     def make_old_id(self, token: str) -> str:
515         """Generate old styled node_id for tokens.
516 
517         .. note:: Old Styled node_id was used until Sphinx-3.0.
518                   This will be removed in Sphinx-5.0.
519         """
520         return nodes.make_id('grammar-token-' + token)

187 def _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode: desc_signature, arglist: str) -> None:
188     """"Parse" a list of arguments separated by commas.
189 
190     Arguments can have "optional" annotations given by enclosing them in
191     brackets.  Currently, this will split at any comma, even if it's inside a
192     string literal (e.g. default argument value).
193     """
194     paramlist = addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
195     stack = [paramlist]  # type: List[Element]
196     try:
197         for argument in arglist.split(','):
198             argument = argument.strip()
199             ends_open = ends_close = 0
200             while argument.startswith('['):
201                 stack.append(addnodes.desc_optional())
202                 stack[-2] += stack[-1]
203                 argument = argument[1:].strip()
204             while argument.startswith(']'):
205                 stack.pop()
206                 argument = argument[1:].strip()
207             while argument.endswith(']') and not argument.endswith('[]'):
208                 ends_close += 1
209                 argument = argument[:-1].strip()
210             while argument.endswith('['):
211                 ends_open += 1
212                 argument = argument[:-1].strip()
213             if argument:
214                 stack[-1] += addnodes.desc_parameter(argument, argument)
215             while ends_open:
216                 stack.append(addnodes.desc_optional())
217                 stack[-2] += stack[-1]
218                 ends_open -= 1
219             while ends_close:
220                 stack.pop()
221                 ends_close -= 1
222         if len(stack) != 1:
223             raise IndexError
224     except IndexError:
225         # if there are too few or too many elements on the stack, just give up
226         # and treat the whole argument list as one argument, discarding the
227         # already partially populated paramlist node
228         paramlist = addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
229         paramlist += addnodes.desc_parameter(arglist, arglist)
230         signode += paramlist
231     else:
232         signode += paramlist

459     def before_content(self) -> None:
460         """Handle object nesting before content
461 
462         :py:class:`PyObject` represents Python language constructs. For
463         constructs that are nestable, such as a Python classes, this method will
464         build up a stack of the nesting heirarchy so that it can be later
465         de-nested correctly, in :py:meth:`after_content`.
466 
467         For constructs that aren't nestable, the stack is bypassed, and instead
468         only the most recent object is tracked. This object prefix name will be
469         removed with :py:meth:`after_content`.
470         """
471         prefix = None
472         if self.names:
473             # fullname and name_prefix come from the `handle_signature` method.
474             # fullname represents the full object name that is constructed using
475             # object nesting and explicit prefixes. `name_prefix` is the
476             # explicit prefix given in a signature
477             (fullname, name_prefix) = self.names[-1]
478             if self.allow_nesting:
479                 prefix = fullname
480             elif name_prefix:
481                 prefix = name_prefix.strip('.')
482         if prefix:
483             self.env.ref_context['py:class'] = prefix
484             if self.allow_nesting:
485                 classes = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:classes', [])
486                 classes.append(prefix)
487         if 'module' in self.options:
488             modules = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:modules', [])
489             modules.append(self.env.ref_context.get('py:module'))
490             self.env.ref_context['py:module'] = self.options['module']
491 
492     def after_content(self) -> None:
493         """Handle object de-nesting after content
494 
495         If this class is a nestable object, removing the last nested class prefix
496         ends further nesting in the object.
497 
498         If this class is not a nestable object, the list of classes should not
499         be altered as we didn't affect the nesting levels in
500         :py:meth:`before_content`.
501         """
502         classes = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:classes', [])
503         if self.allow_nesting:
504             try:
505                 classes.pop()
506             except IndexError:
507                 pass
508         self.env.ref_context['py:class'] = (classes[-1] if len(classes) > 0
509                                             else None)
510         if 'module' in self.options:
511             modules = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:modules', [])
512             if modules:
513                 self.env.ref_context['py:module'] = modules.pop()
514             else:
515                 self.env.ref_context.pop('py:module')

1018 class PythonModuleIndex(Index):
1019     """
1020     Index subclass to provide the Python module index.
1021     """
1022 
1023     name = 'modindex'
1024     localname = _('Python Module Index')
1025     shortname = _('modules')
1026 
1027     def generate(self, docnames: Iterable[str] = None
1028                  ) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[str, List[IndexEntry]]], bool]:
1029         content = {}  # type: Dict[str, List[IndexEntry]]
1030         # list of prefixes to ignore
1031         ignores = None  # type: List[str]
1032         ignores = self.domain.env.config['modindex_common_prefix']  # type: ignore
1033         ignores = sorted(ignores, key=len, reverse=True)
1034         # list of all modules, sorted by module name
1035         modules = sorted(self.domain.data['modules'].items(),
1036                          key=lambda x: x[0].lower())
1037         # sort out collapsable modules
1038         prev_modname = ''
1039         num_toplevels = 0
1040         for modname, (docname, node_id, synopsis, platforms, deprecated) in modules:
1041             if docnames and docname not in docnames:
1042                 continue
1043 
1044             for ignore in ignores:
1045                 if modname.startswith(ignore):
1046                     modname = modname[len(ignore):]
1047                     stripped = ignore
1048                     break
1049             else:
1050                 stripped = ''
1051 
1052             # we stripped the whole module name?
1053             if not modname:
1054                 modname, stripped = stripped, ''
1055 
1056             entries = content.setdefault(modname[0].lower(), [])
1057 
1058             package = modname.split('.')[0]
1059             if package != modname:
1060                 # it's a submodule
1061                 if prev_modname == package:
1062                     # first submodule - make parent a group head
1063                     if entries:
1064                         last = entries[-1]
1065                         entries[-1] = IndexEntry(last[0], 1, last[2], last[3],
1066                                                  last[4], last[5], last[6])
1067                 elif not prev_modname.startswith(package):
1068                     # submodule without parent in list, add dummy entry
1069                     entries.append(IndexEntry(stripped + package, 1, '', '', '', '', ''))
1070                 subtype = 2
1071             else:
1072                 num_toplevels += 1
1073                 subtype = 0
1074 
1075             qualifier = _('Deprecated') if deprecated else ''
1076             entries.append(IndexEntry(stripped + modname, subtype, docname,
1077                                       node_id, platforms, qualifier, synopsis))

102 class ASTIdentifier(ASTBaseBase):
103     def __init__(self, identifier: str) -> None:
104         assert identifier is not None
105         assert len(identifier) != 0
106         self.identifier = identifier
107 
108     def is_anon(self) -> bool:
109         return self.identifier[0] == '@'
110 
111     # and this is where we finally make a difference between __str__ and the display string
112 
113     def __str__(self) -> str:
114         return self.identifier
115 
116     def get_display_string(self) -> str:
117         return "[anonymous]" if self.is_anon() else self.identifier
118 
119     def describe_signature(self, signode: TextElement, mode: str, env: "BuildEnvironment",
120                            prefix: str, symbol: "Symbol") -> None:
121         # note: slightly different signature of describe_signature due to the prefix
122         verify_description_mode(mode)
123         if mode == 'markType':
124             targetText = prefix + self.identifier
125             pnode = addnodes.pending_xref('', refdomain='c',
126                                           reftype='identifier',
127                                           reftarget=targetText, modname=None,
128                                           classname=None)
129             # key = symbol.get_lookup_key()
130             # pnode['c:parent_key'] = key
131             if self.is_anon():
132                 pnode += nodes.strong(text="[anonymous]")
133             else:
134                 pnode += nodes.Text(self.identifier)
135             signode += pnode
136         elif mode == 'lastIsName':
137             if self.is_anon():
138                 signode += nodes.strong(text="[anonymous]")
139             else:
140                 signode += addnodes.desc_name(self.identifier, self.identifier)
141         elif mode == 'noneIsName':
142             if self.is_anon():
143                 signode += nodes.strong(text="[anonymous]")
144             else:
145                 signode += nodes.Text(self.identifier)
146         else:
147             raise Exception('Unknown description mode: %s' % mode)

150 class ASTNestedName(ASTBase):
151     def __init__(self, names: List[ASTIdentifier], rooted: bool) -> None:
152         assert len(names) > 0
153         self.names = names
154         self.rooted = rooted
155 
156     @property
157     def name(self) -> "ASTNestedName":
158         return self
159 
160     def get_id(self, version: int) -> str:
161         return '.'.join(str(n) for n in self.names)
162 
163     def _stringify(self, transform: StringifyTransform) -> str:
164         res = '.'.join(transform(n) for n in self.names)
165         if self.rooted:
166             return '.' + res
167         else:
168             return res
169 
170     def describe_signature(self, signode: TextElement, mode: str,
171                            env: "BuildEnvironment", symbol: "Symbol") -> None:
172         verify_description_mode(mode)
173         # just print the name part, with template args, not template params
174         if mode == 'noneIsName':
175             signode += nodes.Text(str(self))
176         elif mode == 'param':
177             name = str(self)
178             signode += nodes.emphasis(name, name)
179         elif mode == 'markType' or mode == 'lastIsName' or mode == 'markName':
180             # Each element should be a pending xref targeting the complete
181             # prefix.
182             prefix = ''
183             first = True
184             names = self.names[:-1] if mode == 'lastIsName' else self.names
185             # If lastIsName, then wrap all of the prefix in a desc_addname,
186             # else append directly to signode.
187             # TODO: also for C?
188             #  NOTE: Breathe relies on the prefix being in the desc_addname node,
189             #       so it can remove it in inner declarations.
190             dest = signode
191             if mode == 'lastIsName':
192                 dest = addnodes.desc_addname()
193             for i in range(len(names)):
194                 ident = names[i]
195                 if not first:
196                     dest += nodes.Text('.')
197                     prefix += '.'
198                 first = False
199                 txt_ident = str(ident)
200                 if txt_ident != '':
201                     ident.describe_signature(dest, 'markType', env, prefix, symbol)
202                 prefix += txt_ident
203             if mode == 'lastIsName':
204                 if len(self.names) > 1:
205                     dest += addnodes.desc_addname('.', '.')
206                     signode += dest
207                 self.names[-1].describe_signature(signode, mode, env, '', symbol)
208         else:
209             raise Exception('Unknown description mode: %s' % mode)

672 class ASTDeclSpecsSimple(ASTBaseBase):
673     def __init__(self, storage: str, threadLocal: str, inline: bool,
674                  restrict: bool, volatile: bool, const: bool, attrs: List[Any]) -> None:
675         self.storage = storage
676         self.threadLocal = threadLocal
677         self.inline = inline
678         self.restrict = restrict
679         self.volatile = volatile
680         self.const = const
681         self.attrs = attrs
682 
683     def mergeWith(self, other: "ASTDeclSpecsSimple") -> "ASTDeclSpecsSimple":
684         if not other:
685             return self
686         return ASTDeclSpecsSimple(self.storage or other.storage,
687                                   self.threadLocal or other.threadLocal,
688                                   self.inline or other.inline,
689                                   self.volatile or other.volatile,
690                                   self.const or other.const,
691                                   self.restrict or other.restrict,
692                                   self.attrs + other.attrs)
693 
694     def _stringify(self, transform: StringifyTransform) -> str:
695         res = []  # type: List[str]
696         res.extend(transform(attr) for attr in self.attrs)
697         if self.storage:
698             res.append(self.storage)
699         if self.threadLocal:
700             res.append(self.threadLocal)
701         if self.inline:
702             res.append('inline')
703         if self.restrict:
704             res.append('restrict')
705         if self.volatile:
706             res.append('volatile')
707         if self.const:
708             res.append('const')
709         return ' '.join(res)
710 
711     def describe_signature(self, modifiers: List[Node]) -> None:
712         def _add(modifiers: List[Node], text: str) -> None:
713             if len(modifiers) > 0:
714                 modifiers.append(nodes.Text(' '))
715             modifiers.append(addnodes.desc_annotation(text, text))
716 
717         for attr in self.attrs:
718             if len(modifiers) > 0:
719                 modifiers.append(nodes.Text(' '))
720             modifiers.append(attr.describe_signature(modifiers))
721         if self.storage:
722             _add(modifiers, self.storage)
723         if self.threadLocal:
724             _add(modifiers, self.threadLocal)
725         if self.inline:
726             _add(modifiers, 'inline')
727         if self.restrict:
728             _add(modifiers, 'restrict')
729         if self.volatile:
730             _add(modifiers, 'volatile')
731         if self.const:
732             _add(modifiers, 'const')

739                  trailing: ASTTrailingTypeSpec) -> None:
740         # leftSpecs and rightSpecs are used for output

746         self.trailingTypeSpec = trailing

749         res = []  # type: List[str]
750         l = transform(self.leftSpecs)
751         if len(l) > 0:
752             res.append(l)
753         if self.trailingTypeSpec:
754             if len(res) > 0:
755                 res.append(" ")
756             res.append(transform(self.trailingTypeSpec))
757             r = str(self.rightSpecs)
758             if len(r) > 0:
759                 if len(res) > 0:
760                     res.append(" ")
761                 res.append(r)
762         return "".join(res)

764     def describe_signature(self, signode: TextElement, mode: str,
765                            env: "BuildEnvironment", symbol: "Symbol") -> None:
766         verify_description_mode(mode)

768 
769         def _add(modifiers: List[Node], text: str) -> None:
770             if len(modifiers) > 0:
771                 modifiers.append(nodes.Text(' '))
772             modifiers.append(addnodes.desc_annotation(text, text))
773 
774         self.leftSpecs.describe_signature(modifiers)
775 
776         for m in modifiers:
777             signode += m
778         if self.trailingTypeSpec:
779             if len(modifiers) > 0:
780                 signode += nodes.Text(' ')
781             self.trailingTypeSpec.describe_signature(signode, mode, env,
782                                                      symbol=symbol)
783             modifiers = []
784             self.rightSpecs.describe_signature(modifiers)
785             if len(modifiers) > 0:
786                 signode += nodes.Text(' ')
787             for m in modifiers:
788                 signode += m

794 class ASTArray(ASTBase):
795     def __init__(self, static: bool, const: bool, volatile: bool, restrict: bool,
796                  vla: bool, size: ASTExpression):
797         self.static = static
798         self.const = const
799         self.volatile = volatile
800         self.restrict = restrict
801         self.vla = vla
802         self.size = size
803         if vla:
804             assert size is None
805         if size is not None:
806             assert not vla
807 
808     def _stringify(self, transform: StringifyTransform) -> str:
809         el = []
810         if self.static:
811             el.append('static')
812         if self.restrict:
813             el.append('restrict')
814         if self.volatile:
815             el.append('volatile')
816         if self.const:
817             el.append('const')
818         if self.vla:
819             return '[' + ' '.join(el) + '*]'
820         elif self.size:
821             el.append(transform(self.size))
822         return '[' + ' '.join(el) + ']'
823 
824     def describe_signature(self, signode: TextElement, mode: str,
825                            env: "BuildEnvironment", symbol: "Symbol") -> None:
826         verify_description_mode(mode)
827         signode.append(nodes.Text("["))
828         addSpace = False
829 
830         def _add(signode: TextElement, text: str) -> bool:
831             if addSpace:
832                 signode += nodes.Text(' ')
833             signode += addnodes.desc_annotation(text, text)
834             return True
835 
836         if self.static:
837             addSpace = _add(signode, 'static')
838         if self.restrict:
839             addSpace = _add(signode, 'restrict')
840         if self.volatile:
841             addSpace = _add(signode, 'volatile')
842         if self.const:
843             addSpace = _add(signode, 'const')
844         if self.vla:
845             signode.append(nodes.Text('*'))
846         elif self.size:
847             if addSpace:
848                 signode += nodes.Text(' ')
849             self.size.describe_signature(signode, mode, env, symbol)
850         signode.append(nodes.Text("]"))

938 class ASTDeclaratorPtr(ASTDeclarator):

940                  attrs: Any) -> None:
941         assert next
942         self.next = next

944         self.volatile = volatile
945         self.const = const

949     def name(self) -> ASTNestedName:
950         return self.next.name

954         return self.next.function_params
955 
956     def require_space_after_declSpecs(self) -> bool:
957         return self.const or self.volatile or self.restrict or \
958             len(self.attrs) > 0 or \
959             self.next.require_space_after_declSpecs()

961     def _stringify(self, transform: StringifyTransform) -> str:
962         res = ['*']
963         for a in self.attrs:
964             res.append(transform(a))
965         if len(self.attrs) > 0 and (self.restrict or self.volatile or self.const):
966             res.append(' ')
967         if self.restrict:
968             res.append('restrict')
969         if self.volatile:
970             if self.restrict:
971                 res.append(' ')
972             res.append('volatile')
973         if self.const:
974             if self.restrict or self.volatile:
975                 res.append(' ')
976             res.append('const')
977         if self.const or self.volatile or self.restrict or len(self.attrs) > 0:
978             if self.next.require_space_after_declSpecs():
979                 res.append(' ')
980         res.append(transform(self.next))
981         return ''.join(res)
982 
983     def describe_signature(self, signode: TextElement, mode: str,
984                            env: "BuildEnvironment", symbol: "Symbol") -> None:
985         verify_description_mode(mode)
986         signode += nodes.Text("*")
987         for a in self.attrs:
988             a.describe_signature(signode)
989         if len(self.attrs) > 0 and (self.restrict or self.volatile or self.const):
990             signode += nodes.Text(' ')
991 
992         def _add_anno(signode: TextElement, text: str) -> None:
993             signode += addnodes.desc_annotation(text, text)
994 
995         if self.restrict:
996             _add_anno(signode, 'restrict')
997         if self.volatile:
998             if self.restrict:
999                 signode += nodes.Text(' ')
1000             _add_anno(signode, 'volatile')
1001         if self.const:
1002             if self.restrict or self.volatile:
1003                 signode += nodes.Text(' ')
1004             _add_anno(signode, 'const')
1005         if self.const or self.volatile or self.restrict or len(self.attrs) > 0:
1006             if self.next.require_space_after_declSpecs():
1007                 signode += nodes.Text(' ')
1008         self.next.describe_signature(signode, mode, env, symbol)

1354     def describe_signature(self, signode: TextElement, mode: str,
1355                            env: "BuildEnvironment", options: Dict) -> None:
1356         verify_description_mode(mode)
1357         assert self.symbol
1358         # The caller of the domain added a desc_signature node.
1359         # Always enable multiline:
1360         signode['is_multiline'] = True
1361         # Put each line in a desc_signature_line node.
1362         mainDeclNode = addnodes.desc_signature_line()
1363         mainDeclNode.sphinx_line_type = 'declarator'
1364         mainDeclNode['add_permalink'] = not self.symbol.isRedeclaration
1365         signode += mainDeclNode
1366 
1367         if self.objectType == 'member':
1368             pass
1369         elif self.objectType == 'function':
1370             pass
1371         elif self.objectType == 'macro':
1372             pass
1373         elif self.objectType == 'struct':
1374             mainDeclNode += addnodes.desc_annotation('struct ', 'struct ')
1375         elif self.objectType == 'union':
1376             mainDeclNode += addnodes.desc_annotation('union ', 'union ')
1377         elif self.objectType == 'enum':

1379         elif self.objectType == 'enumerator':

1381         elif self.objectType == 'type':
1382             prefix = self.declaration.get_type_declaration_prefix()
1383             prefix += ' '
1384             mainDeclNode += addnodes.desc_annotation(prefix, prefix)
1385         else:
1386             assert False
1387         self.declaration.describe_signature(mainDeclNode, mode, env, self.symbol)

1409 class Symbol:
1410     debug_indent = 0
1411     debug_indent_string = "  "
1412     debug_lookup = False
1413     debug_show_tree = False

1415     @staticmethod
1416     def debug_print(*args: Any) -> None:
1417         print(Symbol.debug_indent_string * Symbol.debug_indent, end="")
1418         print(*args)

1420     def _assert_invariants(self) -> None:
1421         if not self.parent:
1422             # parent == None means global scope, so declaration means a parent
1423             assert not self.declaration
1424             assert not self.docname
1425         else:
1426             if self.declaration:
1427                 assert self.docname
1428 
1429     def __setattr__(self, key: str, value: Any) -> None:

1431             assert False
1432         else:
1433             return super().__setattr__(key, value)

1435     def __init__(self, parent: "Symbol", ident: ASTIdentifier,
1436                  declaration: ASTDeclaration, docname: str) -> None:
1437         self.parent = parent
1438         # declarations in a single directive are linked together
1439         self.siblingAbove = None  # type: Symbol
1440         self.siblingBelow = None  # type: Symbol
1441         self.ident = ident
1442         self.declaration = declaration
1443         self.docname = docname
1444         self.isRedeclaration = False
1445         self._assert_invariants()
1446 
1447         # Remember to modify Symbol.remove if modifications to the parent change.
1448         self._children = []  # type: List[Symbol]
1449         self._anonChildren = []  # type: List[Symbol]
1450         # note: _children includes _anonChildren
1451         if self.parent:
1452             self.parent._children.append(self)
1453         if self.declaration:
1454             self.declaration.symbol = self
1455 
1456         # Do symbol addition after self._children has been initialised.
1457         self._add_function_params()

1459     def _fill_empty(self, declaration: ASTDeclaration, docname: str) -> None:
1460         self._assert_invariants()
1461         assert not self.declaration
1462         assert not self.docname
1463         assert declaration
1464         assert docname
1465         self.declaration = declaration
1466         self.declaration.symbol = self
1467         self.docname = docname
1468         self._assert_invariants()
1469         # and symbol addition should be done as well
1470         self._add_function_params()
1471 
1472     def _add_function_params(self) -> None:
1473         if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1474             Symbol.debug_indent += 1
1475             Symbol.debug_print("_add_function_params:")
1476         # Note: we may be called from _fill_empty, so the symbols we want
1477         #       to add may actually already be present (as empty symbols).
1478 
1479         # add symbols for function parameters, if any
1480         if self.declaration is not None and self.declaration.function_params is not None:
1481             for p in self.declaration.function_params:
1482                 if p.arg is None:
1483                     continue
1484                 nn = p.arg.name
1485                 if nn is None:
1486                     continue
1487                 # (comparing to the template params: we have checked that we are a declaration)
1488                 decl = ASTDeclaration('functionParam', None, p)
1489                 assert not nn.rooted
1490                 assert len(nn.names) == 1
1491                 self._add_symbols(nn, decl, self.docname)
1492         if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1493             Symbol.debug_indent -= 1
1494 
1495     def remove(self) -> None:
1496         if self.parent is None:
1497             return
1498         assert self in self.parent._children
1499         self.parent._children.remove(self)
1500         self.parent = None

1502     def clear_doc(self, docname: str) -> None:
1503         newChildren = []  # type: List[Symbol]
1504         for sChild in self._children:
1505             sChild.clear_doc(docname)
1506             if sChild.declaration and sChild.docname == docname:
1507                 sChild.declaration = None
1508                 sChild.docname = None
1509                 if sChild.siblingAbove is not None:
1510                     sChild.siblingAbove.siblingBelow = sChild.siblingBelow
1511                 if sChild.siblingBelow is not None:
1512                     sChild.siblingBelow.siblingAbove = sChild.siblingAbove
1513                 sChild.siblingAbove = None
1514                 sChild.siblingBelow = None
1515             newChildren.append(sChild)

1521             for s in sChild.get_all_symbols():
1522                 yield s

1524     @property
1525     def children_recurse_anon(self) -> Iterator["Symbol"]:

1527             yield c

1532     def get_lookup_key(self) -> "LookupKey":
1533         # The pickle files for the environment and for each document are distinct.
1534         # The environment has all the symbols, but the documents has xrefs that
1535         # must know their scope. A lookup key is essentially a specification of
1536         # how to find a specific symbol.
1537         symbols = []
1538         s = self
1539         while s.parent:
1540             symbols.append(s)
1541             s = s.parent
1542         symbols.reverse()
1543         key = []
1544         for s in symbols:
1545             if s.declaration is not None:
1546                 # TODO: do we need the ID?
1547                 key.append((s.ident, s.declaration.get_newest_id()))
1548             else:
1549                 key.append((s.ident, None))
1550         return LookupKey(key)

1552     def get_full_nested_name(self) -> ASTNestedName:
1553         symbols = []
1554         s = self
1555         while s.parent:
1556             symbols.append(s)
1557             s = s.parent
1558         symbols.reverse()
1559         names = []
1560         for s in symbols:
1561             names.append(s.ident)
1562         return ASTNestedName(names, rooted=False)

1564     def _find_first_named_symbol(self, ident: ASTIdentifier,
1565                                  matchSelf: bool, recurseInAnon: bool) -> "Symbol":
1566         # TODO: further simplification from C++ to C
1567         if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1568             Symbol.debug_print("_find_first_named_symbol ->")
1569         res = self._find_named_symbols(ident, matchSelf, recurseInAnon,
1570                                        searchInSiblings=False)
1571         try:
1572             return next(res)
1573         except StopIteration:
1574             return None
1575 
1576     def _find_named_symbols(self, ident: ASTIdentifier,
1577                             matchSelf: bool, recurseInAnon: bool,
1578                             searchInSiblings: bool) -> Iterator["Symbol"]:
1579         # TODO: further simplification from C++ to C
1580         if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1581             Symbol.debug_indent += 1
1582             Symbol.debug_print("_find_named_symbols:")
1583             Symbol.debug_indent += 1
1584             Symbol.debug_print("self:")
1585             print(self.to_string(Symbol.debug_indent + 1), end="")
1586             Symbol.debug_print("ident:            ", ident)
1587             Symbol.debug_print("matchSelf:        ", matchSelf)
1588             Symbol.debug_print("recurseInAnon:    ", recurseInAnon)
1589             Symbol.debug_print("searchInSiblings: ", searchInSiblings)
1590 
1591         def candidates() -> Generator["Symbol", None, None]:
1592             s = self
1593             if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1594                 Symbol.debug_print("searching in self:")
1595                 print(s.to_string(Symbol.debug_indent + 1), end="")
1596             while True:
1597                 if matchSelf:
1598                     yield s
1599                 if recurseInAnon:
1600                     yield from s.children_recurse_anon
1601                 else:
1602                     yield from s._children
1603 
1604                 if s.siblingAbove is None:
1605                     break
1606                 s = s.siblingAbove
1607                 if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1608                     Symbol.debug_print("searching in sibling:")
1609                     print(s.to_string(Symbol.debug_indent + 1), end="")
1610 
1611         for s in candidates():
1612             if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1613                 Symbol.debug_print("candidate:")
1614                 print(s.to_string(Symbol.debug_indent + 1), end="")
1615             if s.ident == ident:
1616                 if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1617                     Symbol.debug_indent += 1
1618                     Symbol.debug_print("matches")
1619                     Symbol.debug_indent -= 3
1620                 yield s
1621                 if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1622                     Symbol.debug_indent += 2
1623         if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1624             Symbol.debug_indent -= 2
1625 
1626     def _symbol_lookup(self, nestedName: ASTNestedName,
1627                        onMissingQualifiedSymbol: Callable[["Symbol", ASTIdentifier], "Symbol"],  # NOQA
1628                        ancestorLookupType: str, matchSelf: bool,
1629                        recurseInAnon: bool, searchInSiblings: bool) -> SymbolLookupResult:
1630         # TODO: further simplification from C++ to C
1631         # ancestorLookupType: if not None, specifies the target type of the lookup
1632         if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1633             Symbol.debug_indent += 1
1634             Symbol.debug_print("_symbol_lookup:")
1635             Symbol.debug_indent += 1
1636             Symbol.debug_print("self:")
1637             print(self.to_string(Symbol.debug_indent + 1), end="")
1638             Symbol.debug_print("nestedName:        ", nestedName)
1639             Symbol.debug_print("ancestorLookupType:", ancestorLookupType)
1640             Symbol.debug_print("matchSelf:         ", matchSelf)
1641             Symbol.debug_print("recurseInAnon:     ", recurseInAnon)
1642             Symbol.debug_print("searchInSiblings:  ", searchInSiblings)
1643 
1644         names = nestedName.names
1645 
1646         # find the right starting point for lookup
1647         parentSymbol = self
1648         if nestedName.rooted:
1649             while parentSymbol.parent:
1650                 parentSymbol = parentSymbol.parent
1651         if ancestorLookupType is not None:
1652             # walk up until we find the first identifier
1653             firstName = names[0]
1654             while parentSymbol.parent:
1655                 if parentSymbol.find_identifier(firstName,
1656                                                 matchSelf=matchSelf,
1657                                                 recurseInAnon=recurseInAnon,
1658                                                 searchInSiblings=searchInSiblings):
1659                     break
1660                 parentSymbol = parentSymbol.parent
1661 
1662         if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1663             Symbol.debug_print("starting point:")
1664             print(parentSymbol.to_string(Symbol.debug_indent + 1), end="")
1665 
1666         # and now the actual lookup
1667         for ident in names[:-1]:
1668             symbol = parentSymbol._find_first_named_symbol(
1669                 ident, matchSelf=matchSelf, recurseInAnon=recurseInAnon)
1670             if symbol is None:
1671                 symbol = onMissingQualifiedSymbol(parentSymbol, ident)
1672                 if symbol is None:
1673                     if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1674                         Symbol.debug_indent -= 2
1675                     return None
1676             # We have now matched part of a nested name, and need to match more
1677             # so even if we should matchSelf before, we definitely shouldn't
1678             # even more. (see also issue #2666)
1679             matchSelf = False
1680             parentSymbol = symbol
1681 
1682         if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1683             Symbol.debug_print("handle last name from:")
1684             print(parentSymbol.to_string(Symbol.debug_indent + 1), end="")
1685 
1686         # handle the last name
1687         ident = names[-1]
1688 
1689         symbols = parentSymbol._find_named_symbols(
1690             ident, matchSelf=matchSelf,
1691             recurseInAnon=recurseInAnon,
1692             searchInSiblings=searchInSiblings)
1693         if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1694             symbols = list(symbols)  # type: ignore
1695             Symbol.debug_indent -= 2
1696         return SymbolLookupResult(symbols, parentSymbol, ident)
1697 
1698     def _add_symbols(self, nestedName: ASTNestedName,
1699                      declaration: ASTDeclaration, docname: str) -> "Symbol":
1700         # TODO: further simplification from C++ to C
1701         # Used for adding a whole path of symbols, where the last may or may not
1702         # be an actual declaration.
1703 
1704         if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1705             Symbol.debug_indent += 1
1706             Symbol.debug_print("_add_symbols:")
1707             Symbol.debug_indent += 1
1708             Symbol.debug_print("nn:    ", nestedName)
1709             Symbol.debug_print("decl:  ", declaration)
1710             Symbol.debug_print("doc:   ", docname)
1711 
1712         def onMissingQualifiedSymbol(parentSymbol: "Symbol", ident: ASTIdentifier) -> "Symbol":
1713             if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1714                 Symbol.debug_indent += 1
1715                 Symbol.debug_print("_add_symbols, onMissingQualifiedSymbol:")
1716                 Symbol.debug_indent += 1
1717                 Symbol.debug_print("ident: ", ident)
1718                 Symbol.debug_indent -= 2
1719             return Symbol(parent=parentSymbol, ident=ident,
1720                           declaration=None, docname=None)
1721 
1722         lookupResult = self._symbol_lookup(nestedName,
1723                                            onMissingQualifiedSymbol,
1724                                            ancestorLookupType=None,
1725                                            matchSelf=False,
1726                                            recurseInAnon=False,
1727                                            searchInSiblings=False)
1728         assert lookupResult is not None  # we create symbols all the way, so that can't happen
1729         symbols = list(lookupResult.symbols)
1730         if len(symbols) == 0:
1731             if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1732                 Symbol.debug_print("_add_symbols, result, no symbol:")
1733                 Symbol.debug_indent += 1
1734                 Symbol.debug_print("ident:       ", lookupResult.ident)
1735                 Symbol.debug_print("declaration: ", declaration)
1736                 Symbol.debug_print("docname:     ", docname)
1737                 Symbol.debug_indent -= 1
1738             symbol = Symbol(parent=lookupResult.parentSymbol,
1739                             ident=lookupResult.ident,
1740                             declaration=declaration,
1741                             docname=docname)
1742             if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1743                 Symbol.debug_indent -= 2
1744             return symbol
1745 
1746         if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1747             Symbol.debug_print("_add_symbols, result, symbols:")
1748             Symbol.debug_indent += 1
1749             Symbol.debug_print("number symbols:", len(symbols))
1750             Symbol.debug_indent -= 1
1751 
1752         if not declaration:
1753             if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1754                 Symbol.debug_print("no delcaration")
1755                 Symbol.debug_indent -= 2
1756             # good, just a scope creation
1757             # TODO: what if we have more than one symbol?
1758             return symbols[0]
1759 
1760         noDecl = []
1761         withDecl = []
1762         dupDecl = []
1763         for s in symbols:
1764             if s.declaration is None:
1765                 noDecl.append(s)
1766             elif s.isRedeclaration:
1767                 dupDecl.append(s)
1768             else:
1769                 withDecl.append(s)
1770         if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1771             Symbol.debug_print("#noDecl:  ", len(noDecl))
1772             Symbol.debug_print("#withDecl:", len(withDecl))
1773             Symbol.debug_print("#dupDecl: ", len(dupDecl))
1774 
1775         # With partial builds we may start with a large symbol tree stripped of declarations.
1776         # Essentially any combination of noDecl, withDecl, and dupDecls seems possible.
1777         # TODO: make partial builds fully work. What should happen when the primary symbol gets
1778         #  deleted, and other duplicates exist? The full document should probably be rebuild.
1779 
1780         # First check if one of those with a declaration matches.
1781         # If it's a function, we need to compare IDs,
1782         # otherwise there should be only one symbol with a declaration.
1783         def makeCandSymbol() -> "Symbol":
1784             if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1785                 Symbol.debug_print("begin: creating candidate symbol")
1786             symbol = Symbol(parent=lookupResult.parentSymbol,
1787                             ident=lookupResult.ident,
1788                             declaration=declaration,
1789                             docname=docname)
1790             if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1791                 Symbol.debug_print("end:   creating candidate symbol")
1792             return symbol
1793 
1794         if len(withDecl) == 0:
1795             candSymbol = None
1796         else:
1797             candSymbol = makeCandSymbol()
1798 
1799             def handleDuplicateDeclaration(symbol: "Symbol", candSymbol: "Symbol") -> None:
1800                 if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1801                     Symbol.debug_indent += 1
1802                     Symbol.debug_print("redeclaration")
1803                     Symbol.debug_indent -= 1
1804                     Symbol.debug_indent -= 2
1805                 # Redeclaration of the same symbol.
1806                 # Let the new one be there, but raise an error to the client
1807                 # so it can use the real symbol as subscope.
1808                 # This will probably result in a duplicate id warning.
1809                 candSymbol.isRedeclaration = True
1810                 raise _DuplicateSymbolError(symbol, declaration)
1811 
1812             if declaration.objectType != "function":
1813                 assert len(withDecl) <= 1
1814                 handleDuplicateDeclaration(withDecl[0], candSymbol)
1815                 # (not reachable)
1816 
1817             # a function, so compare IDs
1818             candId = declaration.get_newest_id()
1819             if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1820                 Symbol.debug_print("candId:", candId)
1821             for symbol in withDecl:
1822                 oldId = symbol.declaration.get_newest_id()
1823                 if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1824                     Symbol.debug_print("oldId: ", oldId)
1825                 if candId == oldId:
1826                     handleDuplicateDeclaration(symbol, candSymbol)
1827                     # (not reachable)
1828             # no candidate symbol found with matching ID
1829         # if there is an empty symbol, fill that one
1830         if len(noDecl) == 0:
1831             if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1832                 Symbol.debug_print("no match, no empty, candSybmol is not None?:", candSymbol is not None)  # NOQA
1833                 Symbol.debug_indent -= 2
1834             if candSymbol is not None:
1835                 return candSymbol
1836             else:
1837                 return makeCandSymbol()
1838         else:
1839             if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1840                 Symbol.debug_print(
1841                     "no match, but fill an empty declaration, candSybmol is not None?:",
1842                     candSymbol is not None)  # NOQA
1843                 Symbol.debug_indent -= 2
1844             if candSymbol is not None:
1845                 candSymbol.remove()
1846             # assert len(noDecl) == 1
1847             # TODO: enable assertion when we at some point find out how to do cleanup
1848             # for now, just take the first one, it should work fine ... right?
1849             symbol = noDecl[0]
1850             # If someone first opened the scope, and then later
1851             # declares it, e.g,
1852             # .. namespace:: Test
1853             # .. namespace:: nullptr
1854             # .. class:: Test
1855             symbol._fill_empty(declaration, docname)
1856             return symbol
1857 
1858     def merge_with(self, other: "Symbol", docnames: List[str],
1859                    env: "BuildEnvironment") -> None:
1860         if Symbol.debug_lookup:
1861             Symbol.debug_indent += 1
1862             Symbol.debug_print("merge_with:")
1863         assert other is not None
1864         for otherChild in other._children:
1865             ourChild = self._find_first_named_symbol(
1866                 ident=otherChild.ident, matchSelf=False,
1867                 recurseInAnon=False)
1868             if ourChild is None:
1869                 # TODO: hmm, should we prune by docnames?
1870                 self._children.append(otherChild)
1871                 otherChild.parent = self
1872                 otherChild._assert_invariants()
1873                 continue
1874             if otherChild.declaration and otherChild.docname in docnames:
1875                 if not ourChild.declaration:
1876                     ourChild._fill_empty(otherChild.declaration, otherChild.docname)
1877                 elif ourChild.docname != otherChild.docname:

2068     def _parse_literal(self) -> ASTLiteral:

2182     def _parse_postfix_expression(self) -> ASTPostfixExpr:
2183         # -> primary
2184         #  | postfix "[" expression "]"
2185         #  | postfix "[" braced-init-list [opt] "]"
2186         #  | postfix "(" expression-list [opt] ")"
2187         #  | postfix "." id-expression
2188         #  | postfix "->" id-expression
2189         #  | postfix "++"
2190         #  | postfix "--"
2191 
2192         prefix = self._parse_primary_expression()
2193 
2194         # and now parse postfixes
2195         postFixes = []  # type: List[ASTPostfixOp]
2196         while True:
2197             self.skip_ws()
2198             if self.skip_string_and_ws('['):
2199                 expr = self._parse_expression()
2200                 self.skip_ws()
2201                 if not self.skip_string(']'):
2202                     self.fail("Expected ']' in end of postfix expression.")
2203                 postFixes.append(ASTPostfixArray(expr))
2204                 continue
2205             if self.skip_string('.'):
2206                 if self.skip_string('*'):
2207                     # don't steal the dot
2208                     self.pos -= 2
2209                 elif self.skip_string('..'):
2210                     # don't steal the dot
2211                     self.pos -= 3
2212                 else:
2213                     name = self._parse_nested_name()
2214                     postFixes.append(ASTPostfixMember(name))
2215                     continue
2216             if self.skip_string('->'):
2217                 if self.skip_string('*'):
2218                     # don't steal the arrow
2219                     self.pos -= 3
2220                 else:
2221                     name = self._parse_nested_name()
2222                     postFixes.append(ASTPostfixMemberOfPointer(name))
2223                     continue
2224             if self.skip_string('++'):
2225                 postFixes.append(ASTPostfixInc())
2226                 continue
2227             if self.skip_string('--'):
2228                 postFixes.append(ASTPostfixDec())
2229                 continue
2230             lst = self._parse_paren_expression_list()
2231             if lst is not None:

2237     def _parse_unary_expression(self) -> ASTExpression:
2238         # -> postfix
2239         #  | "++" cast
2240         #  | "--" cast
2241         #  | unary-operator cast -> (* | & | + | - | ! | ~) cast
2242         # The rest:
2243         #  | "sizeof" unary
2244         #  | "sizeof" "(" type-id ")"
2245         #  | "alignof" "(" type-id ")"

2249             if op[0] in 'cn':

2254                 expr = self._parse_cast_expression()

2256         if self.skip_word_and_ws('sizeof'):
2257             if self.skip_string_and_ws('('):

2260                 if not self.skip_string(')'):

2269             self.skip_ws()

2275     def _parse_cast_expression(self) -> ASTExpression:

2298     def _parse_logical_or_expression(self) -> ASTExpression:
2299         # logical-or     = logical-and      ||
2300         # logical-and    = inclusive-or     &&
2301         # inclusive-or   = exclusive-or     |
2302         # exclusive-or   = and              ^
2303         # and            = equality         &
2304         # equality       = relational       ==, !=
2305         # relational     = shift            <, >, <=, >=
2306         # shift          = additive         <<, >>
2307         # additive       = multiplicative   +, -
2308         # multiplicative = pm               *, /, %
2309         # pm             = cast             .*, ->*
2310         def _parse_bin_op_expr(self, opId):
2311             if opId + 1 == len(_expression_bin_ops):
2312                 def parser() -> ASTExpression:
2313                     return self._parse_cast_expression()
2314             else:
2315                 def parser() -> ASTExpression:
2316                     return _parse_bin_op_expr(self, opId + 1)
2317             exprs = []
2318             ops = []
2319             exprs.append(parser())
2320             while True:
2321                 self.skip_ws()
2322                 pos = self.pos
2323                 oneMore = False
2324                 for op in _expression_bin_ops[opId]:
2325                     if op[0] in 'abcnox':
2326                         if not self.skip_word(op):
2327                             continue
2328                     else:
2329                         if not self.skip_string(op):
2330                             continue
2331                     if op == '&' and self.current_char == '&':
2332                         # don't split the && 'token'
2333                         self.pos -= 1
2334                         # and btw. && has lower precedence, so we are done
2335                         break
2336                     try:
2337                         expr = parser()
2338                         exprs.append(expr)
2339                         ops.append(op)
2340                         oneMore = True
2341                         break
2342                     except DefinitionError:
2343                         self.pos = pos
2344                 if not oneMore:
2345                     break
2346             return ASTBinOpExpr(exprs, ops)
2347         return _parse_bin_op_expr(self, 0)

2395     def _parse_expression_fallback(
2396             self, end: List[str],
2397             parser: Callable[[], ASTExpression],
2398             allow: bool = True) -> ASTExpression:
2399         # Stupidly "parse" an expression.
2400         # 'end' should be a list of characters which ends the expression.
2401 
2402         # first try to use the provided parser
2403         prevPos = self.pos
2404         try:
2405             return parser()
2406         except DefinitionError as e:
2407             # some places (e.g., template parameters) we really don't want to use fallback,
2408             # and for testing we may want to globally disable it
2409             if not allow or not self.allowFallbackExpressionParsing:
2410                 raise
2411             self.warn("Parsing of expression failed. Using fallback parser."
2412                       " Error was:\n%s" % e)
2413             self.pos = prevPos
2414         # and then the fallback scanning
2415         assert end is not None
2416         self.skip_ws()
2417         startPos = self.pos
2418         if self.match(_string_re):
2419             value = self.matched_text
2420         else:
2421             # TODO: add handling of more bracket-like things, and quote handling
2422             brackets = {'(': ')', '{': '}', '[': ']'}
2423             symbols = []  # type: List[str]
2424             while not self.eof:
2425                 if (len(symbols) == 0 and self.current_char in end):
2426                     break
2427                 if self.current_char in brackets.keys():
2428                     symbols.append(brackets[self.current_char])
2429                 elif len(symbols) > 0 and self.current_char == symbols[-1]:
2430                     symbols.pop()
2431                 self.pos += 1
2432             if len(end) > 0 and self.eof:
2433                 self.fail("Could not find end of expression starting at %d."
2434                           % startPos)
2435             value = self.definition[startPos:self.pos].strip()
2436         return ASTFallbackExpr(value.strip())

2612     def _parse_declarator_name_suffix(
2613             self, named: Union[bool, str], paramMode: str, typed: bool
2614     ) -> ASTDeclarator:

2616         if named == 'maybe':
2617             pos = self.pos
2618             try:
2619                 declId = self._parse_nested_name()

2621                 self.pos = pos
2622                 declId = None

2624             if self.match(identifier_re):
2625                 identifier = ASTIdentifier(self.matched_text)
2626                 declId = ASTNestedName([identifier], rooted=False)
2627             else:
2628                 declId = None
2629         elif named:
2630             declId = self._parse_nested_name()
2631         else:
2632             declId = None
2633         arrayOps = []
2634         while 1:
2635             self.skip_ws()
2636             if typed and self.skip_string('['):
2637                 self.skip_ws()
2638                 static = False
2639                 const = False
2640                 volatile = False
2641                 restrict = False
2642                 while True:
2643                     if not static:
2644                         if self.skip_word_and_ws('static'):
2645                             static = True
2646                             continue
2647                     if not const:
2648                         if self.skip_word_and_ws('const'):
2649                             const = True
2650                             continue
2651                     if not volatile:
2652                         if self.skip_word_and_ws('volatile'):
2653                             volatile = True
2654                             continue
2655                     if not restrict:
2656                         if self.skip_word_and_ws('restrict'):
2657                             restrict = True
2658                             continue

2660                 vla = False if static else self.skip_string_and_ws('*')

2662                     if not self.skip_string(']'):
2663                         self.fail("Expected ']' in end of array operator.")

2665                 else:
2666                     if self.skip_string(']'):
2667                         size = None
2668                     else:
2669 
2670                         def parser():

2673                         self.skip_ws()
2674                         if not self.skip_string(']'):
2675                             self.fail("Expected ']' in end of array operator.")

2678                 break

2684                 if self.skip_string(':'):

2690     def _parse_declarator(self, named: Union[bool, str], paramMode: str,
2691                           typed: bool = True) -> ASTDeclarator:
2692         # 'typed' here means 'parse return type stuff'
2693         if paramMode not in ('type', 'function'):
2694             raise Exception(
2695                 "Internal error, unknown paramMode '%s'." % paramMode)
2696         prevErrors = []
2697         self.skip_ws()
2698         if typed and self.skip_string('*'):
2699             self.skip_ws()
2700             restrict = False
2701             volatile = False
2702             const = False
2703             attrs = []
2704             while 1:
2705                 if not restrict:
2706                     restrict = self.skip_word_and_ws('restrict')
2707                     if restrict:
2708                         continue
2709                 if not volatile:
2710                     volatile = self.skip_word_and_ws('volatile')
2711                     if volatile:
2712                         continue
2713                 if not const:
2714                     const = self.skip_word_and_ws('const')
2715                     if const:
2716                         continue
2717                 attr = self._parse_attribute()
2718                 if attr is not None:
2719                     attrs.append(attr)
2720                     continue
2721                 break
2722             next = self._parse_declarator(named, paramMode, typed)
2723             return ASTDeclaratorPtr(next=next,
2724                                     restrict=restrict, volatile=volatile, const=const,
2725                                     attrs=attrs)
2726         if typed and self.current_char == '(':  # note: peeking, not skipping
2727             # maybe this is the beginning of params, try that first,
2728             # otherwise assume it's noptr->declarator > ( ptr-declarator )
2729             pos = self.pos
2730             try:
2731                 # assume this is params
2732                 res = self._parse_declarator_name_suffix(named, paramMode,
2733                                                          typed)

2735             except DefinitionError as exParamQual:
2736                 msg = "If declarator-id with parameters"
2737                 if paramMode == 'function':
2738                     msg += " (e.g., 'void f(int arg)')"
2739                 prevErrors.append((exParamQual, msg))
2740                 self.pos = pos
2741                 try:
2742                     assert self.current_char == '('
2743                     self.skip_string('(')
2744                     # TODO: hmm, if there is a name, it must be in inner, right?
2745                     # TODO: hmm, if there must be parameters, they must b
2746                     # inside, right?
2747                     inner = self._parse_declarator(named, paramMode, typed)
2748                     if not self.skip_string(')'):
2749                         self.fail("Expected ')' in \"( ptr-declarator )\"")

2751                                                   paramMode="type",
2752                                                   typed=typed)

2754                 except DefinitionError as exNoPtrParen:
2755                     self.pos = pos
2756                     msg = "If parenthesis in noptr-declarator"
2757                     if paramMode == 'function':
2758                         msg += " (e.g., 'void (*f(int arg))(double)')"

2762         pos = self.pos
2763         try:
2764             return self._parse_declarator_name_suffix(named, paramMode, typed)
2765         except DefinitionError as e:
2766             self.pos = pos
2767             prevErrors.append((e, "If declarator-id"))
2768             header = "Error in declarator or parameters"
2769             raise self._make_multi_error(prevErrors, header)

66 
67     Each signature is in a desc_signature node, where all children are
68     desc_signature_line nodes. Each of these lines will have the attribute
69     'sphinx_line_type' set to one of the following (prioritized):
70     - 'declarator', if the line contains the name of the declared object.
71     - 'templateParams', if the line starts a template parameter list,

81     See https://www.nongnu.org/hcb/ for the grammar,
82     and https://github.com/cplusplus/draft/blob/master/source/grammar.tex,

87         template-declaration ->
88             "template" "<" template-parameter-list ">" declaration
89         template-parameter-list ->
90               template-parameter
91             | template-parameter-list "," template-parameter
92         template-parameter ->
93               type-parameter
94             | parameter-declaration # i.e., same as a function argument
95 
96         type-parameter ->
97               "class"    "..."[opt] identifier[opt]
98             | "class"               identifier[opt] "=" type-id
99             | "typename" "..."[opt] identifier[opt]
100             | "typename"            identifier[opt] "=" type-id
101             | "template" "<" template-parameter-list ">"
102                 "class"  "..."[opt] identifier[opt]
103             | "template" "<" template-parameter-list ">"
104                 "class"             identifier[opt] "=" id-expression
105             # also, from C++17 we can have "typename" in template templates
106         templateDeclPrefix ->
107             "template" "<" template-parameter-list ">"
108 
109         simple-declaration ->
110             attribute-specifier-seq[opt] decl-specifier-seq[opt]
111                 init-declarator-list[opt] ;
112         # Make the semicolon optional.
113         # For now: drop the attributes (TODO).

116         -> decl-specifier-seq declarator initializer
