218 def _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode: desc_signature, arglist: str) -> None:
219     """"Parse" a list of arguments separated by commas.
220 
221     Arguments can have "optional" annotations given by enclosing them in
222     brackets.  Currently, this will split at any comma, even if it's inside a
223     string literal (e.g. default argument value).
224     """
225     paramlist = addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
226     stack = [paramlist]  # type: List[Element]
227     try:
228         for argument in arglist.split(','):
229             argument = argument.strip()
230             ends_open = ends_close = 0
231             while argument.startswith('['):
232                 stack.append(addnodes.desc_optional())
233                 stack[-2] += stack[-1]
234                 argument = argument[1:].strip()
235             while argument.startswith(']'):
236                 stack.pop()
237                 argument = argument[1:].strip()
238             while argument.endswith(']') and not argument.endswith('[]'):
239                 ends_close += 1
240                 argument = argument[:-1].strip()
241             while argument.endswith('['):
242                 ends_open += 1
243                 argument = argument[:-1].strip()
244             if argument:
245                 stack[-1] += addnodes.desc_parameter(argument, argument)
246             while ends_open:
247                 stack.append(addnodes.desc_optional())
248                 stack[-2] += stack[-1]
249                 ends_open -= 1
250             while ends_close:
251                 stack.pop()
252                 ends_close -= 1
253         if len(stack) != 1:
254             raise IndexError
255     except IndexError:
256         # if there are too few or too many elements on the stack, just give up
257         # and treat the whole argument list as one argument, discarding the
258         # already partially populated paramlist node
259         paramlist = addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
260         paramlist += addnodes.desc_parameter(arglist, arglist)
261         signode += paramlist
262     else:
263         signode += paramlist

266 # This override allows our inline type specifiers to behave like :class: link
267 # when it comes to handling "." and "~" prefixes.
268 class PyXrefMixin:
269     def make_xref(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
270                   innernode: "Type[TextlikeNode]" = nodes.emphasis,
271                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> Node:
272         result = super().make_xref(rolename, domain, target,  # type: ignore
273                                    innernode, contnode, env)
274         result['refspecific'] = True
275         if target.startswith(('.', '~')):
276             prefix, result['reftarget'] = target[0], target[1:]
277             if prefix == '.':
278                 text = target[1:]
279             elif prefix == '~':
280                 text = target.split('.')[-1]
281             for node in result.traverse(nodes.Text):
282                 node.parent[node.parent.index(node)] = nodes.Text(text)
283                 break
284         return result
285 
286     def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
287                    innernode: "Type[TextlikeNode]" = nodes.emphasis,
288                    contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
289         delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+)'
290         delims_re = re.compile(delims)
291         sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)
292 
293         split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)
294 
295         results = []
296         for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
297             if split_contnode:
298                 contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)
299 
300             if delims_re.match(sub_target):
301                 results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
302             else:
303                 results.append(self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
304                                               innernode, contnode, env))
305 
306         return results

382     def handle_signature(self, sig: str, signode: desc_signature) -> Tuple[str, str]:
383         """Transform a Python signature into RST nodes.
384 
385         Return (fully qualified name of the thing, classname if any).
386 
387         If inside a class, the current class name is handled intelligently:
388         * it is stripped from the displayed name if present
389         * it is added to the full name (return value) if not present
390         """
391         m = py_sig_re.match(sig)
392         if m is None:
393             raise ValueError
394         prefix, name, arglist, retann = m.groups()
395 
396         # determine module and class name (if applicable), as well as full name
397         modname = self.options.get('module', self.env.ref_context.get('py:module'))
398         classname = self.env.ref_context.get('py:class')
399         if classname:
400             add_module = False
401             if prefix and (prefix == classname or
402                            prefix.startswith(classname + ".")):
403                 fullname = prefix + name
404                 # class name is given again in the signature
405                 prefix = prefix[len(classname):].lstrip('.')
406             elif prefix:
407                 # class name is given in the signature, but different
408                 # (shouldn't happen)
409                 fullname = classname + '.' + prefix + name
410             else:
411                 # class name is not given in the signature
412                 fullname = classname + '.' + name
413         else:
414             add_module = True
415             if prefix:
416                 classname = prefix.rstrip('.')
417                 fullname = prefix + name
418             else:
419                 classname = ''
420                 fullname = name
421 
422         signode['module'] = modname
423         signode['class'] = classname
424         signode['fullname'] = fullname
425 
426         sig_prefix = self.get_signature_prefix(sig)
427         if sig_prefix:
428             signode += addnodes.desc_annotation(sig_prefix, sig_prefix)
429 
430         if prefix:
431             signode += addnodes.desc_addname(prefix, prefix)
432         elif add_module and self.env.config.add_module_names:
433             if modname and modname != 'exceptions':
434                 # exceptions are a special case, since they are documented in the
435                 # 'exceptions' module.
436                 nodetext = modname + '.'
437                 signode += addnodes.desc_addname(nodetext, nodetext)
438 
439         signode += addnodes.desc_name(name, name)
440         if arglist:
441             try:
442                 signode += _parse_arglist(arglist, self.env)
443             except SyntaxError:
444                 # fallback to parse arglist original parser.
445                 # it supports to represent optional arguments (ex. "func(foo [, bar])")
446                 _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode, arglist)
447             except NotImplementedError as exc:
448                 logger.warning("could not parse arglist (%r): %s", arglist, exc,
449                                location=signode)
450                 _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode, arglist)
451         else:
452             if self.needs_arglist():
453                 # for callables, add an empty parameter list
454                 signode += addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
455 
456         if retann:
457             children = _parse_annotation(retann, self.env)
458             signode += addnodes.desc_returns(retann, '', *children)
459 
460         anno = self.options.get('annotation')
461         if anno:
462             signode += addnodes.desc_annotation(' ' + anno, ' ' + anno)
463 
464         return fullname, prefix

492     def before_content(self) -> None:
493         """Handle object nesting before content
494 
495         :py:class:`PyObject` represents Python language constructs. For
496         constructs that are nestable, such as a Python classes, this method will
497         build up a stack of the nesting hierarchy so that it can be later
498         de-nested correctly, in :py:meth:`after_content`.
499 
500         For constructs that aren't nestable, the stack is bypassed, and instead
501         only the most recent object is tracked. This object prefix name will be
502         removed with :py:meth:`after_content`.
503         """

505         if self.names:
506             # fullname and name_prefix come from the `handle_signature` method.
507             # fullname represents the full object name that is constructed using
508             # object nesting and explicit prefixes. `name_prefix` is the
509             # explicit prefix given in a signature
510             (fullname, name_prefix) = self.names[-1]
511             if self.allow_nesting:
512                 prefix = fullname
513             elif name_prefix:
514                 prefix = name_prefix.strip('.')
515         if prefix:
516             self.env.ref_context['py:class'] = prefix
517             if self.allow_nesting:
518                 classes = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:classes', [])
519                 classes.append(prefix)
520         if 'module' in self.options:
521             modules = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:modules', [])
522             modules.append(self.env.ref_context.get('py:module'))
523             self.env.ref_context['py:module'] = self.options['module']

525     def after_content(self) -> None:
526         """Handle object de-nesting after content

528         If this class is a nestable object, removing the last nested class prefix
529         ends further nesting in the object.

531         If this class is not a nestable object, the list of classes should not
532         be altered as we didn't affect the nesting levels in
533         :py:meth:`before_content`.

536         if self.allow_nesting:

538                 classes.pop()
539             except IndexError:
540                 pass
541         self.env.ref_context['py:class'] = (classes[-1] if len(classes) > 0
542                                             else None)
543         if 'module' in self.options:
544             modules = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:modules', [])
545             if modules:

547             else:

1068 class PythonModuleIndex(Index):
1069     """
1070     Index subclass to provide the Python module index.
1071     """
1072 
1073     name = 'modindex'
1074     localname = _('Python Module Index')
1075     shortname = _('modules')
1076 
1077     def generate(self, docnames: Iterable[str] = None
1078                  ) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[str, List[IndexEntry]]], bool]:
1079         content = {}  # type: Dict[str, List[IndexEntry]]
1080         # list of prefixes to ignore
1081         ignores = None  # type: List[str]
1082         ignores = self.domain.env.config['modindex_common_prefix']  # type: ignore
1083         ignores = sorted(ignores, key=len, reverse=True)
1084         # list of all modules, sorted by module name
1085         modules = sorted(self.domain.data['modules'].items(),
1086                          key=lambda x: x[0].lower())
1087         # sort out collapsable modules
1088         prev_modname = ''
1089         num_toplevels = 0
1090         for modname, (docname, node_id, synopsis, platforms, deprecated) in modules:
1091             if docnames and docname not in docnames:
1092                 continue
1093 
1094             for ignore in ignores:
1095                 if modname.startswith(ignore):
1096                     modname = modname[len(ignore):]
1097                     stripped = ignore
1098                     break
1099             else:
1100                 stripped = ''
1101 
1102             # we stripped the whole module name?
1103             if not modname:
1104                 modname, stripped = stripped, ''
1105 
1106             entries = content.setdefault(modname[0].lower(), [])
1107 
1108             package = modname.split('.')[0]
1109             if package != modname:
1110                 # it's a submodule
1111                 if prev_modname == package:
1112                     # first submodule - make parent a group head
1113                     if entries:
1114                         last = entries[-1]
1115                         entries[-1] = IndexEntry(last[0], 1, last[2], last[3],
1116                                                  last[4], last[5], last[6])
1117                 elif not prev_modname.startswith(package):
1118                     # submodule without parent in list, add dummy entry
1119                     entries.append(IndexEntry(stripped + package, 1, '', '', '', '', ''))
1120                 subtype = 2
1121             else:
1122                 num_toplevels += 1
1123                 subtype = 0
1124 
1125             qualifier = _('Deprecated') if deprecated else ''
1126             entries.append(IndexEntry(stripped + modname, subtype, docname,
1127                                       node_id, platforms, qualifier, synopsis))
1128             prev_modname = modname
1129 
1130         # apply heuristics when to collapse modindex at page load:
1131         # only collapse if number of toplevel modules is larger than
1132         # number of submodules
1133         collapse = len(modules) - num_toplevels < num_toplevels
1134 
1135         # sort by first letter
1136         sorted_content = sorted(content.items())
1137 
1138         return sorted_content, collapse

1369 def builtin_resolver(app: Sphinx, env: BuildEnvironment,
1370                      node: pending_xref, contnode: Element) -> Element:
1371     """Do not emit nitpicky warnings for built-in types."""
1372     def istyping(s: str) -> bool:
1373         if s.startswith('typing.'):
1374             s = s.split('.', 1)[1]
1375 
1376         return s in typing.__all__  # type: ignore
1377 
1378     if node.get('refdomain') != 'py':
1379         return None
1380     elif node.get('reftype') in ('class', 'obj') and node.get('reftarget') == 'None':
1381         return contnode
1382     elif node.get('reftype') in ('class', 'exc'):
1383         reftarget = node.get('reftarget')
1384         if inspect.isclass(getattr(builtins, reftarget, None)):
1385             # built-in class
1386             return contnode
1387         elif istyping(reftarget):
1388             # typing class
1389             return contnode
1390 
1391     return None

30 def _is_single_paragraph(node: nodes.field_body) -> bool:
31     """True if the node only contains one paragraph (and system messages)."""
32     if len(node) == 0:
33         return False
34     elif len(node) > 1:
35         for subnode in node[1:]:  # type: nodes.Node
36             if not isinstance(subnode, nodes.system_message):
37                 return False
38     if isinstance(node[0], nodes.paragraph):
39         return True
40     return False

43 class Field:
44     """A doc field that is never grouped.  It can have an argument or not, the
45     argument can be linked using a specified *rolename*.  Field should be used
46     for doc fields that usually don't occur more than once.
47 
48     The body can be linked using a specified *bodyrolename* if the content is
49     just a single inline or text node.
50 
51     Example::
52 
53        :returns: description of the return value
54        :rtype: description of the return type
55     """
56     is_grouped = False
57     is_typed = False
58 
59     def __init__(self, name: str, names: Tuple[str, ...] = (), label: str = None,
60                  has_arg: bool = True, rolename: str = None, bodyrolename: str = None) -> None:
61         self.name = name
62         self.names = names
63         self.label = label
64         self.has_arg = has_arg
65         self.rolename = rolename
66         self.bodyrolename = bodyrolename
67 
68     def make_xref(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
69                   innernode: "Type[TextlikeNode]" = addnodes.literal_emphasis,
70                   contnode: Node = None, env: "BuildEnvironment" = None) -> Node:
71         if not rolename:
72             return contnode or innernode(target, target)
73         refnode = addnodes.pending_xref('', refdomain=domain, refexplicit=False,
74                                         reftype=rolename, reftarget=target)
75         refnode += contnode or innernode(target, target)
76         if env:
77             env.get_domain(domain).process_field_xref(refnode)
78         return refnode
79 
80     def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
81                    innernode: "Type[TextlikeNode]" = addnodes.literal_emphasis,
82                    contnode: Node = None, env: "BuildEnvironment" = None) -> List[Node]:
83         return [self.make_xref(rolename, domain, target, innernode, contnode, env)]
84 
85     def make_entry(self, fieldarg: str, content: List[Node]) -> Tuple[str, List[Node]]:
86         return (fieldarg, content)
87 
88     def make_field(self, types: Dict[str, List[Node]], domain: str,
89                    item: Tuple, env: "BuildEnvironment" = None) -> nodes.field:
90         fieldarg, content = item
91         fieldname = nodes.field_name('', self.label)
92         if fieldarg:
93             fieldname += nodes.Text(' ')
94             fieldname.extend(self.make_xrefs(self.rolename, domain,
95                                              fieldarg, nodes.Text, env=env))
96 
97         if len(content) == 1 and (
98                 isinstance(content[0], nodes.Text) or
99                 (isinstance(content[0], nodes.inline) and len(content[0]) == 1 and
100                  isinstance(content[0][0], nodes.Text))):
101             content = self.make_xrefs(self.bodyrolename, domain,
102                                       content[0].astext(), contnode=content[0], env=env)
103         fieldbody = nodes.field_body('', nodes.paragraph('', '', *content))
104         return nodes.field('', fieldname, fieldbody)

107 class GroupedField(Field):
108     """
109     A doc field that is grouped; i.e., all fields of that type will be
110     transformed into one field with its body being a bulleted list.  It always
111     has an argument.  The argument can be linked using the given *rolename*.
112     GroupedField should be used for doc fields that can occur more than once.
113     If *can_collapse* is true, this field will revert to a Field if only used
114     once.
115 
116     Example::
117 
118        :raises ErrorClass: description when it is raised
119     """
120     is_grouped = True
121     list_type = nodes.bullet_list
122 
123     def __init__(self, name: str, names: Tuple[str, ...] = (), label: str = None,
124                  rolename: str = None, can_collapse: bool = False) -> None:
125         super().__init__(name, names, label, True, rolename)
126         self.can_collapse = can_collapse
127 
128     def make_field(self, types: Dict[str, List[Node]], domain: str,
129                    items: Tuple, env: "BuildEnvironment" = None) -> nodes.field:
130         fieldname = nodes.field_name('', self.label)
131         listnode = self.list_type()
132         for fieldarg, content in items:
133             par = nodes.paragraph()
134             par.extend(self.make_xrefs(self.rolename, domain, fieldarg,
135                                        addnodes.literal_strong, env=env))
136             par += nodes.Text(' -- ')
137             par += content
138             listnode += nodes.list_item('', par)
139 
140         if len(items) == 1 and self.can_collapse:
141             list_item = cast(nodes.list_item, listnode[0])
142             fieldbody = nodes.field_body('', list_item[0])
143             return nodes.field('', fieldname, fieldbody)
144 
145         fieldbody = nodes.field_body('', listnode)
146         return nodes.field('', fieldname, fieldbody)

149 class TypedField(GroupedField):
150     """
151     A doc field that is grouped and has type information for the arguments.  It
152     always has an argument.  The argument can be linked using the given
153     *rolename*, the type using the given *typerolename*.
154 
155     Two uses are possible: either parameter and type description are given
156     separately, using a field from *names* and one from *typenames*,
157     respectively, or both are given using a field from *names*, see the example.
158 
159     Example::
160 
161        :param foo: description of parameter foo
162        :type foo:  SomeClass
163 
164        -- or --
165 
166        :param SomeClass foo: description of parameter foo
167     """
168     is_typed = True
169 
170     def __init__(self, name: str, names: Tuple[str, ...] = (), typenames: Tuple[str, ...] = (),
171                  label: str = None, rolename: str = None, typerolename: str = None,
172                  can_collapse: bool = False) -> None:
173         super().__init__(name, names, label, rolename, can_collapse)
174         self.typenames = typenames
175         self.typerolename = typerolename
176 
177     def make_field(self, types: Dict[str, List[Node]], domain: str,
178                    items: Tuple, env: "BuildEnvironment" = None) -> nodes.field:
179         def handle_item(fieldarg: str, content: str) -> nodes.paragraph:
180             par = nodes.paragraph()
181             par.extend(self.make_xrefs(self.rolename, domain, fieldarg,
182                                        addnodes.literal_strong, env=env))
183             if fieldarg in types:
184                 par += nodes.Text(' (')
185                 # NOTE: using .pop() here to prevent a single type node to be
186                 # inserted twice into the doctree, which leads to
187                 # inconsistencies later when references are resolved
188                 fieldtype = types.pop(fieldarg)
189                 if len(fieldtype) == 1 and isinstance(fieldtype[0], nodes.Text):
190                     typename = fieldtype[0].astext()
191                     par.extend(self.make_xrefs(self.typerolename, domain, typename,
192                                                addnodes.literal_emphasis, env=env))
193                 else:
194                     par += fieldtype
195                 par += nodes.Text(')')
196             par += nodes.Text(' -- ')
197             par += content
198             return par
199 
200         fieldname = nodes.field_name('', self.label)
201         if len(items) == 1 and self.can_collapse:
202             fieldarg, content = items[0]
203             bodynode = handle_item(fieldarg, content)  # type: nodes.Node
204         else:
205             bodynode = self.list_type()
206             for fieldarg, content in items:
207                 bodynode += nodes.list_item('', handle_item(fieldarg, content))
208         fieldbody = nodes.field_body('', bodynode)
209         return nodes.field('', fieldname, fieldbody)

212 class DocFieldTransformer:
213     """
214     Transforms field lists in "doc field" syntax into better-looking
215     equivalents, using the field type definitions given on a domain.
216     """
217     typemap = None  # type: Dict[str, Tuple[Field, bool]]
218 
219     def __init__(self, directive: "ObjectDescription") -> None:
220         self.directive = directive
221 
222         try:
223             self.typemap = directive.get_field_type_map()
224         except Exception:
225             # for 3rd party extensions directly calls this transformer.
226             warnings.warn('DocFieldTransformer expects given directive object is a subclass '
227                           'of ObjectDescription.', RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
228             self.typemap = self.preprocess_fieldtypes(directive.__class__.doc_field_types)
229 
230     def preprocess_fieldtypes(self, types: List[Field]) -> Dict[str, Tuple[Field, bool]]:
231         warnings.warn('DocFieldTransformer.preprocess_fieldtypes() is deprecated.',
232                       RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
233         typemap = {}
234         for fieldtype in types:
235             for name in fieldtype.names:
236                 typemap[name] = fieldtype, False
237             if fieldtype.is_typed:
238                 typed_field = cast(TypedField, fieldtype)
239                 for name in typed_field.typenames:
240                     typemap[name] = typed_field, True
241         return typemap
242 
243     def transform_all(self, node: addnodes.desc_content) -> None:
244         """Transform all field list children of a node."""
245         # don't traverse, only handle field lists that are immediate children
246         for child in node:
247             if isinstance(child, nodes.field_list):
248                 self.transform(child)
249 
250     def transform(self, node: nodes.field_list) -> None:
251         """Transform a single field list *node*."""
252         typemap = self.typemap
253 
254         entries = []        # type: List[Union[nodes.field, Tuple[Field, Any]]]
255         groupindices = {}   # type: Dict[str, int]
256         types = {}          # type: Dict[str, Dict]
257 
258         # step 1: traverse all fields and collect field types and content
259         for field in cast(List[nodes.field], node):
260             assert len(field) == 2
261             field_name = cast(nodes.field_name, field[0])
262             field_body = cast(nodes.field_body, field[1])
263             try:
264                 # split into field type and argument
265                 fieldtype_name, fieldarg = field_name.astext().split(None, 1)
266             except ValueError:
267                 # maybe an argument-less field type?
268                 fieldtype_name, fieldarg = field_name.astext(), ''
269             typedesc, is_typefield = typemap.get(fieldtype_name, (None, None))
270 
271             # collect the content, trying not to keep unnecessary paragraphs
272             if _is_single_paragraph(field_body):
273                 paragraph = cast(nodes.paragraph, field_body[0])
274                 content = paragraph.children
275             else:
276                 content = field_body.children
277 
278             # sort out unknown fields
279             if typedesc is None or typedesc.has_arg != bool(fieldarg):
280                 # either the field name is unknown, or the argument doesn't
281                 # match the spec; capitalize field name and be done with it
282                 new_fieldname = fieldtype_name[0:1].upper() + fieldtype_name[1:]
283                 if fieldarg:
284                     new_fieldname += ' ' + fieldarg
285                 field_name[0] = nodes.Text(new_fieldname)
286                 entries.append(field)
287 
288                 # but if this has a type then we can at least link it
289                 if (typedesc and is_typefield and content and
290                         len(content) == 1 and isinstance(content[0], nodes.Text)):
291                     typed_field = cast(TypedField, typedesc)
292                     target = content[0].astext()
293                     xrefs = typed_field.make_xrefs(
294                         typed_field.typerolename,
295                         self.directive.domain,
296                         target,
297                         contnode=content[0],
298                     )
299                     if _is_single_paragraph(field_body):
300                         paragraph = cast(nodes.paragraph, field_body[0])
301                         paragraph.clear()
302                         paragraph.extend(xrefs)
303                     else:
304                         field_body.clear()
305                         field_body += nodes.paragraph('', '', *xrefs)
306 
307                 continue
308 
309             typename = typedesc.name
310 
311             # if the field specifies a type, put it in the types collection
312             if is_typefield:
313                 # filter out only inline nodes; others will result in invalid
314                 # markup being written out
315                 content = [n for n in content if isinstance(n, nodes.Inline) or
316                            isinstance(n, nodes.Text)]
317                 if content:
318                     types.setdefault(typename, {})[fieldarg] = content
319                 continue
320 
321             # also support syntax like ``:param type name:``
322             if typedesc.is_typed:
323                 try:
324                     argtype, argname = fieldarg.split(None, 1)
325                 except ValueError:
326                     pass
327                 else:
328                     types.setdefault(typename, {})[argname] = \
329                         [nodes.Text(argtype)]
330                     fieldarg = argname
331 
332             translatable_content = nodes.inline(field_body.rawsource,
333                                                 translatable=True)
334             translatable_content.document = field_body.parent.document
335             translatable_content.source = field_body.parent.source
336             translatable_content.line = field_body.parent.line

424                 self.module, self.parent, self.object_name, self.object = ret

428                     raise

430                     logger.warning(exc.args[0], type='autodoc', subtype='import_object')

442     def check_module(self) -> bool:
443         """Check if *self.object* is really defined in the module given by
444         *self.modname*.
445         """
446         if self.options.imported_members:
447             return True

462     def format_name(self) -> str:
463         """Format the name of *self.object*.

466         directive, but doesn't need to be (Sphinx will display it unparsed
467         then).

473     def _call_format_args(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
474         if kwargs:
475             try:
476                 return self.format_args(**kwargs)
477             except TypeError:
478                 # avoid chaining exceptions, by putting nothing here
479                 pass
480 
481         # retry without arguments for old documenters
482         return self.format_args()

484     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
485         """Format the signature (arguments and return annotation) of the object.
486 
487         Let the user process it via the ``autodoc-process-signature`` event.
488         """
489         if self.args is not None:
490             # signature given explicitly
491             args = "(%s)" % self.args
492             retann = self.retann
493         else:
494             # try to introspect the signature
495             try:
496                 retann = None
497                 args = self._call_format_args(**kwargs)
498                 if args:
499                     matched = re.match(r'^(\(.*\))\s+->\s+(.*)$', args)
500                     if matched:
501                         args = matched.group(1)
502                         retann = matched.group(2)
503             except Exception as exc:
504                 logger.warning(__('error while formatting arguments for %s: %s'),
505                                self.fullname, exc, type='autodoc')
506                 args = None
507 
508         result = self.env.events.emit_firstresult('autodoc-process-signature',
509                                                   self.objtype, self.fullname,
510                                                   self.object, self.options, args, retann)
511         if result:
512             args, retann = result
513 
514         if args is not None:
515             return args + ((' -> %s' % retann) if retann else '')
516         else:
517             return ''

519     def add_directive_header(self, sig: str) -> None:
520         """Add the directive header and options to the generated content."""
521         domain = getattr(self, 'domain', 'py')
522         directive = getattr(self, 'directivetype', self.objtype)
523         name = self.format_name()
524         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
525 
526         # one signature per line, indented by column
527         prefix = '.. %s:%s:: ' % (domain, directive)
528         for i, sig_line in enumerate(sig.split("\n")):
529             self.add_line('%s%s%s' % (prefix, name, sig_line),
530                           sourcename)
531             if i == 0:
532                 prefix = " " * len(prefix)
533 
534         if self.options.noindex:
535             self.add_line('   :noindex:', sourcename)
536         if self.objpath:
537             # Be explicit about the module, this is necessary since .. class::
538             # etc. don't support a prepended module name
539             self.add_line('   :module: %s' % self.modname, sourcename)

541     def get_doc(self, encoding: str = None, ignore: int = None) -> Optional[List[List[str]]]:
542         """Decode and return lines of the docstring(s) for the object.
543 
544         When it returns None value, autodoc-process-docstring will not be called for this
545         object.

547         if encoding is not None:
548             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s.get_doc() is deprecated."
549                           % self.__class__.__name__,
550                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)

553                           % self.__class__.__name__,
554                           RemovedInSphinx50Warning, stacklevel=2)

556                            self.parent, self.object_name)

562     def process_doc(self, docstrings: List[List[str]]) -> Iterator[str]:
563         """Let the user process the docstrings before adding them."""
564         for docstringlines in docstrings:
565             if self.env.app:
566                 # let extensions preprocess docstrings
567                 self.env.app.emit('autodoc-process-docstring',
568                                   self.objtype, self.fullname, self.object,
569                                   self.options, docstringlines)
570 
571                 if docstringlines and docstringlines[-1] != '':
572                     # append a blank line to the end of the docstring
573                     docstringlines.append('')
574 
575             yield from docstringlines

577     def get_sourcename(self) -> str:
578         if (getattr(self.object, '__module__', None) and
579                 getattr(self.object, '__qualname__', None)):
580             # Get the correct location of docstring from self.object
581             # to support inherited methods
582             fullname = '%s.%s' % (self.object.__module__, self.object.__qualname__)
583         else:
584             fullname = self.fullname
585 
586         if self.analyzer:
587             return '%s:docstring of %s' % (self.analyzer.srcname, fullname)
588         else:

591     def add_content(self, more_content: Optional[StringList], no_docstring: bool = False
592                     ) -> None:
593         """Add content from docstrings, attribute documentation and user."""
594         if no_docstring:
595             warnings.warn("The 'no_docstring' argument to %s.add_content() is deprecated."
596                           % self.__class__.__name__,
597                           RemovedInSphinx50Warning, stacklevel=2)
598 
599         # set sourcename and add content from attribute documentation
600         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
601         if self.analyzer:
602             attr_docs = self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
603             if self.objpath:
604                 key = ('.'.join(self.objpath[:-1]), self.objpath[-1])
605                 if key in attr_docs:
606                     no_docstring = True
607                     # make a copy of docstring for attributes to avoid cache
608                     # the change of autodoc-process-docstring event.
609                     docstrings = [list(attr_docs[key])]
610 
611                     for i, line in enumerate(self.process_doc(docstrings)):
612                         self.add_line(line, sourcename, i)
613 
614         # add content from docstrings
615         if not no_docstring:
616             docstrings = self.get_doc()
617             if docstrings is None:
618                 # Do not call autodoc-process-docstring on get_doc() returns None.
619                 pass
620             else:
621                 if not docstrings:
622                     # append at least a dummy docstring, so that the event
623                     # autodoc-process-docstring is fired and can add some
624                     # content if desired
625                     docstrings.append([])
626                 for i, line in enumerate(self.process_doc(docstrings)):
627                     self.add_line(line, sourcename, i)
628 
629         # add additional content (e.g. from document), if present
630         if more_content:
631             for line, src in zip(more_content.data, more_content.items):
632                 self.add_line(line, src[0], src[1])

634     def get_object_members(self, want_all: bool) -> Tuple[bool, ObjectMembers]:
635         """Return `(members_check_module, members)` where `members` is a
636         list of `(membername, member)` pairs of the members of *self.object*.
637 
638         If *want_all* is True, return all members.  Else, only return those
639         members given by *self.options.members* (which may also be none).
640         """
641         warnings.warn('The implementation of Documenter.get_object_members() will be '
642                       'removed from Sphinx-6.0.', RemovedInSphinx60Warning)
643         members = get_object_members(self.object, self.objpath, self.get_attr, self.analyzer)
644         if not want_all:
645             if not self.options.members:
646                 return False, []  # type: ignore
647             # specific members given
648             selected = []
649             for name in self.options.members:  # type: str
650                 if name in members:
651                     selected.append((name, members[name].value))
652                 else:
653                     logger.warning(__('missing attribute %s in object %s') %
654                                    (name, self.fullname), type='autodoc')
655             return False, selected
656         elif self.options.inherited_members:
657             return False, [(m.name, m.value) for m in members.values()]
658         else:
659             return False, [(m.name, m.value) for m in members.values()
660                            if m.directly_defined]
661 
662     def filter_members(self, members: ObjectMembers, want_all: bool
663                        ) -> List[Tuple[str, Any, bool]]:
664         """Filter the given member list.
665 
666         Members are skipped if
667 
668         - they are private (except if given explicitly or the private-members
669           option is set)
670         - they are special methods (except if given explicitly or the
671           special-members option is set)
672         - they are undocumented (except if the undoc-members option is set)
673 
674         The user can override the skipping decision by connecting to the
675         ``autodoc-skip-member`` event.
676         """
677         def is_filtered_inherited_member(name: str, obj: Any) -> bool:
678             if inspect.isclass(self.object):
679                 for cls in self.object.__mro__:
680                     if cls.__name__ == self.options.inherited_members and cls != self.object:
681                         # given member is a member of specified *super class*
682                         return True
683                     elif name in cls.__dict__:
684                         return False
685                     elif name in self.get_attr(cls, '__annotations__', {}):
686                         return False
687                     elif isinstance(obj, ObjectMember) and obj.class_ is cls:
688                         return False
689 
690             return False
691 
692         ret = []
693 
694         # search for members in source code too
695         namespace = '.'.join(self.objpath)  # will be empty for modules
696 
697         if self.analyzer:
698             attr_docs = self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
699         else:
700             attr_docs = {}
701 
702         # process members and determine which to skip
703         for obj in members:
704             membername, member = obj
705             # if isattr is True, the member is documented as an attribute
706             if member is INSTANCEATTR:
707                 isattr = True
708             else:
709                 isattr = False
710 
711             doc = getdoc(member, self.get_attr, self.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
712                          self.parent, self.object_name)
713             if not isinstance(doc, str):
714                 # Ignore non-string __doc__
715                 doc = None
716 
717             # if the member __doc__ is the same as self's __doc__, it's just
718             # inherited and therefore not the member's doc
719             cls = self.get_attr(member, '__class__', None)
720             if cls:
721                 cls_doc = self.get_attr(cls, '__doc__', None)
722                 if cls_doc == doc:
723                     doc = None
724 
725             if isinstance(obj, ObjectMember) and obj.docstring:
726                 # hack for ClassDocumenter to inject docstring via ObjectMember
727                 doc = obj.docstring
728 
729             has_doc = bool(doc)
730 
731             metadata = extract_metadata(doc)
732             if 'private' in metadata:
733                 # consider a member private if docstring has "private" metadata
734                 isprivate = True
735             elif 'public' in metadata:
736                 # consider a member public if docstring has "public" metadata
737                 isprivate = False
738             else:
739                 isprivate = membername.startswith('_')
740 
741             keep = False
742             if safe_getattr(member, '__sphinx_mock__', None) is not None:
743                 # mocked module or object
744                 pass
745             elif self.options.exclude_members and membername in self.options.exclude_members:
746                 # remove members given by exclude-members
747                 keep = False
748             elif want_all and special_member_re.match(membername):
749                 # special __methods__
750                 if self.options.special_members and membername in self.options.special_members:
751                     if membername == '__doc__':
752                         keep = False
753                     elif is_filtered_inherited_member(membername, obj):
754                         keep = False
755                     else:
756                         keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
757                 else:
758                     keep = False
759             elif (namespace, membername) in attr_docs:
760                 if want_all and isprivate:
761                     if self.options.private_members is None:
762                         keep = False
763                     else:
764                         keep = membername in self.options.private_members
765                 else:
766                     # keep documented attributes
767                     keep = True
768                 isattr = True
769             elif want_all and isprivate:
770                 if has_doc or self.options.undoc_members:
771                     if self.options.private_members is None:
772                         keep = False
773                     elif is_filtered_inherited_member(membername, obj):
774                         keep = False
775                     else:
776                         keep = membername in self.options.private_members
777                 else:
778                     keep = False
779             else:
780                 if (self.options.members is ALL and
781                         is_filtered_inherited_member(membername, obj)):
782                     keep = False
783                 else:
784                     # ignore undocumented members if :undoc-members: is not given
785                     keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
786 
787             if isinstance(obj, ObjectMember) and obj.skipped:
788                 # forcedly skipped member (ex. a module attribute not defined in __all__)
789                 keep = False
790 
791             # give the user a chance to decide whether this member
792             # should be skipped
793             if self.env.app:
794                 # let extensions preprocess docstrings
795                 try:
796                     skip_user = self.env.app.emit_firstresult(
797                         'autodoc-skip-member', self.objtype, membername, member,
798                         not keep, self.options)
799                     if skip_user is not None:
800                         keep = not skip_user
801                 except Exception as exc:
802                     logger.warning(__('autodoc: failed to determine %r to be documented, '
803                                       'the following exception was raised:\n%s'),
804                                    member, exc, type='autodoc')
805                     keep = False
806 
807             if keep:
808                 ret.append((membername, member, isattr))
809 
810         return ret
811 
812     def document_members(self, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
813         """Generate reST for member documentation.
814 
815         If *all_members* is True, do all members, else those given by
816         *self.options.members*.
817         """
818         # set current namespace for finding members
819         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:module'] = self.modname
820         if self.objpath:
821             self.env.temp_data['autodoc:class'] = self.objpath[0]
822 
823         want_all = all_members or self.options.inherited_members or \
824             self.options.members is ALL
825         # find out which members are documentable
826         members_check_module, members = self.get_object_members(want_all)
827 
828         # document non-skipped members
829         memberdocumenters = []  # type: List[Tuple[Documenter, bool]]
830         for (mname, member, isattr) in self.filter_members(members, want_all):
831             classes = [cls for cls in self.documenters.values()
832                        if cls.can_document_member(member, mname, isattr, self)]
833             if not classes:
834                 # don't know how to document this member
835                 continue
836             # prefer the documenter with the highest priority
837             classes.sort(key=lambda cls: cls.priority)
838             # give explicitly separated module name, so that members
839             # of inner classes can be documented
840             full_mname = self.modname + '::' + \
841                 '.'.join(self.objpath + [mname])
842             documenter = classes[-1](self.directive, full_mname, self.indent)
843             memberdocumenters.append((documenter, isattr))
844 
845         member_order = self.options.member_order or self.config.autodoc_member_order
846         memberdocumenters = self.sort_members(memberdocumenters, member_order)
847 
848         for documenter, isattr in memberdocumenters:
849             documenter.generate(
850                 all_members=True, real_modname=self.real_modname,
851                 check_module=members_check_module and not isattr)
852 
853         # reset current objects
854         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:module'] = None
855         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:class'] = None
856 
857     def sort_members(self, documenters: List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]],
858                      order: str) -> List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]]:
859         """Sort the given member list."""
860         if order == 'groupwise':
861             # sort by group; alphabetically within groups
862             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0].member_order, e[0].name))
863         elif order == 'bysource':
864             if self.analyzer:
865                 # sort by source order, by virtue of the module analyzer
866                 tagorder = self.analyzer.tagorder
867 
868                 def keyfunc(entry: Tuple[Documenter, bool]) -> int:
869                     fullname = entry[0].name.split('::')[1]
870                     return tagorder.get(fullname, len(tagorder))
871                 documenters.sort(key=keyfunc)
872             else:
873                 # Assume that member discovery order matches source order.
874                 # This is a reasonable assumption in Python 3.6 and up, where
875                 # module.__dict__ is insertion-ordered.
876                 pass
877         else:  # alphabetical
878             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: e[0].name)
879 
880         return documenters
881 
882     def generate(self, more_content: Optional[StringList] = None, real_modname: str = None,
883                  check_module: bool = False, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
884         """Generate reST for the object given by *self.name*, and possibly for
885         its members.
886 
887         If *more_content* is given, include that content. If *real_modname* is
888         given, use that module name to find attribute docs. If *check_module* is
889         True, only generate if the object is defined in the module name it is
890         imported from. If *all_members* is True, document all members.
891         """
892         if not self.parse_name():
893             # need a module to import
894             logger.warning(
895                 __('don\'t know which module to import for autodocumenting '
896                    '%r (try placing a "module" or "currentmodule" directive '
897                    'in the document, or giving an explicit module name)') %
898                 self.name, type='autodoc')
899             return
900 
901         # now, import the module and get object to document
902         if not self.import_object():
903             return
904 
905         # If there is no real module defined, figure out which to use.
906         # The real module is used in the module analyzer to look up the module
907         # where the attribute documentation would actually be found in.
908         # This is used for situations where you have a module that collects the
909         # functions and classes of internal submodules.
910         guess_modname = self.get_real_modname()
911         self.real_modname = real_modname or guess_modname
912 
913         # try to also get a source code analyzer for attribute docs
914         try:
915             self.analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(self.real_modname)
916             # parse right now, to get PycodeErrors on parsing (results will
917             # be cached anyway)
918             self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
919         except PycodeError as exc:
920             logger.debug('[autodoc] module analyzer failed: %s', exc)
921             # no source file -- e.g. for builtin and C modules
922             self.analyzer = None
923             # at least add the module.__file__ as a dependency
924             if hasattr(self.module, '__file__') and self.module.__file__:
925                 self.directive.filename_set.add(self.module.__file__)
926         else:
927             self.directive.filename_set.add(self.analyzer.srcname)
928 
929         if self.real_modname != guess_modname:
930             # Add module to dependency list if target object is defined in other module.
931             try:
932                 analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(guess_modname)
933                 self.directive.filename_set.add(analyzer.srcname)
934             except PycodeError:
935                 pass
936 
937         # check __module__ of object (for members not given explicitly)
938         if check_module:
939             if not self.check_module():
940                 return
941 
942         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
943 
944         # make sure that the result starts with an empty line.  This is
945         # necessary for some situations where another directive preprocesses
946         # reST and no starting newline is present
947         self.add_line('', sourcename)
948 
949         # format the object's signature, if any
950         try:
951             sig = self.format_signature()
952         except Exception as exc:
953             logger.warning(__('error while formatting signature for %s: %s'),
954                            self.fullname, exc, type='autodoc')
955             return
956 
957         # generate the directive header and options, if applicable
958         self.add_directive_header(sig)
959         self.add_line('', sourcename)
960 
961         # e.g. the module directive doesn't have content
962         self.indent += self.content_indent
963 
964         # add all content (from docstrings, attribute docs etc.)
965         self.add_content(more_content)
966 
967         # document members, if possible
968         self.document_members(all_members)
969

1150 class DocstringSignatureMixin:
1151     """
1152     Mixin for FunctionDocumenter and MethodDocumenter to provide the
1153     feature of reading the signature from the docstring.
1154     """
1155     _new_docstrings = None  # type: List[List[str]]
1156     _signatures = None      # type: List[str]
1157 
1158     def _find_signature(self, encoding: str = None) -> Tuple[str, str]:
1159         if encoding is not None:
1160             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s._find_signature() is "
1161                           "deprecated." % self.__class__.__name__,
1162                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
1163 
1164         # candidates of the object name
1165         valid_names = [self.objpath[-1]]  # type: ignore
1166         if isinstance(self, ClassDocumenter):
1167             valid_names.append('__init__')
1168             if hasattr(self.object, '__mro__'):
1169                 valid_names.extend(cls.__name__ for cls in self.object.__mro__)
1170 
1171         docstrings = self.get_doc()
1172         self._new_docstrings = docstrings[:]
1173         self._signatures = []
1174         result = None
1175         for i, doclines in enumerate(docstrings):
1176             for j, line in enumerate(doclines):
1177                 if not line:
1178                     # no lines in docstring, no match
1179                     break
1180 
1181                 if line.endswith('\\'):
1182                     multiline = True
1183                     line = line.rstrip('\\').rstrip()
1184                 else:
1185                     multiline = False
1186 
1187                 # match first line of docstring against signature RE
1188                 match = py_ext_sig_re.match(line)
1189                 if not match:
1190                     continue
1191                 exmod, path, base, args, retann = match.groups()
1192 
1193                 # the base name must match ours
1194                 if base not in valid_names:
1195                     continue
1196 
1197                 # re-prepare docstring to ignore more leading indentation
1198                 tab_width = self.directive.state.document.settings.tab_width  # type: ignore
1199                 self._new_docstrings[i] = prepare_docstring('\n'.join(doclines[j + 1:]),
1200                                                             tabsize=tab_width)
1201 
1202                 if result is None:
1203                     # first signature
1204                     result = args, retann
1205                 else:
1206                     # subsequent signatures
1207                     self._signatures.append("(%s) -> %s" % (args, retann))
1208 
1209                 if multiline:
1210                     # the signature have multiple signatures on docstring
1211                     continue
1212                 else:
1213                     # don't look any further
1214                     break
1215 
1216             if result:
1217                 # finish the loop when signature found
1218                 break
1219 
1220         return result
1221 
1222     def get_doc(self, encoding: str = None, ignore: int = None) -> Optional[List[List[str]]]:
1223         if encoding is not None:
1224             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s.get_doc() is deprecated."
1225                           % self.__class__.__name__,
1226                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
1227         if self._new_docstrings is not None:
1228             return self._new_docstrings
1229         return super().get_doc(None, ignore)  # type: ignore
1230 
1231     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
1232         if self.args is None and self.config.autodoc_docstring_signature:  # type: ignore
1233             # only act if a signature is not explicitly given already, and if
1234             # the feature is enabled
1235             result = self._find_signature()
1236             if result is not None:
1237                 self.args, self.retann = result
1238         sig = super().format_signature(**kwargs)  # type: ignore
1239         if self._signatures:
1240             return "\n".join([sig] + self._signatures)
1241         else:
1242             return sig

1434     def _get_signature(self) -> Tuple[Optional[Any], Optional[str], Optional[Signature]]:
1435         def get_user_defined_function_or_method(obj: Any, attr: str) -> Any:
1436             """ Get the `attr` function or method from `obj`, if it is user-defined. """
1437             if inspect.is_builtin_class_method(obj, attr):
1438                 return None
1439             attr = self.get_attr(obj, attr, None)
1440             if not (inspect.ismethod(attr) or inspect.isfunction(attr)):
1441                 return None
1442             return attr
1443 
1444         # This sequence is copied from inspect._signature_from_callable.
1445         # ValueError means that no signature could be found, so we keep going.
1446 
1447         # First, we check the obj has a __signature__ attribute
1448         if (hasattr(self.object, '__signature__') and
1449                 isinstance(self.object.__signature__, Signature)):
1450             return None, None, self.object.__signature__
1451 
1452         # Next, let's see if it has an overloaded __call__ defined
1453         # in its metaclass
1454         call = get_user_defined_function_or_method(type(self.object), '__call__')
1455 
1456         if call is not None:
1457             if "{0.__module__}.{0.__qualname__}".format(call) in _METACLASS_CALL_BLACKLIST:
1458                 call = None
1459 
1460         if call is not None:
1461             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', call, True)
1462             try:
1463                 sig = inspect.signature(call, bound_method=True,
1464                                         type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1465                 return type(self.object), '__call__', sig
1466             except ValueError:
1467                 pass
1468 
1469         # Now we check if the 'obj' class has a '__new__' method
1470         new = get_user_defined_function_or_method(self.object, '__new__')
1471 
1472         if new is not None:
1473             if "{0.__module__}.{0.__qualname__}".format(new) in _CLASS_NEW_BLACKLIST:
1474                 new = None
1475 
1476         if new is not None:
1477             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', new, True)
1478             try:
1479                 sig = inspect.signature(new, bound_method=True,
1480                                         type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1481                 return self.object, '__new__', sig
1482             except ValueError:
1483                 pass
1484 
1485         # Finally, we should have at least __init__ implemented
1486         init = get_user_defined_function_or_method(self.object, '__init__')
1487         if init is not None:
1488             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', init, True)
1489             try:
1490                 sig = inspect.signature(init, bound_method=True,
1491                                         type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1492                 return self.object, '__init__', sig
1493             except ValueError:
1494                 pass
1495 
1496         # None of the attributes are user-defined, so fall back to let inspect
1497         # handle it.
1498         # We don't know the exact method that inspect.signature will read
1499         # the signature from, so just pass the object itself to our hook.
1500         self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', self.object, False)
1501         try:
1502             sig = inspect.signature(self.object, bound_method=False,
1503                                     type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1504             return None, None, sig
1505         except ValueError:
1506             pass
1507 
1508         # Still no signature: happens e.g. for old-style classes
1509         # with __init__ in C and no `__text_signature__`.
1510         return None, None, None

1636         attrdocstring = self.get_attr(self.object, '__doc__', None)
1637         if attrdocstring:
1638             docstrings.append(attrdocstring)
1639 
1640         # for classes, what the "docstring" is can be controlled via a
1641         # config value; the default is only the class docstring
1642         if content in ('both', 'init'):
1643             __init__ = self.get_attr(self.object, '__init__', None)
1644             initdocstring = getdoc(__init__, self.get_attr,
1645                                    self.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
1646                                    self.parent, self.object_name)

1648             if (initdocstring is not None and
1649                 (initdocstring == object.__init__.__doc__ or  # for pypy
1650                  initdocstring.strip() == object.__init__.__doc__)):  # for !pypy
1651                 initdocstring = None

1654                 __new__ = self.get_attr(self.object, '__new__', None)
1655                 initdocstring = getdoc(__new__, self.get_attr,
1656                                        self.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
1657                                        self.parent, self.object_name)

1659                 if (initdocstring is not None and
1660                     (initdocstring == object.__new__.__doc__ or  # for pypy
1661                      initdocstring.strip() == object.__new__.__doc__)):  # for !pypy
1662                     initdocstring = None

1664                 if content == 'init':
1665                     docstrings = [initdocstring]
1666                 else:
1667                     docstrings.append(initdocstring)

1967             return ret

1972             obj = self.object
1973

1975                 inspect.isstaticmethod(obj, cls=self.parent, name=self.object_name)):

1981     def format_args(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
1982         if self.config.autodoc_typehints in ('none', 'description'):
1983             kwargs.setdefault('show_annotation', False)
1984 
1985         try:
1986             if self.object == object.__init__ and self.parent != object:
1987                 # Classes not having own __init__() method are shown as no arguments.
1988                 #
1989                 # Note: The signature of object.__init__() is (self, /, *args, **kwargs).
1990                 #       But it makes users confused.
1991                 args = '()'
1992             else:
1993                 if inspect.isstaticmethod(self.object, cls=self.parent, name=self.object_name):
1994                     self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', self.object, False)
1995                     sig = inspect.signature(self.object, bound_method=False,
1996                                             type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1997                 else:
1998                     self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', self.object, True)
1999                     sig = inspect.signature(self.object, bound_method=True,
2000                                             type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
2001                 args = stringify_signature(sig, **kwargs)
2002         except TypeError as exc:
2003             logger.warning(__("Failed to get a method signature for %s: %s"),
2004                            self.fullname, exc)
2005             return None
2006         except ValueError:
2007             args = ''
2008 
2009         if self.config.strip_signature_backslash:
2010             # escape backslashes for reST
2011             args = args.replace('\\', '\\\\')
2012         return args

2014     def add_directive_header(self, sig: str) -> None:
2015         super().add_directive_header(sig)
2016 
2017         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
2018         obj = self.parent.__dict__.get(self.object_name, self.object)
2019         if inspect.isabstractmethod(obj):
2020             self.add_line('   :abstractmethod:', sourcename)
2021         if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(obj):
2022             self.add_line('   :async:', sourcename)
2023         if inspect.isclassmethod(obj):
2024             self.add_line('   :classmethod:', sourcename)
2025         if inspect.isstaticmethod(obj, cls=self.parent, name=self.object_name):
2026             self.add_line('   :staticmethod:', sourcename)
2027         if self.analyzer and '.'.join(self.objpath) in self.analyzer.finals:
2028             self.add_line('   :final:', sourcename)
2029 
2030     def document_members(self, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
2031         pass
2032 
2033     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
2034         sigs = []
2035         if (self.analyzer and
2036                 '.'.join(self.objpath) in self.analyzer.overloads and
2037                 self.config.autodoc_typehints == 'signature'):
2038             # Use signatures for overloaded methods instead of the implementation method.
2039             overloaded = True
2040         else:
2041             overloaded = False
2042             sig = super().format_signature(**kwargs)
2043             sigs.append(sig)
2044 
2045         meth = self.parent.__dict__.get(self.objpath[-1])
2046         if inspect.is_singledispatch_method(meth):
2047             # append signature of singledispatch'ed functions
2048             for typ, func in meth.dispatcher.registry.items():
2049                 if typ is object:
2050                     pass  # default implementation. skipped.
2051                 else:
2052                     self.annotate_to_first_argument(func, typ)
2053 
2054                     documenter = MethodDocumenter(self.directive, '')
2055                     documenter.parent = self.parent
2056                     documenter.object = func
2057                     documenter.objpath = [None]
2058                     sigs.append(documenter.format_signature())
2059         if overloaded:
2060             __globals__ = safe_getattr(self.object, '__globals__', {})
2061             for overload in self.analyzer.overloads.get('.'.join(self.objpath)):
2062                 overload = evaluate_signature(overload, __globals__,
2063                                               self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
2064 
2065                 if not inspect.isstaticmethod(self.object, cls=self.parent,
2066                                               name=self.object_name):
2067                     parameters = list(overload.parameters.values())
2068                     overload = overload.replace(parameters=parameters[1:])
2069                 sig = stringify_signature(overload, **kwargs)
2070                 sigs.append(sig)
2071 
2072         return "\n".join(sigs)
2073 
2074     def annotate_to_first_argument(self, func: Callable, typ: Type) -> None:
2075         """Annotate type hint to the first argument of function if needed."""
2076         try:
2077             sig = inspect.signature(func, type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
2078         except TypeError as exc:
2079             logger.warning(__("Failed to get a method signature for %s: %s"),
2080                            self.fullname, exc)
2081             return
2082         except ValueError:
2083             return
2084         if len(sig.parameters) == 1:
2085             return
2086 
2087         params = list(sig.parameters.values())
2088         if params[1].annotation is Parameter.empty:
2089             params[1] = params[1].replace(annotation=typ)
2090             try:
2091                 func.__signature__ = sig.replace(parameters=params)  # type: ignore
2092             except TypeError:
2093                 # failed to update signature (ex. built-in or extension types)
2094                 return

Instance variables link to other variables of the same name in the project
**Describe the bug**
Assume autodoc is used via apidoc. In theory other combinations of autodoc (or maybe even without it) can cause this to occur, but this would be the most common occurrence.

If a global variable (or really, any kind of variable, just that this would be the most common occurrence) exists, and inside a class you decide to document a variable of the same name, the document of the instance variable will link to the other occurence of a variable under the same name.

This can even occur across subpackages and even across other classes of those subpackages (although this appears to occur less often and seemingly...randomly? This only occurs sometimes (presumably due to the referencing heuristic?)).

This is a problem, because, for example, `somepackage.subA::Foo.somename` could be and usually is completely unrelated to  `somepackage.subB::Bar.somename`. Furthermore, `somepackage::Foo.somename` (instance variable) could be completely unrelated to `somepackage.somename` (global variable). Of course this latter example is far less likely, but the *auto*linking of these two together, is strange.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
```
$ git clone https://github.com/13steinj/sphinx-issue-examples/
$ cd sphinx-issue-examples
$ git checkout referenced_variables
$ cd docs
$ make html
$ cd _build/html && python -m SimpleHTTPServer 8008
```
then open 127.0.0.1:8008 in a browser

**Expected behavior**
That the class variable documentation not be linked to any other. It is unreasonable to expect these to be in any way related whatsoever. If they *happen* to be, the user can decide to document it as such with a simple reference to the other variable, such as "see :const:\`somename\`".

There is no reason that a `limit` variable on some class of some database-oriented subpackage autolink to the `limit` variable on some class of some config-related subpackage (this is what occurred in my codebase, which is private at least while in development. I cannot provide anything except a heavily censored screenshot, as I do not know of a way to trick the referencing heuristic to cause a link to occur in an demo repo).

167 def _parse_arglist(arglist: str, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> addnodes.desc_parameterlist:
168     """Parse a list of arguments using AST parser"""
169     params = addnodes.desc_parameterlist(arglist)
170     sig = signature_from_str('(%s)' % arglist)
171     last_kind = None
172     for param in sig.parameters.values():
173         if param.kind != param.POSITIONAL_ONLY and last_kind == param.POSITIONAL_ONLY:
174             # PEP-570: Separator for Positional Only Parameter: /
175             params += addnodes.desc_parameter('', '', addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '/'))
176         if param.kind == param.KEYWORD_ONLY and last_kind in (param.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD,
177                                                               param.POSITIONAL_ONLY,
178                                                               None):
179             # PEP-3102: Separator for Keyword Only Parameter: *
180             params += addnodes.desc_parameter('', '', addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '*'))
181 
182         node = addnodes.desc_parameter()
183         if param.kind == param.VAR_POSITIONAL:
184             node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '*')
185             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', param.name)
186         elif param.kind == param.VAR_KEYWORD:
187             node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '**')
188             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', param.name)
189         else:
190             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', param.name)
191 
192         if param.annotation is not param.empty:
193             children = _parse_annotation(param.annotation, env)
194             node += addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', ':')
195             node += nodes.Text(' ')
196             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', '', *children)  # type: ignore
197         if param.default is not param.empty:
198             if param.annotation is not param.empty:
199                 node += nodes.Text(' ')
200                 node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '=')
201                 node += nodes.Text(' ')
202             else:
203                 node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '=')
204             node += nodes.inline('', param.default, classes=['default_value'],
205                                  support_smartquotes=False)
206 
207         params += node
208         last_kind = param.kind
209 
210     if last_kind == Parameter.POSITIONAL_ONLY:
211         # PEP-570: Separator for Positional Only Parameter: /
212         params += addnodes.desc_parameter('', '', addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '/'))
213 
214     return params
215

217 def _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode: desc_signature, arglist: str) -> None:
218     """"Parse" a list of arguments separated by commas.
219 
220     Arguments can have "optional" annotations given by enclosing them in
221     brackets.  Currently, this will split at any comma, even if it's inside a
222     string literal (e.g. default argument value).
223     """
224     paramlist = addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
225     stack = [paramlist]  # type: List[Element]
226     try:
227         for argument in arglist.split(','):
228             argument = argument.strip()
229             ends_open = ends_close = 0
230             while argument.startswith('['):
231                 stack.append(addnodes.desc_optional())
232                 stack[-2] += stack[-1]
233                 argument = argument[1:].strip()
234             while argument.startswith(']'):
235                 stack.pop()
236                 argument = argument[1:].strip()
237             while argument.endswith(']') and not argument.endswith('[]'):
238                 ends_close += 1
239                 argument = argument[:-1].strip()
240             while argument.endswith('['):
241                 ends_open += 1
242                 argument = argument[:-1].strip()
243             if argument:
244                 stack[-1] += addnodes.desc_parameter(argument, argument)
245             while ends_open:
246                 stack.append(addnodes.desc_optional())
247                 stack[-2] += stack[-1]
248                 ends_open -= 1
249             while ends_close:
250                 stack.pop()
251                 ends_close -= 1
252         if len(stack) != 1:
253             raise IndexError
254     except IndexError:
255         # if there are too few or too many elements on the stack, just give up
256         # and treat the whole argument list as one argument, discarding the
257         # already partially populated paramlist node
258         paramlist = addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
259         paramlist += addnodes.desc_parameter(arglist, arglist)
260         signode += paramlist
261     else:
262         signode += paramlist

265 # This override allows our inline type specifiers to behave like :class: link
266 # when it comes to handling "." and "~" prefixes.
267 class PyXrefMixin:
268     def make_xref(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
269                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
270                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> Node:
271         result = super().make_xref(rolename, domain, target,  # type: ignore
272                                    innernode, contnode, env)
273         result['refspecific'] = True
274         result['py:module'] = env.ref_context.get('py:module')
275         result['py:class'] = env.ref_context.get('py:class')
276         if target.startswith(('.', '~')):
277             prefix, result['reftarget'] = target[0], target[1:]
278             if prefix == '.':
279                 text = target[1:]
280             elif prefix == '~':
281                 text = target.split('.')[-1]
282             for node in result.traverse(nodes.Text):
283                 node.parent[node.parent.index(node)] = nodes.Text(text)
284                 break
285         return result
286 
287     def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
288                    innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
289                    contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
290         delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+)'
291         delims_re = re.compile(delims)
292         sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)
293 
294         split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)
295 
296         results = []
297         for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
298             if split_contnode:
299                 contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)
300 
301             if delims_re.match(sub_target):
302                 results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
303             else:
304                 results.append(self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
305                                               innernode, contnode, env))
306 
307         return results
308
