384     def handle_signature(self, sig: str, signode: desc_signature) -> Tuple[str, str]:
385         """Transform a Python signature into RST nodes.
386 
387         Return (fully qualified name of the thing, classname if any).
388 
389         If inside a class, the current class name is handled intelligently:
390         * it is stripped from the displayed name if present
391         * it is added to the full name (return value) if not present
392         """
393         m = py_sig_re.match(sig)
394         if m is None:
395             raise ValueError
396         prefix, name, arglist, retann = m.groups()
397 
398         # determine module and class name (if applicable), as well as full name
399         modname = self.options.get('module', self.env.ref_context.get('py:module'))
400         classname = self.env.ref_context.get('py:class')
401         if classname:
402             add_module = False
403             if prefix and (prefix == classname or
404                            prefix.startswith(classname + ".")):
405                 fullname = prefix + name
406                 # class name is given again in the signature
407                 prefix = prefix[len(classname):].lstrip('.')
408             elif prefix:
409                 # class name is given in the signature, but different
410                 # (shouldn't happen)
411                 fullname = classname + '.' + prefix + name
412             else:
413                 # class name is not given in the signature
414                 fullname = classname + '.' + name
415         else:
416             add_module = True
417             if prefix:
418                 classname = prefix.rstrip('.')
419                 fullname = prefix + name
420             else:
421                 classname = ''
422                 fullname = name
423 
424         signode['module'] = modname
425         signode['class'] = classname
426         signode['fullname'] = fullname
427 
428         sig_prefix = self.get_signature_prefix(sig)
429         if sig_prefix:
430             signode += addnodes.desc_annotation(sig_prefix, sig_prefix)
431 
432         if prefix:
433             signode += addnodes.desc_addname(prefix, prefix)
434         elif add_module and self.env.config.add_module_names:
435             if modname and modname != 'exceptions':
436                 # exceptions are a special case, since they are documented in the
437                 # 'exceptions' module.
438                 nodetext = modname + '.'
439                 signode += addnodes.desc_addname(nodetext, nodetext)
440 
441         signode += addnodes.desc_name(name, name)
442         if arglist:
443             try:
444                 signode += _parse_arglist(arglist, self.env)
445             except SyntaxError:
446                 # fallback to parse arglist original parser.
447                 # it supports to represent optional arguments (ex. "func(foo [, bar])")
448                 _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode, arglist)
449             except NotImplementedError as exc:
450                 logger.warning("could not parse arglist (%r): %s", arglist, exc,
451                                location=signode)
452                 _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode, arglist)
453         else:
454             if self.needs_arglist():
455                 # for callables, add an empty parameter list
456                 signode += addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
457 
458         if retann:
459             children = _parse_annotation(retann, self.env)
460             signode += addnodes.desc_returns(retann, '', *children)
461 
462         anno = self.options.get('annotation')
463         if anno:
464             signode += addnodes.desc_annotation(' ' + anno, ' ' + anno)
465 
466         return fullname, prefix
467

472     def add_target_and_index(self, name_cls: Tuple[str, str], sig: str,
473                              signode: desc_signature) -> None:
474         modname = self.options.get('module', self.env.ref_context.get('py:module'))
475         fullname = (modname + '.' if modname else '') + name_cls[0]
476         node_id = make_id(self.env, self.state.document, '', fullname)

492                                location=signode)

499     def before_content(self) -> None:
500         """Handle object nesting before content
501 
502         :py:class:`PyObject` represents Python language constructs. For
503         constructs that are nestable, such as a Python classes, this method will
504         build up a stack of the nesting hierarchy so that it can be later
505         de-nested correctly, in :py:meth:`after_content`.
506 
507         For constructs that aren't nestable, the stack is bypassed, and instead
508         only the most recent object is tracked. This object prefix name will be
509         removed with :py:meth:`after_content`.
510         """
511         prefix = None
512         if self.names:
513             # fullname and name_prefix come from the `handle_signature` method.
514             # fullname represents the full object name that is constructed using
515             # object nesting and explicit prefixes. `name_prefix` is the
516             # explicit prefix given in a signature
517             (fullname, name_prefix) = self.names[-1]
518             if self.allow_nesting:
519                 prefix = fullname
520             elif name_prefix:
521                 prefix = name_prefix.strip('.')
522         if prefix:
523             self.env.ref_context['py:class'] = prefix
524             if self.allow_nesting:
525                 classes = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:classes', [])
526                 classes.append(prefix)
527         if 'module' in self.options:
528             modules = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:modules', [])
529             modules.append(self.env.ref_context.get('py:module'))
530             self.env.ref_context['py:module'] = self.options['module']
531 
532     def after_content(self) -> None:
533         """Handle object de-nesting after content
534 
535         If this class is a nestable object, removing the last nested class prefix
536         ends further nesting in the object.
537 
538         If this class is not a nestable object, the list of classes should not
539         be altered as we didn't affect the nesting levels in
540         :py:meth:`before_content`.
541         """
542         classes = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:classes', [])
543         if self.allow_nesting:
544             try:
545                 classes.pop()
546             except IndexError:
547                 pass
548         self.env.ref_context['py:class'] = (classes[-1] if len(classes) > 0
549                                             else None)
550         if 'module' in self.options:
551             modules = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:modules', [])
552             if modules:
553                 self.env.ref_context['py:module'] = modules.pop()
554             else:
555                 self.env.ref_context.pop('py:module')
556

966                  ) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[str, List[IndexEntry]]], bool]:
967         content = {}  # type: Dict[str, List[IndexEntry]]
968         # list of prefixes to ignore
969         ignores = None  # type: List[str]
970         ignores = self.domain.env.config['modindex_common_prefix']  # type: ignore
971         ignores = sorted(ignores, key=len, reverse=True)

973         modules = sorted(self.domain.data['modules'].items(),
974                          key=lambda x: x[0].lower())
975         # sort out collapsable modules
976         prev_modname = ''
977         num_toplevels = 0
978         for modname, (docname, node_id, synopsis, platforms, deprecated) in modules:
979             if docnames and docname not in docnames:
980                 continue
981 
982             for ignore in ignores:
983                 if modname.startswith(ignore):
984                     modname = modname[len(ignore):]
985                     stripped = ignore
986                     break
987             else:
988                 stripped = ''
989 
990             # we stripped the whole module name?
991             if not modname:
992                 modname, stripped = stripped, ''
993 
994             entries = content.setdefault(modname[0].lower(), [])
995 
996             package = modname.split('.')[0]
997             if package != modname:
998                 # it's a submodule
999                 if prev_modname == package:
1000                     # first submodule - make parent a group head
1001                     if entries:
1002                         last = entries[-1]
1003                         entries[-1] = IndexEntry(last[0], 1, last[2], last[3],
1004                                                  last[4], last[5], last[6])
1005                 elif not prev_modname.startswith(package):
1006                     # submodule without parent in list, add dummy entry
1007                     entries.append(IndexEntry(stripped + package, 1, '', '', '', '', ''))
1008                 subtype = 2
1009             else:
1010                 num_toplevels += 1
1011                 subtype = 0
1012 
1013             qualifier = _('Deprecated') if deprecated else ''
1014             entries.append(IndexEntry(stripped + modname, subtype, docname,
1015                                       node_id, platforms, qualifier, synopsis))
1016             prev_modname = modname

1018         # apply heuristics when to collapse modindex at page load:
1019         # only collapse if number of toplevel modules is larger than
1020         # number of submodules
1021         collapse = len(modules) - num_toplevels < num_toplevels
1022 
1023         # sort by first letter

82 def type_to_xref(text: str, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> addnodes.pending_xref:
83     """Convert a type string to a cross reference node."""
84     if text == 'None':
85         reftype = 'obj'
86     else:
87         reftype = 'class'
88 
89     if env:
90         kwargs = {'py:module': env.ref_context.get('py:module'),
91                   'py:class': env.ref_context.get('py:class')}
92     else:
93         kwargs = {}
94 
95     if env.config.python_use_unqualified_type_names:
96         # Note: It would be better to use qualname to describe the object to support support
97         # nested classes.  But python domain can't access the real python object because this
98         # module should work not-dynamically.
99         shortname = text.split('.')[-1]
100         contnodes: List[Node] = [pending_xref_condition('', shortname, condition='resolved'),
101                                  pending_xref_condition('', text, condition='*')]
102     else:
103         contnodes = [nodes.Text(text)]
104 
105     return pending_xref('', *contnodes,
106                         refdomain='py', reftype=reftype, reftarget=text, **kwargs)

109 def _parse_annotation(annotation: str, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
110     """Parse type annotation."""
111     def unparse(node: ast.AST) -> List[Node]:
112         if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
113             return [nodes.Text("%s.%s" % (unparse(node.value)[0], node.attr))]
114         elif isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
115             result: List[Node] = unparse(node.left)
116             result.extend(unparse(node.op))
117             result.extend(unparse(node.right))
118             return result
119         elif isinstance(node, ast.BitOr):
120             return [nodes.Text(' '), addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', '|'), nodes.Text(' ')]
121         elif isinstance(node, ast.Constant):  # type: ignore
122             if node.value is Ellipsis:
123                 return [addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', "...")]
124             else:
125                 return [nodes.Text(node.value)]
126         elif isinstance(node, ast.Expr):
127             return unparse(node.value)
128         elif isinstance(node, ast.Index):
129             return unparse(node.value)
130         elif isinstance(node, ast.List):
131             result = [addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', '[')]
132             for elem in node.elts:
133                 result.extend(unparse(elem))
134                 result.append(addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', ', '))
135             result.pop()
136             result.append(addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', ']'))
137             return result
138         elif isinstance(node, ast.Module):
139             return sum((unparse(e) for e in node.body), [])
140         elif isinstance(node, ast.Name):
141             return [nodes.Text(node.id)]
142         elif isinstance(node, ast.Subscript):
143             result = unparse(node.value)
144             result.append(addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', '['))
145             result.extend(unparse(node.slice))
146             result.append(addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', ']'))
147             return result
148         elif isinstance(node, ast.Tuple):
149             if node.elts:
150                 result = []
151                 for elem in node.elts:
152                     result.extend(unparse(elem))
153                     result.append(addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', ', '))
154                 result.pop()
155             else:
156                 result = [addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', '('),
157                           addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', ')')]
158 
159             return result
160         else:
161             if sys.version_info < (3, 8):
162                 if isinstance(node, ast.Ellipsis):
163                     return [addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', "...")]
164                 elif isinstance(node, ast.NameConstant):
165                     return [nodes.Text(node.value)]
166 
167             raise SyntaxError  # unsupported syntax
168 
169     if env is None:
170         warnings.warn("The env parameter for _parse_annotation becomes required now.",
171                       RemovedInSphinx50Warning, stacklevel=2)
172 
173     try:
174         tree = ast_parse(annotation)
175         result = unparse(tree)
176         for i, node in enumerate(result):
177             if isinstance(node, nodes.Text) and node.strip():
178                 result[i] = type_to_xref(str(node), env)
179         return result
180     except SyntaxError:
181         return [type_to_xref(annotation, env)]
182

184 def _parse_arglist(arglist: str, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> addnodes.desc_parameterlist:
185     """Parse a list of arguments using AST parser"""
186     params = addnodes.desc_parameterlist(arglist)
187     sig = signature_from_str('(%s)' % arglist)
188     last_kind = None
189     for param in sig.parameters.values():
190         if param.kind != param.POSITIONAL_ONLY and last_kind == param.POSITIONAL_ONLY:
191             # PEP-570: Separator for Positional Only Parameter: /
192             params += addnodes.desc_parameter('', '', addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '/'))
193         if param.kind == param.KEYWORD_ONLY and last_kind in (param.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD,
194                                                               param.POSITIONAL_ONLY,
195                                                               None):
196             # PEP-3102: Separator for Keyword Only Parameter: *
197             params += addnodes.desc_parameter('', '', addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '*'))
198 
199         node = addnodes.desc_parameter()
200         if param.kind == param.VAR_POSITIONAL:
201             node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '*')
202             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', param.name)
203         elif param.kind == param.VAR_KEYWORD:
204             node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '**')
205             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', param.name)
206         else:
207             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', param.name)
208 
209         if param.annotation is not param.empty:
210             children = _parse_annotation(param.annotation, env)
211             node += addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', ':')
212             node += nodes.Text(' ')
213             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', '', *children)  # type: ignore
214         if param.default is not param.empty:
215             if param.annotation is not param.empty:
216                 node += nodes.Text(' ')
217                 node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '=')
218                 node += nodes.Text(' ')
219             else:
220                 node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '=')
221             node += nodes.inline('', param.default, classes=['default_value'],
222                                  support_smartquotes=False)
223 
224         params += node
225         last_kind = param.kind
226 
227     if last_kind == Parameter.POSITIONAL_ONLY:
228         # PEP-570: Separator for Positional Only Parameter: /
229         params += addnodes.desc_parameter('', '', addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '/'))
230 
231     return params
232

234 def _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode: desc_signature, arglist: str) -> None:
235     """"Parse" a list of arguments separated by commas.
236 
237     Arguments can have "optional" annotations given by enclosing them in
238     brackets.  Currently, this will split at any comma, even if it's inside a
239     string literal (e.g. default argument value).
240     """
241     paramlist = addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
242     stack: List[Element] = [paramlist]
243     try:
244         for argument in arglist.split(','):
245             argument = argument.strip()
246             ends_open = ends_close = 0
247             while argument.startswith('['):
248                 stack.append(addnodes.desc_optional())
249                 stack[-2] += stack[-1]
250                 argument = argument[1:].strip()
251             while argument.startswith(']'):
252                 stack.pop()
253                 argument = argument[1:].strip()
254             while argument.endswith(']') and not argument.endswith('[]'):
255                 ends_close += 1
256                 argument = argument[:-1].strip()
257             while argument.endswith('['):
258                 ends_open += 1
259                 argument = argument[:-1].strip()
260             if argument:
261                 stack[-1] += addnodes.desc_parameter(argument, argument)
262             while ends_open:
263                 stack.append(addnodes.desc_optional())
264                 stack[-2] += stack[-1]
265                 ends_open -= 1
266             while ends_close:
267                 stack.pop()
268                 ends_close -= 1
269         if len(stack) != 1:
270             raise IndexError
271     except IndexError:
272         # if there are too few or too many elements on the stack, just give up
273         # and treat the whole argument list as one argument, discarding the
274         # already partially populated paramlist node
275         paramlist = addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
276         paramlist += addnodes.desc_parameter(arglist, arglist)
277         signode += paramlist
278     else:
279         signode += paramlist

282 # This override allows our inline type specifiers to behave like :class: link
283 # when it comes to handling "." and "~" prefixes.
284 class PyXrefMixin:
285     def make_xref(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
286                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
287                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> Node:
288         result = super().make_xref(rolename, domain, target,  # type: ignore
289                                    innernode, contnode, env)
290         result['refspecific'] = True
291         result['py:module'] = env.ref_context.get('py:module')
292         result['py:class'] = env.ref_context.get('py:class')
293         if target.startswith(('.', '~')):
294             prefix, result['reftarget'] = target[0], target[1:]
295             if prefix == '.':
296                 text = target[1:]
297             elif prefix == '~':
298                 text = target.split('.')[-1]
299             for node in result.traverse(nodes.Text):
300                 node.parent[node.parent.index(node)] = nodes.Text(text)
301                 break
302         return result
303 
304     def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
305                    innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
306                    contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
307         delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
308         delims_re = re.compile(delims)
309         sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)
310 
311         split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)
312 
313         results = []
314         for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
315             if split_contnode:
316                 contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)
317 
318             if delims_re.match(sub_target):
319                 results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
320             else:
321                 results.append(self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
322                                               innernode, contnode, env))
323 
324         return results
325

389     def get_signature_prefix(self, sig: str) -> str:

391         signature.

401     def handle_signature(self, sig: str, signode: desc_signature) -> Tuple[str, str]:
402         """Transform a Python signature into RST nodes.
403 
404         Return (fully qualified name of the thing, classname if any).
405 
406         If inside a class, the current class name is handled intelligently:
407         * it is stripped from the displayed name if present
408         * it is added to the full name (return value) if not present
409         """
410         m = py_sig_re.match(sig)
411         if m is None:
412             raise ValueError
413         prefix, name, arglist, retann = m.groups()
414 
415         # determine module and class name (if applicable), as well as full name
416         modname = self.options.get('module', self.env.ref_context.get('py:module'))
417         classname = self.env.ref_context.get('py:class')
418         if classname:
419             add_module = False
420             if prefix and (prefix == classname or
421                            prefix.startswith(classname + ".")):
422                 fullname = prefix + name
423                 # class name is given again in the signature
424                 prefix = prefix[len(classname):].lstrip('.')
425             elif prefix:
426                 # class name is given in the signature, but different
427                 # (shouldn't happen)
428                 fullname = classname + '.' + prefix + name
429             else:
430                 # class name is not given in the signature
431                 fullname = classname + '.' + name
432         else:
433             add_module = True
434             if prefix:
435                 classname = prefix.rstrip('.')
436                 fullname = prefix + name
437             else:
438                 classname = ''
439                 fullname = name
440 
441         signode['module'] = modname
442         signode['class'] = classname
443         signode['fullname'] = fullname
444 
445         sig_prefix = self.get_signature_prefix(sig)
446         if sig_prefix:
447             signode += addnodes.desc_annotation(sig_prefix, sig_prefix)
448 
449         if prefix:
450             signode += addnodes.desc_addname(prefix, prefix)
451         elif add_module and self.env.config.add_module_names:
452             if modname and modname != 'exceptions':
453                 # exceptions are a special case, since they are documented in the
454                 # 'exceptions' module.
455                 nodetext = modname + '.'
456                 signode += addnodes.desc_addname(nodetext, nodetext)
457 
458         signode += addnodes.desc_name(name, name)
459         if arglist:
460             try:
461                 signode += _parse_arglist(arglist, self.env)
462             except SyntaxError:
463                 # fallback to parse arglist original parser.
464                 # it supports to represent optional arguments (ex. "func(foo [, bar])")
465                 _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode, arglist)
466             except NotImplementedError as exc:
467                 logger.warning("could not parse arglist (%r): %s", arglist, exc,
468                                location=signode)
469                 _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode, arglist)
470         else:
471             if self.needs_arglist():
472                 # for callables, add an empty parameter list
473                 signode += addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
474 
475         if retann:
476             children = _parse_annotation(retann, self.env)
477             signode += addnodes.desc_returns(retann, '', *children)
478 
479         anno = self.options.get('annotation')
480         if anno:
481             signode += addnodes.desc_annotation(' ' + anno, ' ' + anno)
482 
483         return fullname, prefix
484

489     def add_target_and_index(self, name_cls: Tuple[str, str], sig: str,
490                              signode: desc_signature) -> None:
491         modname = self.options.get('module', self.env.ref_context.get('py:module'))
492         fullname = (modname + '.' if modname else '') + name_cls[0]
493         node_id = make_id(self.env, self.state.document, '', fullname)
494         signode['ids'].append(node_id)
495 
496         # Assign old styled node_id(fullname) not to break old hyperlinks (if possible)
497         # Note: Will removed in Sphinx-5.0  (RemovedInSphinx50Warning)
498         if node_id != fullname and fullname not in self.state.document.ids:
499             signode['ids'].append(fullname)

501         self.state.document.note_explicit_target(signode)
502 
503         domain = cast(PythonDomain, self.env.get_domain('py'))
504         domain.note_object(fullname, self.objtype, node_id, location=signode)
505 
506         canonical_name = self.options.get('canonical')
507         if canonical_name:
508             domain.note_object(canonical_name, self.objtype, node_id, aliased=True,
509                                location=signode)
510 
511         if 'noindexentry' not in self.options:
512             indextext = self.get_index_text(modname, name_cls)
513             if indextext:
514                 self.indexnode['entries'].append(('single', indextext, node_id, '', None))

516     def before_content(self) -> None:
517         """Handle object nesting before content
518 
519         :py:class:`PyObject` represents Python language constructs. For
520         constructs that are nestable, such as a Python classes, this method will
521         build up a stack of the nesting hierarchy so that it can be later
522         de-nested correctly, in :py:meth:`after_content`.
523 
524         For constructs that aren't nestable, the stack is bypassed, and instead
525         only the most recent object is tracked. This object prefix name will be
526         removed with :py:meth:`after_content`.
527         """
528         prefix = None
529         if self.names:
530             # fullname and name_prefix come from the `handle_signature` method.
531             # fullname represents the full object name that is constructed using
532             # object nesting and explicit prefixes. `name_prefix` is the
533             # explicit prefix given in a signature
534             (fullname, name_prefix) = self.names[-1]
535             if self.allow_nesting:
536                 prefix = fullname
537             elif name_prefix:
538                 prefix = name_prefix.strip('.')
539         if prefix:
540             self.env.ref_context['py:class'] = prefix
541             if self.allow_nesting:
542                 classes = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:classes', [])
543                 classes.append(prefix)
544         if 'module' in self.options:
545             modules = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:modules', [])
546             modules.append(self.env.ref_context.get('py:module'))
547             self.env.ref_context['py:module'] = self.options['module']
548 
549     def after_content(self) -> None:
550         """Handle object de-nesting after content
551 
552         If this class is a nestable object, removing the last nested class prefix
553         ends further nesting in the object.
554 
555         If this class is not a nestable object, the list of classes should not
556         be altered as we didn't affect the nesting levels in
557         :py:meth:`before_content`.
558         """
559         classes = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:classes', [])
560         if self.allow_nesting:
561             try:
562                 classes.pop()
563             except IndexError:
564                 pass
565         self.env.ref_context['py:class'] = (classes[-1] if len(classes) > 0
566                                             else None)
567         if 'module' in self.options:
568             modules = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:modules', [])
569             if modules:
570                 self.env.ref_context['py:module'] = modules.pop()
571             else:
572                 self.env.ref_context.pop('py:module')
573

1013 class PythonModuleIndex(Index):
1014     """
1015     Index subclass to provide the Python module index.
1016     """
1017 
1018     name = 'modindex'
1019     localname = _('Python Module Index')
1020     shortname = _('modules')
1021 
1022     def generate(self, docnames: Iterable[str] = None
1023                  ) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[str, List[IndexEntry]]], bool]:
1024         content: Dict[str, List[IndexEntry]] = {}
1025         # list of prefixes to ignore
1026         ignores: List[str] = self.domain.env.config['modindex_common_prefix']
1027         ignores = sorted(ignores, key=len, reverse=True)
1028         # list of all modules, sorted by module name
1029         modules = sorted(self.domain.data['modules'].items(),
1030                          key=lambda x: x[0].lower())
1031         # sort out collapsable modules
1032         prev_modname = ''
1033         num_toplevels = 0
1034         for modname, (docname, node_id, synopsis, platforms, deprecated) in modules:
1035             if docnames and docname not in docnames:
1036                 continue
1037 
1038             for ignore in ignores:
1039                 if modname.startswith(ignore):
1040                     modname = modname[len(ignore):]
1041                     stripped = ignore
1042                     break
1043             else:
1044                 stripped = ''
1045 
1046             # we stripped the whole module name?
1047             if not modname:
1048                 modname, stripped = stripped, ''
1049 
1050             entries = content.setdefault(modname[0].lower(), [])
1051 
1052             package = modname.split('.')[0]
1053             if package != modname:
1054                 # it's a submodule
1055                 if prev_modname == package:
1056                     # first submodule - make parent a group head
1057                     if entries:
1058                         last = entries[-1]
1059                         entries[-1] = IndexEntry(last[0], 1, last[2], last[3],
1060                                                  last[4], last[5], last[6])
1061                 elif not prev_modname.startswith(package):
1062                     # submodule without parent in list, add dummy entry
1063                     entries.append(IndexEntry(stripped + package, 1, '', '', '', '', ''))
1064                 subtype = 2
1065             else:
1066                 num_toplevels += 1
1067                 subtype = 0
1068 
1069             qualifier = _('Deprecated') if deprecated else ''
1070             entries.append(IndexEntry(stripped + modname, subtype, docname,
1071                                       node_id, platforms, qualifier, synopsis))
1072             prev_modname = modname
1073 
1074         # apply heuristics when to collapse modindex at page load:
1075         # only collapse if number of toplevel modules is larger than
1076         # number of submodules
1077         collapse = len(modules) - num_toplevels < num_toplevels
1078 
1079         # sort by first letter
1080         sorted_content = sorted(content.items())
1081 
1082         return sorted_content, collapse

1191     def find_obj(self, env: BuildEnvironment, modname: str, classname: str,
1192                  name: str, type: str, searchmode: int = 0
1193                  ) -> List[Tuple[str, ObjectEntry]]:

1195         and/or classname.  Returns a list of (name, object entry) tuples.

1198         if name[-2:] == '()':
1199             name = name[:-2]
1200 
1201         if not name:
1202             return []
1203 
1204         matches: List[Tuple[str, ObjectEntry]] = []
1205 
1206         newname = None
1207         if searchmode == 1:
1208             if type is None:
1209                 objtypes = list(self.object_types)
1210             else:
1211                 objtypes = self.objtypes_for_role(type)
1212             if objtypes is not None:
1213                 if modname and classname:
1214                     fullname = modname + '.' + classname + '.' + name
1215                     if fullname in self.objects and self.objects[fullname].objtype in objtypes:
1216                         newname = fullname
1217                 if not newname:
1218                     if modname and modname + '.' + name in self.objects and \
1219                        self.objects[modname + '.' + name].objtype in objtypes:
1220                         newname = modname + '.' + name
1221                     elif name in self.objects and self.objects[name].objtype in objtypes:
1222                         newname = name
1223                     else:
1224                         # "fuzzy" searching mode
1225                         searchname = '.' + name
1226                         matches = [(oname, self.objects[oname]) for oname in self.objects
1227                                    if oname.endswith(searchname) and
1228                                    self.objects[oname].objtype in objtypes]
1229         else:
1230             # NOTE: searching for exact match, object type is not considered
1231             if name in self.objects:
1232                 newname = name
1233             elif type == 'mod':
1234                 # only exact matches allowed for modules
1235                 return []
1236             elif classname and classname + '.' + name in self.objects:
1237                 newname = classname + '.' + name
1238             elif modname and modname + '.' + name in self.objects:
1239                 newname = modname + '.' + name
1240             elif modname and classname and \
1241                     modname + '.' + classname + '.' + name in self.objects:
1242                 newname = modname + '.' + classname + '.' + name
1243         if newname is not None:
1244             matches.append((newname, self.objects[newname]))

1247     def resolve_xref(self, env: BuildEnvironment, fromdocname: str, builder: Builder,
1248                      type: str, target: str, node: pending_xref, contnode: Element
1249                      ) -> Optional[Element]:
1250         modname = node.get('py:module')
1251         clsname = node.get('py:class')
1252         searchmode = 1 if node.hasattr('refspecific') else 0
1253         matches = self.find_obj(env, modname, clsname, target,
1254                                 type, searchmode)
1255 
1256         if not matches and type == 'attr':
1257             # fallback to meth (for property; Sphinx-2.4.x)
1258             # this ensures that `:attr:` role continues to refer to the old property entry
1259             # that defined by ``method`` directive in old reST files.
1260             matches = self.find_obj(env, modname, clsname, target, 'meth', searchmode)
1261         if not matches and type == 'meth':
1262             # fallback to attr (for property)
1263             # this ensures that `:meth:` in the old reST files can refer to the property
1264             # entry that defined by ``property`` directive.
1265             #
1266             # Note: _prop is a secret role only for internal look-up.
1267             matches = self.find_obj(env, modname, clsname, target, '_prop', searchmode)
1268 
1269         if not matches:
1270             return None
1271         elif len(matches) > 1:
1272             canonicals = [m for m in matches if not m[1].aliased]
1273             if len(canonicals) == 1:
1274                 matches = canonicals
1275             else:
1276                 logger.warning(__('more than one target found for cross-reference %r: %s'),
1277                                target, ', '.join(match[0] for match in matches),
1278                                type='ref', subtype='python', location=node)
1279         name, obj = matches[0]
1280 
1281         if obj[2] == 'module':
1282             return self._make_module_refnode(builder, fromdocname, name, contnode)
1283         else:
1284             # determine the content of the reference by conditions
1285             content = find_pending_xref_condition(node, 'resolved')
1286             if content:
1287                 children = content.children
1288             else:
1289                 # if not found, use contnode
1290                 children = [contnode]
1291 
1292             return make_refnode(builder, fromdocname, obj[0], obj[1], children, name)

1294     def resolve_any_xref(self, env: BuildEnvironment, fromdocname: str, builder: Builder,

1296                          ) -> List[Tuple[str, Element]]:
1297         modname = node.get('py:module')

1322     def _make_module_refnode(self, builder: Builder, fromdocname: str, name: str,

87 class ValidationError(Exception):

91 def is_path(x: str) -> str:
92     x = path.expanduser(x)
93     if not path.isdir(x):
94         raise ValidationError(__("Please enter a valid path name."))
95     return x

98 def allow_empty(x: str) -> str:
99     return x

102 def nonempty(x: str) -> str:
103     if not x:
104         raise ValidationError(__("Please enter some text."))
105     return x

108 def choice(*l: str) -> Callable[[str], str]:
109     def val(x: str) -> str:
110         if x not in l:
111             raise ValidationError(__('Please enter one of %s.') % ', '.join(l))
112         return x
113     return val

116 def boolean(x: str) -> bool:
117     if x.upper() not in ('Y', 'YES', 'N', 'NO'):
118         raise ValidationError(__("Please enter either 'y' or 'n'."))
119     return x.upper() in ('Y', 'YES')

132 def do_prompt(text: str, default: str = None, validator: Callable[[str], Any] = nonempty) -> Union[str, bool]:  # NOQA
133     while True:
134         if default is not None:
135             prompt = PROMPT_PREFIX + '%s [%s]: ' % (text, default)
136         else:
137             prompt = PROMPT_PREFIX + text + ': '
138         if USE_LIBEDIT:
139             # Note: libedit has a problem for combination of ``input()`` and escape
140             # sequence (see #5335).  To avoid the problem, all prompts are not colored
141             # on libedit.
142             pass
143         elif readline:
144             # pass input_mode=True if readline available
145             prompt = colorize(COLOR_QUESTION, prompt, input_mode=True)
146         else:
147             prompt = colorize(COLOR_QUESTION, prompt, input_mode=False)
148         x = term_input(prompt).strip()
149         if default and not x:
150             x = default
151         try:
152             x = validator(x)
153         except ValidationError as err:
154             print(red('* ' + str(err)))
155             continue
156         break
157     return x

161     def __init__(self, templatedir: str) -> None:

165     def _has_custom_template(self, template_name: str) -> bool:
166         """Check if custom template file exists.
167 
168         Note: Please don't use this function from extensions.
169               It will be removed in the future without deprecation period.
170         """
171         template = path.join(self.templatedir, path.basename(template_name))
172         if self.templatedir and path.exists(template):
173             return True
174         else:
175             return False
176 
177     def render(self, template_name: str, context: Dict) -> str:
178         if self._has_custom_template(template_name):
179             custom_template = path.join(self.templatedir, path.basename(template_name))
180             return self.render_from_file(custom_template, context)
181         else:
182             return super().render(template_name, context)

323 def generate(d: Dict, overwrite: bool = True, silent: bool = False, templatedir: str = None
324              ) -> None:
325     """Generate project based on values in *d*."""
326     template = QuickstartRenderer(templatedir=templatedir)
327 
328     if 'mastertoctree' not in d:
329         d['mastertoctree'] = ''
330     if 'mastertocmaxdepth' not in d:
331         d['mastertocmaxdepth'] = 2
332 
333     d['root_doc'] = d['master']
334     d['now'] = time.asctime()
335     d['project_underline'] = column_width(d['project']) * '='
336     d.setdefault('extensions', [])
337     d['copyright'] = time.strftime('%Y') + ', ' + d['author']
338 
339     d["path"] = os.path.abspath(d['path'])
340     ensuredir(d['path'])
341 
342     srcdir = path.join(d['path'], 'source') if d['sep'] else d['path']
343 
344     ensuredir(srcdir)
345     if d['sep']:
346         builddir = path.join(d['path'], 'build')
347         d['exclude_patterns'] = ''
348     else:
349         builddir = path.join(srcdir, d['dot'] + 'build')
350         exclude_patterns = map(repr, [
351             d['dot'] + 'build',
352             'Thumbs.db', '.DS_Store',
353         ])
354         d['exclude_patterns'] = ', '.join(exclude_patterns)
355     ensuredir(builddir)
356     ensuredir(path.join(srcdir, d['dot'] + 'templates'))
357     ensuredir(path.join(srcdir, d['dot'] + 'static'))
358 
359     def write_file(fpath: str, content: str, newline: str = None) -> None:
360         if overwrite or not path.isfile(fpath):
361             if 'quiet' not in d:
362                 print(__('Creating file %s.') % fpath)
363             with open(fpath, 'wt', encoding='utf-8', newline=newline) as f:
364                 f.write(content)
365         else:
366             if 'quiet' not in d:
367                 print(__('File %s already exists, skipping.') % fpath)
368 
369     conf_path = os.path.join(templatedir, 'conf.py_t') if templatedir else None
370     if not conf_path or not path.isfile(conf_path):
371         conf_path = os.path.join(package_dir, 'templates', 'quickstart', 'conf.py_t')
372     with open(conf_path) as f:
373         conf_text = f.read()
374 
375     write_file(path.join(srcdir, 'conf.py'), template.render_string(conf_text, d))
376 
377     masterfile = path.join(srcdir, d['master'] + d['suffix'])
378     if template._has_custom_template('quickstart/master_doc.rst_t'):
379         msg = ('A custom template `master_doc.rst_t` found. It has been renamed to '
380                '`root_doc.rst_t`.  Please rename it on your project too.')
381         print(colorize('red', msg))  # RemovedInSphinx60Warning
382         write_file(masterfile, template.render('quickstart/master_doc.rst_t', d))
383     else:
384         write_file(masterfile, template.render('quickstart/root_doc.rst_t', d))
385 
386     if d.get('make_mode') is True:
387         makefile_template = 'quickstart/Makefile.new_t'
388         batchfile_template = 'quickstart/make.bat.new_t'
389     else:
390         makefile_template = 'quickstart/Makefile_t'
391         batchfile_template = 'quickstart/make.bat_t'
392 
393     if d['makefile'] is True:
394         d['rsrcdir'] = 'source' if d['sep'] else '.'
395         d['rbuilddir'] = 'build' if d['sep'] else d['dot'] + 'build'
396         # use binary mode, to avoid writing \r\n on Windows
397         write_file(path.join(d['path'], 'Makefile'),
398                    template.render(makefile_template, d), '\n')
399 
400     if d['batchfile'] is True:
401         d['rsrcdir'] = 'source' if d['sep'] else '.'
402         d['rbuilddir'] = 'build' if d['sep'] else d['dot'] + 'build'
403         write_file(path.join(d['path'], 'make.bat'),
404                    template.render(batchfile_template, d), '\r\n')
405 
406     if silent:
407         return
408     print()
409     print(bold(__('Finished: An initial directory structure has been created.')))
410     print()
411     print(__('You should now populate your master file %s and create other documentation\n'
412              'source files. ') % masterfile, end='')
413     if d['makefile'] or d['batchfile']:
414         print(__('Use the Makefile to build the docs, like so:\n'
415                  '   make builder'))
416     else:
417         print(__('Use the sphinx-build command to build the docs, like so:\n'
418                  '   sphinx-build -b builder %s %s') % (srcdir, builddir))
419     print(__('where "builder" is one of the supported builders, '
420              'e.g. html, latex or linkcheck.'))
421     print()

424 def valid_dir(d: Dict) -> bool:
425     dir = d['path']
426     if not path.exists(dir):
427         return True
428     if not path.isdir(dir):
429         return False
430 
431     if {'Makefile', 'make.bat'} & set(os.listdir(dir)):
432         return False
433 
434     if d['sep']:
435         dir = os.path.join('source', dir)
436         if not path.exists(dir):
437             return True
438         if not path.isdir(dir):
439             return False
440 
441     reserved_names = [
442         'conf.py',
443         d['dot'] + 'static',
444         d['dot'] + 'templates',
445         d['master'] + d['suffix'],
446     ]
447     if set(reserved_names) & set(os.listdir(dir)):
448         return False
449 
450     return True

538 def main(argv: List[str] = sys.argv[1:]) -> int:
539     sphinx.locale.setlocale(locale.LC_ALL, '')
540     sphinx.locale.init_console(os.path.join(package_dir, 'locale'), 'sphinx')

542     if not color_terminal():
543         nocolor()

545     # parse options
546     parser = get_parser()
547     try:
548         args = parser.parse_args(argv)
549     except SystemExit as err:
550         return err.code
551 
552     d = vars(args)
553     # delete None or False value
554     d = {k: v for k, v in d.items() if v is not None}
555 
556     # handle use of CSV-style extension values
557     d.setdefault('extensions', [])
558     for ext in d['extensions'][:]:
559         if ',' in ext:
560             d['extensions'].remove(ext)
561             d['extensions'].extend(ext.split(','))
562 
563     try:
564         if 'quiet' in d:
565             if not {'project', 'author'}.issubset(d):
566                 print(__('"quiet" is specified, but any of "project" or '
567                          '"author" is not specified.'))
568                 return 1
569 
570         if {'quiet', 'project', 'author'}.issubset(d):
571             # quiet mode with all required params satisfied, use default
572             d.setdefault('version', '')
573             d.setdefault('release', d['version'])
574             d2 = DEFAULTS.copy()
575             d2.update(d)
576             d = d2
577 
578             if not valid_dir(d):
579                 print()
580                 print(bold(__('Error: specified path is not a directory, or sphinx'
581                               ' files already exist.')))
582                 print(__('sphinx-quickstart only generate into a empty directory.'
583                          ' Please specify a new root path.'))
584                 return 1
585         else:
586             ask_user(d)
587     except (KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError):
588         print()
589         print('[Interrupted.]')
590         return 130  # 128 + SIGINT
591 
592     for variable in d.get('variables', []):
593         try:
594             name, value = variable.split('=')

596         except ValueError:
597             print(__('Invalid template variable: %s') % variable)
598 
599     generate(d, overwrite=False, templatedir=args.templatedir)
600     return 0

604     sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

Methods decorated with @classmethod and @property do not get documented.
**EDIT:** The problem seems to be that `type(BaseClass.baseclass_property)` returns `property`, thus sphinx can just lookup `BaseClass.baseclass_property.__doc__`. However, `type(BaseClass.baseclass_class_property)` returns the type of the returned object, since essentially, a `@classmethod@property` ends up behaving like a class attribute. So Sphinx doesn't really have a chance to extract the docstring.

**EDIT 2:** Seems like this will get fixed in python 3.10, cf. https://bugs.python.org/issue43682. 

> Static methods (`@staticmethod`) and class methods (`@classmethod`) now inherit the method attributes (`__module__`, `__name__`, `__qualname__`, `__doc__`, `__annotations__`) and have a new __wrapped__ attribute. 

I will try to test this with the beta release.

-----

### Describe the bug

> Changed in version 3.9: Class methods can now wrap other descriptors such as property().

That is, since python version 3.9 we can write code like

```python
class A:
    @classmethod
    @property
    def f(cls):
        """Some class property."""
        return "property"
```

However, sphinx does not seem to document any such methods (regular `@property` decorated methods get documented just fine.)

### How to Reproduce


```bash
git clone https://github.com/randolf-scholz/sphinx_demo
cd sphinx_demo/docs
make html
# open _build/html/dummy_module.submodule.html
```

The following methods were erroneously not documented:

- `MetaClass.metaclass_class_property`
- `MetaClass.metaclass_abstract_class_property`
- `BaseClass.baseclass_class_property`
- `BaseClass.baseclass_abstract_class_property`
- `SubClass.subclass_class_property`
- `SubClass.subclass_abstract_class_property`


### Expected behavior

Methods that are decorated with both `@classmethod` and `@property` should be documented appropriately.

83 def type_to_xref(text: str, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> addnodes.pending_xref:
84     """Convert a type string to a cross reference node."""
85     if text == 'None':
86         reftype = 'obj'
87     else:
88         reftype = 'class'
89 
90     if env:
91         kwargs = {'py:module': env.ref_context.get('py:module'),
92                   'py:class': env.ref_context.get('py:class')}
93     else:
94         kwargs = {}
95 
96     if env.config.python_use_unqualified_type_names:
97         # Note: It would be better to use qualname to describe the object to support support
98         # nested classes.  But python domain can't access the real python object because this
99         # module should work not-dynamically.
100         shortname = text.split('.')[-1]
101         contnodes: List[Node] = [pending_xref_condition('', shortname, condition='resolved'),
102                                  pending_xref_condition('', text, condition='*')]
103     else:
104         contnodes = [nodes.Text(text)]
105 
106     return pending_xref('', *contnodes,
107                         refdomain='py', reftype=reftype, reftarget=text, **kwargs)

110 def _parse_annotation(annotation: str, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
111     """Parse type annotation."""
112     def unparse(node: ast.AST) -> List[Node]:
113         if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
114             return [nodes.Text("%s.%s" % (unparse(node.value)[0], node.attr))]
115         elif isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
116             result: List[Node] = unparse(node.left)
117             result.extend(unparse(node.op))
118             result.extend(unparse(node.right))
119             return result
120         elif isinstance(node, ast.BitOr):
121             return [nodes.Text(' '), addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', '|'), nodes.Text(' ')]
122         elif isinstance(node, ast.Constant):  # type: ignore
123             if node.value is Ellipsis:
124                 return [addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', "...")]
125             else:
126                 return [nodes.Text(node.value)]
127         elif isinstance(node, ast.Expr):
128             return unparse(node.value)
129         elif isinstance(node, ast.Index):
130             return unparse(node.value)
131         elif isinstance(node, ast.List):
132             result = [addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', '[')]
133             if node.elts:
134                 # check if there are elements in node.elts to only pop the
135                 # last element of result if the for-loop was run at least
136                 # once
137                 for elem in node.elts:
138                     result.extend(unparse(elem))
139                     result.append(addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', ', '))
140                 result.pop()
141             result.append(addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', ']'))
142             return result
143         elif isinstance(node, ast.Module):
144             return sum((unparse(e) for e in node.body), [])
145         elif isinstance(node, ast.Name):
146             return [nodes.Text(node.id)]
147         elif isinstance(node, ast.Subscript):
148             result = unparse(node.value)
149             result.append(addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', '['))
150             result.extend(unparse(node.slice))
151             result.append(addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', ']'))
152             return result
153         elif isinstance(node, ast.Tuple):
154             if node.elts:
155                 result = []
156                 for elem in node.elts:
157                     result.extend(unparse(elem))
158                     result.append(addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', ', '))
159                 result.pop()
160             else:
161                 result = [addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', '('),
162                           addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', ')')]
163 
164             return result
165         else:
166             if sys.version_info < (3, 8):
167                 if isinstance(node, ast.Ellipsis):
168                     return [addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', "...")]
169                 elif isinstance(node, ast.NameConstant):
170                     return [nodes.Text(node.value)]
171 
172             raise SyntaxError  # unsupported syntax
173 
174     if env is None:
175         warnings.warn("The env parameter for _parse_annotation becomes required now.",
176                       RemovedInSphinx50Warning, stacklevel=2)
177 
178     try:
179         tree = ast_parse(annotation)
180         result = unparse(tree)
181         for i, node in enumerate(result):
182             if isinstance(node, nodes.Text) and node.strip():
183                 result[i] = type_to_xref(str(node), env)
184         return result
185     except SyntaxError:
186         return [type_to_xref(annotation, env)]

189 def _parse_arglist(arglist: str, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> addnodes.desc_parameterlist:
190     """Parse a list of arguments using AST parser"""
191     params = addnodes.desc_parameterlist(arglist)
192     sig = signature_from_str('(%s)' % arglist)
193     last_kind = None
194     for param in sig.parameters.values():
195         if param.kind != param.POSITIONAL_ONLY and last_kind == param.POSITIONAL_ONLY:
196             # PEP-570: Separator for Positional Only Parameter: /
197             params += addnodes.desc_parameter('', '', addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '/'))
198         if param.kind == param.KEYWORD_ONLY and last_kind in (param.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD,
199                                                               param.POSITIONAL_ONLY,
200                                                               None):
201             # PEP-3102: Separator for Keyword Only Parameter: *
202             params += addnodes.desc_parameter('', '', addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '*'))
203 
204         node = addnodes.desc_parameter()
205         if param.kind == param.VAR_POSITIONAL:
206             node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '*')
207             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', param.name)
208         elif param.kind == param.VAR_KEYWORD:
209             node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '**')
210             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', param.name)
211         else:
212             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', param.name)
213 
214         if param.annotation is not param.empty:
215             children = _parse_annotation(param.annotation, env)
216             node += addnodes.desc_sig_punctuation('', ':')
217             node += nodes.Text(' ')
218             node += addnodes.desc_sig_name('', '', *children)  # type: ignore
219         if param.default is not param.empty:
220             if param.annotation is not param.empty:
221                 node += nodes.Text(' ')
222                 node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '=')
223                 node += nodes.Text(' ')
224             else:
225                 node += addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '=')
226             node += nodes.inline('', param.default, classes=['default_value'],
227                                  support_smartquotes=False)
228 
229         params += node
230         last_kind = param.kind
231 
232     if last_kind == Parameter.POSITIONAL_ONLY:
233         # PEP-570: Separator for Positional Only Parameter: /
234         params += addnodes.desc_parameter('', '', addnodes.desc_sig_operator('', '/'))
235 
236     return params

239 def _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode: desc_signature, arglist: str) -> None:
240     """"Parse" a list of arguments separated by commas.
241 
242     Arguments can have "optional" annotations given by enclosing them in
243     brackets.  Currently, this will split at any comma, even if it's inside a
244     string literal (e.g. default argument value).
245     """
246     paramlist = addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
247     stack: List[Element] = [paramlist]
248     try:
249         for argument in arglist.split(','):
250             argument = argument.strip()
251             ends_open = ends_close = 0
252             while argument.startswith('['):
253                 stack.append(addnodes.desc_optional())
254                 stack[-2] += stack[-1]
255                 argument = argument[1:].strip()
256             while argument.startswith(']'):
257                 stack.pop()
258                 argument = argument[1:].strip()
259             while argument.endswith(']') and not argument.endswith('[]'):
260                 ends_close += 1
261                 argument = argument[:-1].strip()
262             while argument.endswith('['):
263                 ends_open += 1
264                 argument = argument[:-1].strip()
265             if argument:
266                 stack[-1] += addnodes.desc_parameter(argument, argument)
267             while ends_open:
268                 stack.append(addnodes.desc_optional())
269                 stack[-2] += stack[-1]
270                 ends_open -= 1
271             while ends_close:
272                 stack.pop()
273                 ends_close -= 1
274         if len(stack) != 1:
275             raise IndexError
276     except IndexError:
277         # if there are too few or too many elements on the stack, just give up
278         # and treat the whole argument list as one argument, discarding the
279         # already partially populated paramlist node
280         paramlist = addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
281         paramlist += addnodes.desc_parameter(arglist, arglist)
282         signode += paramlist
283     else:
284         signode += paramlist

287 # This override allows our inline type specifiers to behave like :class: link
288 # when it comes to handling "." and "~" prefixes.
289 class PyXrefMixin:
290     def make_xref(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
291                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
292                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None,
293                   inliner: Inliner = None, location: Node = None) -> Node:
294         # we use inliner=None to make sure we get the old behaviour with a single
295         # pending_xref node
296         result = super().make_xref(rolename, domain, target,  # type: ignore
297                                    innernode, contnode,
298                                    env, inliner=None, location=None)
299         result['refspecific'] = True
300         result['py:module'] = env.ref_context.get('py:module')
301         result['py:class'] = env.ref_context.get('py:class')
302         if target.startswith(('.', '~')):
303             prefix, result['reftarget'] = target[0], target[1:]
304             if prefix == '.':
305                 text = target[1:]
306             elif prefix == '~':
307                 text = target.split('.')[-1]
308             for node in result.traverse(nodes.Text):
309                 node.parent[node.parent.index(node)] = nodes.Text(text)
310                 break
311         elif isinstance(result, pending_xref) and env.config.python_use_unqualified_type_names:
312             children = result.children
313             result.clear()
314 
315             shortname = target.split('.')[-1]
316             textnode = innernode('', shortname)
317             contnodes = [pending_xref_condition('', '', textnode, condition='resolved'),
318                          pending_xref_condition('', '', *children, condition='*')]
319             result.extend(contnodes)
320 
321         return result
322 
323     def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
324                    innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
325                    contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None,
326                    inliner: Inliner = None, location: Node = None) -> List[Node]:
327         delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\s*\|\s*|\.\.\.)'
328         delims_re = re.compile(delims)
329         sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)
330 
331         split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)
332 
333         results = []
334         for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
335             if split_contnode:
336                 contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)
337 
338             if delims_re.match(sub_target):
339                 results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
340             else:
341                 results.append(self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
342                                               innernode, contnode, env, inliner, location))
343 
344         return results
345

425     def handle_signature(self, sig: str, signode: desc_signature) -> Tuple[str, str]:
426         """Transform a Python signature into RST nodes.
427 
428         Return (fully qualified name of the thing, classname if any).
429 
430         If inside a class, the current class name is handled intelligently:
431         * it is stripped from the displayed name if present
432         * it is added to the full name (return value) if not present
433         """
434         m = py_sig_re.match(sig)
435         if m is None:
436             raise ValueError
437         prefix, name, arglist, retann = m.groups()
438 
439         # determine module and class name (if applicable), as well as full name
440         modname = self.options.get('module', self.env.ref_context.get('py:module'))
441         classname = self.env.ref_context.get('py:class')
442         if classname:
443             add_module = False
444             if prefix and (prefix == classname or
445                            prefix.startswith(classname + ".")):
446                 fullname = prefix + name
447                 # class name is given again in the signature
448                 prefix = prefix[len(classname):].lstrip('.')
449             elif prefix:
450                 # class name is given in the signature, but different
451                 # (shouldn't happen)
452                 fullname = classname + '.' + prefix + name
453             else:
454                 # class name is not given in the signature
455                 fullname = classname + '.' + name
456         else:
457             add_module = True
458             if prefix:
459                 classname = prefix.rstrip('.')
460                 fullname = prefix + name
461             else:
462                 classname = ''
463                 fullname = name
464 
465         signode['module'] = modname
466         signode['class'] = classname
467         signode['fullname'] = fullname
468 
469         sig_prefix = self.get_signature_prefix(sig)
470         if sig_prefix:
471             signode += addnodes.desc_annotation(sig_prefix, sig_prefix)
472 
473         if prefix:
474             signode += addnodes.desc_addname(prefix, prefix)
475         elif modname and add_module and self.env.config.add_module_names:
476             nodetext = modname + '.'
477             signode += addnodes.desc_addname(nodetext, nodetext)
478 
479         signode += addnodes.desc_name(name, name)
480         if arglist:
481             try:
482                 signode += _parse_arglist(arglist, self.env)
483             except SyntaxError:
484                 # fallback to parse arglist original parser.
485                 # it supports to represent optional arguments (ex. "func(foo [, bar])")
486                 _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode, arglist)
487             except NotImplementedError as exc:
488                 logger.warning("could not parse arglist (%r): %s", arglist, exc,
489                                location=signode)
490                 _pseudo_parse_arglist(signode, arglist)
491         else:
492             if self.needs_arglist():
493                 # for callables, add an empty parameter list
494                 signode += addnodes.desc_parameterlist()
495 
496         if retann:
497             children = _parse_annotation(retann, self.env)
498             signode += addnodes.desc_returns(retann, '', *children)
499 
500         anno = self.options.get('annotation')
501         if anno:
502             signode += addnodes.desc_annotation(' ' + anno, ' ' + anno)
503 
504         return fullname, prefix

537     def before_content(self) -> None:
538         """Handle object nesting before content
539 
540         :py:class:`PyObject` represents Python language constructs. For
541         constructs that are nestable, such as a Python classes, this method will
542         build up a stack of the nesting hierarchy so that it can be later
543         de-nested correctly, in :py:meth:`after_content`.
544 
545         For constructs that aren't nestable, the stack is bypassed, and instead
546         only the most recent object is tracked. This object prefix name will be
547         removed with :py:meth:`after_content`.
548         """
549         prefix = None
550         if self.names:
551             # fullname and name_prefix come from the `handle_signature` method.
552             # fullname represents the full object name that is constructed using
553             # object nesting and explicit prefixes. `name_prefix` is the
554             # explicit prefix given in a signature
555             (fullname, name_prefix) = self.names[-1]
556             if self.allow_nesting:
557                 prefix = fullname
558             elif name_prefix:
559                 prefix = name_prefix.strip('.')
560         if prefix:
561             self.env.ref_context['py:class'] = prefix
562             if self.allow_nesting:
563                 classes = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:classes', [])
564                 classes.append(prefix)
565         if 'module' in self.options:
566             modules = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:modules', [])
567             modules.append(self.env.ref_context.get('py:module'))
568             self.env.ref_context['py:module'] = self.options['module']
569 
570     def after_content(self) -> None:
571         """Handle object de-nesting after content
572 
573         If this class is a nestable object, removing the last nested class prefix
574         ends further nesting in the object.
575 
576         If this class is not a nestable object, the list of classes should not
577         be altered as we didn't affect the nesting levels in
578         :py:meth:`before_content`.
579         """
580         classes = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:classes', [])
581         if self.allow_nesting:
582             try:
583                 classes.pop()
584             except IndexError:
585                 pass
586         self.env.ref_context['py:class'] = (classes[-1] if len(classes) > 0
587                                             else None)
588         if 'module' in self.options:
589             modules = self.env.ref_context.setdefault('py:modules', [])
590             if modules:
591                 self.env.ref_context['py:module'] = modules.pop()
592             else:
593                 self.env.ref_context.pop('py:module')

1034 class PythonModuleIndex(Index):
1035     """
1036     Index subclass to provide the Python module index.
1037     """
1038 
1039     name = 'modindex'
1040     localname = _('Python Module Index')
1041     shortname = _('modules')
1042 
1043     def generate(self, docnames: Iterable[str] = None
1044                  ) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[str, List[IndexEntry]]], bool]:
1045         content: Dict[str, List[IndexEntry]] = {}
1046         # list of prefixes to ignore
1047         ignores: List[str] = self.domain.env.config['modindex_common_prefix']
1048         ignores = sorted(ignores, key=len, reverse=True)
1049         # list of all modules, sorted by module name
1050         modules = sorted(self.domain.data['modules'].items(),
1051                          key=lambda x: x[0].lower())
1052         # sort out collapsable modules
1053         prev_modname = ''
1054         num_toplevels = 0
1055         for modname, (docname, node_id, synopsis, platforms, deprecated) in modules:
1056             if docnames and docname not in docnames:
1057                 continue
1058 
1059             for ignore in ignores:
1060                 if modname.startswith(ignore):
1061                     modname = modname[len(ignore):]
1062                     stripped = ignore
1063                     break
1064             else:
1065                 stripped = ''
1066 
1067             # we stripped the whole module name?
1068             if not modname:
1069                 modname, stripped = stripped, ''
1070 
1071             entries = content.setdefault(modname[0].lower(), [])
1072 
1073             package = modname.split('.')[0]
1074             if package != modname:
1075                 # it's a submodule
1076                 if prev_modname == package:
1077                     # first submodule - make parent a group head
1078                     if entries:
1079                         last = entries[-1]
1080                         entries[-1] = IndexEntry(last[0], 1, last[2], last[3],
1081                                                  last[4], last[5], last[6])
1082                 elif not prev_modname.startswith(package):
1083                     # submodule without parent in list, add dummy entry
1084                     entries.append(IndexEntry(stripped + package, 1, '', '', '', '', ''))
1085                 subtype = 2
1086             else:
1087                 num_toplevels += 1
1088                 subtype = 0
1089 
1090             qualifier = _('Deprecated') if deprecated else ''
1091             entries.append(IndexEntry(stripped + modname, subtype, docname,
1092                                       node_id, platforms, qualifier, synopsis))
1093             prev_modname = modname
1094 
1095         # apply heuristics when to collapse modindex at page load:
1096         # only collapse if number of toplevel modules is larger than
1097         # number of submodules
1098         collapse = len(modules) - num_toplevels < num_toplevels
1099 
1100         # sort by first letter
1101         sorted_content = sorted(content.items())
1102 
1103         return sorted_content, collapse

1223             return []

1229             if type is None:

1231             else:

1233             if objtypes is not None:

1235                     fullname = modname + '.' + classname + '.' + name
1236                     if fullname in self.objects and self.objects[fullname].objtype in objtypes:
1237                         newname = fullname

1246                         searchname = '.' + name

1248                                    if oname.endswith(searchname) and

1252             if name in self.objects:

1257             elif classname and classname + '.' + name in self.objects:

1259             elif modname and modname + '.' + name in self.objects:
1260                 newname = modname + '.' + name

1262                     modname + '.' + classname + '.' + name in self.objects:
1263                 newname = modname + '.' + classname + '.' + name

1268     def resolve_xref(self, env: BuildEnvironment, fromdocname: str, builder: Builder,
1269                      type: str, target: str, node: pending_xref, contnode: Element
1270                      ) -> Optional[Element]:
1271         modname = node.get('py:module')
1272         clsname = node.get('py:class')
1273         searchmode = 1 if node.hasattr('refspecific') else 0
1274         matches = self.find_obj(env, modname, clsname, target,
1275                                 type, searchmode)

1277         if not matches and type == 'attr':
1278             # fallback to meth (for property; Sphinx-2.4.x)
1279             # this ensures that `:attr:` role continues to refer to the old property entry
1280             # that defined by ``method`` directive in old reST files.
1281             matches = self.find_obj(env, modname, clsname, target, 'meth', searchmode)
1282         if not matches and type == 'meth':
1283             # fallback to attr (for property)

1285             # entry that defined by ``property`` directive.
1286             #
1287             # Note: _prop is a secret role only for internal look-up.
1288             matches = self.find_obj(env, modname, clsname, target, '_prop', searchmode)
1289 
1290         if not matches:
1291             return None
1292         elif len(matches) > 1:
1293             canonicals = [m for m in matches if not m[1].aliased]
1294             if len(canonicals) == 1:
1295                 matches = canonicals
1296             else:
1297                 logger.warning(__('more than one target found for cross-reference %r: %s'),
1298                                target, ', '.join(match[0] for match in matches),
1299                                type='ref', subtype='python', location=node)
1300         name, obj = matches[0]
1301 
1302         if obj[2] == 'module':

1304         else:
1305             # determine the content of the reference by conditions
1306             content = find_pending_xref_condition(node, 'resolved')
1307             if content:

192 def cut_lines(pre: int, post: int = 0, what: str = None) -> Callable:
193     """Return a listener that removes the first *pre* and last *post*
194     lines of every docstring.  If *what* is a sequence of strings,
195     only docstrings of a type in *what* will be processed.
196 
197     Use like this (e.g. in the ``setup()`` function of :file:`conf.py`)::
198 
199        from sphinx.ext.autodoc import cut_lines
200        app.connect('autodoc-process-docstring', cut_lines(4, what=['module']))
201 
202     This can (and should) be used in place of :confval:`automodule_skip_lines`.
203     """
204     def process(app: Sphinx, what_: str, name: str, obj: Any, options: Any, lines: List[str]
205                 ) -> None:
206         if what and what_ not in what:
207             return
208         del lines[:pre]
209         if post:
210             # remove one trailing blank line.
211             if lines and not lines[-1]:
212                 lines.pop(-1)
213             del lines[-post:]
214         # make sure there is a blank line at the end
215         if lines and lines[-1]:
216             lines.append('')
217     return process

220 def between(marker: str, what: Sequence[str] = None, keepempty: bool = False,
221             exclude: bool = False) -> Callable:
222     """Return a listener that either keeps, or if *exclude* is True excludes,
223     lines between lines that match the *marker* regular expression.  If no line
224     matches, the resulting docstring would be empty, so no change will be made
225     unless *keepempty* is true.
226 
227     If *what* is a sequence of strings, only docstrings of a type in *what* will
228     be processed.
229     """
230     marker_re = re.compile(marker)
231 
232     def process(app: Sphinx, what_: str, name: str, obj: Any, options: Any, lines: List[str]
233                 ) -> None:
234         if what and what_ not in what:
235             return
236         deleted = 0
237         delete = not exclude
238         orig_lines = lines[:]
239         for i, line in enumerate(orig_lines):
240             if delete:
241                 lines.pop(i - deleted)
242                 deleted += 1
243             if marker_re.match(line):
244                 delete = not delete
245                 if delete:
246                     lines.pop(i - deleted)
247                     deleted += 1
248         if not lines and not keepempty:
249             lines[:] = orig_lines
250         # make sure there is a blank line at the end
251         if lines and lines[-1]:
252             lines.append('')
253     return process

552     def get_doc(self, ignore: int = None) -> Optional[List[List[str]]]:
553         """Decode and return lines of the docstring(s) for the object.
554 
555         When it returns None value, autodoc-process-docstring will not be called for this
556         object.
557         """
558         if ignore is not None:
559             warnings.warn("The 'ignore' argument to autodoc.%s.get_doc() is deprecated."
560                           % self.__class__.__name__,
561                           RemovedInSphinx50Warning, stacklevel=2)
562         docstring = getdoc(self.object, self.get_attr, self.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
563                            self.parent, self.object_name)
564         if docstring:
565             tab_width = self.directive.state.document.settings.tab_width
566             return [prepare_docstring(docstring, ignore, tab_width)]
567         return []
