1093     def _xreplace(self, rule):
1094         """
1095         Helper for xreplace. Tracks whether a replacement actually occurred.
1096         """
1097         if self in rule:
1098             return rule[self], True
1099         elif rule:
1100             args = []
1101             changed = False
1102             for a in self.args:
1103                 try:
1104                     a_xr = a._xreplace(rule)
1105                     args.append(a_xr[0])
1106                     changed |= a_xr[1]
1107                 except AttributeError:
1108                     args.append(a)
1109             args = tuple(args)
1110             if changed:
1111                 return self.func(*args), True
1112         return self, False

1114     @cacheit
1115     def has(self, *patterns):
1116         """
1117         Test whether any subexpression matches any of the patterns.
1118 
1119         Examples
1120         ========
1121 
1122         >>> from sympy import sin
1123         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
1124         >>> (x**2 + sin(x*y)).has(z)
1125         False
1126         >>> (x**2 + sin(x*y)).has(x, y, z)
1127         True
1128         >>> x.has(x)
1129         True

1131         Note ``has`` is a structural algorithm with no knowledge of
1132         mathematics. Consider the following half-open interval:
1133 
1134         >>> from sympy.sets import Interval
1135         >>> i = Interval.Lopen(0, 5); i
1136         Interval.Lopen(0, 5)
1137         >>> i.args
1138         (0, 5, True, False)
1139         >>> i.has(4)  # there is no "4" in the arguments
1140         False
1141         >>> i.has(0)  # there *is* a "0" in the arguments
1142         True
1143 
1144         Instead, use ``contains`` to determine whether a number is in the
1145         interval or not:
1146 
1147         >>> i.contains(4)
1148         True
1149         >>> i.contains(0)
1150         False
1151

1153         Note that ``expr.has(*patterns)`` is exactly equivalent to
1154         ``any(expr.has(p) for p in patterns)``. In particular, ``False`` is
1155         returned when the list of patterns is empty.
1156 
1157         >>> x.has()
1158         False
1159 
1160         """
1161         return any(self._has(pattern) for pattern in patterns)

1163     def _has(self, pattern):

1171         if isinstance(pattern, BasicMeta):
1172             return any(isinstance(arg, pattern)
1173             for arg in preorder_traversal(self))
1174 
1175         try:
1176             match = pattern._has_matcher()
1177             return any(match(arg) for arg in preorder_traversal(self))
1178         except AttributeError:
1179             return any(arg == pattern for arg in preorder_traversal(self))

1181     def _has_matcher(self):

1183         return self.__eq__

1185     def replace(self, query, value, map=False, simultaneous=True, exact=False):
1186         """
1187         Replace matching subexpressions of ``self`` with ``value``.
1188 
1189         If ``map = True`` then also return the mapping {old: new} where ``old``
1190         was a sub-expression found with query and ``new`` is the replacement
1191         value for it. If the expression itself doesn't match the query, then
1192         the returned value will be ``self.xreplace(map)`` otherwise it should
1193         be ``self.subs(ordered(map.items()))``.
1194 
1195         Traverses an expression tree and performs replacement of matching
1196         subexpressions from the bottom to the top of the tree. The default
1197         approach is to do the replacement in a simultaneous fashion so
1198         changes made are targeted only once. If this is not desired or causes
1199         problems, ``simultaneous`` can be set to False. In addition, if an
1200         expression containing more than one Wild symbol is being used to match
1201         subexpressions and  the ``exact`` flag is True, then the match will only
1202         succeed if non-zero values are received for each Wild that appears in
1203         the match pattern.
1204 
1205         The list of possible combinations of queries and replacement values
1206         is listed below:
1207 
1208         Examples
1209         ========
1210 
1211         Initial setup
1212 
1213             >>> from sympy import log, sin, cos, tan, Wild, Mul, Add
1214             >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
1215             >>> f = log(sin(x)) + tan(sin(x**2))
1216 
1217         1.1. type -> type
1218             obj.replace(type, newtype)
1219 
1220             When object of type ``type`` is found, replace it with the
1221             result of passing its argument(s) to ``newtype``.
1222 
1223             >>> f.replace(sin, cos)
1224             log(cos(x)) + tan(cos(x**2))
1225             >>> sin(x).replace(sin, cos, map=True)
1226             (cos(x), {sin(x): cos(x)})
1227             >>> (x*y).replace(Mul, Add)
1228             x + y
1229 
1230         1.2. type -> func
1231             obj.replace(type, func)
1232 
1233             When object of type ``type`` is found, apply ``func`` to its
1234             argument(s). ``func`` must be written to handle the number
1235             of arguments of ``type``.
1236 
1237             >>> f.replace(sin, lambda arg: sin(2*arg))
1238             log(sin(2*x)) + tan(sin(2*x**2))
1239             >>> (x*y).replace(Mul, lambda *args: sin(2*Mul(*args)))
1240             sin(2*x*y)
1241 
1242         2.1. pattern -> expr
1243             obj.replace(pattern(wild), expr(wild))
1244 
1245             Replace subexpressions matching ``pattern`` with the expression
1246             written in terms of the Wild symbols in ``pattern``.
1247 
1248             >>> a = Wild('a')
1249             >>> f.replace(sin(a), tan(a))
1250             log(tan(x)) + tan(tan(x**2))
1251             >>> f.replace(sin(a), tan(a/2))
1252             log(tan(x/2)) + tan(tan(x**2/2))
1253             >>> f.replace(sin(a), a)
1254             log(x) + tan(x**2)
1255             >>> (x*y).replace(a*x, a)
1256             y
1257 
1258             When the default value of False is used with patterns that have
1259             more than one Wild symbol, non-intuitive results may be obtained:
1260 
1261             >>> b = Wild('b')
1262             >>> (2*x).replace(a*x + b, b - a)
1263             2/x
1264 
1265             For this reason, the ``exact`` option can be used to make the
1266             replacement only when the match gives non-zero values for all
1267             Wild symbols:
1268 
1269             >>> (2*x + y).replace(a*x + b, b - a, exact=True)
1270             y - 2
1271             >>> (2*x).replace(a*x + b, b - a, exact=True)
1272             2*x
1273 
1274         2.2. pattern -> func
1275             obj.replace(pattern(wild), lambda wild: expr(wild))
1276 
1277             All behavior is the same as in 2.1 but now a function in terms of
1278             pattern variables is used rather than an expression:
1279 
1280             >>> f.replace(sin(a), lambda a: sin(2*a))
1281             log(sin(2*x)) + tan(sin(2*x**2))
1282 
1283         3.1. func -> func
1284             obj.replace(filter, func)
1285 
1286             Replace subexpression ``e`` with ``func(e)`` if ``filter(e)``
1287             is True.
1288 
1289             >>> g = 2*sin(x**3)
1290             >>> g.replace(lambda expr: expr.is_Number, lambda expr: expr**2)
1291             4*sin(x**9)
1292 
1293         The expression itself is also targeted by the query but is done in
1294         such a fashion that changes are not made twice.
1295 
1296             >>> e = x*(x*y + 1)
1297             >>> e.replace(lambda x: x.is_Mul, lambda x: 2*x)
1298             2*x*(2*x*y + 1)
1299 
1300         See Also
1301         ========
1302         subs: substitution of subexpressions as defined by the objects
1303               themselves.
1304         xreplace: exact node replacement in expr tree; also capable of
1305                   using matching rules
1306 
1307         """
1308         from sympy.core.symbol import Dummy
1309         from sympy.simplify.simplify import bottom_up
1310 
1311         try:
1312             query = sympify(query)
1313         except SympifyError:
1314             pass
1315         try:
1316             value = sympify(value)
1317         except SympifyError:
1318             pass
1319         if isinstance(query, type):
1320             _query = lambda expr: isinstance(expr, query)
1321 
1322             if isinstance(value, type):
1323                 _value = lambda expr, result: value(*expr.args)
1324             elif callable(value):
1325                 _value = lambda expr, result: value(*expr.args)
1326             else:
1327                 raise TypeError(
1328                     "given a type, replace() expects another "
1329                     "type or a callable")
1330         elif isinstance(query, Basic):
1331             _query = lambda expr: expr.match(query)
1332 
1333             # XXX remove the exact flag and make multi-symbol
1334             # patterns use exact=True semantics; to do this the query must
1335             # be tested to find out how many Wild symbols are present.
1336             # See https://groups.google.com/forum/
1337             # ?fromgroups=#!topic/sympy/zPzo5FtRiqI
1338             # for a method of inspecting a function to know how many
1339             # parameters it has.
1340             if isinstance(value, Basic):
1341                 if exact:
1342                     _value = lambda expr, result: (value.subs(result)
1343                         if all(val for val in result.values()) else expr)
1344                 else:
1345                     _value = lambda expr, result: value.subs(result)
1346             elif callable(value):
1347                 # match dictionary keys get the trailing underscore stripped
1348                 # from them and are then passed as keywords to the callable;
1349                 # if ``exact`` is True, only accept match if there are no null
1350                 # values amongst those matched.
1351                 if exact:
1352                     _value = lambda expr, result: (value(**dict([(
1353                         str(key)[:-1], val) for key, val in result.items()]))
1354                         if all(val for val in result.values()) else expr)
1355                 else:
1356                     _value = lambda expr, result: value(**dict([(
1357                         str(key)[:-1], val) for key, val in result.items()]))
1358             else:
1359                 raise TypeError(
1360                     "given an expression, replace() expects "
1361                     "another expression or a callable")
1362         elif callable(query):
1363             _query = query
1364 
1365             if callable(value):
1366                 _value = lambda expr, result: value(expr)
1367             else:
1368                 raise TypeError(
1369                     "given a callable, replace() expects "
1370                     "another callable")
1371         else:
1372             raise TypeError(
1373                 "first argument to replace() must be a "
1374                 "type, an expression or a callable")
1375 
1376         mapping = {}  # changes that took place
1377         mask = []  # the dummies that were used as change placeholders
1378 
1379         def rec_replace(expr):
1380             result = _query(expr)
1381             if result or result == {}:
1382                 new = _value(expr, result)
1383                 if new is not None and new != expr:
1384                     mapping[expr] = new
1385                     if simultaneous:
1386                         # don't let this expression be changed during rebuilding
1387                         com = getattr(new, 'is_commutative', True)
1388                         if com is None:
1389                             com = True
1390                         d = Dummy(commutative=com)
1391                         mask.append((d, new))
1392                         expr = d
1393                     else:
1394                         expr = new
1395             return expr
1396 
1397         rv = bottom_up(self, rec_replace, atoms=True)
1398 
1399         # restore original expressions for Dummy symbols
1400         if simultaneous:
1401             mask = list(reversed(mask))
1402             for o, n in mask:
1403                 r = {o: n}
1404                 rv = rv.xreplace(r)
1405 
1406         if not map:
1407             return rv
1408         else:
1409             if simultaneous:
1410                 # restore subexpressions in mapping
1411                 for o, n in mask:
1412                     r = {o: n}
1413                     mapping = {k.xreplace(r): v.xreplace(r)
1414                         for k, v in mapping.items()}
1415             return rv, mapping

1417     def find(self, query, group=False):

1421 
1422         if not group:
1423             return set(results)
1424         else:
1425             groups = {}
1426 
1427             for result in results:
1428                 if result in groups:
1429                     groups[result] += 1
1430                 else:
1431                     groups[result] = 1
1432 
1433             return groups

1437         query = _make_find_query(query)

1440     def matches(self, expr, repl_dict={}, old=False):
1441         """
1442         Helper method for match() that looks for a match between Wild symbols
1443         in self and expressions in expr.

1445         Examples
1446         ========

1448         >>> from sympy import symbols, Wild, Basic
1449         >>> a, b, c = symbols('a b c')

1451         >>> Basic(a + x, x).matches(Basic(a + b, c)) is None
1452         True
1453         >>> Basic(a + x, x).matches(Basic(a + b + c, b + c))
1454         {x_: b + c}

1457         if not isinstance(expr, self.__class__):
1458             return None
1459 
1460         if self == expr:
1461             return repl_dict
1462 
1463         if len(self.args) != len(expr.args):
1464             return None
1465 
1466         d = repl_dict.copy()
1467         for arg, other_arg in zip(self.args, expr.args):
1468             if arg == other_arg:
1469                 continue
1470             d = arg.xreplace(d).matches(other_arg, d, old=old)
1471             if d is None:
1472                 return None

1482         with pattern. Otherwise return a dictionary such that::

1486         Examples

1489         >>> from sympy import Wild

1751 def _atomic(e):
1752     """Return atom-like quantities as far as substitution is

1767     {x, f(y)}
1768     >>> _atomic(Derivative(f(x), x) + cos(x) + y)
1769     {y, cos(x), Derivative(f(x), x)}
1770 
1771     """
1772     from sympy import Derivative, Function, Symbol
1773     pot = preorder_traversal(e)
1774     seen = set()
1775     try:
1776         free = e.free_symbols
1777     except AttributeError:
1778         return {e}
1779     atoms = set()
1780     for p in pot:
1781         if p in seen:
1782             pot.skip()
1783             continue

1786             atoms.add(p)

1793 class preorder_traversal(Iterator):
1794     """
1795     Do a pre-order traversal of a tree.
1796 
1797     This iterator recursively yields nodes that it has visited in a pre-order
1798     fashion. That is, it yields the current node then descends through the
1799     tree breadth-first to yield all of a node's children's pre-order
1800     traversal.
1801 
1802 
1803     For an expression, the order of the traversal depends on the order of
1804     .args, which in many cases can be arbitrary.
1805 
1806     Parameters
1807     ==========
1808     node : sympy expression
1809         The expression to traverse.
1810     keys : (default None) sort key(s)
1811         The key(s) used to sort args of Basic objects. When None, args of Basic
1812         objects are processed in arbitrary order. If key is defined, it will
1813         be passed along to ordered() as the only key(s) to use to sort the
1814         arguments; if ``key`` is simply True then the default keys of ordered
1815         will be used.
1816 
1817     Yields
1818     ======
1819     subtree : sympy expression
1820         All of the subtrees in the tree.
1821 
1822     Examples
1823     ========
1824 
1825     >>> from sympy import symbols
1826     >>> from sympy.core.basic import preorder_traversal
1827     >>> x, y, z = symbols('x y z')
1828 
1829     The nodes are returned in the order that they are encountered unless key
1830     is given; simply passing key=True will guarantee that the traversal is
1831     unique.
1832 
1833     >>> list(preorder_traversal((x + y)*z, keys=None)) # doctest: +SKIP
1834     [z*(x + y), z, x + y, y, x]
1835     >>> list(preorder_traversal((x + y)*z, keys=True))
1836     [z*(x + y), z, x + y, x, y]
1837 
1838     """
1839     def __init__(self, node, keys=None):
1840         self._skip_flag = False
1841         self._pt = self._preorder_traversal(node, keys)
1842 
1843     def _preorder_traversal(self, node, keys):
1844         yield node
1845         if self._skip_flag:
1846             self._skip_flag = False
1847             return
1848         if isinstance(node, Basic):
1849             if not keys and hasattr(node, '_argset'):
1850                 # LatticeOp keeps args as a set. We should use this if we
1851                 # don't care about the order, to prevent unnecessary sorting.
1852                 args = node._argset
1853             else:
1854                 args = node.args
1855             if keys:
1856                 if keys != True:
1857                     args = ordered(args, keys, default=False)
1858                 else:
1859                     args = ordered(args)
1860             for arg in args:
1861                 for subtree in self._preorder_traversal(arg, keys):
1862                     yield subtree
1863         elif iterable(node):
1864             for item in node:
1865                 for subtree in self._preorder_traversal(item, keys):
1866                     yield subtree
1867 
1868     def skip(self):
1869         """
1870         Skip yielding current node's (last yielded node's) subtrees.
1871 
1872         Examples
1873         ========
1874 
1875         >>> from sympy.core import symbols
1876         >>> from sympy.core.basic import preorder_traversal
1877         >>> x, y, z = symbols('x y z')
1878         >>> pt = preorder_traversal((x+y*z)*z)
1879         >>> for i in pt:
1880         ...     print(i)
1881         ...     if i == x+y*z:
1882         ...             pt.skip()
1883         z*(x + y*z)
1884         z
1885         x + y*z
1886         """
1887         self._skip_flag = True

31 def _monotonic_sign(self):
32     """Return the value closest to 0 that ``self`` may have if all symbols
33     are signed and the result is uniformly the same sign for all values of symbols.
34     If a symbol is only signed but not known to be an
35     integer or the result is 0 then a symbol representative of the sign of self
36     will be returned. Otherwise, None is returned if a) the sign could be positive
37     or negative or b) self is not in one of the following forms:
38 
39     - L(x, y, ...) + A: a function linear in all symbols x, y, ... with an
40       additive constant; if A is zero then the function can be a monomial whose
41       sign is monotonic over the range of the variables, e.g. (x + 1)**3 if x is
42       nonnegative.
43     - A/L(x, y, ...) + B: the inverse of a function linear in all symbols x, y, ...
44       that does not have a sign change from positive to negative for any set
45       of values for the variables.
46     - M(x, y, ...) + A: a monomial M whose factors are all signed and a constant, A.
47     - A/M(x, y, ...) + B: the inverse of a monomial and constants A and B.
48     - P(x): a univariate polynomial
49 
50     Examples
51     ========
52 
53     >>> from sympy.core.exprtools import _monotonic_sign as F
54     >>> from sympy import Dummy, S
55     >>> nn = Dummy(integer=True, nonnegative=True)
56     >>> p = Dummy(integer=True, positive=True)
57     >>> p2 = Dummy(integer=True, positive=True)
58     >>> F(nn + 1)
59     1
60     >>> F(p - 1)
61     _nneg
62     >>> F(nn*p + 1)
63     1
64     >>> F(p2*p + 1)
65     2
66     >>> F(nn - 1)  # could be negative, zero or positive
67     """
68     if not self.is_real:
69         return
70 
71     if (-self).is_Symbol:
72         rv = _monotonic_sign(-self)
73         return rv if rv is None else -rv
74 
75     if not self.is_Add and self.as_numer_denom()[1].is_number:
76         s = self
77         if s.is_prime:
78             if s.is_odd:
79                 return S(3)
80             else:
81                 return S(2)
82         elif s.is_positive:
83             if s.is_even:
84                 return S(2)
85             elif s.is_integer:
86                 return S.One
87             else:
88                 return _eps
89         elif s.is_negative:
90             if s.is_even:
91                 return S(-2)
92             elif s.is_integer:
93                 return S.NegativeOne
94             else:
95                 return -_eps
96         if s.is_zero or s.is_nonpositive or s.is_nonnegative:
97             return S.Zero
98         return None
99 
100     # univariate polynomial
101     free = self.free_symbols
102     if len(free) == 1:
103         if self.is_polynomial():
104             from sympy.polys.polytools import real_roots
105             from sympy.polys.polyroots import roots
106             from sympy.polys.polyerrors import PolynomialError
107             x = free.pop()

114                     roots = []

117                         roots = real_roots(d)

124                             return y if y.is_positive else Dummy('pos', positive=True)
125                         else:
126                             return Dummy('nneg', nonnegative=True)

128                         if y:

210     This is strictly only valid if the exponent from which
211     the integer is extracted is itself an integer or the

264             base, exp = expr, 1

266         exp, tail = exp.as_coeff_Mul(rational=True)
267 
268         if exp is S.NegativeOne:
269             base, exp = Pow(base, tail), -1
270         elif exp is not S.One:
271             tail = _keep_coeff(Rational(1, exp.q), tail)
272             base, exp = Pow(base, tail), exp.p
273         else:
274             base, exp = expr, 1
275 
276     return base, exp
277

279 class Factors(object):
280     """Efficient representation of ``f_1*f_2*...*f_n``."""
281 
282     __slots__ = ['factors', 'gens']
283 
284     def __init__(self, factors=None):  # Factors
285         """Initialize Factors from dict or expr.
286 
287         Examples
288         ========
289 
290         >>> from sympy.core.exprtools import Factors
291         >>> from sympy.abc import x
292         >>> from sympy import I
293         >>> e = 2*x**3
294         >>> Factors(e)
295         Factors({2: 1, x: 3})
296         >>> Factors(e.as_powers_dict())
297         Factors({2: 1, x: 3})
298         >>> f = _
299         >>> f.factors  # underlying dictionary
300         {2: 1, x: 3}
301         >>> f.gens  # base of each factor
302         frozenset({2, x})
303         >>> Factors(0)
304         Factors({0: 1})
305         >>> Factors(I)
306         Factors({I: 1})
307 
308         Notes
309         =====
310 
311         Although a dictionary can be passed, only minimal checking is
312         performed: powers of -1 and I are made canonical.
313 
314         """
315         if isinstance(factors, (SYMPY_INTS, float)):
316             factors = S(factors)
317 
318         if isinstance(factors, Factors):
319             factors = factors.factors.copy()
320         elif factors is None or factors is S.One:
321             factors = {}
322         elif factors is S.Zero or factors == 0:
323             factors = {S.Zero: S.One}
324         elif isinstance(factors, Number):
325             n = factors
326             factors = {}
327             if n < 0:
328                 factors[S.NegativeOne] = S.One
329                 n = -n
330             if n is not S.One:
331                 if n.is_Float or n.is_Integer or n is S.Infinity:
332                     factors[n] = S.One
333                 elif n.is_Rational:
334                     # since we're processing Numbers, the denominator is
335                     # stored with a negative exponent; all other factors
336                     # are left .
337                     if n.p != 1:
338                         factors[Integer(n.p)] = S.One
339                     factors[Integer(n.q)] = S.NegativeOne
340                 else:
341                     raise ValueError('Expected Float|Rational|Integer, not %s' % n)
342         elif isinstance(factors, Basic) and not factors.args:
343             factors = {factors: S.One}
344         elif isinstance(factors, Expr):
345             c, nc = factors.args_cnc()
346             i = c.count(I)
347             for _ in range(i):
348                 c.remove(I)
349             factors = dict(Mul._from_args(c).as_powers_dict())
350             if i:
351                 factors[I] = S.One*i
352             if nc:
353                 factors[Mul(*nc, evaluate=False)] = S.One
354         else:
355             factors = factors.copy()  # /!\ should be dict-like
356 
357             # tidy up -/+1 and I exponents if Rational
358 
359             handle = []
360             for k in factors:
361                 if k is I or k in (-1, 1):
362                     handle.append(k)
363             if handle:
364                 i1 = S.One
365                 for k in handle:
366                     if not _isnumber(factors[k]):
367                         continue
368                     i1 *= k**factors.pop(k)
369                 if i1 is not S.One:
370                     for a in i1.args if i1.is_Mul else [i1]:  # at worst, -1.0*I*(-1)**e
371                         if a is S.NegativeOne:
372                             factors[a] = S.One
373                         elif a is I:
374                             factors[I] = S.One
375                         elif a.is_Pow:
376                             if S.NegativeOne not in factors:
377                                 factors[S.NegativeOne] = S.Zero
378                             factors[S.NegativeOne] += a.exp
379                         elif a == 1:
380                             factors[a] = S.One
381                         elif a == -1:
382                             factors[-a] = S.One
383                             factors[S.NegativeOne] = S.One
384                         else:
385                             raise ValueError('unexpected factor in i1: %s' % a)
386 
387         self.factors = factors
388         try:
389             self.gens = frozenset(factors.keys())
390         except AttributeError:
391             raise TypeError('expecting Expr or dictionary')
392 
393     def __hash__(self):  # Factors
394         keys = tuple(ordered(self.factors.keys()))
395         values = [self.factors[k] for k in keys]
396         return hash((keys, values))
397 
398     def __repr__(self):  # Factors
399         return "Factors({%s})" % ', '.join(
400             ['%s: %s' % (k, v) for k, v in ordered(self.factors.items())])
401 
402     @property
403     def is_zero(self):  # Factors
404         """
405         >>> from sympy.core.exprtools import Factors
406         >>> Factors(0).is_zero
407         True
408         """
409         f = self.factors
410         return len(f) == 1 and S.Zero in f
411 
412     @property
413     def is_one(self):  # Factors
414         """
415         >>> from sympy.core.exprtools import Factors
416         >>> Factors(1).is_one
417         True
418         """
419         return not self.factors
420 
421     def as_expr(self):  # Factors
422         """Return the underlying expression.
423 
424         Examples
425         ========
426 
427         >>> from sympy.core.exprtools import Factors
428         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
429         >>> Factors((x*y**2).as_powers_dict()).as_expr()
430         x*y**2
431 
432         """
433 
434         args = []
435         for factor, exp in self.factors.items():
436             if exp != 1:
437                 b, e = factor.as_base_exp()
438                 if isinstance(exp, int):
439                     e = _keep_coeff(Integer(exp), e)
440                 elif isinstance(exp, Rational):
441                     e = _keep_coeff(exp, e)
442                 else:
443                     e *= exp
444                 args.append(b**e)
445             else:
446                 args.append(factor)
447         return Mul(*args)
448 
449     def mul(self, other):  # Factors
450         """Return Factors of ``self * other``.
451 
452         Examples
453         ========
454 
455         >>> from sympy.core.exprtools import Factors
456         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
457         >>> a = Factors((x*y**2).as_powers_dict())
458         >>> b = Factors((x*y/z).as_powers_dict())
459         >>> a.mul(b)
460         Factors({x: 2, y: 3, z: -1})
461         >>> a*b
462         Factors({x: 2, y: 3, z: -1})
463         """
464         if not isinstance(other, Factors):
465             other = Factors(other)
466         if any(f.is_zero for f in (self, other)):
467             return Factors(S.Zero)
468         factors = dict(self.factors)
469 
470         for factor, exp in other.factors.items():
471             if factor in factors:
472                 exp = factors[factor] + exp
473 
474                 if not exp:
475                     del factors[factor]
476                     continue
477 
478             factors[factor] = exp
479 
480         return Factors(factors)
481 
482     def normal(self, other):
483         """Return ``self`` and ``other`` with ``gcd`` removed from each.
484         The only differences between this and method ``div`` is that this
485         is 1) optimized for the case when there are few factors in common and
486         2) this does not raise an error if ``other`` is zero.
487 
488         See Also
489         ========
490         div
491 
492         """
493         if not isinstance(other, Factors):
494             other = Factors(other)
495             if other.is_zero:
496                 return (Factors(), Factors(S.Zero))
497             if self.is_zero:
498                 return (Factors(S.Zero), Factors())
499 
500         self_factors = dict(self.factors)
501         other_factors = dict(other.factors)
502 
503         for factor, self_exp in self.factors.items():
504             try:
505                 other_exp = other.factors[factor]
506             except KeyError:
507                 continue
508 
509             exp = self_exp - other_exp
510 
511             if not exp:
512                 del self_factors[factor]
513                 del other_factors[factor]
514             elif _isnumber(exp):
515                 if exp > 0:
516                     self_factors[factor] = exp
517                     del other_factors[factor]
518                 else:
519                     del self_factors[factor]
520                     other_factors[factor] = -exp
521             else:
522                 r = self_exp.extract_additively(other_exp)
523                 if r is not None:
524                     if r:
525                         self_factors[factor] = r
526                         del other_factors[factor]
527                     else:  # should be handled already
528                         del self_factors[factor]
529                         del other_factors[factor]
530                 else:
531                     sc, sa = self_exp.as_coeff_Add()
532                     if sc:
533                         oc, oa = other_exp.as_coeff_Add()
534                         diff = sc - oc
535                         if diff > 0:
536                             self_factors[factor] -= oc
537                             other_exp = oa
538                         elif diff < 0:
539                             self_factors[factor] -= sc
540                             other_factors[factor] -= sc
541                             other_exp = oa - diff
542                         else:
543                             self_factors[factor] = sa
544                             other_exp = oa
545                     if other_exp:
546                         other_factors[factor] = other_exp
547                     else:
548                         del other_factors[factor]
549 
550         return Factors(self_factors), Factors(other_factors)
551 
552     def div(self, other):  # Factors
553         """Return ``self`` and ``other`` with ``gcd`` removed from each.
554         This is optimized for the case when there are many factors in common.
555 
556         Examples
557         ========
558 
559         >>> from sympy.core.exprtools import Factors
560         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
561         >>> from sympy import S
562 
563         >>> a = Factors((x*y**2).as_powers_dict())
564         >>> a.div(a)
565         (Factors({}), Factors({}))
566         >>> a.div(x*z)
567         (Factors({y: 2}), Factors({z: 1}))
568 
569         The ``/`` operator only gives ``quo``:
570 
571         >>> a/x
572         Factors({y: 2})
573 
574         Factors treats its factors as though they are all in the numerator, so
575         if you violate this assumption the results will be correct but will
576         not strictly correspond to the numerator and denominator of the ratio:
577 
578         >>> a.div(x/z)
579         (Factors({y: 2}), Factors({z: -1}))
580 
581         Factors is also naive about bases: it does not attempt any denesting
582         of Rational-base terms, for example the following does not become
583         2**(2*x)/2.
584 
585         >>> Factors(2**(2*x + 2)).div(S(8))
586         (Factors({2: 2*x + 2}), Factors({8: 1}))
587 
588         factor_terms can clean up such Rational-bases powers:
589 
590         >>> from sympy.core.exprtools import factor_terms
591         >>> n, d = Factors(2**(2*x + 2)).div(S(8))
592         >>> n.as_expr()/d.as_expr()
593         2**(2*x + 2)/8
594         >>> factor_terms(_)
595         2**(2*x)/2
596 
597         """
598         quo, rem = dict(self.factors), {}
599 
600         if not isinstance(other, Factors):
601             other = Factors(other)
602             if other.is_zero:
603                 raise ZeroDivisionError
604             if self.is_zero:
605                 return (Factors(S.Zero), Factors())
606 
607         for factor, exp in other.factors.items():
608             if factor in quo:
609                 d = quo[factor] - exp
610                 if _isnumber(d):
611                     if d <= 0:
612                         del quo[factor]
613 
614                     if d >= 0:
615                         if d:
616                             quo[factor] = d
617 
618                         continue
619 
620                     exp = -d
621 
622                 else:
623                     r = quo[factor].extract_additively(exp)
624                     if r is not None:
625                         if r:
626                             quo[factor] = r
627                         else:  # should be handled already
628                             del quo[factor]
629                     else:
630                         other_exp = exp
631                         sc, sa = quo[factor].as_coeff_Add()
632                         if sc:
633                             oc, oa = other_exp.as_coeff_Add()
634                             diff = sc - oc
635                             if diff > 0:
636                                 quo[factor] -= oc
637                                 other_exp = oa
638                             elif diff < 0:
639                                 quo[factor] -= sc
640                                 other_exp = oa - diff
641                             else:
642                                 quo[factor] = sa
643                                 other_exp = oa
644                         if other_exp:
645                             rem[factor] = other_exp
646                         else:
647                             assert factor not in rem
648                     continue
649 
650             rem[factor] = exp
651 
652         return Factors(quo), Factors(rem)
653 
654     def quo(self, other):  # Factors
655         """Return numerator Factor of ``self / other``.
656 
657         Examples
658         ========
659 
660         >>> from sympy.core.exprtools import Factors
661         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
662         >>> a = Factors((x*y**2).as_powers_dict())
663         >>> b = Factors((x*y/z).as_powers_dict())
664         >>> a.quo(b)  # same as a/b
665         Factors({y: 1})
666         """
667         return self.div(other)[0]
668 
669     def rem(self, other):  # Factors
670         """Return denominator Factors of ``self / other``.
671 
672         Examples
673         ========
674 
675         >>> from sympy.core.exprtools import Factors
676         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
677         >>> a = Factors((x*y**2).as_powers_dict())
678         >>> b = Factors((x*y/z).as_powers_dict())
679         >>> a.rem(b)
680         Factors({z: -1})
681         >>> a.rem(a)
682         Factors({})
683         """
684         return self.div(other)[1]
685 
686     def pow(self, other):  # Factors
687         """Return self raised to a non-negative integer power.
688 
689         Examples
690         ========
691 
692         >>> from sympy.core.exprtools import Factors
693         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
694         >>> a = Factors((x*y**2).as_powers_dict())
695         >>> a**2
696         Factors({x: 2, y: 4})
697 
698         """
699         if isinstance(other, Factors):
700             other = other.as_expr()
701             if other.is_Integer:
702                 other = int(other)
703         if isinstance(other, SYMPY_INTS) and other >= 0:
704             factors = {}
705 
706             if other:
707                 for factor, exp in self.factors.items():
708                     factors[factor] = exp*other
709 
710             return Factors(factors)
711         else:
712             raise ValueError("expected non-negative integer, got %s" % other)
713 
714     def gcd(self, other):  # Factors
715         """Return Factors of ``gcd(self, other)``. The keys are
716         the intersection of factors with the minimum exponent for
717         each factor.
718 
719         Examples
720         ========
721 
722         >>> from sympy.core.exprtools import Factors
723         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
724         >>> a = Factors((x*y**2).as_powers_dict())
725         >>> b = Factors((x*y/z).as_powers_dict())
726         >>> a.gcd(b)
727         Factors({x: 1, y: 1})
728         """
729         if not isinstance(other, Factors):
730             other = Factors(other)
731             if other.is_zero:
732                 return Factors(self.factors)
733 
734         factors = {}
735 
736         for factor, exp in self.factors.items():
737             factor, exp = sympify(factor), sympify(exp)
738             if factor in other.factors:
739                 lt = (exp - other.factors[factor]).is_negative
740                 if lt == True:
741                     factors[factor] = exp
742                 elif lt == False:
743                     factors[factor] = other.factors[factor]
744 
745         return Factors(factors)
746 
747     def lcm(self, other):  # Factors
748         """Return Factors of ``lcm(self, other)`` which are
749         the union of factors with the maximum exponent for
750         each factor.
751 
752         Examples
753         ========
754 
755         >>> from sympy.core.exprtools import Factors
756         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
757         >>> a = Factors((x*y**2).as_powers_dict())
758         >>> b = Factors((x*y/z).as_powers_dict())
759         >>> a.lcm(b)
760         Factors({x: 1, y: 2, z: -1})
761         """
762         if not isinstance(other, Factors):
763             other = Factors(other)
764             if any(f.is_zero for f in (self, other)):
765                 return Factors(S.Zero)
766 
767         factors = dict(self.factors)
768 
769         for factor, exp in other.factors.items():
770             if factor in factors:
771                 exp = max(exp, factors[factor])
772 
773             factors[factor] = exp
774 
775         return Factors(factors)
776 
777     def __mul__(self, other):  # Factors
778         return self.mul(other)
779 
780     def __divmod__(self, other):  # Factors
781         return self.div(other)
782 
783     def __div__(self, other):  # Factors
784         return self.quo(other)
785 
786     __truediv__ = __div__
787 
788     def __mod__(self, other):  # Factors
789         return self.rem(other)
790 
791     def __pow__(self, other):  # Factors
792         return self.pow(other)
793 
794     def __eq__(self, other):  # Factors
795         if not isinstance(other, Factors):
796             other = Factors(other)
797         return self.factors == other.factors
798 
799     def __ne__(self, other):  # Factors
800         return not self.__eq__(other)

803 class Term(object):
804     """Efficient representation of ``coeff*(numer/denom)``. """
805 
806     __slots__ = ['coeff', 'numer', 'denom']
807 
808     def __init__(self, term, numer=None, denom=None):  # Term
809         if numer is None and denom is None:
810             if not term.is_commutative:
811                 raise NonCommutativeExpression(
812                     'commutative expression expected')
813 
814             coeff, factors = term.as_coeff_mul()
815             numer, denom = defaultdict(int), defaultdict(int)
816 
817             for factor in factors:
818                 base, exp = decompose_power(factor)
819 
820                 if base.is_Add:
821                     cont, base = base.primitive()
822                     coeff *= cont**exp
823 
824                 if exp > 0:
825                     numer[base] += exp
826                 else:
827                     denom[base] += -exp
828 
829             numer = Factors(numer)
830             denom = Factors(denom)
831         else:
832             coeff = term
833 
834             if numer is None:
835                 numer = Factors()
836 
837             if denom is None:
838                 denom = Factors()
839 
840         self.coeff = coeff
841         self.numer = numer
842         self.denom = denom
843 
844     def __hash__(self):  # Term
845         return hash((self.coeff, self.numer, self.denom))
846 
847     def __repr__(self):  # Term
848         return "Term(%s, %s, %s)" % (self.coeff, self.numer, self.denom)
849 
850     def as_expr(self):  # Term
851         return self.coeff*(self.numer.as_expr()/self.denom.as_expr())
852 
853     def mul(self, other):  # Term
854         coeff = self.coeff*other.coeff
855         numer = self.numer.mul(other.numer)
856         denom = self.denom.mul(other.denom)
857 
858         numer, denom = numer.normal(denom)
859 
860         return Term(coeff, numer, denom)
861 
862     def inv(self):  # Term
863         return Term(1/self.coeff, self.denom, self.numer)
864 
865     def quo(self, other):  # Term
866         return self.mul(other.inv())
867 
868     def pow(self, other):  # Term
869         if other < 0:
870             return self.inv().pow(-other)
871         else:
872             return Term(self.coeff ** other,
873                         self.numer.pow(other),
874                         self.denom.pow(other))
875 
876     def gcd(self, other):  # Term
877         return Term(self.coeff.gcd(other.coeff),
878                     self.numer.gcd(other.numer),
879                     self.denom.gcd(other.denom))
880 
881     def lcm(self, other):  # Term
882         return Term(self.coeff.lcm(other.coeff),
883                     self.numer.lcm(other.numer),
884                     self.denom.lcm(other.denom))
885 
886     def __mul__(self, other):  # Term
887         if isinstance(other, Term):
888             return self.mul(other)
889         else:
890             return NotImplemented
891 
892     def __div__(self, other):  # Term
893         if isinstance(other, Term):
894             return self.quo(other)
895         else:
896             return NotImplemented
897 
898     __truediv__ = __div__
899 
900     def __pow__(self, other):  # Term
901         if isinstance(other, SYMPY_INTS):
902             return self.pow(other)
903         else:
904             return NotImplemented
905 
906     def __eq__(self, other):  # Term
907         return (self.coeff == other.coeff and
908                 self.numer == other.numer and
909                 self.denom == other.denom)
910 
911     def __ne__(self, other):  # Term
912         return not self.__eq__(other)

915 def _gcd_terms(terms, isprimitive=False, fraction=True):
916     """Helper function for :func:`gcd_terms`.
917 
918     If ``isprimitive`` is True then the call to primitive
919     for an Add will be skipped. This is useful when the
920     content has already been extrated.
921 
922     If ``fraction`` is True then the expression will appear over a common
923     denominator, the lcm of all term denominators.
924     """
925 
926     if isinstance(terms, Basic) and not isinstance(terms, Tuple):
927         terms = Add.make_args(terms)
928 
929     terms = list(map(Term, [t for t in terms if t]))
930 
931     # there is some simplification that may happen if we leave this
932     # here rather than duplicate it before the mapping of Term onto
933     # the terms
934     if len(terms) == 0:
935         return S.Zero, S.Zero, S.One
936 
937     if len(terms) == 1:
938         cont = terms[0].coeff
939         numer = terms[0].numer.as_expr()
940         denom = terms[0].denom.as_expr()
941 
942     else:
943         cont = terms[0]
944         for term in terms[1:]:
945             cont = cont.gcd(term)
946 
947         for i, term in enumerate(terms):
948             terms[i] = term.quo(cont)
949 
950         if fraction:
951             denom = terms[0].denom
952 
953             for term in terms[1:]:
954                 denom = denom.lcm(term.denom)
955 
956             numers = []
957             for term in terms:
958                 numer = term.numer.mul(denom.quo(term.denom))
959                 numers.append(term.coeff*numer.as_expr())
960         else:
961             numers = [t.as_expr() for t in terms]
962             denom = Term(S(1)).numer
963 
964         cont = cont.as_expr()
965         numer = Add(*numers)
966         denom = denom.as_expr()
967 
968     if not isprimitive and numer.is_Add:
969         _cont, numer = numer.primitive()
970         cont *= _cont
971 
972     return cont, numer, denom
973 
974 
975 def gcd_terms(terms, isprimitive=False, clear=True, fraction=True):
976     """Compute the GCD of ``terms`` and put them together.
977 
978     ``terms`` can be an expression or a non-Basic sequence of expressions
979     which will be handled as though they are terms from a sum.
980 
981     If ``isprimitive`` is True the _gcd_terms will not run the primitive
982     method on the terms.
983 
984     ``clear`` controls the removal of integers from the denominator of an Add
985     expression. When True (default), all numerical denominator will be cleared;
986     when False the denominators will be cleared only if all terms had numerical
987     denominators other than 1.
988 
989     ``fraction``, when True (default), will put the expression over a common
990     denominator.
991 
992     Examples
993     ========
994 
995     >>> from sympy.core import gcd_terms
996     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
997 
998     >>> gcd_terms((x + 1)**2*y + (x + 1)*y**2)
999     y*(x + 1)*(x + y + 1)
1000     >>> gcd_terms(x/2 + 1)
1001     (x + 2)/2
1002     >>> gcd_terms(x/2 + 1, clear=False)
1003     x/2 + 1
1004     >>> gcd_terms(x/2 + y/2, clear=False)
1005     (x + y)/2
1006     >>> gcd_terms(x/2 + 1/x)
1007     (x**2 + 2)/(2*x)
1008     >>> gcd_terms(x/2 + 1/x, fraction=False)
1009     (x + 2/x)/2
1010     >>> gcd_terms(x/2 + 1/x, fraction=False, clear=False)
1011     x/2 + 1/x
1012

1093 def factor_terms(expr, radical=False, clear=False, fraction=False, sign=True):
1094     """Remove common factors from terms in all arguments without
1095     changing the underlying structure of the expr. No expansion or
1096     simplification (and no processing of non-commutatives) is performed.
1097 
1098     If radical=True then a radical common to all terms will be factored
1099     out of any Add sub-expressions of the expr.
1100 
1101     If clear=False (default) then coefficients will not be separated
1102     from a single Add if they can be distributed to leave one or more
1103     terms with integer coefficients.
1104 
1105     If fraction=True (default is False) then a common denominator will be
1106     constructed for the expression.
1107 
1108     If sign=True (default) then even if the only factor in common is a -1,
1109     it will be factored out of the expression.
1110 
1111     Examples
1112     ========
1113 
1114     >>> from sympy import factor_terms, Symbol
1115     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
1116     >>> factor_terms(x + x*(2 + 4*y)**3)
1117     x*(8*(2*y + 1)**3 + 1)
1118     >>> A = Symbol('A', commutative=False)
1119     >>> factor_terms(x*A + x*A + x*y*A)
1120     x*(y*A + 2*A)
1121 
1122     When ``clear`` is False, a rational will only be factored out of an
1123     Add expression if all terms of the Add have coefficients that are
1124     fractions:
1125 
1126     >>> factor_terms(x/2 + 1, clear=False)
1127     x/2 + 1
1128     >>> factor_terms(x/2 + 1, clear=True)
1129     (x + 2)/2
1130 
1131     If a -1 is all that can be factored out, to *not* factor it out, the
1132     flag ``sign`` must be False:
1133 
1134     >>> factor_terms(-x - y)
1135     -(x + y)
1136     >>> factor_terms(-x - y, sign=False)
1137     -x - y
1138     >>> factor_terms(-2*x - 2*y, sign=False)
1139     -2*(x + y)
1140 
1141     See Also
1142     ========
1143     gcd_terms, sympy.polys.polytools.terms_gcd
1144 
1145     """
1146     def do(expr):
1147         from sympy.concrete.summations import Sum
1148         from sympy.simplify.simplify import factor_sum
1149         is_iterable = iterable(expr)
1150 
1151         if not isinstance(expr, Basic) or expr.is_Atom:
1152             if is_iterable:
1153                 return type(expr)([do(i) for i in expr])
1154             return expr
1155 
1156         if expr.is_Pow or expr.is_Function or \
1157                 is_iterable or not hasattr(expr, 'args_cnc'):
1158             args = expr.args
1159             newargs = tuple([do(i) for i in args])
1160             if newargs == args:
1161                 return expr
1162             return expr.func(*newargs)
1163 
1164         if isinstance(expr, Sum):
1165             return factor_sum(expr, radical=radical, clear=clear, fraction=fraction, sign=sign)
1166 
1167         cont, p = expr.as_content_primitive(radical=radical, clear=clear)
1168         if p.is_Add:
1169             list_args = [do(a) for a in Add.make_args(p)]
1170             # get a common negative (if there) which gcd_terms does not remove
1171             if all(a.as_coeff_Mul()[0] < 0 for a in list_args):
1172                 cont = -cont
1173                 list_args = [-a for a in list_args]
1174             # watch out for exp(-(x+2)) which gcd_terms will change to exp(-x-2)
1175             special = {}
1176             for i, a in enumerate(list_args):
1177                 b, e = a.as_base_exp()
1178                 if e.is_Mul and e != Mul(*e.args):
1179                     list_args[i] = Dummy()
1180                     special[list_args[i]] = a
1181             # rebuild p not worrying about the order which gcd_terms will fix
1182             p = Add._from_args(list_args)
1183             p = gcd_terms(p,
1184                 isprimitive=True,
1185                 clear=clear,
1186                 fraction=fraction).xreplace(special)
1187         elif p.args:
1188             p = p.func(
1189                 *[do(a) for a in p.args])
1190         rv = _keep_coeff(cont, p, clear=clear, sign=sign)
1191         return rv
1192     expr = sympify(expr)
1193     return do(expr)

1196 def _mask_nc(eq, name=None):
1197     """
1198     Return ``eq`` with non-commutative objects replaced with Dummy
1199     symbols. A dictionary that can be used to restore the original
1200     values is returned: if it is None, the expression is noncommutative
1201     and cannot be made commutative. The third value returned is a list
1202     of any non-commutative symbols that appear in the returned equation.
1203 
1204     ``name``, if given, is the name that will be used with numered Dummy
1205     variables that will replace the non-commutative objects and is mainly
1206     used for doctesting purposes.
1207 
1208     Notes
1209     =====
1210     All non-commutative objects other than Symbols are replaced with
1211     a non-commutative Symbol. Identical objects will be identified
1212     by identical symbols.
1213 
1214     If there is only 1 non-commutative object in an expression it will
1215     be replaced with a commutative symbol. Otherwise, the non-commutative
1216     entities are retained and the calling routine should handle
1217     replacements in this case since some care must be taken to keep
1218     track of the ordering of symbols when they occur within Muls.
1219 
1220     Examples
1221     ========
1222 
1223     >>> from sympy.physics.secondquant import Commutator, NO, F, Fd
1224     >>> from sympy import symbols, Mul
1225     >>> from sympy.core.exprtools import _mask_nc
1226     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
1227     >>> A, B, C = symbols('A,B,C', commutative=False)
1228 
1229     One nc-symbol:
1230 
1231     >>> _mask_nc(A**2 - x**2, 'd')
1232     (_d0**2 - x**2, {_d0: A}, [])
1233 
1234     Multiple nc-symbols:
1235 
1236     >>> _mask_nc(A**2 - B**2, 'd')
1237     (A**2 - B**2, None, [A, B])
1238 
1239     An nc-object with nc-symbols but no others outside of it:
1240 
1241     >>> _mask_nc(1 + x*Commutator(A, B), 'd')
1242     (_d0*x + 1, {_d0: Commutator(A, B)}, [])
1243     >>> _mask_nc(NO(Fd(x)*F(y)), 'd')
1244     (_d0, {_d0: NO(CreateFermion(x)*AnnihilateFermion(y))}, [])
1245 
1246     Multiple nc-objects:
1247 
1248     >>> eq = x*Commutator(A, B) + x*Commutator(A, C)*Commutator(A, B)
1249     >>> _mask_nc(eq, 'd')
1250     (x*_d0 + x*_d1*_d0, {_d0: Commutator(A, B), _d1: Commutator(A, C)}, [_d0, _d1])
1251 
1252     Multiple nc-objects and nc-symbols:
1253 
1254     >>> eq = A*Commutator(A, B) + B*Commutator(A, C)
1255     >>> _mask_nc(eq, 'd')
1256     (A*_d0 + B*_d1, {_d0: Commutator(A, B), _d1: Commutator(A, C)}, [_d0, _d1, A, B])
1257 
1258     If there is an object that:
1259 
1260         - doesn't contain nc-symbols
1261         - but has arguments which derive from Basic, not Expr
1262         - and doesn't define an _eval_is_commutative routine
1263 
1264     then it will give False (or None?) for the is_commutative test. Such
1265     objects are also removed by this routine:
1266 
1267     >>> from sympy import Basic
1268     >>> eq = (1 + Mul(Basic(), Basic(), evaluate=False))
1269     >>> eq.is_commutative
1270     False
1271     >>> _mask_nc(eq, 'd')
1272     (_d0**2 + 1, {_d0: Basic()}, [])
1273 
1274     """
1275     name = name or 'mask'
1276     # Make Dummy() append sequential numbers to the name
1277 
1278     def numbered_names():
1279         i = 0
1280         while True:
1281             yield name + str(i)
1282             i += 1
1283 
1284     names = numbered_names()
1285 
1286     def Dummy(*args, **kwargs):
1287         from sympy import Dummy
1288         return Dummy(next(names), *args, **kwargs)
1289 
1290     expr = eq
1291     if expr.is_commutative:
1292         return eq, {}, []
1293 
1294     # identify nc-objects; symbols and other
1295     rep = []
1296     nc_obj = set()
1297     nc_syms = set()
1298     pot = preorder_traversal(expr, keys=default_sort_key)
1299     for i, a in enumerate(pot):
1300         if any(a == r[0] for r in rep):
1301             pot.skip()
1302         elif not a.is_commutative:
1303             if a.is_Symbol:
1304                 nc_syms.add(a)
1305             elif not (a.is_Add or a.is_Mul or a.is_Pow):
1306                 if all(s.is_commutative for s in a.free_symbols):
1307                     rep.append((a, Dummy()))
1308                 else:
1309                     nc_obj.add(a)
1310                 pot.skip()
1311 
1312     # If there is only one nc symbol or object, it can be factored regularly
1313     # but polys is going to complain, so replace it with a Dummy.
1314     if len(nc_obj) == 1 and not nc_syms:
1315         rep.append((nc_obj.pop(), Dummy()))
1316     elif len(nc_syms) == 1 and not nc_obj:
1317         rep.append((nc_syms.pop(), Dummy()))
1318 
1319     # Any remaining nc-objects will be replaced with an nc-Dummy and
1320     # identified as an nc-Symbol to watch out for
1321     nc_obj = sorted(nc_obj, key=default_sort_key)
1322     for n in nc_obj:
1323         nc = Dummy(commutative=False)
1324         rep.append((n, nc))
1325         nc_syms.add(nc)
1326     expr = expr.subs(rep)
1327 
1328     nc_syms = list(nc_syms)
1329     nc_syms.sort(key=default_sort_key)
1330     return expr, {v: k for k, v in rep} or None, nc_syms

1337     Examples

1342     >>> from sympy.abc import x
1343     >>> A = Symbol('A', commutative=False)
1344     >>> B = Symbol('B', commutative=False)
1345     >>> factor_nc((x**2 + 2*A*x + A**2).expand())
1346     (x + A)**2

1360         return expr

1365     if rep:
1366         return factor(expr).subs(rep)
1367     else:
1368         args = [a.args_cnc() for a in Add.make_args(expr)]
1369         c = g = l = r = S.One
1370         hit = False
1371         # find any commutative gcd term
1372         for i, a in enumerate(args):
1373             if i == 0:
1374                 c = Mul._from_args(a[0])
1375             elif a[0]:
1376                 c = gcd(c, Mul._from_args(a[0]))
1377             else:
1378                 c = S.One
1379         if c is not S.One:
1380             hit = True
1381             c, g = c.as_coeff_Mul()
1382             if g is not S.One:
1383                 for i, (cc, _) in enumerate(args):
1384                     cc = list(Mul.make_args(Mul._from_args(list(cc))/g))

1386             for i, (cc, _) in enumerate(args):
1387                 cc[0] = cc[0]/c

1390         for i, a in enumerate(args):
1391             if i == 0:
1392                 n = a[1][:]

1394                 n = common_prefix(n, a[1])

1396                 # is there a power that can be extracted?
1397                 if not args[0][1]:
1398                     break
1399                 b, e = args[0][1][0].as_base_exp()
1400                 ok = False
1401                 if e.is_Integer:
1402                     for t in args:
1403                         if not t[1]:
1404                             break
1405                         bt, et = t[1][0].as_base_exp()
1406                         if et.is_Integer and bt == b:
1407                             e = min(e, et)
1408                         else:
1409                             break
1410                     else:
1411                         ok = hit = True

1413                         il = b**-e

1421             lenn = len(n)

1423             for i, a in enumerate(args):

1426         for i, a in enumerate(args):
1427             if i == 0:
1428                 n = a[1][:]
1429             else:
1430                 n = common_suffix(n, a[1])

1432                 # is there a power that can be extracted?
1433                 if not args[0][1]:

1436                 ok = False
1437                 if e.is_Integer:

1439                         if not t[1]:
1440                             break
1441                         bt, et = t[1][-1].as_base_exp()
1442                         if et.is_Integer and bt == b:

38 def comp(z1, z2, tol=None):
39     """Return a bool indicating whether the error between z1 and z2 is <= tol.
40 
41     If ``tol`` is None then True will be returned if there is a significant
42     difference between the numbers: ``abs(z1 - z2)*10**p <= 1/2`` where ``p``
43     is the lower of the precisions of the values. A comparison of strings will
44     be made if ``z1`` is a Number and a) ``z2`` is a string or b) ``tol`` is ''
45     and ``z2`` is a Number.
46 
47     When ``tol`` is a nonzero value, if z2 is non-zero and ``|z1| > 1``
48     the error is normalized by ``|z1|``, so if you want to see if the
49     absolute error between ``z1`` and ``z2`` is <= ``tol`` then call this
50     as ``comp(z1 - z2, 0, tol)``.
51     """
52     if type(z2) is str:
53         if not isinstance(z1, Number):
54             raise ValueError('when z2 is a str z1 must be a Number')
55         return str(z1) == z2
56     if not z1:
57         z1, z2 = z2, z1
58     if not z1:
59         return True
60     if not tol:
61         if tol is None:
62             if type(z2) is str and getattr(z1, 'is_Number', False):
63                 return str(z1) == z2
64             a, b = Float(z1), Float(z2)
65             return int(abs(a - b)*10**prec_to_dps(
66                 min(a._prec, b._prec)))*2 <= 1
67         elif all(getattr(i, 'is_Number', False) for i in (z1, z2)):
68             return z1._prec == z2._prec and str(z1) == str(z2)
69         raise ValueError('exact comparison requires two Numbers')
70     diff = abs(z1 - z2)
71     az1 = abs(z1)
72     if z2 and az1 > 1:
73         return diff/az1 <= tol
74     else:
75         return diff <= tol

224 # Use Lehmer's algorithm only for very large numbers.
225 # The limit could be different on Python 2.7 and 3.x.
226 # If so, then this could be defined in compatibility.py.
227 BIGBITS = 5000
228 def igcd_lehmer(a, b):
229     """Computes greatest common divisor of two integers.
230 
231     Euclid's algorithm for the computation of the greatest
232     common divisor  gcd(a, b)  of two (positive) integers
233     a and b is based on the division identity
234         a = q*b + r,
235     where the quotient  q  and the remainder  r  are integers
236     and  0 <= r < b. Then each common divisor of  a  and  b
237     divides  r, and it follows that  gcd(a, b) == gcd(b, r).
238     The algorithm works by constructing the sequence
239     r0, r1, r2, ..., where  r0 = a, r1 = b,  and each  rn
240     is the remainder from the division of the two preceding
241     elements.
242 
243     In Python, q = a // b  and  r = a % b  are obtained by the
244     floor division and the remainder operations, respectively.
245     These are the most expensive arithmetic operations, especially
246     for large  a  and  b.
247 
248     Lehmer's algorithm is based on the observation that the quotients
249     qn = r(n-1) // rn  are in general small integers even
250     when  a  and  b  are very large. Hence the quotients can be
251     usually determined from a relatively small number of most
252     significant bits.
253 
254     The efficiency of the algorithm is further enhanced by not
255     computing each long remainder in Euclid's sequence. The remainders
256     are linear combinations of  a  and  b  with integer coefficients
257     derived from the quotients. The coefficients can be computed
258     as far as the quotients can be determined from the chosen
259     most significant parts of  a  and  b. Only then a new pair of
260     consecutive remainders is computed and the algorithm starts
261     anew with this pair.
262 
263     References
264     ==========
265 
266     .. [1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehmer%27s_GCD_algorithm
267 
268     """
269     a, b = abs(as_int(a)), abs(as_int(b))
270     if a < b:
271         a, b = b, a
272 
273     # The algorithm works by using one or two digit division
274     # whenever possible. The outer loop will replace the
275     # pair (a, b) with a pair of shorter consecutive elements
276     # of the Euclidean gcd sequence until a and b
277     # fit into two Python (long) int digits.
278     nbits = 2*int_info.bits_per_digit
279 
280     while a.bit_length() > nbits and b != 0:
281         # Quotients are mostly small integers that can
282         # be determined from most significant bits.
283         n = a.bit_length() - nbits
284         x, y = int(a >> n), int(b >> n)  # most significant bits
285 
286         # Elements of the Euclidean gcd sequence are linear
287         # combinations of a and b with integer coefficients.
288         # Compute the coefficients of consequtive pairs
289         #     a' = A*a + B*b, b' = C*a + D*b
290         # using small integer arithmetic as far as possible.
291         A, B, C, D = 1, 0, 0, 1  # initial values
292 
293         while True:
294             # The coefficients alternate in sign while looping.
295             # The inner loop combines two steps to keep track
296             # of the signs.
297 
298             # At this point we have
299             #   A > 0, B <= 0, C <= 0, D > 0,
300             #   x' = x + B <= x < x" = x + A,
301             #   y' = y + C <= y < y" = y + D,
302             # and
303             #   x'*N <= a' < x"*N, y'*N <= b' < y"*N,
304             # where N = 2**n.
305 
306             # Now, if y' > 0, and x"//y' and x'//y" agree,
307             # then their common value is equal to  q = a'//b'.
308             # In addition,
309             #   x'%y" = x' - q*y" < x" - q*y' = x"%y',
310             # and
311             #   (x'%y")*N < a'%b' < (x"%y')*N.
312 
313             # On the other hand, we also have  x//y == q,
314             # and therefore
315             #   x'%y" = x + B - q*(y + D) = x%y + B',
316             #   x"%y' = x + A - q*(y + C) = x%y + A',
317             # where
318             #    B' = B - q*D < 0, A' = A - q*C > 0.
319 
320             if y + C <= 0:
321                 break
322             q = (x + A) // (y + C)
323 
324             # Now  x'//y" <= q, and equality holds if
325             #   x' - q*y" = (x - q*y) + (B - q*D) >= 0.
326             # This is a minor optimization to avoid division.
327             x_qy, B_qD = x - q*y, B - q*D
328             if x_qy + B_qD < 0:
329                 break
330 
331             # Next step in the Euclidean sequence.
332             x, y = y, x_qy
333             A, B, C, D = C, D, A - q*C, B_qD
334 
335             # At this point the signs of the coefficients
336             # change and their roles are interchanged.
337             #   A <= 0, B > 0, C > 0, D < 0,
338             #   x' = x + A <= x < x" = x + B,
339             #   y' = y + D < y < y" = y + C.
340 
341             if y + D <= 0:
342                 break
343             q = (x + B) // (y + D)
344             x_qy, A_qC = x - q*y, A - q*C
345             if x_qy + A_qC < 0:
346                 break
347 
348             x, y = y, x_qy
349             A, B, C, D = C, D, A_qC, B - q*D
350             # Now the conditions on top of the loop
351             # are again satisfied.
352             #   A > 0, B < 0, C < 0, D > 0.
353 
354         if B == 0:
355             # This can only happen when y == 0 in the beginning
356             # and the inner loop does nothing.
357             # Long division is forced.
358             a, b = b, a % b
359             continue
360 
361         # Compute new long arguments using the coefficients.
362         a, b = A*a + B*b, C*a + D*b
363 
364     # Small divisors. Finish with the standard algorithm.
365     while b:
366         a, b = b, a % b
367 
368     return a
369

397 def igcdex(a, b):
398     """Returns x, y, g such that g = x*a + y*b = gcd(a, b).
399 
400        >>> from sympy.core.numbers import igcdex
401        >>> igcdex(2, 3)
402        (-1, 1, 1)
403        >>> igcdex(10, 12)
404        (-1, 1, 2)
405 
406        >>> x, y, g = igcdex(100, 2004)
407        >>> x, y, g
408        (-20, 1, 4)
409        >>> x*100 + y*2004
410        4
411 
412     """
413     if (not a) and (not b):
414         return (0, 1, 0)
415 
416     if not a:
417         return (0, b//abs(b), abs(b))
418     if not b:
419         return (a//abs(a), 0, abs(a))
420 
421     if a < 0:
422         a, x_sign = -a, -1
423     else:
424         x_sign = 1
425 
426     if b < 0:
427         b, y_sign = -b, -1
428     else:
429         y_sign = 1
430 
431     x, y, r, s = 1, 0, 0, 1
432 
433     while b:
434         (c, q) = (a % b, a // b)
435         (a, b, r, s, x, y) = (b, c, x - q*r, y - q*s, r, s)
436 
437     return (x*x_sign, y*y_sign, a)
438

440 def mod_inverse(a, m):
441     """
442     Return the number c such that, ( a * c ) % m == 1 where
443     c has the same sign as a. If no such value exists, a
444     ValueError is raised.
445 
446     Examples
447     ========
448 
449     >>> from sympy import S
450     >>> from sympy.core.numbers import mod_inverse
451 
452     Suppose we wish to find multiplicative inverse x of
453     3 modulo 11. This is the same as finding x such
454     that 3 * x = 1 (mod 11). One value of x that satisfies
455     this congruence is 4. Because 3 * 4 = 12 and 12 = 1 mod(11).
456     This is the value return by mod_inverse:
457 
458     >>> mod_inverse(3, 11)
459     4
460     >>> mod_inverse(-3, 11)
461     -4
462 
463     When there is a common factor between the numerators of
464     ``a`` and ``m`` the inverse does not exist:
465 
466     >>> mod_inverse(2, 4)
467     Traceback (most recent call last):
468     ...
469     ValueError: inverse of 2 mod 4 does not exist
470 
471     >>> mod_inverse(S(2)/7, S(5)/2)
472     7/2
473 
474     References
475     ==========
476     - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modular_multiplicative_inverse
477     - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_Euclidean_algorithm
478     """
479     c = None
480     try:
481         a, m = as_int(a), as_int(m)
482         if m > 1:
483             x, y, g = igcdex(a, m)
484             if g == 1:
485                 c = x % m
486             if a < 0:
487                 c -= m
488     except ValueError:
489         a, m = sympify(a), sympify(m)
490         if not (a.is_number and m.is_number):
491             raise TypeError(filldedent('''
492                 Expected numbers for arguments; symbolic `mod_inverse`
493                 is not implemented
494                 but symbolic expressions can be handled with the
495                 similar function,
496                 sympy.polys.polytools.invert'''))
497         big = (m > 1)
498         if not (big is S.true or big is S.false):
499             raise ValueError('m > 1 did not evaluate; try to simplify %s' % m)
500         elif big:
501             c = 1/a
502     if c is None:
503         raise ValueError('inverse of %s (mod %s) does not exist' % (a, m))
504     return c

802     1.00000000000000e+20
803     >>> Float(1.23456789123456789)
804     1.23456789123457
805 
806     It may be preferable to enter high-precision decimal numbers
807     as strings:
808 
809     Float('1.23456789123456789')
810     1.23456789123456789
811 
812     The desired number of digits can also be specified:
813 
814     >>> Float('1e-3', 3)
815     0.00100
816     >>> Float(100, 4)
817     100.0
818 
819     Float can automatically count significant figures if a null string
820     is sent for the precision; space are also allowed in the string. (Auto-
821     counting is only allowed for strings, ints and longs).
822 
823     >>> Float('123 456 789 . 123 456', '')
824     123456789.123456
825     >>> Float('12e-3', '')
826     0.012
827     >>> Float(3, '')
828     3.
829 
830     If a number is written in scientific notation, only the digits before the
831     exponent are considered significant if a decimal appears, otherwise the
832     "e" signifies only how to move the decimal:
833 
834     >>> Float('60.e2', '')  # 2 digits significant
835     6.0e+3
836     >>> Float('60e2', '')  # 4 digits significant
837     6000.
838     >>> Float('600e-2', '')  # 3 digits significant
839     6.00
840 
841     Notes
842     =====
843 
844     Floats are inexact by their nature unless their value is a binary-exact
845     value.
846 
847     >>> approx, exact = Float(.1, 1), Float(.125, 1)
848 
849     For calculation purposes, evalf needs to be able to change the precision
850     but this will not increase the accuracy of the inexact value. The
851     following is the most accurate 5-digit approximation of a value of 0.1
852     that had only 1 digit of precision:
853 
854     >>> approx.evalf(5)
855     0.099609
856 
857     By contrast, 0.125 is exact in binary (as it is in base 10) and so it
858     can be passed to Float or evalf to obtain an arbitrary precision with
859     matching accuracy:
860 
861     >>> Float(exact, 5)
862     0.12500
863     >>> exact.evalf(20)
864     0.12500000000000000000
865 
866     Trying to make a high-precision Float from a float is not disallowed,
867     but one must keep in mind that the *underlying float* (not the apparent
868     decimal value) is being obtained with high precision. For example, 0.3
869     does not have a finite binary representation. The closest rational is
870     the fraction 5404319552844595/2**54. So if you try to obtain a Float of
871     0.3 to 20 digits of precision you will not see the same thing as 0.3
872     followed by 19 zeros:
873 
874     >>> Float(0.3, 20)
875     0.29999999999999998890
876 
877     If you want a 20-digit value of the decimal 0.3 (not the floating point
878     approximation of 0.3) you should send the 0.3 as a string. The underlying
879     representation is still binary but a higher precision than Python's float
880     is used:
881 
882     >>> Float('0.3', 20)
883     0.30000000000000000000
884 
885     Although you can increase the precision of an existing Float using Float
886     it will not increase the accuracy -- the underlying value is not changed:
887 
888     >>> def show(f): # binary rep of Float
889     ...     from sympy import Mul, Pow
890     ...     s, m, e, b = f._mpf_
891     ...     v = Mul(int(m), Pow(2, int(e), evaluate=False), evaluate=False)
892     ...     print('%s at prec=%s' % (v, f._prec))
893     ...
894     >>> t = Float('0.3', 3)
895     >>> show(t)
896     4915/2**14 at prec=13
897     >>> show(Float(t, 20)) # higher prec, not higher accuracy
898     4915/2**14 at prec=70
899     >>> show(Float(t, 2)) # lower prec
900     307/2**10 at prec=10
901 
902     The same thing happens when evalf is used on a Float:
903 
904     >>> show(t.evalf(20))
905     4915/2**14 at prec=70
906     >>> show(t.evalf(2))
907     307/2**10 at prec=10
908 
909     Finally, Floats can be instantiated with an mpf tuple (n, c, p) to
910     produce the number (-1)**n*c*2**p:
911 
912     >>> n, c, p = 1, 5, 0
913     >>> (-1)**n*c*2**p
914     -5
915     >>> Float((1, 5, 0))
916     -5.00000000000000
917 
918     An actual mpf tuple also contains the number of bits in c as the last
919     element of the tuple:
920 
921     >>> _._mpf_
922     (1, 5, 0, 3)
923 
924     This is not needed for instantiation and is not the same thing as the
925     precision. The mpf tuple and the precision are two separate quantities
926     that Float tracks.
927

1207     def _eval_power(self, expt):
1208         """

1211         (-p)**r -> exp(r*log(-p)) -> exp(r*(log(p) + I*Pi)) ->
1212                   -> p**r*(sin(Pi*r) + cos(Pi*r)*I)

1214         if self == 0:
1215             if expt.is_positive:
1216                 return S.Zero
1217             if expt.is_negative:
1218                 return Float('inf')

1221                 prec = self._prec
1222                 return Float._new(
1223                     mlib.mpf_pow_int(self._mpf_, expt.p, prec, rnd), prec)

1225                     expt.p == 1 and expt.q % 2 and self.is_negative:

1227                     -self)._eval_power(expt)

1235                     (mpfself, _mpf_zero), (expt, _mpf_zero), prec, rnd)

1358 class Rational(Number):
1359     """Represents integers and rational numbers (p/q) of any size.
1360 
1361     Examples
1362     ========
1363 
1364     >>> from sympy import Rational, nsimplify, S, pi
1365     >>> Rational(3)
1366     3
1367     >>> Rational(1, 2)
1368     1/2
1369 
1370     Rational is unprejudiced in accepting input. If a float is passed, the
1371     underlying value of the binary representation will be returned:
1372 
1373     >>> Rational(.5)
1374     1/2
1375     >>> Rational(.2)
1376     3602879701896397/18014398509481984
1377 
1378     If the simpler representation of the float is desired then consider
1379     limiting the denominator to the desired value or convert the float to
1380     a string (which is roughly equivalent to limiting the denominator to
1381     10**12):
1382 
1383     >>> Rational(str(.2))
1384     1/5
1385     >>> Rational(.2).limit_denominator(10**12)
1386     1/5
1387 
1388     An arbitrarily precise Rational is obtained when a string literal is
1389     passed:
1390 
1391     >>> Rational("1.23")
1392     123/100
1393     >>> Rational('1e-2')
1394     1/100
1395     >>> Rational(".1")
1396     1/10
1397     >>> Rational('1e-2/3.2')
1398     1/320
1399 
1400     The conversion of other types of strings can be handled by
1401     the sympify() function, and conversion of floats to expressions
1402     or simple fractions can be handled with nsimplify:
1403 
1404     >>> S('.[3]')  # repeating digits in brackets
1405     1/3
1406     >>> S('3**2/10')  # general expressions
1407     9/10
1408     >>> nsimplify(.3)  # numbers that have a simple form
1409     3/10
1410 
1411     But if the input does not reduce to a literal Rational, an error will
1412     be raised:
1413 
1414     >>> Rational(pi)
1415     Traceback (most recent call last):
1416     ...
1417     TypeError: invalid input: pi
1418 
1419 
1420     Low-level
1421     ---------
1422 
1423     Access numerator and denominator as .p and .q:
1424 
1425     >>> r = Rational(3, 4)
1426     >>> r
1427     3/4
