2164     def _eval_power(self, expt):
2165         """
2166         Tries to do some simplifications on self**expt
2167 
2168         Returns None if no further simplifications can be done
2169 
2170         When exponent is a fraction (so we have for example a square root),
2171         we try to find a simpler representation by factoring the argument
2172         up to factors of 2**15, e.g.
2173 
2174           - sqrt(4) becomes 2
2175           - sqrt(-4) becomes 2*I
2176           - (2**(3+7)*3**(6+7))**Rational(1,7) becomes 6*18**(3/7)
2177 
2178         Further simplification would require a special call to factorint on
2179         the argument which is not done here for sake of speed.
2180 
2181         """
2182         from sympy import perfect_power
2183 
2184         if expt is S.Infinity:
2185             if self.p > S.One:
2186                 return S.Infinity
2187             # cases -1, 0, 1 are done in their respective classes
2188             return S.Infinity + S.ImaginaryUnit*S.Infinity
2189         if expt is S.NegativeInfinity:
2190             return Rational(1, self)**S.Infinity
2191         if not isinstance(expt, Number):
2192             # simplify when expt is even
2193             # (-2)**k --> 2**k
2194             if self.is_negative and expt.is_even:
2195                 return (-self)**expt
2196         if isinstance(expt, Float):
2197             # Rational knows how to exponentiate by a Float
2198             return super(Integer, self)._eval_power(expt)
2199         if not isinstance(expt, Rational):
2200             return
2201         if expt is S.Half and self.is_negative:
2202             # we extract I for this special case since everyone is doing so
2203             return S.ImaginaryUnit*Pow(-self, expt)
2204         if expt.is_negative:
2205             # invert base and change sign on exponent
2206             ne = -expt
2207             if self.is_negative:
2208                 if expt.q != 1:
2209                     return -(S.NegativeOne)**((expt.p % expt.q) /
2210                             S(expt.q))*Rational(1, -self)**ne
2211                 else:
2212                     return (S.NegativeOne)**ne*Rational(1, -self)**ne
2213             else:
2214                 return Rational(1, self.p)**ne
2215         # see if base is a perfect root, sqrt(4) --> 2
2216         x, xexact = integer_nthroot(abs(self.p), expt.q)
2217         if xexact:
2218             # if it's a perfect root we've finished
2219             result = Integer(x**abs(expt.p))
2220             if self.is_negative:
2221                 result *= S.NegativeOne**expt
2222             return result
2223 
2224         # The following is an algorithm where we collect perfect roots
2225         # from the factors of base.
2226 
2227         # if it's not an nth root, it still might be a perfect power
2228         b_pos = int(abs(self.p))
2229         p = perfect_power(b_pos)
2230         if p is not False:
2231             dict = {p[0]: p[1]}
2232         else:
2233             dict = Integer(self).factors(limit=2**15)
2234 
2235         # now process the dict of factors
2236         if self.is_negative:
2237             dict[-1] = 1
2238         out_int = 1  # integer part
2239         out_rad = 1  # extracted radicals
2240         sqr_int = 1
2241         sqr_gcd = 0
2242         sqr_dict = {}
2243         for prime, exponent in dict.items():
2244             exponent *= expt.p
2245             # remove multiples of expt.q: (2**12)**(1/10) -> 2*(2**2)**(1/10)
2246             div_e, div_m = divmod(exponent, expt.q)
2247             if div_e > 0:
2248                 out_int *= prime**div_e
2249             if div_m > 0:
2250                 # see if the reduced exponent shares a gcd with e.q
2251                 # (2**2)**(1/10) -> 2**(1/5)
2252                 g = igcd(div_m, expt.q)
2253                 if g != 1:
2254                     out_rad *= Pow(prime, Rational(div_m//g, expt.q//g))
2255                 else:
2256                     sqr_dict[prime] = div_m
2257         # identify gcd of remaining powers
2258         for p, ex in sqr_dict.items():
2259             if sqr_gcd == 0:
2260                 sqr_gcd = ex
2261             else:
2262                 sqr_gcd = igcd(sqr_gcd, ex)
2263                 if sqr_gcd == 1:
2264                     break
2265         for k, v in sqr_dict.items():
2266             sqr_int *= k**(v//sqr_gcd)
2267         if sqr_int == self and out_int == 1 and out_rad == 1:
2268             result = None
2269         else:
2270             result = out_int*out_rad*Pow(sqr_int, Rational(sqr_gcd, expt.q))
2271         return result

2307     def __new__(cls, expr, coeffs=None, alias=None, **args):
2308         """Construct a new algebraic number. """
2309         from sympy import Poly
2310         from sympy.polys.polyclasses import ANP, DMP
2311         from sympy.polys.numberfields import minimal_polynomial
2312         from sympy.core.symbol import Symbol
2313 
2314         expr = sympify(expr)
2315 
2316         if isinstance(expr, (tuple, Tuple)):
2317             minpoly, root = expr
2318 
2319             if not minpoly.is_Poly:
2320                 minpoly = Poly(minpoly)
2321         elif expr.is_AlgebraicNumber:
2322             minpoly, root = expr.minpoly, expr.root
2323         else:
2324             minpoly, root = minimal_polynomial(
2325                 expr, args.get('gen'), polys=True), expr
2326 
2327         dom = minpoly.get_domain()
2328 
2329         if coeffs is not None:
2330             if not isinstance(coeffs, ANP):
2331                 rep = DMP.from_sympy_list(sympify(coeffs), 0, dom)
2332                 scoeffs = Tuple(*coeffs)
2333             else:
2334                 rep = DMP.from_list(coeffs.to_list(), 0, dom)
2335                 scoeffs = Tuple(*coeffs.to_list())
2336 
2337             if rep.degree() >= minpoly.degree():
2338                 rep = rep.rem(minpoly.rep)
2339 
2340         else:
2341             rep = DMP.from_list([1, 0], 0, dom)
2342             scoeffs = Tuple(1, 0)
2343 
2344             if root.is_negative:
2345                 rep = -rep
2346                 scoeffs = Tuple(-1, 0)
2347 
2348         sargs = (root, scoeffs)
2349 
2350         if alias is not None:
2351             if not isinstance(alias, Symbol):
2352                 alias = Symbol(alias)
2353             sargs = sargs + (alias,)
2354 
2355         obj = Expr.__new__(cls, *sargs)
2356 
2357         obj.rep = rep
2358         obj.root = root
2359         obj.alias = alias
2360         obj.minpoly = minpoly
2361

2400         from sympy import Poly
2401         f = self.minpoly
2402 
2403         if f.LC() == 1:
2404             return self
2405 
2406         coeff = f.LC()**(f.degree() - 1)
2407         poly = f.compose(Poly(f.gen/f.LC()))
2408 
2409         minpoly = poly*coeff
2410         root = f.LC()*self.root
2411

2415         from sympy.polys import CRootOf, minpoly

2418             if minpoly(self.root - r).is_Symbol:
2419                 # use the matching root if it's simpler
2420                 if measure(r) < ratio*measure(self.root):
2421                     return AlgebraicNumber(r)
2422         return self

355                 return g.scale(y=-1)
356             reps = [(p, p.translate(y=2*(y - p.y))) for p in g.atoms(Point)]
357         elif l.slope == oo:
358             x = l.args[0].x
359             if not x:  # y-axis
360                 return g.scale(x=-1)
361             reps = [(p, p.translate(x=2*(x - p.x))) for p in g.atoms(Point)]

364                     isinstance(arg, Point) for arg in g.args):
365                 raise NotImplementedError(
366                     'reflect undefined or non-Point args in %s' % g)
367             a = atan(l.slope)

549     The angle is measured in radians. To Point a point about a point other
550     then the origin, translate the Point, do the rotation, and

236     def _dict_list(self, other, num):
237         """Creates a list from self to other using _dcm_dict. """
238         outlist = [[self]]
239         oldlist = [[]]
240         while outlist != oldlist:
241             oldlist = outlist[:]
242             for i, v in enumerate(outlist):
243                 templist = v[-1]._dlist[num].keys()
244                 for i2, v2 in enumerate(templist):
245                     if not v.__contains__(v2):
246                         littletemplist = v + [v2]
247                         if not outlist.__contains__(littletemplist):
248                             outlist.append(littletemplist)
249         for i, v in enumerate(oldlist):
250             if v[-1] != other:
251                 outlist.remove(v)
252         outlist.sort(key=len)
253         if len(outlist) != 0:
254             return outlist[0]
255         raise ValueError('No Connecting Path found between ' + self.name +

258     def _w_diff_dcm(self, otherframe):
259         """Angular velocity from time differentiating the DCM. """
260         from sympy.physics.vector.functions import dynamicsymbols
261         dcm2diff = self.dcm(otherframe)
262         diffed = dcm2diff.diff(dynamicsymbols._t)
263         angvelmat = diffed * dcm2diff.T
264         w1 = trigsimp(expand(angvelmat[7]), recursive=True)
265         w2 = trigsimp(expand(angvelmat[2]), recursive=True)
266         w3 = trigsimp(expand(angvelmat[3]), recursive=True)
267         return -Vector([(Matrix([w1, w2, w3]), self)])

382         The format is N.xyz = N.dcm(B) * B.xyz

401         [1,       0,        0],
402         [0, cos(q1), -sin(q1)],
403         [0, sin(q1),  cos(q1)]])

415         #After calculation, store the dcm in dcm cache for faster

421     def orient(self, parent, rot_type, amounts, rot_order=''):
422         """Defines the orientation of this frame relative to a parent frame.
423 
424         Parameters
425         ==========
426 
427         parent : ReferenceFrame
428             The frame that this ReferenceFrame will have its orientation matrix
429             defined in relation to.
430         rot_type : str
431             The type of orientation matrix that is being created. Supported
432             types are 'Body', 'Space', 'Quaternion', 'Axis', and 'DCM'.
433             See examples for correct usage.
434         amounts : list OR value
435             The quantities that the orientation matrix will be defined by.
436             In case of rot_type='DCM', value must be a
437             sympy.matrices.MatrixBase object (or subclasses of it).
438         rot_order : str
439             If applicable, the order of a series of rotations.
440 
441         Examples
442         ========
443 
444         >>> from sympy.physics.vector import ReferenceFrame, Vector
445         >>> from sympy import symbols, eye, ImmutableMatrix
446         >>> q0, q1, q2, q3 = symbols('q0 q1 q2 q3')
447         >>> N = ReferenceFrame('N')
448         >>> B = ReferenceFrame('B')
449 
450         Now we have a choice of how to implement the orientation. First is
451         Body. Body orientation takes this reference frame through three
452         successive simple rotations. Acceptable rotation orders are of length
453         3, expressed in XYZ or 123, and cannot have a rotation about about an
454         axis twice in a row.
455 
456         >>> B.orient(N, 'Body', [q1, q2, q3], '123')
457         >>> B.orient(N, 'Body', [q1, q2, 0], 'ZXZ')
458         >>> B.orient(N, 'Body', [0, 0, 0], 'XYX')
459 
460         Next is Space. Space is like Body, but the rotations are applied in the
461         opposite order.
462 
463         >>> B.orient(N, 'Space', [q1, q2, q3], '312')
464 
465         Next is Quaternion. This orients the new ReferenceFrame with
466         Quaternions, defined as a finite rotation about lambda, a unit vector,
467         by some amount theta.
468         This orientation is described by four parameters:
469         q0 = cos(theta/2)
470         q1 = lambda_x sin(theta/2)
471         q2 = lambda_y sin(theta/2)
472         q3 = lambda_z sin(theta/2)
473         Quaternion does not take in a rotation order.
474 
475         >>> B.orient(N, 'Quaternion', [q0, q1, q2, q3])
476 
477         Next is Axis. This is a rotation about an arbitrary, non-time-varying
478         axis by some angle. The axis is supplied as a Vector. This is how
479         simple rotations are defined.
480 
481         >>> B.orient(N, 'Axis', [q1, N.x + 2 * N.y])
482 
483         Last is DCM (Direction Cosine Matrix). This is a rotation matrix
484         given manually.
485 
486         >>> B.orient(N, 'DCM', eye(3))
487         >>> B.orient(N, 'DCM', ImmutableMatrix([[0, 1, 0], [0, 0, -1], [-1, 0, 0]]))
488 
489         """
490 
491         from sympy.physics.vector.functions import dynamicsymbols
492         _check_frame(parent)
493 
494         # Allow passing a rotation matrix manually.
495         if rot_type == 'DCM':
496             # When rot_type == 'DCM', then amounts must be a Matrix type object
497             # (e.g. sympy.matrices.dense.MutableDenseMatrix).

640         """Creates a new ReferenceFrame oriented with respect to this Frame.
641 
642         See ReferenceFrame.orient() for acceptable rotation types, amounts,
643         and orders. Parent is going to be self.
644 
645         Parameters
646         ==========
647 
648         newname : str
649             The name for the new ReferenceFrame
650         rot_type : str
651             The type of orientation matrix that is being created.
652         amounts : list OR value
653             The quantities that the orientation matrix will be defined by.
654         rot_order : str
655             If applicable, the order of a series of rotations.
656 
657         Examples
658         ========
659 
660         >>> from sympy.physics.vector import ReferenceFrame, Vector
661         >>> from sympy import symbols
662         >>> q0, q1, q2, q3 = symbols('q0 q1 q2 q3')
663         >>> N = ReferenceFrame('N')
664 
665         Now we have a choice of how to implement the orientation. First is
666         Body. Body orientation takes this reference frame through three
667         successive simple rotations. Acceptable rotation orders are of length
668         3, expressed in XYZ or 123, and cannot have a rotation about about an
669         axis twice in a row.
670 
671         >>> A = N.orientnew('A', 'Body', [q1, q2, q3], '123')
672         >>> A = N.orientnew('A', 'Body', [q1, q2, 0], 'ZXZ')
673         >>> A = N.orientnew('A', 'Body', [0, 0, 0], 'XYX')
674 
675         Next is Space. Space is like Body, but the rotations are applied in the
676         opposite order.
677 
678         >>> A = N.orientnew('A', 'Space', [q1, q2, q3], '312')
679 
680         Next is Quaternion. This orients the new ReferenceFrame with
681         Quaternions, defined as a finite rotation about lambda, a unit vector,
682         by some amount theta.
683         This orientation is described by four parameters:
684         q0 = cos(theta/2)
685         q1 = lambda_x sin(theta/2)
686         q2 = lambda_y sin(theta/2)
687         q3 = lambda_z sin(theta/2)
688         Quaternion does not take in a rotation order.
689 
690         >>> A = N.orientnew('A', 'Quaternion', [q0, q1, q2, q3])
691 
692         Last is Axis. This is a rotation about an arbitrary, non-time-varying
693         axis by some angle. The axis is supplied as a Vector. This is how
694         simple rotations are defined.
695 
696         >>> A = N.orientnew('A', 'Axis', [q1, N.x])
697 
698         """
699 
700         newframe = self.__class__(newname, variables, indices, latexs)
701         newframe.orient(self, rot_type, amounts, rot_order)
702         return newframe

493     def diff(self, var, frame, var_in_dcm=True):
494         """Returns the partial derivative of the vector with respect to a
495         variable in the provided reference frame.
496 
497         Parameters
498         ==========
499         var : Symbol
500             What the partial derivative is taken with respect to.
501         frame : ReferenceFrame
502             The reference frame that the partial derivative is taken in.
503         var_in_dcm : boolean
504             If true, the differentiation algorithm assumes that the variable
505             may be present in any of the direction cosine matrices that relate
506             the frame to the frames of any component of the vector. But if it
507             is known that the variable is not present in the direction cosine
508             matrices, false can be set to skip full reexpression in the desired
509             frame.
510 
511         Examples
512         ========
513 
514         >>> from sympy import Symbol
515         >>> from sympy.physics.vector import dynamicsymbols, ReferenceFrame
516         >>> from sympy.physics.vector import Vector
517         >>> Vector.simp = True
518         >>> t = Symbol('t')
519         >>> q1 = dynamicsymbols('q1')
520         >>> N = ReferenceFrame('N')
521         >>> A = N.orientnew('A', 'Axis', [q1, N.y])
522         >>> A.x.diff(t, N)
523         - q1'*A.z
524         >>> B = ReferenceFrame('B')
525         >>> u1, u2 = dynamicsymbols('u1, u2')
526         >>> v = u1 * A.x + u2 * B.y
527         >>> v.diff(u2, N, var_in_dcm=False)
528         B.y
529 
530         """
531 
532         from sympy.physics.vector.frame import _check_frame
533 
534         var = sympify(var)
535         _check_frame(frame)
536 
537         inlist = []
538 
539         for vector_component in self.args:
540             measure_number = vector_component[0]
541             component_frame = vector_component[1]
542             if component_frame == frame:
543                 inlist += [(measure_number.diff(var), frame)]
544             else:
545                 # If the direction cosine matrix relating the component frame
546                 # with the derivative frame does not contain the variable.
547                 if not var_in_dcm or (frame.dcm(component_frame).diff(var) ==
548                                       zeros(3, 3)):
549                     inlist += [(measure_number.diff(var),
550                                         component_frame)]
551                 else:  # else express in the frame
552                     reexp_vec_comp = Vector([vector_component]).express(frame)
553                     deriv = reexp_vec_comp.args[0][0].diff(var)
554                     inlist += Vector([(deriv, frame)]).express(component_frame).args
555 
556         return Vector(inlist)

328         Convert ``elem`` into the internal representation.
329 
330         This method is called implicitly whenever computations involve elements
331         not in the internal representation.
332 
333         >>> from sympy.abc import x
334         >>> from sympy import QQ
335         >>> F = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2)
336         >>> F.convert([1, 0])
337         [1, 0]
338         """
339         if isinstance(elem, FreeModuleElement):
340             if elem.module is self:
341                 return elem
342             if elem.module.rank != self.rank:
343                 raise CoercionFailed
344             return FreeModuleElement(self,
345                      tuple(self.ring.convert(x, elem.module.ring) for x in elem.data))
346         elif iterable(elem):
347             tpl = tuple(self.ring.convert(x) for x in elem)
348             if len(tpl) != self.rank:
349                 raise CoercionFailed
350             return FreeModuleElement(self, tpl)
351         elif elem is 0:
352             return FreeModuleElement(self, (self.ring.convert(0),)*self.rank)
353         else:
354             raise CoercionFailed
355 
356     def is_zero(self):
357         """
358         Returns True if ``self`` is a zero module.
359 
360         (If, as this implementation assumes, the coefficient ring is not the
361         zero ring, then this is equivalent to the rank being zero.)
362 
363         >>> from sympy.abc import x
364         >>> from sympy import QQ
365         >>> QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(0).is_zero()
366         True
367         >>> QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(1).is_zero()
368         False
369         """
370         return self.rank == 0
371 
372     def basis(self):
373         """
374         Return a set of basis elements.
375 
376         >>> from sympy.abc import x
377         >>> from sympy import QQ
378         >>> QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(3).basis()
379         ([1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1])
380         """
381         from sympy.matrices import eye
382         M = eye(self.rank)
383         return tuple(self.convert(M.row(i)) for i in range(self.rank))
384 
385     def quotient_module(self, submodule):
386         """
387         Return a quotient module.
388 
389         >>> from sympy.abc import x
390         >>> from sympy import QQ
391         >>> M = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2)
392         >>> M.quotient_module(M.submodule([1, x], [x, 2]))
393         QQ[x]**2/<[1, x], [x, 2]>
394 
395         Or more conicisely, using the overloaded division operator:
396 
397         >>> QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2) / [[1, x], [x, 2]]
398         QQ[x]**2/<[1, x], [x, 2]>
399         """
400         return QuotientModule(self.ring, self, submodule)
401 
402     def multiply_ideal(self, other):
403         """
404         Multiply ``self`` by the ideal ``other``.
405 
406         >>> from sympy.abc import x
407         >>> from sympy import QQ
408         >>> I = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).ideal(x)
409         >>> F = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2)
410         >>> F.multiply_ideal(I)
411         <[x, 0], [0, x]>
412         """
413         return self.submodule(*self.basis()).multiply_ideal(other)
414 
415     def identity_hom(self):
416         """
417         Return the identity homomorphism on ``self``.
418 
419         >>> from sympy.abc import x
420         >>> from sympy import QQ
421         >>> QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2).identity_hom()
422         Matrix([
423         [1, 0], : QQ[x]**2 -> QQ[x]**2
424         [0, 1]])
425         """
426         from sympy.polys.agca.homomorphisms import homomorphism
427         return homomorphism(self, self, self.basis())
428

474 class FreeModuleQuotientRing(FreeModule):
475     """
476     Free module over a quotient ring.
477 
478     Do not instantiate this, use the constructor method of the ring instead:
479 
480     >>> from sympy.abc import x
481     >>> from sympy import QQ
482     >>> F = (QQ.old_poly_ring(x)/[x**2 + 1]).free_module(3)
483     >>> F
484     (QQ[x]/<x**2 + 1>)**3
485 
486     Attributes
487 
488     - quot - the quotient module `R^n / IR^n`, where `R/I` is our ring
489     """

491     def __init__(self, ring, rank):
492         from sympy.polys.domains.quotientring import QuotientRing
493         FreeModule.__init__(self, ring, rank)
494         if not isinstance(ring, QuotientRing):
495             raise NotImplementedError('This implementation only works over '
496                              + 'quotient rings, got %s' % ring)
497         F = self.ring.ring.free_module(self.rank)
498         self.quot = F / (self.ring.base_ideal*F)
499 
500     def __repr__(self):
501         return "(" + repr(self.ring) + ")" + "**" + repr(self.rank)
502 
503     def submodule(self, *gens, **opts):
504         """
505         Generate a submodule.
506 
507         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
508         >>> from sympy import QQ
509         >>> M = (QQ.old_poly_ring(x, y)/[x**2 - y**2]).free_module(2).submodule([x, x + y])
510         >>> M
511         <[x + <x**2 - y**2>, x + y + <x**2 - y**2>]>
512         >>> M.contains([y**2, x**2 + x*y])
513         True
514         >>> M.contains([x, y])
515         False
516         """
517         return SubModuleQuotientRing(gens, self, **opts)
518 
519     def lift(self, elem):
520         """
521         Lift the element ``elem`` of self to the module self.quot.
522 
523         Note that self.quot is the same set as self, just as an R-module
524         and not as an R/I-module, so this makes sense.
525 
526         >>> from sympy.abc import x
527         >>> from sympy import QQ
528         >>> F = (QQ.old_poly_ring(x)/[x**2 + 1]).free_module(2)
529         >>> e = F.convert([1, 0])
530         >>> e
531         [1 + <x**2 + 1>, 0 + <x**2 + 1>]
532         >>> L = F.quot
533         >>> l = F.lift(e)
534         >>> l
535         [1, 0] + <[x**2 + 1, 0], [0, x**2 + 1]>
536         >>> L.contains(l)
537         True
538         """
539         return self.quot.convert([x.data for x in elem])
540 
541     def unlift(self, elem):
542         """
543         Push down an element of self.quot to self.
544 
545         This undoes ``lift``.
546 
547         >>> from sympy.abc import x
548         >>> from sympy import QQ
549         >>> F = (QQ.old_poly_ring(x)/[x**2 + 1]).free_module(2)
550         >>> e = F.convert([1, 0])
551         >>> l = F.lift(e)
552         >>> e == l
553         False
554         >>> e == F.unlift(l)
555         True
556         """
557         return self.convert(elem.data)

564 class SubModule(Module):
565     """
566     Base class for submodules.
567 
568     Attributes:
569 
570     - container - containing module
571     - gens - generators (subset of containing module)
572     - rank - rank of containing module
573 
574     Non-implemented methods:
575 
576     - _contains
577     - _syzygies
578     - _in_terms_of_generators
579     - _intersect
580     - _module_quotient
581 
582     Methods that likely need change in subclasses:
583 
584     - reduce_element
585     """
586 
587     def __init__(self, gens, container):
588         Module.__init__(self, container.ring)
589         self.gens = tuple(container.convert(x) for x in gens)
590         self.container = container
591         self.rank = container.rank
592         self.ring = container.ring
593         self.dtype = container.dtype
594 
595     def __repr__(self):
596         return "<" + ", ".join(repr(x) for x in self.gens) + ">"
597 
598     def _contains(self, other):
599         """Implementation of containment.
600            Other is guaranteed to be FreeModuleElement."""
601         raise NotImplementedError
602 
603     def _syzygies(self):
604         """Implementation of syzygy computation wrt self generators."""
605         raise NotImplementedError
606 
607     def _in_terms_of_generators(self, e):
608         """Implementation of expression in terms of generators."""
609         raise NotImplementedError
610 
611     def convert(self, elem, M=None):
612         """
613         Convert ``elem`` into the internal represantition.
614 
615         Mostly called implicitly.
616 
617         >>> from sympy.abc import x
618         >>> from sympy import QQ
619         >>> M = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2).submodule([1, x])
620         >>> M.convert([2, 2*x])
621         [2, 2*x]
622         """
623         if isinstance(elem, self.container.dtype) and elem.module is self:
624             return elem
625         r = copy(self.container.convert(elem, M))
626         r.module = self
627         if not self._contains(r):
628             raise CoercionFailed
629         return r
630 
631     def _intersect(self, other):
632         """Implementation of intersection.
633            Other is guaranteed to be a submodule of same free module."""
634         raise NotImplementedError
635 
636     def _module_quotient(self, other):
637         """Implementation of quotient.
638            Other is guaranteed to be a submodule of same free module."""
639         raise NotImplementedError
640 
641     def intersect(self, other, **options):
642         """
643         Returns the intersection of ``self`` with submodule ``other``.
644 
645         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
646         >>> from sympy import QQ
647         >>> F = QQ.old_poly_ring(x, y).free_module(2)
648         >>> F.submodule([x, x]).intersect(F.submodule([y, y]))
649         <[x*y, x*y]>
650 
651         Some implementation allow further options to be passed. Currently, to
652         only one implemented is ``relations=True``, in which case the function
653         will return a triple ``(res, rela, relb)``, where ``res`` is the
654         intersection module, and ``rela`` and ``relb`` are lists of coefficient
655         vectors, expressing the generators of ``res`` in terms of the
656         generators of ``self`` (``rela``) and ``other`` (``relb``).
657 
658         >>> F.submodule([x, x]).intersect(F.submodule([y, y]), relations=True)
659         (<[x*y, x*y]>, [(y,)], [(x,)])
660 
661         The above result says: the intersection module is generated by the
662         single element `(-xy, -xy) = -y (x, x) = -x (y, y)`, where
663         `(x, x)` and `(y, y)` respectively are the unique generators of
664         the two modules being intersected.
665         """
666         if not isinstance(other, SubModule):
667             raise TypeError('%s is not a SubModule' % other)
668         if other.container != self.container:
669             raise ValueError(
670                 '%s is contained in a different free module' % other)
671         return self._intersect(other, **options)
672 
673     def module_quotient(self, other, **options):
674         r"""
675         Returns the module quotient of ``self`` by submodule ``other``.
676 
677         That is, if ``self`` is the module `M` and ``other`` is `N`, then
678         return the ideal `\{f \in R | fN \subset M\}`.
679 
680         >>> from sympy import QQ
681         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
682         >>> F = QQ.old_poly_ring(x, y).free_module(2)
683         >>> S = F.submodule([x*y, x*y])
684         >>> T = F.submodule([x, x])
685         >>> S.module_quotient(T)
686         <y>
687 
688         Some implementations allow further options to be passed. Currently, the
689         only one implemented is ``relations=True``, which may only be passed
690         if ``other`` is prinicipal. In this case the function
691         will return a pair ``(res, rel)`` where ``res`` is the ideal, and
692         ``rel`` is a list of coefficient vectors, expressing the generators of
693         the ideal, multiplied by the generator of ``other`` in terms of
694         generators of ``self``.
695 
696         >>> S.module_quotient(T, relations=True)
697         (<y>, [[1]])
698 
699         This means that the quotient ideal is generated by the single element
700         `y`, and that `y (x, x) = 1 (xy, xy)`, `(x, x)` and `(xy, xy)` being
701         the generators of `T` and `S`, respectively.
702         """
703         if not isinstance(other, SubModule):
704             raise TypeError('%s is not a SubModule' % other)
705         if other.container != self.container:
706             raise ValueError(
707                 '%s is contained in a different free module' % other)
708         return self._module_quotient(other, **options)
709 
710     def union(self, other):
711         """
712         Returns the module generated by the union of ``self`` and ``other``.
713 
714         >>> from sympy.abc import x
715         >>> from sympy import QQ
716         >>> F = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(1)
717         >>> M = F.submodule([x**2 + x]) # <x(x+1)>
718         >>> N = F.submodule([x**2 - 1]) # <(x-1)(x+1)>
719         >>> M.union(N) == F.submodule([x+1])
720         True
721         """
722         if not isinstance(other, SubModule):
723             raise TypeError('%s is not a SubModule' % other)
724         if other.container != self.container:
725             raise ValueError(
726                 '%s is contained in a different free module' % other)
727         return self.__class__(self.gens + other.gens, self.container)
728 
729     def is_zero(self):
730         """
731         Return True if ``self`` is a zero module.
732 
733         >>> from sympy.abc import x
734         >>> from sympy import QQ
735         >>> F = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2)
736         >>> F.submodule([x, 1]).is_zero()
737         False
738         >>> F.submodule([0, 0]).is_zero()
739         True
740         """
741         return all(x == 0 for x in self.gens)
742 
743     def submodule(self, *gens):
744         """
745         Generate a submodule.
746 
747         >>> from sympy.abc import x
748         >>> from sympy import QQ
749         >>> M = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2).submodule([x, 1])
750         >>> M.submodule([x**2, x])
751         <[x**2, x]>
752         """
753         if not self.subset(gens):
754             raise ValueError('%s not a subset of %s' % (gens, self))
755         return self.__class__(gens, self.container)
756 
757     def is_full_module(self):
758         """
759         Return True if ``self`` is the entire free module.
760 
761         >>> from sympy.abc import x
762         >>> from sympy import QQ
763         >>> F = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2)
764         >>> F.submodule([x, 1]).is_full_module()
765         False
766         >>> F.submodule([1, 1], [1, 2]).is_full_module()
767         True
768         """
769         return all(self.contains(x) for x in self.container.basis())
770 
771     def is_submodule(self, other):
772         """
773         Returns True if ``other`` is a submodule of ``self``.
774 
775         >>> from sympy.abc import x
776         >>> from sympy import QQ
777         >>> F = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2)
778         >>> M = F.submodule([2, x])
779         >>> N = M.submodule([2*x, x**2])
780         >>> M.is_submodule(M)
781         True
782         >>> M.is_submodule(N)
783         True
784         >>> N.is_submodule(M)
785         False
786         """
787         if isinstance(other, SubModule):
788             return self.container == other.container and \
789                 all(self.contains(x) for x in other.gens)
790         if isinstance(other, (FreeModule, QuotientModule)):
791             return self.container == other and self.is_full_module()
792         return False
793 
794     def syzygy_module(self, **opts):
795         r"""
796         Compute the syzygy module of the generators of ``self``.
797 
798         Suppose `M` is generated by `f_1, \ldots, f_n` over the ring
799         `R`. Consider the homomorphism `\phi: R^n \to M`, given by
800         sending `(r_1, \ldots, r_n) \to r_1 f_1 + \cdots + r_n f_n`.
801         The syzygy module is defined to be the kernel of `\phi`.
802 
803         The syzygy module is zero iff the generators generate freely a free
804         submodule:
805 
806         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
807         >>> from sympy import QQ
808         >>> QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2).submodule([1, 0], [1, 1]).syzygy_module().is_zero()
809         True
810 
811         A slightly more interesting example:
812 
813         >>> M = QQ.old_poly_ring(x, y).free_module(2).submodule([x, 2*x], [y, 2*y])
814         >>> S = QQ.old_poly_ring(x, y).free_module(2).submodule([y, -x])
815         >>> M.syzygy_module() == S
816         True
817         """
818         F = self.ring.free_module(len(self.gens))
819         # NOTE we filter out zero syzygies. This is for convenience of the
820         # _syzygies function and not meant to replace any real "generating set
821         # reduction" algorithm
822         return F.submodule(*[x for x in self._syzygies() if F.convert(x) != 0],
823                            **opts)
824 
825     def in_terms_of_generators(self, e):
826         """
827         Express element ``e`` of ``self`` in terms of the generators.
828 
829         >>> from sympy.abc import x
830         >>> from sympy import QQ
831         >>> F = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2)
832         >>> M = F.submodule([1, 0], [1, 1])
833         >>> M.in_terms_of_generators([x, x**2])
834         [-x**2 + x, x**2]
835         """
836         try:
837             e = self.convert(e)
838         except CoercionFailed:
839             raise ValueError('%s is not an element of %s' % (e, self))
840         return self._in_terms_of_generators(e)
841 
842     def reduce_element(self, x):
843         """
844         Reduce the element ``x`` of our ring modulo the ideal ``self``.
845 
846         Here "reduce" has no specific meaning, it could return a unique normal
847         form, simplify the expression a bit, or just do nothing.
848         """
849         return x
850 
851     def quotient_module(self, other, **opts):
852         """
853         Return a quotient module.
854 
855         This is the same as taking a submodule of a quotient of the containing
856         module.
857 
858         >>> from sympy.abc import x
859         >>> from sympy import QQ
860         >>> F = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2)
861         >>> S1 = F.submodule([x, 1])
862         >>> S2 = F.submodule([x**2, x])
863         >>> S1.quotient_module(S2)
864         <[x, 1] + <[x**2, x]>>
865 
866         Or more coincisely, using the overloaded division operator:
867 
868         >>> F.submodule([x, 1]) / [(x**2, x)]
869         <[x, 1] + <[x**2, x]>>
870         """
871         if not self.is_submodule(other):
872             raise ValueError('%s not a submodule of %s' % (other, self))
873         return SubQuotientModule(self.gens,
874                 self.container.quotient_module(other), **opts)
875 
876     def __add__(self, oth):
877         return self.container.quotient_module(self).convert(oth)
878 
879     __radd__ = __add__
880 
881     def multiply_ideal(self, I):
882         """
883         Multiply ``self`` by the ideal ``I``.
884 
885         >>> from sympy.abc import x
886         >>> from sympy import QQ
887         >>> I = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).ideal(x**2)
888         >>> M = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2).submodule([1, 1])
889         >>> I*M
890         <[x**2, x**2]>
891         """
892         return self.submodule(*[x*g for [x] in I._module.gens for g in self.gens])
893 
894     def inclusion_hom(self):
895         """
896         Return a homomorphism representing the inclusion map of ``self``.
897 
898         That is, the natural map from ``self`` to ``self.container``.
899 
900         >>> from sympy.abc import x
901         >>> from sympy import QQ
902         >>> QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2).submodule([x, x]).inclusion_hom()
903         Matrix([
904         [1, 0], : <[x, x]> -> QQ[x]**2
905         [0, 1]])
906         """
907         return self.container.identity_hom().restrict_domain(self)
908 
909     def identity_hom(self):
910         """
911         Return the identity homomorphism on ``self``.
912 
913         >>> from sympy.abc import x
914         >>> from sympy import QQ
915         >>> QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2).submodule([x, x]).identity_hom()
916         Matrix([
917         [1, 0], : <[x, x]> -> <[x, x]>
918         [0, 1]])
919         """
920         return self.container.identity_hom().restrict_domain(
921             self).restrict_codomain(self)

924 class SubQuotientModule(SubModule):
925     """
926     Submodule of a quotient module.
927 
928     Equivalently, quotient module of a submodule.
929 
930     Do not instantiate this, instead use the submodule or quotient_module
931     constructing methods:
932 
933     >>> from sympy.abc import x
934     >>> from sympy import QQ
935     >>> F = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2)
936     >>> S = F.submodule([1, 0], [1, x])
937     >>> Q = F/[(1, 0)]
938     >>> S/[(1, 0)] == Q.submodule([5, x])
939     True
940 
941     Attributes:
942 
943     - base - base module we are quotient of
944     - killed_module - submodule used to form the quotient
945     """
946     def __init__(self, gens, container, **opts):
947         SubModule.__init__(self, gens, container)
948         self.killed_module = self.container.killed_module
949         # XXX it is important for some code below that the generators of base
950         #     are in this particular order!
951         self.base = self.container.base.submodule(
952             *[x.data for x in self.gens], **opts).union(self.killed_module)
953 
954     def _contains(self, elem):
955         return self.base.contains(elem.data)
956 
957     def _syzygies(self):
958         # let N = self.killed_module be generated by e_1, ..., e_r
959         # let F = self.base be generated by f_1, ..., f_s and e_1, ..., e_r
960         # Then self = F/N.
961         # Let phi: R**s --> self be the evident surjection.
962         # Similarly psi: R**(s + r) --> F.
963         # We need to find generators for ker(phi). Let chi: R**s --> F be the
964         # evident lift of phi. For X in R**s, phi(X) = 0 iff chi(X) is
965         # contained in N, iff there exists Y in R**r such that
966         # psi(X, Y) = 0.
967         # Hence if alpha: R**(s + r) --> R**s is the projection map, then
968         # ker(phi) = alpha ker(psi).
969         return [X[:len(self.gens)] for X in self.base._syzygies()]

1086     def _syzygies(self):
1087         """Compute syzygies. See [SCA, algorithm 2.5.4]."""
1088         # NOTE if self.gens is a standard basis, this can be done more
1089         #      efficiently using Schreyer's theorem
1090         from sympy.matrices import eye
1091 
1092         # First bullet point
1093         k = len(self.gens)
1094         r = self.rank
1095         im = eye(k)
1096         Rkr = self.ring.free_module(r + k)
1097         newgens = []
1098         for j, f in enumerate(self.gens):
1099             m = [0]*(r + k)
1100             for i, v in enumerate(f):
1101                 m[i] = f[i]
1102             for i in range(k):
1103                 m[r + i] = im[j, i]
1104             newgens.append(Rkr.convert(m))
1105         # Note: we need *descending* order on module index, and TOP=False to
1106         #       get an eliminetaion order
1107         F = Rkr.submodule(*newgens, order='ilex', TOP=False)
1108 
1109         # Second bullet point: standard basis of F
1110         G = F._groebner_vec()
1111 
1112         # Third bullet point: G0 = G intersect the new k components
1113         G0 = [x[r:] for x in G if all(y == self.ring.convert(0)
1114                                       for y in x[:r])]
1115 
1116         # Fourth and fifth bullet points: we are done
1117         return G0

1119     def _in_terms_of_generators(self, e):
1120         """Expression in terms of generators. See [SCA, 2.8.1]."""
1121         # NOTE: if gens is a standard basis, this can be done more efficiently
1122         M = self.ring.free_module(self.rank).submodule(*((e,) + self.gens))
1123         S = M.syzygy_module(
1124             order="ilex", TOP=False)  # We want decreasing order!
1125         G = S._groebner_vec()
1126         # This list cannot not be empty since e is an element
1127         e = [x for x in G if self.ring.is_unit(x[0])][0]
1128         return [-x/e[0] for x in e[1:]]

1136         """
1137         from sympy.polys.distributedmodules import sdm_nf_mora
1138         if NF is None:
1139             NF = sdm_nf_mora

1141             self.ring._vector_to_sdm(x, self.order), self._groebner(),

1143             self.rank))

1145     def _intersect(self, other, relations=False):
1146         # See: [SCA, section 2.8.2]
1147         fi = self.gens
1148         hi = other.gens
1149         r = self.rank
1150         ci = [[0]*(2*r) for _ in range(r)]
1151         for k in range(r):
1152             ci[k][k] = 1
1153             ci[k][r + k] = 1
1154         di = [list(f) + [0]*r for f in fi]
1155         ei = [[0]*r + list(h) for h in hi]
1156         syz = self.ring.free_module(2*r).submodule(*(ci + di + ei))._syzygies()
1157         nonzero = [x for x in syz if any(y != self.ring.zero for y in x[:r])]
1158         res = self.container.submodule(*([-y for y in x[:r]] for x in nonzero))
1159         reln1 = [x[r:r + len(fi)] for x in nonzero]
1160         reln2 = [x[r + len(fi):] for x in nonzero]
1161         if relations:
1162             return res, reln1, reln2
1163         return res

1165     def _module_quotient(self, other, relations=False):
1166         # See: [SCA, section 2.8.4]
1167         if relations and len(other.gens) != 1:
1168             raise NotImplementedError
1169         if len(other.gens) == 0:
1170             return self.ring.ideal(1)
1171         elif len(other.gens) == 1:
1172             # We do some trickery. Let f be the (vector!) generating ``other``
1173             # and f1, .., fn be the (vectors) generating self.
1174             # Consider the submodule of R^{r+1} generated by (f, 1) and
1175             # {(fi, 0) | i}. Then the intersection with the last module
1176             # component yields the quotient.
1177             g1 = list(other.gens[0]) + [1]
1178             gi = [list(x) + [0] for x in self.gens]
1179             # NOTE: We *need* to use an elimination order
1180             M = self.ring.free_module(self.rank + 1).submodule(*([g1] + gi),
1181                                             order='ilex', TOP=False)
1182             if not relations:
1183                 return self.ring.ideal(*[x[-1] for x in M._groebner_vec() if
1184                                          all(y == self.ring.zero for y in x[:-1])])
1185             else:
1186                 G, R = M._groebner_vec(extended=True)
1187                 indices = [i for i, x in enumerate(G) if
1188                            all(y == self.ring.zero for y in x[:-1])]
1189                 return (self.ring.ideal(*[G[i][-1] for i in indices]),
1190                         [[-x for x in R[i][1:]] for i in indices])
1191         # For more generators, we use I : <h1, .., hn> = intersection of
1192         #                                    {I : <hi> | i}
1193         # TODO this can be done more efficiently
1194         return reduce(lambda x, y: x.intersect(y),
1195             (self._module_quotient(self.container.submodule(x)) for x in other.gens))

1251 class QuotientModule(Module):
1252     """
1253     Class for quotient modules.
1254 
1255     Do not instantiate this directly. For subquotients, see the
1256     SubQuotientModule class.
1257 
1258     Attributes:
1259 
1260     - base - the base module we are a quotient of
1261     - killed_module - the submodule used to form the quotient
1262     - rank of the base
1263     """
1264 
1265     dtype = QuotientModuleElement
1266 
1267     def __init__(self, ring, base, submodule):
1268         Module.__init__(self, ring)
1269         if not base.is_submodule(submodule):
1270             raise ValueError('%s is not a submodule of %s' % (submodule, base))
1271         self.base = base
1272         self.killed_module = submodule
1273         self.rank = base.rank
1274 
1275     def __repr__(self):
1276         return repr(self.base) + "/" + repr(self.killed_module)
1277 
1278     def is_zero(self):
1279         """
1280         Return True if ``self`` is a zero module.
1281 
1282         This happens if and only if the base module is the same as the
1283         submodule being killed.
1284 
1285         >>> from sympy.abc import x
1286         >>> from sympy import QQ
1287         >>> F = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2)
1288         >>> (F/[(1, 0)]).is_zero()
1289         False
1290         >>> (F/[(1, 0), (0, 1)]).is_zero()
1291         True
1292         """
1293         return self.base == self.killed_module
1294 
1295     def is_submodule(self, other):
1296         """
1297         Return True if ``other`` is a submodule of ``self``.
1298 
1299         >>> from sympy.abc import x
1300         >>> from sympy import QQ
1301         >>> Q = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2) / [(x, x)]
1302         >>> S = Q.submodule([1, 0])
1303         >>> Q.is_submodule(S)
1304         True
1305         >>> S.is_submodule(Q)
1306         False
1307         """
1308         if isinstance(other, QuotientModule):
1309             return self.killed_module == other.killed_module and \
1310                 self.base.is_submodule(other.base)
1311         if isinstance(other, SubQuotientModule):
1312             return other.container == self
1313         return False
1314 
1315     def submodule(self, *gens, **opts):
1316         """
1317         Generate a submodule.
1318 
1319         This is the same as taking a quotient of a submodule of the base
1320         module.
1321 
1322         >>> from sympy.abc import x
1323         >>> from sympy import QQ
1324         >>> Q = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2) / [(x, x)]
1325         >>> Q.submodule([x, 0])
1326         <[x, 0] + <[x, x]>>
1327         """
1328         return SubQuotientModule(gens, self, **opts)
1329 
1330     def convert(self, elem, M=None):
1331         """
1332         Convert ``elem`` into the internal representation.
1333 
1334         This method is called implicitly whenever computations involve elements
1335         not in the internal representation.
1336 
1337         >>> from sympy.abc import x
1338         >>> from sympy import QQ
1339         >>> F = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2) / [(1, 2), (1, x)]
1340         >>> F.convert([1, 0])
1341         [1, 0] + <[1, 2], [1, x]>
1342         """
1343         if isinstance(elem, QuotientModuleElement):
1344             if elem.module is self:
1345                 return elem
1346             if self.killed_module.is_submodule(elem.module.killed_module):
1347                 return QuotientModuleElement(self, self.base.convert(elem.data))
1348             raise CoercionFailed
1349         return QuotientModuleElement(self, self.base.convert(elem))
1350 
1351     def identity_hom(self):
1352         """
1353         Return the identity homomorphism on ``self``.
1354 
1355         >>> from sympy.abc import x
1356         >>> from sympy import QQ
1357         >>> M = QQ.old_poly_ring(x).free_module(2) / [(1, 2), (1, x)]
1358         >>> M.identity_hom()
1359         Matrix([
1360         [1, 0], : QQ[x]**2/<[1, 2], [1, x]> -> QQ[x]**2/<[1, 2], [1, x]>
1361         [0, 1]])
1362         """
1363         return self.base.identity_hom().quotient_codomain(
1364             self.killed_module).quotient_domain(self.killed_module)

1367         """
1368         Return the quotient homomorphism to ``self``.

1377         Matrix([
1378         [1, 0], : QQ[x]**2 -> QQ[x]**2/<[1, 2], [1, x]>
1379         [0, 1]])

244     def unify(K0, K1, symbols=None):
245         """
246         Construct a minimal domain that contains elements of ``K0`` and ``K1``.
247 
248         Known domains (from smallest to largest):
249 
250         - ``GF(p)``
251         - ``ZZ``
252         - ``QQ``
253         - ``RR(prec, tol)``
254         - ``CC(prec, tol)``
255         - ``ALG(a, b, c)``
256         - ``K[x, y, z]``
257         - ``K(x, y, z)``
258         - ``EX``
259 
260         """
261         if symbols is not None:
262             return K0.unify_with_symbols(K1, symbols)
263 
264         if K0 == K1:
265             return K0
266 
267         if K0.is_EX:
268             return K0
269         if K1.is_EX:
270             return K1
271 
272         if K0.is_Composite or K1.is_Composite:
273             K0_ground = K0.dom if K0.is_Composite else K0
274             K1_ground = K1.dom if K1.is_Composite else K1
275 
276             K0_symbols = K0.symbols if K0.is_Composite else ()
277             K1_symbols = K1.symbols if K1.is_Composite else ()
278 
279             domain = K0_ground.unify(K1_ground)
280             symbols = _unify_gens(K0_symbols, K1_symbols)
281             order = K0.order if K0.is_Composite else K1.order
282 
283             if ((K0.is_FractionField and K1.is_PolynomialRing or
284                  K1.is_FractionField and K0.is_PolynomialRing) and
285                  (not K0_ground.is_Field or not K1_ground.is_Field) and domain.is_Field):
286                 domain = domain.get_ring()
287 
288             if K0.is_Composite and (not K1.is_Composite or K0.is_FractionField or K1.is_PolynomialRing):
289                 cls = K0.__class__
290             else:
291                 cls = K1.__class__
292 
293             from sympy.polys.domains.old_polynomialring import GlobalPolynomialRing
294             if cls == GlobalPolynomialRing:
295                 return cls(domain, symbols)
296 
297             return cls(domain, symbols, order)
298 
299         def mkinexact(cls, K0, K1):
300             prec = max(K0.precision, K1.precision)
301             tol = max(K0.tolerance, K1.tolerance)
302             return cls(prec=prec, tol=tol)
303 
304         if K0.is_ComplexField and K1.is_ComplexField:
305             return mkinexact(K0.__class__, K0, K1)
306         if K0.is_ComplexField and K1.is_RealField:
307             return mkinexact(K0.__class__, K0, K1)
308         if K0.is_RealField and K1.is_ComplexField:
309             return mkinexact(K1.__class__, K1, K0)
310         if K0.is_RealField and K1.is_RealField:
311             return mkinexact(K0.__class__, K0, K1)
312         if K0.is_ComplexField or K0.is_RealField:
313             return K0
314         if K1.is_ComplexField or K1.is_RealField:
315             return K1
316 
317         if K0.is_AlgebraicField and K1.is_AlgebraicField:
318             return K0.__class__(K0.dom.unify(K1.dom), *_unify_gens(K0.orig_ext, K1.orig_ext))
319         elif K0.is_AlgebraicField:

14 def itermonomials(variables, degree):
15     r"""
16     Generate a set of monomials of the given total degree or less.
17 
18     Given a set of variables `V` and a total degree `N` generate
19     a set of monomials of degree at most `N`. The total number of
20     monomials is huge and is given by the following formula:
21 
22     .. math::
23 
24         \frac{(\#V + N)!}{\#V! N!}
25 
26     For example if we would like to generate a dense polynomial of
27     a total degree `N = 50` in 5 variables, assuming that exponents
28     and all of coefficients are 32-bit long and stored in an array we
29     would need almost 80 GiB of memory! Fortunately most polynomials,
30     that we will encounter, are sparse.
31 
32     Examples
33     ========
34 
35     Consider monomials in variables `x` and `y`::
36 
37         >>> from sympy.polys.monomials import itermonomials
38         >>> from sympy.polys.orderings import monomial_key
39         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
40 
41         >>> sorted(itermonomials([x, y], 2), key=monomial_key('grlex', [y, x]))
42         [1, x, y, x**2, x*y, y**2]
43 
44         >>> sorted(itermonomials([x, y], 3), key=monomial_key('grlex', [y, x]))
45         [1, x, y, x**2, x*y, y**2, x**3, x**2*y, x*y**2, y**3]
46 
47     """
48     if not variables:
49         return set([S.One])
50     else:
51         x, tail = variables[0], variables[1:]
52 
53         monoms = itermonomials(tail, degree)
54 
55         for i in range(1, degree + 1):
56             monoms |= set([ x**i * m for m in itermonomials(tail, degree - i) ])
57 
58         return monoms
59 
60 def monomial_count(V, N):
61     r"""
62     Computes the number of monomials.
63 
64     The number of monomials is given by the following formula:
65 
66     .. math::
67 
68         \frac{(\#V + N)!}{\#V! N!}
69 
70     where `N` is a total degree and `V` is a set of variables.
71 
72     Examples
73     ========
74 
75     >>> from sympy.polys.monomials import itermonomials, monomial_count
76     >>> from sympy.polys.orderings import monomial_key
77     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
78 
79     >>> monomial_count(2, 2)
80     6
81 
82     >>> M = itermonomials([x, y], 2)
83 
84     >>> sorted(M, key=monomial_key('grlex', [y, x]))
85     [1, x, y, x**2, x*y, y**2]
86     >>> len(M)
87     6
88 
89     """
90     from sympy import factorial
91     return factorial(V + N) / factorial(V) / factorial(N)

1075     @classmethod
1076     def _parse(cls, rep, dom, lev=None):
1077         if type(rep) is tuple:
1078             num, den = rep
1079 
1080             if lev is not None:
1081                 if type(num) is dict:
1082                     num = dmp_from_dict(num, lev, dom)
1083 
1084                 if type(den) is dict:
1085                     den = dmp_from_dict(den, lev, dom)
1086             else:
1087                 num, num_lev = dmp_validate(num)
1088                 den, den_lev = dmp_validate(den)
1089 
1090                 if num_lev == den_lev:
1091                     lev = num_lev
1092                 else:
1093                     raise ValueError('inconsistent number of levels')
1094 
1095             if dmp_zero_p(den, lev):
1096                 raise ZeroDivisionError('fraction denominator')
1097 
1098             if dmp_zero_p(num, lev):
1099                 den = dmp_one(lev, dom)
1100             else:
1101                 if dmp_negative_p(den, lev, dom):
1102                     num = dmp_neg(num, lev, dom)
1103                     den = dmp_neg(den, lev, dom)
1104         else:
1105             num = rep
1106 
1107             if lev is not None:
1108                 if type(num) is dict:
1109                     num = dmp_from_dict(num, lev, dom)
1110                 elif type(num) is not list:
1111                     num = dmp_ground(dom.convert(num), lev)
1112             else:
1113                 num, lev = dmp_validate(num)
1114 
1115             den = dmp_one(lev, dom)
1116 
1117         return num, den, lev

1127     def poly_unify(f, g):
1128         """Unify a multivariate fraction and a polynomial. """
1129         if not isinstance(g, DMP) or f.lev != g.lev:
1130             raise UnificationFailed("can't unify %s with %s" % (f, g))
1131 
1132         if f.dom == g.dom and f.ring == g.ring:
1133             return (f.lev, f.dom, f.per, (f.num, f.den), g.rep)
1134         else:
1135             lev, dom = f.lev, f.dom.unify(g.dom)
1136             ring = f.ring
1137             if g.ring is not None:
1138                 if ring is not None:
1139                     ring = ring.unify(g.ring)
1140                 else:
1141                     ring = g.ring
1142 
1143             F = (dmp_convert(f.num, lev, f.dom, dom),
1144                  dmp_convert(f.den, lev, f.dom, dom))
1145 
1146             G = dmp_convert(g.rep, lev, g.dom, dom)
1147 
1148             def per(num, den, cancel=True, kill=False, lev=lev):
1149                 if kill:
1150                     if not lev:
1151                         return num/den
1152                     else:
1153                         lev = lev - 1
1154 
1155                 if cancel:
1156                     num, den = dmp_cancel(num, den, lev, dom)
1157 
1158                 return f.__class__.new((num, den), dom, lev, ring=ring)
1159 
1160             return lev, dom, per, F, G

249     @property
250     def free_symbols(self):
251         """
252         Free symbols of a polynomial expression.
253 
254         Examples
255         ========
256 
257         >>> from sympy import Poly
258         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
259 
260         >>> Poly(x**2 + 1).free_symbols
261         {x}
262         >>> Poly(x**2 + y).free_symbols
263         {x, y}
264         >>> Poly(x**2 + y, x).free_symbols
265         {x, y}
266         >>> Poly(x**2 + y, x, z).free_symbols
267         {x, y}
268 
269         """
270         symbols = set()
271         gens = self.gens
272         for i in range(len(gens)):
273             for monom in self.monoms():
274                 if monom[i]:
275                     symbols |= gens[i].free_symbols
276                     break
277 
278         return symbols | self.free_symbols_in_domain

280     @property

285         Examples

288         >>> from sympy import Poly
289         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y

291         >>> Poly(x**2 + 1).free_symbols_in_domain

293         >>> Poly(x**2 + y).free_symbols_in_domain
294         set()
295         >>> Poly(x**2 + y, x).free_symbols_in_domain
296         {y}
297 
298         """
299         domain, symbols = self.rep.dom, set()
300 
301         if domain.is_Composite:
302             for gen in domain.symbols:
303                 symbols |= gen.free_symbols
304         elif domain.is_EX:
305             for coeff in self.coeffs():
306                 symbols |= coeff.free_symbols
307 
308         return symbols

364     def unify(f, g):
365         """
366         Make ``f`` and ``g`` belong to the same domain.
367 
368         Examples
369         ========
370 
371         >>> from sympy import Poly
372         >>> from sympy.abc import x
373 
374         >>> f, g = Poly(x/2 + 1), Poly(2*x + 1)
375 
376         >>> f
377         Poly(1/2*x + 1, x, domain='QQ')
378         >>> g
379         Poly(2*x + 1, x, domain='ZZ')
380 
381         >>> F, G = f.unify(g)
382 
383         >>> F
384         Poly(1/2*x + 1, x, domain='QQ')
385         >>> G
386         Poly(2*x + 1, x, domain='QQ')
387 
388         """
389         _, per, F, G = f._unify(g)
390         return per(F), per(G)
391 
392     def _unify(f, g):
393         g = sympify(g)
394 
395         if not g.is_Poly:
396             try:
397                 return f.rep.dom, f.per, f.rep, f.rep.per(f.rep.dom.from_sympy(g))
398             except CoercionFailed:
399                 raise UnificationFailed("can't unify %s with %s" % (f, g))
400 
401         if isinstance(f.rep, DMP) and isinstance(g.rep, DMP):
402             gens = _unify_gens(f.gens, g.gens)
403 
404             dom, lev = f.rep.dom.unify(g.rep.dom, gens), len(gens) - 1
405 
406             if f.gens != gens:
407                 f_monoms, f_coeffs = _dict_reorder(
408                     f.rep.to_dict(), f.gens, gens)
409 
410                 if f.rep.dom != dom:
411                     f_coeffs = [dom.convert(c, f.rep.dom) for c in f_coeffs]
412 
413                 F = DMP(dict(list(zip(f_monoms, f_coeffs))), dom, lev)
414             else:
415                 F = f.rep.convert(dom)
416 
417             if g.gens != gens:
418                 g_monoms, g_coeffs = _dict_reorder(
419                     g.rep.to_dict(), g.gens, gens)
420 
421                 if g.rep.dom != dom:
422                     g_coeffs = [dom.convert(c, g.rep.dom) for c in g_coeffs]
423 
424                 G = DMP(dict(list(zip(g_monoms, g_coeffs))), dom, lev)
425             else:
426                 G = g.rep.convert(dom)
427         else:
428             raise UnificationFailed("can't unify %s with %s" % (f, g))
429 
430         cls = f.__class__
431 
432         def per(rep, dom=dom, gens=gens, remove=None):
433             if remove is not None:
434                 gens = gens[:remove] + gens[remove + 1:]
435 
436                 if not gens:
437                     return dom.to_sympy(rep)
438 
439             return cls.new(rep, *gens)
440 
441         return dom, per, F, G
442 
443     def per(f, rep, gens=None, remove=None):
444         """
445         Create a Poly out of the given representation.
446 
447         Examples
448         ========
449 
450         >>> from sympy import Poly, ZZ
451         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
452 
453         >>> from sympy.polys.polyclasses import DMP
454 
455         >>> a = Poly(x**2 + 1)
456 
457         >>> a.per(DMP([ZZ(1), ZZ(1)], ZZ), gens=[y])
458         Poly(y + 1, y, domain='ZZ')
459 
460         """
461         if gens is None:
462             gens = f.gens
463 
464         if remove is not None:
465             gens = gens[:remove] + gens[remove + 1:]
466 
467             if not gens:
468                 return f.rep.dom.to_sympy(rep)
469 
470         return f.__class__.new(rep, *gens)
471

555     def replace(f, x, y=None):
556         """
557         Replace ``x`` with ``y`` in generators list.
558 
559         Examples
560         ========
561 
562         >>> from sympy import Poly
563         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
564 
565         >>> Poly(x**2 + 1, x).replace(x, y)
566         Poly(y**2 + 1, y, domain='ZZ')
567 
568         """
569         if y is None:
570             if f.is_univariate:
571                 x, y = f.gen, x
572             else:
573                 raise PolynomialError(
574                     "syntax supported only in univariate case")
575 
576         if x == y:
577             return f
578 
579         if x in f.gens and y not in f.gens:
580             dom = f.get_domain()
581 
582             if not dom.is_Composite or y not in dom.symbols:
583                 gens = list(f.gens)
584                 gens[gens.index(x)] = y
585                 return f.per(f.rep, gens=gens)
586 
587         raise PolynomialError("can't replace %s with %s in %s" % (x, y, f))

589     def reorder(f, *gens, **args):

598 
599         >>> Poly(x**2 + x*y**2, x, y).reorder(y, x)
600         Poly(y**2*x + x**2, y, x, domain='ZZ')
601 
602         """
603         opt = options.Options((), args)

605         if not gens:
606             gens = _sort_gens(f.gens, opt=opt)
607         elif set(f.gens) != set(gens):
608             raise PolynomialError(
609                 "generators list can differ only up to order of elements")

611         rep = dict(list(zip(*_dict_reorder(f.rep.to_dict(), f.gens, gens))))

613         return f.per(DMP(rep, f.rep.dom, len(gens) - 1), gens=gens)

615     def ltrim(f, gen):
616         """
617         Remove dummy generators from ``f`` that are to the left of
618         specified ``gen`` in the generators as ordered. When ``gen``
619         is an integer, it refers to the generator located at that
620         position within the tuple of generators of ``f``.
621 
622         Examples
623         ========
624 
625         >>> from sympy import Poly
626         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
627 
628         >>> Poly(y**2 + y*z**2, x, y, z).ltrim(y)
629         Poly(y**2 + y*z**2, y, z, domain='ZZ')
630         >>> Poly(z, x, y, z).ltrim(-1)
631         Poly(z, z, domain='ZZ')
632 
633         """
634         rep = f.as_dict(native=True)
635         j = f._gen_to_level(gen)
636 
637         terms = {}
638 
639         for monom, coeff in rep.items():
640 
641             if any(i for i in monom[:j]):
642                 # some generator is used in the portion to be trimmed
643                 raise PolynomialError("can't left trim %s" % f)
644 
645             terms[monom[j:]] = coeff
646 
647         gens = f.gens[j:]
648 
649         return f.new(DMP.from_dict(terms, len(gens) - 1, f.rep.dom), *gens)

651     def has_only_gens(f, *gens):
652         """
653         Return ``True`` if ``Poly(f, *gens)`` retains ground domain.
654 
655         Examples
656         ========
657 
658         >>> from sympy import Poly
659         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
660 
661         >>> Poly(x*y + 1, x, y, z).has_only_gens(x, y)
662         True
663         >>> Poly(x*y + z, x, y, z).has_only_gens(x, y)
664         False
665 
666         """
667         indices = set()
668 
669         for gen in gens:
670             try:
671                 index = f.gens.index(gen)
672             except ValueError:
673                 raise GeneratorsError(
674                     "%s doesn't have %s as generator" % (f, gen))
675             else:
676                 indices.add(index)
677 
678         for monom in f.monoms():
679             for i, elt in enumerate(monom):
680                 if i not in indices and elt:
681                     return False
682 
683         return True

1097     def eject(f, *gens):

2614     def dispersionset(f, g=None):
2615         r"""Compute the *dispersion set* of two polynomials.
2616 
2617         For two polynomials `f(x)` and `g(x)` with `\deg f > 0`
2618         and `\deg g > 0` the dispersion set `\operatorname{J}(f, g)` is defined as:
2619 
2620         .. math::
2621             \operatorname{J}(f, g)
2622             & := \{a \in \mathbb{N}_0 | \gcd(f(x), g(x+a)) \neq 1\} \\
2623             &  = \{a \in \mathbb{N}_0 | \deg \gcd(f(x), g(x+a)) \geq 1\}
2624 
2625         For a single polynomial one defines `\operatorname{J}(f) := \operatorname{J}(f, f)`.
2626 
2627         Examples
2628         ========
2629 
2630         >>> from sympy import poly
2631         >>> from sympy.polys.dispersion import dispersion, dispersionset
2632         >>> from sympy.abc import x
2633 
2634         Dispersion set and dispersion of a simple polynomial:
2635 
2636         >>> fp = poly((x - 3)*(x + 3), x)
2637         >>> sorted(dispersionset(fp))
2638         [0, 6]
2639         >>> dispersion(fp)
2640         6
2641 
2642         Note that the definition of the dispersion is not symmetric:
2643 
2644         >>> fp = poly(x**4 - 3*x**2 + 1, x)
2645         >>> gp = fp.shift(-3)
2646         >>> sorted(dispersionset(fp, gp))
2647         [2, 3, 4]
2648         >>> dispersion(fp, gp)
2649         4
2650         >>> sorted(dispersionset(gp, fp))
2651         []
2652         >>> dispersion(gp, fp)
2653         -oo
2654 
2655         Computing the dispersion also works over field extensions:
2656 
2657         >>> from sympy import sqrt
2658         >>> fp = poly(x**2 + sqrt(5)*x - 1, x, domain='QQ<sqrt(5)>')
2659         >>> gp = poly(x**2 + (2 + sqrt(5))*x + sqrt(5), x, domain='QQ<sqrt(5)>')
2660         >>> sorted(dispersionset(fp, gp))
2661         [2]
2662         >>> sorted(dispersionset(gp, fp))
2663         [1, 4]
2664 
2665         We can even perform the computations for polynomials
2666         having symbolic coefficients:
2667 
2668         >>> from sympy.abc import a
2669         >>> fp = poly(4*x**4 + (4*a + 8)*x**3 + (a**2 + 6*a + 4)*x**2 + (a**2 + 2*a)*x, x)
2670         >>> sorted(dispersionset(fp))
2671         [0, 1]
2672 
2673         See Also
2674         ========
2675 
2676         dispersion
2677 
2678         References
2679         ==========
2680 
2681         1. [ManWright94]_
2682         2. [Koepf98]_
2683         3. [Abramov71]_
2684         4. [Man93]_
2685         """
2686         from sympy.polys.dispersion import dispersionset
2687         return dispersionset(f, g)
2688 
2689     def dispersion(f, g=None):

2697             & := \max\{ J(f,g) \cup \{0\} \} \\
2698             &  = \max\{ \{a \in \mathbb{N} | \gcd(f(x), g(x+a)) \neq 1\} \cup \{0\} \}

2734         >>> gp = poly(x**2 + (2 + sqrt(5))*x + sqrt(5), x, domain='QQ<sqrt(5)>')

3244     def intervals(f, all=False, eps=None, inf=None, sup=None, fast=False, sqf=False):
3245         """
3246         Compute isolating intervals for roots of ``f``.
3247 
3248         For real roots the Vincent-Akritas-Strzebonski (VAS) continued fractions method is used.
3249 
3250         References:
3251         ===========
3252            1. Alkiviadis G. Akritas and Adam W. Strzebonski: A Comparative Study of Two Real Root
3253            Isolation Methods . Nonlinear Analysis: Modelling and Control, Vol. 10, No. 4, 297-304, 2005.
3254            2. Alkiviadis G. Akritas, Adam W. Strzebonski and Panagiotis S. Vigklas: Improving the
3255            Performance of the Continued Fractions Method Using new Bounds of Positive Roots. Nonlinear
3256            Analysis: Modelling and Control, Vol. 13, No. 3, 265-279, 2008.
3257 
3258         Examples
3259         ========
3260 
3261         >>> from sympy import Poly
3262         >>> from sympy.abc import x
3263 
3264         >>> Poly(x**2 - 3, x).intervals()
3265         [((-2, -1), 1), ((1, 2), 1)]
3266         >>> Poly(x**2 - 3, x).intervals(eps=1e-2)
3267         [((-26/15, -19/11), 1), ((19/11, 26/15), 1)]
3268 
3269         """
3270         if eps is not None:
3271             eps = QQ.convert(eps)
3272 
3273             if eps <= 0:
3274                 raise ValueError("'eps' must be a positive rational")
3275 
3276         if inf is not None:
3277             inf = QQ.convert(inf)
3278         if sup is not None:
3279             sup = QQ.convert(sup)
3280 
3281         if hasattr(f.rep, 'intervals'):
3282             result = f.rep.intervals(
3283                 all=all, eps=eps, inf=inf, sup=sup, fast=fast, sqf=sqf)
3284         else:  # pragma: no cover
3285             raise OperationNotSupported(f, 'intervals')
3286 
3287         if sqf:
3288             def _real(interval):
3289                 s, t = interval
3290                 return (QQ.to_sympy(s), QQ.to_sympy(t))
3291 
3292             if not all:
3293                 return list(map(_real, result))
3294 
3295             def _complex(rectangle):
3296                 (u, v), (s, t) = rectangle
3297                 return (QQ.to_sympy(u) + I*QQ.to_sympy(v),
3298                         QQ.to_sympy(s) + I*QQ.to_sympy(t))
3299 
3300             real_part, complex_part = result
3301 
3302             return list(map(_real, real_part)), list(map(_complex, complex_part))
3303         else:
3304             def _real(interval):
3305                 (s, t), k = interval
3306                 return ((QQ.to_sympy(s), QQ.to_sympy(t)), k)
3307 
3308             if not all:
3309                 return list(map(_real, result))
3310 
3311             def _complex(rectangle):
3312                 ((u, v), (s, t)), k = rectangle
3313                 return ((QQ.to_sympy(u) + I*QQ.to_sympy(v),
3314                          QQ.to_sympy(s) + I*QQ.to_sympy(t)), k)
3315 
3316             real_part, complex_part = result
3317 
3318             return list(map(_real, real_part)), list(map(_complex, complex_part))
3319

3357     def count_roots(f, inf=None, sup=None):
3358         """
3359         Return the number of roots of ``f`` in ``[inf, sup]`` interval.

3361         Examples
3362         ========

3370         1

3381                 re, im = inf.as_real_imag()
3382 
3383                 if not im:
3384                     inf = QQ.convert(inf)

3386                     inf, inf_real = list(map(QQ.convert, (re, im))), False

3388         if sup is not None:

3391             if sup is S.Infinity:
3392                 sup = None
3393             else:
3394                 re, im = sup.as_real_imag()
3395 
3396                 if not im:
3397                     sup = QQ.convert(sup)
3398                 else:
3399                     sup, sup_real = list(map(QQ.convert, (re, im))), False
3400 
3401         if inf_real and sup_real:
3402             if hasattr(f.rep, 'count_real_roots'):

3404             else:  # pragma: no cover

3406         else:
3407             if inf_real and inf is not None:
3408                 inf = (inf, QQ.zero)
3409

3497     def nroots(f, n=15, maxsteps=50, cleanup=True):
3498         """
3499         Compute numerical approximations of roots of ``f``.
3500 
3501         Parameters
3502         ==========
3503 
3504         n ... the number of digits to calculate
3505         maxsteps ... the maximum number of iterations to do
3506 
3507         If the accuracy `n` cannot be reached in `maxsteps`, it will raise an
3508         exception. You need to rerun with higher maxsteps.
3509 
3510         Examples
3511         ========
3512 
3513         >>> from sympy import Poly
3514         >>> from sympy.abc import x
3515 
3516         >>> Poly(x**2 - 3).nroots(n=15)
3517         [-1.73205080756888, 1.73205080756888]
3518         >>> Poly(x**2 - 3).nroots(n=30)
3519         [-1.73205080756887729352744634151, 1.73205080756887729352744634151]
3520 
3521         """
3522         if f.is_multivariate:
3523             raise MultivariatePolynomialError(
3524                 "can't compute numerical roots of %s" % f)
3525 
3526         if f.degree() <= 0:
3527             return []
3528 
3529         # For integer and rational coefficients, convert them to integers only
3530         # (for accuracy). Otherwise just try to convert the coefficients to
3531         # mpmath.mpc and raise an exception if the conversion fails.
3532         if f.rep.dom is ZZ:
3533             coeffs = [int(coeff) for coeff in f.all_coeffs()]
3534         elif f.rep.dom is QQ:
3535             denoms = [coeff.q for coeff in f.all_coeffs()]
3536             from sympy.core.numbers import ilcm
3537             fac = ilcm(*denoms)
3538             coeffs = [int(coeff*fac) for coeff in f.all_coeffs()]
3539         else:
3540             coeffs = [coeff.evalf(n=n).as_real_imag()
3541                     for coeff in f.all_coeffs()]
3542             try:
3543                 coeffs = [mpmath.mpc(*coeff) for coeff in coeffs]
3544             except TypeError:
3545                 raise DomainError("Numerical domain expected, got %s" % \
3546                         f.rep.dom)
3547 
3548         dps = mpmath.mp.dps
3549         mpmath.mp.dps = n
3550 
3551         try:
3552             # We need to add extra precision to guard against losing accuracy.
3553             # 10 times the degree of the polynomial seems to work well.
3554             roots = mpmath.polyroots(coeffs, maxsteps=maxsteps,
3555                     cleanup=cleanup, error=False, extraprec=f.degree()*10)
3556 
3557             # Mpmath puts real roots first, then complex ones (as does all_roots)
3558             # so we make sure this convention holds here, too.
3559             roots = list(map(sympify,
3560                 sorted(roots, key=lambda r: (1 if r.imag else 0, r.real, r.imag))))
3561         except NoConvergence:
3562             raise NoConvergence(
3563                 'convergence to root failed; try n < %s or maxsteps > %s' % (
3564                 n, maxsteps))
3565         finally:
3566             mpmath.mp.dps = dps
3567 
3568         return roots
3569

3637     def cancel(f, g, include=False):
3638         """
3639         Cancel common factors in a rational function ``f/g``.
3640 
3641         Examples
3642         ========
3643 
3644         >>> from sympy import Poly
3645         >>> from sympy.abc import x
3646 
3647         >>> Poly(2*x**2 - 2, x).cancel(Poly(x**2 - 2*x + 1, x))
3648         (1, Poly(2*x + 2, x, domain='ZZ'), Poly(x - 1, x, domain='ZZ'))
3649 
3650         >>> Poly(2*x**2 - 2, x).cancel(Poly(x**2 - 2*x + 1, x), include=True)
3651         (Poly(2*x + 2, x, domain='ZZ'), Poly(x - 1, x, domain='ZZ'))
3652 
3653         """
3654         dom, per, F, G = f._unify(g)
3655 
3656         if hasattr(F, 'cancel'):
3657             result = F.cancel(G, include=include)
3658         else:  # pragma: no cover
3659             raise OperationNotSupported(f, 'cancel')
3660 
3661         if not include:
3662             if dom.has_assoc_Ring:
3663                 dom = dom.get_ring()
3664 
3665             cp, cq, p, q = result
3666 
3667             cp = dom.to_sympy(cp)
3668             cq = dom.to_sympy(cq)
3669 
3670             return cp/cq, per(p), per(q)
3671         else:
3672             return tuple(map(per, result))
