373 class MultisetPartitionTraverser():
374     """
375     Has methods to ``enumerate`` and ``count`` the partitions of a multiset.
376 
377     This implements a refactored and extended version of Knuth's algorithm
378     7.1.2.5M [AOCP]_."
379 
380     The enumeration methods of this class are generators and return
381     data structures which can be interpreted by the same visitor
382     functions used for the output of ``multiset_partitions_taocp``.
383 
384     See Also
385     ========
386     multiset_partitions_taocp
387     sympy.utilities.iterables.multiset_partititions
388 
389     Examples
390     ========
391 
392     >>> from sympy.utilities.enumerative import MultisetPartitionTraverser
393     >>> m = MultisetPartitionTraverser()
394     >>> m.count_partitions([4,4,4,2])
395     127750
396     >>> m.count_partitions([3,3,3])
397     686
398 
399     References
400     ==========
401 
402     .. [AOCP] Algorithm 7.1.2.5M in Volume 4A, Combinatoral Algorithms,
403            Part 1, of The Art of Computer Programming, by Donald Knuth.
404 
405     .. [Factorisatio] On a Problem of Oppenheim concerning
406            "Factorisatio Numerorum" E. R. Canfield, Paul Erdos, Carl
407            Pomerance, JOURNAL OF NUMBER THEORY, Vol. 17, No. 1. August
408            1983.  See section 7 for a description of an algorithm
409            similar to Knuth's.
410 
411     .. [Yorgey] Generating Multiset Partitions, Brent Yorgey, The
412            Monad.Reader, Issue 8, September 2007.
413 
414     """
415 
416     def __init__(self):
417         self.debug = False
418         # TRACING variables.  These are useful for gathering
419         # statistics on the algorithm itself, but have no particular
420         # benefit to a user of the code.
421         self.k1 = 0
422         self.k2 = 0
423         self.p1 = 0
424 
425     def db_trace(self, msg):
426         """Useful for usderstanding/debugging the algorithms.  Not
427         generally activated in end-user code."""
428         if self.debug:
429             letters = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'
430             state = [self.f, self.lpart, self.pstack]
431             print("DBG:", msg,
432                   ["".join(part) for part in list_visitor(state, letters)],
433                   animation_visitor(state))
434 
435     #
436     # Helper methods for enumeration
437     #
438     def _initialize_enumeration(self, multiplicities):
439         """Allocates and initializes the partition stack.
440 
441         This is called from the enumeration/counting routines, so
442         there is no need to call it separately."""
443 
444         num_components = len(multiplicities)
445         # cardinality is the total number of elements, whether or not distinct
446         cardinality = sum(multiplicities)
447 
448         # pstack is the partition stack, which is segmented by
449         # f into parts.
450         self.pstack = [PartComponent() for i in
451                        range(num_components * cardinality + 1)]
452         self.f = [0] * (cardinality + 1)
453 
454         # Initial state - entire multiset in one part.
455         for j in range(num_components):
456             ps = self.pstack[j]
457             ps.c = j
458             ps.u = multiplicities[j]
459             ps.v = multiplicities[j]
460 
461         self.f[0] = 0
462         self.f[1] = num_components
463         self.lpart = 0
464 
465     # The decrement_part() method corresponds to step M5 in Knuth's
466     # algorithm.  This is the base version for enum_all().  Modified
467     # versions of this method are needed if we want to restrict
468     # sizes of the partitions produced.
469     def decrement_part(self, part):
470         """Decrements part (a subrange of pstack), if possible, returning
471         True iff the part was successfully decremented.
472 
473         If you think of the v values in the part as a multi-digit
474         integer (least significant digit on the right) this is
475         basically decrementing that integer, but with the extra
476         constraint that the leftmost digit cannot be decremented to 0.
477 
478         Parameters
479         ==========
480 
481         part
482            The part, represented as a list of PartComponent objects,
483            which is to be decremented.
484 
485         """
486         plen = len(part)
487         for j in range(plen - 1, -1, -1):
488             if (j == 0 and part[j].v > 1) or (j > 0 and part[j].v > 0):
489                 # found val to decrement
490                 part[j].v -= 1
491                 # Reset trailing parts back to maximum
492                 for k in range(j + 1, plen):
493                     part[k].v = part[k].u
494                 return True
495         return False
496 
497     # Version to allow number of parts to be bounded from above.
498     # Corresponds to (a modified) step M5.
499     def decrement_part_small(self, part, ub):
500         """Decrements part (a subrange of pstack), if possible, returning
501         True iff the part was successfully decremented.
502 
503         Parameters
504         ==========
505 
506         part
507             part to be decremented (topmost part on the stack)
508 
509         ub
510             the maximum number of parts allowed in a partition
511             returned by the calling traversal.
512 
513         Notes
514         =====
515 
516         The goal of this modification of the ordinary decrement method
517         is to fail (meaning that the subtree rooted at this part is to
518         be skipped) when it can be proved that this part can only have
519         child partitions which are larger than allowed by ``ub``. If a
520         decision is made to fail, it must be accurate, otherwise the
521         enumeration will miss some partitions.  But, it is OK not to
522         capture all the possible failures -- if a part is passed that
523         shouldn't be, the resulting too-large partitions are filtered
524         by the enumeration one level up.  However, as is usual in
525         constrained enumerations, failing early is advantageous.
526 
527         The tests used by this method catch the most common cases,
528         although this implementation is by no means the last word on
529         this problem.  The tests include:
530 
531         1) ``lpart`` must be less than ``ub`` by at least 2.  This is because
532            once a part has been decremented, the partition
533            will gain at least one child in the spread step.
534 
535         2) If the leading component of the part is about to be
536            decremented, check for how many parts will be added in
537            order to use up the unallocated multiplicity in that
538            leading component, and fail if this number is greater than
539            allowed by ``ub``.  (See code for the exact expression.)  This
540            test is given in the answer to Knuth's problem 7.2.1.5.69.
541 
542         3) If there is *exactly* enough room to expand the leading
543            component by the above test, check the next component (if
544            it exists) once decrementing has finished.  If this has
545            ``v == 0``, this next component will push the expansion over the
546            limit by 1, so fail.
547         """
548         if self.lpart >= ub - 1:
549             self.p1 += 1  # increment to keep track of usefulness of tests
550             return False
551         plen = len(part)
552         for j in range(plen - 1, -1, -1):
553             # Knuth's mod, (answer to problem 7.2.1.5.69)
554             if (j == 0) and (part[0].v - 1)*(ub - self.lpart) < part[0].u:
555                 self.k1 += 1
556                 return False
557 
558             if (j == 0 and part[j].v > 1) or (j > 0 and part[j].v > 0):
559                 # found val to decrement
560                 part[j].v -= 1
561                 # Reset trailing parts back to maximum
562                 for k in range(j + 1, plen):
563                     part[k].v = part[k].u
564 
565                 # Have now decremented part, but are we doomed to
566                 # failure when it is expanded?  Check one oddball case
567                 # that turns out to be surprisingly common - exactly
568                 # enough room to expand the leading component, but no
569                 # room for the second component, which has v=0.
570                 if (plen > 1 and (part[1].v == 0) and
571                     (part[0].u - part[0].v) ==
572                         ((ub - self.lpart - 1) * part[0].v)):
573                     self.k2 += 1
574                     self.db_trace("Decrement fails test 3")
575                     return False
576                 return True
577         return False
578 
579     def decrement_part_large(self, part, amt, lb):
580         """Decrements part, while respecting size constraint.
581 
582         A part can have no children which are of sufficient size (as
583         indicated by ``lb``) unless that part has sufficient
584         unallocated multiplicity.  When enforcing the size constraint,
585         this method will decrement the part (if necessary) by an
586         amount needed to ensure sufficient unallocated multiplicity.
587 
588         Returns True iff the part was successfully decremented.
589 
590         Parameters
591         ==========
592 
593         part
594             part to be decremented (topmost part on the stack)
595 
596         amt
597             Can only take values 0 or 1.  A value of 1 means that the
598             part must be decremented, and then the size constraint is
599             enforced.  A value of 0 means just to enforce the ``lb``
600             size constraint.
601 
602         lb
603             The partitions produced by the calling enumeration must
604             have more parts than this value.
605 
606         """
607 
608         if amt == 1:
609             # In this case we always need to increment, *before*
610             # enforcing the "sufficient unallocated multiplicity"
611             # constraint.  Easiest for this is just to call the
612             # regular decrement method.
613             if not self.decrement_part(part):
614                 return False
615 
616         # Next, perform any needed additional decrementing to respect
617         # "sufficient unallocated multiplicity" (or fail if this is
618         # not possible).
619         min_unalloc = lb - self.lpart
620         if min_unalloc <= 0:
621             return True
622         total_mult = sum(pc.u for pc in part)
623         total_alloc = sum(pc.v for pc in part)
624         if total_mult <= min_unalloc:
625             return False
626 
627         deficit = min_unalloc - (total_mult - total_alloc)
628         if deficit <= 0:
629             return True
630 
631         for i in range(len(part) - 1, -1, -1):
632             if i == 0:
633                 if part[0].v > deficit:
634                     part[0].v -= deficit
635                     return True
636                 else:
637                     return False  # This shouldn't happen, due to above check
638             else:
639                 if part[i].v >= deficit:
640                     part[i].v -= deficit
641                     return True
642                 else:
643                     deficit -= part[i].v
644                     part[i].v = 0
645 
646     def decrement_part_range(self, part, lb, ub):
647         """Decrements part (a subrange of pstack), if possible, returning
648         True iff the part was successfully decremented.
649 
650         Parameters
651         ==========
652 
653          part
654             part to be decremented (topmost part on the stack)
655 
656         ub
657             the maximum number of parts allowed in a partition
658             returned by the calling traversal.
659 
660         lb
661             The partitions produced by the calling enumeration must
662             have more parts than this value.
663 
664         Notes
665         =====
666 
667         Combines the constraints of _small and _large decrement
668         methods.  If returns success, part has been decremented at
669         least once, but perhaps by quite a bit more if needed to meet
670         the lb constraint.
671         """
672 
673         # Constraint in the range case is just enforcing both the
674         # constraints from _small and _large cases.  Note the 0 as the
675         # second argument to the _large call -- this is the signal to
676         # decrement only as needed to for constraint enforcement.  The
677         # short circuiting and left-to-right order of the 'and'
678         # operator is important for this to work correctly.
679         return self.decrement_part_small(part, ub) and \
680             self.decrement_part_large(part, 0, lb)
681 
682     def spread_part_multiplicity(self):
683         """Returns True if a new part has been created, and
684         adjusts pstack, f and lpart as needed.
685 
686         Notes
687         =====
688

1011         explored.  The dictionary used in order to accelerate the
1012         counting process is stored in the ``MultisetPartitionTraverser``
1013         object and persists across calls.  If the the user does not
1014         expect to call ``count_partitions`` for any additional
1015         multisets, the object should be cleared to save memory.  On
1016         the other hand, the cache built up from one count run can
1017         significantly speed up subsequent calls to ``count_partitions``,
1018         so it may be advantageous not to clear the object.

1021         ========

1032         =====
1033 
1034         If one looks at the workings of Knuth's algorithm M [AOCP]_, it
1035         can be viewed as a traversal of a binary tree of parts.  A
1036         part has (up to) two children, the left child resulting from
1037         the spread operation, and the right child from the decrement
1038         operation.  The ordinary enumeration of multiset partitions is
1039         an in-order traversal of this tree, and with the partitions
1040         corresponding to paths from the root to the leaves. The
1041         mapping from paths to partitions is a little complicated,
1042         since the partition would contain only those parts which are
1043         leaves or the parents of a spread link, not those which are
1044         parents of a decrement link.

1050         potential to speed up the counting dramatically.

1053         to the hypothetical memoized recursive function, but with two

1057            other enumerations and maintaining an explicit stack of
1058            parts which are in the process of being counted.  (There
1059            may be multisets which can be counted reasonably quickly by
1060            this implementation, but which would overflow the default
1061            Python recursion limit with a recursive implementation.)

1064            compact key is constructed.  This saves space, but more
1065            importantly coalesces some parts which would remain
1066            separate with physical keys.

1068         Unlike the enumeration functions, there is currently no _range
1069         version of count_partitions.  If someone wants to stretch
1070         their brain, it should be possible to construct one by
1071         memoizing with a histogram of counts rather than a single
1072         count, and combining the histograms.

1075         self.pcount = 0
1076         # dp_stack is list of lists of (part_key, start_count) pairs
1077         self.dp_stack = []
1078 
1079         # dp_map is map part_key-> count, where count represents the
1080         # number of multiset which are descendants of a part with this
1081         # key, **or any of its decrements**
1082 
1083         # Thus, when we find a part in the map, we add its count
1084         # value to the running total, cut off the enumeration, and
1085         # backtrack
1086 
1087         if not hasattr(self, 'dp_map'):
1088             self.dp_map = {}
1089 
1090         self._initialize_enumeration(multiplicities)
1091         pkey = part_key(self.top_part())
1092         self.dp_stack.append([(pkey, 0), ])

1094             while self.spread_part_multiplicity():

1096                 if pkey in self.dp_map:

1098                     # subtree rooted at this part.  Add it to the
1099                     # running counter, and break out of the spread
1100                     # loop.  The -1 below is to compensate for the
1101                     # leaf that this code path would otherwise find,
1102                     # and which gets incremented for below.
1103

1106                     break

1109

1111             self.pcount += 1

1113             # M5 (Decrease v)
1114             while not self.decrement_part(self.top_part()):

1125             pkey = part_key(self.top_part())

182 SymPy was started by Ondřej Čertík in 2005, he wrote some code during the
183 summer, then he wrote some more code during the summer 2006. In February 2007,
184 Fabian Pedregosa joined the project and helped fixed many things, contributed
185 documentation and made it alive again. 5 students (Mateusz Paprocki, Brian
186 Jorgensen, Jason Gedge, Robert Schwarz and Chris Wu) improved SymPy incredibly
187 during the summer 2007 as part of the Google Summer of Code. Pearu Peterson
188 joined the development during the summer 2007 and he has made SymPy much more

190 100x faster. Jurjen N.E. Bos has contributed pretty printing and other patches.

24 class HyperbolicFunction(Function):
25     """
26     Base class for hyperbolic functions.

37 def _peeloff_ipi(arg):
38     """
39     Split ARG into two parts, a "rest" and a multiple of I*pi/2.
40     This assumes ARG to be an Add.
41     The multiple of I*pi returned in the second position is always a Rational.
42 
43     Examples
44     ========
45 
46     >>> from sympy.functions.elementary.hyperbolic import _peeloff_ipi as peel
47     >>> from sympy import pi, I
48     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
49     >>> peel(x + I*pi/2)
50     (x, I*pi/2)
51     >>> peel(x + I*2*pi/3 + I*pi*y)
52     (x + I*pi*y + I*pi/6, I*pi/2)
53     """
54     for a in Add.make_args(arg):
55         if a == S.Pi*S.ImaginaryUnit:
56             K = S.One
57             break
58         elif a.is_Mul:
59             K, p = a.as_two_terms()
60             if p == S.Pi*S.ImaginaryUnit and K.is_Rational:
61                 break
62     else:
63         return arg, S.Zero
64 
65     m1 = (K % S.Half)*S.Pi*S.ImaginaryUnit
66     m2 = K*S.Pi*S.ImaginaryUnit - m1
67     return arg - m2, m2

14 class Product(ExprWithIntLimits):
15     r"""Represents unevaluated products.
16 
17     ``Product`` represents a finite or infinite product, with the first
18     argument being the general form of terms in the series, and the second
19     argument being ``(dummy_variable, start, end)``, with ``dummy_variable``
20     taking all integer values from ``start`` through ``end``. In accordance
21     with long-standing mathematical convention, the end term is included in
22     the product.
23 
24     Finite products
25     ===============
26 
27     For finite products (and products with symbolic limits assumed to be finite)
28     we follow the analogue of the summation convention described by Karr [1],
29     especially definition 3 of section 1.4. The product:
30 
31     .. math::
32 
33         \prod_{m \leq i < n} f(i)
34 
35     has *the obvious meaning* for `m < n`, namely:
36 
37     .. math::
38 
39         \prod_{m \leq i < n} f(i) = f(m) f(m+1) \cdot \ldots \cdot f(n-2) f(n-1)
40 
41     with the upper limit value `f(n)` excluded. The product over an empty set is
42     one if and only if `m = n`:
43 
44     .. math::
45 
46         \prod_{m \leq i < n} f(i) = 1  \quad \mathrm{for} \quad  m = n
47 
48     Finally, for all other products over empty sets we assume the following
49     definition:
50 
51     .. math::
52 
53         \prod_{m \leq i < n} f(i) = \frac{1}{\prod_{n \leq i < m} f(i)}  \quad \mathrm{for} \quad  m > n
54 
55     It is important to note that above we define all products with the upper
56     limit being exclusive. This is in contrast to the usual mathematical notation,
57     but does not affect the product convention. Indeed we have:
58 
59     .. math::
60 
61         \prod_{m \leq i < n} f(i) = \prod_{i = m}^{n - 1} f(i)
62 
63     where the difference in notation is intentional to emphasize the meaning,
64     with limits typeset on the top being inclusive.
65

67     ========
68

70     >>> from sympy import Product, factorial, oo

74     factorial(m)
75     >>> Product(k**2,(k, 1, m))
76     Product(k**2, (k, 1, m))
77     >>> Product(k**2,(k, 1, m)).doit()
78     factorial(m)**2
79

188     def _complement(self, other):
189         # this behaves as other - self
190         if isinstance(other, ProductSet):
191             # For each set consider it or it's complement
192             # We need at least one of the sets to be complemented
193             # Consider all 2^n combinations.
194             # We can conveniently represent these options easily using a
195             # ProductSet
196 
197             # XXX: this doesn't work if the dimensions of the sets isn't same.
198             # A - B is essentially same as A if B has a different
199             # dimensionality than A
200             switch_sets = ProductSet(FiniteSet(o, o - s) for s, o in
201                                      zip(self.sets, other.sets))
202             product_sets = (ProductSet(*set) for set in switch_sets)
203             # Union of all combinations but this one
204             return Union(p for p in product_sets if p != other)
205 
206         elif isinstance(other, Interval):
207             if isinstance(self, Interval) or isinstance(self, FiniteSet):
208                 return Intersection(other, self.complement(S.Reals))
209 
210         elif isinstance(other, Union):
211             return Union(o - self for o in other.args)
212 
213         elif isinstance(other, Complement):
214             return Complement(other.args[0], Union(other.args[1], self), evaluate=False)
215 
216         elif isinstance(other, EmptySet):
217             return S.EmptySet
218 
219         elif isinstance(other, FiniteSet):
220             return FiniteSet(*[el for el in other if self.contains(el) != True])

586 class ProductSet(Set):
587     """
588     Represents a Cartesian Product of Sets.
589 
590     Returns a Cartesian product given several sets as either an iterable
591     or individual arguments.
592 
593     Can use '*' operator on any sets for convenient shorthand.
594 
595     Examples
596     ========
597 
598     >>> from sympy import Interval, FiniteSet, ProductSet
599     >>> I = Interval(0, 5); S = FiniteSet(1, 2, 3)
600     >>> ProductSet(I, S)
601     Interval(0, 5) x {1, 2, 3}
602 
603     >>> (2, 2) in ProductSet(I, S)
604     True
605 
606     >>> Interval(0, 1) * Interval(0, 1) # The unit square
607     Interval(0, 1) x Interval(0, 1)
608 
609     >>> coin = FiniteSet('H', 'T')
610     >>> set(coin**2)
611     {(H, H), (H, T), (T, H), (T, T)}
612 
613 
614     Notes
615     =====
616 
617     - Passes most operations down to the argument sets
618     - Flattens Products of ProductSets
619 
620     References
621     ==========
622 
623     .. [1] http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartesian_product
624     """
625     is_ProductSet = True
626 
627     def __new__(cls, *sets, **assumptions):
628         def flatten(arg):
629             if isinstance(arg, Set):
630                 if arg.is_ProductSet:
631                     return sum(map(flatten, arg.args), [])
632                 else:
633                     return [arg]
634             elif iterable(arg):
635                 return sum(map(flatten, arg), [])
636             raise TypeError("Input must be Sets or iterables of Sets")
637         sets = flatten(list(sets))
638 
639         if EmptySet() in sets or len(sets) == 0:
640             return EmptySet()
641 
642         if len(sets) == 1:
643             return sets[0]
644 
645         return Basic.__new__(cls, *sets, **assumptions)

647     def _eval_Eq(self, other):
648         if not other.is_ProductSet:
649             return
650 
651         if len(self.args) != len(other.args):
652             return false
653 
654         return And(*(Eq(x, y) for x, y in zip(self.args, other.args)))
655 
656     def _contains(self, element):
657         """
658         'in' operator for ProductSets
659 
660         Examples
661         ========
662 
663         >>> from sympy import Interval
664         >>> (2, 3) in Interval(0, 5) * Interval(0, 5)
665         True
666 
667         >>> (10, 10) in Interval(0, 5) * Interval(0, 5)
668         False
669 
670         Passes operation on to constituent sets
671         """
672         try:
673             if len(element) != len(self.args):
674                 return false
675         except TypeError:  # maybe element isn't an iterable
676             return false
677         return And(*
678             [set.contains(item) for set, item in zip(self.sets, element)])
679 
680     def _intersect(self, other):
681         """
682         This function should only be used internally
683 
684         See Set._intersect for docstring
685         """
686         if not other.is_ProductSet:
687             return None
688         if len(other.args) != len(self.args):
689             return S.EmptySet
690         return ProductSet(a.intersect(b)
691                 for a, b in zip(self.sets, other.sets))

693     def _union(self, other):
694         if other.is_subset(self):
695             return self
696         if not other.is_ProductSet:
697             return None
698         if len(other.args) != len(self.args):
699             return None
700         if self.args[0] == other.args[0]:
701             return self.args[0] * Union(ProductSet(self.args[1:]),
702                                         ProductSet(other.args[1:]))
703         if self.args[-1] == other.args[-1]:
704             return Union(ProductSet(self.args[:-1]),
705                          ProductSet(other.args[:-1])) * self.args[-1]
706         return None
707

767     """
768     Represents a real interval as a Set.

770     Usage:
771         Returns an interval with end points "start" and "end".
772 
773         For left_open=True (default left_open is False) the interval
774         will be open on the left. Similarly, for right_open=True the interval
775         will be open on the right.

778     ========
779

781     >>> Interval(0, 1)

783     >>> Interval.Ropen(0, 1)

785     >>> Interval.Ropen(0, 1)
786     Interval.Ropen(0, 1)
787     >>> Interval.Lopen(0, 1)
788     Interval.Lopen(0, 1)
789     >>> Interval.open(0, 1)
790     Interval.open(0, 1)
791 
792     >>> a = Symbol('a', real=True)
793     >>> Interval(0, a)
794     Interval(0, a)
795 
796     Notes
797     =====
798     - Only real end points are supported
799     - Interval(a, b) with a > b will return the empty set
800     - Use the evalf() method to turn an Interval into an mpmath
801       'mpi' interval instance
802 
803     References
804     ==========
805 
806     .. [1] http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interval_%28mathematics%29

810     def __new__(cls, start, end, left_open=False, right_open=False):
811 
812         start = _sympify(start)
813         end = _sympify(end)
814         left_open = _sympify(left_open)
815         right_open = _sympify(right_open)
816 
817         if not all(isinstance(a, (type(true), type(false)))
818             for a in [left_open, right_open]):
819             raise NotImplementedError(
820                 "left_open and right_open can have only true/false values, "
821                 "got %s and %s" % (left_open, right_open))
822 
823         inftys = [S.Infinity, S.NegativeInfinity]

825         if not all(i.is_real is not False or i in inftys for i in (start, end)):
826             raise ValueError("Non-real intervals are not supported")

828         # evaluate if possible
829         if (end < start) == True:
830             return S.EmptySet
831         elif (end - start).is_negative:
832             return S.EmptySet
833 
834         if end == start and (left_open or right_open):
835             return S.EmptySet

837             if start == S.Infinity or start == S.NegativeInfinity:
838                 return S.EmptySet

841         # Make sure infinite interval end points are open.
842         if start == S.NegativeInfinity:
843             left_open = true
844         if end == S.Infinity:
845             right_open = true

936     def _intersect(self, other):
937         """
938         This function should only be used internally
939 
940         See Set._intersect for docstring
941         """
942         if other.is_EmptySet:
943             return other
944         # We only know how to intersect with other intervals
945         if not other.is_Interval:
946             return None
947 
948         # handle (-oo, oo)
949         infty = S.NegativeInfinity, S.Infinity
950         if self == Interval(*infty):
951             l, r = self.left, self.right
952             if l.is_real or l in infty or r.is_real or r in infty:
953                 return other
954 
955         # We can't intersect [0,3] with [x,6] -- we don't know if x>0 or x<0
956         if not self._is_comparable(other):
957             return None
958 
959         empty = False
960 
961         if self.start <= other.end and other.start <= self.end:
962             # Get topology right.
963             if self.start < other.start:
964                 start = other.start
965                 left_open = other.left_open
966             elif self.start > other.start:
967                 start = self.start
968                 left_open = self.left_open
969             else:
970                 start = self.start
971                 left_open = self.left_open or other.left_open
972 
973             if self.end < other.end:
974                 end = self.end
975                 right_open = self.right_open
976             elif self.end > other.end:
977                 end = other.end
978                 right_open = other.right_open
979             else:
980                 end = self.end
981                 right_open = self.right_open or other.right_open
982 
983             if end - start == 0 and (left_open or right_open):
984                 empty = True
985         else:
986             empty = True
987 
988         if empty:
989             return S.EmptySet
990 
991         return Interval(start, end, left_open, right_open)

995         if other == S.Reals:
996             a = Interval(S.NegativeInfinity, self.start,
997                          True, not self.left_open)
998             b = Interval(self.end, S.Infinity, not self.right_open, True)
999             return Union(a, b)
1000 
1001         if isinstance(other, FiniteSet):
1002             nums = [m for m in other.args if m.is_number]
1003             if nums == []:
1004                 return None
1005 
1006         return Set._complement(self, other)

1009     def _union(self, other):
1010         """
1011         This function should only be used internally
1012 
1013         See Set._union for docstring
1014         """
1015         if other.is_UniversalSet:
1016             return S.UniversalSet
1017         if other.is_Interval and self._is_comparable(other):
1018             from sympy.functions.elementary.miscellaneous import Min, Max
1019             # Non-overlapping intervals
1020             end = Min(self.end, other.end)
1021             start = Max(self.start, other.start)
1022             if (end < start or
1023                (end == start and (end not in self and end not in other))):
1024                 return None
1025             else:
1026                 start = Min(self.start, other.start)
1027                 end = Max(self.end, other.end)
1028 
1029                 left_open = ((self.start != start or self.left_open) and
1030                              (other.start != start or other.left_open))
1031                 right_open = ((self.end != end or self.right_open) and
1032                               (other.end != end or other.right_open))
1033 
1034                 return Interval(start, end, left_open, right_open)
1035 
1036         # If I have open end points and these endpoints are contained in other.
1037         # But only in case, when endpoints are finite. Because
1038         # interval does not contain oo or -oo.
1039         open_left_in_other_and_finite = (self.left_open and
1040                                          sympify(other.contains(self.start)) is S.true and
1041                                          self.start.is_finite)
1042         open_right_in_other_and_finite = (self.right_open and
1043                                           sympify(other.contains(self.end)) is S.true and
1044                                           self.end.is_finite)
1045         if open_left_in_other_and_finite or open_right_in_other_and_finite:
1046             # Fill in my end points and return
1047             open_left = self.left_open and self.start not in other
1048             open_right = self.right_open and self.end not in other
1049             new_self = Interval(self.start, self.end, open_left, open_right)
1050             return set((new_self, other))
1051 
1052         return None

1057                          if abs(p) != S.Infinity]

1062                 other is S.Infinity or
1063                 other is S.NegativeInfinity or
1064                 other is S.NaN or
1065                 other is S.ComplexInfinity) or other.is_real is False:
1066             return false

1068         if self.start is S.NegativeInfinity and self.end is S.Infinity:
1069             if not other.is_real is None:
1070                 return other.is_real
1071 
1072         if self.left_open:
1073             expr = other > self.start
1074         else:
1075             expr = other >= self.start
1076 
1077         if self.right_open:
1078             expr = And(expr, other < self.end)
1079         else:
1080             expr = And(expr, other <= self.end)

1084     def _eval_imageset(self, f):
1085         from sympy.functions.elementary.miscellaneous import Min, Max
1086         from sympy.solvers.solveset import solveset
1087         from sympy.core.function import diff, Lambda
1088         from sympy.series import limit
1089         from sympy.calculus.singularities import singularities
1090         # TODO: handle functions with infinitely many solutions (eg, sin, tan)
1091         # TODO: handle multivariate functions
1092 
1093         expr = f.expr
1094         if len(expr.free_symbols) > 1 or len(f.variables) != 1:
1095             return
1096         var = f.variables[0]
1097 
1098         if expr.is_Piecewise:
1099             result = S.EmptySet
1100             domain_set = self
1101             for (p_expr, p_cond) in expr.args:
1102                 if p_cond is true:
1103                     intrvl = domain_set
1104                 else:
1105                     intrvl = p_cond.as_set()
1106                     intrvl = Intersection(domain_set, intrvl)
1107 
1108                 if p_expr.is_Number:
1109                     image = FiniteSet(p_expr)
1110                 else:
1111                     image = imageset(Lambda(var, p_expr), intrvl)
1112                 result = Union(result, image)
1113 
1114                 # remove the part which has been `imaged`
1115                 domain_set = Complement(domain_set, intrvl)
1116                 if domain_set.is_EmptySet:
1117                     break
1118             return result
1119 
1120         if not self.start.is_comparable or not self.end.is_comparable:
1121             return
1122 
1123         try:
1124             sing = [x for x in singularities(expr, var)
1125                 if x.is_real and x in self]
1126         except NotImplementedError:
1127             return
1128 
1129         if self.left_open:
1130             _start = limit(expr, var, self.start, dir="+")
1131         elif self.start not in sing:
1132             _start = f(self.start)
1133         if self.right_open:
1134             _end = limit(expr, var, self.end, dir="-")
1135         elif self.end not in sing:
1136             _end = f(self.end)
1137 
1138         if len(sing) == 0:
1139             solns = list(solveset(diff(expr, var), var))
1140 
1141             extr = [_start, _end] + [f(x) for x in solns
1142                                      if x.is_real and x in self]
1143             start, end = Min(*extr), Max(*extr)
1144 
1145             left_open, right_open = False, False
1146             if _start <= _end:
1147                 # the minimum or maximum value can occur simultaneously
1148                 # on both the edge of the interval and in some interior
1149                 # point
1150                 if start == _start and start not in solns:
1151                     left_open = self.left_open
1152                 if end == _end and end not in solns:
1153                     right_open = self.right_open
1154             else:
1155                 if start == _end and start not in solns:
1156                     left_open = self.right_open
1157                 if end == _start and end not in solns:
1158                     right_open = self.left_open
1159 
1160             return Interval(start, end, left_open, right_open)
1161         else:
1162             return imageset(f, Interval(self.start, sing[0],
1163                                         self.left_open, True)) + \
1164                 Union(*[imageset(f, Interval(sing[i], sing[i + 1], True, True))
1165                         for i in range(0, len(sing) - 1)]) + \
1166                 imageset(f, Interval(sing[-1], self.end, True, self.right_open))
1167

1226 class Union(Set, EvalfMixin):
1227     """
1228     Represents a union of sets as a :class:`Set`.
1229 
1230     Examples
1231     ========
1232 
1233     >>> from sympy import Union, Interval
1234     >>> Union(Interval(1, 2), Interval(3, 4))
1235     Union(Interval(1, 2), Interval(3, 4))
1236 
1237     The Union constructor will always try to merge overlapping intervals,
1238     if possible. For example:
1239 
1240     >>> Union(Interval(1, 2), Interval(2, 3))
1241     Interval(1, 3)
1242 
1243     See Also
1244     ========
1245 
1246     Intersection
1247 
1248     References
1249     ==========
1250 
1251     .. [1] http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_%28set_theory%29
1252     """
1253     is_Union = True

1255     def __new__(cls, *args, **kwargs):
1256         evaluate = kwargs.get('evaluate', global_evaluate[0])
1257 
1258         # flatten inputs to merge intersections and iterables
1259         args = list(args)
1260 
1261         def flatten(arg):
1262             if isinstance(arg, Set):
1263                 if arg.is_Union:
1264                     return sum(map(flatten, arg.args), [])
1265                 else:
1266                     return [arg]
1267             if iterable(arg):  # and not isinstance(arg, Set) (implicit)
1268                 return sum(map(flatten, arg), [])
1269             raise TypeError("Input must be Sets or iterables of Sets")
1270         args = flatten(args)
1271 
1272         # Union of no sets is EmptySet
1273         if len(args) == 0:
1274             return S.EmptySet
1275 
1276         # Reduce sets using known rules
1277         if evaluate:
1278             return Union.reduce(args)
1279 
1280         args = list(ordered(args, Set._infimum_key))
1281 
1282         return Basic.__new__(cls, *args)

1284     @staticmethod
1285     def reduce(args):
1286         """
1287         Simplify a :class:`Union` using known rules
1288 
1289         We first start with global rules like
1290         'Merge all FiniteSets'
1291 
1292         Then we iterate through all pairs and ask the constituent sets if they
1293         can simplify themselves with any other constituent
1294         """
1295 
1296         # ===== Global Rules =====
1297         # Merge all finite sets
1298         finite_sets = [x for x in args if x.is_FiniteSet]
1299         if len(finite_sets) > 1:
1300             a = (x for set in finite_sets for x in set)
1301             finite_set = FiniteSet(*a)
1302             args = [finite_set] + [x for x in args if not x.is_FiniteSet]
1303 
1304         # ===== Pair-wise Rules =====
1305         # Here we depend on rules built into the constituent sets
1306         args = set(args)
1307         new_args = True
1308         while(new_args):
1309             for s in args:
1310                 new_args = False
1311                 for t in args - set((s,)):
1312                     new_set = s._union(t)
1313                     # This returns None if s does not know how to intersect
1314                     # with t. Returns the newly intersected set otherwise
1315                     if new_set is not None:
1316                         if not isinstance(new_set, set):
1317                             new_set = set((new_set, ))
1318                         new_args = (args - set((s, t))).union(new_set)
1319                         break
1320                 if new_args:
1321                     args = new_args
1322                     break
1323 
1324         if len(args) == 1:
1325             return args.pop()
1326         else:
1327             return Union(args, evaluate=False)
1328 
1329     def _complement(self, universe):
1330         # DeMorgan's Law
1331         return Intersection(s.complement(universe) for s in self.args)

1333     @property

1350     @property
1351     def _measure(self):
1352         # Measure of a union is the sum of the measures of the sets minus
1353         # the sum of their pairwise intersections plus the sum of their
1354         # triple-wise intersections minus ... etc...
1355 
1356         # Sets is a collection of intersections and a set of elementary
1357         # sets which made up those intersections (called "sos" for set of sets)
1358         # An example element might of this list might be:
1359         #    ( {A,B,C}, A.intersect(B).intersect(C) )
1360 
1361         # Start with just elementary sets (  ({A}, A), ({B}, B), ... )
1362         # Then get and subtract (  ({A,B}, (A int B), ... ) while non-zero
1363         sets = [(FiniteSet(s), s) for s in self.args]
1364         measure = 0
1365         parity = 1
1366         while sets:
1367             # Add up the measure of these sets and add or subtract it to total
1368             measure += parity * sum(inter.measure for sos, inter in sets)
1369 
1370             # For each intersection in sets, compute the intersection with every
1371             # other set not already part of the intersection.
1372             sets = ((sos + FiniteSet(newset), newset.intersect(intersection))
1373                     for sos, intersection in sets for newset in self.args
1374                     if newset not in sos)
1375 
1376             # Clear out sets with no measure
1377             sets = [(sos, inter) for sos, inter in sets if inter.measure != 0]
1378 
1379             # Clear out duplicates
1380             sos_list = []
1381             sets_list = []
1382             for set in sets:
1383                 if set[0] in sos_list:
1384                     continue
1385                 else:
1386                     sos_list.append(set[0])
1387                     sets_list.append(set)
1388             sets = sets_list
1389 
1390             # Flip Parity - next time subtract/add if we added/subtracted here
1391             parity *= -1
1392         return measure
1393

1397             """ The boundary of set i minus interior of all other sets """
1398             b = self.args[i].boundary
1399             for j, a in enumerate(self.args):
1400                 if j != i:
1401                     b = b - a.interior
1402             return b
1403         return Union(map(boundary_of_set, range(len(self.args))))

1412             if (a.sup == b.inf and a.inf is S.NegativeInfinity
1413                     and b.sup is S.Infinity):

1415         return Or(*[set.as_relational(symbol) for set in self.args])

1436             "roundrobin('ABC', 'D', 'EF') --> A D E B F C"
1437             # Recipe credited to George Sakkis
1438             pending = len(iterables)
1439             if PY3:
1440                 nexts = itertools.cycle(iter(it).__next__ for it in iterables)
1441             else:
1442                 nexts = itertools.cycle(iter(it).next for it in iterables)
1443             while pending:
1444                 try:
1445                     for next in nexts:
1446                         yield next()
1447                 except StopIteration:
1448                     pending -= 1
1449                     nexts = itertools.cycle(itertools.islice(nexts, pending))
1450 
1451         if all(set.is_iterable for set in self.args):
1452             return roundrobin(*(iter(arg) for arg in self.args))
1453         else:
1454             raise TypeError("Not all constituent sets are iterable")

1484     def __new__(cls, *args, **kwargs):

1497                 return sum(map(flatten, arg), [])

1500

1505         if 'Partition' not in [type(a).__name__ for a in args]:
1506             args = list(ordered(args, Set._infimum_key))

1538                 other = Intersection(other_sets, evaluate=False)
1539                 for x in s:
1540                     c = sympify(other.contains(x))
1541                     if c is S.true:
1542                         yield x
1543                     elif c is S.false:
1544                         pass
1545                     else:
1546                         yield c

1551     @staticmethod
1552     def _handle_finite_sets(args):
1553         from sympy.core.logic import fuzzy_and, fuzzy_bool
1554         from sympy.core.compatibility import zip_longest
1555 
1556         fs_args, other = sift(args, lambda x: x.is_FiniteSet,
1557             binary=True)
1558         if not fs_args:
1559             return
1560         s = fs_args[0]
1561         fs_args = fs_args[1:]
1562 
1563         res = []
1564         unk = []
1565         for x in s:
1566             c = fuzzy_and(fuzzy_bool(o.contains(x))
1567                 for o in fs_args + other)
1568             if c:
1569                 res.append(x)
1570             elif c is None:
1571                 unk.append(x)
1572             else:
1573                 pass  # drop arg
1574         res = FiniteSet(
1575             *res, evaluate=False) if res else S.EmptySet
1576         if unk:
1577             symbolic_s_list = [x for x in s if x.has(Symbol)]
1578             non_symbolic_s = s - FiniteSet(
1579                 *symbolic_s_list, evaluate=False)
1580             while fs_args:
1581                 v = fs_args.pop()
1582                 if all(i == j for i, j in zip_longest(
1583                         symbolic_s_list,
1584                         (x for x in v if x.has(Symbol)))):
1585                     # all the symbolic elements of `v` are the same
1586                     # as in `s` so remove the non-symbol containing
1587                     # expressions from `unk`, since they cannot be
1588                     # contained
1589                     for x in non_symbolic_s:
1590                         if x in unk:
1591                             unk.remove(x)
1592                 else:
1593                     # if only a subset of elements in `s` are
1594                     # contained in `v` then remove them from `v`
1595                     # and add this as a new arg
1596                     contained = [x for x in symbolic_s_list
1597                         if sympify(v.contains(x)) is S.true]
1598                     if contained != symbolic_s_list:
1599                         other.append(
1600                             v - FiniteSet(
1601                             *contained, evaluate=False))
1602                     else:
1603                         pass  # for coverage
1604 
1605             other_sets = Intersection(*other)
1606             if not other_sets:
1607                 return S.EmptySet  # b/c we use evaluate=False below
1608             res += Intersection(
1609                 FiniteSet(*unk),
1610                 other_sets, evaluate=False)

1613     @staticmethod
1614     def reduce(args):
1615         """
1616         Return a simplified intersection by applying rules.
1617 
1618         We first start with global rules like
1619         'if any empty sets, return empty set' and 'distribute unions'.
1620 
1621         Then we iterate through all pairs and ask the constituent sets if they
1622         can simplify themselves with any other constituent
1623         """
1624         from sympy.simplify.simplify import clear_coefficients
1625 
1626         # ===== Global Rules =====
1627         # If any EmptySets return EmptySet
1628         if any(s.is_EmptySet for s in args):
1629             return S.EmptySet
1630 
1631         # Handle Finite sets
1632         rv = Intersection._handle_finite_sets(args)
1633         if rv is not None:
1634             return rv
1635 
1636         # If any of the sets are unions, return a Union of Intersections
1637         for s in args:
1638             if s.is_Union:
1639                 other_sets = set(args) - set((s,))
1640                 if len(other_sets) > 0:
1641                     other = Intersection(other_sets)
1642                     return Union(Intersection(arg, other) for arg in s.args)
1643                 else:
1644                     return Union(arg for arg in s.args)
1645 
1646         for s in args:
1647             if s.is_Complement:
1648                 args.remove(s)
1649                 other_sets = args + [s.args[0]]
1650                 return Complement(Intersection(*other_sets), s.args[1])
1651 
1652         # At this stage we are guaranteed not to have any
1653         # EmptySets, FiniteSets, or Unions in the intersection
1654 
1655         # ===== Pair-wise Rules =====
1656         # Here we depend on rules built into the constituent sets
1657         args = set(args)
1658         new_args = True
1659         while(new_args):
1660             for s in args:
1661                 new_args = False
1662                 for t in args - set((s,)):
1663                     new_set = s._intersect(t)
1664                     # This returns None if s does not know how to intersect
1665                     # with t. Returns the newly intersected set otherwise
1666                     if new_set is not None:
1667                         new_args = (args - set((s, t))).union(set((new_set, )))
1668                         break
1669                 if new_args:
1670                     args = new_args
1671                     break
1672 
1673         if len(args) == 1:
1674             return args.pop()
1675         else:
1676             return Intersection(args, evaluate=False)
1677 
1678     def as_relational(self, symbol):
1679         """Rewrite an Intersection in terms of equalities and logic operators"""
1680         return And(*[set.as_relational(symbol) for set in self.args])

290         [9, 10, 11]])
291         >>> m.extract([0, 1, 3], [0, 1])
292         Matrix([
293         [0,  1],
294         [3,  4],
295         [9, 10]])

297         Rows or columns can be repeated:
298 
299         >>> m.extract([0, 0, 1], [-1])

301         [2],
302         [2],
303         [5]])

305         Every other row can be taken by using range to provide the indices:
306 
307         >>> m.extract(range(0, m.rows, 2), [-1])

310         [8]])

312         RowsList or colsList can also be a list of booleans, in which case
313         the rows or columns corresponding to the True values will be selected:
314 
315         >>> m.extract([0, 1, 2, 3], [True, False, True])
316         Matrix([

318         [3,  5],
319         [6,  8],
320         [9, 11]])

324             raise TypeError("rowsList and colsList must be iterable")
325         # ensure rowsList and colsList are lists of integers
326         if rowsList and all(isinstance(i, bool) for i in rowsList):
327             rowsList = [index for index, item in enumerate(rowsList) if item]
328         if colsList and all(isinstance(i, bool) for i in colsList):
329             colsList = [index for index, item in enumerate(colsList) if item]
330 
331         # ensure everything is in range
332         rowsList = [a2idx(k, self.rows) for k in rowsList]
333         colsList = [a2idx(k, self.cols) for k in colsList]
334 
335         return self._eval_extract(rowsList, colsList)

654     @classmethod
655     def diag(kls, *args, **kwargs):
656         """Returns a matrix with the specified diagonal.
657         If matrices are passed, a block-diagonal matrix
658         is created.
659 
660         kwargs
661         ======
662 
663         rows : rows of the resulting matrix; computed if
664                not given.
665         cols : columns of the resulting matrix; computed if
666                not given.
667         cls : class for the resulting matrix
668 
669         Examples
670         ========
671 
672         >>> from sympy.matrices import Matrix
673         >>> Matrix.diag(1, 2, 3)
674         Matrix([
675         [1, 0, 0],
676         [0, 2, 0],
677         [0, 0, 3]])
678         >>> Matrix.diag([1, 2, 3])
679         Matrix([
680         [1, 0, 0],
681         [0, 2, 0],
682         [0, 0, 3]])
683 
684         The diagonal elements can be matrices; diagonal filling will
685         continue on the diagonal from the last element of the matrix:
686 
687         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
688         >>> a = Matrix([x, y, z])
689         >>> b = Matrix([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
690         >>> c = Matrix([[5, 6]])
691         >>> Matrix.diag(a, 7, b, c)
692         Matrix([
693         [x, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
694         [y, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
695         [z, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
696         [0, 7, 0, 0, 0, 0],
697         [0, 0, 1, 2, 0, 0],
698         [0, 0, 3, 4, 0, 0],
699         [0, 0, 0, 0, 5, 6]])
700 
701         A given band off the diagonal can be made by padding with a
702         vertical or horizontal "kerning" vector:
703 
704         >>> hpad = Matrix(0, 2, [])
705         >>> vpad = Matrix(2, 0, [])
706         >>> Matrix.diag(vpad, 1, 2, 3, hpad) + Matrix.diag(hpad, 4, 5, 6, vpad)
707         Matrix([
708         [0, 0, 4, 0, 0],
709         [0, 0, 0, 5, 0],
710         [1, 0, 0, 0, 6],
711         [0, 2, 0, 0, 0],
712         [0, 0, 3, 0, 0]])
713 
714         The type of the resulting matrix can be affected with the ``cls``
715         keyword.
716 
717         >>> type(Matrix.diag(1))
718         <class 'sympy.matrices.dense.MutableDenseMatrix'>
719         >>> from sympy.matrices import ImmutableMatrix
720         >>> type(Matrix.diag(1, cls=ImmutableMatrix))
721         <class 'sympy.matrices.immutable.ImmutableDenseMatrix'>
722         """
723 
724         klass = kwargs.get('cls', kls)
725         # allow a sequence to be passed in as the only argument
726         if len(args) == 1 and is_sequence(args[0]) and not getattr(args[0], 'is_Matrix', False):
727             args = args[0]
728 
729         def size(m):
730             """Compute the size of the diagonal block"""
731             if hasattr(m, 'rows'):
732                 return m.rows, m.cols
733             return 1, 1
734         diag_rows = sum(size(m)[0] for m in args)
735         diag_cols =  sum(size(m)[1] for m in args)
736         rows = kwargs.get('rows', diag_rows)
737         cols = kwargs.get('cols', diag_cols)
738         if rows < diag_rows or cols < diag_cols:
739             raise ValueError("A {} x {} diagnal matrix cannot accomodate a"
740                              "diagonal of size at least {} x {}.".format(rows, cols,
741                                                                          diag_rows, diag_cols))
742 
743         # fill a default dict with the diagonal entries
744         diag_entries = collections.defaultdict(lambda: S.Zero)
745         row_pos, col_pos = 0, 0
746         for m in args:
747             if hasattr(m, 'rows'):
748                 # in this case, we're a matrix
749                 for i in range(m.rows):
750                     for j in range(m.cols):
751                         diag_entries[(i + row_pos, j + col_pos)] = m[i, j]
752                 row_pos += m.rows
753                 col_pos += m.cols
754             else:
755                 # in this case, we're a single value
756                 diag_entries[(row_pos, col_pos)] = m
757                 row_pos += 1
758                 col_pos += 1
759         return klass._eval_diag(rows, cols, diag_entries)
760

782     @classmethod
783     def jordan_block(kls, *args, **kwargs):
784         """Returns a Jordan block with the specified size
785         and eigenvalue.  You may call `jordan_block` with
786         two args (size, eigenvalue) or with keyword arguments.
787 
788         kwargs
789         ======
790 
791         size : rows and columns of the matrix
792         rows : rows of the matrix (if None, rows=size)
793         cols : cols of the matrix (if None, cols=size)
794         eigenvalue : value on the diagonal of the matrix
795         band : position of off-diagonal 1s.  May be 'upper' or
796                'lower'. (Default: 'upper')
797 
798         cls : class of the returned matrix
799 
800         Examples
801         ========
802 
803         >>> from sympy import Matrix
804         >>> from sympy.abc import x
805         >>> Matrix.jordan_block(4, x)
806         Matrix([
807         [x, 1, 0, 0],
808         [0, x, 1, 0],
809         [0, 0, x, 1],
810         [0, 0, 0, x]])
811         >>> Matrix.jordan_block(4, x, band='lower')
812         Matrix([
813         [x, 0, 0, 0],
814         [1, x, 0, 0],
815         [0, 1, x, 0],
816         [0, 0, 1, x]])
817         >>> Matrix.jordan_block(size=4, eigenvalue=x)
818         Matrix([
819         [x, 1, 0, 0],
820         [0, x, 1, 0],
821         [0, 0, x, 1],
822         [0, 0, 0, x]])
823         """
824 
825         klass = kwargs.get('cls', kls)
826         size, eigenvalue = None, None
827         if len(args) == 2:
828             size, eigenvalue = args
829         elif len(args) == 1:
830             size = args[0]
831         elif len(args) != 0:
832             raise ValueError("'jordan_block' accepts 0, 1, or 2 arguments, not {}".format(len(args)))
833         rows, cols = kwargs.get('rows', None), kwargs.get('cols', None)
834         size = kwargs.get('size', size)
835         band = kwargs.get('band', 'upper')
836         # allow for a shortened form of `eigenvalue`
837         eigenvalue = kwargs.get('eigenval', eigenvalue)
838         eigenvalue = kwargs.get('eigenvalue', eigenvalue)
839 
840         if eigenvalue is None:
841             raise ValueError("Must supply an eigenvalue")
842 
843         if (size, rows, cols) == (None, None, None):

846         if size is not None:
847             rows, cols = size, size
848         elif rows is not None and cols is None:
849             cols = rows
850         elif cols is not None and rows is None:
851             rows = cols
852 
853         rows, cols = as_int(rows), as_int(cols)
854 
855         return klass._eval_jordan_block(rows, cols, eigenvalue, band)

1039         the SymPy simplify function is used. To use a custom function
1040         set simplify to a function that accepts a single argument which
1041         returns a simplified expression. To skip simplification, set
1042         simplify to False but note that although this will be faster,
1043         it may induce false negatives.
1044 
1045         Examples
1046         ========
1047 
1048         >>> from sympy import Matrix, symbols
1049         >>> m = Matrix(2, 2, [0, 1, -1, 0])
1050         >>> m
1051         Matrix([
1052         [ 0, 1],
1053         [-1, 0]])
1054         >>> m.is_anti_symmetric()
1055         True
1056         >>> x, y = symbols('x y')
1057         >>> m = Matrix(2, 3, [0, 0, x, -y, 0, 0])
1058         >>> m
1059         Matrix([
1060         [ 0, 0, x],
1061         [-y, 0, 0]])
1062         >>> m.is_anti_symmetric()
1063         False
1064 
1065         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
1066         >>> m = Matrix(3, 3, [0, x**2 + 2*x + 1, y,
1067         ...                   -(x + 1)**2 , 0, x*y,
1068         ...                   -y, -x*y, 0])
1069 
1070         Simplification of matrix elements is done by default so even
1071         though two elements which should be equal and opposite wouldn't
1072         pass an equality test, the matrix is still reported as
1073         anti-symmetric:
1074 
1075         >>> m[0, 1] == -m[1, 0]
1076         False
1077         >>> m.is_anti_symmetric()
1078         True
1079 
1080         If 'simplify=False' is used for the case when a Matrix is already
1081         simplified, this will speed things up. Here, we see that without
1082         simplification the matrix does not appear anti-symmetric:
1083 
1084         >>> m.is_anti_symmetric(simplify=False)
1085         False
1086 
1087         But if the matrix were already expanded, then it would appear
1088         anti-symmetric and simplification in the is_anti_symmetric routine
1089         is not needed:
1090 
1091         >>> m = m.expand()
1092         >>> m.is_anti_symmetric(simplify=False)
1093         True
1094         """
1095         # accept custom simplification
1096         simpfunc = simplify
1097         if not isinstance(simplify, FunctionType):
1098             simpfunc = _simplify if simplify else lambda x: x
1099 
1100         if not self.is_square:
1101             return False
1102         return self._eval_is_anti_symmetric(simpfunc)

1634     def permute(self, perm, orientation='rows', direction='forward'):
1635         """Permute the rows or columns of a matrix by the given list of swaps.
1636 
1637         Parameters
1638         ==========
1639 
1640         perm : a permutation.  This may be a list swaps (e.g., `[[1, 2], [0, 3]]`),
1641             or any valid input to the `Permutation` constructor, including a `Permutation()`
1642             itself.  If `perm` is given explicitly as a list of indices or a `Permutation`,
1643             `direction` has no effect.
1644         orientation : ('rows' or 'cols') whether to permute the rows or the columns
1645         direction : ('forward', 'backward') whether to apply the permutations from
1646             the start of the list first, or from the back of the list first
1647 
1648         Examples
1649         ========
1650 
1651         >>> from sympy.matrices import eye
1652         >>> M = eye(3)
1653         >>> M.permute([[0, 1], [0, 2]], orientation='rows', direction='forward')
1654         Matrix([
1655         [0, 0, 1],
1656         [1, 0, 0],
1657         [0, 1, 0]])
1658 
1659         >>> from sympy.matrices import eye
1660         >>> M = eye(3)
1661         >>> M.permute([[0, 1], [0, 2]], orientation='rows', direction='backward')
1662         Matrix([
1663         [0, 1, 0],
1664         [0, 0, 1],
1665         [1, 0, 0]])
1666 
1667         """
1668 
1669         # allow british variants and `columns`
1670         if direction == 'forwards':
1671             direction = 'forward'
1672         if direction == 'backwards':
1673             direction = 'backward'
1674         if orientation == 'columns':
1675             orientation = 'cols'
1676 
1677         if direction not in ('forward', 'backward'):
1678             raise TypeError("direction='{}' is an invalid kwarg. "
1679                             "Try 'forward' or 'backward'".format(direction))
1680         if orientation not in ('rows', 'cols'):
1681             raise TypeError("orientation='{}' is an invalid kwarg. "
1682                             "Try 'rows' or 'cols'".format(orientation))
1683 
1684         # ensure all swaps are in range
1685         max_index = self.rows if orientation == 'rows' else self.cols
1686         if not all(0 <= t <= max_index for t in flatten(list(perm))):
1687             raise IndexError("`swap` indices out of range.")
1688 
1689         # see if we are a list of pairs
1690         try:
1691             assert len(perm[0]) == 2
1692             # we are a list of swaps, so `direction` matters
1693             if direction == 'backward':
1694                 perm = reversed(perm)
1695 
1696             # since Permutation doesn't let us have non-disjoint cycles,
1697             # we'll construct the explict mapping ourselves XXX Bug #12479
1698             mapping = list(range(max_index))
1699             for (i, j) in perm:
1700                 mapping[i], mapping[j] = mapping[j], mapping[i]
1701             perm = mapping
1702         except (TypeError, AssertionError, IndexError):
1703             pass
1704 
1705         from sympy.combinatorics import Permutation
1706         perm = Permutation(perm, size=max_index)
1707 
1708         if orientation == 'rows':
1709             return self._eval_permute_rows(perm)
1710         if orientation == 'cols':
1711             return self._eval_permute_cols(perm)
1712

179 Brief History
180 -------------
181 
182 SymPy was started by Ondřej Čertík in 2005, he wrote some code during the
183 summer, then he wrote some more code during the summer 2006. In February 2007,
184 Fabian Pedregosa joined the project and helped fixed many things, contributed
185 documentation and made it alive again. 5 students (Mateusz Paprocki, Brian
186 Jorgensen, Jason Gedge, Robert Schwarz and Chris Wu) improved SymPy incredibly
187 during the summer 2007 as part of the Google Summer of Code. Pearu Peterson
188 joined the development during the summer 2007 and he has made SymPy much more
189 competitive by rewriting the core from scratch, that has made it from 10x to
190 100x faster. Jurjen N.E. Bos has contributed pretty printing and other patches.
191 Fredrik Johansson has written mpmath and contributed a lot of patches.
192 
193 SymPy has participated in every Google Summer of Code since 2007. You can see
194 https://github.com/sympy/sympy/wiki#google-summer-of-code for full details.
195 Each year has improved SymPy by bounds. Most of SymPy's development has come
196 from Google Summer of Code students.
197 
198 In 2011, Ondřej Čertík stepped down as lead developer, with Aaron Meurer, who
199 also started as a Google Summer of Code student, taking his place. Ondřej
200 Čertík is still active in the community, but is too busy with work and family
201 to play a lead development role.
202 
203 Since then, a lot more people have joined the development and some people have
204 also left. You can see the full list in doc/src/aboutus.rst, or online at:
205 
206 http://docs.sympy.org/dev/aboutus.html#sympy-development-team
207 
208 The git history goes back to 2007, when development moved from svn to hg.  To
209 see the history before that point, look at http://github.com/sympy/sympy-old.
210 
211 You can use git to see the biggest developers.  The command::

215 will show each developer, sorted by commits to the project.  The command::

64     Generic class for representing and operating on polynomial expressions.
65     Subclasses Expr class.
66

68     ========
69 
70     >>> from sympy import Poly
71     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
72 
73     Create a univariate polynomial:
74 
75     >>> Poly(x*(x**2 + x - 1)**2)

80     >>> from sympy import sqrt

91     >>> Poly(y*x**2 + x*y + 1,x)

93 
94     You can evaluate the above polynomial as a function of y:

363     def unify(f, g):
364         """
365         Make ``f`` and ``g`` belong to the same domain.
366 
367         Examples
368         ========
369 
370         >>> from sympy import Poly
371         >>> from sympy.abc import x
372 
373         >>> f, g = Poly(x/2 + 1), Poly(2*x + 1)
374 
375         >>> f
376         Poly(1/2*x + 1, x, domain='QQ')
377         >>> g
378         Poly(2*x + 1, x, domain='ZZ')
379 
380         >>> F, G = f.unify(g)
381 
382         >>> F
383         Poly(1/2*x + 1, x, domain='QQ')
384         >>> G
385         Poly(2*x + 1, x, domain='QQ')
386 
387         """
388         _, per, F, G = f._unify(g)
389         return per(F), per(G)
390 
391     def _unify(f, g):
392         g = sympify(g)
393 
394         if not g.is_Poly:
395             try:
396                 return f.rep.dom, f.per, f.rep, f.rep.per(f.rep.dom.from_sympy(g))
397             except CoercionFailed:
398                 raise UnificationFailed("can't unify %s with %s" % (f, g))
399 
400         if isinstance(f.rep, DMP) and isinstance(g.rep, DMP):
401             gens = _unify_gens(f.gens, g.gens)
402 
403             dom, lev = f.rep.dom.unify(g.rep.dom, gens), len(gens) - 1
404 
405             if f.gens != gens:
406                 f_monoms, f_coeffs = _dict_reorder(
407                     f.rep.to_dict(), f.gens, gens)
408 
409                 if f.rep.dom != dom:
410                     f_coeffs = [dom.convert(c, f.rep.dom) for c in f_coeffs]
411 
412                 F = DMP(dict(list(zip(f_monoms, f_coeffs))), dom, lev)
413             else:
414                 F = f.rep.convert(dom)
415 
416             if g.gens != gens:
417                 g_monoms, g_coeffs = _dict_reorder(
418                     g.rep.to_dict(), g.gens, gens)
419 
420                 if g.rep.dom != dom:
421                     g_coeffs = [dom.convert(c, g.rep.dom) for c in g_coeffs]
422 
423                 G = DMP(dict(list(zip(g_monoms, g_coeffs))), dom, lev)
424             else:
425                 G = g.rep.convert(dom)
426         else:
427             raise UnificationFailed("can't unify %s with %s" % (f, g))
428 
429         cls = f.__class__
430 
431         def per(rep, dom=dom, gens=gens, remove=None):
432             if remove is not None:
433                 gens = gens[:remove] + gens[remove + 1:]
434 
435                 if not gens:
436                     return dom.to_sympy(rep)
437 
438             return cls.new(rep, *gens)
439 
440         return dom, per, F, G

614     def ltrim(f, gen):
615         """
616         Remove dummy generators from ``f`` that are to the left of
617         specified ``gen`` in the generators as ordered. When ``gen``
618         is an integer, it refers to the generator located at that
619         position within the tuple of generators of ``f``.

621         Examples

634         j = f._gen_to_level(gen)
635 
636         terms = {}
637 
638         for monom, coeff in rep.items():
639 
640             if any(i for i in monom[:j]):
641                 # some generator is used in the portion to be trimmed
642                 raise PolynomialError("can't left trim %s" % f)
643 
644             terms[monom[j:]] = coeff

646         gens = f.gens[j:]

648         return f.new(DMP.from_dict(terms, len(gens) - 1, f.rep.dom), *gens)

2304     def eval(self, x, a=None, auto=True):
2305         """
2306         Evaluate ``f`` at ``a`` in the given variable.
2307 
2308         Examples
2309         ========
2310 
2311         >>> from sympy import Poly
2312         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
2313 
2314         >>> Poly(x**2 + 2*x + 3, x).eval(2)
2315         11
2316 
2317         >>> Poly(2*x*y + 3*x + y + 2, x, y).eval(x, 2)
2318         Poly(5*y + 8, y, domain='ZZ')
2319 
2320         >>> f = Poly(2*x*y + 3*x + y + 2*z, x, y, z)
2321 
2322         >>> f.eval({x: 2})
2323         Poly(5*y + 2*z + 6, y, z, domain='ZZ')
2324         >>> f.eval({x: 2, y: 5})
2325         Poly(2*z + 31, z, domain='ZZ')
2326         >>> f.eval({x: 2, y: 5, z: 7})
2327         45
2328 
2329         >>> f.eval((2, 5))
2330         Poly(2*z + 31, z, domain='ZZ')
2331         >>> f(2, 5)
2332         Poly(2*z + 31, z, domain='ZZ')
2333 
2334         """
2335         f = self
2336 
2337         if a is None:
2338             if isinstance(x, dict):
2339                 mapping = x
2340 
2341                 for gen, value in mapping.items():
2342                     f = f.eval(gen, value)
2343 
2344                 return f
2345             elif isinstance(x, (tuple, list)):
2346                 values = x
2347 
2348                 if len(values) > len(f.gens):
2349                     raise ValueError("too many values provided")
2350 
2351                 for gen, value in zip(f.gens, values):
2352                     f = f.eval(gen, value)
2353 
2354                 return f
2355             else:
2356                 j, a = 0, x
2357         else:
2358             j = f._gen_to_level(x)
2359 
2360         if not hasattr(f.rep, 'eval'):  # pragma: no cover
2361             raise OperationNotSupported(f, 'eval')
2362 
2363         try:
2364             result = f.rep.eval(a, j)
2365         except CoercionFailed:
2366             if not auto:
2367                 raise DomainError("can't evaluate at %s in %s" % (a, f.rep.dom))
2368             else:
2369                 a_domain, [a] = construct_domain([a])
2370                 new_domain = f.get_domain().unify_with_symbols(a_domain, f.gens)
2371 
2372                 f = f.set_domain(new_domain)
2373                 a = new_domain.convert(a, a_domain)
2374 
2375                 result = f.rep.eval(a, j)
2376 
2377         return f.per(result, remove=j)

2613     def dispersionset(f, g=None):
2614         r"""Compute the *dispersion set* of two polynomials.
2615 
2616         For two polynomials `f(x)` and `g(x)` with `\deg f > 0`
2617         and `\deg g > 0` the dispersion set `\operatorname{J}(f, g)` is defined as:
2618 
2619         .. math::
2620             \operatorname{J}(f, g)
2621             & := \{a \in \mathbb{N}_0 | \gcd(f(x), g(x+a)) \neq 1\} \\
2622             &  = \{a \in \mathbb{N}_0 | \deg \gcd(f(x), g(x+a)) \geq 1\}
2623 
2624         For a single polynomial one defines `\operatorname{J}(f) := \operatorname{J}(f, f)`.
2625 
2626         Examples
2627         ========
2628 
2629         >>> from sympy import poly
2630         >>> from sympy.polys.dispersion import dispersion, dispersionset
2631         >>> from sympy.abc import x
2632 
2633         Dispersion set and dispersion of a simple polynomial:
2634 
2635         >>> fp = poly((x - 3)*(x + 3), x)
2636         >>> sorted(dispersionset(fp))
2637         [0, 6]
2638         >>> dispersion(fp)
2639         6
2640 
2641         Note that the definition of the dispersion is not symmetric:
2642 
2643         >>> fp = poly(x**4 - 3*x**2 + 1, x)
2644         >>> gp = fp.shift(-3)
2645         >>> sorted(dispersionset(fp, gp))
2646         [2, 3, 4]
2647         >>> dispersion(fp, gp)
2648         4
2649         >>> sorted(dispersionset(gp, fp))
2650         []
2651         >>> dispersion(gp, fp)
2652         -oo
2653 
2654         Computing the dispersion also works over field extensions:
2655 
2656         >>> from sympy import sqrt
2657         >>> fp = poly(x**2 + sqrt(5)*x - 1, x, domain='QQ<sqrt(5)>')
2658         >>> gp = poly(x**2 + (2 + sqrt(5))*x + sqrt(5), x, domain='QQ<sqrt(5)>')
2659         >>> sorted(dispersionset(fp, gp))
2660         [2]
2661         >>> sorted(dispersionset(gp, fp))
2662         [1, 4]
2663 
2664         We can even perform the computations for polynomials
2665         having symbolic coefficients:
2666 
2667         >>> from sympy.abc import a
2668         >>> fp = poly(4*x**4 + (4*a + 8)*x**3 + (a**2 + 6*a + 4)*x**2 + (a**2 + 2*a)*x, x)
2669         >>> sorted(dispersionset(fp))
2670         [0, 1]
2671 
2672         See Also
2673         ========
2674 
2675         dispersion
2676 
2677         References
2678         ==========
2679 
2680         1. [ManWright94]_
2681         2. [Koepf98]_
2682         3. [Abramov71]_
2683         4. [Man93]_
2684         """
2685         from sympy.polys.dispersion import dispersionset
2686         return dispersionset(f, g)
2687 
2688     def dispersion(f, g=None):
2689         r"""Compute the *dispersion* of polynomials.
2690 
2691         For two polynomials `f(x)` and `g(x)` with `\deg f > 0`
2692         and `\deg g > 0` the dispersion `\operatorname{dis}(f, g)` is defined as:
2693 
2694         .. math::
2695             \operatorname{dis}(f, g)
2696             & := \max\{ J(f,g) \cup \{0\} \} \\
2697             &  = \max\{ \{a \in \mathbb{N} | \gcd(f(x), g(x+a)) \neq 1\} \cup \{0\} \}
2698 
2699         and for a single polynomial `\operatorname{dis}(f) := \operatorname{dis}(f, f)`.

2701         Examples
2702         ========
2703 
2704         >>> from sympy import poly
2705         >>> from sympy.polys.dispersion import dispersion, dispersionset
2706         >>> from sympy.abc import x
2707 
2708         Dispersion set and dispersion of a simple polynomial:
2709 
2710         >>> fp = poly((x - 3)*(x + 3), x)
2711         >>> sorted(dispersionset(fp))
2712         [0, 6]
2713         >>> dispersion(fp)
2714         6

2717 
2718         >>> fp = poly(x**4 - 3*x**2 + 1, x)
2719         >>> gp = fp.shift(-3)
2720         >>> sorted(dispersionset(fp, gp))
2721         [2, 3, 4]
2722         >>> dispersion(fp, gp)

2724         >>> sorted(dispersionset(gp, fp))
2725         []

2734         >>> sorted(dispersionset(fp, gp))

2736         >>> sorted(dispersionset(gp, fp))

2743         >>> fp = poly(4*x**4 + (4*a + 8)*x**3 + (a**2 + 6*a + 4)*x**2 + (a**2 + 2*a)*x, x)
2744         >>> sorted(dispersionset(fp))

2758         4. [Man93]_

2760         from sympy.polys.dispersion import dispersion

3288            2. Alkiviadis G. Akritas, Adam W. Strzebonski and Panagiotis S. Vigklas: Improving the
3289            Performance of the Continued Fractions Method Using new Bounds of Positive Roots. Nonlinear
3290            Analysis: Modelling and Control, Vol. 13, No. 3, 265-279, 2008.

3293         ========

3295         >>> from sympy import Poly
3296         >>> from sympy.abc import x

3298         >>> Poly(x**2 - 3, x).intervals()
3299         [((-2, -1), 1), ((1, 2), 1)]

3305             eps = QQ.convert(eps)
3306

3309 
3310         if inf is not None:

3325

3331                 return (QQ.to_sympy(u) + I*QQ.to_sympy(v),

3333

3391     def count_roots(f, inf=None, sup=None):

3428                 re, im = sup.as_real_imag()
