64 def sqrt(arg, evaluate=None):
65     """The square root function
66 
67     sqrt(x) -> Returns the principal square root of x.
68 
69     The parameter evaluate determines if the expression should be evaluated.
70     If None, its value is taken from global_evaluate
71 
72     Examples
73     ========
74 
75     >>> from sympy import sqrt, Symbol
76     >>> x = Symbol('x')
77 
78     >>> sqrt(x)
79     sqrt(x)
80 
81     >>> sqrt(x)**2
82     x
83 
84     Note that sqrt(x**2) does not simplify to x.
85 
86     >>> sqrt(x**2)
87     sqrt(x**2)
88 
89     This is because the two are not equal to each other in general.
90     For example, consider x == -1:
91 
92     >>> from sympy import Eq
93     >>> Eq(sqrt(x**2), x).subs(x, -1)
94     False
95 
96     This is because sqrt computes the principal square root, so the square may
97     put the argument in a different branch.  This identity does hold if x is
98     positive:
99 
100     >>> y = Symbol('y', positive=True)
101     >>> sqrt(y**2)
102     y
103 
104     You can force this simplification by using the powdenest() function with
105     the force option set to True:
106 
107     >>> from sympy import powdenest
108     >>> sqrt(x**2)
109     sqrt(x**2)
110     >>> powdenest(sqrt(x**2), force=True)
111     x
112 
113     To get both branches of the square root you can use the rootof function:
114 
115     >>> from sympy import rootof
116 
117     >>> [rootof(x**2-3,i) for i in (0,1)]
118     [-sqrt(3), sqrt(3)]
119 
120     See Also
121     ========
122 
123     sympy.polys.rootoftools.rootof, root, real_root
124 
125     References
126     ==========
127 
128     .. [1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_root
129     .. [2] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_value
130     """
131     # arg = sympify(arg) is handled by Pow
132     return Pow(arg, S.Half, evaluate=evaluate)

178     References

188 def root(arg, n, k=0, evaluate=None):
189     """root(x, n, k) -> Returns the k-th n-th root of x, defaulting to the
190     principal root (k=0).
191 
192     The parameter evaluate determines if the expression should be evaluated.
193     If None, its value is taken from global_evaluate.
194 
195     Examples
196     ========
197 
198     >>> from sympy import root, Rational
199     >>> from sympy.abc import x, n
200 
201     >>> root(x, 2)
202     sqrt(x)
203 
204     >>> root(x, 3)
205     x**(1/3)
206 
207     >>> root(x, n)
208     x**(1/n)
209 
210     >>> root(x, -Rational(2, 3))
211     x**(-3/2)
212 
213     To get the k-th n-th root, specify k:
214 
215     >>> root(-2, 3, 2)
216     -(-1)**(2/3)*2**(1/3)
217 
218     To get all n n-th roots you can use the rootof function.
219     The following examples show the roots of unity for n
220     equal 2, 3 and 4:
221 
222     >>> from sympy import rootof, I
223 
224     >>> [rootof(x**2 - 1, i) for i in range(2)]
225     [-1, 1]
226 
227     >>> [rootof(x**3 - 1,i) for i in range(3)]
228     [1, -1/2 - sqrt(3)*I/2, -1/2 + sqrt(3)*I/2]
229 
230     >>> [rootof(x**4 - 1,i) for i in range(4)]
231     [-1, 1, -I, I]
232 
233     SymPy, like other symbolic algebra systems, returns the
234     complex root of negative numbers. This is the principal
235     root and differs from the text-book result that one might
236     be expecting. For example, the cube root of -8 does not
237     come back as -2:
238 
239     >>> root(-8, 3)
240     2*(-1)**(1/3)
241 
242     The real_root function can be used to either make the principal
243     result real (or simply to return the real root directly):
244 
245     >>> from sympy import real_root
246     >>> real_root(_)
247     -2
248     >>> real_root(-32, 5)
249     -2
250 
251     Alternatively, the n//2-th n-th root of a negative number can be
252     computed with root:
253 
254     >>> root(-32, 5, 5//2)
255     -2
256 
257     See Also
258     ========
259 
260     sympy.polys.rootoftools.rootof
261     sympy.core.power.integer_nthroot
262     sqrt, real_root
263 
264     References
265     ==========
266 
267     * https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_root
268     * https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_root
269     * https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root_of_unity
270     * https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_value
271     * http://mathworld.wolfram.com/CubeRoot.html
272 
273     """
274     n = sympify(n)
275     if k:
276         return Mul(Pow(arg, S.One/n, evaluate=evaluate), S.NegativeOne**(2*k/n), evaluate=evaluate)
277     return Pow(arg, 1/n, evaluate=evaluate)

280 def real_root(arg, n=None, evaluate=None):
281     """Return the real nth-root of arg if possible. If n is omitted then
282     all instances of (-n)**(1/odd) will be changed to -n**(1/odd); this
283     will only create a real root of a principal root -- the presence of
284     other factors may cause the result to not be real.
285 
286     The parameter evaluate determines if the expression should be evaluated.
287     If None, its value is taken from global_evaluate.
288 
289     Examples
290     ========
291 
292     >>> from sympy import root, real_root, Rational
293     >>> from sympy.abc import x, n
294 
295     >>> real_root(-8, 3)
296     -2
297     >>> root(-8, 3)
298     2*(-1)**(1/3)
299     >>> real_root(_)
300     -2
301 
302     If one creates a non-principal root and applies real_root, the
303     result will not be real (so use with caution):
304 
305     >>> root(-8, 3, 2)
306     -2*(-1)**(2/3)
307     >>> real_root(_)
308     -2*(-1)**(2/3)
309 
310 
311     See Also
312     ========
313 
314     sympy.polys.rootoftools.rootof
315     sympy.core.power.integer_nthroot
316     root, sqrt
317     """
318     from sympy.functions.elementary.complexes import Abs, im, sign
319     from sympy.functions.elementary.piecewise import Piecewise
320     if n is not None:
321         return Piecewise(
322             (root(arg, n, evaluate=evaluate), Or(Eq(n, S.One), Eq(n, S.NegativeOne))),
323             (Mul(sign(arg), root(Abs(arg), n, evaluate=evaluate), evaluate=evaluate),
324             And(Eq(im(arg), S.Zero), Eq(Mod(n, 2), S.One))),
325             (root(arg, n, evaluate=evaluate), True))
326     rv = sympify(arg)
327     n1pow = Transform(lambda x: -(-x.base)**x.exp,
328                       lambda x:
329                       x.is_Pow and
330                       x.base.is_negative and
331                       x.exp.is_Rational and
332                       x.exp.p == 1 and x.exp.q % 2)
333     return rv.xreplace(n1pow)

340 class MinMaxBase(Expr, LatticeOp):
341     def __new__(cls, *args, **assumptions):
342         if not args:
343             raise ValueError("The Max/Min functions must have arguments.")
344 
345         args = (sympify(arg) for arg in args)
346 
347         # first standard filter, for cls.zero and cls.identity
348         # also reshape Max(a, Max(b, c)) to Max(a, b, c)
349         try:
350             args = frozenset(cls._new_args_filter(args))
351         except ShortCircuit:
352             return cls.zero
353 
354         if assumptions.pop('evaluate', True):
355             # remove redundant args that are easily identified
356             args = cls._collapse_arguments(args, **assumptions)
357 
358         # find local zeros
359         args = cls._find_localzeros(args, **assumptions)
360 
361         if not args:
362             return cls.identity
363 
364         if len(args) == 1:
365             return list(args).pop()
366 
367         # base creation
368         _args = frozenset(args)
369         obj = Expr.__new__(cls, _args, **assumptions)
370         obj._argset = _args

373     @classmethod
374     def _collapse_arguments(cls, args, **assumptions):
375         """Remove redundant args.
376 
377         Examples
378         ========
379 
380         >>> from sympy import Min, Max
381         >>> from sympy.abc import a, b, c, d, e
382 
383         Any arg in parent that appears in any
384         parent-like function in any of the flat args
385         of parent can be removed from that sub-arg:
386 
387         >>> Min(a, Max(b, Min(a, c, d)))
388         Min(a, Max(b, Min(c, d)))
389 
390         If the arg of parent appears in an opposite-than parent
391         function in any of the flat args of parent that function
392         can be replaced with the arg:
393 
394         >>> Min(a, Max(b, Min(c, d, Max(a, e))))
395         Min(a, Max(b, Min(a, c, d)))
396 
397         """
398         from sympy.utilities.iterables import ordered
399         from sympy.utilities.iterables import sift
400         from sympy.simplify.simplify import walk
401 
402         if not args:
403             return args
404         args = list(ordered(args))
405         if cls == Min:
406             other = Max
407         else:
408             other = Min
409 
410         # find global comparable max of Max and min of Min if a new
411         # value is being introduced in these args at position 0 of
412         # the ordered args
413         if args[0].is_number:
414             sifted = mins, maxs = [], []
415             for i in args:
416                 for v in walk(i, Min, Max):
417                     if v.args[0].is_comparable:
418                         sifted[isinstance(v, Max)].append(v)
419             small = Min.identity
420             for i in mins:
421                 v = i.args[0]
422                 if v.is_number and (v < small) == True:
423                     small = v
424             big = Max.identity
425             for i in maxs:
426                 v = i.args[0]
427                 if v.is_number and (v > big) == True:
428                     big = v
429             # at the point when this function is called from __new__,
430             # there may be more than one numeric arg present since
431             # local zeros have not been handled yet, so look through
432             # more than the first arg
433             if cls == Min:
434                 for i in range(len(args)):
435                     if not args[i].is_number:
436                         break
437                     if (args[i] < small) == True:
438                         small = args[i]
439             elif cls == Max:
440                 for i in range(len(args)):
441                     if not args[i].is_number:
442                         break
443                     if (args[i] > big) == True:
444                         big = args[i]
445             T = None
446             if cls == Min:
447                 if small != Min.identity:
448                     other = Max
449                     T = small
450             elif big != Max.identity:
451                 other = Min
452                 T = big
453             if T is not None:
454                 # remove numerical redundancy
455                 for i in range(len(args)):
456                     a = args[i]
457                     if isinstance(a, other):
458                         a0 = a.args[0]
459                         if ((a0 > T) if other == Max else (a0 < T)) == True:
460                             args[i] = cls.identity
461 
462         # remove redundant symbolic args
463         def do(ai, a):
464             if not isinstance(ai, (Min, Max)):
465                 return ai
466             cond = a in ai.args
467             if not cond:
468                 return ai.func(*[do(i, a) for i in ai.args],
469                     evaluate=False)
470             if isinstance(ai, cls):
471                 return ai.func(*[do(i, a) for i in ai.args if i != a],
472                     evaluate=False)
473             return a
474         for i, a in enumerate(args):
475             args[i + 1:] = [do(ai, a) for ai in args[i + 1:]]
476 
477         # factor out common elements as for
478         # Min(Max(x, y), Max(x, z)) -> Max(x, Min(y, z))
479         # and vice versa when swapping Min/Max -- do this only for the
480         # easy case where all functions contain something in common;
481         # trying to find some optimal subset of args to modify takes
482         # too long
483         if len(args) > 1:
484             common = None
485             remove = []
486             sets = []
487             for i in range(len(args)):
488                 a = args[i]
489                 if not isinstance(a, other):
490                     continue
491                 s = set(a.args)
492                 common = s if common is None else (common & s)
493                 if not common:
494                     break
495                 sets.append(s)
496                 remove.append(i)
497             if common:
498                 sets = filter(None, [s - common for s in sets])
499                 sets = [other(*s, evaluate=False) for s in sets]
500                 for i in reversed(remove):
501                     args.pop(i)
502                 oargs = [cls(*sets)] if sets else []
503                 oargs.extend(common)
504                 args.append(other(*oargs, evaluate=False))
505 
506         return args

509     def _new_args_filter(cls, arg_sequence):
510         """
511         Generator filtering args.
512 
513         first standard filter, for cls.zero and cls.identity.
514         Also reshape Max(a, Max(b, c)) to Max(a, b, c),
515         and check arguments for comparability
516         """
517         for arg in arg_sequence:
518 
519             # pre-filter, checking comparability of arguments
520             if not isinstance(arg, Expr) or arg.is_real is False or (
521                     arg.is_number and
522                     not arg.is_comparable):
523                 raise ValueError("The argument '%s' is not comparable." % arg)
524 
525             if arg == cls.zero:
526                 raise ShortCircuit(arg)
527             elif arg == cls.identity:
528                 continue
529             elif arg.func == cls:
530                 for x in arg.args:
531                     yield x
532             else:
533                 yield arg

535     @classmethod
536     def _find_localzeros(cls, values, **options):
537         """
538         Sequentially allocate values to localzeros.
539 
540         When a value is identified as being more extreme than another member it
541         replaces that member; if this is never true, then the value is simply
542         appended to the localzeros.
543         """
544         localzeros = set()
545         for v in values:
546             is_newzero = True
547             localzeros_ = list(localzeros)
548             for z in localzeros_:
549                 if id(v) == id(z):
550                     is_newzero = False
551                 else:
552                     con = cls._is_connected(v, z)
553                     if con:
554                         is_newzero = False
555                         if con is True or con == cls:
556                             localzeros.remove(z)
557                             localzeros.update([v])
558             if is_newzero:
559                 localzeros.update([v])
560         return localzeros

645 class Max(MinMaxBase, Application):
646     """
647     Return, if possible, the maximum value of the list.
648 
649     When number of arguments is equal one, then
650     return this argument.
651 
652     When number of arguments is equal two, then
653     return, if possible, the value from (a, b) that is >= the other.
654 
655     In common case, when the length of list greater than 2, the task
656     is more complicated. Return only the arguments, which are greater
657     than others, if it is possible to determine directional relation.
658 
659     If is not possible to determine such a relation, return a partially
660     evaluated result.
661 
662     Assumptions are used to make the decision too.
663 
664     Also, only comparable arguments are permitted.
665 
666     It is named ``Max`` and not ``max`` to avoid conflicts
667     with the built-in function ``max``.
668 
669 
670     Examples
671     ========
672 
673     >>> from sympy import Max, Symbol, oo
674     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
675     >>> p = Symbol('p', positive=True)
676     >>> n = Symbol('n', negative=True)
677 
678     >>> Max(x, -2)                  #doctest: +SKIP
679     Max(x, -2)
680     >>> Max(x, -2).subs(x, 3)
681     3
682     >>> Max(p, -2)
683     p
684     >>> Max(x, y)
685     Max(x, y)
686     >>> Max(x, y) == Max(y, x)
687     True
688     >>> Max(x, Max(y, z))           #doctest: +SKIP
689     Max(x, y, z)
690     >>> Max(n, 8, p, 7, -oo)        #doctest: +SKIP
691     Max(8, p)
692     >>> Max (1, x, oo)
693     oo
694 
695     * Algorithm
696 
697     The task can be considered as searching of supremums in the
698     directed complete partial orders [1]_.
699 
700     The source values are sequentially allocated by the isolated subsets
701     in which supremums are searched and result as Max arguments.
702 
703     If the resulted supremum is single, then it is returned.
704 
705     The isolated subsets are the sets of values which are only the comparable
706     with each other in the current set. E.g. natural numbers are comparable with
707     each other, but not comparable with the `x` symbol. Another example: the
708     symbol `x` with negative assumption is comparable with a natural number.
709 
710     Also there are "least" elements, which are comparable with all others,
711     and have a zero property (maximum or minimum for all elements). E.g. `oo`.
712     In case of it the allocation operation is terminated and only this value is
713     returned.
714 
715     Assumption:
716        - if A > B > C then A > C
717        - if A == B then B can be removed
718 
719     References
720     ==========
721 
722     .. [1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directed_complete_partial_order
723     .. [2] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lattice_%28order%29
724 
725     See Also
726     ========
727 
728     Min : find minimum values
729     """

731     identity = S.NegativeInfinity

24 def _unevaluated_Add(*args):
25     """Return a well-formed unevaluated Add: Numbers are collected and
26     put in slot 0 and args are sorted. Use this when args have changed
27     but you still want to return an unevaluated Add.
28 
29     Examples
30     ========
31 
32     >>> from sympy.core.add import _unevaluated_Add as uAdd
33     >>> from sympy import S, Add
34     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
35     >>> a = uAdd(*[S(1.0), x, S(2)])
36     >>> a.args[0]
37     3.00000000000000
38     >>> a.args[1]
39     x
40 
41     Beyond the Number being in slot 0, there is no other assurance of
42     order for the arguments since they are hash sorted. So, for testing
43     purposes, output produced by this in some other function can only
44     be tested against the output of this function or as one of several
45     options:
46 
47     >>> opts = (Add(x, y, evaluated=False), Add(y, x, evaluated=False))
48     >>> a = uAdd(x, y)
49     >>> assert a in opts and a == uAdd(x, y)
50     >>> uAdd(x + 1, x + 2)
51     x + x + 3
52     """
53     args = list(args)
54     newargs = []
55     co = S.Zero
56     while args:
57         a = args.pop()
58         if a.is_Add:
59             # this will keep nesting from building up
60             # so that x + (x + 1) -> x + x + 1 (3 args)
61             args.extend(a.args)
62         elif a.is_Number:
63             co += a
64         else:
65             newargs.append(a)
66     _addsort(newargs)
67     if co:
68         newargs.insert(0, co)
69     return Add._from_args(newargs)

78     @classmethod
79     def flatten(cls, seq):
80         """
81         Takes the sequence "seq" of nested Adds and returns a flatten list.
82 
83         Returns: (commutative_part, noncommutative_part, order_symbols)
84 
85         Applies associativity, all terms are commutable with respect to
86         addition.
87 
88         NB: the removal of 0 is already handled by AssocOp.__new__
89 
90         See also
91         ========
92 
93         sympy.core.mul.Mul.flatten
94 
95         """
96         from sympy.calculus.util import AccumBounds
97         from sympy.matrices.expressions import MatrixExpr
98         from sympy.tensor.tensor import TensExpr
99         rv = None
100         if len(seq) == 2:
101             a, b = seq
102             if b.is_Rational:
103                 a, b = b, a
104             if a.is_Rational:
105                 if b.is_Mul:
106                     rv = [a, b], [], None
107             if rv:
108                 if all(s.is_commutative for s in rv[0]):
109                     return rv
110                 return [], rv[0], None
111 
112         terms = {}      # term -> coeff
113                         # e.g. x**2 -> 5   for ... + 5*x**2 + ...
114 
115         coeff = S.Zero  # coefficient (Number or zoo) to always be in slot 0
116                         # e.g. 3 + ...
117         order_factors = []
118 
119         for o in seq:
120 
121             # O(x)
122             if o.is_Order:
123                 for o1 in order_factors:
124                     if o1.contains(o):
125                         o = None
126                         break
127                 if o is None:
128                     continue
129                 order_factors = [o] + [
130                     o1 for o1 in order_factors if not o.contains(o1)]
131                 continue
132 
133             # 3 or NaN
134             elif o.is_Number:
135                 if (o is S.NaN or coeff is S.ComplexInfinity and
136                         o.is_finite is False):
137                     # we know for sure the result will be nan
138                     return [S.NaN], [], None
139                 if coeff.is_Number:
140                     coeff += o
141                     if coeff is S.NaN:
142                         # we know for sure the result will be nan
143                         return [S.NaN], [], None
144                 continue
145 
146             elif isinstance(o, AccumBounds):
147                 coeff = o.__add__(coeff)
148                 continue
149 
150             elif isinstance(o, MatrixExpr):
151                 # can't add 0 to Matrix so make sure coeff is not 0
152                 coeff = o.__add__(coeff) if coeff else o
153                 continue
154 
155             elif isinstance(o, TensExpr):
156                 coeff = o.__add__(coeff) if coeff else o
157                 continue
158 
159             elif o is S.ComplexInfinity:
160                 if coeff.is_finite is False:
161                     # we know for sure the result will be nan
162                     return [S.NaN], [], None
163                 coeff = S.ComplexInfinity
164                 continue
165 
166             # Add([...])
167             elif o.is_Add:
168                 # NB: here we assume Add is always commutative
169                 seq.extend(o.args)  # TODO zerocopy?
170                 continue
171 
172             # Mul([...])
173             elif o.is_Mul:
174                 c, s = o.as_coeff_Mul()
175 
176             # check for unevaluated Pow, e.g. 2**3 or 2**(-1/2)
177             elif o.is_Pow:
178                 b, e = o.as_base_exp()
179                 if b.is_Number and (e.is_Integer or
180                                    (e.is_Rational and e.is_negative)):
181                     seq.append(b**e)
182                     continue
183                 c, s = S.One, o
184 
185             else:
186                 # everything else
187                 c = S.One
188                 s = o
189 
190             # now we have:
191             # o = c*s, where
192             #
193             # c is a Number
194             # s is an expression with number factor extracted
195             # let's collect terms with the same s, so e.g.
196             # 2*x**2 + 3*x**2  ->  5*x**2
197             if s in terms:
198                 terms[s] += c
199                 if terms[s] is S.NaN:
200                     # we know for sure the result will be nan
201                     return [S.NaN], [], None
202             else:
203                 terms[s] = c
204 
205         # now let's construct new args:
206         # [2*x**2, x**3, 7*x**4, pi, ...]
207         newseq = []
208         noncommutative = False
209         for s, c in terms.items():
210             # 0*s
211             if c is S.Zero:
212                 continue
213             # 1*s
214             elif c is S.One:
215                 newseq.append(s)
216             # c*s
217             else:
218                 if s.is_Mul:
219                     # Mul, already keeps its arguments in perfect order.
220                     # so we can simply put c in slot0 and go the fast way.
221                     cs = s._new_rawargs(*((c,) + s.args))
222                     newseq.append(cs)
223                 elif s.is_Add:
224                     # we just re-create the unevaluated Mul
225                     newseq.append(Mul(c, s, evaluate=False))
226                 else:
227                     # alternatively we have to call all Mul's machinery (slow)
228                     newseq.append(Mul(c, s))
229 
230             noncommutative = noncommutative or not s.is_commutative
231 
232         # oo, -oo
233         if coeff is S.Infinity:
234             newseq = [f for f in newseq if not
235                       (f.is_nonnegative or f.is_real and f.is_finite)]
236 
237         elif coeff is S.NegativeInfinity:
238             newseq = [f for f in newseq if not
239                       (f.is_nonpositive or f.is_real and f.is_finite)]
240 
241         if coeff is S.ComplexInfinity:
242             # zoo might be
243             #   infinite_real + finite_im
244             #   finite_real + infinite_im
245             #   infinite_real + infinite_im
246             # addition of a finite real or imaginary number won't be able to
247             # change the zoo nature; adding an infinite qualtity would result
248             # in a NaN condition if it had sign opposite of the infinite
249             # portion of zoo, e.g., infinite_real - infinite_real.
250             newseq = [c for c in newseq if not (c.is_finite and
251                                                 c.is_real is not None)]
252 
253         # process O(x)
254         if order_factors:
255             newseq2 = []
256             for t in newseq:
257                 for o in order_factors:
258                     # x + O(x) -> O(x)
259                     if o.contains(t):
260                         t = None
261                         break
262                 # x + O(x**2) -> x + O(x**2)
263                 if t is not None:
264                     newseq2.append(t)
265             newseq = newseq2 + order_factors
266             # 1 + O(1) -> O(1)
267             for o in order_factors:
268                 if o.contains(coeff):
269                     coeff = S.Zero
270                     break
271 
272         # order args canonically
273         _addsort(newseq)
274 
275         # current code expects coeff to be first
276         if coeff is not S.Zero:
277             newseq.insert(0, coeff)
278 
279         # we are done
280         if noncommutative:
281             return [], newseq, None
282         else:
283             return newseq, [], None

290     def as_coefficients_dict(a):
291         """Return a dictionary mapping terms to their Rational coefficient.
292         Since the dictionary is a defaultdict, inquiries about terms which
293         were not present will return a coefficient of 0. If an expression is
294         not an Add it is considered to have a single term.
295 
296         Examples
297         ========
298 
299         >>> from sympy.abc import a, x
300         >>> (3*x + a*x + 4).as_coefficients_dict()
301         {1: 4, x: 3, a*x: 1}
302         >>> _[a]
303         0
304         >>> (3*a*x).as_coefficients_dict()
305         {a*x: 3}
306         """
307 
308         d = defaultdict(list)
309         for ai in a.args:
310             c, m = ai.as_coeff_Mul()
311             d[m].append(c)
312         for k, v in d.items():
313             if len(v) == 1:
314                 d[k] = v[0]
315             else:
316                 d[k] = Add(*v)
317         di = defaultdict(int)
318         di.update(d)
319         return di

321     @cacheit
322     def as_coeff_add(self, *deps):
323         """
324         Returns a tuple (coeff, args) where self is treated as an Add and coeff
325         is the Number term and args is a tuple of all other terms.
326 
327         Examples
328         ========
329 
330         >>> from sympy.abc import x
331         >>> (7 + 3*x).as_coeff_add()
332         (7, (3*x,))
333         >>> (7*x).as_coeff_add()
334         (0, (7*x,))
335         """
336         if deps:
337             l1 = []
338             l2 = []
339             for f in self.args:
340                 if f.has(*deps):
341                     l2.append(f)
342                 else:
343                     l1.append(f)
344             return self._new_rawargs(*l1), tuple(l2)
345         coeff, notrat = self.args[0].as_coeff_add()
346         if coeff is not S.Zero:
347             return coeff, notrat + self.args[1:]
348         return S.Zero, self.args

362     def _eval_power(self, e):
363         if e.is_Rational and self.is_number:
364             from sympy.core.evalf import pure_complex
365             from sympy.core.mul import _unevaluated_Mul
366             from sympy.core.exprtools import factor_terms
367             from sympy.core.function import expand_multinomial
368             from sympy.functions.elementary.complexes import sign
369             from sympy.functions.elementary.miscellaneous import sqrt
370             ri = pure_complex(self)
371             if ri:
372                 r, i = ri
373                 if e.q == 2:
374                     D = sqrt(r**2 + i**2)
375                     if D.is_Rational:
376                         # (r, i, D) is a Pythagorean triple
377                         root = sqrt(factor_terms((D - r)/2))**e.p
378                         return root*expand_multinomial((
379                             # principle value
380                             (D + r)/abs(i) + sign(i)*S.ImaginaryUnit)**e.p)
381                 elif e == -1:
382                     return _unevaluated_Mul(
383                         r - i*S.ImaginaryUnit,
384                         1/(r**2 + i**2))

405     def _combine_inverse(lhs, rhs):
406         """
407         Returns lhs - rhs, but treats oo like a symbol so oo - oo
408         returns 0, instead of a nan.
409         """
410         from sympy.core.function import expand_mul
411         from sympy.core.symbol import Dummy
412         inf = (S.Infinity, S.NegativeInfinity)
413         if lhs.has(*inf) or rhs.has(*inf):
414             oo = Dummy('oo')
415             reps = {
416                 S.Infinity: oo,
417                 S.NegativeInfinity: -oo}
418             ireps = dict([(v, k) for k, v in reps.items()])
419             eq = expand_mul(lhs.xreplace(reps) - rhs.xreplace(reps))
420             if eq.has(oo):
421                 eq = eq.replace(
422                     lambda x: x.is_Pow and x.base == oo,
423                     lambda x: x.base)
424             return eq.xreplace(ireps)
425         else:
426             return expand_mul(lhs - rhs)

432         This is the most efficient way to get the head and tail of an

448     def as_numer_denom(self):
449 
450         # clear rational denominator
451         content, expr = self.primitive()
452         ncon, dcon = content.as_numer_denom()
453 
454         # collect numerators and denominators of the terms
455         nd = defaultdict(list)
456         for f in expr.args:
457             ni, di = f.as_numer_denom()
458             nd[di].append(ni)
459 
460         # check for quick exit
461         if len(nd) == 1:
462             d, n = nd.popitem()
463             return self.func(
464                 *[_keep_coeff(ncon, ni) for ni in n]), _keep_coeff(dcon, d)
465 
466         # sum up the terms having a common denominator
467         for d, n in nd.items():
468             if len(n) == 1:
469                 nd[d] = n[0]
470             else:
471                 nd[d] = self.func(*n)
472 
473         # assemble single numerator and denominator
474         denoms, numers = [list(i) for i in zip(*iter(nd.items()))]
475         n, d = self.func(*[Mul(*(denoms[:i] + [numers[i]] + denoms[i + 1:]))
476                    for i in range(len(numers))]), Mul(*denoms)
477 
478         return _keep_coeff(ncon, n), _keep_coeff(dcon, d)

509     def _eval_is_imaginary(self):
510         nz = []
511         im_I = []
512         for a in self.args:
513             if a.is_real:
514                 if a.is_zero:
515                     pass
516                 elif a.is_zero is False:
517                     nz.append(a)
518                 else:
519                     return
520             elif a.is_imaginary:
521                 im_I.append(a*S.ImaginaryUnit)
522             elif (S.ImaginaryUnit*a).is_real:
523                 im_I.append(a*S.ImaginaryUnit)
524             else:
525                 return
526         b = self.func(*nz)
527         if b.is_zero:
528             return fuzzy_not(self.func(*im_I).is_zero)
529         elif b.is_zero is False:
530             return False

532     def _eval_is_zero(self):
533         if self.is_commutative is False:
534             # issue 10528: there is no way to know if a nc symbol
535             # is zero or not
536             return
537         nz = []
538         z = 0
539         im_or_z = False
540         im = False
541         for a in self.args:
542             if a.is_real:
543                 if a.is_zero:
544                     z += 1
545                 elif a.is_zero is False:
546                     nz.append(a)
547                 else:
548                     return
549             elif a.is_imaginary:
550                 im = True
551             elif (S.ImaginaryUnit*a).is_real:
552                 im_or_z = True
553             else:
554                 return
555         if z == len(self.args):
556             return True
557         if len(nz) == len(self.args):
558             return None
559         b = self.func(*nz)
560         if b.is_zero:
561             if not im_or_z and not im:
562                 return True
563             if im and not im_or_z:
564                 return False
565         if b.is_zero is False:
566             return False

588     def _eval_is_positive(self):
589         from sympy.core.exprtools import _monotonic_sign
590         if self.is_number:
591             return super(Add, self)._eval_is_positive()
592         c, a = self.as_coeff_Add()
593         if not c.is_zero:
594             v = _monotonic_sign(a)
595             if v is not None:
596                 s = v + c
597                 if s != self and s.is_positive and a.is_nonnegative:
598                     return True
599                 if len(self.free_symbols) == 1:
600                     v = _monotonic_sign(self)
601                     if v is not None and v != self and v.is_positive:
602                         return True
603         pos = nonneg = nonpos = unknown_sign = False
604         saw_INF = set()
605         args = [a for a in self.args if not a.is_zero]
606         if not args:
607             return False
608         for a in args:
609             ispos = a.is_positive
610             infinite = a.is_infinite
611             if infinite:
612                 saw_INF.add(fuzzy_or((ispos, a.is_nonnegative)))
613                 if True in saw_INF and False in saw_INF:
614                     return
615             if ispos:
616                 pos = True
617                 continue
618             elif a.is_nonnegative:
619                 nonneg = True
620                 continue
621             elif a.is_nonpositive:
622                 nonpos = True
623                 continue
624 
625             if infinite is None:
626                 return
627             unknown_sign = True
628 
629         if saw_INF:
630             if len(saw_INF) > 1:
631                 return
632             return saw_INF.pop()
633         elif unknown_sign:
634             return
635         elif not nonpos and not nonneg and pos:
636             return True
637         elif not nonpos and pos:
638             return True
639         elif not pos and not nonneg:
640             return False
641

672     def _eval_is_negative(self):

674         if self.is_number:
675             return super(Add, self)._eval_is_negative()
676         c, a = self.as_coeff_Add()

679             if v is not None:

691             return False
692         for a in args:

Posify ignores is_finite assmptions
Posify removes a finite assumption from a symbol:
```julia
In [1]: x = Symbol('x', finite=True)                                                                                                           

In [2]: x._assumptions                                                                                                                         
Out[2]: {'finite': True, 'infinite': False, 'commutative': True}

In [3]: x.is_finite                                                                                                                            
Out[3]: True

In [4]: xp, _ = posify(x)                                                                                                                      

In [5]: xp._assumptions                                                                                                                        
Out[5]: 
{'positive': True,
 'real': True,
 'hermitian': True,
 'imaginary': False,
 'negative': False,
 'nonnegative': True,
 'nonzero': True,
 'zero': False,
 'complex': True,
 'nonpositive': False,
 'commutative': True}

In [6]: xp.is_finite                                                                                                                           

In [7]: print(xp.is_finite)                                                                                                                    
None
```
I think that posify should preserve the finiteness assumption. Possibly other assumptions should be preserved as well (integer, rational, prime, even, odd...).

37 def separatevars(expr, symbols=[], dict=False, force=False):
38     """
39     Separates variables in an expression, if possible.  By
40     default, it separates with respect to all symbols in an
41     expression and collects constant coefficients that are
42     independent of symbols.
43 
44     If dict=True then the separated terms will be returned
45     in a dictionary keyed to their corresponding symbols.
46     By default, all symbols in the expression will appear as
47     keys; if symbols are provided, then all those symbols will
48     be used as keys, and any terms in the expression containing
49     other symbols or non-symbols will be returned keyed to the
50     string 'coeff'. (Passing None for symbols will return the
51     expression in a dictionary keyed to 'coeff'.)
52 
53     If force=True, then bases of powers will be separated regardless
54     of assumptions on the symbols involved.
55 
56     Notes
57     =====
58 
59     The order of the factors is determined by Mul, so that the
60     separated expressions may not necessarily be grouped together.
61 
62     Although factoring is necessary to separate variables in some
63     expressions, it is not necessary in all cases, so one should not
64     count on the returned factors being factored.
65 
66     Examples
67     ========
68 
69     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z, alpha
70     >>> from sympy import separatevars, sin
71     >>> separatevars((x*y)**y)
72     (x*y)**y
73     >>> separatevars((x*y)**y, force=True)
74     x**y*y**y
75 
76     >>> e = 2*x**2*z*sin(y)+2*z*x**2
77     >>> separatevars(e)
78     2*x**2*z*(sin(y) + 1)
79     >>> separatevars(e, symbols=(x, y), dict=True)
80     {'coeff': 2*z, x: x**2, y: sin(y) + 1}
81     >>> separatevars(e, [x, y, alpha], dict=True)
82     {'coeff': 2*z, alpha: 1, x: x**2, y: sin(y) + 1}
83 
84     If the expression is not really separable, or is only partially
85     separable, separatevars will do the best it can to separate it
86     by using factoring.
87 
88     >>> separatevars(x + x*y - 3*x**2)
89     -x*(3*x - y - 1)
90 
91     If the expression is not separable then expr is returned unchanged
92     or (if dict=True) then None is returned.
93 
94     >>> eq = 2*x + y*sin(x)
95     >>> separatevars(eq) == eq
96     True
97     >>> separatevars(2*x + y*sin(x), symbols=(x, y), dict=True) == None
98     True
99 
100     """
101     expr = sympify(expr)
102     if dict:
103         return _separatevars_dict(_separatevars(expr, force), symbols)
104     else:
105         return _separatevars(expr, force)
106

108 def _separatevars(expr, force):
109     if len(expr.free_symbols) == 1:
110         return expr
111     # don't destroy a Mul since much of the work may already be done
112     if expr.is_Mul:
113         args = list(expr.args)
114         changed = False
115         for i, a in enumerate(args):
116             args[i] = separatevars(a, force)
117             changed = changed or args[i] != a
118         if changed:
119             expr = expr.func(*args)
120         return expr
121 
122     # get a Pow ready for expansion
123     if expr.is_Pow:
124         expr = Pow(separatevars(expr.base, force=force), expr.exp)
125 
126     # First try other expansion methods
127     expr = expr.expand(mul=False, multinomial=False, force=force)
128 
129     _expr, reps = posify(expr) if force else (expr, {})
130     expr = factor(_expr).subs(reps)
131 
132     if not expr.is_Add:
133         return expr
134 
135     # Find any common coefficients to pull out
136     args = list(expr.args)
137     commonc = args[0].args_cnc(cset=True, warn=False)[0]
138     for i in args[1:]:
139         commonc &= i.args_cnc(cset=True, warn=False)[0]
140     commonc = Mul(*commonc)
141     commonc = commonc.as_coeff_Mul()[1]  # ignore constants
142     commonc_set = commonc.args_cnc(cset=True, warn=False)[0]
143 
144     # remove them
145     for i, a in enumerate(args):
146         c, nc = a.args_cnc(cset=True, warn=False)
147         c = c - commonc_set
148         args[i] = Mul(*c)*Mul(*nc)
149     nonsepar = Add(*args)
150 
151     if len(nonsepar.free_symbols) > 1:
152         _expr = nonsepar
153         _expr, reps = posify(_expr) if force else (_expr, {})
154         _expr = (factor(_expr)).subs(reps)
155 
156         if not _expr.is_Add:
157             nonsepar = _expr
158 
159     return commonc*nonsepar
160

162 def _separatevars_dict(expr, symbols):
163     if symbols:
164         if not all((t.is_Atom for t in symbols)):
165             raise ValueError("symbols must be Atoms.")
166         symbols = list(symbols)
167     elif symbols is None:
168         return {'coeff': expr}
169     else:
170         symbols = list(expr.free_symbols)
171         if not symbols:
172             return None
173 
174     ret = dict(((i, []) for i in symbols + ['coeff']))
175 
176     for i in Mul.make_args(expr):
177         expsym = i.free_symbols
178         intersection = set(symbols).intersection(expsym)
179         if len(intersection) > 1:
180             return None
181         if len(intersection) == 0:
182             # There are no symbols, so it is part of the coefficient
183             ret['coeff'].append(i)
184         else:
185             ret[intersection.pop()].append(i)
186 
187     # rebuild
188     for k, v in ret.items():
189         ret[k] = Mul(*v)
190 
191     return ret
192

202 def posify(eq):
203     """Return eq (with generic symbols made positive) and a
204     dictionary containing the mapping between the old and new
205     symbols.
206 
207     Any symbol that has positive=None will be replaced with a positive dummy
208     symbol having the same name. This replacement will allow more symbolic
209     processing of expressions, especially those involving powers and
210     logarithms.
211 
212     A dictionary that can be sent to subs to restore eq to its original
213     symbols is also returned.
214 
215     >>> from sympy import posify, Symbol, log, solve
216     >>> from sympy.abc import x
217     >>> posify(x + Symbol('p', positive=True) + Symbol('n', negative=True))
218     (_x + n + p, {_x: x})
219 
220     >>> eq = 1/x
221     >>> log(eq).expand()
222     log(1/x)
223     >>> log(posify(eq)[0]).expand()
224     -log(_x)
225     >>> p, rep = posify(eq)
226     >>> log(p).expand().subs(rep)
227     -log(x)
228 
229     It is possible to apply the same transformations to an iterable
230     of expressions:
231 
232     >>> eq = x**2 - 4
233     >>> solve(eq, x)
234     [-2, 2]
235     >>> eq_x, reps = posify([eq, x]); eq_x
236     [_x**2 - 4, _x]
237     >>> solve(*eq_x)
238     [2]
239     """
240     eq = sympify(eq)
241     if iterable(eq):
242         f = type(eq)
243         eq = list(eq)
244         syms = set()
245         for e in eq:
246             syms = syms.union(e.atoms(Symbol))
247         reps = {}
248         for s in syms:
249             reps.update(dict((v, k) for k, v in posify(s)[1].items()))
250         for i, e in enumerate(eq):
251             eq[i] = e.subs(reps)
252         return f(eq), {r: s for s, r in reps.items()}
253 
254     reps = {s: Dummy(s.name, positive=True)
255                  for s in eq.free_symbols if s.is_positive is None}
256     eq = eq.subs(reps)
257     return eq, {r: s for s, r in reps.items()}
258

260 def hypersimp(f, k):
261     """Given combinatorial term f(k) simplify its consecutive term ratio
262        i.e. f(k+1)/f(k).  The input term can be composed of functions and
263        integer sequences which have equivalent representation in terms
264        of gamma special function.
265 
266        The algorithm performs three basic steps:
267 
268        1. Rewrite all functions in terms of gamma, if possible.
269 
270        2. Rewrite all occurrences of gamma in terms of products
271           of gamma and rising factorial with integer,  absolute
272           constant exponent.
273 
274        3. Perform simplification of nested fractions, powers
275           and if the resulting expression is a quotient of
276           polynomials, reduce their total degree.
277 
278        If f(k) is hypergeometric then as result we arrive with a
279        quotient of polynomials of minimal degree. Otherwise None
280        is returned.
281 
282        For more information on the implemented algorithm refer to:
283 
284        1. W. Koepf, Algorithms for m-fold Hypergeometric Summation,
285           Journal of Symbolic Computation (1995) 20, 399-417
286     """
287     f = sympify(f)
288 
289     g = f.subs(k, k + 1) / f
290 
291     g = g.rewrite(gamma)
292     g = expand_func(g)
293     g = powsimp(g, deep=True, combine='exp')
294 
295     if g.is_rational_function(k):
296         return simplify(g, ratio=S.Infinity)
297     else:
298         return None
299

301 def hypersimilar(f, g, k):
302     """Returns True if 'f' and 'g' are hyper-similar.
303 
304        Similarity in hypergeometric sense means that a quotient of
305        f(k) and g(k) is a rational function in k.  This procedure
306        is useful in solving recurrence relations.
307 
308        For more information see hypersimp().
309 
310     """
311     f, g = list(map(sympify, (f, g)))
312 
313     h = (f/g).rewrite(gamma)
314     h = h.expand(func=True, basic=False)
315 
316     return h.is_rational_function(k)

319 def signsimp(expr, evaluate=None):
320     """Make all Add sub-expressions canonical wrt sign.
321 
322     If an Add subexpression, ``a``, can have a sign extracted,
323     as determined by could_extract_minus_sign, it is replaced
324     with Mul(-1, a, evaluate=False). This allows signs to be
325     extracted from powers and products.
326 
327     Examples
328     ========
329 
330     >>> from sympy import signsimp, exp, symbols
331     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
332     >>> i = symbols('i', odd=True)
333     >>> n = -1 + 1/x
334     >>> n/x/(-n)**2 - 1/n/x
335     (-1 + 1/x)/(x*(1 - 1/x)**2) - 1/(x*(-1 + 1/x))
336     >>> signsimp(_)
337     0
338     >>> x*n + x*-n
339     x*(-1 + 1/x) + x*(1 - 1/x)
340     >>> signsimp(_)
341     0
342 
343     Since powers automatically handle leading signs
344 
345     >>> (-2)**i
346     -2**i
347 
348     signsimp can be used to put the base of a power with an integer
349     exponent into canonical form:
350 
351     >>> n**i
352     (-1 + 1/x)**i
353 
354     By default, signsimp doesn't leave behind any hollow simplification:
355     if making an Add canonical wrt sign didn't change the expression, the
356     original Add is restored. If this is not desired then the keyword
357     ``evaluate`` can be set to False:
358 
359     >>> e = exp(y - x)
360     >>> signsimp(e) == e
361     True
362     >>> signsimp(e, evaluate=False)
363     exp(-(x - y))
364 
365     """
366     if evaluate is None:
367         evaluate = global_evaluate[0]
368     expr = sympify(expr)
369     if not isinstance(expr, Expr) or expr.is_Atom:
370         return expr
371     e = sub_post(sub_pre(expr))
372     if not isinstance(e, Expr) or e.is_Atom:
373         return e
374     if e.is_Add:
375         return e.func(*[signsimp(a, evaluate) for a in e.args])
376     if evaluate:
377         e = e.xreplace({m: -(-m) for m in e.atoms(Mul) if -(-m) != m})
378     return e
379

381 def simplify(expr, ratio=1.7, measure=count_ops, rational=False, inverse=False):
382     """Simplifies the given expression.
383 
384     Simplification is not a well defined term and the exact strategies
385     this function tries can change in the future versions of SymPy. If
386     your algorithm relies on "simplification" (whatever it is), try to
387     determine what you need exactly  -  is it powsimp()?, radsimp()?,
388     together()?, logcombine()?, or something else? And use this particular
389     function directly, because those are well defined and thus your algorithm
390     will be robust.
391 
392     Nonetheless, especially for interactive use, or when you don't know
393     anything about the structure of the expression, simplify() tries to apply
394     intelligent heuristics to make the input expression "simpler".  For
395     example:
396 
397     >>> from sympy import simplify, cos, sin
398     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
399     >>> a = (x + x**2)/(x*sin(y)**2 + x*cos(y)**2)
400     >>> a
401     (x**2 + x)/(x*sin(y)**2 + x*cos(y)**2)
402     >>> simplify(a)
403     x + 1
404 
405     Note that we could have obtained the same result by using specific
406     simplification functions:
407 
408     >>> from sympy import trigsimp, cancel
409     >>> trigsimp(a)
410     (x**2 + x)/x
411     >>> cancel(_)
412     x + 1
413 
414     In some cases, applying :func:`simplify` may actually result in some more
415     complicated expression. The default ``ratio=1.7`` prevents more extreme
416     cases: if (result length)/(input length) > ratio, then input is returned
417     unmodified.  The ``measure`` parameter lets you specify the function used
418     to determine how complex an expression is.  The function should take a
419     single argument as an expression and return a number such that if
420     expression ``a`` is more complex than expression ``b``, then
421     ``measure(a) > measure(b)``.  The default measure function is
422     :func:`count_ops`, which returns the total number of operations in the
423     expression.
424 
425     For example, if ``ratio=1``, ``simplify`` output can't be longer
426     than input.
427 
428     ::
429 
430         >>> from sympy import sqrt, simplify, count_ops, oo
431         >>> root = 1/(sqrt(2)+3)
432 
433     Since ``simplify(root)`` would result in a slightly longer expression,
434     root is returned unchanged instead::
435 
436        >>> simplify(root, ratio=1) == root
437        True
438 
439     If ``ratio=oo``, simplify will be applied anyway::
440 
441         >>> count_ops(simplify(root, ratio=oo)) > count_ops(root)
442         True
443 
444     Note that the shortest expression is not necessary the simplest, so
445     setting ``ratio`` to 1 may not be a good idea.
446     Heuristically, the default value ``ratio=1.7`` seems like a reasonable
447     choice.
448 
449     You can easily define your own measure function based on what you feel
450     should represent the "size" or "complexity" of the input expression.  Note
451     that some choices, such as ``lambda expr: len(str(expr))`` may appear to be
452     good metrics, but have other problems (in this case, the measure function
453     may slow down simplify too much for very large expressions).  If you don't
454     know what a good metric would be, the default, ``count_ops``, is a good
455     one.
456 
457     For example:
458 
459     >>> from sympy import symbols, log
460     >>> a, b = symbols('a b', positive=True)
461     >>> g = log(a) + log(b) + log(a)*log(1/b)
462     >>> h = simplify(g)
463     >>> h
464     log(a*b**(1 - log(a)))
465     >>> count_ops(g)
466     8
467     >>> count_ops(h)
468     5
469 
470     So you can see that ``h`` is simpler than ``g`` using the count_ops metric.
471     However, we may not like how ``simplify`` (in this case, using
472     ``logcombine``) has created the ``b**(log(1/a) + 1)`` term.  A simple way
473     to reduce this would be to give more weight to powers as operations in
474     ``count_ops``.  We can do this by using the ``visual=True`` option:
475 
476     >>> print(count_ops(g, visual=True))
477     2*ADD + DIV + 4*LOG + MUL
478     >>> print(count_ops(h, visual=True))
479     2*LOG + MUL + POW + SUB
480 
481     >>> from sympy import Symbol, S
482     >>> def my_measure(expr):
483     ...     POW = Symbol('POW')
484     ...     # Discourage powers by giving POW a weight of 10
485     ...     count = count_ops(expr, visual=True).subs(POW, 10)
486     ...     # Every other operation gets a weight of 1 (the default)
487     ...     count = count.replace(Symbol, type(S.One))
488     ...     return count
489     >>> my_measure(g)
490     8
491     >>> my_measure(h)
492     14
493     >>> 15./8 > 1.7 # 1.7 is the default ratio
494     True
495     >>> simplify(g, measure=my_measure)
496     -log(a)*log(b) + log(a) + log(b)
497 
498     Note that because ``simplify()`` internally tries many different
499     simplification strategies and then compares them using the measure
500     function, we get a completely different result that is still different
501     from the input expression by doing this.
502 
503     If rational=True, Floats will be recast as Rationals before simplification.
504     If rational=None, Floats will be recast as Rationals but the result will
505     be recast as Floats. If rational=False(default) then nothing will be done
506     to the Floats.
507 
508     If inverse=True, it will be assumed that a composition of inverse
509     functions, such as sin and asin, can be cancelled in any order.
510     For example, ``asin(sin(x))`` will yield ``x`` without checking whether
511     x belongs to the set where this relation is true. The default is
512     False.
513     """
514     expr = sympify(expr)
515 
516     _eval_simplify = getattr(expr, '_eval_simplify', None)
517     if _eval_simplify is not None:
518         return _eval_simplify(ratio=ratio, measure=measure, rational=rational, inverse=inverse)
519 
520     original_expr = expr = signsimp(expr)
521 
522     from sympy.simplify.hyperexpand import hyperexpand
523     from sympy.functions.special.bessel import BesselBase
524     from sympy import Sum, Product
525 
526     if not isinstance(expr, Basic) or not expr.args:  # XXX: temporary hack
527         return expr
528 
529     if inverse and expr.has(Function):
530         expr = inversecombine(expr)
531         if not expr.args:  # simplified to atomic
532             return expr
533 
534     if not isinstance(expr, (Add, Mul, Pow, ExpBase)):
535         return expr.func(*[simplify(x, ratio=ratio, measure=measure, rational=rational, inverse=inverse)
536                          for x in expr.args])
537 
538     if not expr.is_commutative:
539         expr = nc_simplify(expr)
540 
541     # TODO: Apply different strategies, considering expression pattern:
542     # is it a purely rational function? Is there any trigonometric function?...
543     # See also https://github.com/sympy/sympy/pull/185.
544 
545     def shorter(*choices):
546         '''Return the choice that has the fewest ops. In case of a tie,
547         the expression listed first is selected.'''
548         if not has_variety(choices):
549             return choices[0]
550         return min(choices, key=measure)
551 
552     # rationalize Floats
553     floats = False
554     if rational is not False and expr.has(Float):
555         floats = True
556         expr = nsimplify(expr, rational=True)
557 
558     expr = bottom_up(expr, lambda w: getattr(w, 'normal', lambda: w)())
559     expr = Mul(*powsimp(expr).as_content_primitive())
560     _e = cancel(expr)
561     expr1 = shorter(_e, _mexpand(_e).cancel())  # issue 6829
562     expr2 = shorter(together(expr, deep=True), together(expr1, deep=True))
563 
564     if ratio is S.Infinity:
565         expr = expr2
566     else:
567         expr = shorter(expr2, expr1, expr)
568     if not isinstance(expr, Basic):  # XXX: temporary hack
569         return expr
570 
571     expr = factor_terms(expr, sign=False)
572 
573     # hyperexpand automatically only works on hypergeometric terms
574     expr = hyperexpand(expr)
575 
576     expr = piecewise_fold(expr)
577 
578     if expr.has(BesselBase):
579         expr = besselsimp(expr)
580 
581     if expr.has(TrigonometricFunction, HyperbolicFunction):
582         expr = trigsimp(expr, deep=True)
583 
584     if expr.has(log):
585         expr = shorter(expand_log(expr, deep=True), logcombine(expr))
586 
587     if expr.has(CombinatorialFunction, gamma):
588         # expression with gamma functions or non-integer arguments is
589         # automatically passed to gammasimp
590         expr = combsimp(expr)
591 
592     if expr.has(Sum):
593         expr = sum_simplify(expr)
594 
595     if expr.has(Product):
596         expr = product_simplify(expr)
597 
598     from sympy.physics.units import Quantity
599     from sympy.physics.units.util import quantity_simplify
600 
601     if expr.has(Quantity):
602         expr = quantity_simplify(expr)
603 
604     short = shorter(powsimp(expr, combine='exp', deep=True), powsimp(expr), expr)
605     short = shorter(short, cancel(short))
606     short = shorter(short, factor_terms(short), expand_power_exp(expand_mul(short)))
607     if short.has(TrigonometricFunction, HyperbolicFunction, ExpBase):
608         short = exptrigsimp(short)
609 
610     # get rid of hollow 2-arg Mul factorization
611     hollow_mul = Transform(
612         lambda x: Mul(*x.args),
613         lambda x:
614         x.is_Mul and
615         len(x.args) == 2 and
616         x.args[0].is_Number and
617         x.args[1].is_Add and
618         x.is_commutative)
619     expr = short.xreplace(hollow_mul)
620 
621     numer, denom = expr.as_numer_denom()
622     if denom.is_Add:
623         n, d = fraction(radsimp(1/denom, symbolic=False, max_terms=1))
624         if n is not S.One:
625             expr = (numer*n).expand()/d
626 
627     if expr.could_extract_minus_sign():
628         n, d = fraction(expr)
629         if d != 0:
630             expr = signsimp(-n/(-d))
631 
632     if measure(expr) > ratio*measure(original_expr):
633         expr = original_expr
634 
635     # restore floats
636     if floats and rational is None:
637         expr = nfloat(expr, exponent=False)
638 
639     return expr
640

642 def sum_simplify(s):
643     """Main function for Sum simplification"""
644     from sympy.concrete.summations import Sum
645     from sympy.core.function import expand
646 
647     terms = Add.make_args(expand(s))
648     s_t = [] # Sum Terms
649     o_t = [] # Other Terms
650 
651     for term in terms:
652         if isinstance(term, Mul):
653             other = 1
654             sum_terms = []
655 
656             if not term.has(Sum):
657                 o_t.append(term)
658                 continue
659 
660             mul_terms = Mul.make_args(term)
661             for mul_term in mul_terms:
662                 if isinstance(mul_term, Sum):
663                     r = mul_term._eval_simplify()
664                     sum_terms.extend(Add.make_args(r))
665                 else:
666                     other = other * mul_term
667             if len(sum_terms):
668                 #some simplification may have happened
669                 #use if so
670                 s_t.append(Mul(*sum_terms) * other)
671             else:
672                 o_t.append(other)
673         elif isinstance(term, Sum):
674             #as above, we need to turn this into an add list
675             r = term._eval_simplify()
676             s_t.extend(Add.make_args(r))
677         else:
678             o_t.append(term)
679 
680 
681     result = Add(sum_combine(s_t), *o_t)
682 
683     return result
684 
685 def sum_combine(s_t):
686     """Helper function for Sum simplification
687 
688        Attempts to simplify a list of sums, by combining limits / sum function's
689        returns the simplified sum
690     """
691     from sympy.concrete.summations import Sum
692 
693 
694     used = [False] * len(s_t)
695 
696     for method in range(2):
697         for i, s_term1 in enumerate(s_t):
698             if not used[i]:
699                 for j, s_term2 in enumerate(s_t):
700                     if not used[j] and i != j:
701                         temp = sum_add(s_term1, s_term2, method)
702                         if isinstance(temp, Sum) or isinstance(temp, Mul):
703                             s_t[i] = temp
704                             s_term1 = s_t[i]
705                             used[j] = True
706 
707     result = S.Zero
708     for i, s_term in enumerate(s_t):
709         if not used[i]:
710             result = Add(result, s_term)
711 
712     return result

714 def factor_sum(self, limits=None, radical=False, clear=False, fraction=False, sign=True):
715     """Helper function for Sum simplification
716 
717        if limits is specified, "self" is the inner part of a sum
718 
719        Returns the sum with constant factors brought outside
720     """
721     from sympy.core.exprtools import factor_terms
722     from sympy.concrete.summations import Sum
723 
724     result = self.function if limits is None else self
725     limits = self.limits if limits is None else limits
726     #avoid any confusion w/ as_independent
727     if result == 0:
728         return S.Zero
729 
730     #get the summation variables
731     sum_vars = set([limit.args[0] for limit in limits])
732 
733     #finally we try to factor out any common terms
734     #and remove the from the sum if independent
735     retv = factor_terms(result, radical=radical, clear=clear, fraction=fraction, sign=sign)
736     #avoid doing anything bad
737     if not result.is_commutative:
738         return Sum(result, *limits)
739 
740     i, d = retv.as_independent(*sum_vars)
741     if isinstance(retv, Add):
742         return i * Sum(1, *limits) + Sum(d, *limits)
743     else:
744         return i * Sum(d, *limits)
745 
746 def sum_add(self, other, method=0):
747     """Helper function for Sum simplification"""
748     from sympy.concrete.summations import Sum
749     from sympy import Mul
750 
751     #we know this is something in terms of a constant * a sum
752     #so we temporarily put the constants inside for simplification
753     #then simplify the result
754     def __refactor(val):
755         args = Mul.make_args(val)
756         sumv = next(x for x in args if isinstance(x, Sum))
757         constant = Mul(*[x for x in args if x != sumv])
758         return Sum(constant * sumv.function, *sumv.limits)
759 
760     if isinstance(self, Mul):
761         rself = __refactor(self)
762     else:
763         rself = self
764 
765     if isinstance(other, Mul):
766         rother = __refactor(other)
767     else:
768         rother = other
769 
770     if type(rself) == type(rother):
771         if method == 0:
772             if rself.limits == rother.limits:
773                 return factor_sum(Sum(rself.function + rother.function, *rself.limits))
774         elif method == 1:
775             if simplify(rself.function - rother.function) == 0:
776                 if len(rself.limits) == len(rother.limits) == 1:
777                     i = rself.limits[0][0]
778                     x1 = rself.limits[0][1]
779                     y1 = rself.limits[0][2]
780                     j = rother.limits[0][0]
781                     x2 = rother.limits[0][1]
782                     y2 = rother.limits[0][2]
783 
784                     if i == j:
785                         if x2 == y1 + 1:
786                             return factor_sum(Sum(rself.function, (i, x1, y2)))
787                         elif x1 == y2 + 1:
788                             return factor_sum(Sum(rself.function, (i, x2, y1)))

793 def product_simplify(s):
794     """Main function for Product simplification"""
795     from sympy.concrete.products import Product
796 
797     terms = Mul.make_args(s)
798     p_t = [] # Product Terms
799     o_t = [] # Other Terms
800 
801     for term in terms:
802         if isinstance(term, Product):
803             p_t.append(term)
804         else:
805             o_t.append(term)
806 
807     used = [False] * len(p_t)
808 
809     for method in range(2):
810         for i, p_term1 in enumerate(p_t):
811             if not used[i]:
812                 for j, p_term2 in enumerate(p_t):
813                     if not used[j] and i != j:
814                         if isinstance(product_mul(p_term1, p_term2, method), Product):
815                             p_t[i] = product_mul(p_term1, p_term2, method)
816                             used[j] = True
817 
818     result = Mul(*o_t)
819 
820     for i, p_term in enumerate(p_t):
821         if not used[i]:
822             result = Mul(result, p_term)
823 
824     return result

827 def product_mul(self, other, method=0):
828     """Helper function for Product simplification"""
829     from sympy.concrete.products import Product
830 
831     if type(self) == type(other):
832         if method == 0:
833             if self.limits == other.limits:
834                 return Product(self.function * other.function, *self.limits)
835         elif method == 1:
836             if simplify(self.function - other.function) == 0:
837                 if len(self.limits) == len(other.limits) == 1:
838                     i = self.limits[0][0]
839                     x1 = self.limits[0][1]
840                     y1 = self.limits[0][2]
841                     j = other.limits[0][0]
842                     x2 = other.limits[0][1]
843                     y2 = other.limits[0][2]
844 
845                     if i == j:
846                         if x2 == y1 + 1:
847                             return Product(self.function, (i, x1, y2))
848                         elif x1 == y2 + 1:
849                             return Product(self.function, (i, x2, y1))
850 
851     return Mul(self, other)

854 def _nthroot_solve(p, n, prec):
855     """
856      helper function for ``nthroot``
857      It denests ``p**Rational(1, n)`` using its minimal polynomial
858     """
859     from sympy.polys.numberfields import _minimal_polynomial_sq
860     from sympy.solvers import solve
861     while n % 2 == 0:
862         p = sqrtdenest(sqrt(p))
863         n = n // 2
864     if n == 1:
865         return p
866     pn = p**Rational(1, n)
867     x = Symbol('x')
868     f = _minimal_polynomial_sq(p, n, x)
869     if f is None:
870         return None
871     sols = solve(f, x)
872     for sol in sols:
873         if abs(sol - pn).n() < 1./10**prec:
874             sol = sqrtdenest(sol)
875             if _mexpand(sol**n) == p:
876                 return sol

879 def logcombine(expr, force=False):
880     """
881     Takes logarithms and combines them using the following rules:
882 
883     - log(x) + log(y) == log(x*y) if both are positive
884     - a*log(x) == log(x**a) if x is positive and a is real
885 
886     If ``force`` is True then the assumptions above will be assumed to hold if
887     there is no assumption already in place on a quantity. For example, if
888     ``a`` is imaginary or the argument negative, force will not perform a
889     combination but if ``a`` is a symbol with no assumptions the change will
890     take place.
891 
892     Examples
893     ========
894 
895     >>> from sympy import Symbol, symbols, log, logcombine, I
896     >>> from sympy.abc import a, x, y, z
897     >>> logcombine(a*log(x) + log(y) - log(z))
898     a*log(x) + log(y) - log(z)
899     >>> logcombine(a*log(x) + log(y) - log(z), force=True)
900     log(x**a*y/z)
901     >>> x,y,z = symbols('x,y,z', positive=True)
902     >>> a = Symbol('a', real=True)
903     >>> logcombine(a*log(x) + log(y) - log(z))
904     log(x**a*y/z)
905 
906     The transformation is limited to factors and/or terms that
907     contain logs, so the result depends on the initial state of
908     expansion:
909 
910     >>> eq = (2 + 3*I)*log(x)
911     >>> logcombine(eq, force=True) == eq
912     True
913     >>> logcombine(eq.expand(), force=True)
914     log(x**2) + I*log(x**3)
915 
916     See Also
917     ========
918 
919     posify: replace all symbols with symbols having positive assumptions
920     sympy.core.function.expand_log: expand the logarithms of products
921         and powers; the opposite of logcombine
922 
923     """
924 
925     def f(rv):
926         if not (rv.is_Add or rv.is_Mul):
927             return rv
928 
929         def gooda(a):
930             # bool to tell whether the leading ``a`` in ``a*log(x)``
931             # could appear as log(x**a)
932             return (a is not S.NegativeOne and  # -1 *could* go, but we disallow
933                 (a.is_real or force and a.is_real is not False))
934 
935         def goodlog(l):
936             # bool to tell whether log ``l``'s argument can combine with others
937             a = l.args[0]
938             return a.is_positive or force and a.is_nonpositive is not False
939 
940         other = []
941         logs = []
942         log1 = defaultdict(list)
943         for a in Add.make_args(rv):
944             if isinstance(a, log) and goodlog(a):
945                 log1[()].append(([], a))
946             elif not a.is_Mul:
947                 other.append(a)
948             else:
949                 ot = []
950                 co = []
951                 lo = []
952                 for ai in a.args:
953                     if ai.is_Rational and ai < 0:
954                         ot.append(S.NegativeOne)
955                         co.append(-ai)
956                     elif isinstance(ai, log) and goodlog(ai):
957                         lo.append(ai)
958                     elif gooda(ai):
959                         co.append(ai)
960                     else:
961                         ot.append(ai)
962                 if len(lo) > 1:
963                     logs.append((ot, co, lo))
964                 elif lo:
965                     log1[tuple(ot)].append((co, lo[0]))
966                 else:
967                     other.append(a)
968 
969         # if there is only one log in other, put it with the
970         # good logs
971         if len(other) == 1 and isinstance(other[0], log):
972             log1[()].append(([], other.pop()))
973         # if there is only one log at each coefficient and none have
974         # an exponent to place inside the log then there is nothing to do
975         if not logs and all(len(log1[k]) == 1 and log1[k][0] == [] for k in log1):
976             return rv
977 
978         # collapse multi-logs as far as possible in a canonical way
979         # TODO: see if x*log(a)+x*log(a)*log(b) -> x*log(a)*(1+log(b))?
980         # -- in this case, it's unambiguous, but if it were were a log(c) in
981         # each term then it's arbitrary whether they are grouped by log(a) or
982         # by log(c). So for now, just leave this alone; it's probably better to
983         # let the user decide
984         for o, e, l in logs:
985             l = list(ordered(l))
986             e = log(l.pop(0).args[0]**Mul(*e))
987             while l:
988                 li = l.pop(0)
989                 e = log(li.args[0]**e)
990             c, l = Mul(*o), e
991             if isinstance(l, log):  # it should be, but check to be sure
992                 log1[(c,)].append(([], l))
993             else:
994                 other.append(c*l)
995 
996         # logs that have the same coefficient can multiply
997         for k in list(log1.keys()):
998             log1[Mul(*k)] = log(logcombine(Mul(*[
999                 l.args[0]**Mul(*c) for c, l in log1.pop(k)]),
1000                 force=force), evaluate=False)
1001 
1002         # logs that have oppositely signed coefficients can divide
1003         for k in ordered(list(log1.keys())):
1004             if not k in log1:  # already popped as -k
1005                 continue
1006             if -k in log1:
1007                 # figure out which has the minus sign; the one with
1008                 # more op counts should be the one
1009                 num, den = k, -k
1010                 if num.count_ops() > den.count_ops():
1011                     num, den = den, num
1012                 other.append(
1013                     num*log(log1.pop(num).args[0]/log1.pop(den).args[0],
1014                             evaluate=False))
1015             else:
1016                 other.append(k*log1.pop(k))
1017 
1018         return Add(*other)
1019 
1020     return bottom_up(expr, f)

1052 def walk(e, *target):
1053     """iterate through the args that are the given types (target) and
1054     return a list of the args that were traversed; arguments
1055     that are not of the specified types are not traversed.
1056

1058     ========

1063     >>> list(walk(Min(x, Max(y, Min(1, z))), Min))
1064     [Min(x, Max(y, Min(1, z)))]
1065     >>> list(walk(Min(x, Max(y, Min(1, z))), Min, Max))
1066     [Min(x, Max(y, Min(1, z))), Max(y, Min(1, z)), Min(1, z)]
1067 
1068     See Also
1069     ========
1070 
1071     bottom_up
1072     """
1073     if isinstance(e, target):
1074         yield e
1075         for i in e.args:
1076             for w in walk(i, *target):
1077                 yield w

1080 def bottom_up(rv, F, atoms=False, nonbasic=False):
1081     """Apply ``F`` to all expressions in an expression tree from the
1082     bottom up. If ``atoms`` is True, apply ``F`` even if there are no args;
1083     if ``nonbasic`` is True, try to apply ``F`` to non-Basic objects.
1084     """
1085     args = getattr(rv, 'args', None)
1086     if args is not None:
1087         if args:
1088             args = tuple([bottom_up(a, F, atoms, nonbasic) for a in args])
1089             if args != rv.args:
1090                 rv = rv.func(*args)
1091             rv = F(rv)
1092         elif atoms:
1093             rv = F(rv)
1094     else:
1095         if nonbasic:
1096             try:
1097                 rv = F(rv)
1098             except TypeError:
1099                 pass
1100 
1101     return rv

1104 def besselsimp(expr):
1105     """
1106     Simplify bessel-type functions.
1107 
1108     This routine tries to simplify bessel-type functions. Currently it only
1109     works on the Bessel J and I functions, however. It works by looking at all
1110     such functions in turn, and eliminating factors of "I" and "-1" (actually
1111     their polar equivalents) in front of the argument. Then, functions of
1112     half-integer order are rewritten using strigonometric functions and
1113     functions of integer order (> 1) are rewritten using functions
1114     of low order.  Finally, if the expression was changed, compute
1115     factorization of the result with factor().
1116 
1117     >>> from sympy import besselj, besseli, besselsimp, polar_lift, I, S
1118     >>> from sympy.abc import z, nu
1119     >>> besselsimp(besselj(nu, z*polar_lift(-1)))
1120     exp(I*pi*nu)*besselj(nu, z)
1121     >>> besselsimp(besseli(nu, z*polar_lift(-I)))
1122     exp(-I*pi*nu/2)*besselj(nu, z)
1123     >>> besselsimp(besseli(S(-1)/2, z))
1124     sqrt(2)*cosh(z)/(sqrt(pi)*sqrt(z))
1125     >>> besselsimp(z*besseli(0, z) + z*(besseli(2, z))/2 + besseli(1, z))
1126     3*z*besseli(0, z)/2
1127     """
1128     # TODO
1129     # - better algorithm?
1130     # - simplify (cos(pi*b)*besselj(b,z) - besselj(-b,z))/sin(pi*b) ...
1131     # - use contiguity relations?
1132 
1133     def replacer(fro, to, factors):
1134         factors = set(factors)
1135 
1136         def repl(nu, z):
1137             if factors.intersection(Mul.make_args(z)):
1138                 return to(nu, z)
1139             return fro(nu, z)
1140         return repl
1141 
1142     def torewrite(fro, to):
1143         def tofunc(nu, z):
1144             return fro(nu, z).rewrite(to)
1145         return tofunc
1146 
1147     def tominus(fro):
1148         def tofunc(nu, z):
1149             return exp(I*pi*nu)*fro(nu, exp_polar(-I*pi)*z)
1150         return tofunc
1151 
1152     orig_expr = expr
1153 
1154     ifactors = [I, exp_polar(I*pi/2), exp_polar(-I*pi/2)]
1155     expr = expr.replace(
1156         besselj, replacer(besselj,
1157         torewrite(besselj, besseli), ifactors))
1158     expr = expr.replace(
1159         besseli, replacer(besseli,
1160         torewrite(besseli, besselj), ifactors))
1161 
1162     minusfactors = [-1, exp_polar(I*pi)]
1163     expr = expr.replace(
1164         besselj, replacer(besselj, tominus(besselj), minusfactors))
1165     expr = expr.replace(
1166         besseli, replacer(besseli, tominus(besseli), minusfactors))
1167 
1168     z0 = Dummy('z')
1169 
1170     def expander(fro):
1171         def repl(nu, z):
1172             if (nu % 1) == S(1)/2:
1173                 return simplify(trigsimp(unpolarify(
1174                         fro(nu, z0).rewrite(besselj).rewrite(jn).expand(
1175                             func=True)).subs(z0, z)))
1176             elif nu.is_Integer and nu > 1:
1177                 return fro(nu, z).expand(func=True)
1178             return fro(nu, z)
1179         return repl
1180 
1181     expr = expr.replace(besselj, expander(besselj))
1182     expr = expr.replace(bessely, expander(bessely))
1183     expr = expr.replace(besseli, expander(besseli))
1184     expr = expr.replace(besselk, expander(besselk))
1185 
1186     if expr != orig_expr:
1187         expr = expr.factor()
1188 
1189     return expr
