535 def collect_const(expr, *vars, **kwargs):
536     """A non-greedy collection of terms with similar number coefficients in
537     an Add expr. If ``vars`` is given then only those constants will be
538     targeted. Although any Number can also be targeted, if this is not
539     desired set ``Numbers=False`` and no Float or Rational will be collected.
540 
541     Parameters
542     ==========
543 
544     expr : sympy expression
545         This parameter defines the expression the expression from which
546         terms with similar coefficients are to be collected. A non-Add
547         expression is returned as it is.
548 
549     vars : variable length collection of Numbers, optional
550         Specifies the constants to target for collection. Can be multiple in
551         number.
552 
553     kwargs : ``Numbers`` is the only possible argument to pass.
554         Numbers (default=True) specifies to target all instance of
555         :class:`sympy.core.numbers.Number` class. If ``Numbers=False``, then
556         no Float or Rational will be collected.
557 
558     Returns
559     =======
560 
561     expr : Expr
562         Returns an expression with similar coefficient terms collected.
563 
564     Examples
565     ========
566 
567     >>> from sympy import sqrt
568     >>> from sympy.abc import a, s, x, y, z
569     >>> from sympy.simplify.radsimp import collect_const
570     >>> collect_const(sqrt(3) + sqrt(3)*(1 + sqrt(2)))
571     sqrt(3)*(sqrt(2) + 2)
572     >>> collect_const(sqrt(3)*s + sqrt(7)*s + sqrt(3) + sqrt(7))
573     (sqrt(3) + sqrt(7))*(s + 1)
574     >>> s = sqrt(2) + 2
575     >>> collect_const(sqrt(3)*s + sqrt(3) + sqrt(7)*s + sqrt(7))
576     (sqrt(2) + 3)*(sqrt(3) + sqrt(7))
577     >>> collect_const(sqrt(3)*s + sqrt(3) + sqrt(7)*s + sqrt(7), sqrt(3))
578     sqrt(7) + sqrt(3)*(sqrt(2) + 3) + sqrt(7)*(sqrt(2) + 2)
579 
580     The collection is sign-sensitive, giving higher precedence to the
581     unsigned values:
582 
583     >>> collect_const(x - y - z)
584     x - (y + z)
585     >>> collect_const(-y - z)
586     -(y + z)
587     >>> collect_const(2*x - 2*y - 2*z, 2)
588     2*(x - y - z)
589     >>> collect_const(2*x - 2*y - 2*z, -2)
590     2*x - 2*(y + z)
591 
592     See Also
593     ========
594 
595     collect, collect_sqrt, rcollect
596     """
597     if not expr.is_Add:
598         return expr
599 
600     recurse = False
601     Numbers = kwargs.get('Numbers', True)
602 
603     if not vars:
604         recurse = True
605         vars = set()
606         for a in expr.args:
607             for m in Mul.make_args(a):
608                 if m.is_number:
609                     vars.add(m)
610     else:
611         vars = sympify(vars)
612     if not Numbers:
613         vars = [v for v in vars if not v.is_Number]
614 
615     vars = list(ordered(vars))
616     for v in vars:
617         terms = defaultdict(list)
618         Fv = Factors(v)
619         for m in Add.make_args(expr):
620             f = Factors(m)
621             q, r = f.div(Fv)
622             if r.is_one:
623                 # only accept this as a true factor if
624                 # it didn't change an exponent from an Integer
625                 # to a non-Integer, e.g. 2/sqrt(2) -> sqrt(2)
626                 # -- we aren't looking for this sort of change
627                 fwas = f.factors.copy()
628                 fnow = q.factors
629                 if not any(k in fwas and fwas[k].is_Integer and not
630                         fnow[k].is_Integer for k in fnow):
631                     terms[v].append(q.as_expr())
632                     continue
633             terms[S.One].append(m)
634 
635         args = []
636         hit = False
637         uneval = False
638         for k in ordered(terms):
639             v = terms[k]
640             if k is S.One:
641                 args.extend(v)
642                 continue
643 
644             if len(v) > 1:
645                 v = Add(*v)
646                 hit = True
647                 if recurse and v != expr:
648                     vars.append(v)
649             else:
650                 v = v[0]
651 
652             # be careful not to let uneval become True unless
653             # it must be because it's going to be more expensive
654             # to rebuild the expression as an unevaluated one
655             if Numbers and k.is_Number and v.is_Add:
656                 args.append(_keep_coeff(k, v, sign=True))
657                 uneval = True
658             else:
659                 args.append(k*v)
660 
661         if hit:
662             if uneval:
663                 expr = _unevaluated_Add(*args)
664             else:
665                 expr = Add(*args)
666             if not expr.is_Add:
667                 break
668 
669     return expr
670

672 def radsimp(expr, symbolic=True, max_terms=4):
673     r"""
674     Rationalize the denominator by removing square roots.
675 
676     Note: the expression returned from radsimp must be used with caution
677     since if the denominator contains symbols, it will be possible to make
678     substitutions that violate the assumptions of the simplification process:
679     that for a denominator matching a + b*sqrt(c), a != +/-b*sqrt(c). (If
680     there are no symbols, this assumptions is made valid by collecting terms
681     of sqrt(c) so the match variable ``a`` does not contain ``sqrt(c)``.) If
682     you do not want the simplification to occur for symbolic denominators, set
683     ``symbolic`` to False.
684 
685     If there are more than ``max_terms`` radical terms then the expression is
686     returned unchanged.
687 
688     Examples
689     ========
690 
691     >>> from sympy import radsimp, sqrt, Symbol, denom, pprint, I
692     >>> from sympy import factor_terms, fraction, signsimp
693     >>> from sympy.simplify.radsimp import collect_sqrt
694     >>> from sympy.abc import a, b, c
695 
696     >>> radsimp(1/(2 + sqrt(2)))
697     (2 - sqrt(2))/2
698     >>> x,y = map(Symbol, 'xy')
699     >>> e = ((2 + 2*sqrt(2))*x + (2 + sqrt(8))*y)/(2 + sqrt(2))
700     >>> radsimp(e)
701     sqrt(2)*(x + y)
702 
703     No simplification beyond removal of the gcd is done. One might
704     want to polish the result a little, however, by collecting
705     square root terms:
706 
707     >>> r2 = sqrt(2)
708     >>> r5 = sqrt(5)
709     >>> ans = radsimp(1/(y*r2 + x*r2 + a*r5 + b*r5)); pprint(ans)
710         ___       ___       ___       ___
711       \/ 5 *a + \/ 5 *b - \/ 2 *x - \/ 2 *y
712     ------------------------------------------
713        2               2      2              2
714     5*a  + 10*a*b + 5*b  - 2*x  - 4*x*y - 2*y
715 
716     >>> n, d = fraction(ans)
717     >>> pprint(factor_terms(signsimp(collect_sqrt(n))/d, radical=True))
718             ___             ___
719           \/ 5 *(a + b) - \/ 2 *(x + y)
720     ------------------------------------------
721        2               2      2              2
722     5*a  + 10*a*b + 5*b  - 2*x  - 4*x*y - 2*y
723 
724     If radicals in the denominator cannot be removed or there is no denominator,
725     the original expression will be returned.
726 
727     >>> radsimp(sqrt(2)*x + sqrt(2))
728     sqrt(2)*x + sqrt(2)
729 
730     Results with symbols will not always be valid for all substitutions:
731 
732     >>> eq = 1/(a + b*sqrt(c))
733     >>> eq.subs(a, b*sqrt(c))
734     1/(2*b*sqrt(c))
735     >>> radsimp(eq).subs(a, b*sqrt(c))
736     nan
737 
738     If symbolic=False, symbolic denominators will not be transformed (but
739     numeric denominators will still be processed):
740 
741     >>> radsimp(eq, symbolic=False)
742     1/(a + b*sqrt(c))
743 
744     """
745     from sympy.simplify.simplify import signsimp
746 
747     syms = symbols("a:d A:D")
748     def _num(rterms):
749         # return the multiplier that will simplify the expression described
750         # by rterms [(sqrt arg, coeff), ... ]
751         a, b, c, d, A, B, C, D = syms
752         if len(rterms) == 2:
753             reps = dict(list(zip([A, a, B, b], [j for i in rterms for j in i])))
754             return (
755             sqrt(A)*a - sqrt(B)*b).xreplace(reps)
756         if len(rterms) == 3:
757             reps = dict(list(zip([A, a, B, b, C, c], [j for i in rterms for j in i])))
758             return (
759             (sqrt(A)*a + sqrt(B)*b - sqrt(C)*c)*(2*sqrt(A)*sqrt(B)*a*b - A*a**2 -
760             B*b**2 + C*c**2)).xreplace(reps)
761         elif len(rterms) == 4:
762             reps = dict(list(zip([A, a, B, b, C, c, D, d], [j for i in rterms for j in i])))
763             return ((sqrt(A)*a + sqrt(B)*b - sqrt(C)*c - sqrt(D)*d)*(2*sqrt(A)*sqrt(B)*a*b
764                 - A*a**2 - B*b**2 - 2*sqrt(C)*sqrt(D)*c*d + C*c**2 +
765                 D*d**2)*(-8*sqrt(A)*sqrt(B)*sqrt(C)*sqrt(D)*a*b*c*d + A**2*a**4 -
766                 2*A*B*a**2*b**2 - 2*A*C*a**2*c**2 - 2*A*D*a**2*d**2 + B**2*b**4 -
767                 2*B*C*b**2*c**2 - 2*B*D*b**2*d**2 + C**2*c**4 - 2*C*D*c**2*d**2 +
768                 D**2*d**4)).xreplace(reps)
769         elif len(rterms) == 1:
770             return sqrt(rterms[0][0])
771         else:
772             raise NotImplementedError
773 
774     def ispow2(d, log2=False):
775         if not d.is_Pow:
776             return False
777         e = d.exp
778         if e.is_Rational and e.q == 2 or symbolic and denom(e) == 2:
779             return True
780         if log2:
781             q = 1
782             if e.is_Rational:
783                 q = e.q
784             elif symbolic:
785                 d = denom(e)
786                 if d.is_Integer:
787                     q = d
788             if q != 1 and log(q, 2).is_Integer:
789                 return True
790         return False
791 
792     def handle(expr):
793         # Handle first reduces to the case
794         # expr = 1/d, where d is an add, or d is base**p/2.
795         # We do this by recursively calling handle on each piece.
796         from sympy.simplify.simplify import nsimplify
797 
798         n, d = fraction(expr)
799 
800         if expr.is_Atom or (d.is_Atom and n.is_Atom):
801             return expr
802         elif not n.is_Atom:
803             n = n.func(*[handle(a) for a in n.args])
804             return _unevaluated_Mul(n, handle(1/d))
805         elif n is not S.One:
806             return _unevaluated_Mul(n, handle(1/d))
807         elif d.is_Mul:
808             return _unevaluated_Mul(*[handle(1/d) for d in d.args])
809 
810         # By this step, expr is 1/d, and d is not a mul.
811         if not symbolic and d.free_symbols:
812             return expr
813 
814         if ispow2(d):
815             d2 = sqrtdenest(sqrt(d.base))**numer(d.exp)
816             if d2 != d:
817                 return handle(1/d2)
818         elif d.is_Pow and (d.exp.is_integer or d.base.is_positive):
819             # (1/d**i) = (1/d)**i
820             return handle(1/d.base)**d.exp
821 
822         if not (d.is_Add or ispow2(d)):
823             return 1/d.func(*[handle(a) for a in d.args])
824 
825         # handle 1/d treating d as an Add (though it may not be)
826 
827         keep = True  # keep changes that are made
828 
829         # flatten it and collect radicals after checking for special
830         # conditions
831         d = _mexpand(d)
832 
833         # did it change?
834         if d.is_Atom:
835             return 1/d
836 
837         # is it a number that might be handled easily?
838         if d.is_number:
839             _d = nsimplify(d)
840             if _d.is_Number and _d.equals(d):
841                 return 1/_d
842 
843         while True:
844             # collect similar terms
845             collected = defaultdict(list)
846             for m in Add.make_args(d):  # d might have become non-Add
847                 p2 = []
848                 other = []
849                 for i in Mul.make_args(m):
850                     if ispow2(i, log2=True):
851                         p2.append(i.base if i.exp is S.Half else i.base**(2*i.exp))
852                     elif i is S.ImaginaryUnit:
853                         p2.append(S.NegativeOne)
854                     else:
855                         other.append(i)
856                 collected[tuple(ordered(p2))].append(Mul(*other))
857             rterms = list(ordered(list(collected.items())))
858             rterms = [(Mul(*i), Add(*j)) for i, j in rterms]
859             nrad = len(rterms) - (1 if rterms[0][0] is S.One else 0)
860             if nrad < 1:
861                 break
862             elif nrad > max_terms:
863                 # there may have been invalid operations leading to this point
864                 # so don't keep changes, e.g. this expression is troublesome
865                 # in collecting terms so as not to raise the issue of 2834:
866                 # r = sqrt(sqrt(5) + 5)
867                 # eq = 1/(sqrt(5)*r + 2*sqrt(5)*sqrt(-sqrt(5) + 5) + 5*r)
868                 keep = False
869                 break
870             if len(rterms) > 4:
871                 # in general, only 4 terms can be removed with repeated squaring
872                 # but other considerations can guide selection of radical terms
873                 # so that radicals are removed
874                 if all([x.is_Integer and (y**2).is_Rational for x, y in rterms]):
875                     nd, d = rad_rationalize(S.One, Add._from_args(
876                         [sqrt(x)*y for x, y in rterms]))
877                     n *= nd
878                 else:
879                     # is there anything else that might be attempted?
880                     keep = False
881                 break
882             from sympy.simplify.powsimp import powsimp, powdenest
883 
884             num = powsimp(_num(rterms))
885             n *= num
886             d *= num
887             d = powdenest(_mexpand(d), force=symbolic)
888             if d.is_Atom:
889                 break
890 
891         if not keep:
892             return expr
893         return _unevaluated_Mul(n, 1/d)
894 
895     coeff, expr = expr.as_coeff_Add()
896     expr = expr.normal()
897     old = fraction(expr)
898     n, d = fraction(handle(expr))
899     if old != (n, d):
900         if not d.is_Atom:
901             was = (n, d)

920 def rad_rationalize(num, den):
921     """
922     Rationalize num/den by removing square roots in the denominator;
923     num and den are sum of terms whose squares are rationals

943     """Returns a pair with expression's numerator and denominator.
944        If the given expression is not a fraction then this function
945        will return the tuple (expr, 1).
946

948        fractions or to do any term rewriting at all.
949 
950        If only one of the numerator/denominator pair is needed then
951        use numer(expr) or denom(expr) functions respectively.
952 
953        >>> from sympy import fraction, Rational, Symbol
954        >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
955 
956        >>> fraction(x/y)
957        (x, y)
958        >>> fraction(x)
959        (x, 1)
960 
961        >>> fraction(1/y**2)
962        (1, y**2)
963 
964        >>> fraction(x*y/2)
965        (x*y, 2)
966        >>> fraction(Rational(1, 2))
967        (1, 2)
968 
969        This function will also work fine with assumptions:
970 
971        >>> k = Symbol('k', negative=True)
972        >>> fraction(x * y**k)
973        (x, y**(-k))
974 
975        If we know nothing about sign of some exponent and 'exact'
976        flag is unset, then structure this exponent's structure will
977        be analyzed and pretty fraction will be returned:
978 
979        >>> from sympy import exp, Mul
980        >>> fraction(2*x**(-y))
981        (2, x**y)
982 
983        >>> fraction(exp(-x))
984        (1, exp(x))
985 
986        >>> fraction(exp(-x), exact=True)
987        (exp(-x), 1)
988 
989        The `exact` flag will also keep any unevaluated Muls from
990        being evaluated:
991 
992        >>> u = Mul(2, x + 1, evaluate=False)
993        >>> fraction(u)
994        (2*x + 2, 1)
995        >>> fraction(u, exact=True)
996        (2*(x  + 1), 1)

1000     numer, denom = [], []
1001 
1002     for term in Mul.make_args(expr):
1003         if term.is_commutative and (term.is_Pow or isinstance(term, exp)):
1004             b, ex = term.as_base_exp()
1005             if ex.is_negative:

1007                     denom.append(b)

1010                         denom.append(Pow(b, -ex))
1011                     else:
1012                         numer.append(term)
1013                 else:
1014                     denom.append(Pow(b, -ex))
1015             elif ex.is_positive:
1016                 numer.append(term)
1017             elif not exact and ex.is_Mul:

1019                 numer.append(n)
1020                 denom.append(d)
1021             else:
1022                 numer.append(term)

1026             denom.append(d)

1062 def split_surds(expr):
1063     """
1064     split an expression with terms whose squares are rationals
1065     into a sum of terms whose surds squared have gcd equal to g
1066     and a sum of terms with surds squared prime with g
1067 
1068     Examples
1069     ========
1070 
1071     >>> from sympy import sqrt
1072     >>> from sympy.simplify.radsimp import split_surds
1073     >>> split_surds(3*sqrt(3) + sqrt(5)/7 + sqrt(6) + sqrt(10) + sqrt(15))
1074     (3, sqrt(2) + sqrt(5) + 3, sqrt(5)/7 + sqrt(10))
1075     """
1076     args = sorted(expr.args, key=default_sort_key)
1077     coeff_muls = [x.as_coeff_Mul() for x in args]
1078     surds = [x[1]**2 for x in coeff_muls if x[1].is_Pow]
1079     surds.sort(key=default_sort_key)
1080     g, b1, b2 = _split_gcd(*surds)
1081     g2 = g
1082     if not b2 and len(b1) >= 2:
1083         b1n = [x/g for x in b1]
1084         b1n = [x for x in b1n if x != 1]
1085         # only a common factor has been factored; split again
1086         g1, b1n, b2 = _split_gcd(*b1n)
1087         g2 = g*g1
1088     a1v, a2v = [], []
1089     for c, s in coeff_muls:
1090         if s.is_Pow and s.exp == S.Half:
1091             s1 = s.base
1092             if s1 in b1:
1093                 a1v.append(c*sqrt(s1/g2))
1094             else:
1095                 a2v.append(c*s)
1096         else:
1097             a2v.append(c*s)
1098     a = Add(*a1v)
1099     b = Add(*a2v)
1100     return g2, a, b

1103 def _split_gcd(*a):
1104     """
1105     split the list of integers ``a`` into a list of integers, ``a1`` having
1106     ``g = gcd(a1)``, and a list ``a2`` whose elements are not divisible by
1107     ``g``.  Returns ``g, a1, a2``
1108 
1109     Examples
1110     ========
1111 
1112     >>> from sympy.simplify.radsimp import _split_gcd
1113     >>> _split_gcd(55, 35, 22, 14, 77, 10)
1114     (5, [55, 35, 10], [22, 14, 77])
1115     """
1116     g = a[0]
1117     b1 = [g]
1118     b2 = []
1119     for x in a[1:]:
1120         g1 = gcd(g, x)
1121         if g1 == 1:
1122             b2.append(x)
1123         else:
1124             g = g1
1125             b1.append(x)
1126     return g, b1, b2

21     >>> from sympy.functions.elementary.miscellaneous import sqrt
22     >>> from sympy.simplify.sqrtdenest import sqrt_depth

75 def _subsets(n):
76     """
77     Returns all possible subsets of the set (0, 1, ..., n-1) except the
78     empty set, listed in reversed lexicographical order according to binary
79     representation, so that the case of the fourth root is treated last.
80 
81     Examples
82     ========
83 
84     >>> from sympy.simplify.sqrtdenest import _subsets
85     >>> _subsets(2)
86     [[1, 0], [0, 1], [1, 1]]
87 
88     """
89     if n == 1:
90         a = [[1]]
91     elif n == 2:
92         a = [[1, 0], [0, 1], [1, 1]]
93     elif n == 3:
94         a = [[1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [1, 1, 0],
95              [0, 0, 1], [1, 0, 1], [0, 1, 1], [1, 1, 1]]
96     else:
97         b = _subsets(n - 1)
98         a0 = [x + [0] for x in b]
99         a1 = [x + [1] for x in b]
100         a = a0 + [[0]*(n - 1) + [1]] + a1
101     return a

104 def sqrtdenest(expr, max_iter=3):
105     """Denests sqrts in an expression that contain other square roots
106     if possible, otherwise returns the expr unchanged. This is based on the
107     algorithms of [1].
108 
109     Examples
110     ========
111 
112     >>> from sympy.simplify.sqrtdenest import sqrtdenest
113     >>> from sympy import sqrt
114     >>> sqrtdenest(sqrt(5 + 2 * sqrt(6)))

116 
117     See Also
118     ========
119 
120     sympy.solvers.solvers.unrad

122     References
123     ==========
124 
125     .. [1] http://researcher.watson.ibm.com/researcher/files/us-fagin/symb85.pdf
126 
127     .. [2] D. J. Jeffrey and A. D. Rich, 'Symplifying Square Roots of Square Roots
128            by Denesting' (available at http://www.cybertester.com/data/denest.pdf)
129

140 def _sqrt_match(p):
141     """Return [a, b, r] for p.match(a + b*sqrt(r)) where, in addition to
142     matching, sqrt(r) also has then maximal sqrt_depth among addends of p.
143 
144     Examples
145     ========
146 
147     >>> from sympy.functions.elementary.miscellaneous import sqrt
148     >>> from sympy.simplify.sqrtdenest import _sqrt_match
149     >>> _sqrt_match(1 + sqrt(2) + sqrt(2)*sqrt(3) +  2*sqrt(1+sqrt(5)))
150     [1 + sqrt(2) + sqrt(6), 2, 1 + sqrt(5)]
151     """
152     from sympy.simplify.radsimp import split_surds
153 
154     p = _mexpand(p)
155     if p.is_Number:
156         res = (p, S.Zero, S.Zero)
157     elif p.is_Add:
158         pargs = sorted(p.args, key=default_sort_key)
159         if all((x**2).is_Rational for x in pargs):
160             r, b, a = split_surds(p)
161             res = a, b, r
162             return list(res)
163         # to make the process canonical, the argument is included in the tuple
164         # so when the max is selected, it will be the largest arg having a
165         # given depth
166         v = [(sqrt_depth(x), x, i) for i, x in enumerate(pargs)]
167         nmax = max(v, key=default_sort_key)
168         if nmax[0] == 0:
169             res = []
170         else:
171             # select r
172             depth, _, i = nmax
173             r = pargs.pop(i)
174             v.pop(i)
175             b = S.One
176             if r.is_Mul:
177                 bv = []
178                 rv = []
179                 for x in r.args:
180                     if sqrt_depth(x) < depth:
181                         bv.append(x)
182                     else:
183                         rv.append(x)
184                 b = Mul._from_args(bv)
185                 r = Mul._from_args(rv)
186             # collect terms comtaining r
187             a1 = []
188             b1 = [b]
189             for x in v:
190                 if x[0] < depth:
191                     a1.append(x[1])
192                 else:
193                     x1 = x[1]
194                     if x1 == r:
195                         b1.append(1)
196                     else:
197                         if x1.is_Mul:
198                             x1args = list(x1.args)
199                             if r in x1args:
200                                 x1args.remove(r)
201                                 b1.append(Mul(*x1args))
202                             else:
203                                 a1.append(x[1])
204                         else:
205                             a1.append(x[1])
206             a = Add(*a1)
207             b = Add(*b1)
208             res = (a, b, r**2)
209     else:
210         b, r = p.as_coeff_Mul()
211         if is_sqrt(r):
212             res = (S.Zero, b, r**2)
213         else:
214             res = []
215     return list(res)

259 def _sqrtdenest_rec(expr):
260     """Helper that denests the square root of three or more surds.
261 
262     It returns the denested expression; if it cannot be denested it
263     throws SqrtdenestStopIteration
264 
265     Algorithm: expr.base is in the extension Q_m = Q(sqrt(r_1),..,sqrt(r_k));
266     split expr.base = a + b*sqrt(r_k), where `a` and `b` are on
267     Q_(m-1) = Q(sqrt(r_1),..,sqrt(r_(k-1))); then a**2 - b**2*r_k is
268     on Q_(m-1); denest sqrt(a**2 - b**2*r_k) and so on.
269     See [1], section 6.
270 
271     Examples
272     ========
273 
274     >>> from sympy import sqrt
275     >>> from sympy.simplify.sqrtdenest import _sqrtdenest_rec
276     >>> _sqrtdenest_rec(sqrt(-72*sqrt(2) + 158*sqrt(5) + 498))
277     -sqrt(10) + sqrt(2) + 9 + 9*sqrt(5)
278     >>> w=-6*sqrt(55)-6*sqrt(35)-2*sqrt(22)-2*sqrt(14)+2*sqrt(77)+6*sqrt(10)+65
279     >>> _sqrtdenest_rec(sqrt(w))
280     -sqrt(11) - sqrt(7) + sqrt(2) + 3*sqrt(5)
281     """
282     from sympy.simplify.radsimp import radsimp, rad_rationalize, split_surds
283     if not expr.is_Pow:
284         return sqrtdenest(expr)
285     if expr.base < 0:
286         return sqrt(-1)*_sqrtdenest_rec(sqrt(-expr.base))
287     g, a, b = split_surds(expr.base)
288     a = a*sqrt(g)
289     if a < b:
290         a, b = b, a
291     c2 = _mexpand(a**2 - b**2)
292     if len(c2.args) > 2:
293         g, a1, b1 = split_surds(c2)
294         a1 = a1*sqrt(g)
295         if a1 < b1:
296             a1, b1 = b1, a1
297         c2_1 = _mexpand(a1**2 - b1**2)
298         c_1 = _sqrtdenest_rec(sqrt(c2_1))
299         d_1 = _sqrtdenest_rec(sqrt(a1 + c_1))
300         num, den = rad_rationalize(b1, d_1)
301         c = _mexpand(d_1/sqrt(2) + num/(den*sqrt(2)))
302     else:
303         c = _sqrtdenest1(sqrt(c2))
304 
305     if sqrt_depth(c) > 1:
306         raise SqrtdenestStopIteration
307     ac = a + c
308     if len(ac.args) >= len(expr.args):
309         if count_ops(ac) >= count_ops(expr.base):
310             raise SqrtdenestStopIteration
311     d = sqrtdenest(sqrt(ac))
312     if sqrt_depth(d) > 1:
313         raise SqrtdenestStopIteration
314     num, den = rad_rationalize(b, d)
315     r = d/sqrt(2) + num/(den*sqrt(2))
316     r = radsimp(r)
317     return _mexpand(r)

379 def _sqrt_symbolic_denest(a, b, r):
380     """Given an expression, sqrt(a + b*sqrt(b)), return the denested
381     expression or None.
382 
383     Algorithm:
384     If r = ra + rb*sqrt(rr), try replacing sqrt(rr) in ``a`` with
385     (y**2 - ra)/rb, and if the result is a quadratic, ca*y**2 + cb*y + cc, and
386     (cb + b)**2 - 4*ca*cc is 0, then sqrt(a + b*sqrt(r)) can be rewritten as
387     sqrt(ca*(sqrt(r) + (cb + b)/(2*ca))**2).
388 
389     Examples
390     ========
391 
392     >>> from sympy.simplify.sqrtdenest import _sqrt_symbolic_denest, sqrtdenest
393     >>> from sympy import sqrt, Symbol
394     >>> from sympy.abc import x
395 
396     >>> a, b, r = 16 - 2*sqrt(29), 2, -10*sqrt(29) + 55
397     >>> _sqrt_symbolic_denest(a, b, r)
398     sqrt(11 - 2*sqrt(29)) + sqrt(5)
399 
400     If the expression is numeric, it will be simplified:
401 
402     >>> w = sqrt(sqrt(sqrt(3) + 1) + 1) + 1 + sqrt(2)
403     >>> sqrtdenest(sqrt((w**2).expand()))
404     1 + sqrt(2) + sqrt(1 + sqrt(1 + sqrt(3)))
405 
406     Otherwise, it will only be simplified if assumptions allow:
407 
408     >>> w = w.subs(sqrt(3), sqrt(x + 3))
409     >>> sqrtdenest(sqrt((w**2).expand()))
410     sqrt((sqrt(sqrt(sqrt(x + 3) + 1) + 1) + 1 + sqrt(2))**2)
411 
412     Notice that the argument of the sqrt is a square. If x is made positive
413     then the sqrt of the square is resolved:
414 
415     >>> _.subs(x, Symbol('x', positive=True))
416     sqrt(sqrt(sqrt(x + 3) + 1) + 1) + 1 + sqrt(2)
417     """
418 
419     a, b, r = map(sympify, (a, b, r))
420     rval = _sqrt_match(r)
421     if not rval:
422         return None
423     ra, rb, rr = rval
424     if rb:
425         y = Dummy('y', positive=True)
426         try:
427             newa = Poly(a.subs(sqrt(rr), (y**2 - ra)/rb), y)
428         except PolynomialError:
429             return None
430         if newa.degree() == 2:

458     """denest expr = sqrt(a + b*sqrt(r))

467     4*A**4 - 4*a*A**2 + b**2*r = 0                               (1)
468     sqd = sqrt(a**2 - b**2*r)

470     A = sqrt(a/2 +/- sqd/2)

472     so if sqd can be denested, it is done by

474     Similarly for A.
475     Examples of solutions (in both cases a and sqd are positive):
476

487       sqd = 29 + 20*sqrt(3)

489     Define B = b/2*A; eq.(1) implies a = A**2 + B**2*r; then
490     expr**2 = a + b*sqrt(r) = (A + B*sqrt(r))**2
491

392     @staticmethod
393     def from_index_summation(expr, first_index=None, last_index=None, dimensions=None):
394         r"""
395         Parse expression of matrices with explicitly summed indices into a
396         matrix expression without indices, if possible.
397 
398         This transformation expressed in mathematical notation:
399 
400         `\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} A_{i,j} B_{j,k} \Longrightarrow \mathbf{A}\cdot \mathbf{B}`
401 
402         Optional parameter ``first_index``: specify which free index to use as
403         the index starting the expression.
404 
405         Examples
406         ========
407 
408         >>> from sympy import MatrixSymbol, MatrixExpr, Sum, Symbol
409         >>> from sympy.abc import i, j, k, l, N
410         >>> A = MatrixSymbol("A", N, N)
411         >>> B = MatrixSymbol("B", N, N)
412         >>> expr = Sum(A[i, j]*B[j, k], (j, 0, N-1))
413         >>> MatrixExpr.from_index_summation(expr)
414         A*B
415 
416         Transposition is detected:
417 
418         >>> expr = Sum(A[j, i]*B[j, k], (j, 0, N-1))
419         >>> MatrixExpr.from_index_summation(expr)
420         A.T*B
421 
422         Detect the trace:
423 
424         >>> expr = Sum(A[i, i], (i, 0, N-1))
425         >>> MatrixExpr.from_index_summation(expr)
426         Trace(A)
427 
428         More complicated expressions:
429 
430         >>> expr = Sum(A[i, j]*B[k, j]*A[l, k], (j, 0, N-1), (k, 0, N-1))
431         >>> MatrixExpr.from_index_summation(expr)
432         A*B.T*A.T
433         """
434         from sympy import Sum, Mul, Add, MatMul, transpose, trace
435         from sympy.strategies.traverse import bottom_up
436 
437         def remove_matelement(expr, i1, i2):
438 
439             def repl_match(pos):
440                 def func(x):
441                     if not isinstance(x, MatrixElement):
442                         return False
443                     if x.args[pos] != i1:
444                         return False
445                     if x.args[3-pos] == 0:
446                         if x.args[0].shape[2-pos] == 1:
447                             return True
448                         else:
449                             return False
450                     return True
451                 return func
452 
453             expr = expr.replace(repl_match(1),
454                 lambda x: x.args[0])
455             expr = expr.replace(repl_match(2),
456                 lambda x: transpose(x.args[0]))
457 
458             # Make sure that all Mul are transformed to MatMul and that they
459             # are flattened:
460             rule = bottom_up(lambda x: reduce(lambda a, b: a*b, x.args) if isinstance(x, (Mul, MatMul)) else x)
461             return rule(expr)
462 
463         def recurse_expr(expr, index_ranges={}):
464             if expr.is_Mul:
465                 nonmatargs = []
466                 pos_arg = []
467                 pos_ind = []
468                 dlinks = {}
469                 link_ind = []
470                 counter = 0
471                 args_ind = []
472                 for arg in expr.args:
473                     retvals = recurse_expr(arg, index_ranges)
474                     assert isinstance(retvals, list)
475                     if isinstance(retvals, list):
476                         for i in retvals:
477                             args_ind.append(i)
478                     else:
479                         args_ind.append(retvals)
480                 for arg_symbol, arg_indices in args_ind:
481                     if arg_indices is None:
482                         nonmatargs.append(arg_symbol)
483                         continue
484                     if isinstance(arg_symbol, MatrixElement):
485                         arg_symbol = arg_symbol.args[0]
486                     pos_arg.append(arg_symbol)
487                     pos_ind.append(arg_indices)
488                     link_ind.append([None]*len(arg_indices))
489                     for i, ind in enumerate(arg_indices):
490                         if ind in dlinks:
491                             other_i = dlinks[ind]
492                             link_ind[counter][i] = other_i
493                             link_ind[other_i[0]][other_i[1]] = (counter, i)
494                         dlinks[ind] = (counter, i)
495                     counter += 1
496                 counter2 = 0
497                 lines = {}
498                 while counter2 < len(link_ind):
499                     for i, e in enumerate(link_ind):
500                         if None in e:
501                             line_start_index = (i, e.index(None))
502                             break
503                     cur_ind_pos = line_start_index
504                     cur_line = []
505                     index1 = pos_ind[cur_ind_pos[0]][cur_ind_pos[1]]
506                     while True:
507                         d, r = cur_ind_pos
508                         if pos_arg[d] != 1:
509                             if r % 2 == 1:
510                                 cur_line.append(transpose(pos_arg[d]))
511                             else:
512                                 cur_line.append(pos_arg[d])
513                         next_ind_pos = link_ind[d][1-r]
514                         counter2 += 1
515                         # Mark as visited, there will be no `None` anymore:
516                         link_ind[d] = (-1, -1)
517                         if next_ind_pos is None:
518                             index2 = pos_ind[d][1-r]
519                             lines[(index1, index2)] = cur_line
520                             break
521                         cur_ind_pos = next_ind_pos
522                 lines = {k: MatMul.fromiter(v) if len(v) != 1 else v[0] for k, v in lines.items()}
523                 return [(Mul.fromiter(nonmatargs), None)] + [
524                     (MatrixElement(a, i, j), (i, j)) for (i, j), a in lines.items()
525                 ]
526             elif expr.is_Add:
527                 res = [recurse_expr(i) for i in expr.args]
528                 d = collections.defaultdict(list)
529                 for res_addend in res:
530                     scalar = 1
531                     for elem, indices in res_addend:
532                         if indices is None:
533                             scalar = elem
534                             continue
535                         indices = tuple(sorted(indices, key=default_sort_key))
536                         d[indices].append(scalar*remove_matelement(elem, *indices))
537                         scalar = 1
538                 return [(MatrixElement(Add.fromiter(v), *k), k) for k, v in d.items()]
539             elif isinstance(expr, KroneckerDelta):
540                 i1, i2 = expr.args
541                 if dimensions is not None:
542                     identity = Identity(dimensions[0])
543                 else:
544                     identity = S.One
545                 return [(MatrixElement(identity, i1, i2), (i1, i2))]
546             elif isinstance(expr, MatrixElement):
547                 matrix_symbol, i1, i2 = expr.args
548                 if i1 in index_ranges:
549                     r1, r2 = index_ranges[i1]
550                     if r1 != 0 or matrix_symbol.shape[0] != r2+1:
551                         raise ValueError("index range mismatch: {0} vs. (0, {1})".format(
552                             (r1, r2), matrix_symbol.shape[0]))
553                 if i2 in index_ranges:
554                     r1, r2 = index_ranges[i2]
555                     if r1 != 0 or matrix_symbol.shape[1] != r2+1:
556                         raise ValueError("index range mismatch: {0} vs. (0, {1})".format(
557                             (r1, r2), matrix_symbol.shape[1]))
558                 if (i1 == i2) and (i1 in index_ranges):
559                     return [(trace(matrix_symbol), None)]
560                 return [(MatrixElement(matrix_symbol, i1, i2), (i1, i2))]
561             elif isinstance(expr, Sum):
562                 return recurse_expr(
563                     expr.args[0],
564                     index_ranges={i[0]: i[1:] for i in expr.args[1:]}
565                 )
566             else:
567                 return [(expr, None)]
568 
569         retvals = recurse_expr(expr)
570         factors, indices = zip(*retvals)
571         retexpr = Mul.fromiter(factors)
572         if len(indices) == 0 or list(set(indices)) == [None]:
573             return retexpr
574         if first_index is None:
575             for i in indices:
576                 if i is not None:
577                     ind0 = i
578                     break
579             return remove_matelement(retexpr, *ind0)
580         else:
581             return remove_matelement(retexpr, first_index, last_index)

198 SymPy was started by Ondřej Čertík in 2005, he wrote some code during the
199 summer, then he wrote some more code during summer 2006. In February 2007,
200 Fabian Pedregosa joined the project and helped fixed many things, contributed
201 documentation and made it alive again. 5 students (Mateusz Paprocki, Brian
202 Jorgensen, Jason Gedge, Robert Schwarz, and Chris Wu) improved SymPy incredibly
203 during summer 2007 as part of the Google Summer of Code. Pearu Peterson
204 joined the development during the summer 2007 and he has made SymPy much more
205 competitive by rewriting the core from scratch, that has made it from 10x to
206 100x faster. Jurjen N.E. Bos has contributed pretty printing and other patches.
207 Fredrik Johansson has written mpmath and contributed a lot of patches.
208 
209 SymPy has participated in every Google Summer of Code since 2007. You can see
210 https://github.com/sympy/sympy/wiki#google-summer-of-code for full details.
211 Each year has improved SymPy by bounds. Most of SymPy's development has come
212 from Google Summer of Code students.

214 In 2011, Ondřej Čertík stepped down as lead developer, with Aaron Meurer, who
215 also started as a Google Summer of Code student, taking his place. Ondřej
216 Čertík is still active in the community but is too busy with work and family

65 def _remove_gcd(*x):

101 def diophantine(eq, param=symbols("t", integer=True), syms=None,
102                 permute=False):
103     """
104     Simplify the solution procedure of diophantine equation ``eq`` by
105     converting it into a product of terms which should equal zero.
106 
107     For example, when solving, `x^2 - y^2 = 0` this is treated as
108     `(x + y)(x - y) = 0` and `x + y = 0` and `x - y = 0` are solved
109     independently and combined. Each term is solved by calling
110     ``diop_solve()``. (Although it is possible to call ``diop_solve()``
111     directly, one must be careful to pass an equation in the correct
112     form and to interpret the output correctly; ``diophantine()`` is
113     the public-facing function to use in general.)
114 
115     Output of ``diophantine()`` is a set of tuples. The elements of the
116     tuple are the solutions for each variable in the equation and
117     are arranged according to the alphabetic ordering of the variables.
118     e.g. For an equation with two variables, `a` and `b`, the first
119     element of the tuple is the solution for `a` and the second for `b`.
120 
121     Usage
122     =====
123 
124     ``diophantine(eq, t, syms)``: Solve the diophantine
125     equation ``eq``.
126     ``t`` is the optional parameter to be used by ``diop_solve()``.
127     ``syms`` is an optional list of symbols which determines the
128     order of the elements in the returned tuple.
129 
130     By default, only the base solution is returned. If ``permute`` is set to
131     True then permutations of the base solution and/or permutations of the
132     signs of the values will be returned when applicable.
133 
134     >>> from sympy.solvers.diophantine import diophantine
135     >>> from sympy.abc import a, b
136     >>> eq = a**4 + b**4 - (2**4 + 3**4)
137     >>> diophantine(eq)
138     {(2, 3)}
139     >>> diophantine(eq, permute=True)
140     {(-3, -2), (-3, 2), (-2, -3), (-2, 3), (2, -3), (2, 3), (3, -2), (3, 2)}
141 
142     Details
143     =======
144 
145     ``eq`` should be an expression which is assumed to be zero.
146     ``t`` is the parameter to be used in the solution.
147 
148     Examples
149     ========
150 
151     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
152     >>> diophantine(x**2 - y**2)
153     {(t_0, -t_0), (t_0, t_0)}
154 
155     >>> diophantine(x*(2*x + 3*y - z))
156     {(0, n1, n2), (t_0, t_1, 2*t_0 + 3*t_1)}
157     >>> diophantine(x**2 + 3*x*y + 4*x)
158     {(0, n1), (3*t_0 - 4, -t_0)}
159 
160     See Also
161     ========
162 
163     diop_solve()
164     sympy.utilities.iterables.permute_signs
165     sympy.utilities.iterables.signed_permutations
166     """
167 
168     from sympy.utilities.iterables import (
169         subsets, permute_signs, signed_permutations)
170 
171     if isinstance(eq, Eq):
172         eq = eq.lhs - eq.rhs
173 
174     try:
175         var = list(eq.expand(force=True).free_symbols)
176         var.sort(key=default_sort_key)
177         if syms:
178             if not is_sequence(syms):
179                 raise TypeError(
180                     'syms should be given as a sequence, e.g. a list')
181             syms = [i for i in syms if i in var]
182             if syms != var:
183                 dict_sym_index = dict(zip(syms, range(len(syms))))
184                 return {tuple([t[dict_sym_index[i]] for i in var])
185                             for t in diophantine(eq, param)}
186         n, d = eq.as_numer_denom()
187         if n.is_number:
188             return set()
189         if not d.is_number:
190             dsol = diophantine(d)
191             good = diophantine(n) - dsol
192             return {s for s in good if _mexpand(d.subs(zip(var, s)))}
193         else:
194             eq = n
195         eq = factor_terms(eq)
196         assert not eq.is_number
197         eq = eq.as_independent(*var, as_Add=False)[1]
198         p = Poly(eq)
199         assert not any(g.is_number for g in p.gens)
200         eq = p.as_expr()
201         assert eq.is_polynomial()
202     except (GeneratorsNeeded, AssertionError, AttributeError):
203         raise TypeError(filldedent('''
204     Equation should be a polynomial with Rational coefficients.'''))
205 
206     # permute only sign
207     do_permute_signs = False
208     # permute sign and values
209     do_permute_signs_var = False
210     # permute few signs
211     permute_few_signs = False
212     try:
213         # if we know that factoring should not be attempted, skip
214         # the factoring step
215         v, c, t = classify_diop(eq)
216 
217         # check for permute sign
218         if permute:
219             len_var = len(v)
220             permute_signs_for = [
221                 'general_sum_of_squares',
222                 'general_sum_of_even_powers']
223             permute_signs_check = [
224                 'homogeneous_ternary_quadratic',
225                 'homogeneous_ternary_quadratic_normal',
226                 'binary_quadratic']
227             if t in permute_signs_for:
228                 do_permute_signs_var = True
229             elif t in permute_signs_check:
230                 # if all the variables in eq have even powers
231                 # then do_permute_sign = True
232                 if len_var == 3:
233                     var_mul = list(subsets(v, 2))
234                     # here var_mul is like [(x, y), (x, z), (y, z)]
235                     xy_coeff = True
236                     x_coeff = True
237                     var1_mul_var2 = map(lambda a: a[0]*a[1], var_mul)
238                     # if coeff(y*z), coeff(y*x), coeff(x*z) is not 0 then
239                     # `xy_coeff` => True and do_permute_sign => False.
240                     # Means no permuted solution.
241                     for v1_mul_v2 in var1_mul_var2:
242                         try:
243                             coeff = c[v1_mul_v2]
244                         except KeyError:
245                             coeff = 0
246                         xy_coeff = bool(xy_coeff) and bool(coeff)
247                     var_mul = list(subsets(v, 1))
248                     # here var_mul is like [(x,), (y, )]
249                     for v1 in var_mul:
250                         try:
251                             coeff = c[v1[0]]
252                         except KeyError:
253                             coeff = 0
254                         x_coeff = bool(x_coeff) and bool(coeff)
255                     if not any([xy_coeff, x_coeff]):
256                         # means only x**2, y**2, z**2, const is present
257                         do_permute_signs = True
258                     elif not x_coeff:
259                         permute_few_signs = True
260                 elif len_var == 2:
261                     var_mul = list(subsets(v, 2))
262                     # here var_mul is like [(x, y)]
263                     xy_coeff = True
264                     x_coeff = True
265                     var1_mul_var2 = map(lambda x: x[0]*x[1], var_mul)
266                     for v1_mul_v2 in var1_mul_var2:
267                         try:
268                             coeff = c[v1_mul_v2]
269                         except KeyError:
270                             coeff = 0
271                         xy_coeff = bool(xy_coeff) and bool(coeff)
272                     var_mul = list(subsets(v, 1))
273                     # here var_mul is like [(x,), (y, )]
274                     for v1 in var_mul:
275                         try:
276                             coeff = c[v1[0]]
277                         except KeyError:
278                             coeff = 0
279                         x_coeff = bool(x_coeff) and bool(coeff)
280                     if not any([xy_coeff, x_coeff]):
281                         # means only x**2, y**2 and const is present
282                         # so we can get more soln by permuting this soln.
283                         do_permute_signs = True
284                     elif not x_coeff:
285                         # when coeff(x), coeff(y) is not present then signs of
286                         #  x, y can be permuted such that their sign are same
287                         # as sign of x*y.
288                         # e.g 1. (x_val,y_val)=> (x_val,y_val), (-x_val,-y_val)
289                         # 2. (-x_vall, y_val)=> (-x_val,y_val), (x_val,-y_val)
290                         permute_few_signs = True
291         if t == 'general_sum_of_squares':
292             # trying to factor such expressions will sometimes hang
293             terms = [(eq, 1)]
294         else:
295             raise TypeError
296     except (TypeError, NotImplementedError):
297         terms = factor_list(eq)[1]
298 
299     sols = set([])
300 
301     for term in terms:
302 
303         base, _ = term
304         var_t, _, eq_type = classify_diop(base, _dict=False)
305         _, base = signsimp(base, evaluate=False).as_coeff_Mul()
306         solution = diop_solve(base, param)
307 
308         if eq_type in [
309                 "linear",
310                 "homogeneous_ternary_quadratic",
311                 "homogeneous_ternary_quadratic_normal",
312                 "general_pythagorean"]:
313             sols.add(merge_solution(var, var_t, solution))
314 
315         elif eq_type in [
316                 "binary_quadratic",
317                 "general_sum_of_squares",
318                 "general_sum_of_even_powers",
319                 "univariate"]:
320             for sol in solution:
321                 sols.add(merge_solution(var, var_t, sol))
322 
323         else:
324             raise NotImplementedError('unhandled type: %s' % eq_type)

326     # remove null merge results
327     if () in sols:
328         sols.remove(())
329     null = tuple([0]*len(var))
330     # if there is no solution, return trivial solution
331     if not sols and eq.subs(zip(var, null)).is_zero:
332         sols.add(null)

334     for sol in sols:
335         if all(_is_int(s) for s in sol):
336             if do_permute_signs:
337                 permuted_sign = set(permute_signs(sol))
338                 final_soln.update(permuted_sign)
339             elif permute_few_signs:
340                 lst = list(permute_signs(sol))
341                 lst = list(filter(lambda x: x[0]*x[1] == sol[1]*sol[0], lst))
342                 permuted_sign = set(lst)
343                 final_soln.update(permuted_sign)
344             elif do_permute_signs_var:
345                 permuted_sign_var = set(signed_permutations(sol))
346                 final_soln.update(permuted_sign_var)
347             else:
348                 final_soln.add(sol)
349         else:
350                 final_soln.add(sol)
351     return final_soln

354 def merge_solution(var, var_t, solution):
355     """
356     This is used to construct the full solution from the solutions of sub
357     equations.
358 
359     For example when solving the equation `(x - y)(x^2 + y^2 - z^2) = 0`,
360     solutions for each of the equations `x - y = 0` and `x^2 + y^2 - z^2` are
361     found independently. Solutions for `x - y = 0` are `(x, y) = (t, t)`. But
362     we should introduce a value for z when we output the solution for the
363     original equation. This function converts `(t, t)` into `(t, t, n_{1})`
364     where `n_{1}` is an integer parameter.
365     """
366     sol = []
367 
368     if None in solution:
369         return ()
370 
371     solution = iter(solution)
372     params = numbered_symbols("n", integer=True, start=1)
373     for v in var:
374         if v in var_t:
375             sol.append(next(solution))
376         else:
377             sol.append(next(params))
378 
379     for val, symb in zip(sol, var):
380         if check_assumptions(val, **symb.assumptions0) is False:
381             return tuple()
382 
383     return tuple(sol)

386 def diop_solve(eq, param=symbols("t", integer=True)):
387     """
388     Solves the diophantine equation ``eq``.
389 
390     Unlike ``diophantine()``, factoring of ``eq`` is not attempted. Uses
391     ``classify_diop()`` to determine the type of the equation and calls
392     the appropriate solver function.
393 
394     Use of ``diophantine()`` is recommended over other helper functions.
395     ``diop_solve()`` can return either a set or a tuple depending on the
396     nature of the equation.
397 
398     Usage
399     =====
400 
401     ``diop_solve(eq, t)``: Solve diophantine equation, ``eq`` using ``t``
402     as a parameter if needed.
403 
404     Details
405     =======
406 
407     ``eq`` should be an expression which is assumed to be zero.
408     ``t`` is a parameter to be used in the solution.
409 
410     Examples
411     ========
412 
413     >>> from sympy.solvers.diophantine import diop_solve
414     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z, w
415     >>> diop_solve(2*x + 3*y - 5)
416     (3*t_0 - 5, 5 - 2*t_0)
417     >>> diop_solve(4*x + 3*y - 4*z + 5)
418     (t_0, 8*t_0 + 4*t_1 + 5, 7*t_0 + 3*t_1 + 5)
419     >>> diop_solve(x + 3*y - 4*z + w - 6)
420     (t_0, t_0 + t_1, 6*t_0 + 5*t_1 + 4*t_2 - 6, 5*t_0 + 4*t_1 + 3*t_2 - 6)
421     >>> diop_solve(x**2 + y**2 - 5)
422     {(-2, -1), (-2, 1), (-1, -2), (-1, 2), (1, -2), (1, 2), (2, -1), (2, 1)}
423 
424 
425     See Also
426     ========
427 
428     diophantine()
429     """
430     var, coeff, eq_type = classify_diop(eq, _dict=False)
431 
432     if eq_type == "linear":
433         return _diop_linear(var, coeff, param)
434 
435     elif eq_type == "binary_quadratic":
436         return _diop_quadratic(var, coeff, param)
437 
438     elif eq_type == "homogeneous_ternary_quadratic":
439         x_0, y_0, z_0 = _diop_ternary_quadratic(var, coeff)
440         return _parametrize_ternary_quadratic(
441             (x_0, y_0, z_0), var, coeff)
442 
443     elif eq_type == "homogeneous_ternary_quadratic_normal":
444         x_0, y_0, z_0 = _diop_ternary_quadratic_normal(var, coeff)
445         return _parametrize_ternary_quadratic(
446             (x_0, y_0, z_0), var, coeff)
447 
448     elif eq_type == "general_pythagorean":
449         return _diop_general_pythagorean(var, coeff, param)
450 
451     elif eq_type == "univariate":
452         return set([(int(i),) for i in solveset_real(
453             eq, var[0]).intersect(S.Integers)])
454 
455     elif eq_type == "general_sum_of_squares":
456         return _diop_general_sum_of_squares(var, -int(coeff[1]), limit=S.Infinity)
457 
458     elif eq_type == "general_sum_of_even_powers":
459         for k in coeff.keys():
460             if k.is_Pow and coeff[k]:
461                 p = k.exp
462         return _diop_general_sum_of_even_powers(var, p, -int(coeff[1]), limit=S.Infinity)
463 
464     if eq_type is not None and eq_type not in diop_known:
465             raise ValueError(filldedent('''
466     Alhough this type of equation was identified, it is not yet
467     handled. It should, however, be listed in `diop_known` at the
468     top of this file. Developers should see comments at the end of
469     `classify_diop`.
470             '''))  # pragma: no cover
471     else:
472         raise NotImplementedError(
473             'No solver has been written for %s.' % eq_type)
474

476 def classify_diop(eq, _dict=True):
477     # docstring supplied externally
478     try:
479         var = list(eq.free_symbols)
480         assert var
481     except (AttributeError, AssertionError):
482         raise ValueError('equation should have 1 or more free symbols')
483     var.sort(key=default_sort_key)
484     eq = eq.expand(force=True)
485     coeff = eq.as_coefficients_dict()
486     if not all(_is_int(c) for c in coeff.values()):
487         raise TypeError("Coefficients should be Integers")
488 
489     diop_type = None
490     total_degree = Poly(eq).total_degree()
491     homogeneous = 1 not in coeff
492     if total_degree == 1:
493         diop_type = "linear"
494 
495     elif len(var) == 1:
496         diop_type = "univariate"
497 
498     elif total_degree == 2 and len(var) == 2:
499         diop_type = "binary_quadratic"
500 
501     elif total_degree == 2 and len(var) == 3 and homogeneous:
502         if set(coeff) & set(var):
503             diop_type = "inhomogeneous_ternary_quadratic"
504         else:
505             nonzero = [k for k in coeff if coeff[k]]
506             if len(nonzero) == 3 and all(i**2 in nonzero for i in var):
507                 diop_type = "homogeneous_ternary_quadratic_normal"
508             else:
509                 diop_type = "homogeneous_ternary_quadratic"
510 
511     elif total_degree == 2 and len(var) >= 3:
512         if set(coeff) & set(var):
513             diop_type = "inhomogeneous_general_quadratic"
514         else:
515             # there may be Pow keys like x**2 or Mul keys like x*y
516             if any(k.is_Mul for k in coeff):  # cross terms
517                 if not homogeneous:
518                     diop_type = "inhomogeneous_general_quadratic"
519                 else:
520                     diop_type = "homogeneous_general_quadratic"
521             else:  # all squares: x**2 + y**2 + ... + constant
522                 if all(coeff[k] == 1 for k in coeff if k != 1):
523                     diop_type = "general_sum_of_squares"
524                 elif all(is_square(abs(coeff[k])) for k in coeff):
525                     if abs(sum(sign(coeff[k]) for k in coeff)) == \
526                             len(var) - 2:
527                         # all but one has the same sign
528                         # e.g. 4*x**2 + y**2 - 4*z**2
529                         diop_type = "general_pythagorean"
530 
531     elif total_degree == 3 and len(var) == 2:
532         diop_type = "cubic_thue"
533 
534     elif (total_degree > 3 and total_degree % 2 == 0 and
535             all(k.is_Pow and k.exp == total_degree for k in coeff if k != 1)):
536         if all(coeff[k] == 1 for k in coeff if k != 1):
537             diop_type = 'general_sum_of_even_powers'
538 
539     if diop_type is not None:
540         return var, dict(coeff) if _dict else coeff, diop_type
541 
542     # new diop type instructions
543     # --------------------------
544     # if this error raises and the equation *can* be classified,
545     #  * it should be identified in the if-block above
546     #  * the type should be added to the diop_known
547     # if a solver can be written for it,
548     #  * a dedicated handler should be written (e.g. diop_linear)
549     #  * it should be passed to that handler in diop_solve
550     raise NotImplementedError(filldedent('''
551         This equation is not yet recognized or else has not been
552         simplified sufficiently to put it in a form recognized by
553         diop_classify().'''))
554

594 def diop_linear(eq, param=symbols("t", integer=True)):
595     """
596     Solves linear diophantine equations.
597 
598     A linear diophantine equation is an equation of the form `a_{1}x_{1} +
599     a_{2}x_{2} + .. + a_{n}x_{n} = 0` where `a_{1}, a_{2}, ..a_{n}` are
600     integer constants and `x_{1}, x_{2}, ..x_{n}` are integer variables.
601 
602     Usage
603     =====
604 
605     ``diop_linear(eq)``: Returns a tuple containing solutions to the
606     diophantine equation ``eq``. Values in the tuple is arranged in the same
607     order as the sorted variables.
608 
609     Details
610     =======
611 
612     ``eq`` is a linear diophantine equation which is assumed to be zero.
613     ``param`` is the parameter to be used in the solution.
614 
615     Examples
616     ========
617 
618     >>> from sympy.solvers.diophantine import diop_linear
619     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z, t
620     >>> diop_linear(2*x - 3*y - 5) # solves equation 2*x - 3*y - 5 == 0
621     (3*t_0 - 5, 2*t_0 - 5)
622 
623     Here x = -3*t_0 - 5 and y = -2*t_0 - 5
624 
625     >>> diop_linear(2*x - 3*y - 4*z -3)
626     (t_0, 2*t_0 + 4*t_1 + 3, -t_0 - 3*t_1 - 3)
627 
628     See Also
629     ========
630 
631     diop_quadratic(), diop_ternary_quadratic(), diop_general_pythagorean(),
632     diop_general_sum_of_squares()
633     """
634     var, coeff, diop_type = classify_diop(eq, _dict=False)
635 
636     if diop_type == "linear":
637         return _diop_linear(var, coeff, param)
638

640 def _diop_linear(var, coeff, param):
641     """
642     Solves diophantine equations of the form:
643 
644     a_0*x_0 + a_1*x_1 + ... + a_n*x_n == c
645 
646     Note that no solution exists if gcd(a_0, ..., a_n) doesn't divide c.
647     """
648 
649     if 1 in coeff:
650         # negate coeff[] because input is of the form: ax + by + c ==  0
651         #                              but is used as: ax + by     == -c
652         c = -coeff[1]
653     else:
654         c = 0
655 
656     # Some solutions will have multiple free variables in their solutions.
657     if param is None:
658         params = [symbols('t')]*len(var)
659     else:
660         temp = str(param) + "_%i"
661         params = [symbols(temp % i, integer=True) for i in range(len(var))]
662 
663     if len(var) == 1:
664         q, r = divmod(c, coeff[var[0]])
665         if not r:
666             return (q,)
667         else:
668             return (None,)
669 
670     '''
671     base_solution_linear() can solve diophantine equations of the form:
672 
673     a*x + b*y == c
674 
675     We break down multivariate linear diophantine equations into a
676     series of bivariate linear diophantine equations which can then
677     be solved individually by base_solution_linear().
678 
679     Consider the following:
680 
681     a_0*x_0 + a_1*x_1 + a_2*x_2 == c
682 
683     which can be re-written as:
684 
685     a_0*x_0 + g_0*y_0 == c
686 
687     where
688 
689     g_0 == gcd(a_1, a_2)
690 
691     and
692 
693     y == (a_1*x_1)/g_0 + (a_2*x_2)/g_0
694 
695     This leaves us with two binary linear diophantine equations.
696     For the first equation:
697 
698     a == a_0
699     b == g_0
700     c == c
701 
702     For the second:
703 
704     a == a_1/g_0
705     b == a_2/g_0
706     c == the solution we find for y_0 in the first equation.
707 
708     The arrays A and B are the arrays of integers used for
709     'a' and 'b' in each of the n-1 bivariate equations we solve.
710     '''
711 
712     A = [coeff[v] for v in var]
713     B = []
714     if len(var) > 2:
715         B.append(igcd(A[-2], A[-1]))
716         A[-2] = A[-2] // B[0]
717         A[-1] = A[-1] // B[0]
718         for i in range(len(A) - 3, 0, -1):
719             gcd = igcd(B[0], A[i])
720             B[0] = B[0] // gcd
721             A[i] = A[i] // gcd
722             B.insert(0, gcd)
723     B.append(A[-1])
724 
725     '''
726     Consider the trivariate linear equation:
727 
728     4*x_0 + 6*x_1 + 3*x_2 == 2
729 
730     This can be re-written as:
731 
732     4*x_0 + 3*y_0 == 2
733 
734     where
735 
736     y_0 == 2*x_1 + x_2
737     (Note that gcd(3, 6) == 3)
738 
739     The complete integral solution to this equation is:
740 
741     x_0 ==  2 + 3*t_0
742     y_0 == -2 - 4*t_0
743 
744     where 't_0' is any integer.
745 
746     Now that we have a solution for 'x_0', find 'x_1' and 'x_2':
747 
748     2*x_1 + x_2 == -2 - 4*t_0
749 
750     We can then solve for '-2' and '-4' independently,
751     and combine the results:
752 
753     2*x_1a + x_2a == -2
754     x_1a == 0 + t_0
755     x_2a == -2 - 2*t_0
756 
757     2*x_1b + x_2b == -4*t_0
758     x_1b == 0*t_0 + t_1
759     x_2b == -4*t_0 - 2*t_1
760 
761     ==>
762 
763     x_1 == t_0 + t_1
764     x_2 == -2 - 6*t_0 - 2*t_1
765 
766     where 't_0' and 't_1' are any integers.
767 
768     Note that:
769 
770     4*(2 + 3*t_0) + 6*(t_0 + t_1) + 3*(-2 - 6*t_0 - 2*t_1) == 2
771 
772     for any integral values of 't_0', 't_1'; as required.
773 
774     This method is generalised for many variables, below.
775 
776     '''
777     solutions = []
778     for i in range(len(B)):
779         tot_x, tot_y = [], []
780 
781         for j, arg in enumerate(Add.make_args(c)):
782             if arg.is_Integer:
783                 # example: 5 -> k = 5
784                 k, p = arg, S.One
785                 pnew = params[0]
786             else:  # arg is a Mul or Symbol
787                 # example: 3*t_1 -> k = 3
788                 # example: t_0 -> k = 1
789                 k, p = arg.as_coeff_Mul()
790                 pnew = params[params.index(p) + 1]
791 
792             sol = sol_x, sol_y = base_solution_linear(k, A[i], B[i], pnew)
793 
794             if p is S.One:
795                 if None in sol:
796                     return tuple([None]*len(var))
797             else:
798                 # convert a + b*pnew -> a*p + b*pnew
799                 if isinstance(sol_x, Add):
800                     sol_x = sol_x.args[0]*p + sol_x.args[1]
801                 if isinstance(sol_y, Add):
802                     sol_y = sol_y.args[0]*p + sol_y.args[1]
803 
804             tot_x.append(sol_x)
805             tot_y.append(sol_y)
806 
807         solutions.append(Add(*tot_x))
808         c = Add(*tot_y)
809 
810     solutions.append(c)
811     if param is None:
812         # just keep the additive constant (i.e. replace t with 0)
813         solutions = [i.as_coeff_Add()[0] for i in solutions]
814     return tuple(solutions)
815

817 def base_solution_linear(c, a, b, t=None):
818     """
819     Return the base solution for the linear equation, `ax + by = c`.
820 
821     Used by ``diop_linear()`` to find the base solution of a linear
822     Diophantine equation. If ``t`` is given then the parametrized solution is
823     returned.
824 
825     Usage
826     =====
827 
828     ``base_solution_linear(c, a, b, t)``: ``a``, ``b``, ``c`` are coefficients
829     in `ax + by = c` and ``t`` is the parameter to be used in the solution.
830 
831     Examples
832     ========
833 
834     >>> from sympy.solvers.diophantine import base_solution_linear
835     >>> from sympy.abc import t
836     >>> base_solution_linear(5, 2, 3) # equation 2*x + 3*y = 5
837     (-5, 5)
838     >>> base_solution_linear(0, 5, 7) # equation 5*x + 7*y = 0
839     (0, 0)
840     >>> base_solution_linear(5, 2, 3, t) # equation 2*x + 3*y = 5
841     (3*t - 5, 5 - 2*t)
842     >>> base_solution_linear(0, 5, 7, t) # equation 5*x + 7*y = 0
843     (7*t, -5*t)
844     """
845     a, b, c = _remove_gcd(a, b, c)
846 
847     if c == 0:
848         if t is not None:
849             if b < 0:
850                 t = -t
851             return (b*t , -a*t)
852         else:
853             return (0, 0)
854     else:
855         x0, y0, d = igcdex(abs(a), abs(b))
856 
857         x0 *= sign(a)
858         y0 *= sign(b)
859 
860         if divisible(c, d):
861             if t is not None:
862                 if b < 0:
863                     t = -t
864                 return (c*x0 + b*t, c*y0 - a*t)
865             else:
866                 return (c*x0, c*y0)
867         else:
868             return (None, None)
869 
870 
871 def divisible(a, b):
872     """
873     Returns `True` if ``a`` is divisible by ``b`` and `False` otherwise.
874     """
875     return not a % b
876

878 def diop_quadratic(eq, param=symbols("t", integer=True)):
879     """
880     Solves quadratic diophantine equations.
881 
882     i.e. equations of the form `Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0`. Returns a
883     set containing the tuples `(x, y)` which contains the solutions. If there
884     are no solutions then `(None, None)` is returned.
885 
886     Usage
887     =====
888 
889     ``diop_quadratic(eq, param)``: ``eq`` is a quadratic binary diophantine
890     equation. ``param`` is used to indicate the parameter to be used in the
891     solution.
892 
893     Details
894     =======
895 
896     ``eq`` should be an expression which is assumed to be zero.
897     ``param`` is a parameter to be used in the solution.
898 
899     Examples
900     ========
901 
902     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, t
903     >>> from sympy.solvers.diophantine import diop_quadratic
904     >>> diop_quadratic(x**2 + y**2 + 2*x + 2*y + 2, t)
905     {(-1, -1)}
906 
907     References
908     ==========
909 
910     .. [1] Methods to solve Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0, [online],
911           Available: http://www.alpertron.com.ar/METHODS.HTM
912     .. [2] Solving the equation ax^2+ bxy + cy^2 + dx + ey + f= 0, [online],
913           Available: http://www.jpr2718.org/ax2p.pdf
914 
915     See Also
916     ========
917 
918     diop_linear(), diop_ternary_quadratic(), diop_general_sum_of_squares(),
919     diop_general_pythagorean()
920     """
921     var, coeff, diop_type = classify_diop(eq, _dict=False)
922 
923     if diop_type == "binary_quadratic":
924         return _diop_quadratic(var, coeff, param)
925 
926 
927 def _diop_quadratic(var, coeff, t):
928 
929     x, y = var
930 
931     A = coeff[x**2]
932     B = coeff[x*y]
933     C = coeff[y**2]
934     D = coeff[x]
935     E = coeff[y]
936     F = coeff[S.One]
937 
938     A, B, C, D, E, F = [as_int(i) for i in _remove_gcd(A, B, C, D, E, F)]
939 
940     # (1) Simple-Hyperbolic case: A = C = 0, B != 0
941     # In this case equation can be converted to (Bx + E)(By + D) = DE - BF
942     # We consider two cases; DE - BF = 0 and DE - BF != 0
943     # More details, http://www.alpertron.com.ar/METHODS.HTM#SHyperb
944 
945     sol = set([])
946     discr = B**2 - 4*A*C
947     if A == 0 and C == 0 and B != 0:
948 
949         if D*E - B*F == 0:
950             q, r = divmod(E, B)
951             if not r:
952                 sol.add((-q, t))
953             q, r = divmod(D, B)
954             if not r:
955                 sol.add((t, -q))
956         else:
957             div = divisors(D*E - B*F)
958             div = div + [-term for term in div]
959             for d in div:
960                 x0, r = divmod(d - E, B)
961                 if not r:
962                     q, r = divmod(D*E - B*F, d)
963                     if not r:
964                         y0, r = divmod(q - D, B)
965                         if not r:
966                             sol.add((x0, y0))
967 
968     # (2) Parabolic case: B**2 - 4*A*C = 0
969     # There are two subcases to be considered in this case.
970     # sqrt(c)D - sqrt(a)E = 0 and sqrt(c)D - sqrt(a)E != 0
971     # More Details, http://www.alpertron.com.ar/METHODS.HTM#Parabol
972 
973     elif discr == 0:
974 
975         if A == 0:
976             s = _diop_quadratic([y, x], coeff, t)
977             for soln in s:
978                 sol.add((soln[1], soln[0]))
979 
980         else:
981             g = sign(A)*igcd(A, C)
982             a = A // g
983             c = C // g
984             e = sign(B/A)
985 
986             sqa = isqrt(a)
987             sqc = isqrt(c)
988             _c = e*sqc*D - sqa*E
989             if not _c:
990                 z = symbols("z", real=True)
991                 eq = sqa*g*z**2 + D*z + sqa*F
992                 roots = solveset_real(eq, z).intersect(S.Integers)
993                 for root in roots:
994                     ans = diop_solve(sqa*x + e*sqc*y - root)
995                     sol.add((ans[0], ans[1]))
996 
997             elif _is_int(c):
998                 solve_x = lambda u: -e*sqc*g*_c*t**2 - (E + 2*e*sqc*g*u)*t\
999                     - (e*sqc*g*u**2 + E*u + e*sqc*F) // _c
1000 
1001                 solve_y = lambda u: sqa*g*_c*t**2 + (D + 2*sqa*g*u)*t \
1002                     + (sqa*g*u**2 + D*u + sqa*F) // _c
1003 
1004                 for z0 in range(0, abs(_c)):
1005                     # Check if the coefficients of y and x obtained are integers or not
1006                     if (divisible(sqa*g*z0**2 + D*z0 + sqa*F, _c) and
1007                             divisible(e*sqc*g*z0**2 + E*z0 + e*sqc*F, _c)):
1008                         sol.add((solve_x(z0), solve_y(z0)))
1009 
1010     # (3) Method used when B**2 - 4*A*C is a square, is described in p. 6 of the below paper
1011     # by John P. Robertson.
1012     # http://www.jpr2718.org/ax2p.pdf
1013 
1014     elif is_square(discr):
1015         if A != 0:
1016             r = sqrt(discr)
1017             u, v = symbols("u, v", integer=True)
1018             eq = _mexpand(
1019                 4*A*r*u*v + 4*A*D*(B*v + r*u + r*v - B*u) +
1020                 2*A*4*A*E*(u - v) + 4*A*r*4*A*F)
1021 
1022             solution = diop_solve(eq, t)
1023 
1024             for s0, t0 in solution:
1025 
1026                 num = B*t0 + r*s0 + r*t0 - B*s0
1027                 x_0 = S(num)/(4*A*r)
1028                 y_0 = S(s0 - t0)/(2*r)
1029                 if isinstance(s0, Symbol) or isinstance(t0, Symbol):
1030                     if check_param(x_0, y_0, 4*A*r, t) != (None, None):
1031                         ans = check_param(x_0, y_0, 4*A*r, t)
1032                         sol.add((ans[0], ans[1]))
1033                 elif x_0.is_Integer and y_0.is_Integer:
1034                     if is_solution_quad(var, coeff, x_0, y_0):
1035                         sol.add((x_0, y_0))
1036 
1037         else:
1038             s = _diop_quadratic(var[::-1], coeff, t)  # Interchange x and y
1039             while s:                                  #         |
1040                 sol.add(s.pop()[::-1])  # and solution <--------+
1041 
1042 
1043     # (4) B**2 - 4*A*C > 0 and B**2 - 4*A*C not a square or B**2 - 4*A*C < 0
1044 
1045     else:
1046 
1047         P, Q = _transformation_to_DN(var, coeff)
1048         D, N = _find_DN(var, coeff)
1049         solns_pell = diop_DN(D, N)
1050 
1051         if D < 0:
1052             for x0, y0 in solns_pell:
1053                 for x in [-x0, x0]:
1054                     for y in [-y0, y0]:
1055                         s = P*Matrix([x, y]) + Q
1056                         try:
1057                             sol.add(tuple([as_int(_) for _ in s]))
1058                         except ValueError:
1059                             pass
1060         else:
1061             # In this case equation can be transformed into a Pell equation
1062 
1063             solns_pell = set(solns_pell)
1064             for X, Y in list(solns_pell):
1065                 solns_pell.add((-X, -Y))
1066 
1067             a = diop_DN(D, 1)
1068             T = a[0][0]
1069             U = a[0][1]
1070 
1071             if all(_is_int(_) for _ in P[:4] + Q[:2]):
1072                 for r, s in solns_pell:
1073                     _a = (r + s*sqrt(D))*(T + U*sqrt(D))**t
1074                     _b = (r - s*sqrt(D))*(T - U*sqrt(D))**t
1075                     x_n = _mexpand(S(_a + _b)/2)
1076                     y_n = _mexpand(S(_a - _b)/(2*sqrt(D)))
1077                     s = P*Matrix([x_n, y_n]) + Q
1078                     sol.add(tuple(s))
1079 
1080             else:
1081                 L = ilcm(*[_.q for _ in P[:4] + Q[:2]])
1082 
1083                 k = 1
1084 
1085                 T_k = T
1086                 U_k = U
1087 
1088                 while (T_k - 1) % L != 0 or U_k % L != 0:
1089                     T_k, U_k = T_k*T + D*U_k*U, T_k*U + U_k*T
1090                     k += 1
1091 
1092                 for X, Y in solns_pell:
1093 
1094                     for i in range(k):
1095                         if all(_is_int(_) for _ in P*Matrix([X, Y]) + Q):
1096                             _a = (X + sqrt(D)*Y)*(T_k + sqrt(D)*U_k)**t
1097                             _b = (X - sqrt(D)*Y)*(T_k - sqrt(D)*U_k)**t
1098                             Xt = S(_a + _b)/2
1099                             Yt = S(_a - _b)/(2*sqrt(D))
1100                             s = P*Matrix([Xt, Yt]) + Q
1101                             sol.add(tuple(s))
1102 
1103                         X, Y = X*T + D*U*Y, X*U + Y*T
1104 
1105     return sol
1106

1108 def is_solution_quad(var, coeff, u, v):
1109     """
1110     Check whether `(u, v)` is solution to the quadratic binary diophantine
1111     equation with the variable list ``var`` and coefficient dictionary
1112     ``coeff``.
1113 
1114     Not intended for use by normal users.
1115     """
1116     reps = dict(zip(var, (u, v)))
1117     eq = Add(*[j*i.xreplace(reps) for i, j in coeff.items()])
1118     return _mexpand(eq) == 0
1119
